declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.isQuasiCompactObject_iff_isQuasiCompact_sheafifiedYoneda
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D06.** Let `C` be a site and `U` an object of `C`. The following are equivalent:

1. `U` is a quasi-compact object of the site (Stacks 090H): every covering of `U` is refined by a
   covering that factors through only finitely many of its members;
2. for every surjection of sheaves `∐_{i ∈ I} F i ⟶ h_U^#` there is a finite `T ⊆ I` for which
   `∐_{i ∈ T} F i ⟶ h_U^#` is still surjective, i.e. `h_U^#` is a quasi-compact object of the
   topos `Sh(C)` (Stacks 0D07).

Here `h_U^# = (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).obj U` is the sheafification of the presheaf represented
by `U`.
declarations.comment:
An object of a site is quasi-compact if and only if the sheafification of the
  presheaf it represents is a quasi-compact object of the topos of sheaves of sets.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.IsQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
An object `F` of the topos `Sh(C)` of sheaves of sets on a site is *quasi-compact* if for
every locally surjective map `∐_{i ∈ I} G i ⟶ F` of sheaves there is a finite subset `T ⊆ I` for
which `∐_{i ∈ T} G i ⟶ F` is still locally surjective.
declarations.statement: def IsQuasiCompact (F : Sheaf J (Type max v u)) : Prop
declarations.comment: A quasi-compact object of the topos of sheaves of sets on a site.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.IsQuasiCompactTopos
declarations.doc:
The topos `Sh(C)` of sheaves of sets on a site is *quasi-compact* if its final object is a
quasi-compact object.
declarations.statement: def IsQuasiCompactTopos (J : GrothendieckTopology C) : Prop
declarations.comment: A quasi-compact topos: its final object is a quasi-compact object.

declarations.name: Algebra.naiveCotangentComplex_quasiIso_henselization_and_strictHenselization
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a local homomorphism of local rings. For the induced local map between
henselizations and the induced local map between strict henselizations associated to a compatible
map of residue fields, the canonical maps
`NL_{B/A} ⊗_B Bʰ ⟶ NL_{Bʰ/Aʰ}` and `NL_{B/A} ⊗_B Bˢʰ ⟶ NL_{Bˢʰ/Aˢʰ}` induce
isomorphisms on all homology groups.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    naiveCotangentComplex_quasiIso_henselization_and_strictHenselization
    (A Ah Ash : Type u) (B Bh Bsh : Type v) (kAsep : Type u) (kBsep : Type v)
    [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    [CommRing Ah] [IsLocalRing Ah] [Algebra A Ah]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) Ah]
    [CommRing Bh] [IsLocalRing Bh] [Algebra B Bh]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization B (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) Bh]
    [Algebra A Bh] [IsScalarTower A B Bh] [Algebra Ah Bh] [IsScalarTower A Ah Bh]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Ah Bh)]
    [Field kAsep] [Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) kAsep]
    [IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) kAsep]
    [CommRing Ash] [IsLocalRing Ash] [Algebra A Ash]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization A kAsep Ash]
    [Field kBsep] [Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) kBsep]
    [IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) kBsep]
    [CommRing Bsh] [IsLocalRing Bsh] [Algebra B Bsh]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization B kBsep Bsh]
    [Algebra A Bsh] [IsScalarTower A B Bsh] [Algebra Ash Bsh] [IsScalarTower A Ash Bsh]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Ash Bsh)]
    (phi : IsLocalRing.ResidueField Ash →+* IsLocalRing.ResidueField Bsh)
    (_hphi : phi.comp ((IsLocalRing.residue Ash).comp (algebraMap A Ash)) =
      (IsLocalRing.residue Bsh).comp (algebraMap A Bsh))
    (_hinduced : (IsLocalRing.residue Bsh).comp (algebraMap Ash Bsh) =
      phi.comp (IsLocalRing.residue Ash)) :
    QuasiIso (Algebra.naiveCotangentComplexBaseChangeComparison A Ah B Bh) ∧
      QuasiIso (Algebra.naiveCotangentComplexBaseChangeComparison A Ash B Bsh)

declarations.name: Algebra.naiveCotangentComplex_quasiIso_henselizationPair
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D08 for the henselization of a pair.** Let `P` be an algebra over a commutative
ring `k`, let `J ⊆ P` be an ideal and let `(Pʰ, Jʰ)` be the henselization of the pair `(P, J)`,
described by the henselian-pair condition on `Pʰ` together with its universal property. Then the
canonical comparison map

`NL_{P/k} ⊗_P Pʰ ⟶ NL_{Pʰ/k}`

induces isomorphisms on all homology groups.

The source states Stacks 0D08 for the henselization and the strict henselization of a local
ring, which is
`naiveCotangentComplex_quasiIso_henselization_and_strictHenselization`. Its proof uses of those
two only that they are filtered colimits of étale algebras over their bases, and the
henselization of a pair is such a colimit by `ind_henselization`; this is the instance Stacks
0DZC's proof appeals to 0D08 for.
declarations.statement:
public theorem naiveCotangentComplex_quasiIso_henselizationPair
    (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (P : Type v) [CommRing P] [Algebra k P] (J : Ideal P)
    (Ph : Type v) [CommRing Ph] [Algebra P Ph] [Algebra k Ph] [IsScalarTower k P Ph]
    (hhens : HenselianPair Ph (J.map (algebraMap P Ph)))
    (huniv : ∀ (C : Type v) (_ : CommRing C) (JC : Ideal C), HenselianPair C JC →
      ∀ f : P →+* C, J ≤ JC.comap f →
        ∃! g : Ph →+* C, g.comp (algebraMap P Ph) = f ∧
          J.map (algebraMap P Ph) ≤ JC.comap g) :
    QuasiIso (naiveCotangentComplexBaseChangeComparison k k P Ph)
declarations.comment: the henselization-of-pairs case, which Stacks 0DZC's proof cites 0D08 for although 0D08's own statement is about the local and strict henselizations of a local ring: the input to the source's proof is that both vertical maps are filtered colimits of étale maps, which `ind_henselization` supplies for the henselization of a pair

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentStalk_eq_naiveCotangentComplexStalk
declarations.doc:
`NL_{𝓑/𝓐, x} = NL_{𝓑ₓ/𝓐ₓ}`: the stalk at `x` of the naive cotangent complex of `B` over `A`
is the naive cotangent complex of `Bₓ` over `Aₓ`.

The underlying additive bijections of the two terms are
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentStalkCotangentEquiv` in degree `-1` and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentStalkCotangentSpaceEquiv` in degree `0`; the three clauses
say that both are semilinear over the stalk `(A[B])ₓ → Bₓ` of the canonical presentation, which
is surjective, so they are `Bₓ`-linear, and that they commute with the differentials.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCotangentStalk_eq_naiveCotangentComplexStalk :
    letI := algebraStalk a.hom x
    (∀ (r : ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (freeAlgebraSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A
          (underlyingPresheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) B)).obj x)) ξ,
        naiveCotangentStalkCotangentEquiv A B a x (r • ξ) =
          (show ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk B.obj x) from
              ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat.{u} x).map
                (presentation (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A B a
                  (underlyingPresheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) B) (𝟙 _)).hom).hom r) •
            naiveCotangentStalkCotangentEquiv A B a x ξ) ∧
      (∀ (r : ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (freeAlgebraSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A
          (underlyingPresheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) B)).obj x)) ξ,
        naiveCotangentStalkCotangentSpaceEquiv A B a x (r • ξ) =
          (show ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk B.obj x) from
              ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat.{u} x).map
                (presentation (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A B a
                  (underlyingPresheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) B) (𝟙 _)).hom).hom r) •
            naiveCotangentStalkCotangentSpaceEquiv A B a x ξ) ∧
      ∀ ξ, naiveCotangentStalkCotangentSpaceEquiv A B a x
            (conormalSequenceStalkMapF A (freeAlgebraSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A
              (underlyingPresheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) B)) B
              (freeAlgebraSheafCoefficientMap (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A
                (underlyingPresheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) B))
              (presentation (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A B a
                (underlyingPresheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) B) (𝟙 _)) x ξ) =
          (Algebra.Generators.self (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk A.obj x))
              (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk B.obj x))).toExtension.cotangentComplex
            (naiveCotangentStalkCotangentEquiv A B a x ξ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ModuleComparison.isIso_piComparison_rightDerivedPlus_evaluation_zero
declarations.doc:
**Degree-zero cohomology of modules on a ringed space commutes with arbitrary products**:
the canonical map from the degree-zero cohomology over an open `U` of a product of sheaves of
modules to the product of their degree-zero cohomologies is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_piComparison_rightDerivedPlus_evaluation_zero
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u}) (U : Opens X)
    {I : Type u} (F : I → SheafOfModules.{u} O) :
    IsIso (piComparison ((SheafOfModules.evaluation O (op U)).rightDerivedPlus 0) F)
declarations.comment: degree zero

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ModuleComparison.mono_piComparison_rightDerivedPlus_evaluation_one
declarations.doc:
**Degree-one cohomology of modules on a ringed space injects into the product**: the
canonical map from the degree-one cohomology over an open `U` of a product of sheaves of
modules to the product of their degree-one cohomologies is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_piComparison_rightDerivedPlus_evaluation_one
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u}) (U : Opens X)
    {I : Type u} (F : I → SheafOfModules.{u} O) :
    Mono (piComparison ((SheafOfModules.evaluation O (op U)).rightDerivedPlus 1) F)
declarations.comment: degree one

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSupportCoherent.derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedPushforward_of_properSupp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0D0B].** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme, let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of
schemes which is locally of finite type and let `E` be an object of `D^+_Coh(𝒪_X)` such that the
support of `H^i(E)` is proper over `S` for all `i`. Then `Rf_*E` is an object of `D^+_Coh(𝒪_S)`.

This is `derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedPushforward_of_isProperOver_supp` with its appeal to
[Stacks, Tag 02O5] supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProperCoherenceWitness.higherDirectImageIsCoherentOverAffineBase`, a
theorem.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedPushforward_of_properSupp [IsNoetherian S]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus (fun M : X.Modules => M.IsCoherent) E)
    (hsupp : ∀ j : ℤ, IsProperOver f
      ⟨SheafOfModules.supp ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E),
        @SheafOfModules.isClosed_supp _ _ _ (hE.2 j).isFiniteType⟩) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus (fun N : S.Modules => N.IsCoherent)
      ((derivedPushforwardModules f).obj E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedCategoryBPlus_coherent_affineDerivedSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**The coherence clause of [Stacks, Tag 0D0C] on an affine scheme.** Let `R` be a Noetherian
ring, let `K` be an object of `D⁻_Coh(R)` and `L` an object of `D⁺_Coh(R)`. Then
`R𝓗om_{𝒪_{Spec R}}(K̃, L̃)` lies in `D⁺_Coh(𝒪_{Spec R})`: it is cohomologically bounded below and
all of its cohomology sheaves are coherent.

Boundedness below is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isBoundedBelow_derivedSheafHom`, the clause of the
tag the library already carries, applied after transporting the bounds of `K` and `L` to their
sheafifications. Coherence is `isCoherent_homology_affineDerivedSheafHom`.

The hypotheses are on the module-level objects `K` and `L`; the source states the tag for objects
of `D⁻_Coh(𝒪_X)` and `D⁺_Coh(𝒪_X)` on an arbitrary locally Noetherian `X`, and neither the
reduction to an affine open nor the identification of a sheaf-level coherent complex with a
sheafification ([Stacks, Tag 06Z0]) is carried out here; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryBPlus_coherent_affineDerivedSheafHom [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBMinus
      (fun M : ModuleCat.{u} R => Module.Finite R M) K)
    (hL : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (fun M : ModuleCat.{u} R => Module.Finite R M) L) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus (A := (Spec R).Modules)
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules (Spec R).ringCatSheaf)
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom (Spec R).sheaf).obj
          (op ((tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategory.obj K))).obj
            ((tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategory.obj L))
declarations.comment: the coherence clause on Spec R, for sheafified D⁻_Coh and D⁺_Coh arguments

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedCategoryBPlus_isCoherent_derivedSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D0C.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme, `K` an object of
`D⁻_Coh(𝒪_X)` and `L` an object of `D⁺_Coh(𝒪_X)`. Then `R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(K, L)` lies in
`D⁺_Coh(𝒪_X)`.

Boundedness below is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isBoundedBelow_derivedSheafHom`, which needs only the
two cohomological bounds; coherence of the cohomology sheaves is
`isCoherent_homology_derivedSheafHom`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryBPlus_isCoherent_derivedSheafHom (Y : Scheme.{u})
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (E F : DerivedCategory Y.Modules)
    (hE : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBMinus
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf) E)
    (hF : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf) F) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf)
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj (op E)).obj F)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isBoundedBelow_derivedSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**The derived internal Hom of a bounded-above complex into a bounded-below complex is
cohomologically bounded below.** If `K` is bounded above and `L` is bounded below, then
`RSheafHom(K, L)` is bounded below, on an arbitrary ringed space.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isBoundedBelow_derivedSheafHom
    (K L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedAbove K) (hL : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow L) :
    DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow (((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op K)).obj L)
declarations.comment: the boundedness clause, on an arbitrary ringed space and with no coherence or Noetherian hypothesis; the coherence clause is not carried

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSupportCoherent.moduleFinite_ext_of_proper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D0D.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, let `X` be a scheme proper over
`A`, let `K` be an object of `D^-_Coh(𝒪_X)` and let `L` be an object of `D^+_Coh(𝒪_X)`. Then the
`A`-module `Ext^n_{𝒪_X}(K, L)` is finite, for every `n`, the `A`-action being the canonical one
induced by the structure morphism `X ⟶ Spec A`.

`Ext^n_{𝒪_X}(K, L)` is `Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(K, L⟦n⟧)`, which is the degree-zero cohomology of
`RΓ(X, R𝓗om(K, L⟦n⟧))` as an `A`-module by `extLinearEquiv`, that is by [Stacks, Tag 08DK];
`R𝓗om(K, L⟦n⟧)` is an object of `D^+_Coh(𝒪_X)` by [Stacks, Tag 0D0C], the shift of `L` being one
by `derivedCategoryBPlus_isCoherent_shift`; and
`moduleFinite_homologyZero_derivedGlobalSections_of_proper` makes the degree-zero
hypercohomology of such an object a finite `A`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleFinite_ext_of_proper {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of A))) [IsProper X.hom]
    (K L : DerivedCategory X.left.Modules)
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBMinus
      (fun M : X.left.Modules => M.IsCoherent) K)
    (hL : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (fun M : X.left.Modules => M.IsCoherent) L)
    (n : ℤ) :
    letI : Linear A X.left.Modules := modulesLinear A X
    Module.Finite A (DerivedCategory.Ext K L n)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Affine.isZero_firstCohomology_sheafHom_of_isLocallyProjective
declarations.doc:
**The first cohomology of an internal hom out of a locally projective module on an affine
scheme vanishes.** The source is a retract of a free module, so the internal hom is a retract of
the internal hom out of that free module, which is a product of copies of the target; the first
cohomology of that product vanishes because the first cohomology of a quasi-coherent module on
an affine scheme does.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_firstCohomology_sheafHom_of_isLocallyProjective (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine T]
    (F G : T.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent] (H : SheafHom T.sheaf F G)
    (hF : Scheme.Modules.IsLocallyProjective F) :
    IsZero (Hgroup T.ringCatSheaf ⊤ 1 H.obj)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smooth.formallySmooth_tfae
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0D0F].** For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` the following are
equivalent: `f` is formally smooth; `f` is formally smooth on a neighbourhood of every point of
`X`; the ring map `Γ(Y, V) ⟶ Γ(X, U)` is formally smooth for every pair of affine opens with
`f(U) ⊆ V`; and there is one affine open covering of `Y` together with, over each of its
members, an affine open covering of its inverse image, on whose charts those ring maps are
formally smooth.

The implications `1 → 3`, `1 → 2`, `3 → 4`, `4 → 2` and `2 → 3` are the formal manipulations of
[Stacks Project, Tag 02H3] and the affine criterion [Stacks Project, Tag 02H4] together with the
affine-locality of formal smoothness of ring maps. The remaining implication `3 → 1` is
`Stacks.Smooth.formallySmooth_of_formallySmooth_appLE`, the torsor argument of the source, whose
pseudo-torsor is `Stacks.Smooth.isLiftPseudoTorsor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallySmooth_tfae {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [AlgebraicGeometry.FormallySmooth f,
        ∀ x : X, ∃ (U : X.Opens) (V : Y.Opens), x ∈ U ∧ f.base x ∈ V ∧
          ∃ hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V, AlgebraicGeometry.FormallySmooth (f.resLE V U hUV),
        ∀ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → ∀ V : Y.Opens, IsAffineOpen V →
          ∀ hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V, (f.appLE V U hUV).hom.FormallySmooth,
        ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → Y.Opens), IsOpenCover V ∧ (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j)) ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens) (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V j),
            (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) ∧
              ∀ i, (f.appLE (V j) (U i) ((le_iSup U i).trans hU.le)).hom.FormallySmooth]
declarations.comment: all four criteria, for an arbitrary morphism of schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0H.** The naive cotangent complex `NL_f = NL_{X/Y}` of a morphism of schemes
`f : X ⟶ Y`: the naive cotangent complex of Stacks 08TN of the underlying morphism of ringed
spaces of `f`, that is, `NL_{𝒪_X / f^{-1}𝒪_Y}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveCotangentComplex :
    CochainComplex (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace.carrier) X.toRingedSpace.sheaf)) ℤ

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentAffineQuasiIso.quasiIso_comparisonMap
declarations.doc:
If `U` and `V` are affine, the canonical map `comparisonMap f hVU` from the sheaf associated
to `NL_{A/R}` to the restriction of `NL_{X/Y}` to `V` is a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_comparisonMap (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
    QuasiIso (comparisonMap f hVU)
declarations.comment: the canonical map (NL_{A/R})~ to NL_{X/Y}|_V is an isomorphism in D(O_V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isZero_homology_naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0J, vanishing clause.** The cohomology sheaves of the naive cotangent complex
`NL_{X/Y}` of a morphism of schemes vanish outside degrees `-1` and `0`: the complex has no
terms in those degrees, so it is exact there.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_homology_naiveCotangentComplex (i : ℤ) (hneg : i ≠ -1) (hzero : i ≠ 0) :
    IsZero ((naiveCotangentComplex f).homology i)
declarations.comment:
the vanishing outside degrees -1 and 0 only; quasi-coherence and H^0 = Omega are
proved separately

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.naiveCotangentExtZeroAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**`Ext⁰_{𝒪_X}(NL_{X/Y}, 𝒢) = Hom_{𝒪_X}(Ω_{X/Y}, 𝒢)`.** The naive cotangent complex of a
morphism of schemes lives in cohomological degrees `≤ 0`, so `Ext⁰` out of it is the group of
homomorphisms out of its degree `0` cohomology sheaf, and that sheaf is the sheaf of relative
differentials by [Stacks Project, Tag 0D0J].

This is the `Ext⁰` term of the infinitesimal-automorphism clause of
[Stacks Project, Tag 0DY9]: the source writes that clause's group first as
`Ext⁰_{𝒪_X}(NL_{X/k}, 𝒪_X)` and then as `Hom_{𝒪_X}(Ω_{X/k}, 𝒪_X)`, and this is the passage
between the two. `f` is an arbitrary morphism of schemes and `𝒢` an arbitrary sheaf of
`𝒪_X`-modules.
declarations.statement:
def naiveCotangentExtZeroAddEquiv {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (G : X.Modules) :
    naiveCotangentExt f G 0 ≃+ (Hom.relativeDifferentials f ⟶ G)
declarations.comment: the Ext^0 reading of the degree-zero identification: Ext^0(NL_{X/Y}, G) = Hom(Omega_{X/Y}, G) for a morphism of schemes and an arbitrary sheaf of coefficients, the naive cotangent complex living in cohomological degrees at most zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isQuasicoherent_homology_naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0J, quasi-coherence clause.** Every cohomology sheaf of the naive cotangent
complex `NL_{X/Y}` of a morphism of schemes is a quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules: in
degree `-1` by the affine-local argument, in degree `0` because it is `Ω_{X/Y}`, and in every
other degree because it is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_homology_naiveCotangentComplex {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (i : ℤ) :
    ((naiveCotangentComplex f).homology i).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: quasi-coherence of the cohomology sheaves; not H^0 = Omega, not the vanishing

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.naiveCotangentComplexHomologyZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0J, degree zero.** The degree `0` cohomology sheaf of the naive cotangent
complex `NL_{X/Y}` of a morphism of schemes is the sheaf of relative differentials
`Ω_{X/Y}`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveCotangentComplexHomologyZeroIso :
    (naiveCotangentComplex f).homology 0 ≅ Hom.relativeDifferentials f
declarations.comment:
the degree-zero identification H^0 of NL with Omega; not quasi-coherence, not
the vanishing in the other degrees

declarations.name: Stacks.NaiveCotangentFinitePresentation.exists_affine_quasiIso_associatedDouble_naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0K.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be locally of finite presentation and let `x` be a point of
`X`.  Then there are affine opens `V ∋ x` of `X` and `U` of `Y` with `V ⊆ f^{-1}U`, a two-term
complex `δ : M₁ ⟶ M₀` of `Γ(X, V)`-modules, and a quasi-isomorphism from the complex of sheaves
of `𝒪_V`-modules associated to `δ` to the restriction of `NL_{X/Y}` to `V`, such that the
degree-`0` term of that complex of sheaves is quasi-coherent of finite presentation and its
degree-`-1` term is quasi-coherent of finite type.

The two-term complex is `NL(P)` for a presentation `A = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(g_1, …, g_m)` of
`A = Γ(X, V)` over `R = Γ(Y, U)` with finitely many variables and finitely many relations, which
exists because `f` is locally of finite presentation.  Its degree-`0` term is finite free on the
variables, hence finitely presented, and its degree-`-1` term `I/I²` is generated by the classes
of the relations, hence finite — and no better, which is why the two degrees are given different
finiteness assertions.  The quasi-isomorphism is the sheafification of the comparison
`NL(P) ⟶ NL_{A/R}` of Stacks 00S1, which is a homotopy equivalence and therefore survives any
additive functor, followed by the canonical map `(NL_{A/R})~ ⟶ NL_{X/Y}|_V` of Stacks 0D0I.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_quasiIso_associatedDouble_naiveCotangentComplex (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (x : X) :
    ∃ (U : Y.Opens) (V : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (_ : IsAffineOpen V) (_ : x ∈ V)
      (_ : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (M₁ M₀ : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, V)) (δ : M₁ ⟶ M₀)
      (ψ : associatedDouble δ ⟶ restrictedNaiveCotangentComplex f (V := V)),
      QuasiIso ψ ∧ ((associatedDouble δ).X 0).IsFinitePresentation ∧
        ((associatedDouble δ).X (-1)).IsFiniteType ∧
        ((associatedDouble δ).X 0).IsQuasicoherent ∧
        ((associatedDouble δ).X (-1)).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the whole statement.  `locally on X` is read as: for every point `x` of `X` there are affine opens `V ∋ x` of `X` and `U` of `Y` with `V ⊆ f^{-1}U`, and the complex of quasi-coherent `O_V`-modules is produced on that `V`. The source says `NL_{X/Y}` is quasi-isomorphic TO the two-term complex; what is produced here is a quasi-isomorphism FROM the two-term complex to `NL_{X/Y}|_V`, which is the same content, a quasi-isomorphism being invertible in `D(O_V)`. The two-term complex is `NL(P)` sheafified, for a presentation of `Gamma(X, V)` over `Gamma(Y, U)` with finitely many variables and finitely many relations, which exists because `f` is locally of finite presentation; its degree-0 term is finite free on the variables and its degree-(-1) term `I/I^2` is generated by the classes of the relations and no better, which is why the two degrees are given DIFFERENT finiteness assertions -- degree 0 `IsFinitePresentation`, degree -1 `IsFiniteType` -- exactly as the tag states. The quasi-isomorphism is the sheafification of the comparison `NL(P) -> NL_{A/R}` of [Stacks, Tag 00S1], taken in its HOMOTOPY EQUIVALENCE form so that it survives an additive functor, composed with the canonical map `(NL_{A/R})~ -> NL_{X/Y}|_V` of [Stacks, Tag 0D0I]; the target is `Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f` ([Stacks, Tag 0D0H]) restricted along `V.iota`. The sole hypothesis is `[LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]`, which is the source's own: [Stacks, Tag 0D0K] is the lemma for a morphism locally of finite presentation. Every other input is proved: [Stacks, Tag 00S1] in `isHomotopyEquiv_nlMapCanonical`, [Stacks, Tag 0D0I] in `Stacks.NaiveCotangentAffineQuasiIso.quasiIso_comparisonMap`, and the finiteness of the two terms in `finitePresentation_cotangentSpace` and `finite_cotangent`

declarations.name: Stacks.Smooth.formallySmooth_iff_isZero_homology_negOne_and_isLocallyProjective_homology_zero
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` is formally smooth if and only if the degree `-1`
cohomology sheaf of its naive cotangent complex vanishes and its degree `0` cohomology sheaf is
locally projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallySmooth_iff_isZero_homology_negOne_and_isLocallyProjective_homology_zero :
    AlgebraicGeometry.FormallySmooth f ↔
      (IsZero ((Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f).homology (-1)) ∧
        Scheme.Modules.IsLocallyProjective ((Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f).homology 0))

declarations.name: Stacks.Smooth.formallyEtale_iff_isZero_homology_naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0D0M].** A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is formally étale if and
only if both cohomology sheaves of its naive cotangent complex vanish,
`H^{-1}(NL_{X/S}) = H^0(NL_{X/S}) = 0`.

The forward implication is
`Stacks.Smooth.isZero_homology_naiveCotangentComplex_of_formallyEtale` and the converse is
`Stacks.Smooth.formallyEtale_of_isZero_homology_naiveCotangentComplex`.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallyEtale_iff_isZero_homology_naiveCotangentComplex :
    FormallyEtale f ↔
      IsZero ((Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f).homology (-1)) ∧
        IsZero ((Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f).homology 0)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smooth.smooth_iff_isZero_homology_negOne_and_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Smoothness read on the naive cotangent complex.** A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is
smooth if and only if it is locally of finite presentation, `H⁻¹(NL_{X/S}) = 0`, and
`Ω_{X/S} = H⁰(NL_{X/S})` is finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_iff_isZero_homology_negOne_and_isFiniteLocallyFree :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth f ↔
      (AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧
        IsZero ((Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f).homology (-1)) ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree (R := X.ringCatSheaf)
          (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f))

declarations.name: Stacks.Smooth.smooth_iff_isZero_homology_negOne_and_isFiniteLocallyFree_homology_zero
declarations.doc:
**Smoothness read on the naive cotangent complex, with the third clause on `H⁰(NL_{X/S})`.**
A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is smooth if and only if it is locally of finite presentation,
`H⁻¹(NL_{X/S}) = 0`, and `H⁰(NL_{X/S})` is finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_iff_isZero_homology_negOne_and_isFiniteLocallyFree_homology_zero :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth f ↔
      (AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧
        IsZero ((Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f).homology (-1)) ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree (R := X.ringCatSheaf)
          ((Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f).homology 0))
declarations.comment: the third clause read on H^0(NL_{X/S}) rather than on Omega_{X/S}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.strictTransformSheaf_isLocallyGeneratedByOnSite
declarations.doc:
Let `F` be a finite type quasi-coherent module on an algebraic space `Bsp`, let `Z ⊆ Bsp` be
the closed subspace cut out by the `k`-th Fitting ideal sheaf of `F`, and let `b : Bsp' ⟶ Bsp` be
the blowup of `Bsp` in `Z`.  Then the strict transform of `F` can locally be generated by `k`
sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem strictTransformSheaf_isLocallyGeneratedByOnSite
    {Bsp Bsp' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Bsp.1 Bsp.2) (k : ℕ)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Bsp.1)
    (hZ : definingIdealSheaf B S hS Bsp Z = fittingIdeal B S hS Bsp.1 Bsp.2 F k)
    {b : Bsp' ⟶ Bsp} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) (hFqc : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hFfin : ∀ W : SmallEtale B S hS Bsp.1,
      IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Bsp.1 ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W) →
        Module.Finite (chartRing B S hS Bsp.1 Bsp.2 W) (F.val.obj (op W))) :
    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyGeneratedByOnSite
      (strictTransformSheaf B S hS (𝟙 Bsp) b (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1 F) k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_strictTransformSheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `F` be a finite type quasi-coherent module on an algebraic space `Bsp`, let `Z ⊆ Bsp` be
the closed subspace cut out by the `k`-th Fitting ideal sheaf of `F`, let `b : Bsp' ⟶ Bsp` be the
blowup of `Bsp` in `Z`, and assume that `F` is locally free of rank `k` on the open complement
`Bsp ∖ Z`.  Then the strict transform of `F` is locally free of rank `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_strictTransformSheaf
    {Bsp Bsp' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Bsp.1 Bsp.2) (k : ℕ)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Bsp.1)
    (hZ : definingIdealSheaf B S hS Bsp Z = fittingIdeal B S hS Bsp.1 Bsp.2 F k)
    {b : Bsp' ⟶ Bsp} (hb : IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b) (hFqc : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hFfin : ∀ W : SmallEtale B S hS Bsp.1,
      IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Bsp.1 ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W) →
        Module.Finite (chartRing B S hS Bsp.1 Bsp.2 W) (F.val.obj (op W)))
    (h : RingedSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (openComplementSpace B S hS Bsp Z).1
        (openComplementSpace B S hS Bsp Z).2)
      ((modulePullback B S hS (openComplementHom B S hS Bsp Z)).obj F) k) :
    RingedSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (strictTransformPullback B S hS (𝟙 Bsp) b).1
        (strictTransformPullback B S hS (𝟙 Bsp) b).2)
      (strictTransformSheaf B S hS (𝟙 Bsp) b (preimageClosedSubspace b Z).1 F) k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedModulePushforward_of_hasProperSupport
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme and `f : X ⟶ Y` a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally
of finite type, with `Y` Noetherian.  Let `E ∈ D^+_{Coh}(𝒪_X)` be such that the support of
`H^i(E)` is proper over `Y` for all `i`.  Then `Rf_*E ∈ D^+_{Coh}(𝒪_Y)`.  (With the support
only proper over `S` the statement is false; see the module documentation.)
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedModulePushforward_of_hasProperSupport
    (hTop : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom)
    (hY : IsNoetherian B S hS hTop Y.1)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hE : derivedCategoryBPlus (isCoherent.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) E)
    (hsupp : ∀ i : ℤ, HasProperSupport B S hS X.2 Y.2 f.hom hf
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) i).obj E))) :
    derivedCategoryBPlus (isCoherent.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
      ((Stacks.DerivedFunctor.totalRightDerived (modulePushforward B S hS f)).obj E)
declarations.comment: with the support of each H^i(E) proper over Y: proper over S, as printed, the statement fails (the open immersion of one chart P^1 into the projective line with doubled origin over a field, with E = O_X), and Y is what the source's proof, through 08GK, uses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBoundedBelow_sheafHomComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0S, the bounded-below clause, on a pair of models.** If `A` is concentrated in
degrees `≤ d` and `J` in degrees `≥ b`, the class of the internal Hom complex `SheafHom(A, J)`
in `D(𝒪_X)` is cohomologically bounded below.

For `A` a model of `K` and `J` a K-injective model of `L` this object is `RSheafHom(K, L)`, so
this is the `D⁺` half of the tag, with no hypothesis beyond the two bounds — neither local
Noetherianity nor coherence of the cohomology of `K` and `L`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isBoundedBelow_sheafHomComplex
    (d b : ℤ) (A J : CochainComplex (Modules.{u, max (u + 1) m} B S hS F hF) ℤ)
    [CochainComplex.IsStrictlyLE A d] [CochainComplex.IsStrictlyGE J b] :
    DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (sheafHomComplex (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF) A J).obj)
declarations.comment: the bounded-below clause, on a pair of models and with no Noetherian or coherence hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBoundedBelow_derivedSheafHomOnSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0S, the bounded-below clause.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`. If `K` is
in `D⁻_Coh(𝒪_X)` and `L` is in `D⁺_Coh(𝒪_X)`, then `RSheafHom(K, L)` is cohomologically bounded
below.

`RSheafHom(K, L)` is the class of the internal Hom complex `SheafHom(A, J)` of a model `A` of
`K` and a K-injective model `J` of `L`; such a pair exists by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isStrictlyLE_isStrictlyGE_isKInjective_model`, and the
conclusion holds for it, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBoundedBelow_sheafHomComplex`.

Only the boundedness halves of `hK` and `hL` are used, and local Noetherianity of `X` is not
needed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isBoundedBelow_derivedSheafHomOnSpace
    (K L : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, max (u + 1) m} B S hS F hF))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBMinus
      (fun N : Modules.{u, max (u + 1) m} B S hS F hF =>
        SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite N) K)
    (hL : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (fun N : Modules.{u, max (u + 1) m} B S hS F hF =>
        SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite N) L) :
    ∃ A J : CochainComplex (Modules.{u, max (u + 1) m} B S hS F hF) ℤ,
      CochainComplex.IsKInjective J ∧ Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj A ≅ K) ∧
        Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj J ≅ L) ∧
        DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
            (sheafHomComplex (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF) A J).obj)
declarations.comment: the bounded-below clause, for K and L themselves and with no Noetherian hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedCategoryBPlus_isCoherentOnSite_sheafHomComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0S.** On a locally Noetherian algebraic space, `RSheafHom(K, L)` lies in
`D⁺_Coh(𝒪_X)` for `K` in `D⁻_Coh(𝒪_X)` and `L` in `D⁺_Coh(𝒪_X)`, read on a model `A` of `K` and
a K-injective model `J` of `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryBPlus_isCoherentOnSite_sheafHomComplex
    [HasDerivedCategory.{t} (Modules.{u, u + 1} B S hS X.1 X.2)]
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun V : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian V))
    (d b : ℤ) (A J : CochainComplex (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) ℤ)
    [CochainComplex.IsStrictlyLE A d] [CochainComplex.IsKInjective J]
    [CochainComplex.IsStrictlyGE J b]
    (hA : ∀ i, SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite (A.homology i))
    (hJ : ∀ i, SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite (J.homology i)) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (fun N : Modules.{u, u + 1} B S hS X.1 X.2 => SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite N)
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (sheafHomComplex (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2) A J).obj)
declarations.comment: read on a model of K and a K-injective model of L

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.moduleFinite_hom_shift_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0T.**  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring and `X` an algebraic space over `A` proper over
`A`.  Let `K ∈ D⁻_Coh(𝒪_X)` and `L ∈ D⁺_Coh(𝒪_X)`.  Then `Ext^n_X(K, L) = Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(K, L[n])`
is a finite `A`-module for every `n ∈ ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleFinite_hom_shift_of_isProper [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseObject A B hA)) (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of A)) hA f)
    (K L : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B (Spec (.of A)) hA X hX))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBMinus (isCoherent.{u, u} B (Spec (.of A)) hA X hX) K)
    (hL : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus (isCoherent.{u, u} B (Spec (.of A)) hA X hX) L)
    (n : ℤ) : Module.Finite A (K ⟶ L⟦n⟧)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0V.** The naive cotangent complex `NL_{X/Y} = NL_f` of a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
algebraic spaces: the naive cotangent complex of the inverse-image form `f⁻¹𝒪_Y ⟶ 𝒪_X` of the
structure map of the morphism of small étale ringed topoi of `f`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.naiveCotangentEtaleLocalisationIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0W, the identification of the two naive cotangent complexes.**  For a commuting
square `p ≫ f = g ≫ q` of algebraic spaces over `S` with `p` and `q` étale,

`NL_{p⁻¹𝒪_X / p⁻¹f⁻¹𝒪_Y} ≅ NL_{U/V}`,

the target read in complexes of sheaves of `p⁻¹𝒪_X`-modules through the identification
`p⁻¹𝒪_X ≅ 𝒪_U` of Stacks 03LV.

Both horizontal morphisms of the square of sheaves of rings
```
p⁻¹𝒪_X ──────▸ 𝒪_U
   ▲             ▲
   │             │
p⁻¹f⁻¹𝒪_Y ────▸ g⁻¹𝒪_V
```
are isomorphisms — the top one by Stacks 03LV at the étale morphism `p`, the bottom one by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleSquareBaseRingIso` — so the canonical chain map of Stacks 08TX
attached to it is an isomorphism.
declarations.comment:
the canonical identification NL_{X/Y}|_{U_étale} = NL_{U/V} for a commutative
square of algebraic spaces with p and q étale, REDUCED TO THE SECOND HALF OF THE SOURCE'S PROOF.
What is proved is `NL_{p⁻¹O_X / p⁻¹f⁻¹O_Y} ≅ NL_{U/V}`: the two identifications of Tag 03LV,
`p⁻¹O_X = O_U` and `q⁻¹O_Y = O_V`, together with the composition law of Tag 03G8 for the square,
make the data defining the two complexes correspond, and the canonical chain map of Tag 08TX
between them is then an isomorphism. The FIRST half, `p⁻¹NL_{X/Y} = NL_{p⁻¹O_X / p⁻¹f⁻¹O_Y}`
(Modules on Sites, Lemma 08TZ), is not instantiated here, so the source of this isomorphism is
not yet known to be the restriction `NL_{X/Y}|_{U_étale}`. Tag 08TZ itself IS carried for sites,
as `Stacks.SheafOfModules.inverseImageNaiveCotangentComplexIso`, for an arbitrary morphism of
topoi; what is missing is only its universe shape, which ties the ambient section universe of
each topos to a universe containing its site's object universe, whereas the small étale site has
objects in `Type (u + 1)` and structure sheaves in `CommRingCat.{u}`.
Carried beyond the source's statement: the étale hypotheses are hypotheses `IsEtale p.hom` and
`IsEtale q.hom` in the big-fppf-site presentation of algebraic spaces; the identification is an
isomorphism of cochain complexes of sheaves of `p⁻¹O_X`-modules, the target being `NL_{U/V}` read
there by restriction of scalars along `p⁻¹O_X ≅ O_U`, and NOTHING is asserted in the derived
category `D(O_U)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.naiveCotangentEtaleLocalisationIso_hom
declarations.doc:
The forward map of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.naiveCotangentEtaleLocalisationIso` is the
canonical chain map of Stacks 08TX attached to the square of sheaves of rings, so the
identification is canonical.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCotangentEtaleLocalisationIso_hom {p : U ⟶ X} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : U ⟶ V}
    {q : V ⟶ Y} (h : p ≫ f = g ≫ q) (hp : IsEtale B S hS p.hom)
    (hq : IsEtale B S hS q.hom) :
    (naiveCotangentEtaleLocalisationIso B S hS h hp hq).hom =
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.naiveCotangentComplexMapOfSquare.{u, u + 1, u, u}
        (smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS U).J _ _ _ _ _ _
        (etaleSquareBaseRingIso B S hS h hq).hom
        (etaleInverseImageStructureSheafIso B S hS p hp).hom
        (etaleSquareBaseRingIso_fSharpInverseImage B S hS h hq)
declarations.comment:
the identification is the canonical chain map of Tag 08TX, not an arbitrary
isomorphism; same scope as `naiveCotangentEtaleLocalisationIso`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.naiveCotangentEtaleRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0W, as an isomorphism of complexes.** For a commutative square `p ≫ f = g ≫ q` of
algebraic spaces over `S` with `p` and `q` étale, the restriction to the small étale site of
`U` of the naive cotangent complex of `f` is the naive cotangent complex of `g`:

`NL_{X/Y}|_{U_étale} ≅ NL_{U/V}`,

as complexes of sheaves of `𝒪_U`-modules. It is the restriction of scalars along
`𝒪_U ≅ 𝒪_X|_{U_étale}` of `Stacks.SheafOfModules.restrictionNaiveCotangentComplexIso`, which
identifies `NL_{X/Y}|_{U_étale}` with the naive cotangent complex of
`(f⁻¹𝒪_Y)|_{U_étale} ⟶ 𝒪_X|_{U_étale}`, followed by the inverse of the canonical chain map of
Stacks 08TX attached to the square of sheaves of rings of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleRestrictionNaiveBaseRingIso_fSharp`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveCotangentEtaleRestrictionIso {p : U ⟶ X} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : U ⟶ V}
    {q : V ⟶ Y} (h : p ≫ f = g ≫ q) (hp : IsEtale B S hS p.hom) (hq : IsEtale B S hS q.hom) :
    ((etaleModuleRestriction B S hS p hp).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
        (naiveCotangentComplex B S hS f) ≅
      naiveCotangentComplex B S hS g
declarations.comment:
the canonical identification NL_{X/Y}|_{U_étale} = NL_{U/V}, as an isomorphism of
complexes of sheaves of O_U-modules, of which the identification in D(O_U) is the image. The
restriction is along the postcomposition functor U_étale ⥤ X_étale, i.e. p_small⁻¹ (Tag 03LQ),
with O_X|_{U_étale} = O_U (Tag 03LV); formation of the naive cotangent complex commutes with it
(Tag 08TZ for that functor), and the square of structure maps is identified through Tags 03LV
and 03G8

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.naiveCotangentEtaleRestrictionDerivedIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0W.** For a commutative square `p ≫ f = g ≫ q` of algebraic spaces over `S` with
`p` and `q` étale, there is a canonical identification

`NL_{X/Y}|_{U_étale} = NL_{U/V}` in `D(𝒪_U)`:

the image in the derived category of sheaves of `𝒪_U`-modules of the isomorphism of complexes
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.naiveCotangentEtaleRestrictionIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def naiveCotangentEtaleRestrictionDerivedIso {p : U ⟶ X} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : U ⟶ V}
    {q : V ⟶ Y} (h : p ≫ f = g ≫ q) (hp : IsEtale B S hS p.hom) (hq : IsEtale B S hS q.hom)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{t} (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u + 1}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u + 1, u, u} (smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS U).O))] :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((etaleModuleRestriction B S hS p hp).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
          (naiveCotangentComplex B S hS f)) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (naiveCotangentComplex B S hS g)
declarations.comment:
the canonical identification NL_{X/Y}|_{U_étale} = NL_{U/V} in D(O_U) for a
commutative square of algebraic spaces over S with p and q étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.representedNaiveCotangentComparison
declarations.doc:
**The canonical chain map `NL_{ε⁻¹𝒪_{X₀}/ε⁻¹f₀⁻¹𝒪_{Y₀}} ⟶ NL_{X/Y}` of the proof of
Stacks 0D0X.**  It is the map of Stacks 08TX attached to the square of sheaves of commutative
rings on the small étale site of `X`
```
ε⁻¹𝒪_{X₀} ─────ε♯────▸ 𝒪_X
    ▲                    ▲
    │                    │
ε⁻¹f₀⁻¹𝒪_{Y₀} ─────────▸ f_small⁻¹𝒪_Y
```
whose bottom arrow is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.representedBaseMap` and whose commutativity is
the square of Remark 08GH, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.representedBaseMap_square`.  The target is
read in complexes of sheaves of `ε⁻¹𝒪_{X₀}`-modules through restriction of scalars along `ε♯`;
this is the adjoint form of a map out of `ε^*NL_{X₀/Y₀} = ε⁻¹NL_{X₀/Y₀} ⊗_{ε⁻¹𝒪_{X₀}} 𝒪_X`.
declarations.comment: the canonical map `ε^*NL_{X₀/Y₀} ⟶ NL_{X/Y}` of the source's proof, in its `ε⁻¹`-adjoint form, for the morphism of algebraic spaces represented by a morphism `T₁ ⟶ T₂` of the big fppf site over `S` (so `X`, `Y` are represented by the schemes `X₀`, `Y₀` underlying `T₁`, `T₂`); `ε` is the comparison of Section 071P (`representedToZariskiRingedToposHom`). WHAT IS PROVED IS THE SECOND STEP OF THE SOURCE'S PROOF: the canonical chain map of Tag 08TX attached to the square of Remark 08GH, `representedBaseMap_square`, from the naive cotangent complex of the inverse image along `ε` of the structure map of `f₀`. Its source is identified with `ε⁻¹NL_{X₀/Y₀}`, which is the source's FIRST step (Modules on Sites, Lemma 08TZ), separately by `representedInverseImageNaiveCotangentComplexIso`; the composite of the two is `representedPulledBackNaiveCotangentComparison`. THE SOURCE'S THIRD STEP IS NOT PROVED: the map is NOT shown to be an ISOMORPHISM; nothing is asserted in the derived category `D(O_X)`. The source checks that on stalks at geometric points, where the stalk maps of `ε` and of `representedBaseMap` are strict henselizations (Tags 04K5, 04KF, 05V1) and the conclusion is More on Algebra, Lemma 0D08; `NL` has no fundamental triangle, so the two-vanishing-vertices factorisation that `quasiIso_representedCotangentComparison` uses for Tag 08VF is unavailable. Carried beyond the source's statement: sections are lifted to `CommRingCat.{u + 1}` throughout, which is the only universe at which `ε` exists, so both ends are the naive cotangent complexes of the lifted structure maps and NOT `Space.naiveCotangentComplex` of Tag 0D0V, whose sections are in `CommRingCat.{u}`; an `NL` analogue of `Scheme.Hom.cotangentComplexULiftIso` is the one remaining input needed to read this at Tag 0D0V. The target is read in complexes of `ε⁻¹O_{X₀}`-modules through restriction of scalars along `ε♯`, the adjoint form of a map out of `ε^*NL_{X₀/Y₀}`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.representedPulledBackNaiveCotangentComparison
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map `ε⁻¹NL_{X₀/Y₀} ⟶ NL_{X/Y}` of the proof of Stacks 0D0X.**  The
identification of Lemma 08TZ at `ε`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.representedInverseImageNaiveCotangentComplexIso`) followed by the
canonical chain map of Stacks 08TX over the square of Remark 08GH
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.representedNaiveCotangentComparison`).  Read through restriction of
scalars along `ε♯`, this is the adjoint form of the map `ε^*NL_{X₀/Y₀} ⟶ NL_{X/Y}` that
Stacks 0D0X asserts to be an isomorphism.
declarations.comment: the canonical map `ε^*NL_{X₀/Y₀} ⟶ NL_{X/Y}` of the source's proof, in its `ε⁻¹`-adjoint form, for the morphism of algebraic spaces represented by a morphism `T₁ ⟶ T₂` of the big fppf site over `S` (so `X`, `Y` are represented by the schemes `X₀`, `Y₀` underlying `T₁`, `T₂`); `ε` is the comparison of Section 071P (`representedToZariskiRingedToposHom`). THE FIRST TWO STEPS OF THE SOURCE'S PROOF ARE WHAT IS PROVED: the identification `ε⁻¹NL_{X₀/Y₀} = NL_{ε⁻¹O_{X₀}/ε⁻¹f₀⁻¹O_{Y₀}}` of Modules on Sites, Lemma 08TZ, instantiated at `ε` (`representedInverseImageNaiveCotangentComplexIso`), and then the canonical chain map of Tag 08TX attached to the square of Remark 08GH, `representedBaseMap_square` (`representedNaiveCotangentComparison`). THE THIRD STEP IS NOT PROVED: this map is NOT shown to be an ISOMORPHISM, and nothing is asserted in the derived category `D(O_X)`. The source checks that on stalks at geometric points, where the stalk maps of `ε` and of `representedBaseMap` are strict henselizations (Tags 04K5, 04KF, 05V1) and the conclusion is More on Algebra, Lemma 0D08; `NL` has no fundamental triangle, so the two-vanishing-vertices factorisation that `quasiIso_representedCotangentComparison` uses for Tag 08VF is unavailable. Carried beyond the source's statement: sections are lifted to `CommRingCat.{u + 1}` throughout, which is the only universe at which `ε` exists, so the two ends are the naive cotangent complexes of the lifted structure maps and NOT `Space.naiveCotangentComplex` of Tag 0D0V, whose sections are in `CommRingCat.{u}`, nor the scheme-level complex of Definition 0D0H at its own section universe; an `NL` analogue of `Scheme.Hom.cotangentComplexULiftIso` is the one remaining input needed to read this at Tag 0D0V. The target is read in complexes of `ε⁻¹O_{X₀}`-modules through restriction of scalars along `ε♯`, the adjoint form of a map out of `ε^*NL_{X₀/Y₀}`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasiIso_representableEpsilonNaiveCotangentIdentification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0X.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` with `X` and `Y`
representable by schemes `X₀` and `Y₀`, through `α : h_U ≅ X` and `β : h_V ≅ Y` for objects `U`,
`V` of the big fppf site of `S` with underlying schemes `X₀`, `Y₀`, and let `f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀` be the
morphism of schemes corresponding to `f` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.representingMorphism`).  Let
`ε : ((X₀)_étale, 𝒪) ⟶ ((X₀)_Zar, 𝒪_{X₀})` be the comparison morphism of Stacks 08H7.  Then the
canonical map

`ε^*NL_{X₀/Y₀} ⟶ NL_{X/Y}`

— the termwise pullback along `ε` of (the universe lift of) `NL_{X₀/Y₀}` of Stacks 0D0H,
followed by the map of Stacks 08TX of the square of Stacks 08GH into `NL_{h_U/h_V}`, followed by
the identification of `NL_{h_U/h_V}` with `NL_{X/Y}` of Stacks 0D0V read on `(X₀)_étale` through
the identification `(X₀)_étale ≌ X_étale` given by `α`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.representingNaiveCotangentComplexIso`) — is a quasi-isomorphism, so
it identifies `NL_{X/Y}` with `ε^*NL_{X₀/Y₀}` in `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_representableEpsilonNaiveCotangentIdentification (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    QuasiIso ((((representedEpsilonModulePullback B S hS U).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map (representedZariskiNaiveCotangentComplexIso B S hS
          (representingMorphism B S hS α β f)).inv ≫
      representedEpsilonNaiveCotangentMap B S hS (representingMorphism B S hS α β f)) ≫
        (representingNaiveCotangentComplexIso B S hS α β
          (comp_eq_representedSpaceMap_representingMorphism B S hS α β f)).hom)
declarations.comment: the canonical map `ε^*NL_{X₀/Y₀} ⟶ NL_{X/Y}` is a quasi-isomorphism, i.e. the canonical identification `NL_{X/Y} = ε^*NL_{X₀/Y₀}` in `D(O_X)`, for an arbitrary morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces with `X ≅ h_U`, `Y ≅ h_V` representable by schemes, `NL_{X/Y}` read on the small étale site of `X₀` through the identification `(X₀)_étale ≌ X_étale` that the representing isomorphism gives

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.naiveCotangentComplex_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0Y.**  Let `S` be a scheme and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S`.  The cohomology sheaves of the naive cotangent complex `NL_{X/Y}` are quasi-coherent,
zero outside degrees `-1` and `0`, and equal to `Ω_{X/Y}` in degree `0`.

`Ω_{X/Y}` is the sheaf of differentials of Stacks 04CT, with its sections lifted to the universe
of the sections of `NL_{X/Y}`; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCotangentComplex_homology :
    (∀ i : ℤ, ((naiveCotangentComplex B S hS f).homology i).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 → IsZero ((naiveCotangentComplex B S hS f).homology i)) ∧
      Nonempty ((naiveCotangentComplex B S hS f).homology 0 ≅
        SheafOfModules.uliftForPresentation.{u + 1, u, u, u, u + 1}
          (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_quasiIso_naiveCotangentComplex_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D0Z.**  Let `S` be a scheme and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` which is locally of finite presentation.  Then `NL_{X/Y}` is étale locally on `X`
quasi-isomorphic to a complex `… → 0 → 𝓕⁻¹ → 𝓕⁰ → 0 → …` of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules with
`𝓕⁰` of finite presentation and `𝓕⁻¹` of finite type.

"Étale locally on `X`" is read as on the small étale site of `X`: every étale scheme chart `U` of
`X` has an étale covering `{Wᵢ ⟶ U}` such that the restriction of `NL_{X/Y}` to the small étale
site of `X` localized at each `Wᵢ` receives a quasi-isomorphism `φ` from a complex `F` of sheaves
of modules over the restricted structure sheaf which vanishes outside degrees `-1` and `0`, whose
degree `0` term is quasi-coherent and of finite presentation and whose degree `-1` term is
quasi-coherent and of finite type.  `NL_{X/Y}` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.naiveCotangentComplex`
(Stacks 0D0V) and the restriction is `SheafOfModules.overFunctor` applied termwise.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quasiIso_naiveCotangentComplex_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom) (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (W : I → SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (g : ∀ i, W i ⟶ U),
      Sieve.ofArrows W g ∈ SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1 U ∧
      ∀ i, ∃ (F : CochainComplex (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u + 1}
          ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X).O).over
            (W i))) ℤ)
        (φ : F ⟶ ((_root_.SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u + 1}
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X).O)
              (W i)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
          (naiveCotangentComplex B S hS f)),
        (∀ j : ℤ, j ≠ -1 → j ≠ 0 → IsZero (F.X j)) ∧ QuasiIso φ ∧
          (F.X 0).IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧ (F.X 0).IsFinitePresentationOnSite ∧
          (F.X (-1)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧ (F.X (-1)).IsFiniteTypeOnSite
declarations.comment: the whole statement.  `etale locally on X` is read on the small etale site of `X`: every etale chart `U` of `X` has an etale covering `{W_i -> U}` (a covering sieve of `SmallEtale.topology`) such that `NL_{X/Y}` restricted to the slice at each `W_i` receives a quasi-isomorphism from a complex `F` concentrated in degrees -1 and 0 with `F^0` quasi-coherent and of finite presentation and `F^{-1}` quasi-coherent and of finite type -- the two degrees carrying DIFFERENT finiteness conditions, exactly as the tag states. The source's `NL_{X/Y} is quasi-isomorphic to F` is realized by a quasi-isomorphism FROM `F`, which is the same content. The only hypothesis is the source's: `f` locally of finite presentation (`IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation`, Stacks 03XP). Nothing is assumed: the covering is by the affine chart diagrams, on which `F = NL(P) (x)_A O` for a finite presentation `P` of the chart ring `A` over `R`, the comparison with `(NL_{A/R}) (x)_A O` is the Stacks 00S1 homotopy equivalence, and `(NL_{A/R}) (x)_A O -> NL_{X/Y}|_V` is proved to be a quasi-isomorphism on kernels (H^{-1} = H_1(L_{A/R}) (x)_A O, using flatness of the etale stalks) and on cokernels (Omega_{X/Y}|_V = Omega_{A/R} (x)_A O, Stacks 0D08 in degree 0 and Stacks 08TP)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallySmooth_iff_isZero_homology_negOne_and_isLocallyProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D10.** A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` is formally
smooth if and only if the cohomology sheaf `H⁻¹(NL_{X/Y})` of its naive cotangent complex
vanishes and its sheaf of differentials `Ω_{X/Y} = H⁰(NL_{X/Y})` is locally projective.

`Ω_{X/Y}` is the degree-zero cohomology sheaf of `NL_{X/Y}` by Stacks 0D0Y,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.naiveCotangentComplexHomologyZeroIsoSheafOfDifferentials`, and is
quasi-coherent by Stacks 04CV, which is the standing hypothesis of local projectivity
(Stacks 060R).
declarations.statement:
theorem formallySmooth_iff_isZero_homology_negOne_and_isLocallyProjective
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    FormallySmooth f.hom ↔
      (IsZero ((naiveCotangentComplex B S hS f).homology (-1)) ∧
        IsLocallyProjective B S hS X.2
          ⟨sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f,
            isQuasicoherentOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f⟩)
declarations.comment:
the second condition read on the sheaf of differentials Ω_{X/Y} of 04CT, which
  the source identifies with H⁰(NL_{X/Y}) (0D0Y)

registrations.name: Stacks.Smooth.formallyEtale_iff_isZero_homology_naiveCotangentComplex
registrations.comment:
the tag prints the statement of 0D0M verbatim, for a morphism of schemes;
registered on the declaration proving 0D0M rather than restated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmooth_iff_isZero_homology_negOne_and_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D12.** A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` is smooth if
and only if it is locally of finite presentation, the cohomology sheaf `H⁻¹(NL_{X/Y})` of its
naive cotangent complex vanishes, and its sheaf of differentials `Ω_{X/Y} = H⁰(NL_{X/Y})` is
finite locally free on the small étale site of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_iff_isZero_homology_negOne_and_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsSmooth B S hS f.hom ↔
      (IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom ∧
        IsZero ((naiveCotangentComplex B S hS f).homology (-1)) ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f))
declarations.comment:
the third clause read on the sheaf of differentials Ω_{X/Y} of 04CT, which the
  source identifies with H⁰(NL_{X/Y})
