registrations.comment:
the tag prints the statement of 0D0N verbatim, for a morphism of schemes;
registered on the declaration proving 0D0N rather than restated

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.FlatDeformation.exists_addTorsor_classes
declarations.doc:
Let `S ⊂ S'` be a first order thickening of schemes (`t : S ⟶ S'` a closed immersion whose
ideal sheaf squares to zero) and let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat. Suppose there exist a flat morphism
`f' : X' ⟶ S'` and an isomorphism `a : X ≅ X' ×_{S'} S` over `S` (a `FlatDeformation t f`,
recording `a` through `i = pr₁ ∘ a` and the cartesian square `IsPullback i f f' t`;
`FlatDeformation.ofPair` and `FlatDeformation.a` pass between the two). Then the set of isomorphism
classes of such pairs (`FlatDeformation.Classes t f`; by `FlatDeformation.nonempty_iso_iff` two
pairs are isomorphic exactly when there is `e : X'₁ ≅ X'₂` over `S'` with `(e ×_{S'} S) ∘ a₁ = a₂`)
is principal homogeneous under `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(NL_{X/S}, f^*𝒞_{S/S'})`
(`Scheme.naiveCotangentExt f _ 1`, with `pullbackConormalModule f t = f^*𝒞_{S/S'}`).

The action is as follows: a pair is the same thing as a solution of the square-zero extension
problem
`0 ⟶ f^*𝒞_{S/S'} ⟶ 𝒪_{X'} ⟶ 𝒪_X ⟶ 0` over `0 ⟶ 𝒞_{S/S'} ⟶ 𝒪_{S'} ⟶ 𝒪_S ⟶ 0`
(`solutionOf`, with the ideal of `X` in `X'` identified with `f^*𝒞_{S/S'}` by
[Stacks Project, Tag 063Y]), and `ξ` sends the class of `(f'₁, a₁)` to the class of `(f'₂, a₂)`
exactly when the obstruction class of [Stacks Project, Tag 08UG] separating the two solutions is
`ξ`, which is the action of [Stacks Project, Tag 08UK]. The relation is independent of the
reference pair `D₀` used to write down the extension problem.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_addTorsor_classes [Flat f]
    (hne : Nonempty (FlatDeformation t f)) :
    ∃ T : AddTorsor (Scheme.naiveCotangentExt f (pullbackConormalModule f t) 1)
        (Classes t f),
      ∀ (ξ : Scheme.naiveCotangentExt f (pullbackConormalModule f t) 1)
        (D₀ D₁ D₂ : FlatDeformation t f),
        T.vadd ξ (Quotient.mk (setoid t f) D₁) = Quotient.mk (setoid t f) D₂ ↔
          CompatibleFirstOrderThickening.pairObstruction (solutionOf hst D₀ D₁)
              (solutionOf hst D₀ D₂) =
            extIso f (pullbackConormalModule f t) 1 ξ

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.flatThickeningAutEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0D14], part (2).** Let `S ⊂ S'` be a first order thickening of
schemes, let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism, let `f' : X' ⟶ S'` be flat and let `i : X ⟶ X'` make the
square cartesian, so that `X = X' ×_{S'} S` over `S`.  Then the set of automorphisms
`φ : X' ⟶ X'` over `S'` which reduce to the identity on `X' ×_{S'} S` is

`Ext⁰_{𝒪_X}(NL_{X/S}, f^*𝒞_{S/S'})`.

The bijection is not merely asserted: its value on a class `ξ` is the morphism
`Stacks.Thickenings.autOfHom` for the `𝒪_X`-linear map
`Stacks.Thickenings.flatThickeningActingGroupAddEquiv ... ξ : Ω_{X/S} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/X'}`, whose
comorphism is `g ↦ g + α(d_{X/S}(i^♯ g))` by
`Stacks.Thickenings.flatThickeningAutEquiv_apply_appLE`.  In particular the identity
automorphism corresponds to `0` (`Stacks.Thickenings.autOfHom_zero`) and composition to
addition (`Stacks.Thickenings.autOfHom_add`), so the bijection is an isomorphism of groups.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isThickeningHom_iff_isThickening_smallEtaleRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D16.**  Let `S` be a scheme and `i : Z ⟶ Z'` a morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S`.  Then `i` is a thickening of algebraic spaces (Stacks 05ZJ, Definition 05ZK: a closed
immersion identifying `Z` with a closed subspace of `Z'` having the same points, here in the
morphism form `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsThickeningHom`) if and only if the associated morphism
`i_small : (Sh(Z_étale), 𝒪_Z) ⟶ (Sh(Z'_étale), 𝒪_{Z'})` of ringed topoi (Stacks 03G8,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleRingedToposHom`) is a thickening in the sense of Stacks 08M6
(`Deformation.ToposThickening.IsThickening`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickeningHom_iff_isThickening_smallEtaleRingedToposHom
    {Z Z' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (i : Z ⟶ Z') :
    IsThickeningHom B S hS i ↔
      Deformation.ToposThickening.IsThickening.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u}
        (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatThickeningDeformation.classes_naturalAddTorsor_and_autMulEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0D17]**, with its natural structures. Let `S` be a scheme, `Y ⊂ Y'` a
first order thickening of algebraic spaces over `S` (`hZ`) and `f : X ⟶ Y` a flat morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` (`hf`). If there exists a flat `f' : X' ⟶ Y'` with an isomorphism
`a : X ≅ X' ×_{Y'} Y` over `Y` (`hD`; a `Deformation f` is exactly such a pair, see
`Deformation.ofPair`, `Deformation.pairIso`), then
1. the set `Classes f` of isomorphism classes of pairs `(f', a)` is principal homogeneous under
   `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(NL_{X/Y}, f^*𝒞_{Y/Y'})`, for the action of [Stacks 08UK]: `ξ` carries `[D₁]` to
   `[D₂]` exactly when the obstruction class `Deformation.obstruction D₁ D₂` of [Stacks 08UG] of
   the two deformations is `ξ`; and
2. for every such pair `D`, the group `Aut D` of automorphisms `φ : X' ⟶ X'` over `Y'` reducing to
   the identity on `X' ×_{Y'} Y` is `Ext⁰_{𝒪_X}(NL_{X/Y}, f^*𝒞_{Y/Y'})`, by the group isomorphism
   sending `φ` to the class in `Ext⁰` of [Stacks 08UG] of the automorphism `(φ^♯)⁻¹` of the
   solution `0 → f^*𝒞_{Y/Y'} → i⁻¹𝒪_{X'} → 𝒪_X → 0` (`Deformation.autMulEquivAmbientSolution`
   followed by `solutionAutMulEquivExtZero`).

`NL_{X/Y}` is the canonical naive cotangent complex `naiveCotangentComplex B S hS f`; the module
`f^*𝒞_{Y/Y'}` is `liftedPulledBackConormal hZ f`; the `Ext` groups are those of any model of the
derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem classes_naturalAddTorsor_and_autMulEquiv (hf : IsFlat B S hS f.hom)
    (hD : Nonempty (Deformation f)) :
    (∃ T : AddTorsor
        (DerivedCategory.Ext (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (naiveCotangentComplex B S hS f))
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (liftedPulledBackConormal hZ f)) 1)
        (Classes f),
      ∀ (ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (naiveCotangentComplex B S hS f))
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (liftedPulledBackConormal hZ f)) 1)
        (D₁ D₂ : Deformation f),
        T.vadd ξ (Quotient.mk (setoid f) D₁) = Quotient.mk (setoid f) D₂ ↔
          D₁.obstruction hZ D₂ = ξ) ∧
      ∀ D : Deformation f, ∃ e : Aut D ≃* Multiplicative (DerivedCategory.Ext
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (naiveCotangentComplex B S hS f))
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (liftedPulledBackConormal hZ f)) 0),
        ∀ φ : Aut D, e φ = solutionAutMulEquivExtZero hZ f (D.ambientSolution hZ)
          (Deformation.autMulEquivAmbientSolution hZ D φ)
declarations.comment: both parts, with the action on isomorphism classes characterised by the obstruction class of 08UG as in 08UK, and the isomorphism Aut = Ext^0 given explicitly through the automorphism (phi^#)^(-1) of the solution and 08UG

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.tangentSpace_deformationCategory_linearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D18, tangent spaces.** For a category fibred in groupoids over the
big fppf site of a locally Noetherian scheme satisfying (RS*), the tangent space of the
deformation category of a finite-type field-valued point is the value of the tangent functor
of Tag 07Y9 at the rank-one vector space. Both sides carry the unique linear structure
compatible with finite products (Tag 06I6), and the identification carries the class of a
deformation to the class of the corresponding lift.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tangentSpace_deformationCategory_linearEquiv
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (hS : B.Contains S)
    {Λ k : Type u} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k]
    (iΛ : Spec (.of Λ) ⟶ S) (toS : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (hfin : LocallyOfFiniteType (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ))
    (hqc : QuasiCompact (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ))
    {X : Type v} [Category.{w} X] (p : X ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hRS : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS p hp) (x₀ : X)
    (hx₀ : (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x₀ =
      Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ))
    (hx : p.obj x₀ = algebraOver k B S hS toS hk) :
    let D := predeformationCategory iΛ (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) x₀ hx₀
    let 𝓕 := BasedCategory.ofFunctor D.projection
    let hD : Deformation.IsDeformationCategory D.projection :=
      isDeformationCategory_predeformationCategory_of_satisfiesRSStar B S hS p hp hRS iΛ x₀
        hx₀ hfin hqc
    letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory 𝓕.p) := ⟨hD.predeformation⟩
    letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2 (Functor.Elements.π
      (isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered))) :=
      ⟨schlessingerConditionS2_isomorphismClasses_of_isDeformationCategory 𝓕 hD⟩
    let M : SiteModule k B := (fgSiteModule B hk).obj (FGModuleCat.of k k)
    let L := tangentFunctor k B S hS toS hk p x₀ hx hp hRS
    ∃ e : artinianTangentSpace Λ k (isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered) ≃ₗ[k]
        L.functor.obj M,
      ∀ z : D.projection.Fiber ((artinianSquareZeroExtensionFunctor Λ k).obj
          (FGModuleCat.of k k)),
        ∃ y : (Under.post p).Fiber
            (Under.mk (eqToHom hx ≫ squareZeroArrow k B S hS toS hk M)),
          L.liftEquiv M (e (classOf 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered z)) = Quotient.mk _ y ∧
            ∃ (η : y.1.right ≅ (D.objects z.1).point)
              (hbase : p.obj y.1.right = p.obj (D.objects z.1).point),
              p.map η.hom = eqToHom hbase ∧
                y.1.hom ≫ η.hom = (D.objects z.1).arrow
declarations.comment: tangent spaces

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.infinitesimalAutomorphisms_deformationCategory_linearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D18, infinitesimal automorphisms.** For a category fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf site of a locally Noetherian scheme satisfying (RS*), the
infinitesimal automorphisms of the deformation category of a finite-type field-valued point
are the value of the infinitesimal automorphism functor of Tag 07Y9 at the rank-one vector
space, by a `k`-linear equivalence carrying an automorphism to the endomorphism of the
trivial deformation given by the same arrow.
declarations.statement:
public theorem infinitesimalAutomorphisms_deformationCategory_linearEquiv
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (hS : B.Contains S)
    {Λ k : Type u} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k]
    (iΛ : Spec (.of Λ) ⟶ S) (toS : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (hfin : LocallyOfFiniteType (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ))
    (hqc : QuasiCompact (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ))
    {X : Type v} [Category.{w} X] (p : X ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hRS : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS p hp) (x₀ : X)
    (hx₀ : (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x₀ =
      Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ))
    (hx : p.obj x₀ = algebraOver k B S hS toS hk) :
    let D := predeformationCategory iΛ (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) x₀ hx₀
    let hD : Deformation.IsDeformationCategory D.projection :=
      isDeformationCategory_predeformationCategory_of_satisfiesRSStar B S hS p hp hRS iΛ x₀
        hx₀ hfin hqc
    let A₀ := (artinianSquareZeroExtensionFunctor Λ k).obj (FGModuleCat.of k PUnit.{u + 1})
    let Aε := (artinianSquareZeroExtensionFunctor Λ k).obj (FGModuleCat.of k k)
    let g : A₀ ⟶ Aε := (artinianSquareZeroExtensionFunctor Λ k).map 0
    let e : Aε ⟶ A₀ := (artinianSquareZeroExtensionFunctor Λ k).map 0
    let M : SiteModule k B := (fgSiteModule B hk).obj (FGModuleCat.of k k)
    let L := infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor k B S hS toS hk p x₀ hx hp hRS
    let t := trivialDeformation k B S hS toS hk p x₀ hx hp M
    ∃ (hge : g ≫ e = 𝟙 A₀) (z₀ : D.projection.Fiber A₀) (zε : D.projection.Fiber Aε)
      (i : z₀.1 ⟶ zε.1) (hi : D.projection.IsHomLift g i)
      (η : (D.objects zε.1).point ≅ t.1.right),
      let G := ↥(infinitesimalAutomorphismsAlongSplitPair hD.predeformation.cofibered g e hge
        i hi)
      (D.objects zε.1).arrow ≫ η.hom = t.1.hom ∧
        ∃ hA : AddCommGroup G,
          letI : AddCommGroup G := hA
          ∃ hM : Module k G,
            letI : Module k G := hM
            ∃ E : G ≃ₗ[k] (L.functor.obj M : Type w),
              ∀ a : G, (L.autEquiv M (E a)).1.right =
                η.inv ≫ (D.morphisms zε.1 zε.1 a.val.asIso.hom.val).arrow ≫ η.hom
declarations.comment: infinitesimal automorphisms

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.localizedAutomorphismTangent_deformationCategory_linearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D18, infinitesimal automorphisms.** For a category fibred in groupoids
over the big fppf site of a locally Noetherian scheme satisfying (RS*), the infinitesimal
automorphisms of the deformation category of a finite-type field-valued point `x₀`, with their
natural vector space structure of Tag 06JX, are the value at the rank-one vector space of the
infinitesimal automorphism functor of Tag 07Y9: there is a `k`-linear equivalence `E`, which is
conjugation by any isomorphism `η` of the object underlying the dual-number pushforward with the
trivial deformation of `x₀` that is compatible with the arrows out of `x₀` and lies over the
comparison of the two presentations of the dual numbers; such an `η` exists.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localizedAutomorphismTangent_deformationCategory_linearEquiv
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (hS : B.Contains S)
    {Λ k : Type u} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k]
    (iΛ : Spec (.of Λ) ⟶ S) (toS : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S)
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (hfin : LocallyOfFiniteType (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ))
    (hqc : QuasiCompact (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ))
    {X : Type v} [Category.{w} X] (p : X ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hRS : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS p hp) (x₀ : X)
    (hx₀ : (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x₀ =
      Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ))
    (hx : p.obj x₀ = algebraOver k B S hS toS hk)
    (y : (predeformationCategory iΛ (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) x₀ hx₀).projection.Fiber
      (residueFieldObject.{u, u, u} Λ k))
    (P : ChosenPushforwardsAt
      (predeformationCategory iΛ (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) x₀ hx₀).projection y.1) :
    let D := predeformationCategory iΛ (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) x₀ hx₀
    let hD : Deformation.IsDeformationCategory D.projection :=
      isDeformationCategory_predeformationCategory_of_satisfiesRSStar B S hS p hp hRS iΛ x₀
        hx₀ hfin hqc
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup P hD.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule P hD.satisfiesRS
    let M : SiteModule k B := (fgSiteModule B hk).obj (FGModuleCat.of k k)
    let L := infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor k B S hS toS hk p x₀ hx hp hRS
    let t := trivialDeformation k B S hS toS hk p x₀ hx hp M
    let yε := P.obj (dualNumbersUnder (p := D.projection) (x := y.1))
    let IsCompatible : ((D.objects yε.1).point ≅ t.1.right) → Prop := fun η =>
      (D.objects yε.1).arrow ≫ η.hom = t.1.hom ∧
        eqToHom (congrArg Over.left (D.objects yε.1).base).symm ≫
            ((p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).map η.hom).left ≫ eqToHom (congrArg Over.left
              (trivialDeformation_right_post B S hS iΛ toS hk p hp x₀ hx₀ hx
                (FGModuleCat.of k k))) =
            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (CategoryTheory.inv
              (dualNumbersUnderHom (p := D.projection) (x := y.1)) ≫
                eqToHom (yε.2.symm.trans (D.object_projection yε.1))).hom.toRingHom)
    ∃ E : localizedAutomorphismFunctorTangent P ≃ₗ[k] (L.functor.obj M : Type w),
      (∃ η, IsCompatible η) ∧
        ∀ η, IsCompatible η → ∀ a, (L.autEquiv M (E a)).1.right =
          η.inv ≫ (D.morphisms yε.1 yε.1 (localizedTangentEquivKernel P a).1.asIso.hom.1).arrow ≫
            η.hom
declarations.comment: infinitesimal automorphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.graphTransformation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1A.** The *graph transformation* `Mor_Q(Z, X) ⟶ Hilb_{Z ×_Q X / Q}`: it carries a
relative morphism `(a, b)` at a test scheme `T` to the graph of `b`, a closed subspace of
`(Z ×_Q X)_T` which is of finite presentation, flat and proper over `T` because `z` is. It is
natural because the graph of a restriction is the inverse image of the graph
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_graphMap_restrict`). The source is composed with the universe lift,
the Hilbert presheaf taking values one universe up.
declarations.statement:
def graphTransformation (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS x) (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS z)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS z) (hproper : IsProper B S hS z) :
    relativeHom B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} ⟶
      hilbertPresheaf (graphAmbientMap B S hS z x hZ hX hQ)
declarations.comment: the graph transformation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.graphTransformation_app_family_Z
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1A.** The graph transformation maps a relative morphism to its graph: the closed
subspace of the family it produces is the range of the graph map.
declarations.statement:
theorem graphTransformation_app_family_Z (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS x)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS z) (hflat : IsFlat B S hS z) (hproper : IsProper B S hS z)
    (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : (relativeHom B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ).obj (Opposite.op T)) :
    ((graphTransformation hZ hX hQ hsep hfp hflat hproper).app (Opposite.op T)
        (ULift.up p)).family.Z =
      Subfunctor.range (graphMap (relativeHomSections B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ T p))
declarations.comment: the transformation is the graph

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.graphTransformation_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1A.** The graph transformation is injective at every test scheme: two relative
morphisms with the same graph have the same first component, and then
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeMorphism_eq_of_range_graphMap_eq` identifies them.
declarations.statement:
theorem graphTransformation_injective (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS x)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS z) (hflat : IsFlat B S hS z) (hproper : IsProper B S hS z)
    (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) :
    Function.Injective
      ((graphTransformation hZ hX hQ hsep hfp hflat hproper).app (Opposite.op T))
declarations.comment: injectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.graphTransformation_relative_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
The graph transformation `Mor_Q(Z, X) ⟶ Hilb_{Z ×_Q X / Q}` is representable by open
immersions.
declarations.statement:
theorem graphTransformation_relative_isOpenImmersion (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS x)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS z) (hflat : IsFlat B S hS z)
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS z) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative
      (yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u})
      (graphTransformation hZ hX hQ hsep hfp hflat hproper)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_relativeHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1C**, algebraicity. For `x` of finite presentation and separated and `z` of finite
presentation, flat and proper, the relative morphism functor `Mor_Q(Z, X)` is an algebraic space
over `S`.

It is realised as an open subspace of a model of the Hilbert functor of `Z ×_Q X` over `Q` by
Stacks 0D1A and 0D1B, and that model is an algebraic space by Stacks 0D01,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasHilbertModelsOver_of_isAlgebraicSpace`; an open immersion is
representable, so Stacks 02WY transfers algebraicity to the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_relativeHom (hx_fp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS x)
    (hx_sep : IsSeparated B S hS x) (hz_fp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS z)
    (hz_flat : IsFlat B S hS z) (hz_proper : IsProper B S hS z) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (relativeHom B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ)
declarations.comment: algebraicity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relativeHomProjection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1C**, local finite presentation over the base. For `x` of finite presentation and
separated and `z` of finite presentation, flat and proper, the projection
`Mor_Q(Z, X) ⟶ Q` is locally of finite presentation.

The projection factors through a model of the Hilbert functor of `Z ×_Q X` over `Q`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.morToHilbertModel_comp_toBase`); the first factor is an open immersion,
hence locally of finite presentation, and the second is locally of finite presentation by
Stacks 0D01, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasHilbertModelsOver_of_isAlgebraicSpace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relativeHomProjection
    (hx_fp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS x) (hx_sep : IsSeparated B S hS x)
    (hz_fp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS z) (hz_flat : IsFlat B S hS z)
    (hz_proper : IsProper B S hS z) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
      (relativeHomProjection B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ)
declarations.comment: local finite presentation over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_relativeHom_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
Let `z : Z ⟶ Q` and `x : X ⟶ Q` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`. Assume `x` is of
finite presentation and separated, and `z` is of finite presentation, flat and proper. Then
`Mor_Q(Z, X)` is an algebraic space, and its projection to `Q` is locally of finite
presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_relativeHom_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    {Z X Q : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (z : Z ⟶ Q) (x : X ⟶ Q)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hQ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Q)
    (hx_fp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS x) (hx_sep : IsSeparated B S hS x)
    (hz_fp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS z) (hz_flat : IsFlat B S hS z)
    (hz_proper : IsProper B S hS z) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (relativeHom B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ) ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
        (relativeHomProjection B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartesianProperFlatInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1D.** The inclusion
`Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper} ⊂ Spaces'_{ft}` of the families of algebraic spaces that are of
finite presentation, flat and proper over their base scheme into all the finite-type families,
both taken with cartesian morphisms only.
declarations.statement:
abbrev cartesianProperFlatInclusion :
    CartesianProperFlatSpaces B S hS ⥤ CartesianFiniteTypeSpaces B S hS
declarations.comment: the subcategory of finitely presented, flat and proper families

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithfulCartesianProperFlatInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1D.** The subcategory `Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}` of `Spaces'_{ft}` is *full*:
a cartesian morphism of finite-type families whose source and target are of finite presentation,
flat and proper is a morphism of `Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}`, with no further condition.
declarations.statement:
def fullyFaithfulCartesianProperFlatInclusion :
    (cartesianProperFlatInclusion B S hS).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: the subcategory is full

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartesianProperFlatInclusion_comp_cartesianFiniteTypeProjection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1D.** The projection `p'_{fp, flat, proper}` is the restriction of the projection
`p'_{ft}` to the subcategory `Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cartesianProperFlatInclusion_comp_cartesianFiniteTypeProjection :
    cartesianProperFlatInclusion B S hS ⋙ cartesianFiniteTypeProjection B S hS =
      cartesianProperFlatProjection B S hS
declarations.comment: the projection of the subcategory is the restriction of the projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartesianFiniteTypeProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
Finite-type algebraic spaces over varying base schemes, with cartesian squares as morphisms,
form a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cartesianFiniteTypeProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids :
    (cartesianFiniteTypeProjection B S hS).IsFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.comment: finite-type families

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartesianProperFlatProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
Algebraic spaces whose structure morphism is of finite presentation, flat and proper over a
varying base scheme, with cartesian squares as morphisms, form a category fibred in groupoids over
the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cartesianProperFlatProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids :
    (cartesianProperFlatProjection B S hS).IsFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.comment: finitely presented, flat and proper families

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasAlgebraicIsomFunctors
declarations.doc:
Criterion (2) of Stacks 045G in concrete form: the isomorphism functor of two finitely
presented, flat and proper families over a scheme of the site is an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasAlgebraicIsomFunctors :
    HasAlgebraicIsomFunctors B S hS
declarations.comment: the Isom functor of two finitely presented, flat and proper families is an algebraic space, which is criterion (2) of Stacks 045G for the diagonal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasRepresentableDiagonal_properFlatSpacesStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1F.** The diagonal

```text
  Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper} ⟶ Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper} × Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}
```

is representable by algebraic spaces, assuming that the isomorphism presheaf of the fibre of the
stack over a scheme `U` is algebraic whenever the isomorphism functors `Isom_U(Z, X)` of finitely
presented, flat and proper families over `U` are (`hcmp`).
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRepresentableDiagonal_properFlatSpacesStack
    (hcmp : HasAlgebraicIsomFunctors B S hS →
      Stack.IsAlgebraicSpaceIsomPresheaf B S hS (properFlatSpacesStack B S hS)) :
    Stack.HasRepresentableDiagonal B S hS (properFlatSpacesStack B S hS)
declarations.comment: the diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properFlatSpacesStack_hasRepresentableDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**The diagonal of `Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}` is representable by algebraic spaces.** The
diagonal

```text
  Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper} ⟶ Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper} × Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}
```

of the stack of Stacks 0D1D over the big fppf site of `S` is representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem properFlatSpacesStack_hasRepresentableDiagonal :
    Stack.HasRepresentableDiagonal B S hS (properFlatSpacesStack B S hS)
declarations.comment: the diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces; Stacks 0D01 is proved, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasHilbertModels`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartesianFiniteTypeProjection_isStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1G**, the finite-type families, in the form of Stacks 02ZJ (3): `Spaces'_ft` is
fibred in groupoids and is a stack over the big fppf site of `S` (Stacks 026F).
declarations.statement:
theorem cartesianFiniteTypeProjection_isStack :
    (cartesianFiniteTypeProjection B S hS).IsFiberedInGroupoids ∧
      (cartesianFiniteTypeProjection B S hS).IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: Spaces'_ft is fibred in groupoids and a stack (Stacks 02ZJ (3))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartesianProperFlatProjection_isStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1G**, the finitely presented, flat and proper families, in the form of Stacks 02ZJ
(3): `Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}` is fibred in groupoids and is a stack over the big fppf site of
`S` (Stacks 026F).
declarations.statement:
theorem cartesianProperFlatProjection_isStack :
    (cartesianProperFlatProjection B S hS).IsFiberedInGroupoids ∧
      (cartesianProperFlatProjection B S hS).IsStack (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper} is fibred in groupoids and a stack (Stacks 02ZJ (3))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stackOfSpaces_isStackInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1G.** The category `Spaces'_ft` is a stack in groupoids over the big fppf site of
`S`, and so is `Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}` (Stacks 02ZI).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CartesianFiniteTypeSpacesOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1H.** The category `Z-Spaces'_{ft}` of finite-type families of algebraic spaces
over a fixed algebraic space `Z`: an object is a finite-type family `X ⟶ T` of algebraic spaces
together with a morphism from its base scheme to `Z`, and a morphism is a cartesian morphism of
families commuting with those morphisms.
declarations.statement: abbrev CartesianFiniteTypeSpacesOver
declarations.comment: the category of finite-type families over a base algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_cartesianFiniteTypeSpacesOverToTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1H** for finite-type families. The absolute and the relative categories of
finite-type families of algebraic spaces form a 2-fibre product square over the big fppf site of
`S`: the canonical comparison from the finite-type families over `Z` to the 2-fibre product of
the finite-type families with the schemes over `Z` is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_cartesianFiniteTypeSpacesOverToTwoFibreProduct :
    (cartesianFiniteTypeSpacesOverToTwoFibreProduct B S hS Z).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the 2-fibre product square for finite-type families

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CartesianProperFlatSpacesOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1H.** The category `Z-Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}` of finitely presented, flat and
proper families of algebraic spaces over a fixed algebraic space `Z`: an object is such a family
`X ⟶ T` together with a morphism from its base scheme to `Z`, and a morphism is a cartesian
morphism of families commuting with those morphisms.
declarations.statement: abbrev CartesianProperFlatSpacesOver
declarations.comment: the category of finitely presented, flat and proper families over a base space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_cartesianProperFlatSpacesOverToTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1H** for finitely presented, flat and proper families. The absolute and the
relative categories of finitely presented, flat and proper families of algebraic spaces form a
2-fibre product square over the big fppf site of `S`: the canonical comparison from such families
over `Z` to the 2-fibre product of such families with the schemes over `Z` is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_cartesianProperFlatSpacesOverToTwoFibreProduct :
    (cartesianProperFlatSpacesOverToTwoFibreProduct B S hS Z).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the 2-fibre product square for finitely presented, flat and proper families

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLimitPreserving_cartesianProperFlatFiberedCategory
declarations.doc:
The stack `p'_{fp, flat, proper} : Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper} ⟶ Sch_fppf` of finitely
presented, flat and proper families of algebraic spaces is limit preserving (Stacks 07XL): for
every directed inverse system of affine schemes `Tᵢ` of the site with limit `T` in the site, base
change is an equivalence from the colimit of the fibre categories over the `Tᵢ` to the fibre
category over `T`.

The base is the big fppf site of an arbitrary scheme `S` of the site, which recovers `Sch_fppf` at
`S = Spec(ℤ)`; the index categories are those of the scheme universe, the smallness of the directed
sets of Stacks 07XL.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitPreserving_cartesianProperFlatFiberedCategory
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    Deformation.Artin.IsLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS
      (cartesianProperFlatFiberedCategory B S hS)
declarations.comment: over the big fppf site of an arbitrary base scheme `S`; the source's `Sch_fppf` is `S = Spec(ℤ)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushoutRS
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0D1J].** For every pushout `S' = S ⨿_T T'` of schemes of the site
along a thickening `T ⟶ T'` and an affine morphism `T ⟶ S`, the canonical restriction functor
from the finitely presented, flat and proper algebraic spaces over `S'` to the compatible pairs
of such spaces over `S` and `T'` is an equivalence.
declarations.statement: def properPushoutRS : ProperPushoutRS B S₀ hS₀

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperFlatSpaceDeformation.finiteDimensional_predeformationCategory
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field of finite type over `ℤ` and let `x = (X → Spec k)` be an object of
`𝒳 = Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}` over `Spec k`. Then the predeformation category `𝓕_{𝒳,k,x}` of
Stacks 07T2, over `𝒞_ℤ`, is a deformation category, its tangent space `T𝓕_{𝒳,k,x}` is a
finite-dimensional `k`-vector space, and so are its infinitesimal automorphisms
`Inf(𝓕_{𝒳,k,x})` (Stacks 07WY), at every object of the special fibre and for every choice of its
pushforwards.

The stack is formed over the big fppf site of `Spec ℤ`, and `𝓕_{𝒳,k,x}` over `𝒞_Λ` with `Λ = ℤ`,
`Spec Λ = Spec ℤ` the affine open of the base containing the image of `Spec k` (Stacks 07T2).
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_predeformationCategory {k : Type u} [Field k]
    [Algebra (ULift.{u} ℤ) k] [Algebra.FiniteType (ULift.{u} ℤ) k]
    (x : CartesianProperFlatSpaces B integerBase hZ)
    (hx : (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase hZ ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x =
      Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (ULift.{u} ℤ) k)) ≫ 𝟙 integerBase)) :
    ∃ hD : IsDeformationCategory.{u, u, u} (predeformationCategory (𝟙 integerBase)
        (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase hZ ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) x hx).projection,
      (letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (predeformationCategory
          (𝟙 integerBase) (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase hZ ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion)
            x hx).projection).p) := ⟨hD.predeformation⟩;
        letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2 (Functor.Elements.π
          (isomorphismClasses (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (predeformationCategory (𝟙 integerBase)
            (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase hZ ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) x
              hx).projection) hD.predeformation.cofibered))) := ⟨tangentConditionS2.{u, u, u} hD⟩;
        FiniteDimensional k (artinianTangentSpace (ULift.{u} ℤ) k
          (isomorphismClasses (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (predeformationCategory (𝟙 integerBase)
            (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase hZ ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) x
              hx).projection) hD.predeformation.cofibered))) ∧
      ∀ y, (predeformationCategory (𝟙 integerBase)
          (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase hZ ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) x
            hx).projection.obj y = residueFieldObject.{u, u, u} (ULift.{u} ℤ) k →
        ∀ PF : ChosenPushforwardsAt (predeformationCategory (𝟙 integerBase)
            (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase hZ ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) x
              hx).projection y,
          FiniteDimensional k ↥((infinitesimalAutomorphismLinearLift.{u, u, u} PF
            hD.satisfiesRS).functor.obj (FGModuleCat.of k (ULift.{u} k)))
declarations.comment: (1): for a field k of finite type over Z and an object x of Spaces'_{fp,flat,proper} over Spec k, the predeformation category F_{X,k,x} over C_Z is a deformation category whose tangent space T F_{X,k,x} and infinitesimal automorphisms Inf(F_{X,k,x}) (Section 07WY) are finite dimensional

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProperFlatSpaceDeformation.finiteDimensional_tangentFunctor_infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `x = (X → Spec k)` be an object of
`𝒳 = Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}` over `Spec k`. Then the tangent functor `T_x` and the functor of
infinitesimal automorphisms `Inf_x` of Stacks 07Y9 (Section 07Y6) exist — `𝒳` satisfies (RS*) by
Stacks 0D1J — and `T_x(k)` and `Inf_x(k)` are finite-dimensional `k`-vector spaces.

Each functor is stated as a structure (`TangentFunctorData`,
`InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData`) carrying a `k`-linear functor on the site modules together
with its identification with the isomorphism classes of lifts of `x`, respectively with the
infinitesimal automorphisms of the trivial lifts of `x`, natural in the module. The statement gives
that such a functor exists and that the value at `k` of *every* such functor is finite-dimensional,
so it holds for the functors `T_x` and `Inf_x` of Stacks 07Y9, which are determined by these
identifications. No condition on `k` is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_tangentFunctor_infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (toS : Spec (.of k) ⟶ integerBase) (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (x : CartesianProperFlatSpaces B integerBase hZ)
    (hx : (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase hZ).obj x =
      algebraOver k B integerBase hZ toS hk) :
    (Nonempty (TangentFunctorData k B integerBase hZ toS hk
        (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase hZ) x hx) ∧
      ∀ T : TangentFunctorData k B integerBase hZ toS hk
          (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase hZ) x hx,
        FiniteDimensional k (T.functor.obj ((fgSiteModule B hk).obj (FGModuleCat.of k k)))) ∧
    (Nonempty (InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData k B integerBase hZ toS hk
        (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase hZ) x hx
        (cartesianProperFlatProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids B integerBase hZ)) ∧
      ∀ I : InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData k B integerBase hZ toS hk
          (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase hZ) x hx
          (cartesianProperFlatProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids B integerBase hZ),
        FiniteDimensional k (I.functor.obj ((fgSiteModule B hk).obj (FGModuleCat.of k k))))
declarations.comment: (2): for an object x of Spaces'_{fp,flat,proper} over a field k, the functors T_x and Inf_x of Stacks 07Y9 exist (the stack satisfies RS* by 0D1J) and T_x(k) and Inf_x(k) are finite dimensional; both finiteness statements hold for every k-linear functor carrying the identifications of 07Y9

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PolarizedFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1M.** A *polarized family*: a proper, flat, finitely presented morphism from a
scheme to a scheme of the big fppf site, together with an invertible module on the total space
which is relatively ample for that morphism.
declarations.statement: structure PolarizedFamily
declarations.comment: objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PolarizedFamily.Hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1M.** A morphism of polarized families: a morphism of total spaces over a morphism
of base schemes whose square is cartesian, together with an isomorphism from the pullback of the
polarization of the target to the polarization of the source.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (X Y : PolarizedFamily B)
declarations.comment: morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PolarizedFamily.instCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1M.** Polarized families, cartesian squares between them and comparisons of
polarizations form a category: the two underlying morphisms compose componentwise and the
comparisons compose through the pullback pseudofunctor.
declarations.statement: instance instCategory : Category.{u} (PolarizedFamily B)
declarations.comment: category

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedProjection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1M.** The forgetful functor taking a polarized family to its base scheme, which is
how the category of polarized families is viewed as a category over the big fppf site.
declarations.statement: def polarizedProjection : PolarizedFamily B ⥤ B.Schemes
declarations.comment: projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PolarizedFamilyOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1N.** A *polarized family over the space* `A`: a polarized family together with a
structure morphism of its base scheme over the base of the site and a point of `A` there.
declarations.statement: structure PolarizedFamilyOver
declarations.comment: objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PolarizedFamilyOver.Hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1N.** A morphism of polarized families over `A`: a morphism of the underlying
polarized families whose base map lies over the base of the site and carries the point of the
target to the point of the source.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (X Y : PolarizedFamilyOver B S hS A)
declarations.comment: morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PolarizedFamilyOver.instCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1N.** Polarized families over `A` and the morphisms compatible with their points
form a category, with the identities and composition of the underlying polarized families.
declarations.statement: instance instCategory : Category.{u} (PolarizedFamilyOver B S hS A)
declarations.comment: category

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PolarizedFamilyOver.isEquivalence_toCategoricalPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1N.** The canonical comparison from polarized families over `A` to the 2-fibre
product of polarized families and schemes carrying a point of `A`, over the big fppf site of
schemes, is an equivalence: the displayed square is a 2-fibre product square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_toCategoricalPullback :
    (toCategoricalPullback B S hS A).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the 2-fibre product square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.not_isAlgebraicStack_cartesianProperFlatBasedCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1R.** The stack in groupoids
`p'_{fp, flat, proper} : Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper} ⟶ Sch_fppf` whose category of sections over
a scheme `S` is the category of flat, proper, finitely presented algebraic spaces over `S`, over
the big fppf site of `Spec ℤ` (any big fppf site `B`, as in Stacks 021R), is not an algebraic
stack.

As in the source, the proof is: an algebraic stack has effective formal objects (07X8), but over
`Spec ℚ` the versal formal deformation of a smooth quartic surface (here the Fermat quartic) is a
non-effective formal object (`AlgebraicGeometry.properFlatSpacesNonEffectiveInput`), and
algebraicity over `Spec ℤ` would give algebraicity over `Spec ℚ`. The source argues over `ℂ`; by
its footnote any field of characteristic zero works, and `ℚ` (lifted to the universe `u`) is
used here.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isAlgebraicStack_cartesianProperFlatBasedCategory (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hZ : B.Contains integerBase) :
    ¬ Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B integerBase hZ
      (cartesianProperFlatBasedCategory B integerBase hZ)

declarations.name: ModuleCat.hasProjectiveDimensionLT_of_monotone_of_iSup_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1U.** Let `R` be a ring and let `M` be an `R`-module which is the union
`⨆ e, N e = ⊤` of a monotone family of submodules `N` indexed by a well-ordered type `E`. If each
graded piece `N e ⧸ ⨆ e' < e, N e'` has projective dimension `< n`, then so does `M`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ModuleCat.hasProjectiveDimensionLT_of_monotone_of_iSup_eq_top {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    [Small.{v} R] {M : ModuleCat.{v} R} {E : Type w} [LinearOrder E] [WellFoundedLT E]
    (N : E → Submodule R M) (hN : Monotone N) (hNtop : ⨆ e, N e = ⊤) (n : ℕ)
    (hquot : ∀ e, HasProjectiveDimensionLT
      (ModuleCat.of R (↥(N e) ⧸ (⨆ e' < e, N e').submoduleOf (N e))) n) :
    HasProjectiveDimensionLT M n
declarations.comment:
Indexed by `HasProjectiveDimensionLT _ n`, so that the source's `≤ n` is the case
`n + 1`; the source's well-ordered family of submodules is a `Monotone` family over a type with
`[LinearOrder E] [WellFoundedLT E]`, its union is `⨆ e, N e = ⊤`, and the graded piece at `e` is
`↥(N e) ⧸ (⨆ e' < e, N e').submoduleOf (N e)`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.Descent.nonempty_equivalence_galoisDescentData
declarations.doc:
**Galois descent for quasi-coherent modules.**  For a surjective finite étale morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` carrying an action of a finite group `G` over `Y` which identifies `∐_{σ : G} X`
with `X ×_Y X`, quasi-coherent modules on `Y` are the same thing as Galois descent systems
on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_equivalence_galoisDescentData [IsFinite f] [Etale f] [Surjective f] :
    Nonempty ((SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ≌
      GaloisDescentData G f a)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.SmallEtaleModules.allModules_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
Every module on the small étale site of a zero-dimensional local ring is
quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem allModules_isQuasicoherent
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (hdim : ringKrullDim R = 0)
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains (Spec (.of R)))
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u}
      (AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.structureSheaf B (Spec (.of R)) hS)) :
    F.IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtaleLocallyConstructible_setOf_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1Y, the level sets of a Betti-number function are étale locally
constructible.** The Betti-number function is data, characterised by `hβ`: the function of
Stacks 0D1Y is built, but nothing identifies it with a derived-fibre Betti function on a
scheme chart. `constructibleLevels` is part (3) of Stacks 0BDI, the same statement for a
scheme, which holds for every scheme and is supplied in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/Perfect/BettiNumbersOnPointsUnconditional.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleLocallyConstructible_setOf_eq
    (hβ : IsEtaleLocallyDerivedFibreBetti B S hS X β i)
    (constructibleLevels : ∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (F : DerivedCategory Z.Modules)
      (hF : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := Z.toRingedSpace) F) (m : ℕ),
      IsLocallyConstructible {z : Z | DerivedFibreBetti.derivedFiberBetti Z F hF i z = m})
    (n : ℕ) :
    IsEtaleLocallyConstructible B S hS X {x | β x = n}
declarations.comment: constructible levels, for a Betti-number function given as data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.upperSemicontinuous_of_isEtaleLocallyDerivedFibreBetti
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1Y, upper semicontinuity of a Betti-number function.** The Betti-number
function is data, characterised by `hβ`: the function of Stacks 0D1Y is built, but nothing
identifies it with a derived-fibre Betti function on a scheme chart.
`upperSemicontinuousBetti` is part (2) of Stacks 0BDI, the same statement for a scheme, which
holds for every scheme and is supplied in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/Perfect/BettiNumbersOnPointsUnconditional.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperSemicontinuous_of_isEtaleLocallyDerivedFibreBetti
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hβ : IsEtaleLocallyDerivedFibreBetti B S hS X β i)
    (upperSemicontinuousBetti : ∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (F : DerivedCategory Z.Modules)
      (hF : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := Z.toRingedSpace) F),
      UpperSemicontinuous (DerivedFibreBetti.derivedFiberBetti Z F hF i)) :
    UpperSemicontinuous β
declarations.comment: upper semicontinuity, for a Betti-number function given as data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.upperSemicontinuous_geometricFibreBettiFunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1Y, clause (2): the functions `β_i` are upper semi-continuous.**  For a
pseudo-coherent object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` on an algebraic space `X` over `S`, the `i`-th
Betti-number function `β_i : |X| → ℕ` of `E` is upper semicontinuous.

Nothing is assumed beyond pseudo-coherence of `E`.  The scheme-level input is part (2) of
[Stacks, Tag 0BDI].
declarations.statement:
theorem upperSemicontinuous_geometricFibreBettiFunction
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS X)))
    (hE : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPseudoCoherent E) (i : ℤ) :
    UpperSemicontinuous (geometricFibreBettiFunction B S hS E i)
declarations.comment: clause (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtaleLocallyConstructible_setOf_geometricFibreBettiFunction_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1Y, clause (3): the level sets of `β_i` are étale locally constructible.**  For a
pseudo-coherent object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` on an algebraic space `X` over `S` and a natural number
`n`, the level set `{x ∈ |X| : β_i(x) = n}` is étale locally constructible in the sense of
[Stacks, Tag 0ECU].

Nothing is assumed beyond pseudo-coherence of `E`.  The scheme-level input is part (3) of
[Stacks, Tag 0BDI].
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleLocallyConstructible_setOf_geometricFibreBettiFunction_eq
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS X)))
    (hE : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPseudoCoherent E) (i : ℤ) (n : ℕ) :
    IsEtaleLocallyConstructible B S hS X.1 {x | geometricFibreBettiFunction B S hS E i x = n}
declarations.comment: clause (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.geometricFibreBettiFunction_derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1Y, clause (1): formation of `β_i` commutes with arbitrary base change.** For a
morphism `g : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces the Betti-number function of `Lg^*E` is the Betti-number
function of `E` composed with the map `|Y| → |X|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricFibreBettiFunction_derivedPullback {Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : Y ⟶ X)
    (E : @DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS X)) _ _
      (HasDerivedCategory.standard _))
    (_hE : @AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsPseudoCoherent
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2) _ _ _ _ _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard _) E)
    (i : ℤ) :
    geometricFibreBettiFunction B S hS ((smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback B S hS g).obj E) i =
      geometricFibreBettiFunction B S hS E i ∘ pointsMap B S hS Y.1 g.hom
declarations.comment: clause (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyConstant_derivedFibreEuler
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1Z.**  Let `Y` be an algebraic space and `K` a perfect object of `D(𝒪_Y)`.  The
derived-fibre Euler characteristic `y ↦ ∑ (-1)^n dim_k H^n(K ⊗^𝐋 k)` is locally constant on
`|Y|`.

The function is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedFibreEuler`, the alternating sum of the
dimensions of the cohomology of `Lp^*K` for a field-valued point `p` representing the point; by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedFibreEuler_class` it may be computed at any representative.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyConstant_derivedFibreEuler (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf B S hS Y)))
    (hK : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2).IsPerfect K) :
    IsLocallyConstant (derivedFibreEuler Y K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyConstant_of_isEtaleLocallyDerivedFibreChi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D1Z.**  The derived-fibre Euler characteristic of a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`
on an algebraic space `X` is locally constant on `|X|`.

The function is data, characterised by `hχ` (see the implementation notes); the proof
reduces to the case of schemes, Stacks 0BDJ, by étale localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyConstant_of_isEtaleLocallyDerivedFibreChi
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hχ : IsEtaleLocallyDerivedFibreChi B S hS X χ) :
    IsLocallyConstant χ
declarations.comment: for a derived-fibre Euler characteristic given as data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfIntRankInDegree_of_isSingleDegreeRankLocus
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of Stacks 0D20.**  On an open subspace with the universal property of clause
(2), the object `E` is a finite locally free module of rank `r` placed in degree `i`: the
inclusion of the open subspace factors through it by way of the identity, so the universal
property applies to it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOfIntRankInDegree_of_isSingleDegreeRankLocus
    (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    [(smallEtaleModulePullbackOnHomotopy B S hS
        (openSubspaceImmersion B S hS U)).HasLeftDerivedFunctor
      (smallEtaleModuleQuasiIso B S hS X)]
    (hU : IsSingleDegreeRankLocus B S hS X E i r U) :
    IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfIntRankInDegree B S hS (openSubspaceAsSpace B S hS U)
      ((smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback B S hS (openSubspaceImmersion B S hS U)).obj E) i r
declarations.comment: clause (1), for an open subspace with the characterising universal property of clause (2); existence of such an open subspace is not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_of_isSingleDegreeRankLocus
declarations.doc:
**The uniqueness half of "there exists an open subspace characterised by" in Stacks
0D20.**  At most one open subspace of `X` has the universal property of clause (2).

Each of the two inclusions factors through the other open subspace, because by clause (1) the
restriction of `E` along it has the required shape and the other open subspace's universal
property turns that into a factorization; and a subfunctor through which another's inclusion
factors contains it.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_isSingleDegreeRankLocus (U U' : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    [(smallEtaleModulePullbackOnHomotopy B S hS
        (openSubspaceImmersion B S hS U)).HasLeftDerivedFunctor
      (smallEtaleModuleQuasiIso B S hS X)]
    [(smallEtaleModulePullbackOnHomotopy B S hS
        (openSubspaceImmersion B S hS U')).HasLeftDerivedFunctor
      (smallEtaleModuleQuasiIso B S hS X)]
    (hU : IsSingleDegreeRankLocus B S hS X E i r U)
    (hU' : IsSingleDegreeRankLocus B S hS X E i r U') :
    U = U'
declarations.comment: uniqueness of an open subspace with the characterising universal property of clause (2); existence of such an open subspace is not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isSingleDegreeRankLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D20.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`, let `E` be a perfect object of
`D(𝒪_X)` and let `i, r ∈ ℤ`. There is an open subspace `U ⊆ X`, and only one, characterised by:
(1) `E|_U ≅ M[-i]` for a finite locally free `𝒪_U`-module `M` of rank `r` (so `M = H^i(E|_U)`);
(2) a morphism `f : Y → X` factors through `U` if and only if `Lf^*E` is a finite locally free
module of rank `r` placed in degree `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSingleDegreeRankLocus
    (hE : RingedSite.IsPerfect (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2) E) :
    ∃ U : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1,
      IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfIntRankInDegree B S hS (openSubspaceAsSpace B S hS U)
        ((smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback B S hS (openSubspaceImmersion B S hS U)).obj E) i r ∧
      IsSingleDegreeRankLocus B S hS X E i r U ∧
      ∀ U' : OpenSubspaces B S hS X.1, IsSingleDegreeRankLocus B S hS X E i r U' → U' = U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.BottomRankLocus.exists_isBottomRankStratum_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D21.** Let `E` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` of Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` and
`r ≥ 0`. There is an immersion `j : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces, of finite presentation, such that
(1) `H^a(Lj^*E)` is finite locally free of rank `r`, (2) a morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` factors through
`j` exactly when `H^a(L(f ∘ g)^*E)` is finite locally free of rank `r` for every `g : Y' ⟶ Y`,
(3) for `f = j ∘ g` we have `H^a(Lf^*E) ≅ g^*H^a(Lj^*E)`, and (4) if `β_a(p) ≤ r` at every
geometric point `p` of `X` (`bettiAt`, the dimension of `H^a(E ⊗^L k(p))`), then `j` is a closed
immersion, `f` factors through `j` exactly when `H^a(Lf^*E)` is finite locally free of rank `r`,
and, for `r = 1`, exactly when `𝒪_Y → ℋom(H^a(Lf^*E), H^a(Lf^*E))` is injective.

The source writes `H^0` in (4)(b) and (4)(c); for `a ≠ 0` that reading is false: for
`E = 𝒪_X[-a]` and `r = 1` the stratum is all of `X`, so every `f : Y ⟶ X` factors through it, while
`H^0(Lf^*E) = 0` is not locally free of rank `1` when `Y` is nonempty. The statement here uses
`H^a`, as in the corrected scheme version [stacks 0BDL].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isBottomRankStratum_isFinitePresentation
    (T : DerivedTensorProduct (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hE : RingedSite.IsPerfect (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2) E) (b : ℤ)
    (hT : DerivedTensorProduct.HasTorAmplitude T E a b) (r : ℕ) :
    ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (j : Z ⟶ X),
      IsBottomRankStratum E a r j ∧ IsFinitePresentation B S hS j.hom ∧
        (∀ (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : Y ⟶ Z),
          Nonempty (pullbackHomology E a (g ≫ j) ≅ (pb g).obj (pullbackHomology E a j))) ∧
        ((∀ p : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1, bettiAt E a p.val.siteObject p.val.value ≤ r) →
          IsClosedImmersion B S hS j.hom ∧ (∀ (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : Y ⟶ X),
            ((∃ g : Y ⟶ Z, g ≫ j = f) ↔
              SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfIntRank (pullbackHomology E a f) (r : ℤ))) ∧
          (r = 1 → ∀ (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : Y ⟶ X),
            ((∃ g : Y ⟶ Z, g ≫ j = f) ↔
              AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsScalarFaithful (pullbackHomology E a f))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isImmersion_isFinitePresentation_factorsThrough_iff_hasDescentAt
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat, proper morphism of finite presentation of algebraic spaces over
`S`, and `E` a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module. Assume that for every `g : Y' ⟶ Y`, with base
change `f' : X' = X ×_Y Y' ⟶ Y'`, the map `𝒪_{Y'} ⟶ f'_*𝒪_{X'}` is an isomorphism. Then there
is an immersion `j : Z ⟶ Y` of finite presentation such that a morphism `g : Y' ⟶ Y` factors
through `j` exactly when there is a finite locally free `𝒪_{Y'}`-module `N` with
`(f')^*N ≅ (g')^*E` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasDescentAt`; the source's `(g')^*L` is a typo for
`(g')^*E`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImmersion_isFinitePresentation_factorsThrough_iff_hasDescentAt
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hfl : IsFlat B S hS f.hom)
    (hP : IsProper B S hS f.hom) (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (E : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hE : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree E)
    (hiso : ∀ {Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : Y' ⟶ Y),
      IsIso (structureSharp B S hS (pullback.snd f g))) :
    ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (j : Z ⟶ Y),
      IsImmersion B S hS j.hom ∧ IsFinitePresentation B S hS j.hom ∧
      ∀ {Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : Y' ⟶ Y),
        (∃ h : Y' ⟶ Z, h ≫ j = g) ↔ HasDescentAt f E g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D25.**  The standing data of the relative Picard functor: a morphism
`f : X ⟶ base` of algebraic spaces over the scheme `S`.
declarations.statement: structure PicardSituation (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
declarations.comment: the standing data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.picardPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D25.**  The presheaf `T ↦ Pic(X_T)` on the schemes over the base, whose fppf
sheafification is the relative Picard functor.  Its action on a morphism of test schemes is
pullback of Picard classes.
declarations.statement: def picardPresheaf : (s.SchemesOver)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the presheaf of Picard groups of the base changes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.picardFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D25.**  The *relative Picard functor* `Pic_{X/base} : (Sch/base)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Sets`: the
fppf sheafification of the presheaf `T ↦ Pic(X_T)` of isomorphism classes of invertible modules
on the base changes.
declarations.statement: def picardFunctor : (s.SchemesOver)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the relative Picard functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.fibreIsoClassEquiv
declarations.doc:
**`Ob(Picardstack_{X/B, T})/≅` is `Pic(X_T)`.** The isomorphism class of an object of the
fibre of the Picard stack over `T` goes to the class in `Pic(X_T)` of its invertible module.
declarations.comment: ONLY the identification of Ob(Picardstack_{X/B,T})/≅ with Pic(X_T) at one test scheme; the sheafification statement is isIso_sheafifyLift_toPicardFunctorOfIsoClasses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.isoClassPresheafIsoPicardPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**The presheaf `T ↦ Ob(Picardstack_{X/B, T})/≅` is the presheaf `T ↦ Pic(X_T)`.** At each
test scheme it is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.fibreIsoClassEquiv`.
declarations.comment: ONLY the identification of the presheaf T ↦ Ob(Picardstack_{X/B,T})/≅ with the presheaf T ↦ Pic(X_T); the sheafification statement is isIso_sheafifyLift_toPicardFunctorOfIsoClasses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.isIso_sheafifyLift_toPicardFunctorOfIsoClasses
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0D25 the relative Picard functor `Pic_{X/B}` is the fppf
sheafification of the presheaf `T ↦ Ob(Picardstack_{X/B, T})/≅` of isomorphism classes of objects
of the fibre categories of the Picard stack: `Pic_{X/B}` is an fppf sheaf
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.isSheaf_picardFunctor`) and the canonical map
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.toPicardFunctorOfIsoClasses` from that presheaf into it
factors through the sheafification by an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sheafifyLift_toPicardFunctorOfIsoClasses :
    IsIso (sheafifyLift s.fppfTopology s.toPicardFunctorOfIsoClasses s.isSheaf_picardFunctor)
declarations.comment: the relative Picard functor is the fppf sheafification of the presheaf of isomorphism classes of objects of the fibres of the Picard stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.exact_picardSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D27.**  In Situation 0D25, if `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T}` is an isomorphism for every
scheme `T` over the base, then for every such `T` the sequence
`0 ⟶ Pic(T) ⟶ Pic(X_T) ⟶ Pic_{X/B}(T)` is exact: pullback along `f_T` is injective, and a class
of `X_T` maps to the trivial element of the relative Picard functor exactly when it is pulled
back from `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_picardSequence (h : s.StructureSheafMapIso) (T : s.SchemesOver) :
    Function.Injective (s.basePicardPullback T) ∧
      ∀ x : s.picardAt T, s.picardClassMap T x = s.picardClassMap T 0 ↔
        x ∈ Set.range (s.basePicardPullback T)
declarations.comment: the exact sequence 0 → Pic(T) → Pic(X_T) → Pic_{X/B}(T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.picardSequence_splitExact
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0D25 let `σ : B ⟶ X` be a section of `f`, and assume that
`𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T}` is an isomorphism for every scheme `T` over `B`.  Then for every `T`

`0 ⟶ Pic(T) ⟶ Pic(X_T) ⟶ Pic_{X/B}(T) ⟶ 0`

is a split exact sequence with splitting `σ_T^* : Pic(X_T) ⟶ Pic(T)`, the first arrow being
pullback along `f_T : X_T ⟶ T` and the second the canonical map to the fppf sheafification
`Pic_{X/B}`.  Spelled out:

* the first arrow is injective;
* two classes on `X_T` have the same image in `Pic_{X/B}(T)` exactly when they differ by a class
  pulled back from `T`, and in particular (exactness at `Pic(X_T)`) a class maps to the image of
  the trivial class exactly when it is pulled back from `T`;
* the second arrow is surjective;
* `σ_T^*` is a left inverse of the first arrow;
* the second arrow restricts to a bijection from the kernel of `σ_T^*` onto `Pic_{X/B}(T)`, the
  identification `Pic_{X/B}(T) = ker(σ_T^*)` of the proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem picardSequence_splitExact (hstr : s.StructureSheafMapIso) (T : s.SchemesOver) :
    Function.Injective (s.basePicardPullback T) ∧
      (∀ x y : s.picardAt T, s.picardClassMap T x = s.picardClassMap T y ↔
        x - y ∈ Set.range (s.basePicardPullback T)) ∧
      (∀ x : s.picardAt T, s.picardClassMap T x = s.picardClassMap T 0 ↔
        x ∈ Set.range (s.basePicardPullback T)) ∧
      Function.Surjective (s.picardClassMap T) ∧
      Function.LeftInverse (sectionPicardPullback σ hσ T) (s.basePicardPullback T) ∧
      Function.Bijective (fun x : (sectionPicardPullbackHom σ hσ T).ker ↦
        s.picardClassMap T (x : s.picardAt T))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.leftInverse_sectionPicardPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D28, the splitting.**  Pullback of Picard classes along the section
`σ_T : T ⟶ X_T` of the base change retracts pullback along the projection `f_T : X_T ⟶ T`:
`σ_T^* ∘ f_T^*` is the identity of `Pic(T)`.  This is the splitting of the sequence

`0 ⟶ Pic(T) ⟶ Pic(X_T) ⟶ Pic_{X/B}(T) ⟶ 0`

of Stacks 0D28, and it holds with no hypothesis on `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem leftInverse_sectionPicardPullback (hc : ModulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
    (σ : s.base ⟶ s.X) (hσ : σ ≫ s.f = 𝟙 s.base) (T : s.SchemesOver) :
    Function.LeftInverse (sectionPicardPullback σ hσ T) (s.basePicardPullback T)
declarations.comment: auxiliary: the splitting by σ_T^* for an arbitrary 03LU coherence datum; the full statement, with no hypothesis, is picardSequence_splitExact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.injective_basePicardPullback_of_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D28, exactness at `Pic(T)`.**  In Situation 0D25 with a section `σ : B ⟶ X` of `f`,
pullback along the projection `f_T : X_T ⟶ T` of the base change is an injection
`Pic(T) ⟶ Pic(X_T)`: it is retracted by `σ_T^*`.

Stacks 0D27 obtains the same conclusion from `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T}` being an isomorphism; with a
section neither that hypothesis nor the unit of the Stacks 03LU adjunction being an isomorphism at
an invertible module is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_basePicardPullback_of_section (hc : ModulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
    (σ : s.base ⟶ s.X) (hσ : σ ≫ s.f = 𝟙 s.base) (T : s.SchemesOver) :
    Function.Injective (s.basePicardPullback T)
declarations.comment: auxiliary: exactness at Pic(T) for an arbitrary 03LU coherence datum; the full statement, with no hypothesis, is picardSequence_splitExact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.existsUnique_add_sectionPicardPullback_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D28, the direct sum decomposition.**  The splitting makes `Pic(X_T)` the direct sum
of the image of `Pic(T)` under `f_T^*` and the kernel of `σ_T^*`: every Picard class on `X_T` is
the sum of the pullback of a unique Picard class on `T` and a unique class killed by `σ_T^*`.

This is what "the sequence of Stacks 0D28 is split" says internally to `Pic(X_T)`; the
identification of the kernel of `σ_T^*` with `Pic_{X/B}(T)`, which is the remaining content of
Stacks 0D28, is not proved here.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_add_sectionPicardPullback_eq_zero (hc : ModulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
    (σ : s.base ⟶ s.X) (hσ : σ ≫ s.f = 𝟙 s.base) (T : s.SchemesOver) (x : s.picardAt T) :
    ∃! p : s.basePicardAt T × s.picardAt T,
      sectionPicardPullback σ hσ T p.2 = 0 ∧
        x = s.basePicardPullback T p.1 + p.2
declarations.comment: auxiliary: the direct sum decomposition for an arbitrary 03LU coherence datum; the full statement, with no hypothesis, is picardSequence_splitExact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionedPicardCFG_isStackInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D29.** In Situation 0D25, given a section `σ` of `f : X ⟶ B`, the rigidified
Picard stack `Picardstack_{X/B, σ}` is a stack in groupoids over `(Sch/S)_fppf`. The category
is built from the pseudofunctoriality of Stacks 03LU
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence`) and the coherence of the restriction along
the section (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionTransportCoherence`), both proved in the library, so
the statement carries no hypothesis beyond the section.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionedPicardCFG_isStackInGroupoids (s : PicardSituation B S hS) (σ : s.base ⟶ s.X)
    (hσ : σ ≫ s.f = 𝟙 s.base) :
    (sectionedPicardCFG (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
      (sectionTransportCoherence _ σ hσ)).val.p.IsStackInGroupoids.{w}
        (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: the full statement: Picardstack_{X/B,sigma} is a stack in groupoids over (Sch/S)_fppf, for any section sigma of f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.forgetTrivialization_representable_surjective_smooth
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0D25, let `σ : B ⟶ X` be a section.  The 1-morphism
`Picardstack_{X/B, σ} ⟶ Picardstack_{X/B}` forgetting the trivialisation is representable,
surjective and smooth: its base change along every 1-morphism from a slice of the site is
represented by an object of the site (Stacks 02Y7, 04ST), it is representable by algebraic spaces
(Stacks 02ZW), and every algebraic space representing its base change along a scheme-valued point
has surjective and smooth structural morphism (Stacks 03YK, 04SX).
declarations.statement:
theorem forgetTrivialization_representable_surjective_smooth :
    Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism
        (sectionedPicardCFG (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
          (sectionTransportCoherence (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) σ hσ)).val.p
        (picardCFG (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s).val.p
        (forgetTrivialization (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
          (sectionTransportCoherence (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) σ hσ)).hom.toFunctor ∧
      ∃ hf : Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
          (forgetTrivialization (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
            (sectionTransportCoherence (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) σ hσ)).hom,
        Stack.HasRelativeProperty.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u} B S hS
            (Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS)
            (forgetTrivialization (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
              (sectionTransportCoherence (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) σ hσ)) hf ∧
          Stack.HasRelativeProperty.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u} B S hS
            (Space.smoothMorphismProperty B S hS)
            (forgetTrivialization (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
              (sectionTransportCoherence (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) σ hσ)) hf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.forgetTrivializationFibreEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The fibre of the 1-morphism of Stacks 0D2A is the set of trivialisations along the
section.**  The objects of `Picardstack_{X/B, σ}` lying over an object `(T, h, L)` of
`Picardstack_{X/B}` are the quadruples `(T, h, L, α)`, so they correspond bijectively to the
trivialisations `α : 𝒪_T ≅ σ_T^*L`; the fibre is `Isom_T(𝒪_T, σ_T^*L)`, which is the
identification the source's proof of Stacks 0D2A rests on.
declarations.comment: ONLY the fibre identification the proof rests on: the fibre of Picardstack_{X/B,sigma} -> Picardstack_{X/B} over (T,h,L) is the set of trivializations O_T = sigma_T^*L, that is Isom_T(O_T, sigma_T^*L). NONE of the three clauses - representable, surjective, smooth - is proved; see the implementation notes of this file for the three obstructions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_sectionedPicardObject_iff
declarations.doc:
**An object of `Picardstack_{X/B}` lies in the image of the 1-morphism of Stacks 0D2A exactly
when the class of its invertible module is killed by `σ_T^*`.**  By the fibre identification a
lift is a trivialisation of `L` along the section, and by Stacks 0D2B such a trivialisation
exists exactly when `σ_T^*[L] = 0` in `Pic(T)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_sectionedPicardObject_iff (A : PicardObject s) :
    (∃ A' : PicardSituation.SectionedPicardObject σ hσ, A'.toPicardObject = A) ↔
      PicardSituation.sectionPicardPullback σ hσ A.T
        (picardClass (s.baseChange A.T) A.lineBundle A.invertible) = 0
declarations.comment: ONLY the object-level content of clause (2): an object (T,h,L) of Picardstack_{X/B} lifts along the 1-morphism of this tag exactly when sigma_T^*[L] = 0 in Pic(T). The three clauses themselves - representable, surjective and smooth in the sense of Stacks 02ZW and 03YK - are NOT proved; see the implementation notes of this file

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.sectionPicardPullback_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
**The elements of the kernel of `σ_T^*` are exactly the Picard classes of the invertible
`𝒪_{X_T}`-modules carrying a trivialisation along `σ_T`.**

This is the identification of the index set of the disjoint union of Stacks 0D2B: for a test
scheme `(T, h)` over the base, the invertible modules underlying the objects of
`Picardstack_{X/B, σ}` over `(T, h)` — the modules `L` for which a rigidifying isomorphism
`α : σ_T^*L ≅ 𝒪_T` exists — are precisely those whose class is killed by
`σ_T^* : Pic(X_T) ⟶ Pic(T)`.  Stacks 0D2B's description of the isomorphism classes of
`Picardstack_{X/B, σ}` over `T` as `⨿_h ker(σ_T^*)` is the sum of this statement over the
objects `(T, h)` of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.SchemesOver`.

**The two other halves of Stacks 0D2B are not proved**: that the stack is fibred in setoids, and
that two objects with the same underlying class are isomorphic.  Both need the global units of
the structure sheaf of an algebraic space, which this development does not carry; see the
implementation notes of the file.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionPicardPullback_eq_zero_iff (σ : s.base ⟶ s.X) (hσ : σ ≫ s.f = 𝟙 s.base)
    (T : s.SchemesOver) (x : s.picardAt T) :
    sectionPicardPullback σ hσ T x = 0 ↔
      ∃ (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS (s.baseChange T).1 (s.baseChange T).2)
        (hL : IsInvertibleModule (s.baseChange T) L), picardClass _ L hL = x ∧
          Nonempty ((modulePullback B S hS (baseChangeSection σ hσ T)).obj L ≅
            structureModule (s.baseSpaceAt T))
declarations.comment: the index set of the disjoint union: the kernel of σ_T^* on Pic(X_T) is exactly the set of classes of the invertible modules admitting a trivialisation along σ_T, i.e. of those underlying an object of Picardstack_{X/B, σ}. The fibred-in-setoids conclusion and the injectivity of the description are NOT proved: both need the global units of the structure sheaf of an algebraic space, which this development does not carry

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionedPicardCFG_isFiberedInSetoids_and_isoClassEquiv
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0D25, let `σ` be a section of `f : X ⟶ B` and assume that
`𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T}` is an isomorphism for every test scheme `T` over `B`.  Then
`Picardstack_{X/B, σ} ⟶ (Sch/S)_{fppf}` is fibred in setoids, and its set of isomorphism classes
over a scheme `T` is `∐_{h : T ⟶ B} Ker(σ_T^* : Pic(X ×_{B, h} T) ⟶ Pic(T))`, through the
bijection `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionedPicardIsoClassEquiv` sending the class of
`(T, h, L, α)` to `(h, [L])`.

`Picardstack_{X/B, σ}` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionedPicardCFG` at the pseudofunctoriality
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence` of Stacks 03LU and the coherence
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionTransportCoherence` of the restriction along the section, both
unconditional.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionedPicardCFG_isFiberedInSetoids_and_isoClassEquiv {s : PicardSituation B S hS}
    (σ : s.base ⟶ s.X) (hσ : σ ≫ s.f = 𝟙 s.base) (hstr : s.StructureSheafMapIso) :
    (sectionedPicardCFG (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
        (sectionTransportCoherence _ σ hσ)).val.p.IsFiberedInSetoids ∧
      ∀ A : PicardSituation.SectionedPicardObject σ hσ,
        sectionedPicardIsoClassEquiv (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
            (sectionTransportCoherence _ σ hσ) hstr A.testScheme.left
            (Quotient.mk _ ⟨A, rfl⟩) =
          ⟨A.testScheme.hom, ⟨picardClass _ A.toPicardObject.lineBundle
            A.toPicardObject.invertible,
            (PicardSituation.sectionPicardPullback_picardClass_eq_zero_iff σ hσ A.testScheme
              _ _).2 ⟨A.trivialization.symm⟩⟩⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpaceOver_picardFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The Picard functor is an algebraic space.**  Let `S` be a scheme and
`f : X ⟶ Y` a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` such that

1. `f` is flat, of finite presentation and proper, and
2. `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T}` is an isomorphism for all schemes `T` over `Y`.

Then the relative Picard functor `Pic_{X/Y}` is an algebraic space over `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpaceOver_picardFunctor {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f.hom) (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (hstr : (PicardSituation.mk X Y f).StructureSheafMapIso) :
    IsAlgebraicSpaceOver (PicardSituation.mk X Y f).picardFunctor
declarations.comment: the full statement: f flat (hflat), of finite presentation (hfp) and proper (hproper), and O_T -> f_{T,*}O_{X_T} an isomorphism for every scheme T over the base (hstr); Pic_{X/B} is an algebraic space over B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.isImmersion_picardEqualizer_and_isLocallySeparated
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is flat, of finite
presentation and proper, such that `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T,*}𝒪_{X_T}` is an isomorphism for every scheme `T`
over `B`. Then the diagonal `Pic_{X/B} ⟶ Pic_{X/B} ×_B Pic_{X/B}` is representable by
immersions: for every scheme `T` over `B` and all `x, y ∈ Pic_{X/B}(T)`, the subfunctor of `h_T`
of the morphisms `T' ⟶ T` with `x|_{T'} = y|_{T'}` (the base change of the diagonal along
`(x, y)`) is represented by immersions. In other words, `Pic_{X/B} ⟶ B` is locally separated:
every morphism of presheaves `q : F ⟶ B` whose fibres are identified with `Pic_{X/B}`, naturally
in the test scheme, has diagonal an immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isImmersion_picardEqualizer_and_isLocallySeparated (hflat : IsFlat B S hS s.f.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS s.f.hom) (hp : IsProper B S hS s.f.hom)
    (h : s.StructureSheafMapIso) :
    (∀ (T : s.SchemesOver) (x y : s.picardFunctor.obj (op T)),
      IsImmersion B S hS (s.picardEqualizer T x y).ι) ∧
    ∀ (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (q : F ⟶ s.base.1)
      (e : ∀ T : s.SchemesOver, s.picardFunctor.obj (op T) ≃
        {x : F.obj (op T.left) //
          q.app (op T.left) x =
            yonedaEquiv (show yoneda.obj T.left ⟶ s.base.1 from T.hom.hom)}),
      (∀ (T U : s.SchemesOver) (g : T ⟶ U) (x : s.picardFunctor.obj (op U)),
        (e T (s.picardFunctor.map g.op x)).val = F.map g.left.op (e U x).val) →
      IsLocallySeparated B S hS q

declarations.name: ModuleGlueing.extensionOfScalarsToPullback
declarations.doc:
A commutative square of commutative rings induces the
extension-of-scalars functor
`Mod B' ⟶ Mod B ×_(Mod A) Mod A'`. Its value at `L'` consists of the two scalar
extensions of `L'` and their canonical identification after extending scalars to `A`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionOfScalarsToPullback.{u, uB', uB, uA', uA}
    {B' : Type uB'} {B : Type uB} {A' : Type uA'} {A : Type uA}
    [CommRing B'] [CommRing B] [CommRing A'] [CommRing A]
    (toB : B' →+* B) (toA' : B' →+* A') (BtoA : B →+* A) (A'toA : A' →+* A)
    (comm : BtoA.comp toB = A'toA.comp toA') :
    ModuleCat.{max u uB uA' uA} B' ⥤
      CategoricalPullback (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uB, uA, max u uB uA' uA} BtoA)
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uA', uA, max u uB uA' uA} A'toA)

declarations.name: MilnorPatching.exists_rightAdjoint_extensionOfScalarsToPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D2F.** The extension-of-scalars functor associated to a commutative
