declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.bijective_morOfSpaceHom
declarations.doc:
For an algebraic space `T` over `S`, the morphisms of sheaves `T ⟶ Hom(F, G)` are the pairs
`(h, u)` of a morphism `h : T ⟶ base` and a homomorphism `u : F_T ⟶ G_T` of the two modules pulled
back to `X ×_{base, h} T`: the construction `(h, u) ↦ (a ↦ (h ∘ a, a^*u))`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.morOfSpaceHom`, is a bijection.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_morOfSpaceHom (T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) :
    Function.Bijective (s.morOfSpaceHom (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) (T := T))
declarations.comment: Mor(T, Hom(F, G)) = {(h, u)}: the construction (h, u) ↦ (a ↦ (h ∘ a, a^*u)) is a bijection from the pairs onto the morphisms T ⟶ Hom(F, G), for every algebraic space T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HomSituation.bijective_isomMorOfSpaceIsom
declarations.doc:
Let `T` be an algebraic space over `S`. The assignment `(h, u) ↦ isomMorOfSpaceIsom (h, u)`
is a bijection from the pairs of a morphism `h : T ⟶ base` and an isomorphism `u : F_T ⟶ G_T` of
the modules pulled back to `X ×_{base, h} T` onto the morphisms of presheaves `T ⟶ Isom(F, G)` on
the big fppf site of `S`:

`Mor(T, Isom(F, G)) = {(h, u) | h : T ⟶ base, u : F_T ⟶ G_T an isomorphism}`.

Here `Isom(F, G)` is the presheaf built from the pseudofunctoriality of direct images
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_isomMorOfSpaceIsom (T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) :
    Function.Bijective (fun p : (Σ h : T ⟶ s.base,
        {u : s.spaceHomAt (Over.mk h) // s.IsIsomOverAt u}) =>
      s.isomMorOfSpaceIsom (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
declarations.comment: the whole identification, in Situation 08JT: for any algebraic space T over S, the map (h, u) |-> the morphism T -> Isom(F, G) is a bijection from all pairs of h : T -> base and an isomorphism u : F_T -> G_T of the pullbacks to X x_{base, h} T onto all morphisms from T into Isom(F, G); the pseudofunctoriality of direct images and both descent clauses are supplied by library results, so the statement takes no hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.morEquivSpaceQuotientOfAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
For an algebraic space `T` over `S`, the morphisms of sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`
from `T` into the functor of quotients `Q_{F/X/Y}` of Stacks 082P are in bijection with the pairs
`(h, F_T ⟶ Q)` consisting of a morphism `h : T ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces and a quotient of the
pullback `F_T` of `F` to `X ×_{Y, h} T` which is quasi-coherent and flat over `T`.

The sheaf of `T` is lifted to the universe of the functor of quotients. The inverse sends a pair
to the transformation restricting it along the chart `t : V ⟶ T` of each section `t` of `T` over
a scheme `V` of the site (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.SpaceQuotient.toMor`).

The inverse images are composed with `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence`, so
nothing is assumed.  The untagged
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.morEquivSpaceQuotient` is the special case of a
scheme `T` of the site, for any proof of that coherence.
declarations.statement:
def morEquivSpaceQuotientOfAlgebraicSpace (T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) :
    (T.obj ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} ⟶
        D.totalQuotientsFunctor (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)) ≃
      D.SpaceQuotients T
declarations.comment: the first displayed identification, for Q_{F/X/Y} and an arbitrary algebraic space T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.morEquivSpaceFinitePresentationQuotientOfAlgebraicSpaceUnconditional
declarations.doc:
For an algebraic space `T` over `S`, the morphisms of sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`
from `T` into the finite-presentation subfunctor `Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y}` of Stacks 0CZL are in bijection
with the pairs `(h, F_T ⟶ Q)` consisting of a morphism `h : T ⟶ Y` and a quotient of `F_T` which
is of finite presentation and flat over `T`.

The subfunctor is formed with the pseudofunctoriality of inverse images
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence` and the preservation of finite presentation
by the base-change pullbacks
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.pullbackPreservesFinitePresentation`.
declarations.statement:
def morEquivSpaceFinitePresentationQuotientOfAlgebraicSpaceUnconditional
    (T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) :
    (T.obj ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} ⟶
        D.totalFinitePresentationQuotientsFunctor (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
          D.pullbackPreservesFinitePresentation) ≃
      D.SpaceFinitePresentationQuotients T
declarations.comment: the second displayed identification, for Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y} and an arbitrary algebraic space T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.morEquivSpaceProperlySupportedQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D3V for a representable algebraic space.**  The morphisms of sheaves on the big
fppf site of `S` from a scheme `U` of the site into `Quot_{F/X/B}` are the pairs `(h, Q)`
consisting of a morphism `h : U ⟶ B` of algebraic spaces and a quotient of `F_U` which is
quasi-coherent, of finite presentation, flat over `U` and has support proper over `U`, where
`F_U` is the pullback of `F` to `X ×_{B, h} U`.

This is the source's displayed identification in the case where the algebraic space `T` is a
scheme of the site, which is the base of the source's proof: that proof chooses a scheme `U`
with a surjective étale morphism `U ⟶ T`, reads the transformation at it as a pair over `U`, and
descends.  The identification here is the Yoneda lemma for the sheaf of Stacks 09TT, whose value
at `U` is the set of those pairs; the sheaf of the algebraic space of `U` is lifted to the
universe of the Quot presheaf, which adds and loses no morphism.  The general case is not
covered; see the implementation notes for the precise obstruction.
declarations.comment: RESTRICTED: the displayed identification, read as a bijection, only for an algebraic space T that is a scheme of the big fppf site; the general case needs the fullness and effectivity of quasi-coherent descent, which this development lacks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.morEquivSpaceProperlySupportedQuotientOfAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
In Situation 09TR, let `T` be an algebraic space over `S`. The morphisms of sheaves on the
big fppf site of `S` from `T` into `Quot_{F/X/B}` are in bijection with the pairs `(h, F_T ⟶ Q)`
consisting of a morphism `h : T ⟶ B` of algebraic spaces and a quotient `Q` of the pullback
`F_T` of `F` to the algebraic space `X ×_{B, h} T`, with `Q` quasi-coherent, of finite
presentation, flat over `T` and with support proper over `T`.

The left-hand side is the Quot presheaf `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.quotSitePresheaf`,
with the sheaf of `T` lifted to its universe. The inverse sends a pair to the transformation
restricting it along the chart `t : V ⟶ T` of every section `t` of `T` over a scheme `V` of the
site.
declarations.comment: the displayed identification, read as a bijection, for an arbitrary algebraic space T over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.morEquivSpaceHilbertFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D3W.** For an algebraic space `T` over `S` the morphisms of sheaves on the big fppf
site of `S` from `T` into the Hilbert presheaf `Hilb_{X/Y}` of Stacks 0CZY are the pairs `(h, Z)`
consisting of a morphism `h : T ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces and a closed subspace `Z` of
`X_T = X ×_{Y, h} T` which is of finite presentation, flat and proper over `T`.

The source writes `=` between a set of morphisms of sheaves and a set of pairs; those are two
different types here, so the honest reading is a bijection, and it is given as an `Equiv`, that
is as data. Both directions are constructed: the forward map is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hilbertMorFamily`, which reads the morphism `h` off the canonical
morphism to `Y` and glues the closed subspaces of the charts, and the inverse is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SpaceHilbertFamily.toMor`, which restricts a pair to every chart;
nothing is chosen from an existence statement.

The hypothesis `hloc` is the descent input `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsHilbertLocalOnBase`, which
is all that the general case needs beyond the gluing proved here; it holds unconditionally when
`T` is a scheme of the site.
declarations.comment: the identification as a bijection, for an arbitrary algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.morEquivSpaceHilbertFamilyOfScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D3W for a scheme of the big fppf site.** The morphisms of sheaves from a scheme `U`
of the site into the Hilbert presheaf `Hilb_{X/Y}` of Stacks 0CZY are the pairs `(h, Z)`
consisting of a morphism `h : U ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces and a closed subspace `Z` of
`X_U = X ×_{Y, h} U` which is of finite presentation, flat and proper over `U`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.morEquivSpaceHilbertFamily` at the algebraic space of `U`, where
the descent input is discharged by the identity chart, so nothing is assumed.
declarations.comment: the identification for a scheme of the big fppf site, unconditionally

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.morEquivSpaceHilbertFamilyOfAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**The points of the Hilbert functor with values in an algebraic space.** In Situation 0CZY,
for an algebraic space `T` over `S` the morphisms of sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` from `T`
into the Hilbert presheaf `Hilb_{X/Y}` are the pairs `(h, Z)` consisting of a morphism `h : T ⟶ Y`
of algebraic spaces and a closed subspace `Z` of `X_T = X ×_{Y, h} T` which is of finite
presentation, flat and proper over `T`.

The identification is a bijection, given as an `Equiv`; the finite presentation of `f` imposed by
Situation 0CZY is not needed. The sheaf of `T` is lifted to the universe of `Hilb_{X/Y}`, which
adds or loses no morphism.
declarations.statement:
def morEquivSpaceHilbertFamilyOfAlgebraicSpace (f : X ⟶ Y) (T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) :
    (T.obj ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} ⟶ hilbertPresheaf f) ≃ SpaceHilbertFamily f T
declarations.comment: the identification as a bijection, for an arbitrary algebraic space, unconditionally

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.openVersalityOf_cartesianProperFlat
registrations.comment: both assertions: over any locally Noetherian base scheme, in particular `Spec(ℤ)` and, after base change, any Noetherian scheme `S`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.forgetPolarization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D3Y.** Forget the polarization of a polarized family, keeping the finitely
presented, flat and proper family of algebraic spaces over the same base.
declarations.statement:
def forgetPolarization :
    PolarizedFamily B ⥤ CartesianProperFlatSpaces B integerBase B.contains_integerBase
declarations.comment: the forgetful functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.forgetPolarization_obj_base
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D3Y.** Forgetting the polarization keeps the base scheme, so the forgetful functor
is a functor over the big fppf site.
declarations.statement:
theorem forgetPolarization_obj_base (X : PolarizedFamily B) :
    (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase B.contains_integerBase).obj
      ((forgetPolarization B).obj X) = (schemeOverIntegers B).obj X.base
declarations.comment: the forgetful functor is over the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.forgetPolarization_map_base
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0D3Y.** Forgetting the polarization keeps the morphism of base schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem forgetPolarization_map_base {X Y : PolarizedFamily B} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase B.contains_integerBase).map
      ((forgetPolarization B).map f) = (schemeOverIntegers B).map f.baseMap
declarations.comment: the forgetful functor is over the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedSpacesForget_isFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D3Z.** Polarized families are fibred in groupoids over the finitely presented, flat
and proper families of algebraic spaces of Stacks 0D1E.

Condition (a) of Stacks 003S is base change of the polarized family along the base scheme of the
given family of algebraic spaces, and condition (b) holds because the base morphism the fill-in
must lie over is forced by the two comparison isomorphisms, so the fill-in is the one
`AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedProjection_uniqueLift` provides over the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem polarizedSpacesForget_isFiberedInGroupoids :
    (polarizedSpacesForget B).IsFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.comment: fibred in groupoids over the stack of finitely presented, flat and proper families

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.toPolarizedSpaces_comp_polarizedSpacesForget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D3Z.** The comparison equivalence carries the projection of
`AlgebraicGeometry.PolarizedSpaces` to the family of algebraic spaces back to the forgetful
functor of Stacks 0D3Y, so `AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedSpacesForget_isFiberedInGroupoids` is the
assertion of the tag for `AlgebraicGeometry.forgetPolarization`.
declarations.statement:
theorem toPolarizedSpaces_comp_polarizedSpacesForget :
    toPolarizedSpaces B ⋙ polarizedSpacesForget B = forgetPolarization B
declarations.comment: identification of the replacement category with the polarized families

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 003S for polarized families, with no hypothesis.** Polarized families of Stacks
0D1M form a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site.

This is also **Stacks 0D3Z** over the big fppf site of schemes: condition (a) of Stacks 003S is
`AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedProjection_existsLift`, by base change, and condition (b) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedProjection_uniqueLift`.
declarations.statement:
theorem polarizedProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids_unconditional {B : BigFppfSite.{u}} :
    (polarizedProjection B).IsFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.comment: fibred in groupoids over the fppf site of schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.polarized_isStackInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D40.** The category `𝒫olarized` of polarized families is a stack in groupoids over
`Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}`, endowed with the topology inherited from the big fppf site
(Stacks 06NV), and it is a stack in groupoids over the big fppf site of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem polarized_isStackInGroupoids :
    (polarizedSpacesForget B).IsStackInGroupoids.{w}
        ((polarizedFamiliesProperFlatProjection B).inheritedTopology B.topology) ∧
      (polarizedProjection B).IsStackInGroupoids.{w} B.topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicMorphism_forgetPolarizationOneMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D41.** The forgetful functor of Stacks 0D3Y, `(X ⟶ S, ℒ) ↦ (X ⟶ S)`, defines a
1-morphism `Polarized ⟶ Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}` of stacks in groupoids over the big fppf site
of `Spec ℤ` (Stacks 0D40, 0D1G) which is algebraic in the sense of Stacks 06CF: its 2-fibre
product with every scheme-valued point of `Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}` is an algebraic stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicMorphism_forgetPolarizationOneMorphism :
    Stack.IsAlgebraicMorphism.{u, w, w, w} B integerBase B.contains_integerBase
      (𝒳 := polarizedStackInGroupoids.{w} B (polarizedProjection_isStack B))
      (𝒴 := properFlatSpacesStackInGroupoids.{w} B integerBase B.contains_integerBase)
      (forgetPolarizationBased B)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasRepresentableDiagonal_polarizedStackUnconditional
declarations.doc:
The diagonal `𝒫olarized ⟶ 𝒫olarized × 𝒫olarized` of the stack of polarized proper flat
families of finite presentation, over the big fppf site of a terminal base scheme, is representable
by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRepresentableDiagonal_polarizedStackUnconditional :
    Stack.HasRepresentableDiagonal B S hS (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLimitPreservingPolarizedUnconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D43.** The stack in groupoids `𝒫olarized` of polarized proper schemes is limit
preserving in the sense of Stacks 07XL: for every cofiltered inverse system of affine schemes over
the terminal base whose limit of underlying schemes is `T`, the canonical comparison
`colim 𝒫olarized_{Tᵢ} ⥤ 𝒫olarized_T` is an equivalence of categories. The index category is taken
in the scheme universe, which is the smallness the source's directed sets have.
declarations.comment: at a small index category

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedPushoutRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D44.** For a commutative square `f ≫ h = i ≫ g` of schemes of the big fppf site,
the comparison functor from the polarized families with base `S'` to the 2-fibre product of those
with base `S` and those with base `T'` over those with base `T`.
declarations.statement:
def polarizedPushoutRestriction {T T' S S' : B.Schemes} (i : T ⟶ T') (f : T ⟶ S) (g : T' ⟶ S')
    (h : S ⟶ S') (hsq : f ≫ h = i ≫ g) :
    (polarizedProjection B).Fiber S' ⥤
      (polarizedFiberPullback B f) ⊡ (polarizedFiberPullback B i)
declarations.comment: the functor of the comparison on fibre categories; that it is an equivalence is not proved here, Stacks 07RX being absent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_polarizedPushoutRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D44.** Let

```
T  --i-->  T'
|          |
f          g
|          |
v          v
S  --h-->  S'
```

be a pushout in the category of schemes, of schemes of the big fppf site, where `T ⟶ T'` is a
thickening and `T ⟶ S` is affine. Then the functor on fibre categories of the stack of polarized
schemes

`𝒫olarized_{S'} ⟶ 𝒫olarized_S ×_{𝒫olarized_T} 𝒫olarized_{T'}`

is an equivalence. (The source states the lemma "in Situation 08KB"; that situation fixes data
which the statement does not use.)
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_polarizedPushoutRestriction {T T' S S' : B.Schemes} (i : T ⟶ T')
    (f : T ⟶ S) (g : T' ⟶ S') (h : S ⟶ S') (hsq : f ≫ h = i ≫ g)
    (hpush : IsPushout (B.inclusion.map f) (B.inclusion.map i) (B.inclusion.map h)
      (B.inclusion.map g))
    (hi : IsThickening (B.inclusion.map i)) [IsAffineHom (B.inclusion.map f)] :
    (polarizedPushoutRestriction B i f g h hsq).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the comparison functor `polarizedPushoutRestriction` of a pushout square of schemes with `T ⟶ T'` a thickening and `T ⟶ S` affine is an equivalence

registrations.name: Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation
registrations.comment: (2): S finitely presented as an R-module ⇒ R → S of finite presentation

declarations.name: lift_finite_projective_of_locallyNilpotent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0D47 (Lemma 10.77.6).**
Let `R` be a commutative ring and `I ⊆ R` a locally nilpotent ideal. Let `Pbar` be a
finite projective `R/I`-module. Then there exists a finite projective `R`-module `P`
together with an isomorphism of `R/I`-modules `P / I P ≅ Pbar`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lift_finite_projective_of_locallyNilpotent
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (hI : I.IsLocallyNilpotent)
    (Pbar : Type u) [AddCommGroup Pbar] [Module (R ⧸ I) Pbar]
    [Module.Finite (R ⧸ I) Pbar] [Module.Projective (R ⧸ I) Pbar] :
    ∃ (P : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup P) (_ : Module R P),
      Module.Finite R P ∧ Module.Projective R P ∧
      Nonempty ((P ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R P))) ≃ₗ[R ⧸ I] Pbar)

declarations.name: Module.projective_of_projective_quotient_of_le_jacobson
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D48.** Let `I` be an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of `R`, equivalently an
ideal every element of whose coset `1 + I` is a unit. A finite flat `R`-module whose reduction
`M / IM` is projective over `R ⧸ I` is itself projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem projective_of_projective_quotient_of_le_jacobson (I : Ideal R)
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Flat R M]
    (hI : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal R))
    (hM : Module.Projective (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) : Module.Projective R M

declarations.name: henselianPair_finiteProjective_quotient_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D4A.** Reduction modulo the ideal of a henselian pair induces a bijection on
isomorphism classes of finite projective modules. Concretely, every finite projective module
over the quotient lifts, and two finite projective modules lift the same isomorphism class
exactly when they were already isomorphic.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselianPair_finiteProjective_quotient_bijective
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (hI : HenselianPair R I) :
    (∀ (Pbar : Type v) [AddCommGroup Pbar] [Module (R ⧸ I) Pbar]
        [Module.Finite (R ⧸ I) Pbar] [Module.Projective (R ⧸ I) Pbar],
      ∃ (P : Type (max u v)) (_ : AddCommGroup P) (_ : Module R P),
        Module.Finite R P ∧ Module.Projective R P ∧
          Nonempty ((P ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R P))) ≃ₗ[R ⧸ I] Pbar)) ∧
    (∀ (P₁ : Type v) [AddCommGroup P₁] [Module R P₁]
        [Module.Finite R P₁] [Module.Projective R P₁]
        (P₂ : Type w) [AddCommGroup P₂] [Module R P₂]
        [Module.Finite R P₂] [Module.Projective R P₂],
      Nonempty
          ((P₁ ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R P₁))) ≃ₗ[R ⧸ I]
            (P₂ ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R P₂)))) ↔
        Nonempty (P₁ ≃ₗ[R] P₂))

declarations.name: finiteProjective_limit_of_finiteFlat_of_isBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D4B.** A compatible inverse system of finite flat modules over a surjective
inverse system of rings with locally nilpotent transition kernels has finite projective inverse
limit, provided its first term is finite projective. The limit commutes with base change to every
ring in the system.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteProjective_limit_of_finiteFlat_of_isBaseChange
    (A : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (c : Cone A) (hc : IsLimit c)
    (M : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} c.pt)
    (moduleStructure : ∀ n : ℕ, Module (A.obj (.op n)) (M.obj (.op n)))
    (hscalar : ∀ n : ℕ,
      letI := moduleStructure n
      letI : Algebra c.pt (A.obj (.op n)) := (c.π.app (.op n)).hom.toAlgebra
      IsScalarTower c.pt (A.obj (.op n)) (M.obj (.op n)))
    (d : ∀ n : ℕ,
      letI := moduleStructure (n + 1)
      letI := moduleStructure n
      ModuleCat.of (A.obj (.op (n + 1))) (M.obj (.op (n + 1))) ⟶
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom).obj
          (ModuleCat.of (A.obj (.op n)) (M.obj (.op n))))
    (hd : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : M.obj (.op (n + 1))),
      letI := moduleStructure (n + 1)
      letI := moduleStructure n
      d n x = M.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op x)
    (hA : ∀ n : ℕ,
      Function.Surjective (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom ∧
        RingHom.ker (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom ≤
          nilradical (A.obj (.op (n + 1))))
    (hfirst :
      letI := moduleStructure 0
      Module.Finite (A.obj (.op 0)) (M.obj (.op 0)) ∧
        Module.Projective (A.obj (.op 0)) (M.obj (.op 0)))
    (hflat : ∀ n : ℕ,
      letI := moduleStructure n
      Module.Finite (A.obj (.op n)) (M.obj (.op n)) ∧
        Module.Flat (A.obj (.op n)) (M.obj (.op n)))
    (hbaseChange : ∀ n : ℕ,
      letI := moduleStructure (n + 1)
      letI := moduleStructure n
      letI : Algebra (A.obj (.op (n + 1))) (A.obj (.op n)) :=
        (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom.toAlgebra
      ∃ e : TensorProduct (A.obj (.op (n + 1))) (A.obj (.op n)) (M.obj (.op (n + 1)))
          ≃ₗ[A.obj (.op n)] M.obj (.op n),
        ∀ (a : A.obj (.op n)) (x : M.obj (.op (n + 1))),
          e (TensorProduct.tmul (A.obj (.op (n + 1))) a x) = a • d n x) :
    Module.Finite c.pt (limit M : ModuleCat.{v} c.pt) ∧
      Module.Projective c.pt (limit M : ModuleCat.{v} c.pt) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ,
        letI := moduleStructure n
        letI : Algebra c.pt (A.obj (.op n)) := (c.π.app (.op n)).hom.toAlgebra
        ∃ e : TensorProduct c.pt (A.obj (.op n)) (limit M : ModuleCat.{v} c.pt)
            ≃ₗ[A.obj (.op n)] M.obj (.op n),
          ∀ (a : A.obj (.op n)) (x : (limit M : ModuleCat.{v} c.pt)),
            e (TensorProduct.tmul c.pt a x) = a • (limit.π M (.op n) x)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjFlat.flat_toBase
declarations.doc:
If the homogeneous piece `A_n` of a quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_S`-algebra is a flat
`𝒪_S`-module for every sufficiently large `n`, the structure morphism of the relative projective
spectrum of `A` is flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_toBase
    (hflat : ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
      IsFlatOver (𝟙 S : S ⟶ S).toLRSHom.toShHom (A.piece (n : ℤ))) :
    Flat (relativeProj A).toBase
declarations.comment: flatness of relative Proj

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjFlat.isFlatOver_twist
declarations.doc:
**Relative flatness of the twists on a relative projective spectrum.**

If the homogeneous piece `A_n` of a quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_S`-algebra is a flat `𝒪_S`-module for
every sufficiently large `n`, then every homogeneous piece of the glued graded algebra of twists on
the relative projective spectrum of `A` is flat over the base.

The twist data is a parameter, so this is the general form of the assertion, of which the
statement for any particular glued family of twists is an instance — in particular for the
canonical one, `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GluedTwistAlgebra.twistDataOfGradedAlgebra`, which Tag
01NR supplies unconditionally.

The criterion used is the affine-open-covering criterion of `AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOver_tfae`,
with the affine opens of the base downstairs and, over each of them, the images under the chart of
the standard opens of the absolute `Proj` at homogeneous elements of positive degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFlatOver_twist (D : TwistData A) (t : ℤ)
    (hflat : ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
      IsFlatOver (𝟙 S : S ⟶ S).toLRSHom.toShHom (A.piece (n : ℤ))) :
    IsFlatOver (relativeProj A).toBase.toLRSHom.toShHom (D.algebra.piece t)
declarations.comment: relative flatness of the twists

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjFinitePresentation.isFinitePresentation_relativeProjTwist
declarations.doc:
Every twist `𝒪_X(t)` on the relative projective spectrum `X = Proj_S(A)` of a quasi-coherent
graded algebra whose structure map is of finite presentation over every affine open of the base is
a module sheaf of finite presentation. The twists are the homogeneous pieces of the twist datum
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GluedTwistAlgebra.twistDataOfGradedAlgebra` of `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFinitePresentation_relativeProjTwist
    (hA : ∀ U : S.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → (A.strHom U).FinitePresentation) (t : ℤ) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation.{u, u, u}
      ((GluedTwistAlgebra.twistDataOfGradedAlgebra A).algebra.piece t)
declarations.comment: twists_finite_presentation

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjFinitePresentation.isFinitePresentation_twist
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D4D, second assertion.** Every twist on the relative homogeneous spectrum of a
quasi-coherent graded algebra whose structure map is of finite presentation over every affine open
of the base is a module of finite presentation.

The relative `Proj` is covered by the images under the charts of the standard opens of the
absolute `Proj`s of the graded rings of sections, on each of which the glued twist is an absolute
twist; that reduction is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjFinitePresentation.isFinitePresentation_twist_of_charts`,
and the absolute statement it consumes is
`isFinitePresentation_twistingSheaf_grading`.

The twist data is a parameter, for the reason given in the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.comment: twists_finite_presentation

registrations.comment: relative_proj_finite_presentation

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingHigherDirectImages.isFiniteLocallyFree_pushforward_and_isIso_baseChange_of_isZero_higherDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0D4E].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes of finite presentation and
let `ℱ` be an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation, flat over `S`, whose support is proper over
`S`. If `R ⁱ f_* ℱ = 0` for all `i > 0`, then

1. `f_* ℱ` is a finite locally free `𝒪_S`-module, and
2. the formation of `f_* ℱ` commutes with arbitrary base change: for every cartesian square
   with `g' : X' ⟶ X`, `f' : X' ⟶ S'` and `g : S' ⟶ S`, the canonical comparison map
   `g^* f_* ℱ ⟶ f'_* (g')^* ℱ` (`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffinePushforward.baseChangeNatTrans`)
   is an isomorphism.

The first conclusion is `isFiniteLocallyFree_pushforward_of_isZero_higherDirectImage`, the second
`isIso_baseChangeNatTrans_app_of_vanishing`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_pushforward_and_isIso_baseChange_of_isZero_higherDirectImage
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (hf : FinitePresentation f) (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] (hflat : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F)
    (hsupp : letI : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f := hf.locallyOfFinitePresentation
      ∃ Z : Closeds X, IsProperOver f Z ∧ SheafOfModules.supp F ⊆ (Z : Set X))
    (hvanish : ∀ i : ℤ, 0 < i →
      IsZero (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerivedPlus i).obj F)) :
    _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
        (R := S.ringCatSheaf) ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F) ∧
      ∀ {X' S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
        (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g),
        IsIso ((Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffinePushforward.baseChangeNatTrans hsq.w).app F)
declarations.comment: both conclusions: f_*F is finite locally free, and for every cartesian square the canonical comparison g^*f_*F --> f'_*(g')^*F (baseChangeNatTrans, the mate of the two pullback-pushforward adjunctions) is an isomorphism, which is the meaning the source's proof gives to `commutes with arbitrary base change`

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveDeformation.exists_uniform_degreeBound_functorial
declarations.doc:
**Deformations of projective schemes** ([Stacks, Tag 0D4F]).  Let `(f : X ⟶ S, ℒ)` be a
polarized family: `f` proper, flat and of finite presentation, `S` quasi-compact, `ℒ` invertible
and ample relative to `f`.  There is a positive `d₀` such that for every admissible deformation
`(X', S', i, i', f', ℒ')` of it — a cartesian square over a thickening `S ⊂ S'` with `f'` proper,
flat and of finite presentation, and `ℒ'` invertible with `ℒ ≅ (i')^* ℒ'`:

1. `R^p (f')_* (ℒ')^{⊗ d} = 0` for all `p > 0` and `d ≥ d₀`;
2. `𝒜'_d = (f')_* (ℒ')^{⊗ d}` is finite locally free for `d ≥ d₀`;
3. `𝒜' = 𝒪_{S'} ⊕ ⨁_{d ≥ d₀} 𝒜'_d` (`truncatedSectionAlgebra`) is a quasi-coherent graded
   `𝒪_{S'}`-algebra with these pieces, its comparison `𝒜' ⟶ ⨁_{d ≥ 0} 𝒜'_d`
   (`sectionAlgebraComparison`) is an isomorphism in every degree `≥ d₀`, and `𝒜'` is of finite
   presentation over every affine open of `S'`;
4. the canonical morphism `r' : X' ⟶ Proj_{S'}(𝒜')` (`canonicalProjHom`) is an isomorphism over
   `S'`;
5. the canonical map `θ' : (r')^* 𝒪_{Proj_{S'}(𝒜')}(1) ⟶ ℒ'` (`canonicalTwistMap`) is an
   isomorphism;

and the formation of each `𝒜'_d`, `d ≥ d₀`, commutes with arbitrary base change.

**Functoriality.** For every morphism `φ : D₁ ⟶ D₂` of admissible deformations (a cartesian
square `g' : X'₁ ⟶ X'₂` over `g : S'₁ ⟶ S'₂` compatible with the immersions of the family, with
polarization `g'^* ℒ'₂ ≅ ℒ'₁`):

* `𝒜'` is functorial: the homomorphism of graded algebras `g^* 𝒜'(D₂) ⟶ 𝒜'(D₁)` obtained by
  pulling sections back (`algebraPullbackHom`) is an isomorphism in every degree;
* `r'` is functorial: with `M : Proj_{S'₁}(𝒜'(D₁)) ⟶ Proj_{S'₂}(𝒜'(D₂))` the morphism it induces
  followed by the base change morphism of [Stacks, Tag 01O3] (`projBaseChangeHom`),
  `r'₁ ≫ M = g' ≫ r'₂`;
* `θ'` is functorial: `g'^* θ'₂` followed by the polarization equals, through
  `g'^* (r'₂)^* ≅ (r'₁ ≫ M)^* ≅ (r'₁)^* M^*`, the inverse image along `r'₁` of the map of Serre
  twists `M^* 𝒪(1) ⟶ 𝒪(1)` of [Stacks, Tags 01O3, 07ZJ] (`projBaseChangeTwistMap`) followed by
  `θ'₁`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_uniform_degreeBound_functorial (P : PolarizedFamily.{u}) :
    ∃ (d₀ : ℕ) (hd₀ : 0 < d₀), (∀ D : P.AdmissibleDeformation,
      (∀ d : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d → ∀ p : ℤ, 0 < p →
          IsZero (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward D.f').rightDerivedPlus p).obj
            (tensorPowModule D.X' D.L' (d : ℤ)))) ∧
        (∀ d : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d →
          _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
            (R := D.S'.ringCatSheaf) (D.sectionPiece d)) ∧
        (D.IsTruncatedSectionAlgebraWithComparison d₀ (D.truncatedSectionAlgebra d₀ hd₀) ∧
          (∀ d : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d → IsIso ((D.sectionAlgebraComparison d₀ hd₀).app (d : ℤ))) ∧
          (∀ U : D.S'.Opens, IsAffineOpen U →
            RingHom.FinitePresentation ((D.truncatedSectionAlgebra d₀ hd₀).strHom U))) ∧
        (IsIso (D.canonicalProjHom d₀ hd₀) ∧
          D.canonicalProjHom d₀ hd₀ ≫ (relativeProj (D.truncatedSectionAlgebra d₀ hd₀)).toBase =
            D.f') ∧
        IsIso (D.canonicalTwistMap d₀ hd₀) ∧
        ∀ d : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d → ∀ (T Y : Scheme.{u}) (h : T ⟶ D.S') (fT : Y ⟶ T) (h' : Y ⟶ D.X')
          (hsq : IsPullback h' fT D.f' h),
          IsIso ((Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffinePushforward.baseChangeNatTrans hsq.w).app
            (tensorPowModule D.X' D.L' (d : ℤ)))) ∧
      ∀ (D₁ D₂ : P.AdmissibleDeformation) (φ : Hom D₁ D₂),
        ∃ hiso : ∀ n : ℤ, IsIso ((algebraPullbackHom φ d₀ hd₀).app n),
          D₁.canonicalProjHom d₀ hd₀ ≫ projBaseChangeHom φ d₀ hd₀ hiso =
            φ.total ≫ D₂.canonicalProjHom d₀ hd₀ ∧
          (Scheme.Modules.pullback φ.total).map (D₂.canonicalTwistMap d₀ hd₀) ≫
              φ.polarization.hom =
            (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp φ.total (D₂.canonicalProjHom d₀ hd₀)).hom.app _ ≫
              (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr
                (canonicalProjHom_comp_projBaseChangeHom φ d₀ hd₀ hiso).symm).hom.app _ ≫
              (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (D₁.canonicalProjHom d₀ hd₀)
                (projBaseChangeHom φ d₀ hd₀ hiso)).inv.app _ ≫
              (Scheme.Modules.pullback (D₁.canonicalProjHom d₀ hd₀)).map
                (projBaseChangeTwistMap φ d₀ hd₀ hiso) ≫
              D₁.canonicalTwistMap d₀ hd₀

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatAt_of_flat_infinitesimalNeighbourhoods
declarations.doc:
Flatness over a closed subscheme can be checked on every infinitesimal
neighbourhood of that subscheme when the schemes are locally Noetherian.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSituation.exists_hasRelativeDimensionLE_mapAt_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D4K.** In the situation of Stacks 084W, if the base change `f` of `f₀` to the
limit `B` has relative dimension at most `d` and `f₀` is locally of finite type, then the base
change `f_i` of `f₀` to some stage `B_i` has relative dimension at most `d`.

This is the statement under the chapter's convention of Section 70.2 (tag 07SD), which asks
nothing of the index: the situation `D` carries no bound on the size of `I`, and the convention
is the hypothesis `hconv`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SiteContainsBaseChangeLimits` for the system
`(B_i)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hasRelativeDimensionLE_mapAt_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits (D :
    MorphismDescentSituation B S hS hZ I)
    (hconv : SiteContainsBaseChangeLimits B S hS D.base) (d : ℕ)
    (dimension : HasRelativeDimensionLE d B S hS D.mapLimit)
    (ft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS D.map₀) :
    ∃ (i : I) (le : D.initial ≤ i), HasRelativeDimensionLE d B S hS (D.mapAt i le)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fiberDimension_eq_dimension_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D4M.** For a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` of finite type and a field-valued
point `p` of its target, the fibre dimension at the point `p` represents is the dimension of the
fibre of `f` over `p`, and it is not `⊤`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fiberDimension_eq_dimension_pullback
    (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y) :
    fiberDimension B S hS f (p.class B S hS Y) =
      dimension B S hS (pullback (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value) f)
        (isAlgebraicSpace_pullback B S hS (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value) f
          (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS (p.siteObject B S hS Y)) hX hY) ∧
      fiberDimension B S hS f (p.class B S hS Y) ≠ ⊤

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fiberDimension_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D4N.** The fibre-dimension function of the base change of a finite type morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` is the pullback of the fibre-dimension function of the morphism along
the map on points of the morphism of targets.
declarations.statement:
theorem fiberDimension_pullback_snd {X Y Y' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f) :
    fiberDimension B S hS (pullback.snd f g) =
      fiberDimension B S hS f ∘ pointsMap B S hS Y' g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyConstant_fiberDimension
declarations.doc:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PolarizedDeformation.finiteDimensional_tangentFunctor_infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D4S, part (2).** Let `k` be a field and let `x = (X → Spec k, ℒ)` be an
object of `𝒫olarized` over `Spec k`. Then the tangent functor `T_x` and the functor of
infinitesimal automorphisms `Inf_x` of Stacks 07Y9 exist, and `T_x(k)` and `Inf_x(k)` are
finite-dimensional `k`-vector spaces.

Each functor is stated as a structure (`TangentFunctorData`,
`InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData`) carrying a `k`-linear functor on the site modules together
with its identification with the isomorphism classes of lifts of `x`, respectively with the
infinitesimal automorphisms of the trivial lifts of `x`, natural in the module. The statement gives
that such a functor exists and that the value at `k` of every such functor is finite-dimensional.
No condition on `k` is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_tangentFunctor_infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (toS : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S) (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (x : PolarizedFamily B)
    (hx : (polarizedSliceProjection B hS hT).obj x = algebraOver k B S hS toS hk) :
    (Nonempty (TangentFunctorData k B S hS toS hk (polarizedSliceProjection B hS hT) x hx) ∧
      ∀ T : TangentFunctorData k B S hS toS hk (polarizedSliceProjection B hS hT) x hx,
        FiniteDimensional k (T.functor.obj ((fgSiteModule B hk).obj (FGModuleCat.of k k)))) ∧
    (Nonempty (InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData k B S hS toS hk
        (polarizedSliceProjection B hS hT) x hx
        (isFiberedInGroupoids_polarizedSliceProjection B hS hT)) ∧
      ∀ I : InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData k B S hS toS hk
          (polarizedSliceProjection B hS hT) x hx
          (isFiberedInGroupoids_polarizedSliceProjection B hS hT),
        FiniteDimensional k (I.functor.obj ((fgSiteModule B hk).obj (FGModuleCat.of k k))))
declarations.comment: (2): for a polarized proper scheme x over any field k, the functors T_x and Inf_x of Stacks 07Y9 exist (𝒫olarized satisfies RS* by 0D44) and T_x(k) and Inf_x(k) are finite dimensional; both finiteness statements hold for every k-linear functor carrying the identifications of 07Y9

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PolarizedDeformation.isFiniteDimensionalDeformationCategory_predeformationCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D4S, part (1).** Let `k` be a field of finite type over the base (for
the base `Spec ℤ`: of finite type over `ℤ`), presented through `Spec k ⟶ Spec Λ ⟶ S`, and let
`x = (X → Spec k, ℒ)` be an object of `𝒫olarized` over `Spec k`. Then the predeformation category
`𝓕_{𝒳,k,x}` of Stacks 07T2 is a deformation category whose tangent space `T𝓕_{𝒳,k,x}` and whose
infinitesimal automorphisms `Inf(𝓕_{𝒳,k,x})` (Stacks 07WY) are finite-dimensional `k`-vector
spaces.

The base is any scheme `S` which is terminal in the big fppf site; no condition is put on `Λ`
beyond the factorization.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteDimensionalDeformationCategory_predeformationCategory
    {Λ k : Type u} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k] (iΛ : Spec (.of Λ) ⟶ S)
    (x : PolarizedFamily B)
    (hx₀ : (polarizedSliceProjection B hS hT ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x =
      Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ))
    (hfinite : LocallyOfFiniteType (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ) ∧
      QuasiCompact (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ)) :
    IsFiniteDimensionalDeformationCategory
      (predeformationCategory iΛ (polarizedSliceProjection B hS hT ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) x
        hx₀).projection
declarations.comment: (1): for a field k of finite type over the base and a polarized proper scheme x over k, the deformation category F_{X,k,x} has finite dimensional tangent space T F_{X,k,x} and finite dimensional Inf(F_{X,k,x}); the base is any terminal scheme of the site, e.g. Spec Z

declarations.name: Stacks.PolarizedAlgebraization.exists_algebraization
declarations.doc:
**Strong formal effectiveness for polarized schemes.** Let `(R_n)` be an inverse system of
rings with surjective transition maps whose kernels are locally nilpotent, and `R = lim R_n`. Let
`X_n ⟶ Spec R_n` be schemes with cartesian squares over the transitions
`Spec R_n ⟶ Spec R_{n + 1}`, `ℒ_n` invertible `𝒪_{X_n}`-modules and `φ_n : i_n^* ℒ_{n + 1} ≅ ℒ_n`.
If every `X_n ⟶ Spec R_n` is proper, flat and of finite presentation, and `ℒ_0` is ample, then
there are a proper, flat, finitely presented `X ⟶ Spec R`, an ample invertible `ℒ` on `X`,
identifications `X_n ≅ X ×_{Spec R} Spec R_n` (cartesian squares through `j_n : X_n ⟶ X`) and
isomorphisms `e_n : ℒ|_{X_n} ≅ ℒ_n`, compatible with the `i_n` and the `φ_n`. The index `n : ℕ`
stands for the source's `n + 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_algebraization (R : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u})
    (hsurj : ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Surjective (R.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom)
    (hnil : ∀ n : ℕ,
      RingHom.ker (R.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom ≤ nilradical (R.obj (op (n + 1))))
    (X : ℕ → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ n : ℕ, X n ⟶ Spec (R.obj (op n)))
    (i : ∀ n : ℕ, X n ⟶ X (n + 1))
    (hpb : ∀ n : ℕ,
      IsPullback (i n) (f n) (f (n + 1)) (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)))
    (L : ∀ n : ℕ, (X n).Modules) [hL : ∀ n : ℕ, IsInvertibleModule (X n) (L n)]
    (φ : ∀ n : ℕ, (Scheme.Modules.pullback (i n)).obj (L (n + 1)) ≅ L n)
    [hproper : ∀ n : ℕ, IsProper (f n)] [hflat : ∀ n : ℕ, Flat (f n)]
    (hfp : ∀ n : ℕ, _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation (f n))
    (hample : IsAmple (X 0) (L 0)) :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (limit R)) (ℒ : Y.Modules) (_ : IsInvertibleModule Y ℒ)
      (j : ∀ n : ℕ, X n ⟶ Y) (hj : ∀ n : ℕ, i n ≫ j (n + 1) = j n)
      (e : ∀ n : ℕ, (Scheme.Modules.pullback (j n)).obj ℒ ⟶ L n),
      IsProper g ∧ Flat g ∧ _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation g ∧ IsAmple Y ℒ ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, IsPullback (j n) (f n) g (Spec.map (limit.π R (op n)))) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (e n)) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (i n) (j (n + 1))).hom.app ℒ ≫
          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr (hj n)).hom.app ℒ ≫ e n =
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (i n)).map (e (n + 1)) ≫ (φ n).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedFormalObject_isEffective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D4U.** Consider the stack `𝒫olarized` over the base scheme `Spec ℤ`. Then every
formal object (Stacks 07X4) is effective (Stacks 07X7): it is, up to isomorphism, the system of
restrictions to the infinitesimal thickenings `Spec(R / 𝔪^{n+1})` of a polarized family over its
complete local base `Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem polarizedFormalObject_isEffective (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hZ : B.Contains (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))))
    (ξ : FormalObject B _ hZ (polarizedSliceProjection B hZ (isTerminal_obj_specULiftZ B hZ))) :
    FormalObject.IsEffective B _ hZ (polarizedSliceProjection B hZ (isTerminal_obj_specULiftZ B hZ))
      (polarizedProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids_unconditional.sliceAtTerminal
        (isTerminal_obj_specULiftZ B hZ)) ξ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasOpenVersality_polarizedStackUnconditional
declarations.doc:
The stack in groupoids `𝒫olarized` of polarized proper flat families of finite presentation
(Stacks 0D1M), over the big fppf site of `Spec(ℤ)`, satisfies openness of versality: if an object
over a scheme `U` locally of finite type over `Spec(ℤ)` is versal at a finite type point `u₀`, it
is versal at every finite type point of an open neighbourhood of `u₀`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasOpenVersality_polarizedStackUnconditional (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hZ : B.Contains (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) :
    HasOpenVersality
      ((polarizedStackUnconditional B hZ (isTerminal_obj_specULiftZ B hZ)).val.p ⋙
        Over.post B.inclusion)
declarations.comment: openness of versality for `𝒫olarized` over `Spec(ℤ)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasOpenVersality_polarizedOverNoetherian
declarations.doc:
For a Noetherian scheme `S`, the stack `S-𝒫olarized` of Remark 0D1N — polarized proper flat
families of finite presentation together with a morphism of their base to `S` — over the big fppf
site of `S` satisfies openness of versality: if an object over a scheme `U` locally of finite type
over `S` is versal at a finite type point `u₀`, it is versal at every finite type point of an open
neighbourhood of `u₀`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasOpenVersality_polarizedOverNoetherian (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) [IsNoetherian S] :
    HasOpenVersality
      ((PolarizedVersality.PolarizedOver.stack B S hS).val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion)
declarations.comment: openness of versality for `S-𝒫olarized` over a Noetherian base scheme `S`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicStack_polarizedStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D4X.** The stack `𝒫olarized` of polarized proper schemes (Situation 0D1M) over the
big fppf site of `Spec ℤ` is an algebraic stack. In fact, for every algebraic space `A` over
`Spec ℤ`, the stack `A-Polarized` of Remark 0D1N, of polarized proper schemes `(X ⟶ S, ℒ)`
together with a morphism `S ⟶ A`, is an algebraic stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_polarizedStack :
    Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B integerBase B.contains_integerBase
        (polarizedStackUnconditional B B.contains_integerBase
          (isTerminal_obj_specULiftZ B B.contains_integerBase)).val ∧
      ∀ (A : (BigFppfOver B integerBase B.contains_integerBase)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u),
        IsAlgebraicSpace B integerBase B.contains_integerBase A →
        Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B integerBase B.contains_integerBase
          (BasedCategory.ofFunctor
            (AlgebraicGeometry.PolarizedFamilyOver.projection B integerBase
              B.contains_integerBase A))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CurveFamily
declarations.doc:
A *family of curves*: a morphism from an algebraic space to a scheme of
the big fppf site which is flat, proper, of finite presentation and of relative dimension at
most one.
declarations.statement: structure CurveFamily
declarations.comment: objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CurveFamily.Hom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of families of curves: a morphism of total spaces over a
morphism of base schemes whose square is cartesian.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (X Y : CurveFamily B hZ)
declarations.comment: morphisms

declarations.doc:
Families of curves and cartesian squares between them form a category,
with componentwise identities and composition.
declarations.statement: instance : Category (CurveFamily B hZ)
declarations.comment: category

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curvesProjection
declarations.doc:
The forgetful functor taking a family of curves to its base scheme, which makes the category
of families of curves a category over the big fppf site.
declarations.statement: def curvesProjection : CurveFamily B hZ ⥤ B.Schemes
declarations.comment: projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curvesToCartesianProperFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks equation 0D50.** The inclusion of the category of families of curves into the
category of finitely presented, flat and proper families of algebraic spaces over varying base
schemes, forgetting the bound on the relative dimension of the structure morphism: on objects it
is `AlgebraicGeometry.CurveFamily.toCartesianProperFlat` and on morphisms it keeps the morphism
of total spaces and the morphism of base schemes, the cartesian square of a morphism of families
of curves being exactly the strongly cartesian condition on the larger side.

The equation displays only this inclusion. That the two sides are categories fibred in groupoids
over the big fppf site and that the inclusion is one of categories over that site is the ambient
Situation 99.15.1 of the source, realised here by
`AlgebraicGeometry.curvesProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.cartesianProperFlatProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.curvesToCartesianProperFlat_comp_cartesianProperFlatProjection`; that the
inclusion is one of a full subcategory is
`AlgebraicGeometry.curvesToCartesianProperFlat_full` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.curvesToCartesianProperFlat_faithful`.
declarations.statement:
def curvesToCartesianProperFlat :
    CurveFamily B hZ ⥤ CartesianProperFlatSpaces B integerBase hZ
declarations.comment: the inclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curvesProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D51.** The category of families of curves is fibred in groupoids over the big fppf
site of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem curvesProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids :
    (curvesProjection B hZ).IsFiberedInGroupoids

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curvesProjection_isStackInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D52.** The category of families of curves is a stack in groupoids over the big fppf
site of schemes, for covering families indexed in every universe.

It is a stack (`AlgebraicGeometry.curvesProjection_isStack`) whose projection is fibred in
groupoids (Stacks 0D51, `AlgebraicGeometry.curvesProjection_isFiberedInGroupoids`), and such a
stack is a stack in groupoids by the implication (3) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 02ZJ.
declarations.statement:
theorem curvesProjection_isStackInGroupoids :
    (curvesProjection B hZ).IsStackInGroupoids.{w} B.topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CurveFamilyOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D54.** The category of families of curves over a fixed algebraic space `A`: an object
is a family of curves together with a morphism from its base scheme to `A`, and a morphism is a
morphism of families of curves commuting with those morphisms.
declarations.statement: abbrev CurveFamilyOver (A : AlgebraicSpaces B integerBase hZ)
declarations.comment: the category of families of curves over a base algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CurveFamilyOver.isEquivalence_toTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D54.** The absolute and the relative categories of curves form a 2-fibre product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curvePushoutEquivalenceOfIsPushout

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CurveDeformation.finiteDimensional_predeformation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D57, part (1).** Let `k` be a field and let `x = (X → Spec k)` be a
family of curves over `Spec k`, lying over `Spec k → Spec Λ → Spec ℤ`. Then the predeformation
category `𝓕_{𝒳,k,x}` over `𝒞_Λ` is a deformation category, its tangent space `T𝓕_{𝒳,k,x}` is a
finite-dimensional `k`-vector space, and so are its infinitesimal automorphisms
`Inf(𝓕_{𝒳,k,x})`, the kernel of `Aut_{k[ε]}(x'₀) → Aut_k(x₀)`, at every object of the special
fibre and for every choice of its pushforwards.

This generalizes the source: `k` need not be of finite type over `ℤ`, and `Λ` is any ring with
a `Λ`-algebra structure on `k` and any morphism `Spec Λ ⟶ Spec ℤ`. The proof identifies
`𝓕_{𝒳,k,x}` with the deformation category of the scheme `X` (the total space of a curve over a
field is a scheme, Stacks 0ADD) and applies the finiteness of Stacks 0DYA for that category, in
place of the source's appeal to Stacks 0D1K.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_predeformation :
    letI := (predeformation x hx).category
    ∃ hD : IsDeformationCategory.{u, u, u} (predeformation x hx).projection,
      (letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory
          (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (predeformation x hx).projection).p) := ⟨hD.predeformation⟩;
        letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2 (Functor.Elements.π
          (isomorphismClasses (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (predeformation x hx).projection)
            hD.predeformation.cofibered))) := ⟨tangentConditionS2.{u, u, u} hD⟩;
        FiniteDimensional k (artinianTangentSpace Λ k
          (isomorphismClasses (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (predeformation x hx).projection)
            hD.predeformation.cofibered))) ∧
      ∀ y, (predeformation x hx).projection.obj y = residueFieldObject.{u, u, u} Λ k →
        ∀ PF : ChosenPushforwardsAt (predeformation x hx).projection y,
          FiniteDimensional k ↥((infinitesimalAutomorphismLinearLift.{u, u, u} PF
            hD.satisfiesRS).functor.obj (FGModuleCat.of k (ULift.{u} k)))
declarations.comment: (1): for a family of curves x over any field k and any Λ with Spec k → Spec Λ, the predeformation category F_{X,k,x} is a deformation category whose tangent space T F and infinitesimal automorphisms Inf(F) are finite dimensional; k need not be of finite type over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteDimensional_curves_tangentFunctor_infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `x = (X → Spec k)` be a family of curves over `Spec k`. Then the
tangent functor `T_x` and the functor of infinitesimal automorphisms `Inf_x` of Stacks 07Y9 exist,
and `T_x(k)` and `Inf_x(k)` are finite-dimensional `k`-vector spaces.

Each functor is stated as a structure (`TangentFunctorData`,
`InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData`) carrying a `k`-linear functor on the site modules together
with its identification with the isomorphism classes of lifts of `x`, respectively with the
infinitesimal automorphisms of the trivial lifts of `x`, natural in the module. The statement
gives that such a functor exists and that the value at `k` of *every* such functor is
finite-dimensional, so it holds for the functors `T_x` and `Inf_x` of Stacks 07Y9, which are
determined by these identifications. No condition on `k` is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_curves_tangentFunctor_infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor {k : Type u}
    [Field k] {toS : Spec (.of k) ⟶ integerBase} {hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))}
    (x : CurveFamily B hZ)
    (hx : (curvesProjectionOver B hZ).obj x = algebraOver k B integerBase hZ toS hk) :
    (Nonempty (TangentFunctorData k B integerBase hZ toS hk (curvesProjectionOver B hZ) x hx) ∧
      ∀ T : TangentFunctorData k B integerBase hZ toS hk (curvesProjectionOver B hZ) x hx,
        FiniteDimensional k (T.functor.obj ((fgSiteModule B hk).obj (FGModuleCat.of k k)))) ∧
    (Nonempty (InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData k B integerBase hZ toS hk
        (curvesProjectionOver B hZ) x hx
        CurveDeformation.curvesProjectionOver_isFiberedInGroupoids) ∧
      ∀ I : InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData k B integerBase hZ toS hk
          (curvesProjectionOver B hZ) x hx
          CurveDeformation.curvesProjectionOver_isFiberedInGroupoids,
        FiniteDimensional k (I.functor.obj ((fgSiteModule B hk).obj (FGModuleCat.of k k))))
declarations.comment: (2): for a family of curves x over a field k, the tangent functor T_x and the functor Inf_x of Stacks 07Y9 exist, and T_x(k) and Inf_x(k) are finite dimensional; both are stated for every k-linear functor carrying the identifications of 07Y9

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curvesFormalObject_isEffective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedCurvesToCurves_isAlgebraic_smooth_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D5C.** Let `PolarizedCurves = 𝒞urves ×_{𝒮paces'_{fp, flat, proper}} 𝒫olarized`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedCurvesUnconditional`), over the big fppf site of `Spec ℤ`.

1. PolarizedCurves parametrizes polarized curves: its first projection is an equivalence onto the
   category of polarized families of relative dimension at most one, i.e. of families of curves
   endowed with a relatively ample invertible sheaf.
2. PolarizedCurves is an open and closed substack of the algebraic stack `𝒫olarized`: `𝒫olarized`
   is an algebraic stack, the projection `PolarizedCurves ⟶ 𝒫olarized` is representable by
   algebraic spaces, an open immersion and a closed immersion, and PolarizedCurves is an algebraic
   stack.
3. `PolarizedCurves ⟶ 𝒞urves` is a base change of the arrow `𝒫olarized ⟶ 𝒮paces'_{fp,flat,proper}`
   of Stacks 0D41: its base change along every scheme point `z` of `𝒞urves` is equivalent over the
   site to the base change of the forgetful 1-morphism of Stacks 0D41 along the image of `z` in
   `𝒮paces'_{fp, flat, proper}`.
4. `PolarizedCurves ⟶ 𝒞urves` is algebraic (Stacks 06CF): its base change along every scheme point
   of `𝒞urves` is an algebraic stack.
5. `PolarizedCurves ⟶ 𝒞urves` is smooth: each of these base changes is smooth over the scheme
   (Stacks 075U).
6. `PolarizedCurves ⟶ 𝒞urves` is surjective: every point of `𝒞urves` is in the image
   (surjectivity on objects, Stacks 06D4), and the 1-morphism of algebraic stacks is surjective on
   points (Stacks 04ZS).
7. Another approach to the algebraicity of `𝒞urves`: `𝒞urves` is an algebraic stack, as the
   target of the smooth, surjective, algebraic 1-morphism `PolarizedCurves ⟶ 𝒞urves` from the
   algebraic stack PolarizedCurves.

Clauses 4–6 are stated for the hom-shrunk models `AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedCurvesSmall` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.curvesSmall`, equivalent over the site to PolarizedCurves and `𝒞urves`, with
the projection `AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedCurvesSmallToCurvesSmall`; surjectivity on objects in
clause 6 is also stated for PolarizedCurves itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem polarizedCurvesToCurves_isAlgebraic_smooth_surjective :
    -- (1) PolarizedCurves parametrizes polarized curves
    (polarizedCurvesToIsPolarizedCurve B hZ).IsEquivalence ∧
    -- (2) PolarizedCurves is an open and closed substack of the algebraic stack `𝒫olarized`
    (Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B integerBase hZ (polarizedFiberedCategory B hZ
        (polarizedProjection_comp_schemeOverIntegers_isFiberedInGroupoids B)).val ∧
      Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B integerBase hZ
        (polarizedCurvesToPolarizedUnconditional B hZ).hom ∧
      Stack.IsOpenImmersion B integerBase hZ (polarizedCurvesToPolarizedUnconditional B hZ) ∧
      Stack.IsClosedImmersion B integerBase hZ (polarizedCurvesToPolarizedUnconditional B hZ) ∧
      Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B integerBase hZ (polarizedCurvesUnconditional B hZ).val) ∧
    -- (3) `PolarizedCurves ⟶ 𝒞urves` is a base change of the arrow of Stacks 0D41
    (∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B integerBase hZ)
      (z : BigFppfOver B Z.left.1 Z.left.2 ⥤ (curvesFiberedCategory B hZ).val.obj),
      z ⋙ (curvesFiberedCategory B hZ).val.p = Over.map Z.hom →
      Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor (Over.map Z.hom)
          (polarizedProjection B ⋙ schemeOverIntegers B)
          (cartesianProperFlatProjection B integerBase hZ)
          (z ⋙ curvesToCartesianProperFlat B hZ) (forgetPolarization B))
        (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor (Over.map Z.hom)
          (polarizedCurvesUnconditional B hZ).val.p (curvesFiberedCategory B hZ).val.p z
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (polarizedCurvesSquare B hZ
            (polarizedProjection_comp_schemeOverIntegers_isFiberedInGroupoids B)).snd)))) ∧
    -- (4) `PolarizedCurves ⟶ 𝒞urves` is algebraic
    (∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B integerBase hZ)
      (z : BigFppfOver B Z.left.1 Z.left.2 ⥤ (curvesSmall B hZ).val.obj)
      (hz : z ⋙ (curvesSmall B hZ).val.p = Over.map Z.hom),
      Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B integerBase hZ
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.twoFibreProductSquare.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1}
          (Stack.schemeSliceMap B integerBase hZ Z z hz)
          (polarizedCurvesSmallToCurvesSmall B hZ
            (polarizedProjection_comp_schemeOverIntegers_isFiberedInGroupoids B))).pt.val) ∧
    -- (5) `PolarizedCurves ⟶ 𝒞urves` is smooth
    (∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B integerBase hZ)
      (z : BigFppfOver B Z.left.1 Z.left.2 ⥤ (curvesSmall B hZ).val.obj)
      (hz : z ⋙ (curvesSmall B hZ).val.p = Over.map Z.hom),
      Stack.HasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram B integerBase hZ
        (fun _ _ h => Space.IsSmooth B integerBase hZ h)
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.twoFibreProductSquare.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1}
          (Stack.schemeSliceMap B integerBase hZ Z z hz)
          (polarizedCurvesSmallToCurvesSmall B hZ
            (polarizedProjection_comp_schemeOverIntegers_isFiberedInGroupoids B))).fst) ∧
    -- (6) `PolarizedCurves ⟶ 𝒞urves` is surjective
    (Stack.IsSurjectiveOnObjects B integerBase hZ
        (polarizedCurvesUnconditional B hZ).val.p (curvesFiberedCategory B hZ).val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (polarizedCurvesSquare B hZ
          (polarizedProjection_comp_schemeOverIntegers_isFiberedInGroupoids B)).snd) ∧
      Stack.IsSurjectiveOnObjects B integerBase hZ
        (polarizedCurvesSmall B hZ
          (polarizedProjection_comp_schemeOverIntegers_isFiberedInGroupoids B)).val.p
        (curvesSmall B hZ).val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (polarizedCurvesSmallToCurvesSmall B hZ
          (polarizedProjection_comp_schemeOverIntegers_isFiberedInGroupoids B))) ∧
      ∃ (hX : Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B integerBase hZ
          (polarizedCurvesUnconditional B hZ).val)
        (hY : Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B integerBase hZ (curvesFiberedCategory B hZ).val),
        Stack.IsSurjective B integerBase hZ (polarizedCurvesToCurvesAlgebraic B hZ
          (polarizedProjection_comp_schemeOverIntegers_isFiberedInGroupoids B) hX hY)) ∧
    -- (7) `𝒞urves` is an algebraic stack
    Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B integerBase hZ (curvesFiberedCategory B hZ).val

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.CurveFamilyNotScheme.exists_curveFamily_total_not_scheme
declarations.doc:
**A family of curves whose total space is not a scheme** ([Stacks, Tag 0D5E]). There are a
field `k` and a family of curves `F` (Stacks 0D4Z: a flat, proper morphism of finite
presentation of relative dimension at most one, from an algebraic space over `Spec ℤ` to a
scheme) in a big fppf site, whose base is the affine line `A¹_k = Spec k[t]` and whose total space
is not isomorphic to the algebraic space of any scheme.

The construction is that of Stacks, Section 0D5D, with `k = ℂ`: `Y ⊆ ℙ²_{k[t]}` is the cubic
surface `T₀ ^ 3 + T₁ ^ 3 + T₂ ^ 3 - t T₀ T₁ T₂ = 0`, `y` a point of the central fibre `Y₀` with
property (2), `Z` the blowup of `Y` at `y` and `C ⊆ Z` the strict transform of `Y₀`; the total
space of `F` is Artin's contraction of `C` (Stacks 0GIB), read over `Spec ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_curveFamily_total_not_scheme :
    ∃ (k : Type) (_ : Field k) (B : BigFppfSite.{0}) (hZ : B.Contains integerBase)
      (F : AlgebraicGeometry.CurveFamily B hZ),
      Nonempty (F.base.left.obj ≅ Spec (CommRingCat.of (Polynomial k))) ∧
        ¬ ∃ V : BigFppfOver B integerBase hZ, Nonempty (F.total ≅ schemeSpace V)
declarations.comment: with k = ℂ: a family of curves over A¹_ℂ in the sense of Tag 0D4Z, Artin's contraction of the strict transform of the central fibre of the blown-up cubic surface, whose total space is not isomorphic to the algebraic space of any scheme

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.isTopologicalBasis_generateFrom
declarations.doc:
A collection `B` of subsets of `X` which covers `X` and which refines its own pairwise
intersections is a topological basis for the topology it generates. The intersection condition
requires that, for all `B₁, B₂ ∈ B` and `x ∈ B₁ ∩ B₂`, some `B₃ ∈ B` satisfies
`x ∈ B₃` and `B₃ ⊆ B₁ ∩ B₂`.
declarations.comment: existence

registrations.name: TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis.eq_generateFrom
registrations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: create_map_from_subcollection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D5Q.** Given a collection `B` of opens covering `X` such that every pairwise
intersection of members of `B` is a union of members of `B` contained in it, there is a continuous
map `f : X → Y` of topological spaces such that for `U ∈ B` the image `f '' U` is open,
`f ⁻¹' (f '' U) = U`, and the opens `f '' U` form a basis for the topology on `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem create_map_from_subcollection {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] (B : Set (Set X))
    (hB_open : ∀ U ∈ B, IsOpen U)
    (h_cover : ⋃₀ B = Set.univ)
    (h_inter : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ V ∈ B, U ∩ V = ⋃₀ {W ∈ B | W ⊆ U ∩ V}) :
    ∃ (Y : Type u) (τ : TopologicalSpace Y) (f : X → Y),
      @Continuous X Y _ τ f ∧
      (∀ U ∈ B, @IsOpen Y τ (f '' U)) ∧
      (∀ U ∈ B, f ⁻¹' (f '' U) = U) ∧
      @TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis Y τ ((fun U => f '' U) '' B)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_grothendieckTopology_costructuredArrow
declarations.doc:
Let `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` be sites, let `u : C ⥤ D` be cocontinuous and let
`V` be an object of `D`. Let `{}^u_V I = CostructuredArrow u V` be the category of pairs
`(U, ψ : u(U) ⟶ V)` of Section 00XF, with the two projections `j = CostructuredArrow.proj u V`,
`(U, ψ) ↦ U`, and `u' = CostructuredArrow.toOver u V`, `(U, ψ) ↦ (ψ : u(U) ⟶ V)`. Then the square
```
  {}^u_V I --j--> C
     |            |
     u'           u
     v            v
    D/V --j_V---> D
```
commutes, and declaring a sieve of `(U, ψ)` to be covering when its image under `j` is a covering
sieve of `U`:

1. this is a Grothendieck topology `H` on `{}^u_V I`, i.e. `{}^u_V I` is a site;
2. `j` is continuous and cocontinuous;
3. `u'` is cocontinuous;
4. the induced square of topoi commutes, `j_* ⋙ f_* ≅ f'_* ⋙ j_{V*}`, where `f` and `f'` are the
   morphisms of topoi of Stacks 00XO attached to the cocontinuous functors `u` and `u'`; and
5. `f'_* ∘ j⁻¹ = j_V⁻¹ ∘ f_*`, where the inverse images of the continuous and cocontinuous functors
   `j` and `j_V` are restriction (Stacks 00XR).
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_grothendieckTopology_costructuredArrow {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    (u : C ⥤ D) [u.IsCocontinuous J K] (V : D) :
    CostructuredArrow.proj u V ⋙ u = CostructuredArrow.toOver u V ⋙ Over.forget V ∧
      ∃ H : GrothendieckTopology (CostructuredArrow u V),
        (∀ (X : CostructuredArrow u V) (S : Sieve X),
            S ∈ H X ↔ Sieve.functorPushforward (CostructuredArrow.proj u V) S ∈ J X.left) ∧
          ∃ (_ : (CostructuredArrow.proj u V).IsContinuous H J) (_ :
            (CostructuredArrow.proj u V).IsCocontinuous H J) (_ :
            (CostructuredArrow.toOver u V).IsCocontinuous H (K.over V)),
            Nonempty
                ((CostructuredArrow.proj u V).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) H J ⋙
                    u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) J K ≅
                  (CostructuredArrow.toOver u V).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) H
                      (K.over V) ⋙
                    (Over.forget V).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) (K.over V) K) ∧
              Nonempty
                ((CostructuredArrow.proj u V).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u) H J ⋙
                    (CostructuredArrow.toOver u V).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) H
                      (K.over V) ≅
                  u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) J K ⋙
                    (Over.forget V).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u) (K.over V) K)
declarations.comment:
The site of pairs `(U, ψ : u(U) → V)` for a cocontinuous `u`: `j` is continuous and
  cocontinuous, `u'` is cocontinuous, the resulting square of topoi commutes and
  `f'_* j⁻¹ = j_V⁻¹ f_*`. For sheaves of sets on small sites.
