declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPushforwardComposition.isIso_derivedPushforwardComparison_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D5T.**  For composable morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` of ringed spaces, the
canonical comparison from a right derived pushforward along `f ≫ g` to the composite of right
derived pushforwards along `f` and `g` is an isomorphism.

No hypothesis beyond the two morphisms and the three derived functors: the condition
`PushforwardComputesDerived`, which `isIso_derivedPushforwardComparison_iff` shows to be
equivalent to this statement, is discharged by `pushforwardComputesDerived`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedPushforwardComparison_unconditional
    [Rf.IsRightDerivedFunctor αf
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves.{u} X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Rg.IsRightDerivedFunctor αg
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves.{u} Y) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Rgf.IsRightDerivedFunctor αgf
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves.{u} X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    IsIso (derivedPushforwardComparison f g Rf Rg Rgf αf αg αgf)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.OpenSubspace.cohomologyOnOpenIsoRestriction
declarations.doc:
Degree-`p` cohomology over an open agrees naturally with degree-`p` cohomology after
restriction to that open.  The component at `K` is the isomorphism
`H^p(U, K) ≅ H^p(U, K|_U)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def cohomologyOnOpenIsoRestriction {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u}) (U : Opens X)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} O)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wU} (SheafOfModules.{u} (resRing U O))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wG} AddCommGrpCat.{u}] (p : ℤ) :
    derivedSectionsOnOpen O U ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} p ≅
      derivedRestriction O U ⋙ derivedSectionsOnOpenSubspace O U ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} p
declarations.comment: `H^p(U, K) ≅ H^p(U, K|_U)`, natural in `K` in `D(O_X)`, for every open `U` of a ringed space `X` and every degree `p`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedSectionsLeray.isIso_lerayComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D5W, over an open.**  For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of ringed spaces and an open
`V ⊆ Y`, derived sections over `V` after derived pushforward along `f` agree with derived sections
over `f⁻¹ V`, as functors `D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(Γ(V, 𝒪_Y))`: the canonical Leray comparison is an
isomorphism, with no hypothesis on `f`.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_lerayComparison : IsIso (lerayComparison f V)
declarations.comment: over an open

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedSectionsLeray.isIso_lerayComparison_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D5W, global sections.**  `R Γ(Y, -) ∘ Rf_*` and `R Γ(X, -)` agree as functors
`D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y))`: the Leray comparison at `V = ⊤` is an isomorphism.  Its source is
derived sections over `f⁻¹ ⊤ = ⊤`, that is global derived sections on `X`, regarded as complexes
of `Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y)`-modules by restriction of scalars along `f^♯`.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_lerayComparison_top : IsIso (lerayComparison f ⊤)
declarations.comment: global sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedSectionsLeray.isIso_lerayComparison_top_and_forall_open
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D5W**, the whole lemma, stated for an arbitrary morphism of ringed spaces
`f : X ⟶ Y` with no further hypothesis.  The canonical Leray comparison
`RΓ(X, -) ⟶ RΓ(Y, -) ∘ Rf_*` of functors `D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y))` is an isomorphism, and more
generally for every open `V ⊆ Y` with `U = f⁻¹ V` the comparison
`RΓ(U, -) ⟶ RΓ(V, -) ∘ Rf_*` of functors `D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(Γ(V, 𝒪_Y))` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_lerayComparison_top_and_forall_open {X₀ Y₀ : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (g : X₀ ⟶ Y₀) :
    IsIso (lerayComparison g ⊤) ∧ ∀ W : Opens Y₀.carrier, IsIso (lerayComparison g W)
declarations.comment: both statements, for a morphism of ringed spaces: `RΓ(Y, -) ∘ Rf_* = RΓ(X, -)`, and `RΓ(U, -) = RΓ(V, -) ∘ Rf_*` for `V ⊆ Y` open and `U = f⁻¹ V`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.UnboundedHigherDirectImage.preimageCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
Cohomology over the inverse image `f⁻¹ V` agrees with cohomology over `V` after derived
pushforward: `H^i(f⁻¹ V, K) = H^i(V, Rf_* K)`, naturally in `K`.
declarations.statement:
def preimageCohomologyIso (V : Opens Y.carrier) (i : ℤ) :
    derivedPreimageSections f V ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing Y).obj.obj (op V))) i ≅
      derivedPushforward f ⋙ derivedSectionsOverOpen Y V ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing Y).obj.obj (op V))) i
declarations.comment: preimage formula

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.UnboundedHigherDirectImage.preimageCohomologyEvaluationIso
declarations.doc:
The value on an open `V ⊆ Y` of the presheaf `derivedPreimageCohomologyPresheaf` is the
hypercohomology `H^i(f⁻¹ V, K)` of `K` over the inverse image of `V`, naturally in `K`.
declarations.statement:
def preimageCohomologyEvaluationIso (V : Opens Y.carrier) (i : ℤ) :
    derivedPushforward f ⋙
        Stacks.Cohomology.HypercohomologyEdge.derivedSectionsPresheaf (structureSheafRing Y) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (PresheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y).obj) i ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.evaluation (structureSheafRing Y).obj (op V) ≅
      derivedPreimageSections f V ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing Y).obj.obj (op V))) i
declarations.comment: values on opens

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.UnboundedHigherDirectImage.higherDirectImageIsoSheafifyPreimageCohomology
declarations.doc:
The `i`-th cohomology sheaf of `Rf_* K` is the sheaf associated to the presheaf
`V ↦ H^i(f⁻¹ V, K)`, naturally in `K`.
declarations.statement:
def higherDirectImageIsoSheafifyPreimageCohomology (i : ℤ) :
    derivedPushforward f ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)) i ≅
      derivedPushforward f ⋙
        Stacks.Cohomology.HypercohomologyEdge.derivedSectionsPresheaf (structureSheafRing Y) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (PresheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y).obj) i ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 (structureSheafRing Y).obj)
declarations.comment: associated sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.UnderlyingAbelianSheaf.sectionsForgetComparison_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D5Y, part (1).** Unbounded derived sections of modules agree canonically and
naturally with derived sections after forgetting to abelian sheaves: for every open `U ⊆ X` the
canonical map `RΓ(U, K) ⟶ RΓ(U, K_ab)` is an isomorphism in `D(Ab)`.
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.UnderlyingAbelianPushforward.pushforwardForgetComparison_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D5Y, part (2).**  The unbounded derived pushforward of a complex of
`𝒪_X`-modules, with the module structure forgotten, agrees canonically and naturally with the
unbounded derived pushforward of the underlying complex of abelian sheaves:
`Rf_* K ⟶ Rf_*(K_ab)` is an isomorphism in `D(Ab_Y)`.

The morphism `f` of ringed spaces is the only argument: there is no `HasRightDerivedFunctor`
precondition here, both derived pushforwards being supplied by the proved instances
`abelianPushforward_hasRightDerivedFunctor` and
`isRightDerivedFunctor_pushforwardForgetSource` above.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforwardForgetComparison_isIso :
    IsIso (Stacks.Cohomology.UnderlyingAbelianPushforward.pushforwardForgetComparison f)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.isKInjective_modulePushforward_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D5Z.** If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a flat morphism of ringed spaces and `ℐ^•` is a
K-injective complex of `𝒪_X`-modules, then `f_* ℐ^•` is K-injective as a complex of
`𝒪_Y`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKInjective_modulePushforward_of_isFlat {X Y : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlat f)
    (I : CochainComplex (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ℤ)
    (hI : I.IsKInjective) :
    CochainComplex.IsKInjective
      (((modulePushforward f).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimitSections.isDerivedLimit_map_derivedSections
declarations.doc:
Derived sections over an open of a ringed space carry a countable derived inverse limit to a
derived inverse limit: `RΓ(U, R\lim Kₙ) = R\lim RΓ(U, Kₙ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_map_derivedSections
    (RGamma : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (comparison : (sections X U).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RGamma)
    (hRGamma : RGamma.IsRightDerivedFunctor comparison
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩]
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) (hL : IsDerivedLimit K L) :
    ∃ h : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦ RGamma.obj (K.obj ⟨n⟩)),
      @IsDerivedLimit (DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u}) _ _ _ _ _ _
        (K ⋙ RGamma) h (RGamma.obj L)
declarations.comment: commutation with derived limits

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimitSections.exists_shortExact_limOne_cohomology_derivedLimit
declarations.doc:
For every open `U` of a ringed space and every degree `m`, the cohomology of a countable
derived inverse limit lies in the Milnor short exact sequence

`0 ⟶ R¹\lim H^{m-1}(U, Kₙ) ⟶ H^m(U, R\lim Kₙ) ⟶ \lim H^m(U, Kₙ) ⟶ 0`.

Here `R¹\lim` is the cokernel of the difference map `1 - shift` on the product of the groups
`H^{m-1}(U, Kₙ)`. The map to the inverse limit is characterised by its composites with the limit
projections, which are the maps on cohomology induced by the given structural maps `L ⟶ Kₙ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExact_limOne_cohomology_derivedLimit
    (RGamma : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (comparison : (sections X U).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RGamma)
    (hRGamma : RGamma.IsRightDerivedFunctor comparison
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩]
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hL : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
            K.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))))
    (m : ℤ) :
    let Hprev := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (m - 1)
    let Hcur := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} m
    let Fprev := K ⋙ RGamma ⋙ Hprev
    let Fcur := K ⋙ RGamma ⋙ Hcur
    let dprev : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ Fprev.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ Fprev.obj ⟨n⟩) :=
      Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ Fprev.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ Fprev.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
            Fprev.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
    ∃ (i : cokernel dprev ⟶ Hcur.obj (RGamma.obj L))
      (q : Hcur.obj (RGamma.obj L) ⟶ limit Fcur) (zero : i ≫ q = 0),
      ((ShortComplex.mk i q zero).ShortExact ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, q ≫ limit.π Fcur ⟨n⟩ =
          Hcur.map (RGamma.map (p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n)))
declarations.comment: short exact sequence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.isDerivedLimit_map_derivedSectionsLocallySmall
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0D60], first assertion, for `RΓ(U, -)` at the locally small model.** If `K` is a
derived limit of an inverse system `(Kₙ)` in `D(𝒪_X)`, then `RΓ(U, K)` is a derived limit of the
system `(RΓ(U, Kₙ))` in `D(Γ(X, U))`; the existence of the product of the images is part of the
conclusion.

This is [Stacks, Tag 08U1]: `𝒪_X`-modules are Grothendieck abelian, `Γ(X, U)`-modules have exact
countable products, and sections over `U` preserve countable products, so the right derived
functor of sections carries a derived-limit triangle to a derived-limit triangle. The instances of
Tag 0D60 already in the library are stated either for `Ab`-valued derived sections over an open, or
for module-valued derived sections over the base ring at `HasDerivedCategory.standard`; this one is
`Γ(X, U)`-module valued at the locally small model, which is the model
`Stacks.Duality.Coherator.AffineAmplitudeIn` is set at.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_map_derivedSectionsLocallySmall (U : X.Opens)
    (L : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory X.Modules) [HasProduct fun n : ℕ => L.obj ⟨n⟩]
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hK : IsDerivedLimit L K) :
    ∃ h : HasProduct fun n : ℕ => (derivedSectionsLocallySmall X U).obj (L.obj ⟨n⟩),
      @IsDerivedLimit (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U))) _ _ _ _ _ _
        (L ⋙ derivedSectionsLocallySmall X U) h ((derivedSectionsLocallySmall X U).obj K)
declarations.comment: commutation with derived limits, for the Γ(X, U)-module valued derived sections over an open at the locally small model

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedSectionsOverBase.isDerivedLimit_map_derivedSectionsOver
declarations.doc:
**Derived sections over a base ring commute with derived limits.** If a distinguished triangle
exhibits `L` as the derived limit of a countable inverse system `(K_n)` of objects of `D(𝒪_X)`,
then `RΓ(X, L)` is the derived limit of the system `(RΓ(X, K_n))` in `D(A)`; the existence of the
product of the images is part of the conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_map_derivedSectionsOver
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (hL : IsDerivedLimit K L) :
    ∃ h : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦ (derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj (K.obj ⟨n⟩)),
      @IsDerivedLimit (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) _ _ _ _ _ _
        (K ⋙ derivedSectionsOver X ρ) h ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj L)
declarations.comment: commutation with derived limits, for derived sections over a base ring

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedSectionsOverBase.exists_shortExact_homology_derivedSectionsOver
declarations.doc:
**The Milnor short exact sequence for the cohomology of derived sections of a derived limit.**
With `L` the derived limit of `(K_n)` in `D(𝒪_X)`, the cohomology modules `Hʳ(X, L)` of its derived
sections over `A` fit into short exact sequences

`0 ⟶ R¹lim Hʳ⁻¹(X, K_n) ⟶ Hʳ(X, L) ⟶ lim Hʳ(X, K_n) ⟶ 0`,

where `R¹lim` is the cokernel of `1 - shift` on the product of the cohomologies. The inclusion
descends the connecting morphism of the Milnor triangle and the projection is characterized by the
limit projections.

The product of the images is taken as a hypothesis here, as it is in the general Milnor sequence;
`isDerivedLimit_map_derivedSectionsOver` provides it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExact_homology_derivedSectionsOver
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (hL : IsDerivedLimit K L) :
    let F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) := K ⋙ derivedSectionsOver X ρ
    let Y : ℕ → DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) := fun n ↦ F.obj (op n)
    let d : (∏ᶜ Y) ⟶ ∏ᶜ Y := Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
      Pi.π Y n - Pi.π Y (n + 1) ≫ F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
    ∃ (a : (derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj L ⟶ ∏ᶜ Y)
      (b : (∏ᶜ Y) ⟶ ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj L)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      let T := Triangle.mk a d b
      T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) ∧
        ∀ r : ℤ,
          let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) r
          let H₁ := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (r - 1)
          let homologySystem : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} A := F ⋙ H
          let shiftedHomologySystem : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} A := F ⋙ H₁
          let P : ModuleCat.{u} A :=
            ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ shiftedHomologySystem.obj (op n)
          let δ : P ⟶ P := Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ shiftedHomologySystem.obj (op n)) n -
              Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ shiftedHomologySystem.obj (op n)) (n + 1) ≫
                shiftedHomologySystem.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
          ∃ (e : H₁.obj (∏ᶜ Y) ≅ P)
            (i : cokernel δ ⟶ H.obj ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj L))
            (q : H.obj ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj L) ⟶ limit homologySystem)
            (w : i ≫ q = 0),
            e.hom = piComparison H₁ Y ∧
              cokernel.π δ ≫ i = e.inv ≫
                DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.δ T (r - 1) r ∧
              (∀ n : ℕ, q ≫ limit.π homologySystem (op n) =
                H.map a ≫ H.map (Pi.π Y n)) ∧
              (ShortComplex.mk i q w).ShortExact
declarations.comment: short exact sequence, for derived sections over a base ring; both maps normalized

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimits.isDerivedLimit_map_derivedSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D60, first assertion.** Derived sections over an open carry a countable derived
inverse limit to a derived inverse limit.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_map_derivedSections
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (U : Opens X.carrier)
    (RGamma : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (comparison :
      (SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheafRing X) ⋙
          (sheafSections (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
            (op U)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RGamma)
    (hRGamma : RGamma.IsRightDerivedFunctor comparison
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩]
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (hL : IsDerivedLimit K L) :
    ∃ h : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦ RGamma.obj (K.obj ⟨n⟩)),
      @IsDerivedLimit
        (DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u}) _ _ _ _ _ _
        (K ⋙ RGamma) h (RGamma.obj L)
declarations.comment: commutation with derived limits

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimits.exists_shortExact_limOne_cohomology_derivedLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D60, second assertion.** For every open `U` and degree `m`, the cohomology of a
derived inverse limit lies in the Milnor short exact sequence
`0 ⟶ R¹ lim Hᵐ⁻¹(U,Kₙ) ⟶ Hᵐ(U,R lim Kₙ) ⟶ lim Hᵐ(U,Kₙ) ⟶ 0`.

Here `R¹ lim` is represented by the cokernel of the standard difference map on the product of
the underlying cohomology groups. The last map is characterized by its composites with the
limit projections, which are induced by the structural maps `L ⟶ Kₙ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExact_limOne_cohomology_derivedLimit
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (U : Opens X.carrier)
    (RGamma : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (comparison :
      (SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheafRing X) ⋙
          (sheafSections (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
            (op U)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RGamma)
    (hRGamma : RGamma.IsRightDerivedFunctor comparison
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩]
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hL : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
            K.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))))
    (m : ℤ) :
    let A := AddCommGrpCat.{u}
    let Hprev := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A (m - 1)
    let Hcur := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A m
    let Fprev := K ⋙ RGamma ⋙ Hprev
    let Fcur := K ⋙ RGamma ⋙ Hcur
    let dprev := Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
      Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ Fprev.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ Fprev.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
          Fprev.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
    ∃ (i : cokernel dprev ⟶
        Hcur.obj (RGamma.obj L))
      (q : Hcur.obj (RGamma.obj L) ⟶ limit Fcur)
      (zero : i ≫ q = 0),
      ((ShortComplex.mk i q zero).ShortExact ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, q ≫ limit.π Fcur ⟨n⟩ =
          Hcur.map (RGamma.map (p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n)))
declarations.comment: short exact sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimitStalk.cohomology_derivedLimit_projection_mono_on_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D61.** A locally vanishing `R¹ lim` in degree `m - 1` and eventual
injectivity on cohomology in degree `m`, over a fundamental system of open neighbourhoods of `x`,
force the projection from a derived limit to the stage `n₀` to be injective on the stalk at `x`
of the degree-`m` cohomology sheaf.

Both numbered conditions of the source appear as binders, in the source's own position —
universally quantified over the members `U` of the fundamental system `𝔘`: `hlimOne` is
`R¹ lim Hᵐ⁻¹(U, Kₙ) = 0`, as the vanishing of the cokernel of the `1 - shift` endomorphism of the
product, and `hinj` is the injectivity of `Hᵐ(U, Kₙ) ⟶ Hᵐ(U, K_{n₀})` for `n ≥ n₀`. The source's
`n(x)` is `n₀` and its `𝔘ₓ` is `𝔘`, given here as arguments rather than existentially; the derived
limit `R lim Kₙ` is `L` together with `p` and `hL`, which say that `p` is the structural map of
the defining distinguished triangle, so `p ≫ Pi.π n₀` is the source's `R lim Kₙ ⟶ K_{n₀}` and not
an arbitrary map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cohomology_derivedLimit_projection_mono_on_stalk {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} O)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wP} (PresheafOfModules.{u} O.obj)]
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hL : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
            K.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)))
    (x : X) (m : ℤ) (n₀ : ℕ) (𝔘 : Set (Opens X))
    (hbasis : (nhds x).HasBasis (fun U : Opens X ↦ U ∈ 𝔘) (fun U ↦ (U : Set X)))
    (hlimOne : ∀ U ∈ 𝔘,
      let F := K ⋙ derivedSectionsPresheaf O ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (PresheafOfModules.{u} O.obj) (m - 1) ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.evaluation O.obj (Opposite.op U)
      IsZero (cokernel (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ F.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ F.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
            F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)))
    (hinj : ∀ U ∈ 𝔘,
      let F := K ⋙ derivedSectionsPresheaf O ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (PresheafOfModules.{u} O.obj) m ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.evaluation O.obj (Opposite.op U)
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : n₀ ≤ n), Mono (F.map (homOfLE hn).op)) :
    Mono ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} x).map
      ((SheafOfModules.forget O ⋙ PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf O.obj).map
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} O) m).map
          (p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n₀))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimitStalk.exists_and_forall_isIso_to_derivedLimit_truncGETower_of_local_vanishing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D62.** Let `E` be an object of the derived category of sheaves of
`𝒪_X`-modules on a ringed space, and suppose every point `x` carries a function `p(x, -)` and a
fundamental system `𝔘ₓ` of open neighbourhoods on whose members `Hᵖ(U, H^{m-p}(E))` vanishes
whenever `p > p(x, m)`. Then the tower of truncations `τ_{≥ -n} E` from below has a derived
limit `R lim τ_{≥ -n} E` with a canonical map of Remark 0H72 from `E`, and every such canonical
map to every derived limit of the tower is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_and_forall_isIso_to_derivedLimit_truncGETower_of_local_vanishing
    {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} O)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wP} (PresheafOfModules.{u} O.obj)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))
    (hvanishing : ∀ x : X, ∃ (pb : ℤ → ℤ) (𝔘 : Set (Opens X)),
      (nhds x).HasBasis (fun U : Opens X ↦ U ∈ 𝔘) (fun U ↦ (U : Set X)) ∧
        ∀ U ∈ 𝔘, ∀ (p : ℕ) (m : ℤ), pb m < (p : ℤ) →
          IsZero ((PresheafOfModules.evaluation O.obj (Opposite.op U)).obj
            (cohomologyPresheaf O
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} O) 0).obj
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} O)
                  (m - (p : ℤ))).obj E)) (p : ℤ)))) :
    (∃ (_ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦
        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩)
      (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (c : E ⟶ L)
      (pr : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩),
      (∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
          (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
        Triangle.mk pr (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
            (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n -
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
              (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
              (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).map
                (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ pr ≫ Pi.π
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n =
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-(n : ℤ))).app E)) ∧
    ∀ (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (c : E ⟶ L)
      (pr : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩),
      (∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
          (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
        Triangle.mk pr (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
            (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n -
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
              (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
              (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).map
                (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))) →
      (∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ pr ≫ Pi.π
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n =
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-(n : ℤ))).app E) →
      IsIso c
declarations.comment: the derived limit and the canonical map of Remark 0H72 exist, and every such canonical map is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimitStalk.isIso_to_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_of_local_bound
declarations.doc:
Let `E` be an object of the derived category of sheaves of `𝒪_X`-modules on a ringed space, and
suppose every point `x` carries an integer `dₓ ≥ 0` and a fundamental system `𝔘ₓ` of open
neighbourhoods on whose members `Hᵖ(U, Hᵠ(E))` vanishes whenever `p > dₓ` and `q < 0`. Then the
canonical map from `E` to a derived limit of its tower of truncations `τ_{≥ -n} E` from below is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_to_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_of_local_bound {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} O)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wP} (PresheafOfModules.{u} O.obj)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O))
    (hvanishing : ∀ x : X, ∃ (d : ℕ) (𝔘 : Set (Opens X)),
      (nhds x).HasBasis (fun U : Opens X ↦ U ∈ 𝔘) (fun U ↦ (U : Set X)) ∧
        ∀ U ∈ 𝔘, ∀ (p : ℕ) (q : ℤ), (d : ℤ) < (p : ℤ) → q < 0 →
          IsZero ((PresheafOfModules.evaluation O.obj (Opposite.op U)).obj
            (cohomologyPresheaf O
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} O) 0).obj
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} O) q).obj E))
              (p : ℤ))))
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (c : E ⟶ L)
    (pr : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
      (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hL : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk pr (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
          (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
            (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
            (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).map
              (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)))
    (hc : ∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ pr ≫ Pi.π
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n =
      (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-(n : ℤ))).app E) :
    IsIso c

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimitStalk.exists_and_forall_isIso_to_derivedLimit_truncGETower_of_dimension_bound
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D64.** Let `E` be an object of the derived category of sheaves of
`𝒪_X`-modules on a ringed space, and suppose there are an integer `d ≥ 0` and a basis `𝔅` for the
topology of `X` on whose members `Hᵖ(U, Hᵠ(E))` vanishes whenever `p > d` and `q < 0`. Then the

canonical map of Remark 0H72 from `E`, and every such canonical map to every derived limit of the
tower is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_and_forall_isIso_to_derivedLimit_truncGETower_of_dimension_bound
    {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} O)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wP} (PresheafOfModules.{u} O.obj)]

    (∃ (_ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦
        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩)
      (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (c : E ⟶ L)

          (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
        Triangle.mk pr (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
            (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n -

              (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫

        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-(n : ℤ))).app E)) ∧
    ∀ (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (c : E ⟶ L)
      (pr : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩),
      (∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦
          (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
        Triangle.mk pr (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
            (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n -
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦
              (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
              (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).map
                (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈

      (∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ pr ≫ Pi.π
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{u} O) E).obj ⟨n⟩) n =

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.UnboundedHigherDirectImage.isZero_homologyDerivedPushforward_of_isBasis
declarations.doc:
**Vanishing of the cohomology sheaves of `Rf_* K`.** If the degree-`i` hypercohomology
`H^i(f⁻¹ V, K)` vanishes for every `V` in a basis of the topology of `Y`, then the degree-`i`
cohomology sheaf of `Rf_* K` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_homologyDerivedPushforward_of_isBasis (i : ℤ)
    (hK : ∀ V ∈ B, IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing Y).obj.obj (op V))) i).obj
        ((derivedPreimageSections f V).obj K))) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)) i).obj
      ((derivedPushforward f).obj K))
declarations.comment: negative_sheaves

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.UnboundedHigherDirectImage.isZero_homologyDerivedPreimageSections_of_isBasis
declarations.doc:
**Negative hypercohomology over every inverse image.** If `H^i(f⁻¹ V, K) = 0` for `i < 0` and
every `V` in a basis of the topology of `Y`, then `H^i(f⁻¹ V, K) = 0` for `i < 0` and *every* open
`V ⊆ Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_homologyDerivedPreimageSections_of_isBasis
    (hK : ∀ V ∈ B, ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing Y).obj.obj (op V))) i).obj
        ((derivedPreimageSections f V).obj K)))
    (V : Opens Y.carrier) (i : ℤ) (hi : i < 0) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing Y).obj.obj (op V))) i).obj
        ((derivedPreimageSections f V).obj K))
declarations.comment: negative_hypercohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.UnboundedHigherDirectImage.isSheaf_zerothDerivedPreimageCohomologyPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**The rule `V ↦ H^0(f⁻¹ V, K)` is a sheaf.** If `H^i(f⁻¹ V, K) = 0` for `i < 0` and every `V`
in a basis of the topology of `Y`, then the presheaf of `𝒪_Y`-modules `V ↦ H^0(f⁻¹ V, K)` — that
is `derivedPreimageCohomologyPresheaf f K 0`, whose values are identified with `H^0(f⁻¹ V, K)` by
`preimageCohomologyEvaluationIso` — satisfies the sheaf condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_zerothDerivedPreimageCohomologyPresheaf
    (hK : ∀ V ∈ B, ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing Y).obj.obj (op V))) i).obj
        ((derivedPreimageSections f V).obj K))) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y.carrier)
      (derivedPreimageCohomologyPresheaf f K 0).presheaf
declarations.comment: zeroth_sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.UnboundedHigherDirectImage.subsingleton_shiftedHom_preimageRestrict_of_isBasis
declarations.doc:
**Negative `Ext` over every inverse image.** If `Ext^i(K|_{f⁻¹ V}, L|_{f⁻¹ V}) = 0` for
`i < 0` and every `V` in a basis of the topology of `Y`, then the same vanishing holds for `i < 0`
and *every* open `V ⊆ Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_shiftedHom_preimageRestrict_of_isBasis
    (hExt : ∀ V ∈ B, ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 →
      Subsingleton (ShiftedHom ((preimageRestrict f V).obj K)
        ((preimageRestrict f V).obj L) i))
    (V : Opens Y.carrier) (i : ℤ) (hi : i < 0) :
    Subsingleton (ShiftedHom ((preimageRestrict f V).obj K)
      ((preimageRestrict f V).obj L) i)
declarations.comment: hom_negative_ext

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.UnboundedHigherDirectImage.isSheaf_derivedPreimageHomPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**The rule `V ↦ Hom(K|_{f⁻¹ V}, L|_{f⁻¹ V})` is a sheaf.** If
`Ext^i(K|_{f⁻¹ V}, L|_{f⁻¹ V}) = 0` for `i < 0` and every `V` in a basis of the topology of `Y`,
then the presheaf of `𝒪_Y`-modules `V ↦ Hom(K|_{f⁻¹ V}, L|_{f⁻¹ V})` satisfies the sheaf
condition. Here the presheaf is `derivedPreimageCohomologyPresheaf f (RSheafHom(K, L)) 0`, whose
value on `V` is identified with `Hom(K|_{f⁻¹ V}, L|_{f⁻¹ V})` by
`derivedPreimageHomPresheafValueEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_derivedPreimageHomPresheaf
    (hExt : ∀ V ∈ B, ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 →
      Subsingleton (ShiftedHom ((preimageRestrict f V).obj K)
        ((preimageRestrict f V).obj L) i)) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y.carrier)
      (derivedPreimageCohomologyPresheaf f (homSheafObject X.sheaf K L) 0).presheaf
declarations.comment: hom_sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.LocallyGiven
declarations.doc:
A system of locally given derived objects on a ringed space.

The `restrictionComp` field is the canonical identification between direct restriction and
restriction in two steps. With this identification inserted, `cocycle` says exactly
`ρ W U = ρ W V ∘ (ρ V U)|_W`.
declarations.statement: structure LocallyGiven (X : RingedSpace.{u})

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.subsingleton_shiftedHom_self_of_covers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D68, the vanishing of negative self-Ext.** Let `(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space and
let `ℬ` be a collection of open subsets covering `X` such that the intersection of two members
of `ℬ` is the union of the members of `ℬ` contained in it. If `K` is an object of `D(𝒪_X)` with
`Ext^i(K|_U, K|_U) = 0` for `i < 0` and every `U ∈ ℬ`, then `Ext^i(K, K) = 0` for `i < 0`.

The members of `ℬ` need not form a basis; by Tag 0D5Q there is a continuous `f : X → Y` whose
images of the members of `ℬ` do form a basis of `Y` and satisfy `f⁻¹(f(U)) = U`, and Tag 0D66
part (2) applied to `f` with `𝒪_Y = f_* 𝒪_X` gives the vanishing over every open of `Y`,
including `⊤`.

Here `K` is an arbitrary object of `D(𝒪_X)` and `ℬ` an arbitrary collection;
`Stacks.DerivedGlueing.Solution.subsingleton_shiftedHom_self` is this statement applied to the
global object of a `Stacks.DerivedGlueing.Solution` of a system of locally given objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_shiftedHom_self_of_covers {X : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (ℬ : Set (Opens X.carrier)) (hcover : sSup ℬ = ⊤)
    (hinter : ∀ U ∈ ℬ, ∀ V ∈ ℬ, U ⊓ V = sSup {W | W ∈ ℬ ∧ W ≤ U ⊓ V})
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (hExt : ∀ U ∈ ℬ, ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 → Subsingleton (ShiftedHom
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (structureSheafRing X) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (structureSheafRing X) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj K) i))
    (i : ℤ) (hi : i < 0) :
    Subsingleton (ShiftedHom K K i)
declarations.comment:
the vanishing of negative self-Ext, for an arbitrary object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)`
  and an arbitrary collection of opens covering `X` with intersections covered by members, such
  that `K|_U` has no negative self-Ext for every member `U`

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.Solution.subsingleton_shiftedHom_self
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D68, the vanishing of negative self-Ext.** In Situation 0D67, suppose that the
displayed opens cover `X` and that the intersection of two of them is the union of the members
of the collection it contains, and that the prescribed local objects have no negative
self-Ext.  Then the global object of a solution has no negative self-Ext either.

The restrictions of the global object are the prescribed local objects, by
`Stacks.DerivedGlueing.Solution.restrictionIso`, so this is
`Stacks.DerivedGlueing.subsingleton_shiftedHom_self_of_covers` read through the equivalences
comparing the models of restriction of modules to an open.
declarations.statement:
theorem Solution.subsingleton_shiftedHom_self {S : LocallyGiven X} (A : Solution S)
    (hcover : sSup S.opens = ⊤)
    (hinter : ∀ U ∈ S.opens, ∀ V ∈ S.opens, U ⊓ V = sSup {W | W ∈ S.opens ∧ W ≤ U ⊓ V})
    (hExt : ∀ (U : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ S.opens), ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 →
      Subsingleton (ShiftedHom (S.obj U hU) (S.obj U hU) i))
    (i : ℤ) (hi : i < 0) :
    Subsingleton (ShiftedHom A.obj A.obj i)
declarations.comment: the vanishing of negative self-Ext of the global object of a solution

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_unique_solutionIso_of_covers_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**The uniqueness clause of [Stacks, Tag 0D68]**: in Situation 0D67, if
the displayed opens cover `X`, if the intersection of two of them is the union of the members of
the collection it contains, and if the prescribed local objects have no negative self-`Ext`, then
any two solutions are identified by exactly one isomorphism of solutions.

The three conditions are (1) and (2) of the tag, as in
`Stacks.DerivedGlueing.Solution.subsingleton_shiftedHom_self`, the tag's other clause.  The proof
applies `Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_unique_solutionIso_of_covers_of_coherence`, its coherence
input being `Stacks.DerivedGlueing.restrictHomBelow_eq_restrictDerivedHom`.

The conclusion `Stacks.DerivedGlueing.Solution.IsCompatibleHom A B ψ.hom` is by definition
`∀ (U : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ S.opens), (S.restriction U ⊤ le_top).map ψ.hom ≫
(B.rho U hU).hom = (A.rho U hU).hom`, which is the clause as the source states it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unique_solutionIso_of_covers_unconditional (S : LocallyGiven X)
    (hcover : sSup S.opens = ⊤)
    (hinter : ∀ U ∈ S.opens, ∀ V ∈ S.opens, U ⊓ V = sSup {W | W ∈ S.opens ∧ W ≤ U ⊓ V})
    (hExt : ∀ (U : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ S.opens), ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 →
      Subsingleton (ShiftedHom (S.obj U hU) (S.obj U hU) i))
    (A B : Solution S) :
    ∃! ψ : A.obj ≅ B.obj, A.IsCompatibleHom B ψ.hom
declarations.comment:
the uniqueness of a solution up to unique isomorphism, under the tag's conditions
  (1) and (2); the vanishing of negative self-Ext is `subsingleton_shiftedHom_self_of_covers` and
  `Solution.subsingleton_shiftedHom_self`

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_unique_overlapIso_of_covers
declarations.doc:
**The comparison isomorphism over an overlap.**  For members `U` and `V` of the collection
there is a unique isomorphism `ρ_{U,V} : K_U|_{U ∩ V} ≅ K_V|_{U ∩ V}` compatible with the
prescribed transitions on the members contained in `U ∩ V`.  Here `hinter` is hypothesis (1) of
[Stacks, Tag 0D68] and `hExt` is its hypothesis (2); the collection need not cover `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unique_overlapIso_of_covers (S : LocallyGiven X)
    (hinter : ∀ U ∈ S.opens, ∀ V ∈ S.opens, U ⊓ V = sSup {W | W ∈ S.opens ∧ W ≤ U ⊓ V})
    (hExt : ∀ (U : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ S.opens), ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 →
      Subsingleton (ShiftedHom (S.obj U hU) (S.obj U hU) i))
    (U V : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ S.opens) (hV : V ∈ S.opens) :
    ∃! φ : (S.restriction (U ⊓ V) U inf_le_left).obj (S.obj U hU) ≅
        (S.restriction (U ⊓ V) V inf_le_right).obj (S.obj V hV),
      IsOverlapHom S hU hV inf_le_left inf_le_right φ.hom
declarations.comment:
the comparison isomorphism over an overlap: for `U, V ∈ ℬ` a unique isomorphism
  `K_U|_{U ⊓ V} ≅ K_V|_{U ⊓ V}` compatible with the prescribed transitions on the members of `ℬ`
  contained in `U ⊓ V`, for a collection satisfying `hinter` (condition (1) of 0D68) and `hExt`
  (condition (2) of 0D68)

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.restrictOverlapHom_cocycle_of_covers
declarations.doc:
**The cocycle condition over a triple intersection.**  For members `U`, `V` and `W` and
compatible isomorphisms over the three overlaps, `ρ_{U,W} = ρ_{V,W} ∘ ρ_{U,V}` over `U ∩ V ∩ W`.
By `Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_unique_overlapIso_of_covers` the compatible isomorphisms over the
overlaps are unique.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictOverlapHom_cocycle_of_covers (S : LocallyGiven X)
    (hinter : ∀ U ∈ S.opens, ∀ V ∈ S.opens, U ⊓ V = sSup {W | W ∈ S.opens ∧ W ≤ U ⊓ V})
    (hExt : ∀ (U : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ S.opens), ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 →
      Subsingleton (ShiftedHom (S.obj U hU) (S.obj U hU) i))
    (U V W : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ S.opens) (hV : V ∈ S.opens) (hW : W ∈ S.opens)
    (φUV : (S.restriction (U ⊓ V) U inf_le_left).obj (S.obj U hU) ≅
      (S.restriction (U ⊓ V) V inf_le_right).obj (S.obj V hV))
    (hφUV : IsOverlapHom S hU hV inf_le_left inf_le_right φUV.hom)
    (φVW : (S.restriction (V ⊓ W) V inf_le_left).obj (S.obj V hV) ≅
      (S.restriction (V ⊓ W) W inf_le_right).obj (S.obj W hW))
    (hφVW : IsOverlapHom S hV hW inf_le_left inf_le_right φVW.hom)
    (φUW : (S.restriction (U ⊓ W) U inf_le_left).obj (S.obj U hU) ≅
      (S.restriction (U ⊓ W) W inf_le_right).obj (S.obj W hW))
    (hφUW : IsOverlapHom S hU hW inf_le_left inf_le_right φUW.hom) :
    restrictOverlapHom S hU hW inf_le_left inf_le_right
        (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left) inf_le_right : U ⊓ V ⊓ W ≤ U ⊓ W) φUW.hom =
      restrictOverlapHom S hU hV inf_le_left inf_le_right
          (inf_le_left : U ⊓ V ⊓ W ≤ U ⊓ V) φUV.hom ≫
        restrictOverlapHom S hV hW inf_le_left inf_le_right
          (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right) inf_le_right : U ⊓ V ⊓ W ≤ V ⊓ W) φVW.hom
declarations.comment:
the cocycle condition `ρ_{U,W} = ρ_{V,W} ∘ ρ_{U,V}` over a triple intersection,
  for any three compatible isomorphisms over the three overlaps -- which by
  `exists_unique_overlapIso_of_covers` are the source's own `ρ_{U,V}`, `ρ_{V,W}` and `ρ_{U,W}`,
  being the unique compatible ones -- for a collection satisfying `hinter` (condition (1) of
  0D68) and `hExt` (condition (2) of 0D68)

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.restrictedSystemOverInf_covers
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0D69], the restricted system covers the overlap.** The overlap of two members
is the union of the members of the restricted collection contained in it — which is condition
(1) of [Stacks, Tag 0D68] for the restricted system, read at `U ⊓ V`.  It is the condition that
intersections of members are unions of members, read at the pair `U, V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictedSystemOverInf_covers (S : LocallyGiven X)
    (hinter : ∀ U ∈ S.opens, ∀ V ∈ S.opens, U ⊓ V = sSup {W | W ∈ S.opens ∧ W ≤ U ⊓ V})
    (U V : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ S.opens) (hV : V ∈ S.opens) :
    U ⊓ V = sSup {W | W ∈ (restrictedSystemOverInf S U V).opens ∧ W ≤ U ⊓ V}
declarations.comment:
the restricted system covers the overlap: condition (1) of 0D68 for the
  subsystem on the members contained in `U ⊓ V`, from the condition that the intersection of two
  members is the union of the members contained in it

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.restrictedSystemOverInf_intersections_covered
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0D69], the restricted system's intersection condition.** The intersection of
two members of the restricted collection is the union of the members of the restricted
collection contained in it — condition (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0D68] for the restricted system, at
an arbitrary pair of its members.

The members of the restricted collection contained in `A ⊓ B` are exactly the members of the
whole collection contained in it, because `A ⊓ B ≤ A ≤ U ⊓ V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictedSystemOverInf_intersections_covered (S : LocallyGiven X)
    (hinter : ∀ U ∈ S.opens, ∀ V ∈ S.opens, U ⊓ V = sSup {W | W ∈ S.opens ∧ W ≤ U ⊓ V})
    (U V : Opens X.carrier) :
    ∀ A ∈ (restrictedSystemOverInf S U V).opens, ∀ B ∈ (restrictedSystemOverInf S U V).opens,
      A ⊓ B = sSup {W | W ∈ (restrictedSystemOverInf S U V).opens ∧ W ≤ A ⊓ B}
declarations.comment:
the restricted system's intersection condition: condition (1) of 0D68 for the
  subsystem on the members contained in `U ⊓ V`, at an arbitrary pair of its members

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.restrictedSystemOverInf_ext
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0D69], the restricted system's `Ext` condition.** The prescribed objects of
the restricted system have no negative self-`Ext`, since they are prescribed objects of the
whole system — condition (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0D68] for the restricted system.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictedSystemOverInf_ext (S : LocallyGiven X)
    (hExt : ∀ (W : Opens X.carrier) (hW : W ∈ S.opens), ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 →
      Subsingleton (ShiftedHom (S.obj W hW) (S.obj W hW) i))
    (U V : Opens X.carrier) :
    ∀ (W : Opens X.carrier) (hW : W ∈ (restrictedSystemOverInf S U V).opens), ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 →
      Subsingleton (ShiftedHom ((restrictedSystemOverInf S U V).obj W hW)
        ((restrictedSystemOverInf S U V).obj W hW) i)
declarations.comment:
the restricted system's `Ext` condition: condition (2) of 0D68 for the
  subsystem on the members contained in `U ⊓ V`, from the vanishing of negative self-`Ext` of
  the prescribed objects

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_solutionOver_inf
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0D69], both restrictions are solutions over the overlap.** The prescribed
object on a member is a solution over that member,
`Stacks.DerivedGlueing.selfSolutionOver`, and a solution over an open restricts to a solution
over a smaller one, `Stacks.DerivedGlueing.SolutionOver.restrictOpen`.  So `K_U|_{U ∩ V}` and
`K_V|_{U ∩ V}` are each a solution for the system over `U ∩ V`, and these are the two solutions
the source feeds to the uniqueness clause of [Stacks, Tag 0D68].  This holds for all
`U, V ∈ ℬ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_solutionOver_inf (S : LocallyGiven X) (U V : Opens X.carrier)
    (hU : U ∈ S.opens) (hV : V ∈ S.opens) :
    (∃ A : SolutionOver S (U ⊓ V),
        A.obj = (S.restriction (U ⊓ V) U inf_le_left).obj (S.obj U hU)) ∧
      ∃ B : SolutionOver S (U ⊓ V),
        B.obj = (S.restriction (U ⊓ V) V inf_le_right).obj (S.obj V hV)
declarations.comment:
the two restricted objects are solutions over the overlap: `K_U|_{U ∩ V}` and
  `K_V|_{U ∩ V}` are each a solution for the system over `U ∩ V`, for every `U, V ∈ ℬ`

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_solution_of_finite_cover_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0D6A], existence.**
In Situation 0D67, suppose that `X = U_1 ∪ … ∪ U_n` with the `U_i` in the displayed collection,
that the intersection of two members of the collection is the union of the members contained in
it, and that the prescribed objects have no negative self-`Ext`.  Then the system has a solution.

The proof applies `Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_solution_of_finite_cover_of_homs`; the sheaf
condition of [Stacks, Tag 0D66] part (2) for every subsystem is
`Stacks.DerivedGlueing.hasGluingForHomsOver_of_covers`, a theorem with no binder beyond the
system.  The nonemptiness `hs` of the cover is
used here: the induction of `Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_solutionOver_finsetSup` runs on
`Finset.Nonempty.cons_induction` and starts from a single member.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_solution_of_finite_cover_unconditional (S : LocallyGiven X)
    (s : Finset (Opens X.carrier)) (hs : s.Nonempty) (hmem : ∀ U ∈ s, U ∈ S.opens)
    (hcover : s.sup id = ⊤)
    (hinter : ∀ U ∈ S.opens, ∀ V ∈ S.opens, U ⊓ V = sSup {W | W ∈ S.opens ∧ W ≤ U ⊓ V})
    (hExt : ∀ (U : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ S.opens), ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 →
      Subsingleton (ShiftedHom (S.obj U hU) (S.obj U hU) i)) :
    Nonempty (Solution S)
declarations.comment:
existence: for X = U_1 ∪ … ∪ U_n with U_i in the collection, intersections of
  members covered by members, and no negative self-Ext of the prescribed objects, the system has
  a solution

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_solution_and_unique_solutionIso_of_finite_cover_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0D6A] in full**: under the conditions (1), (2) and (3) of the tag the
system has a solution, and any two solutions are identified by exactly one isomorphism of
solutions.

Both clauses of the tag in one statement, the existence clause above together with the
uniqueness clause of [Stacks, Tag 0D68] over the finite cover.  The conclusion
`Stacks.DerivedGlueing.Solution.IsCompatibleHom A B ψ.hom` is by definition
`∀ (U : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ S.opens), (S.restriction U ⊤ le_top).map ψ.hom ≫
(B.rho U hU).hom = (A.rho U hU).hom`, which is "compatible with the `ρ_U`" as the source means
it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_solution_and_unique_solutionIso_of_finite_cover_unconditional (S : LocallyGiven X)
    (s : Finset (Opens X.carrier)) (hs : s.Nonempty) (hmem : ∀ U ∈ s, U ∈ S.opens)
    (hcover : s.sup id = ⊤)
    (hinter : ∀ U ∈ S.opens, ∀ V ∈ S.opens, U ⊓ V = sSup {W | W ∈ S.opens ∧ W ≤ U ⊓ V})
    (hExt : ∀ (U : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ S.opens), ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 →
      Subsingleton (ShiftedHom (S.obj U hU) (S.obj U hU) i)) :
    Nonempty (Solution S) ∧
      ∀ A B : Solution S, ∃! ψ : A.obj ≅ B.obj, A.IsCompatibleHom B ψ.hom
declarations.comment:
the whole tag: for X = U_1 ∪ … ∪ U_n with U_i in the collection, intersections
  of members covered by members, and no negative self-Ext of the prescribed objects, a solution
  exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_solution_of_top_mem
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0D6A] when the cover has a single member.** If the whole of `X` belongs to
the collection, then the system has a solution: the prescribed object on `⊤` is one.

This is the case `n = 1` of the tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_solution_of_top_mem (S : LocallyGiven X) (htop : ⊤ ∈ S.opens) :
    Nonempty (Solution S)
declarations.comment: existence when a single member of the collection is all of X

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_unique_solutionIso_of_top_mem
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0D6A] when the cover has a single member: uniqueness up to unique
isomorphism.** If the whole of `X` belongs to the collection, then any two solutions are
identified by exactly one isomorphism of solutions.

This is the case `n = 1` of the tag: restriction from `⊤` to `⊤` is the identity functor, by
`Stacks.DerivedGlueing.restrictionSelfIso`, so the identifications over `⊤` of the two solutions
compose to the required isomorphism and determine it; and compatibility over `⊤` forces
compatibility over every member, by `Stacks.DerivedGlueing.Solution.isCompatibleHom_of_top`.

Together with `Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_solution_of_top_mem` this is the whole of Tag 0D6A
for `n = 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unique_solutionIso_of_top_mem (S : LocallyGiven X) (htop : ⊤ ∈ S.opens)
    (A B : Solution S) :
    ∃! φ : A.obj ≅ B.obj, A.IsCompatibleHom B φ.hom
declarations.comment:
uniqueness up to unique isomorphism when a single member of the collection is all
  of X, the case n = 1

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_glueing_of_wellOrderedCover
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0D6B].** Let `X` be a ringed space, let `E` be a well ordered set and let
`X = ⋃_{α ∈ E} W_α` be an open covering with `W_α ⊆ W_{α+1}` and `W_α = ⋃_{β < α} W_β` when `α`
is not a successor.  Let `K_α` be an object of `D(𝒪_{W_α})` with `Ext^i(K_α, K_α) = 0` for
`i < 0`, and let `ρ^α_β : K_α|_{W_β} ≅ K_β` for `β < α` satisfy
`ρ^α_γ = ρ^β_γ ∘ ρ^α_β|_{W_γ}` for `γ < β < α`.  Then there is an object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)` and
isomorphisms `K|_{W_α} ≅ K_α` compatible with the `ρ^α_β`.

"`β` is the immediate predecessor of `α`" is rendered as "`β < α` and every `γ < α` satisfies
`γ ≤ β`", so `hsucc` is the inclusion `W_α ⊆ W_{α+1}` and `hlimit` the continuity at the stages
that are not successors; `Stacks.DerivedGlueing.le_of_succ_of_limit` derives from them the
inclusion `W_β ⊆ W_α` for every `β < α` along which the transitions are stated.

The system `S : Stacks.DerivedGlueing.LocallyGiven X` (the structure of
`StacksFrontier/Topology/Sheaves/Cohomology/DerivedCategory/LocallyGivenObjects.lean`, not
`RingedSite.LocallyGiven`) is exactly Situation 0D67 and carries no further data: its restriction
functors `S.restriction V U` are the canonical derived restrictions `j^*` along the inclusions
`V ⊆ U`, since the field `restrictionFactors` identifies each with the derived functor of the
restriction of complexes `openModuleRestriction` through the localization, and its comparisons
`S.restrictionComp` are the canonical ones, by the field `restrictionCompFactors`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_glueing_of_wellOrderedCover (S : Stacks.DerivedGlueing.LocallyGiven X)
    (E : Type v) [LinearOrder E] [WellFoundedLT E]
    (W : E → Opens X.carrier)
    (hsucc : ∀ β α : E, β < α → (∀ γ : E, γ < α → γ ≤ β) → W β ≤ W α)
    (hlimit : ∀ α : E, (¬ ∃ β : E, β < α ∧ ∀ γ : E, γ < α → γ ≤ β) →
      W α = ⨆ (β : E) (_ : β < α), W β)
    (hcover : (⨆ α : E, W α) = ⊤) (K : ∀ α : E, OpenDerivedCategory X (W α))
    (hExt : ∀ (α : E) (i : ℤ), i < 0 → Subsingleton (ShiftedHom (K α) (K α) i))
    (rho : ∀ (β α : E) (h : β < α),
      (S.restriction (W β) (W α) (le_of_succ_of_limit W hsucc hlimit β α h)).obj (K α) ≅ K β)
    (hcocycle : ∀ (γ β α : E) (hγβ : γ < β) (hβα : β < α),
      (rho γ α (hγβ.trans hβα)).hom =
        (S.restrictionComp (W γ) (W β) (W α) (le_of_succ_of_limit W hsucc hlimit γ β hγβ)
            (le_of_succ_of_limit W hsucc hlimit β α hβα)).hom.app (K α) ≫
          (S.restriction (W γ) (W β)
            (le_of_succ_of_limit W hsucc hlimit γ β hγβ)).map (rho β α hβα).hom ≫
            (rho γ β hγβ).hom) :
    ∃ (G : OpenDerivedCategory X ⊤)
      (sigma : ∀ α : E, (S.restriction (W α) ⊤ le_top).obj G ≅ K α),
      ∀ (β α : E) (h : β < α),
        (S.restrictionComp (W β) (W α) ⊤
              (le_of_succ_of_limit W hsucc hlimit β α h) le_top).hom.app G ≫
            (S.restriction (W β) (W α)
              (le_of_succ_of_limit W hsucc hlimit β α h)).map (sigma α).hom ≫ (rho β α h).hom =
          (sigma β).hom
declarations.comment:
the glued object `G` over `⊤` with identifications `sigma α` of its restrictions
  with the `K α`, compatible with the prescribed `ρ^α_β` for every `β < α`, for a well ordered
  covering with `hsucc` (`W_α ⊆ W_{α+1}`), `hlimit` (continuity at the stages that are not
  successors), `hcover`, `hExt` (no negative self-Ext) and the cocycle condition `hcocycle`

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedGlueing.exists_solution_and_unique_solutionIso_of_covers_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0D6C] (BBD gluing lemma).** In Situation 0D67 suppose that the members of the
collection cover `X`, that for two members `U, V` the intersection `U ∩ V` is the union of the
members contained in it, and that `Ext^i(K_U, K_U) = 0` for `i < 0` and every member `U`.  Then
the system has a solution, and any two solutions are identified by exactly one isomorphism of
solutions.

A solution is a `Stacks.DerivedGlueing.Solution`: an object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)` with isomorphisms
`ρ_U : K|_U ≅ K_U` satisfying `ρ^U_V ∘ ρ_U|_V = ρ_V`.  The conclusion
`Stacks.DerivedGlueing.Solution.IsCompatibleHom A B ψ.hom` says that `ψ` is compatible with the
`ρ_U` of the two solutions.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_solution_and_unique_solutionIso_of_covers_unconditional (S : LocallyGiven X)
    (hcover : sSup S.opens = ⊤)
    (hinter : ∀ U ∈ S.opens, ∀ V ∈ S.opens, U ⊓ V = sSup {W | W ∈ S.opens ∧ W ≤ U ⊓ V})
    (hExt : ∀ (U : Opens X.carrier) (hU : U ∈ S.opens), ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 →
      Subsingleton (ShiftedHom (S.obj U hU) (S.obj U hU) i)) :
    Nonempty (Solution S) ∧
      ∀ A B : Solution S, ∃! ψ : A.obj ≅ B.obj, A.IsCompatibleHom B ψ.hom
declarations.comment:
existence of a solution `(K, ρ_U)` and its uniqueness up to unique isomorphism,
  for a collection satisfying (1) `hcover`, (2) `hinter` and (3) `hExt`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isIso_derivedTransitionCompComparison
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison from the composite of the derived pullbacks along the transitions
of `ψ` and `φ` to the derived pullback along the transition of `ψ ≫ φ` is an isomorphism, so
`Lf_ψ^* ∘ Lf_φ^* = Lf_{ψ ≫ φ}^*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTransitionCompComparison {l m n : SimplexCategory} (ψ : l ⟶ m)
    (φ : m ⟶ n) :
    IsIso (S.derivedTransitionCompComparison O ψ φ)
declarations.comment: for the transition morphisms of a simplicial-site situation

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.derivedTransitionCompIso
declarations.doc:
The natural isomorphism `Lf_ψ^* ⋙ Lf_φ^* ≅ Lf_{ψ ≫ φ}^*` given by the canonical
comparison.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedTransitionCompIso {l m n : SimplexCategory} (ψ : l ⟶ m) (φ : m ⟶ n) :
    S.derivedTransitionPullback O ψ ⋙ S.derivedTransitionPullback O φ ≅
      S.derivedTransitionPullback O (ψ ≫ φ)
declarations.comment:
for the transition morphisms of a simplicial-site situation, as a natural
isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackCompositionOfToposHom.isIso_derivedPullbackCompComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D6D.** For composable morphisms of ringed topoi `f` and `g`, the canonical
comparison from the composite of the derived pullbacks to the derived pullback along `g ∘ f` is
an isomorphism, so `Lf^* ∘ Lg^* = L(g ∘ f)^*`.

There is no hypothesis: the geometric datum is the two-field morphism of ringed topoi of
Stacks 01D3, part (2), with no continuous functor between underlying sites and no
morphism-of-sites condition. Both functors are left derived functors of degreewise pullback
along `g ∘ f`, and a map between left derived functors induced by the universal property is
invertible exactly then.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedPullbackCompComparison :
    IsIso (derivedPullbackCompComparison f g)
declarations.comment:
for a morphism of ringed topoi whose geometric datum is a morphism of the
underlying topoi rather than a continuous functor between the underlying sites, with no
morphism-of-sites hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackCompositionOfToposHom.derivedPullbackCompIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D6D as a natural isomorphism** `Lg^* ⋙ Lf^* ≅ L(g ∘ f)^*`, for morphisms of
ringed topoi and with no hypothesis, obtained by inverting the canonical comparison.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPullbackCompIso :
    derivedPullback g ⋙ derivedPullback f ≅ derivedPullback (g.comp f)
declarations.comment:
as a natural isomorphism, for a morphism of ringed topoi whose geometric datum
is a morphism of the underlying topoi rather than a continuous functor between the underlying
sites, with no morphism-of-sites hypothesis

Both functors are left derived functors of degreewise pullback along `g ∘ f`, and a map between

declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedPullbackCompComparison :

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackCompositionOnTopoi.derivedPullbackCompIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D6D as a natural isomorphism** `Lg^* ⋙ Lf^* ≅ L(g ∘ f)^*`, obtained by inverting
