declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D6Z.** An augmentation of a simplicial site towards `(D, K)`. In case (A) it is
a morphism of sites represented by a continuous functor in the opposite direction; in case (B)
it is represented by a cocontinuous functor. In either case its composite with a vertex functor
is independent of the chosen vertex.
declarations.statement:
def Augmentation (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u}) (D : Cat.{u, u})
    (K : GrothendieckTopology D) : Type u

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.componentAugmentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D70, part (1).** The morphism of topoi from the sheaves on the component in
simplicial degree `n` to the sheaves on the augmentation site, obtained by composing the
degree-zero morphism of the augmentation with the transition morphism of a vertex.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def componentAugmentation (n : SimplexCategory) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (Sheaf (S.componentTopology n) (Type u)) (Sheaf K (Type u))
declarations.comment: part (1): the morphisms of topoi of the components

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.transitionPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D70, compatibility (1).** Composing the direct image of a simplicial transition
with the direct image of the component augmentation of its target agrees canonically with the
direct image of the component augmentation of its source.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def transitionPushforwardIso {m n : SimplexCategory} (φ : m ⟶ n) :
    (S.transitionMorphism φ).pushforward ⋙
        (componentAugmentation S D K a m).pushforward ≅
      (componentAugmentation S D K a n).pushforward
declarations.comment: compatibility (1): composition with a simplicial transition

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.totalPushforwardForkIsLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D70, compatibility (3).** For a sheaf `F` on the total site, the direct image
`a_* F` along the total augmentation is the equalizer of the two maps
`a_{0,*} F_0 ⟶ a_{1,*} F_1` attached to the two maps `[0] ⟶ [1]`.
declarations.statement:
def totalPushforwardForkIsLimit (F : Sheaf S.totalTopology (Type u)) :
    IsLimit (totalPushforwardFork S D K a F)
declarations.comment: compatibility (3): the total direct image is the equalizer

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.totalMorphismOfTopoi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D70, part (2).** The morphism of topoi from the sheaves on the total site to the
sheaves on the augmentation site induced by an augmentation: its inverse image is the descent of
the inverse images along the component augmentations, its direct image is the limit of the
cosimplicial sheaf of their direct images, and the two are adjoint.
declarations.statement:
def totalMorphismOfTopoi :
    MorphismOfTopoi (Sheaf S.totalTopology (Type u)) (Sheaf K (Type u))
declarations.comment: part (2): the morphism of topoi of the total site

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.totalMorphismOfTopoi_componentMorphism_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D70, compatibility (2), in inverse images.** The inverse image of the total
augmentation followed by the inverse image of the morphism of topoi which Stacks 09WG attaches
to the simplicial degree `n` is the inverse image of the augmentation of that degree: the
augmentation of a simplicial degree is the total augmentation composed with that morphism.
declarations.comment: compatibility (2): composition with a component inclusion

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.componentRingedTopos_restrictionIso
declarations.doc:
The inverse image of sheaves of commutative rings along the component morphism of topoi is
canonically and naturally isomorphic to restriction along the component inclusion.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def componentRingedTopos_restrictionIso (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u})
    (n : SimplexCategory) :
    inverseImageCommRingFunctor (J := S.componentTopology n) (K := S.totalTopology)
        (componentMorphism S n) ≅
      (componentFunctor S n).sheafPushforwardContinuous CommRingCat.{u}
        (S.componentTopology n) S.totalTopology
declarations.comment: component_ringed_topos

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.componentRingedTopos_restrictionIso_forget
declarations.doc:
The restriction isomorphism is the canonical comparison of Stacks 09WG after forgetting the
ring operations. In particular its scalar map is not an arbitrary natural automorphism of
restriction.
declarations.statement:
theorem componentRingedTopos_restrictionIso_forget (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u})
    (n : SimplexCategory) (O : Sheaf S.totalTopology CommRingCat.{u}) :
    (sheafCompose (S.componentTopology n) (forget CommRingCat.{u})).map
        ((componentRingedTopos_restrictionIso S n).hom.app O) =
      (inverseImageCommRingForgetIso (S.componentTopology n)
          (componentMorphism S n)).hom.app O ≫
        ((componentFunctor S n).sheafPullbackCocontinuousIsoSheafPushforwardContinuous
          (Type u) (S.componentTopology n) S.totalTopology).hom.app
          ((sheafCompose S.totalTopology (forget CommRingCat.{u})).obj O)
declarations.comment: component_ringed_topos

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.componentRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism of ringed topoi from a simplicial component to the total site. Its
structure map is the adjoint of the comparison `gₙ⁻¹O ⟶ Oₙ` of structure sheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def componentRingedToposHom (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u})
    (O : Sheaf S.totalTopology CommRingCat.{u}) (n : SimplexCategory) :
    RingedToposHom (componentRingedTopos S O n) (totalRingedTopos S O)
declarations.comment: component_ringed_topos

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.componentRingedToposHom_toToposHom
declarations.doc: The underlying geometric morphism is the component morphism of Stacks 09WG.
declarations.statement:
theorem componentRingedToposHom_toToposHom (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u})
    (O : Sheaf S.totalTopology CommRingCat.{u}) (n : SimplexCategory) :
    (componentRingedToposHom S O n).toToposHom = componentMorphism S n
declarations.comment: component_ringed_topos

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.moduleSumFormulaLegEq
declarations.doc:
**The leg equation of Stacks 0D72 (6) in every simplicial-site situation.** For every simplex
map `φ : [n] ⟶ [m]` the `φ`th summand inclusion of the componentwise direct-sum formula for
sheaves of modules, followed by the inverse of that formula, is the canonical map attached to
`φ`. In case (A) of Stacks 09WE this is
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSite.moduleSumFormulaLegEq_situation`, and in case (B) it is
`CategoryTheory.CocontinuousSimplicialSite.moduleSumFormulaLegEqB`.
declarations.statement: theorem moduleSumFormulaLegEq : S.ModuleSumFormulaLegEq O
declarations.comment: the summand inclusions of the direct-sum formula on sheaves of modules are the canonical maps f_φ^*G ⟶ g_m^*g_{n!}G, in Situation 09WE (both cases)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.componentRingedToposHom_fSharpInverseImageRing_ringSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**The inverse-image form of the structure map of `g_n` on underlying sheaves of sets is the
comparison of Stacks 09WG.** The structure map is recorded through the adjunction for sheaves of
commutative rings and used through the adjunction for sheaves of rings; the two agree on
underlying sheaves of sets, where the first is Stacks 09WG by construction of the component
ringed topos.
declarations.statement:
theorem componentRingedToposHom_fSharpInverseImageRing_ringSheafMap :
    (sheafCompose (S.componentTopology n) (forget RingCat.{u})).map
        (componentRingedToposHom S O n).fSharpInverseImageRing =
      (componentRingedTopos_setRestrictionIso S n).hom.app
        ((sheafCompose S.totalTopology (forget CommRingCat.{u})).obj O)
declarations.comment: the structure map of the component morphism on underlying sheaves of sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.componentPullbackModulesRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D72: the pullback of sheaves of modules to a simplicial component is the literal
restriction.** The two presentations of restriction to the degree-`n` component that this
development carries — pullback of modules along the component morphism of ringed topoi, and
restriction of sections along the component inclusion — are canonically isomorphic.
declarations.comment: the pullback of modules along g_n is restriction to the component

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.componentPullbackModulesRestrictionIso_underlying
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D72 on underlying sheaves of sets is Stacks 09WG.** Read through the identification
of the underlying sheaf of a pullback of modules with an inverse image, the comparison of
Stacks 0D72 between the pullback of sheaves of modules along the component morphism of ringed
topoi and the literal restriction to the component is the comparison of Stacks 09WG between the
inverse image of sheaves of sets and restriction along the component inclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem componentPullbackModulesRestrictionIso_underlying
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (S.totalRingSheaf O)) :
    (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pullbackUnderlyingIsoOfIsIso
          (componentRingedToposHom S O n)).inv.app M ≫
        (Sheaf.moduleSheafFunctor
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (S.componentRingedTopos O n).O)).map
          ((componentPullbackModulesRestrictionIso S O n).hom.app M) =
      (componentRingedTopos_setRestrictionIso S n).hom.app
        (Sheaf.moduleSheaf.{u, u, u} (S.totalRingSheaf O) M)
declarations.comment:
the comparison of the two presentations of restriction, on underlying sheaves of
sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.componentPullbackComplexRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D72 on cochain complexes.** Degreewise pullback of complexes of modules along the
component morphism of ringed topoi is degreewise restriction to the component.
declarations.statement:
def componentPullbackComplexRestrictionIso :
    Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.pullbackComplexFunctor
        (X := S.componentRingedTopos O n) (Y := S.totalRingedTopos O)
        (componentRingedToposHom S O n).toModulesHom ≅
      S.componentModulesRestrictionComplex O n
declarations.comment: degreewise pullback of complexes along g_n is degreewise restriction

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.componentModuleLowerShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D72.** The defining adjunction `g_{n!} ⊣ g_n^*` of lower shriek of modules on a
simplicial component, exhibiting the left adjoint `g_{n!}` of `g_n^*` whose existence the tag
asserts.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def componentModuleLowerShriekAdjunction :
    componentModuleLowerShriek S O n ⊣ componentModuleRestriction S O n
declarations.comment: existence of the left adjoint g_{n!} of g_n^* on modules

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSite.componentModuleSumFormulaA
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D72, the componentwise direct-sum formula for sheaves of modules in case (A).**
The restriction to simplicial degree `m` of lower shriek `g_{n!}` of sheaves of `O`-modules from
degree `n` is the direct sum, over the simplex maps `φ : [n] ⟶ [m]`, of the pullbacks `f_φ^*` of
sheaves of modules along the transitions, each taken along the ring map `O(φ)`.
declarations.statement:
def componentModuleSumFormulaA (n m : SimplexCategory) :
    (∐ fun φ : n ⟶ m => transitionModulePullbackA C O φ) ≅
      (situation C).componentModuleLowerShriek O n ⋙
        (situation C).componentModuleRestriction O m
declarations.comment: direct-sum formula in case (A), on sheaves of modules

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CocontinuousSimplicialSite.componentModuleSumFormulaB
declarations.doc:
**The componentwise direct-sum formula for sheaves of modules in case (B).** The restriction
to simplicial degree `m` of lower shriek `g_{n!}` of sheaves of `O`-modules from degree `n` is the
direct sum, over the simplex maps `φ : [n] ⟶ [m]`, of the pullbacks `f_φ^*` of sheaves of modules
along the transitions.
declarations.statement:
def componentModuleSumFormulaB :
    (∐ fun φ : n ⟶ m => transitionModulePullbackB C P n m φ) ≅
      (situation C).componentModuleLowerShriek (totalRingSheafB C P) n ⋙
        (situation C).componentModuleRestriction (totalRingSheafB C P) m
declarations.comment: direct-sum formula in case (B), on sheaves of modules

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.moduleSumFormula
declarations.doc:
**The componentwise direct-sum formula of Stacks 0D72 (6) for sheaves of modules**, for an
arbitrary simplicial-site situation and in the summand spelling Stacks 0D74 consumes: the
restriction to degree `m` of lower shriek from degree `n` is the direct sum, over the simplex maps
`φ : [n] ⟶ [m]`, of the pullbacks of sheaves of modules along the transition morphisms of ringed
topoi.

A situation is one of the two cases of Stacks 09WE, and the formula is proved in each:
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSite.moduleSumFormulaA` in case (A), where the transitions are
morphisms of sites, and `CategoryTheory.CocontinuousSimplicialSite.moduleSumFormulaB` in case
(B), where they are cocontinuous functors.
declarations.statement:
def moduleSumFormula : ∀ (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u})
    (P : Sheaf S.totalTopology CommRingCat.{u}) (n : SimplexCategory), S.ModuleSumFormula' P n
declarations.comment: direct-sum formula on sheaves of modules, in Situation 09WE (both cases)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.ComponentModuleSumFormula.colimitPullbackRestrictionIsoCoproduct
declarations.doc:
The restriction to simplicial degree `m` of the presheaf-level module lower shriek from degree
`n` is, as a functor, the direct sum over the simplex maps `φ : [n] ⟶ [m]` of the presheaf-level
module pullbacks `f_φ^*` along the transitions, the summand labelled `φ` being the pullback along
the transition of `φ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def colimitPullbackRestrictionIsoCoproduct :
    Stacks.PullbackColimit.colimitPullback (Grothendieck.ι C.underlying (op n)) R ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.pushforward₀OfCommRingCat
          (Grothendieck.ι C.underlying (op m)) R ≅
      ∐ fun φ : n ⟶ m => transitionPullbackPresheafModules C R φ
declarations.comment: direct-sum formula in case (B), on presheaves of modules

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.componentRingedToposHom_fSharpInverseImage
declarations.doc:
The structure map of the canonical morphism from a simplicial component to the total ringed
topos is, in inverse-image form, the comparison of structure sheaves of Stacks 0D72.
declarations.statement:
theorem componentRingedToposHom_fSharpInverseImage (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u})
    (O : Sheaf S.totalTopology CommRingCat.{u}) (n : SimplexCategory) :
    (componentRingedToposHom S O n).fSharpInverseImage =
      (componentRingedTopos_restrictionIso S n).hom.app O
declarations.comment: the structure map of the component morphism, in inverse-image form

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isTotallyAcyclic_component_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D73.** Let `O` be a sheaf of rings on the total site of a
simplicial-site situation and let `I` be an injective sheaf of `O`-modules. The abelian sheaf
underlying the restriction `I_n` of `I` to the degree-`n` simplicial component is totally
acyclic: its cohomology over every sheaf of sets on `C_n` vanishes in every positive degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTotallyAcyclic_component_of_injective
    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (S.componentTopology n) AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf S.totalTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    (O : Sheaf S.totalTopology RingCat.{u}) (I : SheafOfModules.{u} O) [Injective I] :
    IsTotallyAcyclic.{u} (S.componentTopology n)
      ((S.restrictAb n).obj ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf O).obj I))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isTotallyAcyclic_componentModule_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0D73**, with the conclusion read on the restricted sheaf of modules.
The restriction of an injective sheaf of `O`-modules to the degree-`n` simplicial component —
reindexing the sections and restricting the scalars along the identity of the restricted sheaf
of rings — has totally acyclic underlying abelian sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTotallyAcyclic_componentModule_of_injective
    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (S.componentTopology n) AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf S.totalTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    (O : Sheaf S.totalTopology RingCat.{u}) (I : SheafOfModules.{u} O) [Injective I] :
    IsTotallyAcyclic.{u} (S.componentTopology n)
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj
        ((SheafOfModules.pushforward (F := componentFunctor S n)
          (𝟙 (((componentFunctor S n).sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{u}
            (S.componentTopology n) S.totalTopology).obj O))).obj I))
declarations.comment:
the conclusion read on the restricted sheaf of modules rather than on the
  restriction of the underlying abelian sheaf

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.exactFunctor_componentModuleLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D74.** Lower shriek `g_{n!}` of sheaves of modules from the degree-`n` simplicial
component is exact as soon as every structure-sheaf transition `f_φ⁻¹O_n ⟶ O_m` out of degree `n`
is flat.

Right exactness is formal. For left exactness: the restrictions to the components detect finite
limits, the componentwise direct-sum formula of Stacks 0D72
(`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.moduleSumFormula`) presents the restriction of `g_{n!}`
to degree `m` as the direct sum over the finitely many simplex maps `[n] ⟶ [m]` of the transition
pullbacks, hence as their product, and each of those is left exact by Stacks 04JC. This is
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.exactFunctor_componentModuleLowerShriek'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exactFunctor_componentModuleLowerShriek
    (hflat : ∀ (m : SimplexCategory) (φ : n ⟶ m), (S.transitionRingedToposHom P φ).IsFlat) :
    exactFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (S.componentRingSheaf
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := S.totalTopology)) P) n))
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := S.totalTopology)) P))
      (S.componentModuleLowerShriek
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := S.totalTopology)) P) n)
declarations.comment: with the componentwise direct-sum formula of Tag 0D72 proved in either case of 09WE

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.exactFunctor_componentModuleLowerShriek'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D74.** Lower shriek `g_{n!}` of sheaves of modules from the degree-`n` simplicial
component is exact as soon as every structure-sheaf transition `f_φ⁻¹O_n ⟶ O_m` out of degree `n`
is flat.

Right exactness is formal. For left exactness: the restrictions to the components detect finite
limits, the componentwise direct-sum formula of Stacks 0D72 presents the restriction of `g_{n!}`
to degree `m` as the direct sum over the finitely many simplex maps `[n] ⟶ [m]` of the transition
pullbacks, hence as their product, and each of those is left exact by Stacks 04JC.
declarations.statement:
theorem exactFunctor_componentModuleLowerShriek'
    (hflat : ∀ (m : SimplexCategory) (φ : n ⟶ m), (S.transitionRingedToposHom P φ).IsFlat) :
    exactFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (S.componentRingSheaf
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := S.totalTopology) P)) n))
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := S.totalTopology) P)))
      (S.componentModuleLowerShriek
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := S.totalTopology) P)) n)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.injective_componentModuleRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D75.** Let `O` be a sheaf of rings on the total site whose structure-sheaf
transitions `f_φ⁻¹O_n ⟶ O_m` out of degree `n` are flat. An injective sheaf of `O`-modules
restricts to an injective sheaf of `O_n`-modules on the degree-`n` simplicial component.

Restriction is right adjoint to `g_{n!}`, which is exact by Stacks 0D74, so Homology 015Z
applies; the componentwise direct-sum formula of Tag 0D72 that Stacks 0D74 starts from is
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.moduleSumFormula`.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_componentModuleRestriction
    (hflat : ∀ (m : SimplexCategory) (φ : n ⟶ m), (S.transitionRingedToposHom P φ).IsFlat)
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := S.totalTopology)) P))
    [Injective I] :
    Injective ((S.componentModuleRestriction
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := S.totalTopology)) P) n).obj I)
declarations.comment: with the componentwise direct-sum formula of Tag 0D72 proved in either case of 09WE

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.injective_componentModuleRestriction'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D75.** Let `O` be a sheaf of rings on the total site whose structure-sheaf
transitions `f_φ⁻¹O_n ⟶ O_m` out of degree `n` are flat. An injective sheaf of `O`-modules
restricts to an injective sheaf of `O_n`-modules on the degree-`n` simplicial component.

Restriction is right adjoint to `g_{n!}`, which is exact by Stacks 0D74, so Homology 015Z
applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_componentModuleRestriction'
    (hflat : ∀ (m : SimplexCategory) (φ : n ⟶ m), (S.transitionRingedToposHom P φ).IsFlat)
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := S.totalTopology) P))) [Injective I] :
    Injective ((S.componentModuleRestriction
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := S.totalTopology) P)) n).obj I)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cechSectionsComplex
declarations.doc:
The canonical complex `Γ(C_0, F_0) → Γ(C_1, F_1) → Γ(C_2, F_2) → …` of an abelian sheaf `F`
on the total site of a simplicial site, functorially in `F`. Its augmentation by `Γ(C_total, F)`
is `cechSectionsAugmentation`.
declarations.statement: def cechSectionsComplex : Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u} ⥤ CochainComplex Ab.{u} ℕ
declarations.comment: the canonical complex

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cechSectionsAugmentation
declarations.doc:
The augmentation `Γ(C_total, F) → Γ(C_0, F_0)` of the canonical complex, natural in the
abelian sheaf `F`. It is the canonical restriction of a global section to
simplicial degree zero; see `cechSectionsAugmentation_eq`.
declarations.statement:
def cechSectionsAugmentation :
    Sheaf.Γ S.totalTopology Ab.{u} ⟶ S.componentSectionsFunctor ⦋0⦌
declarations.comment: the augmentation

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cechSectionsAugmentation_app_mono
declarations.doc:
Exactness in degree `-1`: the augmentation `Γ(C_total, F) → Γ(C_0, F_0)` of the canonical
complex is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechSectionsAugmentation_app_mono (F : Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) :
    Mono ((S.cechSectionsAugmentation).app F)
declarations.comment: exactness in degree -1

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cechSectionsAugmentation_app_injective
declarations.doc:
Exactness in degree `-1`, concretely: the augmentation `Γ(C_total, F) → Γ(C_0, F_0)` of the
canonical complex is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechSectionsAugmentation_app_injective (F : Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) :
    Function.Injective ((S.cechSectionsAugmentation).app F)
declarations.comment: exactness in degree -1

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cechSectionsComplex_exactAt_of_injective
declarations.doc:
Exactness in positive degrees for an injective sheaf: if `F` is an injective abelian sheaf on
the total site, the canonical complex `Γ(C_0, F_0) → Γ(C_1, F_1) → Γ(C_2, F_2) → …` is exact at
`Γ(C_n, F_n)` for every `n > 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechSectionsComplex_exactAt_of_injective (F : Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u})
    [Injective F] (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    ((S.cechSectionsComplex).obj F).ExactAt n
declarations.comment: exactness in positive degrees for an injective sheaf

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cechSectionsComplex_shortComplexZero_exact
declarations.doc:
Exactness in degree `0`: the sequence `Γ(C_total, F) → Γ(C_0, F_0) → Γ(C_1, F_1)` is exact
at `Γ(C_0, F_0)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechSectionsComplex_shortComplexZero_exact (F : Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) :
    (ShortComplex.mk ((S.cechSectionsAugmentation).app F)
      (((S.cechSectionsComplex).obj F).d 0 1)
      (S.cechSectionsAugmentation_comp_d F)).Exact
declarations.comment: exactness in degree 0

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.resolution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D78.** The exact complex
`… ⟶ g_{1!}(a_1⁻¹𝒢) ⟶ g_{0!}(a_0⁻¹𝒢) ⟶ a⁻¹𝒢 ⟶ 0`
of abelian sheaves on the total site: the alternating-face complex of the simplex-coefficient
resolution of `a⁻¹𝒢`, whose degree-`n` term is the extension by zero `g_{n!}(a_n⁻¹𝒢)`.
declarations.statement: def resolution : Resolution S D K a G

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.augmentedCechComplex_exactAt_zero
declarations.doc:
Exactness in degree `-1`: the complex

`0 ⟶ a_*F ⟶ a_{0,*}F_0 ⟶ a_{1,*}F_1 ⟶ …`

is exact at `a_*F`, which is Lean degree `0` because the augmentation shifts the complex by
one.
declarations.statement: theorem augmentedCechComplex_exactAt_zero : (augmentedCechComplex S D K a F).ExactAt 0
declarations.comment: exactness in degree -1

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.augmentedCechComplex_exactAt_one
declarations.doc:
Exactness in degree `0`: the complex

`0 ⟶ a_*F ⟶ a_{0,*}F_0 ⟶ a_{1,*}F_1 ⟶ …`

is exact at `a_{0,*}F_0`, which is Lean degree `1` because the augmentation shifts the complex by
one.
declarations.statement: theorem augmentedCechComplex_exactAt_one : (augmentedCechComplex S D K a F).ExactAt 1
declarations.comment: exactness in degree 0

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.augmentedCechComplex_exactAt_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D79**, exactness in every degree for an injective abelian sheaf: the complex

`0 ⟶ a_*F ⟶ a_{0,*}F_0 ⟶ a_{1,*}F_1 ⟶ a_{2,*}F_2 ⟶ …`

is exact at every term when `F` is an injective abelian sheaf on the total site. Degrees `0` and
`1` — the source's degrees `-1` and `0` — hold for every `F` and are
`augmentedCechComplex_exactAt_zero` and `augmentedCechComplex_exactAt_one`. Above them the
argument is the source's: a complex of abelian sheaves is exact at a term as soon as `Hom(𝒢, -)`
of it is exact for every `𝒢`, each term of this complex is a right adjoint whose left adjoint is
the corresponding term of the resolution of Stacks 0D78, the mate of each cosimplicial transition
is the corresponding structure map of that resolution, and `Hom(-, F)` of the resolution is exact
because `F` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem augmentedCechComplex_exactAt_of_injective (F : Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u})
    [Injective F] (k : ℕ) : (augmentedCechComplex S D K a F).ExactAt k
declarations.comment: exactness in every degree for an injective abelian sheaf

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.higherDirectImageSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7A.** For an augmentation `a` of a simplicial-site situation towards a site
`(D, K)` and `M` in `D⁺(C_total)` there is a spectral sequence

`E_1^{p,q} = R^q a_{p,*} M_p  ⇒  R^{p+q} a_* M`,

functorial in `M`. It is the spectral sequence of the double complex `A^{q,p} = a_{p,*} I^q_p` of
a bounded below complex of injectives `I^•` representing `M`, filtered by the simplicial
degree.
declarations.statement: def higherDirectImageSpectralSequence : HigherDirectImageSpectralSequence S D K a

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.RingedAugmentation.nonempty_moduleResolution
declarations.doc:
With the notation of Stacks 0D9D, for a sheaf of `O_D`-modules `G` there is an exact complex

`… ⟶ g_{2!}(a_2^*G) ⟶ g_{1!}(a_1^*G) ⟶ g_{0!}(a_0^*G) ⟶ a^*G ⟶ 0`

of sheaves of `O`-modules on the total site, with `g_{n!}` the lower shriek of Stacks 0D72: a
chain complex whose degree-`n` term is `g_{n!}(a_n^*G)`, whose differentials are the alternating
sums of the face maps of a simplicial structure on its terms, augmented onto `a^*G`, exact in
every positive degree and at the augmentation, the augmentation being an epimorphism.
declarations.statement: alias nonempty_moduleResolution

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.RingedAugmentation.nonempty_moduleResolution_of_iso_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7C.** With the notation of Stacks 0D9D, for a sheaf of `O_D`-modules `G` the
lower shriek images `g_{n!}(a_n^*G)` of Stacks 0D72 carry an exact complex

`… ⟶ g_{2!}(a_2^*G) ⟶ g_{1!}(a_1^*G) ⟶ g_{0!}(a_0^*G) ⟶ a^*G ⟶ 0`

of sheaves of `O`-modules on the total site, with differentials the alternating sums of the
canonical face maps. The complex is `simplexModuleResolution`, the simplex-coefficient
resolution of `a^*G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_moduleResolution_of_iso_unit
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf A.OD)) :
    Nonempty (A.ModuleResolution G)
declarations.comment: for an arbitrary coefficient module, by the simplex-coefficient resolution

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.RingedAugmentation.moduleCechComplex_spec
declarations.doc:
With the notation of Stacks 0D9D, let `F` be a sheaf of `O`-modules on the
total site. The canonical complex of `O_D`-modules

`0 ⟶ a_*F ⟶ a_{0,*}F_0 ⟶ a_{1,*}F_1 ⟶ a_{2,*}F_2 ⟶ …`

(`moduleCechComplex`, with `a_*F` in degree `0` and `a_{n,*}F_n` in degree `n + 1`) is exact in
degrees `-1` and `0` (the Lean degrees `0` and `1`). If `F` is an injective `O`-module, the
complex is exact in all degrees and remains exact on applying `Hom_{O_D}(G, -)` for any
`O_D`-module `G`.

The complex is the source's: its differentials are the transposes, along the adjunctions
`a^* ⊣ a_*` and `g_{n!}a_n^* ⊣ a_{n,*}g_n^*`, of the augmentation and of the differentials of the
resolution `… ⟶ g_{1!}(a_1^*G) ⟶ g_{0!}(a_0^*G) ⟶ a^*G ⟶ 0` of Stacks 0D7C
(`homEquiv_cechAug`, `homEquiv_cechD`), so `Hom(G, -)` of it is `Hom(-, F)` of that resolution;
`Hom(-, F)` is left exact, and exact when `F` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleCechComplex_spec :
    (A.moduleCechComplex F).X 0 = A.totalRingedHom.pushforwardModules.obj F ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, (A.moduleCechComplex F).X (n + 1) =
      (A.componentRingedHom ⦋n⦌).pushforwardModules.obj
        ((S.componentModulesRestriction A.O ⦋n⦌).obj F)) ∧
    (A.moduleCechComplex F).ExactAt 0 ∧ (A.moduleCechComplex F).ExactAt 1 ∧
    (Injective F →
      (∀ k : ℕ, (A.moduleCechComplex F).ExactAt k) ∧
      ∀ (G : A.augmentationRingedTopos.Modules) (k : ℕ),
        (((preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (op G)).mapHomologicalComplex _).obj
          (A.moduleCechComplex F)).ExactAt k)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.SimplicialModuleResolution.exists_sectionsSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7E.** In Situation 09WE let `O` be a sheaf of rings on the total site. For `K` in
`D⁺(O)` there is a spectral sequence `(E_r, d_r)`, functorial in `K` and presented from its first
page, with

`E_1^{p,q} = H^q(C_p, K_p),  d_1^{p,q} : E_1^{p,q} → E_1^{p+1,q}`

converging to `H^{p+q}(C_total, K)`. Here `K_p = g_p^* K` is the restriction of `K` to the
component `C_p` (Stacks 0D72), `H^q(C_p, -)` is the cohomology of `RΓ(C_p, -)` on `D⁺(O_p)` and
`H^n(C_total, -)` that of `RΓ(C_total, -)` on `D⁺(O)`, global sections of a sheaf of modules
being those of its underlying abelian sheaf. The identification of the first page is natural in
`K`, and the first page vanishes in the negative columns.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_sectionsSpectralSequence :
    ∃ E : DerivedCategory.Plus (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ⥤
        CohomologicalSpectralSequence AddCommGrpCat.{u} 1,
      (∀ (p : ℕ) (q : ℤ), Nonempty (E ⋙
          CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.pageFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} _ 1 1 le_rfl ⋙
            HomologicalComplex.eval AddCommGrpCat.{u} _ ((p : ℤ), q) ≅
        (componentModuleRestriction S O ⦋p⦌).mapDerivedCategoryPlus ⋙
          (SheafOfModules.toSheaf (componentRingSheaf S O ⦋p⦌) ⋙
            Sheaf.Γ (S.componentTopology ⦋p⦌) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
            DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} q)) ∧
      (∀ (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (SheafOfModules.{u} O)) (p q : ℤ), p < 0 →
        IsZero (((E.obj K).page 1 le_rfl).X (p, q))) ∧
      ∀ K : DerivedCategory.Plus (SheafOfModules.{u} O),
        CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.AbutsTo (E.obj K)
          (fun n => (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} n).obj
            ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf O ⋙
              Sheaf.Γ S.totalTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj K))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.RingedAugmentation.higherDirectImageSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7F.** With the notation of Stacks 0D9D (a ringed augmentation `A` of a
simplicial-site situation towards a ringed site `(D, K, O_D)`), for `M` in `D⁺(O)` there is a
spectral sequence `(E_r, d_r)` in `Mod(O_D)`, presented from its first page and functorial in
`M`, with

`E_1^{p,q} = R^q a_{p,*} M_p  ⇒  R^{p+q} a_* M`.

Here `M_p` is the restriction of `M` to the component `C_p` (Stacks 0D72), `R^q a_{p,*}` the
cohomology of the right derived direct image along `a_p = a ∘ g_p` and `R^n a_*` that of the
right derived direct image along `a`. The identification of the first page is natural in `M`,
and the first page vanishes in the negative columns.

It is the spectral sequence of the double complex `A^{p,q} = a_{p,*} I^q_p` of a bounded below
complex of injectives `I^•` representing `M`, whose horizontal maps are those of the complex of
Stacks 0D7D, filtered by `p`.
declarations.statement: def higherDirectImageSpectralSequence : A.HigherDirectImageSpectralSequence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.RingedAugmentation.isCartesianDerivedModule_derivedPullbackModules
declarations.doc:
Let `E` be an object of `D(O_D)`. Then the derived pullback `La^*E` along the ringed
augmentation of Stacks 0D9D is a cartesian object of `D(O)`: every derived transition
`Lf_φ^*(La^*E)_m ⟶ (La^*E)_n` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianDerivedModule_derivedPullbackModules
    (E : DerivedCategory A.augmentationRingedTopos.Modules) :
    S.IsCartesianDerivedModule A.O (A.derivedPullbackModules.obj E)
declarations.comment: part (4)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.isCartesian_pullbacks
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesian_pullbacks (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u}) (D : Cat.{u, u})
    (K : GrothendieckTopology D) (a : Augmentation S D K) :
    ((∀ G : Sheaf K (Type u),
        IsCartesianSheaf S ((totalMorphismOfTopoi S D K a).inverseImage.obj G)) ∧
      ∀ G : Sheaf K Ab.{u}, IsCartesianAbSheaf S ((totalInverseImageAb S D K a).obj G)) ∧
    (∀ E : DerivedCategory (Sheaf K AddCommGrpCat.{u}),
      S.IsCartesianDerived ((derivedTotalInverseImage S D K a).obj E)) ∧
    (∀ (A : RingedAugmentation S D K a)
      (F : SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := A.augmentationRingedTopos.J)
          A.augmentationRingedTopos.O))),
      S.IsModuleFiberTransitionIso A.O (A.totalRingedHom.toModulesHom.pullbackModules.obj F)) ∧
    ∀ (A : RingedAugmentation S D K a) (E : DerivedCategory A.augmentationRingedTopos.Modules),
      S.IsCartesianDerivedModule A.O (A.derivedPullbackModules.obj E)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.RingedAugmentation.isCartesianModule_pullbackModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7H (3).** The pullback `a^*F` of a sheaf of `O_D`-modules along the ringed
augmentation of Stacks 0D9D is a cartesian sheaf of `O`-modules on the total site: every
transition `f_φ^*(a^*F)_m ⟶ (a^*F)_n` of sheaves of modules is invertible.

The transition is the compositor of Stacks 03D8 followed by the transformation of pullbacks
induced by the 2-morphism `g_n ⟶ g_m ∘ f_φ`, and that transformation is invertible after the
pullback along the ringed augmentation by
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.RingedAugmentation.isIso_whiskerLeft_pullbackModulesMap`,
which rests on Stacks 0D7H (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianModule_pullbackModules
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf A.augmentationRingedTopos.O)) :
    S.IsModuleFiberTransitionIso A.O ((A.totalRingedHom.toModulesHom.pullbackModules).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.isCartesianSheaf_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
The inverse image along the total augmentation of a sheaf of sets on the augmentation site is
a cartesian sheaf on the total site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianSheaf_inverseImage (G : Sheaf K (Type u)) :
    IsCartesianSheaf S ((inverseImage S D K a).obj G)
declarations.comment: part (1), sheaves of sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.isCartesianAbSheaf_totalInverseImageAb
declarations.doc:
The inverse image along the total augmentation of an abelian sheaf on the augmentation site
is a cartesian abelian sheaf on the total site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianAbSheaf_totalInverseImageAb (G : Sheaf K Ab.{u}) :
    IsCartesianAbSheaf S ((totalInverseImageAb S D K a).obj G)
declarations.comment: part (1), sheaves of abelian groups

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.isCartesianDerived_derivedTotalInverseImage
declarations.doc:
For an object `E` of the derived category of abelian sheaves on the augmentation site, the
derived inverse image `a⁻¹E` is a cartesian object of the derived category of abelian sheaves on
the total site.

It suffices that every cohomology sheaf of `a⁻¹E` be cartesian
(`isCartesianDerived_iff_forall_isCartesianAbSheaf_homology'`); those cohomology sheaves are the
inverse images of the cohomology sheaves of `E`, since `a⁻¹` is exact, and the inverse image of
an abelian sheaf along the augmentation is cartesian (`isCartesianAbSheaf_totalInverseImageAb`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianDerived_derivedTotalInverseImage
    (E : DerivedCategory (Sheaf K AddCommGrpCat.{u})) :
    S.IsCartesianDerived ((derivedTotalInverseImage S D K a).obj E)
declarations.comment: part (2), the derived inverse image of an object of D(D) is cartesian

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cartesianAbSheafEquivCartesianAbPair
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7I.** The category of cartesian sheaves of abelian groups on the total site of a
simplicial-site situation is equivalent to the category of pairs `(ℱ, α)` consisting of a sheaf of
abelian groups `ℱ` on the degree-zero component and an isomorphism
`α : (f_{δ¹₁})⁻¹ℱ ≅ (f_{δ¹₀})⁻¹ℱ` of sheaves of abelian groups on the degree-one component
satisfying the cocycle condition `(f_{δ²₁})⁻¹α = (f_{δ²₀})⁻¹α ∘ (f_{δ²₂})⁻¹α` on the degree-two
component.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cartesianAbSheafEquivCartesianAbPair :
    CartesianAbSheaf S ≌ CartesianAbPair S
declarations.comment: sheaves of abelian groups

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cartesianSheafEquivCartesianPair
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7I.** The category of cartesian sheaves of sets on the total site of a
simplicial-site situation is equivalent to the category of pairs `(ℱ, α)` consisting of a sheaf
of sets `ℱ` on the degree-zero component and an isomorphism `α : (f_{δ¹₁})⁻¹ℱ ≅ (f_{δ¹₀})⁻¹ℱ` of
sheaves on the degree-one component satisfying the cocycle condition
`(f_{δ²₁})⁻¹α = (f_{δ²₀})⁻¹α ∘ (f_{δ²₂})⁻¹α` on the degree-two component.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def cartesianSheafEquivCartesianPair : CartesianSheaf S ≌ CartesianPair S
declarations.comment: sheaves of sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isCartesianAbSheaf_weakSerre_colimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7J (1).** The cartesian abelian sheaves on the total site of a simplicial site form
a weak Serre subcategory of all abelian sheaves there, and colimits of systems of cartesian abelian
sheaves are cartesian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianAbSheaf_weakSerre_colimits (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u}) :
    ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass (IsCartesianAbSheaf S) ∧
      ∀ (J : Type*) [Category* J],
        ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (IsCartesianAbSheaf S) J
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isCartesianModule_isWeakSerreClass
declarations.doc:
Let `O` be a sheaf of rings on the total site of a simplicial site such that the pullback of
sheaves of modules along the transition morphism of every face map is left exact. Then the
cartesian `O`-modules form a weak Serre subcategory of `Mod(O)`.

By Stacks 07TG (3) it is enough to test the face maps, which is why only the face transitions
occur in the hypothesis; at a face the conditions are the zero module, which is cartesian with
no hypothesis, and the four lemma applied to the transition read as a natural transformation of
the two restriction functors.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianModule_isWeakSerreClass
    (hflat : ∀ (k : ℕ) (i : Fin (k + 2)),
      PreservesFiniteLimits
        ((S.transitionRingedToposHom O (SimplexCategory.δ i)).toModulesHom.pullbackModules)) :
    ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass (IsCartesianModule S O)
declarations.comment:
part (2), cartesian modules are a weak Serre subcategory of Mod(O). The
hypothesis is left exactness of the pullback of sheaves of modules along the transition morphism
of each face map, which for a flat face transition is Stacks 04JC and is weaker than flatness of
the face transitions, so the statement is more general than the source's; the implementation
notes record why flatness itself cannot be fed in at this pullback. NOT covered here: the second
sentence of part (2), that colimits of systems of cartesian O-modules are cartesian, for which
the argument needs restriction of modules to a component to preserve colimits of arbitrary shape
and this development has only the finite case

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isCartesianModule_weakSerre_colimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7J (2).** Let `O` be a sheaf of rings on the total site of a simplicial site such
that the morphisms of ringed topoi `f_{δ^n_j} : (Sh(C_n), O_n) ⟶ (Sh(C_{n-1}), O_{n-1})` are
flat. Then the cartesian `O`-modules form a weak Serre subcategory of `Mod(O)`, and colimits of
systems of cartesian `O`-modules are cartesian.

Flatness of a face transition makes its pullback of modules exact (Stacks 04JC), which is what
the four lemma consumes; the colimit statement holds with no hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianModule_weakSerre_colimits
    (flat : ∀ (k : ℕ) (i : Fin (k + 2)),
      (S.transitionRingedToposHom O (SimplexCategory.δ i)).IsFlat) :
    ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass (IsCartesianModule S O) ∧
      ∀ (J : Type*) [Category* J] [Small.{u} J],
        ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (IsCartesianModule S O) J
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cartesianModuleSheafAbelian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7K, corrected form.** If the morphisms of ringed topoi `f_{δ¹₁}` and `f_{δ¹₀}` are
flat, and so is one of the three degree-two faces `f_{δ²₀}`, `f_{δ²₁}`, `f_{δ²₂}`, then the
cartesian `O`-modules form an abelian category, with the additive structure of `Mod(O)`; its
cokernels are those of `Mod(O)`, and its kernels are those of the pairs of Stacks 07TH, computed
in degree zero.

The source asserts this under flatness of `f_{δ¹₁}` and `f_{δ¹₀}` alone, which is false: see
`CategoryTheory.PointSimplicialSite.RatioCounterexample.exists_not_abelian_cartesianModuleSheaf`.
The kernel of a morphism of pairs carries the restricted comparison isomorphism, but its cocycle
condition lives on the degree-two component; it can be cancelled against the pullback of the
kernel inclusion to the vertex `2` (through `δ²₁` or `δ²₀`) or to the vertex `0` (through `δ²₁`
or `δ²₂`), which is a monomorphism as soon as one degree-two face is flat.
declarations.statement:
abbrev cartesianModuleSheafAbelian
    (h₁ : (S.transitionRingedToposHom O (SimplexCategory.δ (1 : Fin 2))).IsFlat)
    (h₀ : (S.transitionRingedToposHom O (SimplexCategory.δ (0 : Fin 2))).IsFlat)
    (h₂ : ∃ i : Fin 3, (S.transitionRingedToposHom O (SimplexCategory.δ i)).IsFlat) :
    Abelian (S.CartesianModuleSheaf O)
declarations.comment: corrected form of the positive assertion, which is false as written (the source's hypothesis, flatness of f_{δ¹₁} and f_{δ¹₀} alone, does not suffice: see CategoryTheory.PointSimplicialSite.RatioCounterexample.exists_not_abelian_cartesianModuleSheaf); with one of f_{δ²₀}, f_{δ²₁}, f_{δ²₂} flat as well the cartesian O-modules form an abelian category, with the additive structure of Mod(O)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PointSimplicialSite.RatioCounterexample.exists_not_abelian_cartesianModuleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7K: the positive assertion is false as written.** There is a simplicial site
(the constant simplicial site on the point, in case (A) of Stacks 09WE) and a sheaf of rings `O`
on its total site (the cosimplicial ring of unit ratios
`Rₙ = ℤ[xᵢ, wᵢⱼ^{±1} (i ≤ j)]/(xᵢ = wᵢⱼxⱼ, wᵢᵢ = 1)`) such that the morphisms of ringed topoi
`f_{δ¹₁}` and `f_{δ¹₀}` are flat, but the category of cartesian `O`-modules is not abelian, for
any choice of abelian structure: the quotient map `𝒪 ⟶ 𝒪/(x₀)` is a monomorphism and an
epimorphism of cartesian modules, but not an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_abelian_cartesianModuleSheaf :
    ∃ (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u}) (O : Sheaf S.totalTopology CommRingCat.{u}),
      (S.transitionRingedToposHom O (SimplexCategory.δ (1 : Fin 2))).IsFlat ∧
      (S.transitionRingedToposHom O (SimplexCategory.δ (0 : Fin 2))).IsFlat ∧
      IsEmpty (Abelian (S.CartesianModuleSheaf O))
declarations.comment: the positive assertion is false as written: counterexample with f_{δ¹₁} and f_{δ¹₀} flat but the cartesian O-modules not an abelian category (constant simplicial site on the point, O the cosimplicial ring of unit ratios); the corrected form is CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cartesianModuleSheafAbelian

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PointSimplicialSite.SphereExample.exists_abelian_not_isSerreClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7K: cartesian modules can be abelian without being a Serre subcategory.** There is a
simplicial site (the constant simplicial site on the point, in case (A) of Stacks 09WE) and a sheaf
of rings `O` on its total site with `f_{δ¹₁}` and `f_{δ¹₀}` flat, such that the cartesian
`O`-modules form an abelian category but are neither a Serre subcategory nor a weak Serre
subcategory of `Mod(O)`: they are not closed under kernels in `Mod(O)`. Here `O` is the
cosimplicial ring of functions on `Spec ℤ ⊔ (Δ[3] / ∂Δ[3])`; the non-flat transitions are those
into degree three.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_abelian_not_isSerreClass :
    ∃ (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u}) (O : Sheaf S.totalTopology CommRingCat.{u}),
      (S.transitionRingedToposHom O (SimplexCategory.δ (1 : Fin 2))).IsFlat ∧
      (S.transitionRingedToposHom O (SimplexCategory.δ (0 : Fin 2))).IsFlat ∧
      Nonempty (Abelian (S.CartesianModuleSheaf O)) ∧
      ¬ ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass (S.IsCartesianModule O) ∧
      ¬ ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass (S.IsCartesianModule O)
declarations.comment: the assertion that the category of cartesian O-modules can be abelian without being a Serre subcategory of Mod(O): an example with f_{δ¹₁}, f_{δ¹₀} flat where the cartesian O-modules form an abelian category but are neither a Serre nor a weak Serre subcategory of Mod(O). The source's remark that, when f_{δ²₀} is not flat, there is no reason for the inclusion into Mod(O) to be exact is a heuristic, not an assertion; in this example the non-flat transitions are those into degree three

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.CartesianModulePair.kernelIso_hom_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7K**, the kernel half of the positive assertion, in degree one. If the two
degree-one pullbacks are left exact — which, for flat `f_{δ¹₁}` and `f_{δ¹₀}`, is Stacks 04JC —
then the kernel of the degree-zero morphism of a morphism of pairs carries a comparison
isomorphism restricting the comparison isomorphism of the source pair along the kernel
inclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem kernelIso_hom_comp :
    (kernelIso S O f).hom ≫
        (S.componentModulePullback O (SimplexCategory.δ (0 : Fin 2))).map (kernel.ι f.map) =
      (S.componentModulePullback O (SimplexCategory.δ (1 : Fin 2))).map (kernel.ι f.map) ≫
        A.iso.hom
declarations.comment:
the kernel half of the positive assertion, in degree one: under left exactness of
f_{δ¹₁}^* and f_{δ¹₀}^* (which flatness of f_{δ¹₁} and f_{δ¹₀} gives by Stacks 04JC), the kernel
of a morphism of the pairs of Stacks 07TH carries a comparison isomorphism restricting that of
the source pair, and it is the only morphism that does. NOT covered here: the degree-two cocycle
condition for that isomorphism, hence not the kernel object in the category of pairs and not the
abelian structure; and not the assertion that the inclusion of cartesian O-modules into all
O-modules fails to be exact, which the source states as the absence of a reason for exactness
and not as a counterexample

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.CartesianModulePair.map_comp_cokernelIso_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7K**, the cokernel half of the positive assertion, in degree one. The pullback of
sheaves of modules is right exact unconditionally, so with no flatness hypothesis at all the
cokernel of the degree-zero morphism of a morphism of pairs carries a comparison isomorphism
corestricting the comparison isomorphism of the target pair along the cokernel projection.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_comp_cokernelIso_hom :
    (S.componentModulePullback O (SimplexCategory.δ (1 : Fin 2))).map (cokernel.π f.map) ≫
        (cokernelIso S O f).hom =
      B.iso.hom ≫
        (S.componentModulePullback O (SimplexCategory.δ (0 : Fin 2))).map (cokernel.π f.map)
declarations.comment:
the cokernel half of the positive assertion, in degree one, and with no flatness
hypothesis at all, the pullback of modules being right exact unconditionally: the cokernel of a
morphism of the pairs of Stacks 07TH carries a comparison isomorphism corestricting that of the
target pair, and it is the only morphism that does. NOT covered here: the degree-two cocycle
condition for that isomorphism, hence not the cokernel object in the category of pairs and not
the abelian structure; and not the assertion that the inclusion of cartesian O-modules into all
O-modules fails to be exact, which the source states as the absence of a reason for exactness
and not as a counterexample

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isCartesianDerivedModule_iff_forall_isCartesianModule_homology
declarations.doc:
Let `O` be a sheaf of rings on the total site of a simplicial site such
that the morphisms of ringed topoi `f_{δ^n_j} : (Sh(C_n), O_n) ⟶ (Sh(C_{n-1}), O_{n-1})` of the
face maps are flat. Then an object `K` of `D(O)` is cartesian if and only if `H^q(K)` is a
cartesian `O`-module for all `q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianDerivedModule_iff_forall_isCartesianModule_homology
    (flat : ∀ (k : ℕ) (i : Fin (k + 2)),
      (S.transitionRingedToposHom O (SimplexCategory.δ i)).IsFlat)
    (K : DerivedCategory (S.totalRingedTopos O).Modules) :
    S.IsCartesianDerivedModule O K ↔
      ∀ q : ℤ, IsCartesianModule S O
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (S.totalRingedTopos O).Modules q).obj K)
declarations.comment: part (2), cartesian objects of D(O) for flat face transitions

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isCartesianDerived_iff_forall_isCartesianAbSheaf_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7L (1).** An object of the derived category of abelian sheaves on the total site of
a simplicial site is cartesian if and only if all of its cohomology sheaves are cartesian abelian
sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianDerived_iff_forall_isCartesianAbSheaf_homology
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u})) :
    IsCartesianDerived' S K ↔
      ∀ q : ℤ, IsCartesianAbSheaf S
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) q).obj K)
declarations.comment: cartesian derived sheaves are those with cartesian cohomology

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isCartesianDerived_iff_forall_isCartesianAbSheaf_homology'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7L (1).** An object of the derived category of abelian sheaves on the total site of
a simplicial site is cartesian if and only if all of its cohomology sheaves are cartesian abelian
sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianDerived_iff_forall_isCartesianAbSheaf_homology'
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u})) :
    IsCartesianDerived S K ↔
      ∀ q : ℤ, IsCartesianAbSheaf S
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) q).obj K)
declarations.comment: cartesian derived sheaves are those with cartesian cohomology

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsCartesianWithQuasicoherentComponents
declarations.doc:
**The right-hand side of Stacks 0D7M.** A sheaf of `O`-modules on the total site of a
simplicial-site situation is cartesian in the sense of Stacks 07TF (2) and each of its
component modules `F_n` is a quasi-coherent `O_n`-module in the sense of Stacks 03DL (6).

The source asserts that this condition is equivalent to quasi-coherence of `F` itself on the
total site; that equivalence is not proved in this development.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsCartesianWithQuasicoherentComponents
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (S.totalRingSheaf O)) : Prop
declarations.comment: the right-hand side of the equivalence only: `F` is cartesian in the sense of 07TF (2) and every component module `F_n` is a quasi-coherent `O_n`-module in the sense of 03DL (6). Neither direction of the equivalence with quasi-coherence of `F` on the total site is proved: both need a localization of the total site at an object, which the development does not have

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_isCartesianModule_and_isQuasicoherentOnSite_componentModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7M.** In Situation 09WE, let `O` be a sheaf of rings on the total site and `F` a
sheaf of `O`-modules. Then `F` is quasi-coherent in the sense of Stacks 03DL if and only if `F` is
cartesian in the sense of Stacks 07TF (2) and every component `Fₙ` is a quasi-coherent
`Oₙ`-module.

The right-hand side is
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsCartesianWithQuasicoherentComponents`, spelled out.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_isCartesianModule_and_isQuasicoherentOnSite_componentModule
    (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u}) (O : Sheaf S.totalTopology CommRingCat.{u})
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (S.totalRingSheaf O)) :
    F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔
      S.IsCartesianModule O F ∧
        ∀ n : SimplexCategory, (S.componentModule O F n).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_isCartesianModule_and_components
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7M for the total Zariski site of a simplicial scheme.** A sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules
on the total Zariski site is quasi-coherent in the sense of Stacks 03DL (6) if and only if it is
cartesian in the sense of Stacks 07TF (2) and every one of its component modules `F_n` is a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_{X_n}`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_isCartesianModule_and_components (F : Modules X) :
    F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔
      IsCartesianModule X F ∧
        ∀ k : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ,
          ((componentModule X k).obj F).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: for the total Zariski site of a simplicial scheme, which is the site of 09VL; the cartesian condition is `AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.IsCartesianModule`, 07TF (2) at the transition of 09WF, and quasi-coherence of the components is 03DL (6) over the structure sheaf of the degree, with the component functors of `ZariskiModulePushforward`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.unitIsIso
declarations.doc:
The objects `K` of the source of the left adjoint of an adjunction `F ⊣ G` at which the
unit `K ⟶ G (F K)` is invertible.
declarations.statement: def unitIsIso : ObjectProperty C
declarations.comment: variant: the subcategory of objects at which the unit is invertible, for an arbitrary adjunction F ⊣ G; the tag, for the derived adjunction Lf^* ⊣ Rf_* of a morphism of ringed topoi, is Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.unitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_unitIsIso
declarations.doc:
**The unit subcategory is strictly full**: it is closed under isomorphisms, by naturality
of the unit.
declarations.statement: lemma isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_unitIsIso : adj.unitIsIso.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms
declarations.comment: variant: the unit subcategory is strictly full, for an arbitrary adjunction F ⊣ G; the tag, for the derived adjunction Lf^* ⊣ Rf_* of a morphism of ringed topoi, is Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.unitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.unitIsIso_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
**The unit subcategory is saturated**: a direct summand of an object at which the unit is
invertible is again such an object.
declarations.statement: instance unitIsIso_isSaturated [HasZeroMorphisms C] : adj.unitIsIso.IsSaturated
declarations.comment: variant: the unit subcategory is saturated, for an arbitrary adjunction F ⊣ G; the tag, for the derived adjunction Lf^* ⊣ Rf_* of a morphism of ringed topoi, is Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.unitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.fullyFaithfulιCompLeftAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**The left adjoint is fully faithful on the unit subcategory.** The preimage of
`g : F K ⟶ F L` is the morphism `K ⟶ G (F L)` adjoint to `g`, followed by the inverse of the
unit at `L`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def fullyFaithfulιCompLeftAdjoint : (adj.unitIsIso.ι ⋙ F).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: variant: the left adjoint is fully faithful on the unit subcategory, for an arbitrary adjunction F ⊣ G; the tag, for the derived adjunction Lf^* ⊣ Rf_* of a morphism of ringed topoi, is Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.unitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.unitIsIso_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**The unit subcategory is triangulated**: it contains the zero object, is stable under the
shift because the unit commutes with it, and passes from two vertices of a distinguished
triangle to the third by the five lemma for triangles.
declarations.statement: instance unitIsIso_isTriangulated : adj.unitIsIso.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: variant: the unit subcategory is triangulated, for a triangulated adjunction, for an arbitrary adjunction F ⊣ G; the tag, for the derived adjunction Lf^* ⊣ Rf_* of a morphism of ringed topoi, is Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.unitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.unitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful
declarations.doc:
**The subcategory of `D(O_D)` on which the unit of `Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` is invertible.** For a
morphism of ringed topoi `f : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)`, the full subcategory `D'` of
`D(O_D)` of the objects `K` such that the unit `K ⟶ Rf_* Lf^* K` is an isomorphism is strictly
full (closed under isomorphisms), saturated and triangulated, and `Lf^* : D' ⥤ D(O_C)` is full
and faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem unitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful :
    (derivedAdjunction f).unitIsIso.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
      (derivedAdjunction f).unitIsIso.IsSaturated ∧
      (derivedAdjunction f).unitIsIso.IsTriangulated ∧
      ((derivedAdjunction f).unitIsIso.ι ⋙ derivedPullback f).Full ∧
      ((derivedAdjunction f).unitIsIso.ι ⋙ derivedPullback f).Faithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.counitIsIso
declarations.doc:
The objects `K` of the source of the right adjoint of an adjunction `F ⊣ G` at which the
counit `F (G K) ⟶ K` is invertible.
declarations.statement: def counitIsIso : ObjectProperty D
declarations.comment: variant: the subcategory of objects at which the counit is invertible, for an arbitrary adjunction F ⊣ G; the tag, for the derived adjunction Lf^* ⊣ Rf_* of a morphism of ringed topoi, is Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.counitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_counitIsIso
declarations.doc:
**The counit subcategory is strictly full**: it is closed under isomorphisms, by naturality
of the counit.
declarations.statement: lemma isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_counitIsIso : adj.counitIsIso.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms
declarations.comment: variant: the counit subcategory is strictly full, for an arbitrary adjunction F ⊣ G; the tag, for the derived adjunction Lf^* ⊣ Rf_* of a morphism of ringed topoi, is Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.counitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.counitIsIso_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
**The counit subcategory is saturated**: a direct summand of an object at which the counit
is invertible is again such an object.
declarations.statement: instance counitIsIso_isSaturated [HasZeroMorphisms D] : adj.counitIsIso.IsSaturated
declarations.comment: variant: the counit subcategory is saturated, for an arbitrary adjunction F ⊣ G; the tag, for the derived adjunction Lf^* ⊣ Rf_* of a morphism of ringed topoi, is Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.counitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.fullyFaithfulιCompRightAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**The right adjoint is fully faithful on the counit subcategory.** The preimage of
`g : G A ⟶ G B` is the inverse of the counit at `A`, followed by the morphism `F (G A) ⟶ B`
adjoint to `g`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def fullyFaithfulιCompRightAdjoint : (adj.counitIsIso.ι ⋙ G).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: variant: the right adjoint is fully faithful on the counit subcategory, for an arbitrary adjunction F ⊣ G; the tag, for the derived adjunction Lf^* ⊣ Rf_* of a morphism of ringed topoi, is Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.counitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.counitIsIso_isTriangulated
declarations.doc: **The counit subcategory is triangulated.**
declarations.statement: instance counitIsIso_isTriangulated : adj.counitIsIso.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: variant: the counit subcategory is triangulated, for a triangulated adjunction, for an arbitrary adjunction F ⊣ G; the tag, for the derived adjunction Lf^* ⊣ Rf_* of a morphism of ringed topoi, is Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.counitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.counitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful
declarations.doc:
**The subcategory of `D(O_C)` on which the counit of `Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` is invertible.** For a
morphism of ringed topoi `f : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)`, the full subcategory `D'` of
`D(O_C)` of the objects `K` such that the counit `Lf^* Rf_* K ⟶ K` is an isomorphism is strictly
full (closed under isomorphisms), saturated and triangulated, and `Rf_* : D' ⥤ D(O_D)` is full
and faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem counitIsIso_saturated_triangulated_fullyFaithful :
    (derivedAdjunction f).counitIsIso.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
      (derivedAdjunction f).counitIsIso.IsSaturated ∧
      (derivedAdjunction f).counitIsIso.IsTriangulated ∧
      ((derivedAdjunction f).counitIsIso.ι ⋙ derivedPushforward (X := X) (Y := Y) f).Full ∧
      ((derivedAdjunction f).counitIsIso.ι ⋙ derivedPushforward (X := X) (Y := Y) f).Faithful

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.isIso_derivedCounit_app_of_isIso_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7S.** Let `f` be a flat morphism of ringed topoi and let `K` be a bounded below
object of `D(O_X)`. If the counit `Lf^*Rf_*H^q(K) ⟶ H^q(K)` of the derived adjunction is an
isomorphism for every `q`, with each cohomology object placed in degree zero, then the counit
`Lf^*Rf_*K ⟶ K` is an isomorphism.

This is the previous statement with the pair of functors reversed: here it is
`(Rf_* ⋙ Lf^*, 𝟭)`, and the theorem applied at the counit.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCounit_app_of_isIso_homology :
    letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits hmos hf
    letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
    letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f
    ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))),
      DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.plus K →
      (∀ q : ℤ, IsIso ((derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunctionOfExact f).counit.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) q).obj K)))) →
      IsIso ((derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunctionOfExact f).counit.app K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.isIso_derivedUnit_app_of_isIso_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7T.** Let `f` be a flat morphism of ringed topoi and let `K` be a bounded below
object of `D(O_Y)`. If the unit `H^q(K) ⟶ Rf_*Lf^*H^q(K)` of the derived adjunction is an
isomorphism for every `q`, with each cohomology object placed in degree zero, then the unit
`K ⟶ Rf_*Lf^*K` is an isomorphism.

The pair of functors is `(𝟭, Lf^* ⋙ Rf_*)`: both are exact, both commute with the shift, and
both carry `D^{≥m}` into `D^{≥m}`, so this is
`CategoryTheory.NatTrans.isIso_app_of_isGE` at the unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedUnit_app_of_isIso_homology :
    letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits hmos hf
    letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
    letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f
    ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))),
      DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.plus K →
      (∀ q : ℤ, IsIso ((derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunctionOfExact f).unit.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) 0).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) q).obj K)))) →
      IsIso ((derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunctionOfExact f).unit.app K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedPullback_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7U**, the assertion that derived pullback restricts. Let `f` be a flat morphism of
ringed topoi and let `𝒜 ⊂ Mod(𝒪)`, `𝒜' ⊂ Mod(𝒪')` be weak Serre subcategories with
`f^*𝒜' ⊂ 𝒜`. Then `Lf^*` carries `D⁺_{𝒜'}(𝒪')` into `D⁺_𝒜(𝒪)`.

theorem derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedPullback_obj :
    letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits hmos hf
    letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
    letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f
    ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))),

declarations.comment: derived pullback

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedPushforward_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7U**, the assertion that derived pushforward restricts. Under the hypotheses of the
source — `f` flat, `f^*` inducing an equivalence `𝒜' ⟶ 𝒜`, and the unit `ℱ' ⟶ Rf_*f^*ℱ'`
invertible on `𝒜'` — the pushforward `Rf_*` carries `D⁺_𝒜(𝒪)` into `D⁺_{𝒜'}(𝒪')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedPushforward_obj :
    letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits hmos hf
    letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
    letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f
    (∀ M, A' M → IsIso ((derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunctionOfExact f).unit.app
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) 0).obj M))) →
      ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))),

          DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus A' ((derivedPushforward f).obj K)
declarations.comment: derived pushforward

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.derivedPullbackEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7U.** For a flat morphism of ringed topoi `f` and weak Serre subcategories
`𝒜 ⊂ Mod(𝒪)`, `𝒜' ⊂ Mod(𝒪')` such that `f^*` induces an equivalence `𝒜' ⟶ 𝒜` and the unit
`ℱ' ⟶ Rf_*f^*ℱ'` is invertible for every `ℱ'` of `𝒜'`, the derived pullback is an **equivalence**
`D⁺_{𝒜'}(𝒪') ≌ D⁺_𝒜(𝒪)`.

The hypothesis on the unit propagates from `𝒜'` to all of `D⁺_{𝒜'}(𝒪')` by Tag 0D7T, and the
corresponding statement for the counit from `𝒜` to all of `D⁺_𝒜(𝒪)` by Tag 0D7S.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedPullbackEquivalence
    (hUnit :
      letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits hmos hf
      letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
      letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f
      ∀ M, A' M → IsIso ((derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunctionOfExact f).unit.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) 0).obj M))) :
    (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus A').FullSubcategory ≌
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus A).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment: equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.derivedPullbackEquivalence_functor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7U**, the identification of the forward functor of the equivalence with the
restriction of the derived pullback.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPullbackEquivalence_functor
    (hUnit :
      letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits hmos hf
      letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
      letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f
      ∀ M, A' M → IsIso ((derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunctionOfExact f).unit.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) 0).obj M))) :
    letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits hmos hf
    letI := f.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
    letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f
    (derivedPullbackEquivalence f A A' hmos hf hA hEquiv hUnit).functor =
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus A).lift
        ((DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus A').ι ⋙ derivedPullback f)
        (fun K ↦ derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedPullback_obj f A A' hmos hf hA K.obj K.property)
declarations.comment: forward functor

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.derivedPullbackEquivalence_inverse

      letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f
      ∀ M, A' M → IsIso ((derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunctionOfExact f).unit.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor

declarations.comment: quasi-inverse

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.OfRingedToposHom.derivedCategoryB_derivedPullback_obj

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.OfRingedToposHom.derivedCategoryB_derivedPushforward_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7V for a morphism of ringed topoi**, the assertion that derived pushforward

        (SheafOfModules.{w} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := X.J) X.O))),

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.OfRingedToposHom.derivedPullbackEquivalenceUnbounded
declarations.doc:

equivalence `𝒜' ⟶ 𝒜` and the unit `ℱ' ⟶ Rf_*f^*ℱ'` is invertible for every `ℱ'` of `𝒜'`, and

the derived pullback is an **equivalence** `D_{𝒜'}(𝒪') ≌ D_𝒜(𝒪)`.
declarations.comment: equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.OfRingedToposHom.derivedPullbackEquivalenceUnbounded_functor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7V for a morphism of ringed topoi**, the identification of the forward functor of
the equivalence with the restriction of the derived pullback.

theorem derivedPullbackEquivalenceUnbounded_functor :
    (derivedPullbackEquivalenceUnbounded f hf A A' hA hEquiv hUnit

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.OfRingedToposHom.derivedPullbackEquivalenceUnbounded_inverse

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.derivedCategoryB_derivedPullback_obj_relative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7W**, the assertion that derived pullback restricts. Let `f` be a flat morphism of
ringed sites and let `𝒜 ⊂ Mod(𝒪)`, `𝒜' ⊂ Mod(𝒪')` be weak Serre subcategories with
`f^*𝒜' ⊂ 𝒜`. Then `Lf^*` carries `D_{𝒜'}(𝒪')` into `D_𝒜(𝒪)`. Neither standing hypothesis is
needed: derived pullback is degreewise pullback, which is exact, so `Hʲ(Lf^*K)` is `f^*Hʲ(K)`,
and `f^*` carries `𝒜'` into `𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryB_derivedPullback_obj_relative :
    letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits
      f.isMorphismOfSites_toRingedToposSiteHom hf
    letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
    letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f.toRingedToposSiteHom
    ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))),
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB A' K →
        DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB A
          ((derivedPullback f.toRingedToposSiteHom).obj K)
declarations.comment: derived pullback

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.derivedCategoryB_derivedPushforward_obj_relative
declarations.doc:
