the source — `f` flat, `f^*` inducing an equivalence `𝒜' ⟶ 𝒜`, the unit `ℱ' ⟶ Rf_*f^*ℱ'`
invertible on `𝒜'`, the source satisfying the Olsson--Laszlo hypothesis of Tag 0D6R and `f`
together with `𝒜` satisfying the relative hypothesis of Tag 0D6V — the pushforward `Rf_*`
carries `D_𝒜(𝒪)` into `D_{𝒜'}(𝒪')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryB_derivedPushforward_obj_relative
    (hUnit :
      letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits
        f.isMorphismOfSites_toRingedToposSiteHom hf
      letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
      letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f.toRingedToposSiteHom
      ∀ M, A' M → IsIso
        ((derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunctionOfExact f.toRingedToposSiteHom).unit.app
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u}
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) 0).obj M))) :
    letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits
      f.isMorphismOfSites_toRingedToposSiteHom hf
    letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
    letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f.toRingedToposSiteHom
    ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))),
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB A K →
        DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB A'
          ((derivedPushforward f.toRingedToposSiteHom).obj K)
declarations.comment: derived pushforward

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.derivedPullbackEquivalenceUnboundedRelative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7W.** Let `f : (C, 𝒪) ⟶ (C', 𝒪')` be a flat morphism of ringed sites and let
`𝒜 ⊂ Mod(𝒪)`, `𝒜' ⊂ Mod(𝒪')` be weak Serre subcategories such that `f^*` induces an equivalence
`𝒜' ⟶ 𝒜` and the unit `ℱ' ⟶ Rf_*f^*ℱ'` is invertible for every `ℱ'` of `𝒜'`, and assume that
`C, 𝒪, 𝒜` satisfy the standing hypothesis of Tag 0D6R and that `f` together with `𝒜` satisfies
the relative standing hypothesis of Tag 0D6V. Then the derived pullback is an **equivalence**
`D_{𝒜'}(𝒪') ≌ D_𝒜(𝒪)`.

The hypothesis on the unit propagates from `𝒜` to all of `D⁺_𝒜(𝒪)` by Tag 0D7S; the two standing
hypotheses then carry the counit from the bounded below subcategory to the whole derived
category, through Tag 0D6W. This is Tag 0D7V with its appeal to Tag 0D6U replaced by one to Tag
0D6W, which is the source's own description of the proof.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPullbackEquivalenceUnboundedRelative
    (hUnit :
      letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits
        f.isMorphismOfSites_toRingedToposSiteHom hf
      letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
      letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f.toRingedToposSiteHom
      ∀ M, A' M → IsIso
        ((derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunctionOfExact f.toRingedToposSiteHom).unit.app
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u}
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) 0).obj M))) :
    (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB A').FullSubcategory ≌
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB A).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment: equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.derivedPullbackEquivalenceUnboundedRelative_functor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7W**, the identification of the forward functor of the equivalence with the
restriction of the derived pullback.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPullbackEquivalenceUnboundedRelative_functor
    (hUnit :
      letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits
        f.isMorphismOfSites_toRingedToposSiteHom hf
      letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
      letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f.toRingedToposSiteHom
      ∀ M, A' M → IsIso
        ((derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunctionOfExact f.toRingedToposSiteHom).unit.app
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u}
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) 0).obj M))) :
    letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits
      f.isMorphismOfSites_toRingedToposSiteHom hf
    letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
    letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f.toRingedToposSiteHom
    (derivedPullbackEquivalenceUnboundedRelative f hf A A' hA hEquiv
      B basisCover degreeBound coverings vanishing
      B' basisCover' degreeBound' coverings' vanishing' hUnit).functor =
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB A).lift
        ((DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB A').ι ⋙
          derivedPullback.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom)
        (fun K ↦ derivedCategoryB_derivedPullback_obj_relative f hf A A' hA K.obj
          K.property)
declarations.comment: forward functor

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.derivedPullbackEquivalenceUnboundedRelative_inverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7W**, the identification of the quasi-inverse of the equivalence with the
restriction of the derived pushforward.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPullbackEquivalenceUnboundedRelative_inverse
    (hUnit :
      letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits
        f.isMorphismOfSites_toRingedToposSiteHom hf
      letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
      letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f.toRingedToposSiteHom
      ∀ M, A' M → IsIso
        ((derivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunctionOfExact f.toRingedToposSiteHom).unit.app
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u}
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) 0).obj M))) :
    letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteLimits
      f.isMorphismOfSites_toRingedToposSiteHom hf
    letI := f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos_preservesFiniteColimits
    letI := pullbackOnHomotopy_hasLeftDerivedFunctor_of_exact f.toRingedToposSiteHom
    (derivedPullbackEquivalenceUnboundedRelative f hf A A' hA hEquiv
      B basisCover degreeBound coverings vanishing
      B' basisCover' degreeBound' coverings' vanishing' hUnit).inverse =
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB A').lift
        ((DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB A).ι ⋙
          derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom)
        (fun K ↦ derivedCategoryB_derivedPushforward_obj_relative f hf A A' hA hEquiv
          B basisCover degreeBound coverings vanishing
          B' basisCover' degreeBound' coverings' vanishing' hUnit K.obj K.property)
declarations.comment: quasi-inverse

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.sheafHomYonedaSheafifyNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D7X.** For an object `U` of a small site `(C, J)`, the internal hom sheaf
`SheafHom(h_U^\#, -)` out of the sheafification of the representable presheaf `h_U` is the
composite `j_{U*} \circ j_U^{-1}`: that is,
`SheafHom(h_U^\#, \mathcal{F}) = j_{U*}(\mathcal{F}|_{\mathcal{C}/U})`, naturally in the sheaf
`\mathcal{F}`.

Both functors are right adjoint to `\mathcal{G} \mapsto h_U^\# \times \mathcal{G}`, the first by
Stacks 0BWQ and the second by the localization adjunctions together with Stacks 03EE, so they agree
by uniqueness of right adjoints. This is the source's argument, whose last step is the Yoneda
lemma.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomYonedaSheafifyNatIso :
    SheafHomAdj.sheafHomFunctor ((presheafToSheaf J (Type u)).obj (yoneda.obj U)) ≅
      localizationPullback U J ⋙ localizationPushforward U J

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.PostnikovSystem
declarations.doc:
A *Postnikov system* for a complex `Xₙ ⟶ Xₙ₋₁ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X₀` in a pretriangulated category,
the morphisms of the complex being `d i : X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc`: objects `Y₀, …, Yₙ` together
with an isomorphism `Y₀ ⟶ X₀` and distinguished triangles
`Yᵢ₊₁ ⟶ Xᵢ₊₁ ⟶ Yᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ₊₁⟦1⟧` in which the composition `Xᵢ₊₁ ⟶ Yᵢ ⟶ Xᵢ` is the given morphism
`Xᵢ₊₁ ⟶ Xᵢ`. The morphisms of Postnikov systems, the second notion of this Stacks definition, are
`CategoryTheory.Triangulated.PostnikovSystem.Hom`.
declarations.statement:
public structure PostnikovSystem {n : ℕ} (X : Fin (n + 1) → D)
    (d : ∀ i : Fin n, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc)
declarations.comment: Postnikov system; the morphisms of Postnikov systems are `PostnikovSystem.Hom`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.PostnikovSystem.Hom
declarations.doc:
A *morphism of Postnikov systems* `S ⟶ S'` lying over a family of morphisms
`f i : Xᵢ ⟶ X'ᵢ` between two complexes `Xₙ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X₀` and `X'ₙ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X'₀` of the same length:
morphisms `hom i : Yᵢ ⟶ Y'ᵢ` making every diagram of the two systems commute, that is compatible
with the morphisms `Yᵢ ⟶ Xᵢ`, `Xᵢ₊₁ ⟶ Yᵢ` and `Yᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ₊₁⟦1⟧`. Equivalently, `f` and `hom`
form morphisms of all the distinguished triangles `Yᵢ₊₁ ⟶ Xᵢ₊₁ ⟶ Yᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ₊₁⟦1⟧` of the two
systems. That `f` is a morphism of complexes is not imposed: it follows, see `Hom.comm_d`.
declarations.statement:
public structure Hom (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ X' i) (S : PostnikovSystem X d)
    (S' : PostnikovSystem X' d')
declarations.comment: morphism of Postnikov systems

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.postnikovSystem_small_cases
declarations.doc:
Let `D` be a pretriangulated category and consider Postnikov systems for complexes
`Xₙ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X₀` of length `n`, with morphisms of Postnikov systems in the sense of
`PostnikovSystem.IsHomOver`.

1. For `n = 0` Postnikov systems always exist and any morphism of complexes extends to a unique
   morphism of Postnikov systems.
2. For `n = 1` Postnikov systems always exist and any morphism of complexes extends to a morphism
   of Postnikov systems; this extension is not unique in general.
3. For `n = 2` Postnikov systems always exist, but morphisms of complexes do not extend to
   morphisms of Postnikov systems in general.
4. For `n > 2` Postnikov systems do not always exist.

The failures in (2), (3) and (4) are exhibited in the homotopy category of `ℤ`-modules, which is
triangulated.
declarations.statement:
theorem postnikovSystem_small_cases :
    ((∀ (X : Fin 1 → D) (d : ∀ i : Fin 0, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc),
        Nonempty (PostnikovSystem X d)) ∧
      ∀ {X X' : Fin 1 → D} {d : ∀ i : Fin 0, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc}
        {d' : ∀ i : Fin 0, X' i.succ ⟶ X' i.castSucc} (S : PostnikovSystem X d)
        (S' : PostnikovSystem X' d') (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ X' i),
        (∀ i : Fin 0, d i ≫ f i.castSucc = f i.succ ≫ d' i) →
        ∃! g : ∀ i, S.obj i ⟶ S'.obj i, S.IsHomOver S' f g) ∧
    ((∀ (X : Fin 2 → D) (d : ∀ i : Fin 1, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc),
        Nonempty (PostnikovSystem X d)) ∧
      (∀ {X X' : Fin 2 → D} {d : ∀ i : Fin 1, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc}
        {d' : ∀ i : Fin 1, X' i.succ ⟶ X' i.castSucc} (S : PostnikovSystem X d)
        (S' : PostnikovSystem X' d') (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ X' i),
        (∀ i : Fin 1, d i ≫ f i.castSucc = f i.succ ≫ d' i) →
        ∃ g : ∀ i, S.obj i ⟶ S'.obj i, S.IsHomOver S' f g) ∧
      ∃ (X : Fin 2 → HomotopyCategory (ModuleCat.{0} ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
        (d : ∀ i : Fin 1, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc) (S : PostnikovSystem X d)
        (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ X i), (∀ i : Fin 1, d i ≫ f i.castSucc = f i.succ ≫ d i) ∧
        ∃ g g' : ∀ i, S.obj i ⟶ S.obj i, S.IsHomOver S f g ∧ S.IsHomOver S f g' ∧ g ≠ g') ∧
    ((∀ (X : Fin 3 → D) (d : ∀ i : Fin 2, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc), d 1 ≫ d 0 = 0 →
        Nonempty (PostnikovSystem X d)) ∧
      ∃ (X : Fin 3 → HomotopyCategory (ModuleCat.{0} ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
        (d : ∀ i : Fin 2, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc), d 1 ≫ d 0 = 0 ∧
        ∃ S S' : PostnikovSystem X d, ¬ ∃ g, S.IsHomOver S' (fun i => 𝟙 (X i)) g) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, 2 < n → ∃ (X : Fin (n + 1) → HomotopyCategory (ModuleCat.{0} ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
      (d : ∀ i : Fin n, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc),
      (∀ (i : Fin n) (h : (i : ℕ) + 1 < n), d ⟨(i : ℕ) + 1, h⟩ ≫ d i = 0) ∧
        IsEmpty (PostnikovSystem X d)) ∧
    IsTriangulated (HomotopyCategory (ModuleCat.{0} ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
declarations.comment: existence in (1)–(3), the unique extension of morphisms in (1) and the extension in (2) hold in every pretriangulated category; the non-uniqueness in (2), the non-extension in (3) and the non-existence in (4), for every n > 2, are witnessed in the triangulated homotopy category K(ℤ-Mod).

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.PostnikovSystem.hom_shift_obj_eq_zero_and_exists_hom
declarations.doc:
Let `Xₙ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X₀` and `X'ₙ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X'₀` be complexes in a pretriangulated category, let `S'`
be a Postnikov system for the second one, and assume that every morphism `Xᵢ⟦i - j - 1⟧ ⟶ X'ⱼ`
with `i > j + 1` is zero. Then

1. every morphism `Xᵢ⟦i - j - 1⟧ ⟶ Y'ⱼ` with `i > j + 1` is zero, and
2. for every Postnikov system `S` for the first complex, every morphism of complexes
   `f i : Xᵢ ⟶ X'ᵢ` extends to a (nonunique) morphism of Postnikov systems `S ⟶ S'`, i.e. to a
   family `g i : Yᵢ ⟶ Y'ᵢ` compatible with the morphisms `Yᵢ ⟶ Xᵢ`, `Xᵢ₊₁ ⟶ Yᵢ` and
   `Yᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ₊₁⟦1⟧` of the two systems.
declarations.statement:
theorem PostnikovSystem.hom_shift_obj_eq_zero_and_exists_hom {n : ℕ}
    (X : Fin (n + 1) → D) (d : ∀ i : Fin n, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc)
    {X' : Fin (n + 1) → D} {d' : ∀ i : Fin n, X' i.succ ⟶ X' i.castSucc}
    (S' : PostnikovSystem X' d')
    (h : ∀ i j : Fin (n + 1), (j : ℕ) + 1 < (i : ℕ) →
      ∀ f : (X i)⟦((i : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((j : ℕ) : ℤ) - 1⟧ ⟶ X' j, f = 0) :
    (∀ i j : Fin (n + 1), (j : ℕ) + 1 < (i : ℕ) →
        ∀ f : (X i)⟦((i : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((j : ℕ) : ℤ) - 1⟧ ⟶ S'.obj j, f = 0) ∧
      ∀ (S : PostnikovSystem X d) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ X' i),
        (∀ i : Fin n, d i ≫ f i.castSucc = f i.succ ≫ d' i) →
        ∃ g : ∀ i, S.obj i ⟶ S'.obj i,
          (∀ i, g i ≫ S'.π i = S.π i ≫ f i) ∧
          (∀ i : Fin n, S.p i ≫ g i.castSucc = f i.succ ≫ S'.p i) ∧
          (∀ i : Fin n, S.δ i ≫ (g i.succ)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = g i.castSucc ≫ S'.δ i)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.nonempty_postnikovSystem_of_hom_shift_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
A complex `Xₙ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X₀` in a pretriangulated category, with morphisms `d i : Xᵢ₊₁ ⟶ Xᵢ`,
admits a Postnikov system as soon as every morphism `Xᵢ⟦i - j - 2⟧ ⟶ Xⱼ` with `i > j + 2` is
zero. Without that vanishing condition Postnikov systems need not exist once `n > 2`; for
`n ≤ 2` the condition is vacuous and this is
`CategoryTheory.Triangulated.nonempty_postnikovSystem_of_length_le_two`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_postnikovSystem_of_hom_shift_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (X : Fin (n + 1) → D)
    (d : ∀ i : Fin n, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc)
    (hd : ∀ (i : Fin n) (h : (i : ℕ) + 1 < n), d ⟨(i : ℕ) + 1, h⟩ ≫ d i = 0)
    (h : ∀ i j : Fin (n + 1), (j : ℕ) + 2 < (i : ℕ) →
      ∀ u : (X i)⟦((i : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((j : ℕ) : ℤ) - 2⟧ ⟶ X j, u = 0) :
    Nonempty (PostnikovSystem X d)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.PostnikovSystem.exists_iso
declarations.doc:
Let `Xₙ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X₀` be a diagram in a pretriangulated category, with morphisms
`d i : Xᵢ₊₁ ⟶ Xᵢ`, such that every morphism `Xᵢ⟦i - j - 1⟧ ⟶ Xⱼ` with `i > j + 1` is zero. Then
for every diagram `X'ₙ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X'₀` and every isomorphism `f i : Xᵢ ≅ X'ᵢ` of diagrams, any
Postnikov systems `S`, `S'` for the two are isomorphic over `f`: there is a family of isomorphisms
`g i : Yᵢ ≅ Y'ᵢ` compatible with the morphisms `Yᵢ ⟶ Xᵢ`, `Xᵢ₊₁ ⟶ Yᵢ` and `Yᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ₊₁⟦1⟧` of the
two systems. In particular, at `X' = X`, `d' = d` and `f = 𝟙`, any two Postnikov systems for
`Xₙ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X₀` are isomorphic.
declarations.statement:
theorem PostnikovSystem.exists_iso {n : ℕ} {X X' : Fin (n + 1) → D}
    {d : ∀ i : Fin n, X i.succ ⟶ X i.castSucc} {d' : ∀ i : Fin n, X' i.succ ⟶ X' i.castSucc}
    (h : ∀ i j : Fin (n + 1), (j : ℕ) + 1 < (i : ℕ) →
      ∀ u : (X i)⟦((i : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((j : ℕ) : ℤ) - 1⟧ ⟶ X j, u = 0)
    (S : PostnikovSystem X d) (S' : PostnikovSystem X' d') (f : ∀ i, X i ≅ X' i)
    (hf : ∀ i : Fin n, d i ≫ (f i.castSucc).hom = (f i.succ).hom ≫ d' i) :
    ∃ g : ∀ i, S.obj i ≅ S'.obj i,
      (∀ i, (g i).hom ≫ S'.π i = S.π i ≫ (f i).hom) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, S.p i ≫ (g i.castSucc).hom = (f i.succ).hom ≫ S'.p i) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, S.δ i ≫ ((g i.succ).hom)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' =
        (g i.castSucc).hom ≫ S'.δ i)

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.fibreRestrictionAb_exact
declarations.doc: **Restriction of abelian sheaves to the fibre is exact.**
declarations.statement:
theorem fibreRestrictionAb_exact :
    exactFunctor (Sheaf (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X) Ab.{u})
      (Sheaf (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology (fibreSpace X Y a V)) Ab.{u})
      (fibreRestrictionAb X Y a V)
declarations.comment: the proof's use of exactness of restriction to the fibre

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.fibreRestrictedSections_rightDerived_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D84, the reduction step of the proof.** The `n`-th right derived functor of
`F ↦ Γ((X ×_Y V)_Zar, F|)` is the cohomology `Hⁿ((X ×_Y V)_Zar, F|)` of the restriction.

An injective resolution of `F` on `X_Zar` restricts to an injective resolution of `F|` on
`(X ×_Y V)_Zar`, because restriction is exact (`fibreRestrictionAb_exact`) and carries
injectives to injectives (part (1) of the source proof,
`fibreRestrictionAb_preservesInjectiveObjects`); so one and the same complex computes both
sides.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fibreRestrictedSections_rightDerived_iso (n : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X) Ab.{u}) :
    ((fibreRestrictedSections X Y a V).rightDerived n).obj F ≅
      (fibreCohomology X Y a V n).obj ((fibreRestrictionAb X Y a V).obj F)
declarations.comment: the proof's reduction: derived sections of the restriction are fibre cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.fibreRestrictionAb_preservesInjectiveObjects
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D84, part (1) of the proof.** The restriction of an abelian sheaf on `X_Zar` to
`(X ×_Y V)_Zar` preserves injective objects: its left adjoint, extension by zero, is exact, and
a right adjoint of a functor preserving monomorphisms preserves injectives
([Stacks, Tag 015Z]).
declarations.statement:
theorem fibreRestrictionAb_preservesInjectiveObjects :
    (fibreRestrictionAb X Y a V).PreservesInjectiveObjects
declarations.comment: part (1) of the proof: restriction to the fibre preserves injectives

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.injective_fibreRestrictionAb_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D84, part (1) of the proof.** The restriction to `(X ×_Y V)_Zar` of an injective
abelian sheaf on `X_Zar` is an injective abelian sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_fibreRestrictionAb_obj
    (I : Sheaf (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X) Ab.{u}) [Injective I] :
    Injective ((fibreRestrictionAb X Y a V).obj I)
declarations.comment: part (1) of the proof: the restriction of an injective is injective

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.augmentationCohomologyPresheaf_obj_iso_fibreCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D84.** The value over an open `V` of the target of the cohomology presheaf of an
augmentation is the cohomology `Hⁿ((X ×_Y V)_Zar, F|)` of the restriction of `F` to the total
site of the fibre `X ×_Y V`.

This is the displayed rule of the statement.  Three steps: the value of the cohomology presheaf
over `V` is the `n`-th right derived functor of the sections of the direct image over `V`
(exactness of evaluation); those sections are the global sections of the restriction to the
fibre, which is part (2) of the source proof; and the derived functors of the global sections of
the restriction are the cohomology of the fibre, because restriction is exact and carries
injectives to injectives, which is part (1) of the source proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem augmentationCohomologyPresheaf_obj_iso_fibreCohomology (n : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X) Ab.{u}) :
    Nonempty (((augmentationCohomologyPresheaf X Y a n).obj F).obj (op V) ≅
      (fibreCohomology X Y a V n).obj ((fibreRestrictionAb X Y a V).obj F))
declarations.comment: the values of the displayed presheaf are the cohomology of the fibre

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.higherDirectImage_iso_sheafify_fibreCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D84.** Let `X` be a simplicial space, let `a : X ⟶ Y` be an augmentation and let
`F` be an abelian sheaf on `X_Zar`.  Then `Rⁿa_*F` is the sheaf associated to the presheaf whose
value over an open `V` of `Y` is `Hⁿ((X ×_Y V)_Zar, F|_{(X ×_Y V)_Zar})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem higherDirectImage_iso_sheafify_fibreCohomology (n : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X) Ab.{u}) :
    Nonempty (((augmentationPushforwardAb X Y a).rightDerived n).obj F ≅
        (presheafToSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Ab.{u}).obj
          ((augmentationCohomologyPresheaf X Y a n).obj F)) ∧
      ∀ V : Opens Y,
        Nonempty (((augmentationCohomologyPresheaf X Y a n).obj F).obj (op V) ≅
          (fibreCohomology X Y a V n).obj ((fibreRestrictionAb X Y a V).obj F))

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.augmentationFibreSections_iso_fibreRestrictedSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D84, part (2) of the proof.** The sections over `V` of the direct image of an
abelian sheaf `F` on `X_Zar` along an augmentation are the global sections over the total site of
the fibre `X ×_Y V` of the restriction of `F`, naturally in `F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def augmentationFibreSections_iso_fibreRestrictedSections :
    augmentationFibreSections X Y a V ≅ fibreRestrictedSections X Y a V
declarations.comment: part (2) of the proof: the direct image over V is the sections over the fibre

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.higherDirectImage_iso_sheafify_augmentationCohomologyPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D84.** Let `X` be a simplicial space, let `a : X ⟶ Y` be an augmentation and let
`F` be an abelian sheaf on `X_Zar`.  Then the `n`-th higher direct image `Rⁿa_*F` is the sheaf
associated to the cohomology presheaf of the augmentation, whose value over an open `V` of `Y`
is `Hⁿ((X ×_Y V)_Zar, F|_{(X ×_Y V)_Zar})`.

Sheafification is exact, so it commutes with the right derived functors of the presheaf-valued
direct image; the higher direct image is the right derived functor of the sheaf-valued one,
which is the sheafification of the presheaf-valued one.
declarations.statement:
theorem higherDirectImage_iso_sheafify_augmentationCohomologyPresheaf (n : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X) Ab.{u}) :
    Nonempty (((augmentationPushforwardAb X Y a).rightDerived n).obj F ≅
      (presheafToSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Ab.{u}).obj
        ((augmentationCohomologyPresheaf X Y a n).obj F))
declarations.comment: the sheafification of the cohomology presheaf; not its fibrewise values

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.augmentationCohomologyPresheaf_evaluation_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D84.** The value over an open `V` of the target of the cohomology presheaf of an
augmentation is the `n`-th right derived functor of the sections of the direct image over `V`.
By part (2) of the source proof the latter functor is `F ↦ H⁰((X ×_Y V)_Zar, F|)`, so this is
the displayed rule `V ↦ Hⁿ((X ×_Y V)_Zar, F|)` of the statement.

Evaluation of a presheaf of abelian groups at an open is exact, so it commutes with right
derived functors.
declarations.statement:
theorem augmentationCohomologyPresheaf_evaluation_iso (n : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X) Ab.{u}) (V : Opens Y) :
    Nonempty (((augmentationCohomologyPresheaf X Y a n).obj F).obj (op V) ≅
      ((augmentationFibreSections X Y a V).rightDerived n).obj F)
declarations.comment: those values as derived sections of the direct image, not as fibre cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.augmentationPushforwardAb_forget_isoEqualizer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D84, part (2a) of the proof.** The underlying sheaf of sets of the direct image
`a_*F` of an abelian sheaf along an augmentation is the equalizer of the two maps induced by
the vertices of the one-simplex between the direct images of the degree-zero and the
degree-one components of `F`.

Over an open `V` of the target the two sheaves of that equalizer have sections the sections of
`F` over the simplicial opens `a_0⁻¹(V)` and `a_1⁻¹(V)`, which are the degree-zero and
degree-one components of the simplicial space `X ×_Y V`.  This is the fibrewise description of
the sections of `a_*F` used in the source proof.
declarations.statement:
def augmentationPushforwardAb_forget_isoEqualizer
    (F : Sheaf (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X) Ab.{u}) :
    (sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) (forget Ab.{u})).obj
        ((augmentationPushforwardAb X Y a).obj F) ≅
      equalizer
        (augmentationFaceMap X Y a
          ((sheafCompose (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X) (forget Ab.{u})).obj F) 0)
        (augmentationFaceMap X Y a
          ((sheafCompose (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X) (forget Ab.{u})).obj F) 1)
declarations.comment: degree zero: the direct image as an equalizer of fibrewise direct images

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.LocalizationSites.localizationFunctor_isContinuous_isCocontinuous_hasCoverPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D85 (1).** Let `(C, IsCov)` be a site and `K` a semi-representable object. The
localization functor `j : C / K ⥤ C` is continuous and cocontinuous for the topologies generated by
the coverings of `C / K` and of `C`, and has property P of Stacks 09W7 for those coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizationFunctor_isContinuous_isCocontinuous_hasCoverPullbacks
    (hCov : IsSite IsCov) (S : LocalizationSites.{max u v} C (topologyOfCoverings IsCov)) :
    S.localizationFunctor.IsContinuous (topologyOfCoverings (componentCoverings IsCov S.K))
        (topologyOfCoverings IsCov) ∧
      S.localizationFunctor.IsCocontinuous (topologyOfCoverings (componentCoverings IsCov S.K))
        (topologyOfCoverings IsCov) ∧
      ∀ (𝒱 : Covering.{u, v, max u v} C), IsCov 𝒱 →
        ∀ (U : S.source) (g : S.localizationFunctor.obj U ⟶ 𝒱.1),
          ∃ (P : 𝒱.2.I₀ → S.source) (p₁ : ∀ i, P i ⟶ U)
            (p₂ : ∀ i, S.localizationFunctor.obj (P i) ⟶ 𝒱.2.X i),
            (∀ i,
              S.localizationFunctor.map (p₁ i) ≫ g = p₂ i ≫ 𝒱.2.f i ∧
                ∀ (T : S.source) (a : T ⟶ U)
                  (b : S.localizationFunctor.obj T ⟶ 𝒱.2.X i),
                  S.localizationFunctor.map a ≫ g = b ≫ 𝒱.2.f i →
                    ∃! l : T ⟶ P i,
                      (l ≫ p₁ i = a ∧ S.localizationFunctor.map l ≫ p₂ i = b)) ∧
              componentCoverings IsCov S.K ⟨U, PreZeroHypercover.mk 𝒱.2.I₀ P p₁⟩

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.LocalizationSites.relocalizationFunctor_isContinuous_isCocontinuous_hasCoverPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D85 (2).** Let `(C, IsCov)` be a site and `f : K ⟶ L` a morphism of
semi-representable objects. The relocalization functor `v : C / K ⥤ C / L` is continuous and
cocontinuous for the topologies generated by the coverings of `C / K` and of `C / L`, and has
property P of Stacks 09W7 for those coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem relocalizationFunctor_isContinuous_isCocontinuous_hasCoverPullbacks
    (hCov : IsSite IsCov) (S : LocalizationSites.{max u v} C (topologyOfCoverings IsCov)) :
    S.relocalizationFunctor.IsContinuous (topologyOfCoverings (componentCoverings IsCov S.K))
        (topologyOfCoverings (componentCoverings IsCov S.L)) ∧
      S.relocalizationFunctor.IsCocontinuous (topologyOfCoverings (componentCoverings IsCov S.K))
        (topologyOfCoverings (componentCoverings IsCov S.L)) ∧
      S.relocalizationFunctor.HasCoverPullbacks (componentCoverings IsCov S.K)
        (componentCoverings IsCov S.L)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.abelianLocalizationPushforwardPullbackNatIsoSheafHomPrime
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D86 for abelian coefficients.** For a semi-representable object `K = {U i}` of a
small site `(C, J)`, the product of the localization push-pull functors `j_{i,*} j_i^{-1}` on
abelian sheaves is naturally isomorphic to `ℋom'(F(K)^#, -)`.

This is the source's `j_* j^{-1} F = ℋom'(F(K)^#, F)` under the product description of sheaves on
`C / K`, for `F` an abelian sheaf and naturally in `F`, which is the form in which Stacks 0D8F
uses Stacks 0D86. Both sides are the abelian readings of Stacks 04DB of the corresponding
functors of sheaves of sets — the same reading by which the terms `a_{n,*}a_n^{-1}F` of the Čech
complex of Stacks 0D79 are built — and the isomorphism is the one of Stacks 0D86 carried through
that reading, which is possible because both functors preserve finite products and the reading is
functorial in the finite-product-preserving functor.
declarations.statement:
def abelianLocalizationPushforwardPullbackNatIsoSheafHomPrime
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : FormalCoproduct.{u} C) :
    abelianLocalizationPushPull J K ≅ abelianSheafHomPrime J K
declarations.comment: the abelian form: abelian-sheaf coefficients, primed internal hom

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.localizationPushforwardPullbackNatIsoSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D86.** For a semi-representable object `K = {U i}`, the product of the
localization push-pull functors `j_{i,*} j_i^{-1}` is naturally isomorphic to
`SheafHom(F(K)^#, -)`. This is the source's `j_* j^{-1} F = SheafHom(F(K)^#, F)` under the
product description of sheaves on `C / K`, naturally in `F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationPushforwardPullbackNatIsoSheafHom
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : FormalCoproduct.{u} C) :
    (Functor.pi' (fun i : K.I =>
        localizationPullback (K.obj i) J ⋙ localizationPushforward (K.obj i) J) ⋙
        Pi.functor K.I) ≅
      CategoryTheory.SheafHomAdj.sheafHomFunctor
        ((presheafToSheaf J (Type u)).obj ((FormalCoproduct.yoneda (C := C)).obj K))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.componentwiseRelocalization_comp_sheafEquivalence_iso_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D87 part (3).** Under the identifications of part (1), the relocalization inverse
image `f^{-1} : Sh(C / L) ⥤ Sh(C / K)` along a morphism `f : K ⟶ L` of semi-representable objects
is base change along `F(K)^♯ ⟶ F(L)^♯`: an object `G ⟶ F(L)^♯` is sent to
`G ×_{F(L)^♯} F(K)^♯ ⟶ F(K)^♯`.

Following the source, this is Stacks 04IL applied to each re-localization morphism
`C / K.obj i ⟶ C / L.obj (f.f i)` — that is `hComponent` — and then assembled over the index set
by `assembleOverPullbackIso`, which is where the van Kampen property of the coproduct
`F(K)^♯ = ∐ i, h_{K.obj i}^♯` is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem componentwiseRelocalization_comp_sheafEquivalence_iso_pullback
    {K L : FormalCoproduct.{v} C} (f : K ⟶ L) :
    Nonempty
      (componentwiseRelocalization J f ⋙ (sheafEquivalence J K).functor ≅
        (sheafEquivalence J L).functor ⋙
          Over.pullback (formalCoproductSheafificationMap J f))
declarations.comment: (3): f^{-1} corresponds to base change along F(K)^sharp to F(L)^sharp

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.isEquivalence_sheafFunctorToOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D87 part (1).** The lower shriek functor `j_!` identifies sheaves on the
localization of `C` at a semi-representable object `K` with sheaves over the associated sheaf
`F(K)^♯`.

Following the source: `Sh(C / K)` is the product of the `Sh(C / K.obj i)` — which is how
`SheafOverFormalCoproduct` presents it — and `Sh(C)/F(K)^♯` is the product of the
`Sh(C)/h_{K.obj i}^♯` by `isEquivalence_sheafCoproductToOver`, so the statement follows from
Stacks 00Y1 for each component.
declarations.statement: theorem isEquivalence_sheafFunctorToOver : (sheafFunctorToOver J K).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: (1): the functor j_! is an equivalence Sh(C/K) to Sh(C)/F(K)^sharp

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.sheafEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D87 part (1)**, as an equivalence of categories
`Sh(C / K) ≌ Sh(C) / F(K)^♯`. Its functor is `sheafFunctorToOver`, the sheaf level `j_!` viewed
as a functor into the slice (`sheafEquivalence_functor`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafEquivalence :
    SheafOverFormalCoproduct J K ≌ Over (formalCoproductSheafification J K)
declarations.comment: (1): the resulting equivalence of categories Sh(C/K) to Sh(C)/F(K)^sharp

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.componentwiseRestrictionCompSheafFunctorToOverIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D87 part (2).** Under the identification of part (1), restriction
`j^{-1} : Sh(C) ⥤ Sh(C / K)` is `F ↦ (F × F(K)^♯ ⟶ F(K)^♯)`, i.e. Mathlib's
`CategoryTheory.toOver (F(K)^♯)`.

Following the source: `toOver A` is right adjoint to `Over.forget A`, and so is
`j^{-1} ⋙ j_!` read in the slice, because `j_! ⋙ Over.forget A ⊣ j^{-1}`
(`sheafFunctorToOverForgetAdjunction`) and `j_!` is an equivalence by part (1). Uniqueness of
right adjoints identifies them.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def componentwiseRestrictionCompSheafFunctorToOverIso :
    componentwiseRestriction J K ⋙ sheafFunctorToOver J K ≅
      toOver (formalCoproductSheafification J K)
declarations.comment: (2): j^{-1} corresponds to F maps to (F times F(K)^sharp over F(K)^sharp)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.componentwiseRestriction_comp_sheafEquivalence_iso_toOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D87 part (2)**, stated through the equivalence of categories of part (1): under
`sheafEquivalence`, componentwise restriction corresponds to `toOver (F(K)^♯)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem componentwiseRestriction_comp_sheafEquivalence_iso_toOver :
    Nonempty (componentwiseRestriction J K ⋙ (sheafEquivalence J K).functor ≅
      toOver (formalCoproductSheafification J K))
declarations.comment: (2): under the equivalence of (1), j^{-1} is toOver of F(K)^sharp

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.injective_localizationInverseImage_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D88.** The inverse image along the localization at a semi-representable object
sends injective abelian sheaves to injective abelian sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_localizationInverseImage_obj
    (I : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v t}) [Injective I] :
    Injective ((localizationInverseImage J K AddCommGrpCat.{max u v t}).obj I)
declarations.comment: injectives are preserved

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.isKInjective_localizationInverseImage_mapHomologicalComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D88.** Inverse image along the localization at a semi-representable object sends a
K-injective complex of abelian sheaves to a K-injective complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKInjective_localizationInverseImage_mapHomologicalComplex
    (I : CochainComplex (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] :
    ((localizationInverseImageMapHomologicalComplex J K).obj I).IsKInjective
declarations.comment: K-injective complexes are preserved

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.componentwiseLocalizationFunctor
declarations.doc:
The localization functor from the componentwise site `C / K` of a semi-representable object
`K` over `X` to `C / X`. On the component indexed by `i` it is relocalization along
`K.obj i : U i ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
def componentwiseLocalizationFunctor {X : C} (K : FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)) :
    ComponentOver (⟨K.I, fun i => (K.obj i).left⟩ : FormalCoproduct.{w} C) ⥤ Over X
declarations.comment: localization

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.componentwiseLocalizationFunctorCompIso
declarations.doc:
On each component, the functor `C / K ⥤ C / X` is canonically the relocalization functor
associated to the structural map `U i ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
def componentwiseLocalizationFunctorCompIso {X : C} (K : FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X))
    (i : K.I) :
    CategoryTheory.Sigma.incl (C := fun i : K.I => Over (K.obj i).left) i ⋙
      componentwiseLocalizationFunctor K ≅ Over.map (K.obj i).hom
declarations.comment: localization

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.componentwiseLocalization_isContinuous
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0D89.** The componentwise localization functor to `C / X` is continuous.
declarations.statement:
instance componentwiseLocalization_isContinuous :
    (componentwiseLocalizationFunctor K).IsContinuous
      (componentwiseTopology J
        (⟨K.I, fun i => (K.obj i).left⟩ : FormalCoproduct.{w} C))
  (J.over X)
declarations.comment: localization_property

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.componentwiseLocalization_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0D89.** The componentwise localization functor to `C / X` is cocontinuous.
declarations.statement:
instance componentwiseLocalization_isCocontinuous :
    (componentwiseLocalizationFunctor K).IsCocontinuous
      (componentwiseTopology J
        (⟨K.I, fun i => (K.obj i).left⟩ : FormalCoproduct.{w} C))
  (J.over X)
declarations.comment: localization_property

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.componentwiseLocalization_hasCoverPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D89.** The componentwise localization functor to `C / X` has property P:
pullbacks of covering families along maps out of its image are representable and cover.
declarations.statement:
lemma componentwiseLocalization_hasCoverPullbacks
    [(J.over X).toCoverage.HasPullbacks] :
    ∀ (𝒱 : Covering.{max u v, v, w'} (Over X)),
      𝒱.2.presieve₀ ∈ (J.over X).toCoverage 𝒱.1 →
      ∀ (U : ComponentOver
        (⟨K.I, fun i => (K.obj i).left⟩ : FormalCoproduct.{w} C))
        (g : (componentwiseLocalizationFunctor K).obj U ⟶ 𝒱.1),
        ∃ (P : 𝒱.2.I₀ → ComponentOver
            (⟨K.I, fun i => (K.obj i).left⟩ : FormalCoproduct.{w} C))
          (p₁ : ∀ i, P i ⟶ U)
          (p₂ : ∀ i, (componentwiseLocalizationFunctor K).obj (P i) ⟶ 𝒱.2.X i),
          (∀ i,
            (componentwiseLocalizationFunctor K).map (p₁ i) ≫ g =
              p₂ i ≫ 𝒱.2.f i ∧
              ∀ (T : ComponentOver
                  (⟨K.I, fun i => (K.obj i).left⟩ : FormalCoproduct.{w} C))
                (a : T ⟶ U)
                (b : (componentwiseLocalizationFunctor K).obj T ⟶ 𝒱.2.X i),
                (componentwiseLocalizationFunctor K).map a ≫ g = b ≫ 𝒱.2.f i →
                  ∃! l : T ⟶ P i,
                    (l ≫ p₁ i = a ∧
                      (componentwiseLocalizationFunctor K).map l ≫ p₂ i = b)) ∧
            (PreZeroHypercover.mk 𝒱.2.I₀ P p₁).presieve₀ ∈
              (componentwiseTopology J
                (⟨K.I, fun i => (K.obj i).left⟩ : FormalCoproduct.{w} C)).toCoverage U
declarations.comment: localization_property

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.componentwiseRelocalizationMorphismOfTopoi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D89.** The morphism of topoi from `Sh(C / K)` to `Sh(C / L)` induced by
componentwise relocalization along a morphism `K ⟶ L` of `SR(C, X)`, together with the
identification of its inverse image with restriction along the componentwise functor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def componentwiseRelocalizationMorphismOfTopoi
    {K L : FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)} (f : K ⟶ L) :
    let S := componentwiseLocalizationSitesOver J X f
    { g : MorphismOfTopoi
        (Sheaf S.sourceTopology (Type (max w v u)))
        (Sheaf S.targetTopology (Type (max w v u))) //
      g.inverseImage ⋙ sheafToPresheaf S.sourceTopology (Type (max w v u)) =
        sheafToPresheaf S.targetTopology (Type (max w v u)) ⋙
          (CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ _).obj S.relocalizationFunctor.op }
declarations.comment: relocalization

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.componentwiseRelocalization_isContinuous
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0D89.** The componentwise relocalization functor is continuous.
declarations.statement:
instance componentwiseRelocalization_isContinuous
    {K L : FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)} (f : K ⟶ L) :
    let S := componentwiseLocalizationSitesOver J X f
    S.relocalizationFunctor.IsContinuous S.sourceTopology S.targetTopology
declarations.comment: relocalization_property

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.componentwiseRelocalization_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0D89.** The componentwise relocalization functor is cocontinuous.
declarations.statement:
instance componentwiseRelocalization_isCocontinuous
    {K L : FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)} (f : K ⟶ L) :
    let S := componentwiseLocalizationSitesOver J X f
    S.relocalizationFunctor.IsCocontinuous S.sourceTopology S.targetTopology
declarations.comment: relocalization_property

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.componentwiseRelocalization_hasCoverPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D89.** The componentwise relocalization functor has property P: pullbacks of
covering families along maps out of its image are representable and covering.
declarations.statement:
lemma componentwiseRelocalization_hasCoverPullbacks
    {K L : FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)} (f : K ⟶ L)
    [J.toCoverage.HasPullbacks] :
    let S := componentwiseLocalizationSitesOver J X f
    S.relocalizationFunctor.HasCoverPullbacks
      (fun 𝒰 ↦ 𝒰.2.presieve₀ ∈ S.sourceTopology.toCoverage 𝒰.1)
      (fun 𝒱 ↦ 𝒱.2.presieve₀ ∈ S.targetTopology.toCoverage 𝒱.1)
declarations.comment: relocalization_property

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SemiRepresentable.componentwiseLocalizationPushforwardPullbackNatIsoSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D89.** The localization push-pull on `C / X` at a semi-representable object `K`
over `X` is naturally the sheaf internal hom out of the sheafification of the semi-representable
presheaf associated to `K`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def componentwiseLocalizationPushforwardPullbackNatIsoSheafHom
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (X : C)
    (K : FormalCoproduct.{u} (Over X)) :
    ((componentwiseLocalizationFunctor K).sheafPushforwardContinuous
      (Type u)
      (componentwiseTopology J
        (⟨K.I, fun i => (K.obj i).left⟩ : FormalCoproduct.{u} C))
      (J.over X)) ⋙
      ((componentwiseLocalizationFunctor K).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous
        (Type u)
        (componentwiseTopology J
          (⟨K.I, fun i => (K.obj i).left⟩ : FormalCoproduct.{u} C))
        (J.over X)) ≅
      CategoryTheory.SheafHomAdj.sheafHomFunctor
        ((presheafToSheaf (J.over X) (Type u)).obj
        ((FormalCoproduct.yoneda (C := Over X)).obj K))
declarations.comment: push_pull

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.stableAugmentation_functor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8B.** For an arbitrary site, the functor underlying the augmentation
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.stableAugmentation` is the degree-zero localization
functor `j_0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stableAugmentation_functor :
    (stableAugmentation J K).functor = sliceForget K (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))
declarations.comment: the functor underlying that augmentation is j_0

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.stableTotalPushforward_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8B.** For an arbitrary site, the morphism of topoi `a : Sh((C/K)_total) ⟶ Sh(C)`
which Stacks 0D70 attaches to the augmentation `j_0` is the morphism of topoi of the
localization functor `j_total`: their direct images are *equal*, because the cocontinuous
functor which Stacks 0D70 attaches to the augmentation is `j_total` on the nose.
declarations.statement:
theorem stableTotalPushforward_eq :
    (CocontinuousSimplicialSite.Augmentation.totalMorphismOfTopoi
        (stableAugmentation J K)).pushforward =
      (stableTotalLocalizationMorphism J K).pushforward
declarations.comment: a is the morphism of topoi of j_total: the direct images are equal

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.stableAugmentation
declarations.doc:
The localization functor `j_0 : C/K_0 ⥤ C` defines an augmentation of the simplicial site
`n ↦ C/K_n` towards `(C, J)`, as in case (B) of Stacks 0D6Z, as in Stacks 0D8B, for an arbitrary
site.
declarations.statement: def stableAugmentation : (stableSimplicialSite J K).Augmentation (Cat.of C) J
declarations.comment: j_0 defines an augmentation a_0 : Sh(C/K_0) to Sh(C), case (B) of 0D6Z

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.stableComponentPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
The morphism of topoi `a_n : Sh(C/K_n) ⟶ Sh(C)` which Stacks 0D70 attaches to the
augmentation `j_0` is the morphism of topoi of the localization functor `j_n`: their direct
images agree canonically, as in Stacks 0D8B, for an arbitrary site.
declarations.statement:
def stableComponentPushforwardIso (n : SimplexCategory) :
    (SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.componentAugmentation (stableSituation J K) (Cat.of C)
        J (stableSituationAugmentation J K) n).pushforward ≅
      (stableLocalizationMorphism J K n).pushforward
declarations.comment: a_n is the morphism of topoi of j_n: direct images

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.stableComponentInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8B.** The same identification in inverse images, obtained from uniqueness of left
adjoints.
declarations.statement:
def stableComponentInverseImageIso (n : SimplexCategory) :
    (SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.componentAugmentation (stableSituation J K) (Cat.of C)
        J (stableSituationAugmentation J K) n).inverseImage ≅
      (stableLocalizationMorphism J K n).inverseImage
declarations.comment: a_n is the morphism of topoi of j_n: inverse images

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.stableTotalInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8B.** The same identification in inverse images, obtained from uniqueness of left
adjoints.
declarations.statement:
def stableTotalInverseImageIso :
    (CocontinuousSimplicialSite.Augmentation.totalMorphismOfTopoi
        (stableAugmentation J K)).inverseImage ≅
      (stableTotalLocalizationMorphism J K).inverseImage
declarations.comment: a is the morphism of topoi of j_total: inverse images

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.faithful_situationTotalInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), the faithfulness half**, for the inverse image of the total augmentation
as Stacks 0D70 constructs it from the simplicial-site situation of a hypercovering: that inverse
image is faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithful_situationTotalInverseImage :
    (SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.totalMorphismOfTopoi
      (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject) (Cat.of C) P.toGrothendieck
      (situationAugmentation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject)).inverseImage.Faithful
declarations.comment: part (1): a^{-1} of Stacks 0D70 on sheaves of sets is faithful, for the simplicial-site situation attached to a hypercovering

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.faithful_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), the faithfulness half.** For a hypercovering `K` the inverse image
`a^{-1} : Sh(C) ⥤ Sh((C/K)_total)` of the augmentation is faithful.

The inverse image is restriction along `j_total`, which is continuous and cover dense, and
restriction along such a functor is faithful by Stacks 04D9.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithful_inverseImage [HasEqualizers C] [HasPullbacks C] (P : Pretopology C)
    (H : HypercoveringOfTerminal.{u, u, u} P) :
    (totalLocalizationMorphism P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).inverseImage.Faithful
declarations.comment: part (1): a^{-1} on sheaves of sets is faithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.faithful_totalInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), the faithfulness half**, for the inverse image of the morphism of topoi
which Stacks 0D70 attaches to the augmentation. By Stacks 0D8B that functor is isomorphic to
restriction along `j_total`, and faithfulness is invariant under isomorphism of functors.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithful_totalInverseImage [HasEqualizers C] [HasPullbacks C] (P : Pretopology C)
    (H : HypercoveringOfTerminal.{u, u, u} P) :
    Functor.Faithful
      (augmentation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalMorphismOfTopoi.inverseImage
declarations.comment: part (1): a^{-1} of Stacks 0D70 on sheaves of sets is faithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.faithful_abelianInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (2), the faithfulness half.** For a hypercovering `K` the inverse image
`a^{-1} : Ab(C) ⥤ Ab((C/K)_total)` of the augmentation — restriction along `j_total` on abelian
sheaves, as in Stacks 09WM (2) — is faithful.

Cover density of `j_total` is a statement about the site, so the argument of
`faithful_inverseImage` applies at any coefficient category.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithful_abelianInverseImage [HasEqualizers C] [HasPullbacks C] (P : Pretopology C)
    (H : HypercoveringOfTerminal.{u, u, u} P) :
    ((totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).sheafPushforwardContinuous Ab.{u}
      ((situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology)
      P.toGrothendieck).Faithful
declarations.comment: part (2): a^{-1} on abelian sheaves is faithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isCartesianSheaf_of_mem_essImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), the inclusion of the essential image in the cartesian sheaves.** Every
sheaf of sets on the total site isomorphic to an inverse image along the augmentation is
cartesian.

This is Stacks 0D7H (1) together with invariance of cartesianness under isomorphism, and uses no
condition on the simplicial semi-representable object `K`.
declarations.comment: part (1): the essential image of a^{-1} consists of cartesian sheaves of sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isCartesianAbSheaf_of_mem_essImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (2), the inclusion of the essential image in the cartesian sheaves.** Every
sheaf of abelian groups on the total site isomorphic to an inverse image along the augmentation is
cartesian.

Cartesianness of an abelian sheaf is cartesianness of its underlying sheaf of sets, and the
underlying sheaf of the restriction of `𝒢` along `j_total` is the restriction of the underlying
sheaf of `𝒢`, both being a composition of functors. So the abelian statement follows from the
statement for sheaves of sets applied to the underlying sheaf.
declarations.comment: part (2): the essential image of a^{-1} consists of cartesian abelian sheaves

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.full_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), fullness**, carrying local fullness of `j_total`.

For a hypercovering `K` the inverse image `a^{-1} : Sh(C) ⥤ Sh((C/K)_total)` of the augmentation
is full as soon as the localization functor `j_total` is locally full for the topology of `C`.
That local fullness — unwound at two objects of the total site, the local existence of a simplex
of `K` carrying two prescribed charts on two of its faces — is the input the degree-zero
condition does not supply, and it is carried here as a hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem full_inverseImage
    (hlf : (totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).IsLocallyFull P.toGrothendieck) :
    (totalLocalizationMorphism P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).inverseImage.Full
declarations.comment: part (1): a^{-1} on sheaves of sets is full, carrying local fullness of j_total

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.fullyFaithfulInverseImageHypercovering
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0D8E (1), full faithfulness**, carrying local fullness of `j_total`.
declarations.statement:
def fullyFaithfulInverseImageHypercovering
    (hlf : (totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).IsLocallyFull P.toGrothendieck) :
    (totalLocalizationMorphism P.toGrothendieck
      H.toSimplicialObject).inverseImage.FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: part (1): a^{-1} on sheaves of sets is fully faithful, carrying local fullness

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isIso_unit_hypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), the unit is invertible**, carrying local fullness of `j_total`: for every
sheaf of sets `E` on `C` the canonical map `E ⟶ a_* a^{-1} E` is an isomorphism. This is the
half of "`a_*` is a quasi-inverse" that holds on all of `Sh(C)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_unit_hypercovering
    (hlf : (totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).IsLocallyFull P.toGrothendieck) :
    IsIso (totalLocalizationMorphism P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).adj.unit
declarations.comment: part (1): E = a_* a^{-1} E on sheaves of sets, carrying local fullness

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.mem_essImage_iff_isCartesianSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), the essential image is exactly the cartesian sheaves**, carrying
essential surjectivity onto them. One inclusion is `isCartesianSheaf_of_mem_essImage`; the other
is the clause the degree-zero condition does not supply, and it is carried as a hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_essImage_iff_isCartesianSheaf
    (hsurj : ∀ G : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology
        (Type u),
      (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianSheaf G →
        (totalLocalizationMorphism P.toGrothendieck
          H.toSimplicialObject).inverseImage.essImage G)
    (F : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology (Type u)) :
    (totalLocalizationMorphism P.toGrothendieck
        H.toSimplicialObject).inverseImage.essImage F ↔
      (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianSheaf F
declarations.comment: part (1): essential image = cartesian sheaves of sets, carrying surjectivity

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isIso_counit_app_hypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), the counit is invertible on cartesian sheaves**, carrying both of the two
clauses: for a cartesian sheaf of sets `F` on the total site the canonical map
`a^{-1} a_* F ⟶ F` is an isomorphism. This is the half of "`a_*` is a quasi-inverse" that holds
on the cartesian sheaves; the two carried hypotheses supply full faithfulness of `a^{-1}` and
membership of `F` in its essential image.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_counit_app_hypercovering
    (hlf : (totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).IsLocallyFull P.toGrothendieck)
    (hsurj : ∀ G : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology
        (Type u),
      (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianSheaf G →
        (totalLocalizationMorphism P.toGrothendieck
          H.toSimplicialObject).inverseImage.essImage G)
    {F : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology (Type u)}
    (hF : (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianSheaf F) :
    IsIso ((totalLocalizationMorphism P.toGrothendieck
      H.toSimplicialObject).adj.counit.app F)
declarations.comment: part (1): a^{-1} a_* F = F for cartesian F, carrying both remaining clauses

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.full_abelianInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (2), fullness**, carrying local fullness of `j_total`. Local fullness is a
condition on the site, so the same input serves at abelian coefficients.
declarations.statement:
theorem full_abelianInverseImage
    (hlf : (totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).IsLocallyFull P.toGrothendieck) :
    ((totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).sheafPushforwardContinuous Ab.{u}
      ((situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology)
      P.toGrothendieck).Full
declarations.comment: part (2): a^{-1} on abelian sheaves is full, carrying local fullness of j_total

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.fullyFaithfulAbelianInverseImageHypercovering
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0D8E (2), full faithfulness**, carrying local fullness of `j_total`.
declarations.statement:
def fullyFaithfulAbelianInverseImageHypercovering
    (hlf : (totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).IsLocallyFull P.toGrothendieck) :
    ((totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).sheafPushforwardContinuous Ab.{u}
      ((situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology)
      P.toGrothendieck).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: part (2): a^{-1} on abelian sheaves is fully faithful, carrying local fullness

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isIso_abelianUnit_hypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (2), the unit is invertible**, carrying local fullness of `j_total`: for every
sheaf of abelian groups `E` on `C` the canonical map `E ⟶ a_* a^{-1} E` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_abelianUnit_hypercovering
    (hlf : (totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).IsLocallyFull P.toGrothendieck) :
    IsIso (abelianTotalAdjunction P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).unit
declarations.comment: part (2): E = a_* a^{-1} E on abelian sheaves, carrying local fullness

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.mem_essImage_iff_isCartesianAbSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (2), the essential image is exactly the cartesian abelian sheaves**, carrying
essential surjectivity onto them.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_essImage_iff_isCartesianAbSheaf
    (hsurj : ∀ G : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology Ab.{u},
      (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianAbSheaf G →
        ((totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).sheafPushforwardContinuous Ab.{u}
          ((situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology)
          P.toGrothendieck).essImage G)
    (F : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology Ab.{u}) :
    ((totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).sheafPushforwardContinuous Ab.{u}
        ((situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology)
        P.toGrothendieck).essImage F ↔
      (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianAbSheaf F
declarations.comment: part (2): essential image = cartesian abelian sheaves, carrying surjectivity

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isIso_abelianCounit_app_hypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (2), the counit is invertible on cartesian abelian sheaves**, carrying both of
the two clauses: for a cartesian sheaf of abelian groups `F` on the total site the canonical map
`a^{-1} a_* F ⟶ F` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_abelianCounit_app_hypercovering
    (hlf : (totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).IsLocallyFull P.toGrothendieck)
    (hsurj : ∀ G : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology Ab.{u},
      (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianAbSheaf G →
        ((totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).sheafPushforwardContinuous Ab.{u}
          ((situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology)
          P.toGrothendieck).essImage G)
    {F : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology Ab.{u}}
    (hF : (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianAbSheaf F) :
    IsIso ((abelianTotalAdjunction P.toGrothendieck
      H.toSimplicialObject).counit.app F)
declarations.comment: part (2): a^{-1} a_* F = F for cartesian F, carrying both remaining clauses

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.mem_essImage_iff_isCartesianSheaf'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), the essential image is exactly the cartesian sheaves of sets.** A sheaf of
sets on the total site of a hypercovering of the final presheaf lies in the essential image of
restriction along the localization functor `j_total` if and only if it is cartesian.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_essImage_iff_isCartesianSheaf' (P : Pretopology C)
    (H : HypercoveringOfTerminal.{u, u, u} P)
    (E : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology (Type u)) :
    (totalLocalizationMorphism P.toGrothendieck
        H.toSimplicialObject).inverseImage.essImage E ↔
      (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianSheaf E
declarations.comment: part (1): essential image = cartesian sheaves of sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isIso_counit_app_hypercovering'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), `a⁻¹ a_* F = F` for cartesian `F`.** For a cartesian sheaf of sets `E` on
the total site of a hypercovering of the final presheaf, the counit `a⁻¹ a_* E ⟶ E` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_counit_app_hypercovering' (P : Pretopology C)
    (H : HypercoveringOfTerminal.{u, u, u} P)
    (E : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology (Type u))
    (hE : (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianSheaf E) :
    IsIso ((totalLocalizationMorphism P.toGrothendieck
      H.toSimplicialObject).adj.counit.app E)
declarations.comment: part (1): a^{-1} a_* F = F for cartesian F

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.mem_essImage_iff_isCartesianAbSheaf'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (2), the essential image is exactly the cartesian abelian sheaves.** One
inclusion is `isCartesianAbSheaf_of_mem_essImage`, the other is
`essImage_of_isCartesianAbSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_essImage_iff_isCartesianAbSheaf' (P : Pretopology C)
    (H : HypercoveringOfTerminal.{u, u, u} P)
    (G : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology Ab.{u}) :
    ((totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).sheafPushforwardContinuous Ab.{u}
        ((situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology)
        P.toGrothendieck).essImage G ↔
      (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianAbSheaf G
declarations.comment: part (2): essential image = cartesian abelian sheaves

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isIso_abelianCounit_app_hypercovering'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (2), `a⁻¹ a_* F = F` for cartesian `F`.** For a cartesian sheaf of abelian
groups `F` on the total site the canonical map `a⁻¹ a_* F ⟶ F` is an isomorphism. This is the
half of "`a_*` is a quasi-inverse" that holds on the cartesian abelian sheaves: `a⁻¹` is fully
faithful, so its counit is invertible exactly on its essential image, and
`essImage_of_isCartesianAbSheaf` puts `F` there.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_abelianCounit_app_hypercovering' (P : Pretopology C)
    (H : HypercoveringOfTerminal.{u, u, u} P)
    (G : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology Ab.{u})
    (hG : (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianAbSheaf G) :
    IsIso ((abelianTotalAdjunction P.toGrothendieck
      H.toSimplicialObject).counit.app G)
declarations.comment: part (2): a^{-1} a_* F = F for cartesian abelian F

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.essImage_situationTotalInverseImage_of_isCartesianSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), essential surjectivity onto the cartesian sheaves of sets**, for the
inverse image of the morphism of topoi which Stacks 0D70 attaches to the augmentation of the
simplicial-site situation of a hypercovering.

By Stacks 0D8B that inverse image is restriction along `j_total`, for which every cartesian sheaf
of sets is an inverse image by
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.essImage_of_isCartesianSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_situationTotalInverseImage_of_isCartesianSheaf
    (E : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology (Type u))
    (hE : (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianSheaf E) :
    (Augmentation.totalMorphismOfTopoi
      (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject) (Cat.of C) P.toGrothendieck
      (situationAugmentation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject)).inverseImage.essImage E
declarations.comment: part (1): every cartesian sheaf of sets is an a^{-1}E for the a of Stacks 0D70 at the simplicial-site situation

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.mem_essImage_situationTotalInverseImage_iff_isCartesianSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), the essential image is exactly the cartesian sheaves of sets**, for the
inverse image of the morphism of topoi of Stacks 0D70 at the simplicial-site situation. One
inclusion is `mem_essImage_iff_isCartesianSheaf'` carried across Stacks 0D8B, the other is
`essImage_situationTotalInverseImage_of_isCartesianSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_essImage_situationTotalInverseImage_iff_isCartesianSheaf
    (E : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology (Type u)) :
    (Augmentation.totalMorphismOfTopoi
        (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject) (Cat.of C) P.toGrothendieck
        (situationAugmentation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject)).inverseImage.essImage E ↔
      (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianSheaf E
declarations.comment: part (1): the essential image of the a^{-1} of Stacks 0D70 at the simplicial-site situation is exactly the cartesian sheaves of sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.essImage_situationTotalInverseImageAb_of_isCartesianAbSheaf
declarations.doc:
Every cartesian abelian sheaf on the total site lies in the essential image of the abelian
inverse image of the morphism of topoi which Stacks 0D70 attaches to the augmentation of the
simplicial-site situation of a hypercovering.
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_situationTotalInverseImageAb_of_isCartesianAbSheaf (P : Pretopology C)
    (H : HypercoveringOfTerminal.{u, u, u} P)
    (G : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology Ab.{u})
    (hG : (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianAbSheaf G) :
    (Augmentation.totalInverseImageAb (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject)
      (Cat.of C) P.toGrothendieck
      (situationAugmentation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject)).essImage G
declarations.comment: part (2): every cartesian abelian sheaf is an a^{-1}G for the a of Stacks 0D70 at the simplicial-site situation

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.mem_essImage_situationTotalInverseImageAb_iff_isCartesianAbSheaf
declarations.doc:
The essential image of the abelian inverse image of the morphism of topoi of Stacks 0D70 at
the simplicial-site situation of a hypercovering is exactly the cartesian abelian sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_essImage_situationTotalInverseImageAb_iff_isCartesianAbSheaf (P : Pretopology C)
    (H : HypercoveringOfTerminal.{u, u, u} P)
    (G : Sheaf (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology Ab.{u}) :
    (Augmentation.totalInverseImageAb (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject)
        (Cat.of C) P.toGrothendieck
        (situationAugmentation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject)).essImage G ↔
      (situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).IsCartesianAbSheaf G
declarations.comment: part (2): the essential image of the a^{-1} of Stacks 0D70 at the simplicial-site situation is exactly the cartesian abelian sheaves

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.full_inverseImage'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), fullness.** For a hypercovering `K` the inverse image
`a^{-1} : Sh(C) ⥤ Sh((C/K)_total)` of the augmentation is full.

The localization functor `j_total` is cover dense by `isCoverDense_totalForget` and locally full
by `isLocallyFull_totalForget`, and restriction along a continuous functor which is both is
full.
declarations.statement:
theorem full_inverseImage' :
    (totalLocalizationMorphism P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).inverseImage.Full
declarations.comment: part (1): a^{-1} on sheaves of sets is full

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.fullyFaithfulInverseImageHypercovering'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), full faithfulness.** For a hypercovering `K` the inverse image
`a^{-1} : Sh(C) ⥤ Sh((C/K)_total)` of the augmentation is fully faithful: it is faithful by
`faithful_inverseImage_of_isCoverDense` and full by `full_inverseImage'`.
declarations.comment: part (1): a^{-1} on sheaves of sets is fully faithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isIso_unit_hypercovering'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (1), `E = a_* a^{-1} E`.** For every sheaf of sets `E` on `C` the canonical
map `E ⟶ a_* a^{-1} E` is an isomorphism, `a^{-1}` being restriction along `j_total`. This is the
half of "`a_*` is a quasi-inverse" that holds on all of `Sh(C)`: the unit of an adjunction with
fully faithful left adjoint is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_unit_hypercovering' :
    IsIso (totalLocalizationMorphism P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).adj.unit
declarations.comment: part (1): E = a_* a^{-1} E on sheaves of sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.full_abelianInverseImage'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (2), fullness.** For a hypercovering `K` the inverse image
`a^{-1} : Ab(C) ⥤ Ab((C/K)_total)` of the augmentation is full. Cover density and local fullness
of `j_total` are conditions on the site, so the same input serves at abelian coefficients.
declarations.statement:
theorem full_abelianInverseImage' :
    ((totalForget H.toSimplicialObject).sheafPushforwardContinuous Ab.{u}
      ((situation P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).totalTopology)
      P.toGrothendieck).Full
declarations.comment: part (2): a^{-1} on abelian sheaves is full

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.fullyFaithfulAbelianInverseImageHypercovering'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (2), full faithfulness.** For a hypercovering `K` the inverse image
`a^{-1} : Ab(C) ⥤ Ab((C/K)_total)` of the augmentation is fully faithful.
declarations.comment: part (2): a^{-1} on abelian sheaves is fully faithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isIso_abelianUnit_hypercovering'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8E (2), `E = a_* a^{-1} E`.** For every sheaf of abelian groups `E` on `C` the
canonical map `E ⟶ a_* a^{-1} E` is an isomorphism, `a^{-1}` being restriction along
`j_total`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_abelianUnit_hypercovering' :
    IsIso (abelianTotalAdjunction P.toGrothendieck H.toSimplicialObject).unit
declarations.comment: part (2): E = a_* a^{-1} E on abelian sheaves

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.cechComplexIsoSheafHomComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8F.** The Čech complex of Stacks 0D79 associated to `a⁻¹F`,

`a_{0,*}a_0⁻¹F ⟶ a_{1,*}a_1⁻¹F ⟶ a_{2,*}a_2⁻¹F ⟶ …`

is canonically isomorphic — the source says equal, and the comparison is indeed the identity in
every degree once the terms are identified — to the cochain complex
`SheafHom(s(ℤ_{F(K)}^#), F)` obtained by applying the abelian internal hom `ℋom(-, F)` to the
complex of free abelian sheaves of Stacks 01GB.

The differentials of both complexes are the alternating sums induced by the simplicial structure
of `K`, so a cosimplicial identification of the terms suffices; that is the whole of the source's
argument. The identification of the terms itself,
`a_{n,*}a_n⁻¹F = ℋom'(F(K_n)^#, F) = ℋom(ℤ_{F(K_n)}^#, F)`, is
`cechCosimplicialObjectIsoSheafHomCosimplicialObject`.
declarations.statement:
def cechComplexIsoSheafHomComplex (F : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u}) :
    cechComplex J K F ≅ sheafHomComplex J K F

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isIso_derivedAugmentationUnit_app_of_hypercovering_unconditional
declarations.doc:
For a site `C` with equalizers and fibre products, a hypercovering `K` of it and the
augmentation `a : Sh((C/K)_total) ⟶ Sh(C)` of Stacks 0D8B, the canonical map `E ⟶ Ra_* a⁻¹ E` is
an isomorphism at every object `E` of the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on `C`.

No boundedness is assumed on `E`, as in the source. The untagged forms
`Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isIso_derivedAugmentationUnit_app_of_hypercovering'` and
`Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isIso_derivedAugmentationUnit_app_of_hypercovering` take the
`Ra_*`-acyclicity of `a⁻¹` of a K-injective complex (and, for the latter, Stacks 0D8E) as
hypotheses; here the acyclicity is
`inverseImageComputesDerivedPushforward_of_hypercoveringOfTerminal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedAugmentationUnit_app_of_hypercovering_unconditional
    (E : DerivedCategory (Sheaf P.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{u})) :
    IsIso ((Augmentation.derivedAugmentationUnit (hypercoveringSituation P H) (Cat.of C)
      P.toGrothendieck (hypercoveringAugmentation P H)).app E)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIsoOfHypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8H.** For a site `C` with equalizers and fibre products, a hypercovering `K` of
it, and the augmentation `a : Sh((C/K)_total) ⟶ Sh(C)` of Stacks 0D8B, derived global sections on
`C` are derived global sections on the total site of the inverse image:

`RΓ(C, E) = RΓ((C/K)_total, a⁻¹E)`.

The statement is an isomorphism of functors on the *unbounded* derived category of abelian
sheaves on `C`, so it holds at every object `E` with no boundedness assumption, which is the form
the source states.

No hypothesis beyond the hypercovering conditions on `K` is carried: the three inputs of the
general `CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIso`
are proved for this augmentation. The underived unit `F ⟶ a_*a⁻¹F` is invertible by
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isIso_situationAbelianTotalAdjunctionUnit` (Stacks
0D8E in its abelian form), `a⁻¹` of a K-injective complex computes `R a_*` by
`SimplicialSemiRepresentable.inverseImageComputesDerivedPushforward_of_hypercoveringOfTerminal`,
and the underived identity `Γ(C, a_*F) = Γ((C/K)_total, F)` is
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.abelianTotalPushforwardGammaIso`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIsoOfHypercovering :
    Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsBase (Cat.of C) J.toGrothendieck ≅
      Augmentation.derivedTotalInverseImage (hypercoveringSituation J H) (Cat.of C)
          J.toGrothendieck (hypercoveringAugmentation J H) ⋙
        Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsTotal (hypercoveringSituation J H)
declarations.comment: for the augmentation of Tag 0D8B attached to a hypercovering

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIsoOfHypercovering'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8H.** For a site `C` with equalizers
and fibre products, a hypercovering `K` of it, and the augmentation
`a : Sh((C/K)_total) ⟶ Sh(C)` of Stacks 0D8B, derived global sections on `C` are derived global
sections on the total site of the inverse image:

`RΓ(C, E) = RΓ((C/K)_total, a⁻¹E)`.

The statement is an isomorphism of functors on the *unbounded* derived category of abelian
sheaves on `C`, so it holds at every object `E` with no boundedness assumption, which is the form
the source states.

No hypothesis beyond the hypercovering conditions on `K` is carried. The `R a_*`-acyclicity of
`a⁻¹` of a K-injective complex, which is the one remaining input of Stacks 0D8G, is
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable`
`.inverseImageComputesDerivedPushforward_of_hypercoveringOfTerminal`. The other input of
Stacks 0D8G, that the underived unit `F ⟶ a_*a⁻¹F` is an isomorphism, is Stacks 0D8E in its
abelian form, which
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isIso_situationAbelianTotalAdjunctionUnit` proves for
this augmentation. The underived identity `Γ(C, a_*F) = Γ((C/K)_total, F)` on which the
factorisation of Stacks 08J6 rests is
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.abelianTotalPushforwardGammaIso`. The derived content
of Stacks 08J6 is *not* assumed: see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
def derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIsoOfHypercovering' :
    Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsBase (Cat.of C) J.toGrothendieck ≅
      Augmentation.derivedTotalInverseImage (hypercoveringSituation J H) (Cat.of C)
          J.toGrothendieck (hypercoveringAugmentation J H) ⋙
        Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsTotal (hypercoveringSituation J H)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.derivedTotalInverseImageEquivalenceOfHypercovering'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8I.** For a site `C` with
equalizers and fibre products, a hypercovering `K` of it, the augmentation `a` of Stacks 0D8B and
the weak Serre subcategory `𝒜 ⊂ Ab((C/K)_total)` of cartesian abelian sheaves of Stacks 0D7J, the
derived inverse image is an equivalence

`a⁻¹ : D⁺(C) ⟶ D⁺_𝒜((C/K)_total)`

with quasi-inverse `R a_*`. Both functors of the equivalence are the restrictions of `a⁻¹` and
of `R a_*` on the nose, since the equivalence is the restricted adjunction.

The `Ra_*`-acyclicity input of Stacks 0D8G, that `a⁻¹` of a K-injective complex computes
`R a_*`, is `CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable`
`.inverseImageComputesDerivedPushforward_of_hypercoveringOfTerminal`. The other input of
Stacks 0D8G, that the underived unit `F ⟶ a_*a⁻¹F` is an isomorphism, is Stacks 0D8E in its
abelian form, which
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.isIso_situationAbelianTotalAdjunctionUnit` proves for
this augmentation. The essential surjectivity input of
`Augmentation.isIso_derivedCounit_app_of_isCartesian`, that every cartesian abelian sheaf on the
total site lies in the essential image of `a⁻¹`, is discharged here by
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable`
`.essImage_situationTotalInverseImageAb_of_isCartesianAbSheaf`,
the Stacks 0D8E (2) clause in the spelling of `a⁻¹` as `Augmentation.totalInverseImageAb`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTotalInverseImageEquivalenceOfHypercovering' :
    (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
        (⊤ : ObjectProperty (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{u}))).FullSubcategory ≌
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
        ((hypercoveringSituation J H).IsCartesianAbSheaf)).FullSubcategory

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.derivedTotalInverseImageEquivalenceOfHypercovering_functor'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8I, the forward functor of the equivalence is `a⁻¹`:** it is the restriction of
the derived inverse image to the bounded below subcategories.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTotalInverseImageEquivalenceOfHypercovering_functor' :
    (derivedTotalInverseImageEquivalenceOfHypercovering' J H).functor =
      Augmentation.derivedTotalInverseImagePlus (hypercoveringSituation J H) (Cat.of C)
        J.toGrothendieck (hypercoveringAugmentation J H)
declarations.comment: the forward functor of the equivalence is a⁻¹

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.derivedTotalInverseImageEquivalenceOfHypercovering_inverse'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8I, the quasi-inverse of the equivalence is `R a_*`:** it is the restriction of
the derived direct image to the bounded below subcategories.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTotalInverseImageEquivalenceOfHypercovering_inverse' :
    (derivedTotalInverseImageEquivalenceOfHypercovering' J H).inverse =
      Augmentation.derivedTotalPushforwardPlus (hypercoveringSituation J H) (Cat.of C)
        J.toGrothendieck (hypercoveringAugmentation J H)
declarations.comment: the quasi-inverse of the equivalence is Ra_*

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactQcSite.mem_essImage_iff_isCartesianSheaf_qcAugmentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0D8K (1) for a hypercovering augmentation of `LC_qc`.** Let `a : U ⟶ Y` be a
hypercovering augmentation of an object `Y` of the quasi-compact site, in the sense of
