declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocallyFiniteTypeEtale.exists_isQuasiCompactCovering
declarations.doc:
Every scheme locally of finite type over `S` has an étale covering whose members are
quasi-compact.
declarations.comment: every object of C is covered by members of B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocallyFiniteTypeEtale.exists_isQuasiCompactCovering_le
declarations.doc:
Every étale covering sieve of a scheme locally of finite type over `S` is refined by an
étale covering whose members are quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isQuasiCompactCovering_le (V : LocallyFiniteTypeEtale S) (R : Sieve V)
    (hR : R ∈ topology S V) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → LocallyFiniteTypeEtale S) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ V),
      IsQuasiCompactCovering U f ∧ Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows U f) ≤ R
declarations.comment: Cov_V is a cofinal system of coverings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsUnboundedDescentEtaleBase
declarations.doc:
**The types of base scheme of Stacks 0DC6.**  `S` is the spectrum of a finite field, the
spectrum of a separably closed field, the spectrum of a strictly henselian Noetherian local ring,
or the spectrum of a henselian Noetherian local ring with finite residue field.
declarations.statement: def IsUnboundedDescentEtaleBase (S : Scheme.{u}) : Prop
declarations.comment: the four types of base scheme S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsUnboundedDescentEtaleBase.exists_natCast_eq_etaleCohomologyBound
declarations.doc:
**The bound `d_V` of Stacks 0DC6 is an integer.**  For `S` of one of the four types of
Stacks 0DC6 and `V` a quasi-compact scheme locally of finite type over `S`, the bound
`d_V = 1 + 2 dim(S) + sup_{v ∈ V} (trdeg_{κ(s)} κ(v) + 2 dim 𝒪_{V, v})` is a natural number.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_natCast_eq_etaleCohomologyBound {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (hS : IsUnboundedDescentEtaleBase S) (V : LocallyFiniteTypeEtale S)
    (hV : LocallyFiniteTypeEtale.IsQuasiCompact V) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, V.obj.hom.etaleCohomologyBound = d
declarations.comment: d_V is an integer for V in B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocallyFiniteTypeEtale.localSerre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DC6.** Let `S` be the spectrum of a finite field, of a separably closed field, of a
strictly henselian Noetherian local ring, or of a henselian Noetherian local ring with finite
residue field, and let `Λ` be a finite ring whose order is invertible on `S`. On the ringed site
`(C, Λ)` of schemes locally of finite type over `S`, the family `A_U` of all sheaves of
`Λ`-modules satisfies conditions (1), (2), (3) of Stacks 0DC1, with `B` the quasi-compact
objects, `d_V = 1 + 2 dim(S) + sup_{v ∈ V} (trdeg_{κ(s)} κ(v) + 2 dim 𝒪_{V, v})` and `Cov_V`
the étale coverings of `V` by quasi-compact objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem localSerre (Λ : Type u) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    (hS : IsUnboundedDescentEtaleBase S) (hn : IsUnit (Nat.card Λ : Γ(S, ⊤))) :
    (∀ U, (allModules S Λ U).IsWeakSerreClass) ∧
      IsStableUnderRestriction (ringedSite S Λ) (allModules S Λ) ∧
      IsLocalOnCoverings (ringedSite S Λ) (allModules S Λ) ∧
      ∃ b : LocalCohomologicalBound (ringedSite S Λ) (allModules S Λ),
        b.B = {V | IsQuasiCompact ((liftedEquiv S).inverse.obj V)} ∧
        (∀ V hV, ∃ d : ℕ, b.degreeBound V hV = d ∧
          ((liftedEquiv S).inverse.obj V).obj.hom.etaleCohomologyBound = d) ∧
        ∀ V hV (𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} V),
          (b.coverings V hV).cov 𝒰 ↔ IsQuasiCompactEtaleCovering 𝒰
declarations.comment: all four types

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.exists_derivedPullbackEquivalence_localSerreFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DC7.** Let `(C, O_C)` be a ringed site with equalizers and fibre products, and let
`A_U ⊂ Mod(O_U)` be weak Serre subcategories satisfying conditions 0DC2, 0DC3 and 0DC4 (the
fields of `T : LocalSerreFamily`), with `A ⊂ Mod(O_C)` the modules whose restriction to every
`C/U` lies in `A_U`. Let `K` be a hypercovering of `C`, let
`a : ((C/K)_total, O) ⟶ (C, O_C)` be the ringed augmentation of Remark 0D9W, with `O = a⁻¹O_C`,
and let `A_total ⊂ Mod(O)` be the cartesian `O`-modules `F` whose restriction `F_n` lies in
`A_{K_n} = ∏_i A_{U_{n,i}}` for every `n`. Then `A_total` is a weak Serre subcategory of
`Mod(O)`, and `La^*` defines an equivalence

`D_A(O_C) ⟶ D_{A_total}(O)`

with quasi-inverse `Ra_*`: there is an equivalence of the full subcategories of the unbounded
derived categories on the objects with cohomology in `A`, respectively `A_total`, whose functor
is the restriction of the derived pullback `La^*` and whose inverse is the restriction of the
derived direct image `Ra_*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedPullbackEquivalence_localSerreFamily :
    (totalLocalSerre J H OC T).IsWeakSerreClass ∧
      ∃ e : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (baseLocalSerre J OC T)).FullSubcategory ≌
          (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (totalLocalSerre J H OC T)).FullSubcategory,
        e.functor ⋙ (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (totalLocalSerre J H OC T)).ι =
            (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (baseLocalSerre J OC T)).ι ⋙
              (RingedToposHom.leftDerivedPullbackOfIsIsoFSharp
                (hypercoveringRingedAugmentation J H OC).totalRingedHom).functor ∧
          e.inverse ⋙ (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (baseLocalSerre J OC T)).ι =
            (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (totalLocalSerre J H OC T)).ι ⋙
              derivedPushforward (X := (hypercoveringSituation J H).totalRingedTopos
                (hypercoveringRingedAugmentation J H OC).O)
                (Y := (hypercoveringRingedAugmentation J H OC).augmentationRingedTopos)
                (hypercoveringRingedAugmentation J H OC).totalRingedHom

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.isWeakSerreClass_cartesianDegreewiseModules
declarations.doc:
`A_total` is a weak Serre subcategory of `Mod(O)`. Let `O` be a sheaf of commutative rings on
the total site of a simplicial-site situation such that the pullback of modules along the
transition morphism of each face map is left exact, and let `A_n` be a weak Serre subcategory of
the category of modules on the degree-`n` component, for every `n`. Then the cartesian
`O`-modules whose restriction to each component lies in the class there form a weak Serre
subcategory of `Mod(O)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakSerreClass_cartesianDegreewiseModules
    (hflat : ∀ (k : ℕ) (i : Fin (k + 2)),
      PreservesFiniteLimits
        ((S.transitionRingedToposHom O (SimplexCategory.δ i)).toModulesHom.pullbackModules))
    (hA : ∀ n : SimplexCategory, (A n).IsWeakSerreClass) :
    (cartesianDegreewiseModules S O A).IsWeakSerreClass
declarations.comment: the class A_total of cartesian O-modules whose restriction to each simplicial component lies in the prescribed class there is a weak Serre subcategory of Mod(O). Two hypotheses are carried: hflat, left exactness of the pullback of modules along the transition morphism of each face map, which is the hypothesis in the shape this library's Tag 0D7J (2) takes it and is weaker than the source's flatness of the face transitions; and hA, that each A_n is a weak Serre subcategory. The family A_n is arbitrary, where the source takes the family A_{K_n} = prod_i A_{U_{n,i}} attached to a LocalSerreFamily, i.e. to Tags 0DC2, 0DC3 and 0DC4; assembling that particular family needs the module form of Tag 0D89 and is not available. NOT covered: the equivalence D_A(O_C) = D_{A_total}(O), the two assertions that La^* and Ra_* preserve the classes, and the identification of the two functors of the equivalence -- the unbounded engine of Tag 0D7V is stated for a RingedToposSiteHom and the augmentation of a hypercovering admits no such presentation. NOT covered either: that a^* induces an equivalence A = A_total, whose descent half needs the covering argument on the slices C/U_{n,i}

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CohomologicalDescent.isWeakSerreClass_cartesianDegreewiseModules_hypercovering
declarations.doc:
`A_total` is a weak Serre subcategory, at the total ringed site of a hypercovering. Let `C` be
a site with equalizers and fibre products, let `O_C` be a sheaf of commutative rings on it and let
`K` be a hypercovering of `C`; let `a : (Sh((C/K)_total), O) ⟶ (Sh(C), O_C)` be the ringed
augmentation of Stacks 0D9W, so that `O = a⁻¹O_C`. For a family `A_n` of weak Serre
subcategories of the categories of modules on the localizations `C/K_n`, the cartesian
`O`-modules whose restriction `F_n` lies in `A_n` for every `n` form a weak Serre subcategory of
`Mod(O)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakSerreClass_cartesianDegreewiseModules_hypercovering {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasEqualizers C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasPullbacks C]
    (J : Pretopology C)
    (H : Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.HypercoveringOfTerminal.{u, u} J)
    (OC : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck CommRingCat.{u})
    (A : ∀ n : SimplexCategory, ObjectProperty (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (componentRingSheaf (hypercoveringSituation J H)
        ((hypercoveringSituation J H).totalRingSheaf
          (hypercoveringRingedAugmentation J H OC).O) n)))
    (hflat : ∀ (k : ℕ) (i : Fin (k + 2)), PreservesFiniteLimits
      (((hypercoveringSituation J H).transitionRingedToposHom
        (hypercoveringRingedAugmentation J H OC).O
        (SimplexCategory.δ i)).toModulesHom.pullbackModules))
    (hA : ∀ n : SimplexCategory, (A n).IsWeakSerreClass) :
    (cartesianDegreewiseModules (hypercoveringSituation J H)
      (hypercoveringRingedAugmentation J H OC).O A).IsWeakSerreClass
declarations.comment: the class A_total is a weak Serre subcategory of Mod(O), at the total ringed site of a hypercovering with O = a^{-1}O_C, i.e. for the site and structure sheaf of Tag 0D9W. Same two hypotheses as the general form: hflat, left exactness of the pullback of modules along the transition morphism of each face map, and hA, that each A_n is a weak Serre subcategory; and the same restriction, that the family A_n is arbitrary rather than the source's prod_i A_{U_{n,i}}. None of the derived assertions of the tag are covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.LocallyGiven
declarations.doc:
Derived objects given locally on a category mapping to a ringed site, with isomorphisms on
restriction satisfying the cocycle condition: a category `B` with a functor `u : B ⥤ 𝒞`, an object
`E_U` of `D(𝒪_{u(U)})` for every object `U` of `B`, and an isomorphism
`ρ_a : E_U|_{𝒞/u(V)} ⟶ E_V` for every arrow `a : V ⟶ U` of `B`, such that
`ρ_{a ∘ b} = ρ_b ∘ ρ_a|_{𝒞/u(W)}` for composable arrows `b : W ⟶ V` and `a : V ⟶ U`.
declarations.statement: structure LocallyGiven.{uM, u, v, w, uB, vB} (X : RingedSite.{u, v, w})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.LocallyGiven.exists_unique_cartesian_summandIdentification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCA.** In Situation 0DC9, assume the negative self-exts of every `E_U` in
`D(O_{u(U)})` vanish. Let `L` be a simplicial object of `SR(B)`, let `K = u(L)` and let
`((C/K)_total, O)` be the ringed site of Remark 0D9W, with `O = a⁻¹O_C`. Then

* there is a cartesian object `E` of `D(O)` whose restriction to `D(O_{C/u(U_{n,i})})` is
  `E_{U_{n,i}}` compatibly with the isomorphisms `ρ_a` (a
  `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.LocallyGiven.SummandIdentification`), and
* such an `E` is unique up to unique isomorphism: for two of them, `(E, σ)` and `(E', σ')`,
  there is exactly one isomorphism `E ≅ E'` carrying `σ` to `σ'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unique_cartesian_summandIdentification
    (hneg : ∀ (U : G.B) (t : ℤ), 0 < t →
      ∀ g : (shiftFunctor (LocalDerivedCategory.{0} X (G.u.obj U)) t).obj (G.obj U) ⟶ G.obj U,
        g = 0) :
    (∃ E : DerivedCategory ((situation X.J (G.image L)).totalRingedTopos
        (structureSheaf X (G.image L))).Modules,
      (situation X.J (G.image L)).IsCartesianDerivedModule (structureSheaf X (G.image L)) E ∧
        Nonempty (G.SummandIdentification L E)) ∧
    ∀ (E E' : DerivedCategory ((situation X.J (G.image L)).totalRingedTopos
        (structureSheaf X (G.image L))).Modules),
      (situation X.J (G.image L)).IsCartesianDerivedModule (structureSheaf X (G.image L)) E →
      (situation X.J (G.image L)).IsCartesianDerivedModule (structureSheaf X (G.image L)) E' →
      ∀ (σ : G.SummandIdentification L E) (σ' : G.SummandIdentification L E'),
        ∃! ε : E ≅ E', ∀ (n : SimplexCategory) (i : (L.obj (op n)).I),
          (G.summandDerivedRestriction L n i).map
              (((situation X.J (G.image L)).derivedComponentModuleRestriction
                (structureSheaf X (G.image L)) n).map ε.hom) ≫ (σ'.iso n i).hom =
            (σ.iso n i).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.LocallyGiven.exists_unique_solution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCB (BBD glueing lemma).** In Situation 0DC9 — a ringed site `(C, O_C)`, a category
`B` with a functor `u : B ⥤ C`, objects `E_U` of `D(O_{u(U)})` and isomorphisms
`ρ_a : E_U|_{C/u(V)} ⟶ E_V` satisfying the cocycle condition — assume

1. `C` has equalizers and fibre products;
2. there is a morphism of sites `f : C ⟶ D` given by a continuous functor `u : D ⥤ C` (here
   `f`, with `IsMorphismOfSites`), such that `D` has equalizers and fibre products and `u`
   commutes with them, `B` is a full subcategory of `D` (a fully faithful `i : B ⥤ D`) with
   `u : B ⥤ C` the restriction of `u` (`i ⋙ f = G.u`), and every object of `D` has a covering
   whose members are objects of `B`;
3. for all `U` in `B` all negative self-exts of `E_U` in `D(O_{u(U)})` are zero, that is,
   every map `E_U[t] ⟶ E_U` with `t > 0` vanishes;
4. there exists `t ∈ ℤ` with `H^i(E_U) = 0` for `i < t` and all `U`.

Then there exists a solution `(E, ρ_U)`, and it is unique up to unique isomorphism: between two
solutions there is exactly one isomorphism compatible with their identifications `ρ_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unique_solution {X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}} [HasEqualizers X.C] [HasPullbacks X.C]
    (G : LocallyGiven.{0, u, u, u, u, u} X)
    {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D] [HasEqualizers D] [HasPullbacks D] (P : Pretopology D)
    (f : D ⥤ X.C) [IsMorphismOfSites.{u} f P.toGrothendieck X.J]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair f] [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan f]
    (i : G.B ⥤ D) [i.Full] [i.Faithful] (hi : i ⋙ f = G.u)
    (hcover : ∀ V : D, ∃ (ι : Type u) (U : ι → G.B) (g : ∀ k, i.obj (U k) ⟶ V),
      Presieve.ofArrows (fun k ↦ i.obj (U k)) g ∈ P V)
    (hneg : ∀ (U : G.B) (t : ℤ), 0 < t →
      ∀ g : (shiftFunctor (LocalDerivedCategory.{0} X (G.u.obj U)) t).obj (G.obj U) ⟶ G.obj U,
        g = 0)
    (hbound : ∃ t : ℤ, ∀ (U : G.B) (q : ℤ), q < t → IsZero
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over (G.u.obj U))) q).obj (G.obj U))) :
    Nonempty G.Solution ∧
      ∀ S S' : G.Solution, ∃! e : S.obj ≅ S'.obj, Solution.IsCompatibleIso G e

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.LocallyGiven.exists_unique_solution_localSerre
declarations.doc:
The unbounded BBD glueing lemma. In Situation 0DC9 — a ringed site `(C, O_C)`, a category
`B` with a functor `u : B ⥤ C`, objects `E_U` of `D(O_{u(U)})` and isomorphisms
`ρ_a : E_U|_{C/u(V)} ⟶ E_V` satisfying the cocycle condition — assume

1. `C` has equalizers and fibre products;
2. there is a morphism of sites `f : C ⟶ D` given by a continuous functor `u : D ⥤ C` (here
   `f`, with `IsMorphismOfSites`), such that `D` has equalizers and fibre products and `u`
   commutes with them, `B` is a full subcategory of `D` (a fully faithful `i : B ⥤ D`) with
   `u : B ⥤ C` the restriction of `u` (`i ⋙ f = G.u`), and every object of `D` has a covering
   whose members are objects of `B`;
3. all negative self-exts of `E_U` in `D(O_{u(U)})` are zero, that is, every map
   `E_U[t] ⟶ E_U` with `t > 0` vanishes;
4. there are weak Serre subcategories `A_U ⊂ Mod(O_U)` for all objects `U` of `C` satisfying
   conditions 0DC2, 0DC3 and 0DC4 (`T : LocalSerreFamily X`);
5. `E_U ∈ D_{A_U}(O_U)`: every cohomology module of `E_U` lies in `A_{u(U)}`.

Then there exists a solution `(E, ρ_U)`, and it is unique up to unique isomorphism: between two
solutions there is exactly one isomorphism compatible with their identifications `ρ_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unique_solution_localSerre {X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}} [HasEqualizers X.C]
    [HasPullbacks X.C] (G : LocallyGiven.{0, u, u, u, u, u} X)
    {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D] [HasEqualizers D] [HasPullbacks D] (P : Pretopology D)
    (f : D ⥤ X.C) [IsMorphismOfSites.{u} f P.toGrothendieck X.J]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair f] [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan f]
    (i : G.B ⥤ D) [i.Full] [i.Faithful] (hi : i ⋙ f = G.u)
    (hcover : ∀ V : D, ∃ (ι : Type u) (U : ι → G.B) (g : ∀ k, i.obj (U k) ⟶ V),
      Presieve.ofArrows (fun k ↦ i.obj (U k)) g ∈ P V)
    (hneg : ∀ (U : G.B) (t : ℤ), 0 < t →
      ∀ g : (shiftFunctor (LocalDerivedCategory.{0} X (G.u.obj U)) t).obj (G.obj U) ⟶ G.obj U,
        g = 0)
    (T : LocalSerreFamily.{u} X)
    (hA : ∀ (U : G.B) (q : ℤ), T.A (G.u.obj U)
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over (G.u.obj U))) q).obj (G.obj U))) :
    Nonempty G.Solution ∧
      ∀ S S' : G.Solution, ∃! e : S.obj ≅ S'.obj, Solution.IsCompatibleIso G e

declarations.name: IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCL.**
A ring `A` is *absolutely integrally closed* if every monic polynomial in `A[X]` is the product
of the linear factors `X - C a` over some multiset `s` of elements of `A`.
declarations.statement: def IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed (A : Type*) [CommRing A] : Prop

declarations.name: isAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed_iff_exists_root
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCM**.
A ring `A` is absolutely integrally closed if and only if every monic polynomial of degree at least
`1` has a root in `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed_iff_exists_root (A : Type*) [CommRing A] :
    IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed A ↔
      ∀ f : A[X], f.Monic → 1 ≤ f.natDegree → ∃ a : A, f.eval a = 0

declarations.name: isAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCN** (part 1).
If `A` is absolutely integrally closed, then so is the quotient `A ⧸ I` for every ideal `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed_quotient (A : Type*) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (hA : IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed A) : IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed (A ⧸ I)

declarations.name: isAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCN** (part 2).
If `A` is absolutely integrally closed, then so is every localization `B` of `A` at a submonoid
`S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed_localization (A : Type*) [CommRing A] (S : Submonoid A)
    (B : Type*) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalization S B]
    (hA : IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed A) : IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed B

declarations.name: isAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed_of_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCP**.
Let `B = S⁻¹A` be the localization of `A` at a submonoid `S` of nonzerodivisors. If `B` is
absolutely integrally closed and `A` is integrally closed in `B`, then `A` is absolutely integrally
closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed_of_localization (A : Type*) [CommRing A] (B : Type*)
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] (S : Submonoid A) [IsLocalization S B] (hS : S ≤ nonZeroDivisors A)
    (hB : IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed B) (hAB : IsIntegrallyClosedIn A B) :
    IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed A

declarations.name: isAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed_iff_isAlgClosed_fractionRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCQ**.
A normal domain is absolutely integrally closed if and only if its fraction field is
algebraically closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed_iff_isAlgClosed_fractionRing
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsIntegrallyClosed A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] :
    IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed A ↔ IsAlgClosed K

declarations.name: exists_absolutelyIntegrallyClosed_extension_as_filteredColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCR.** Every commutative ring has an injective extension which is a filtered
colimit of finite free algebras, is free as a module over the original ring, and is absolutely
integrally closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_absolutelyIntegrallyClosed_extension_as_filteredColimit
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B),
      Function.Injective (algebraMap A B) ∧
      (∃ (J : Type u) (_ : SmallCategory J) (_ : IsFiltered J)
        (F : J ⥤ CommAlgCat.{u} A) (c : Cocone F),
          (∀ j, Module.Finite A (F.obj j) ∧ Module.Free A (F.obj j)) ∧
          Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ Nonempty (c.pt ≅ CommAlgCat.of A B)) ∧
      Module.Free A B ∧ IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed B

declarations.name: IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed.isStrictlyHenselian_atPrime
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCS**.
The localization of an absolutely integrally closed ring at a prime ideal is strictly
henselian: it is a henselian local ring and its residue field is separably closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed.isStrictlyHenselian_atPrime
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (hA : IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed A) (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime B p]
    (h : IsLocalRing B := IsLocalization.AtPrime.isLocalRing B p) :
    HenselianLocalRing B ∧ IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)

declarations.name: henselianPair_iff_of_absolutelyIntegrallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCT**.
Let `A` be an absolutely integrally closed ring and `I ⊆ A` an ideal. Then `(A, I)` is a
henselian pair if and only if `I` is contained in the Jacobson radical of `A` and the map
`A → A ⧸ I` induces a bijection on idempotents.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselianPair_iff_of_absolutelyIntegrallyClosed
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (hA : IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed A)
    (I : Ideal A) :
    HenselianPair A I ↔
      IsContainedInJacobson I ∧ InducesBijectionOnIdempotents I

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.properDirectImageComparisonIsoOfProperMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCU, clause (7a): the proper direct image clause.** For a proper morphism `f` of
the locally quasi-compact Zariski site, ordinary direct image of sheaves of sets along the
underlying continuous map commutes with inverse image along the comparison morphisms to the
Zariski slice topoi:

`π_Y^{-1} ∘ f_* ≅ f_{Zar,*} ∘ π_X^{-1}`.

Properness is the only hypothesis. This is `properDirectImageComparisonIso`, whose hypothesis
on the `Y`-side counit is discharged by `isIso_properBaseChangeCounit`, which is proper base
change for sheaves of sets, Stacks 0D90, in the form the Zariski comparison needs.
declarations.statement:
def properDirectImageComparisonIsoOfProperMap
    (hf : StacksDraft.Topology.IsProperMap.{u, u, u}
      (((S.qcSite.inclusion ⋙ locallyQuasiCompactHausdorffToTop).map f) : X.obj → Y.obj)) :
    TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward (Type (max (u + 1) v))
        ((S.qcSite.inclusion ⋙ locallyQuasiCompactHausdorffToTop).map f) ⋙
      S.comparisonInverseImage.{u, w, max (u + 1) v} Y ≅
    S.comparisonInverseImage.{u, w, max (u + 1) v} X ⋙
      (zariskiSliceMorphism.{u, w, max (u + 1) v} S f).pushforward
declarations.comment: proper_direct_image

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.properDerivedImageComparison_isIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DCU], the derived clause: the derived Zariski base-change map of a proper
morphism is an isomorphism.** For `f : X ⟶ Y` a proper morphism of the locally quasi-compact
Zariski site, the comparison
`π_Y^{-1} ∘ Rf_* ⟶ Rf_{Zar,*} ∘ π_X^{-1}` of `properDerivedImageComparison` is invertible.

This is `isIso_properDerivedImageComparison_of_locallyZero_cohomologyPresheaf` fed
`equalizerSieve_mem_over_of_isProperMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properDerivedImageComparison_isIso
    (hf : StacksDraft.Topology.IsProperMap.{u, u, u}
      (((S.qcSite.inclusion ⋙ locallyQuasiCompactHausdorffToTop).map f) : X.obj → Y.obj)) :
    IsIso (properDerivedImageComparison.{u, w, v} S f)
declarations.comment: proper_derived_image

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.properDerivedImageComparison_isIso_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DCU], the derived clause, with properness as the only hypothesis.** For
`f : X ⟶ Y` a proper morphism of the locally quasi-compact Zariski site, the comparison
`π_Y^{-1} ∘ Rf_* ⟶ Rf_{Zar,*} ∘ π_X^{-1}` of `properDerivedImageComparison` is invertible.

The four sheafifications and the three enough-injectives inputs the derived functors are built
from are not assumed: all four sites are essentially small at this coefficient universe, so
`hasSheafify_opensSite`, `hasSheafify_zariskiSlice`, `enoughInjectives_spaceSheaf` and
`enoughInjectives_zariskiSliceSheaf` supply them.
declarations.statement:
theorem properDerivedImageComparison_isIso_unconditional
    (hf : StacksDraft.Topology.IsProperMap.{u, u, u}
      (((S.qcSite.inclusion ⋙ locallyQuasiCompactHausdorffToTop).map f) : X.obj → Y.obj)) :
    letI := hasSheafify_opensSite.{u, w, v} S X
    letI := hasSheafify_opensSite.{u, w, v} S Y
    letI := hasSheafify_zariskiSlice.{u, w, v} S X
    letI := hasSheafify_zariskiSlice.{u, w, v} S Y
    letI := enoughInjectives_spaceSheaf.{u, w, v} S X
    letI := enoughInjectives_spaceSheaf.{u, w, v} S Y
    letI := enoughInjectives_zariskiSliceSheaf.{u, w, v} S X
    IsIso (properDerivedImageComparison.{u, w, v} S f)
declarations.comment: proper_derived_image, with the four sheafifications and the three enough-injectives inputs discharged rather than assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.zariskiCohomologyComparisonIso
declarations.doc:
**The cohomology comparison for the Zariski comparison morphism.** For an abelian sheaf `F`
on the space of an object `X` of the locally quasi-compact Zariski site, the cohomology of the
localized Zariski site with coefficients in `π_X^{-1}F` is the cohomology of the space `X` with
coefficients in `F`:

`H^n_{Zar}(X, π_X^{-1}F) ≅ H^n(X, F)`,

naturally in `F`. This is clause (1) of Stacks 0DCU.
declarations.statement:
def zariskiCohomologyComparisonIso (n : ℕ) :
    S.abelianComparisonInverseImage.{u, w, max (u + 1) v} X ⋙
        Sheaf.functorH (S.zariskiTopology.over X) n ≅
      Sheaf.functorH (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj) n
declarations.comment: cohomology_comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.zariskiCohomologyComparisonIso_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**The cohomology comparison for the Zariski comparison morphism, with no hypothesis.** For
an abelian sheaf `F` on the space of an object `X` of the locally quasi-compact Zariski site,

`H^n_{Zar}(X, π_X^{-1}F) ≅ H^n(X, F)`,

naturally in `F`. This is clause (1) of Stacks 0DCU.

Nothing is assumed of the two sites: both are essentially small at this coefficient universe, so
the sheafifications, the injective resolutions and the universe of the `Ext`-groups that
`Sheaf.functorH` is built from are supplied by `hasSheafify_opensSite`,
`hasSheafify_zariskiSlice`, `hasInjectiveResolutions_spaceSheaf`,
`hasInjectiveResolutions_zariskiSliceSheaf`, `hasExt_spaceSheaf` and
`hasExt_zariskiSliceSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
def zariskiCohomologyComparisonIso_unconditional (n : ℕ) :
    letI := hasSheafify_opensSite.{u, w, v} S X
    letI := hasSheafify_zariskiSlice.{u, w, v} S X
    letI := hasExt_spaceSheaf.{u, w, v} S X
    letI := hasExt_zariskiSliceSheaf.{u, w, v} S X
    letI := hasInjectiveResolutions_spaceSheaf.{u, w, v} S X
    letI := hasInjectiveResolutions_zariskiSliceSheaf.{u, w, v} S X
    S.abelianComparisonInverseImage.{u, w, max (u + 1) v} X ⋙
        Sheaf.functorH (S.zariskiTopology.over X) n ≅
      Sheaf.functorH (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj) n
declarations.comment: cohomology_comparison, with the sheafifications, the injective resolutions and the universe of the Ext-groups discharged rather than assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.abelianComparisonAdjunction_unit_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCU, the unit clause.** The unit of the Zariski comparison adjunction on abelian
sheaves is an isomorphism: the inverse image `π_X^{-1}` is fully faithful, because
`opensToSlice` is continuous, cocontinuous, full and faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelianComparisonAdjunction_unit_isIso
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound)
    (X : S.category) :
    IsIso (S.abelianComparisonAdjunction.{u, w, max (u + 1) v} X).unit
declarations.comment: unit_isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.abelianComparisonDirectImage_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCU, the exact-direct-image clause.** The direct image from the Zariski slice site
of an object to the Zariski site of its underlying space is exact on abelian sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelianComparisonDirectImage_exact
    {S₀ : Set LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.{u}} {Bound : Cardinal.{u} → Cardinal.{u}}
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound)
    (X : S.category) :
    exactFunctor
      (Sheaf (S.zariskiTopology.over X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
      (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
      (S.comparisonDirectImage X AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
declarations.comment: exact_direct_image

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.zariskiComparisonSquareIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCU, clause (5): the commutative square of topoi.** The square whose horizontal
arrows are `f_Zar : Sh(LC_Zar/X) → Sh(LC_Zar/Y)` and `f : Sh(X_Zar) → Sh(Y_Zar)` and whose
vertical arrows are the comparison morphisms `π_X` and `π_Y` commutes: read on inverse images,
which is where a morphism of topoi lives, `π_X^{-1} ∘ f^{-1} ≅ f_Zar^{-1} ∘ π_Y^{-1}`.

It is obtained from `zariskiComparisonDirectImageSquareIso` by uniqueness of left adjoints,
using the specified comparison and slice adjunctions.

The coefficients are types in an arbitrary universe containing the universe of the spaces.
declarations.statement:
def zariskiComparisonSquareIso :
    (Opens.map ((S.qcSite.inclusion ⋙ locallyQuasiCompactHausdorffToTop).map f)).sheafPullback
        (Type (max u t))
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology
          ((S.qcSite.inclusion ⋙ locallyQuasiCompactHausdorffToTop).obj Y))
        (Opens.grothendieckTopology
          ((S.qcSite.inclusion ⋙ locallyQuasiCompactHausdorffToTop).obj X)) ⋙
      comparisonInverseImage.{u, w, t} S X ≅
    comparisonInverseImage.{u, w, t} S Y ⋙ (zariskiSliceMorphism.{u, w, t} S f).inverseImage
declarations.comment: commutative_square

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.abelianDerivedComparisonAdjunction_unit_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCU, the derived-unit clause.** The canonical map from a complex of abelian
sheaves on the space `X` to the derived direct image of its inverse image on the localized
Zariski site is an isomorphism, naturally in the complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelianDerivedComparisonAdjunction_unit_isIso
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound)
    (X : S.category)
    [HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}]
    [HasSheafify (S.zariskiTopology.over X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}] :
    IsIso (abelianDerivedComparisonAdjunction.{u, w, v} S X).unit
declarations.comment: derived_unit

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.abelianDerivedComparisonAdjunction_unit_isIso_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCU, the derived-unit clause, with no hypothesis.** The canonical map from a
complex of abelian sheaves on the space `X` to the derived direct image of its inverse image on
the localized Zariski site is an isomorphism, naturally in the complex.

The two sheafifications the derived adjunction is built from are not assumed: both sites are
essentially small at this coefficient universe, so `hasSheafify_opensSite` and
`hasSheafify_zariskiSlice` supply them.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelianDerivedComparisonAdjunction_unit_isIso_unconditional
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound)
    (X : S.category) :
    letI := hasSheafify_opensSite.{u, w, v} S X
    letI := hasSheafify_zariskiSlice.{u, w, v} S X
    IsIso (abelianDerivedComparisonAdjunction.{u, w, v} S X).unit
declarations.comment: derived_unit, with the two sheafifications discharged rather than assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.relativeZariskiCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCU, clause (6): the relative-cohomology clause.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
the locally quasi-compact Zariski site and `L ∈ D⁺(Y)`, the cohomology of `π_Y^{-1}L` over the
object `X/Y` of the localized Zariski site is the cohomology of the space `X` with coefficients
in `f^{-1}L`:

`H^n_{Zar}(X, π_Y^{-1}L) ≅ H^n(X, f^{-1}L)`,

naturally in `L`.
declarations.statement:
def relativeZariskiCohomologyIso
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) {X Y : S.category} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (n : ℤ)
    [HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}]
    [HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y.obj) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}]
    [HasSheafify (S.zariskiTopology.over X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}]
    [HasSheafify (S.zariskiTopology.over Y) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}]
    [EnoughInjectives
      (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})]
    [EnoughInjectives
      (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y.obj) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})]
    [EnoughInjectives (Sheaf (S.zariskiTopology.over X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})]
    [EnoughInjectives (Sheaf (S.zariskiTopology.over Y) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})] :
    (S.abelianComparisonInverseImage.{u, w, max (u + 1) v} Y).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        ((sheafSections (S.zariskiTopology.over Y)
            AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).obj (op (Over.mk f))).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} n ≅
      ((Opens.map
              ((S.qcSite.inclusion ⋙ locallyQuasiCompactHausdorffToTop).map f)).sheafPullback
            AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y.obj)
            (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj)).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        ((sheafSections (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj)
            AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).obj
          (op (⊤ : Opens X.obj))).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} n
declarations.comment: relative_cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.relativeZariskiCohomologyIso_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCU, clause (6): the relative-cohomology clause, with no hypothesis.** For a
morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of the locally quasi-compact Zariski site and `L ∈ D⁺(Y)`,

`H^n_{Zar}(X, π_Y^{-1}L) ≅ H^n(X, f^{-1}L)`,

naturally in `L`.

Nothing is assumed of the two sites. The four sheafifications and the four enough-injectives
inputs the bounded below right derived functors are built from are supplied by
`hasSheafify_opensSite`, `hasSheafify_zariskiSlice`, `enoughInjectives_spaceSheaf` and
`enoughInjectives_zariskiSliceSheaf`, each of which holds because the site in question is
essentially small at this coefficient universe.
declarations.statement:
def relativeZariskiCohomologyIso_unconditional
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) {X Y : S.category} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (n : ℤ) :
    letI := hasSheafify_opensSite.{u, w, v} S X
    letI := hasSheafify_opensSite.{u, w, v} S Y
    letI := hasSheafify_zariskiSlice.{u, w, v} S X
    letI := hasSheafify_zariskiSlice.{u, w, v} S Y
    letI := enoughInjectives_spaceSheaf.{u, w, v} S X
    letI := enoughInjectives_spaceSheaf.{u, w, v} S Y
    letI := enoughInjectives_zariskiSliceSheaf.{u, w, v} S X
    letI := enoughInjectives_zariskiSliceSheaf.{u, w, v} S Y
    (S.abelianComparisonInverseImage.{u, w, max (u + 1) v} Y).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        ((sheafSections (S.zariskiTopology.over Y)
            AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).obj (op (Over.mk f))).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} n ≅
      ((Opens.map
              ((S.qcSite.inclusion ⋙ locallyQuasiCompactHausdorffToTop).map f)).sheafPullback
            AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y.obj)
            (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj)).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        ((sheafSections (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj)
            AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).obj
          (op (⊤ : Opens X.obj))).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} n
declarations.comment: relative_cohomology, with the four sheafifications and the four enough-injectives inputs discharged rather than assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.isIso_qcAbelianComparisonAdjunction_unit_app_and_isZero_rightDerived
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCY (1).** For `X` in `LC_qc` and an abelian sheaf `F` on `X`, the change-of-topology
unit `π_X^{-1}F ⟶ ε_{X,*}ε_X^{-1}π_X^{-1}F = ε_{X,*}a_X^{-1}F` is an isomorphism, that is
`ε_{X,*}a_X^{-1}F = π_X^{-1}F`, and `R^i ε_{X,*}(a_X^{-1}F) = 0` for `i > 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_qcAbelianComparisonAdjunction_unit_app_and_isZero_rightDerived
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) (X : S.category)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) :
    IsIso ((qcAbelianComparisonAdjunction.{u, w, v} S X).unit.app
        ((S.abelianComparisonInverseImage.{u, w, max (u + 1) v} X).obj F)) ∧
      ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → IsZero (((qcAbelianDirectImage.{u, w, v} S X).rightDerived i).obj
        ((qcTopologicalAbelianInverseImage.{u, w, v} S X).obj F))
declarations.comment:
clause (1): for `X` in `LC_qc` and an abelian sheaf `F` on `X`, the unit
`π_X^{-1}F ⟶ ε_{X,*}a_X^{-1}F` is an isomorphism and `R^i ε_{X,*}(a_X^{-1}F) = 0` for `i > 0`

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.qcTopologicalHigherDirectImageIsoOfProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCY (2).** For a proper morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of `LC_qc` and an abelian sheaf `F` on
`X`, `a_Y^{-1}(R^i f_*F) = R^i f_{qc,*}(a_X^{-1}F)` for every `i`.
declarations.statement:
def qcTopologicalHigherDirectImageIsoOfProper
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) {X Y : S.category} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : S.properMorphisms f) (i : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) :
    (qcTopologicalAbelianInverseImage.{u, w, v} S Y).obj
        (((spaceDirectImage S f AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).rightDerived i).obj F) ≅
      ((qcAbelianSliceDirectImage.{u, w, v} S f).rightDerived i).obj
        ((qcTopologicalAbelianInverseImage.{u, w, v} S X).obj F)
declarations.comment:
clause (2): an isomorphism `a_Y^{-1}(R^i f_* F) ≅ R^i f_{qc,*}(a_X^{-1}F)` for
a proper morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of `LC_qc`, an abelian sheaf `F` on `X` and every `i`

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.isIso_qcDerivedComparisonUnit_app_abelianComparisonInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCY (3).** For `X` in `LC_qc` and `K` in `D⁺(X)`, the canonical map
`π_X^{-1}K ⟶ Rε_{X,*}(a_X^{-1}K)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_qcDerivedComparisonUnit_app_abelianComparisonInverseImage
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) (X : S.category)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus
      (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})) :
    IsIso ((qcDerivedComparisonUnit.{u, w, v} S X).app
      ((S.abelianComparisonInverseImage.{u, w, max (u + 1) v} X).mapDerivedCategoryPlus.obj
        K))
declarations.comment:
clause (3): for `X` in `LC_qc` and `K` in `D⁺(X)`, the canonical map
`π_X^{-1}K ⟶ Rε_{X,*}(a_X^{-1}K)` is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.isIso_qcTopologicalDerivedBaseChangeMap_app_of_proper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DCY (4).** For a proper morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of `LC_qc` and `K` in `D⁺(X)`, the
canonical map `a_Y^{-1}(Rf_*K) ⟶ Rf_{qc,*}(a_X^{-1}K)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_qcTopologicalDerivedBaseChangeMap_app_of_proper
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) {X Y : S.category} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : S.properMorphisms f)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus
      (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})) :
    IsIso ((qcTopologicalDerivedBaseChangeMap.{u, w, v} S f).app K)
declarations.comment:
clause (4): for a proper morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of `LC_qc` and `K` in `D⁺(X)`,
the base change map `a_Y^{-1}(Rf_*K) ⟶ Rf_{qc,*}(a_X^{-1}K)` is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty_isSerreClass
declarations.doc: Torsion abelian sheaves form a Serre subcategory.
