declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isEtale_canonicalReductionMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DED**, the content of the proof. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of formal algebraic
spaces over `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces and étale. Then the induced morphism
of reductions `X_red ⟶ Y_red` is an étale morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_canonicalReductionMap (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (het : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) f.hom hrep) :
    Space.IsEtale B S hS ((canonicalReduction hX).map (canonicalReduction hY) f).hom
declarations.comment:
étaleness of the induced morphism of reductions, which is the content of the
  proof

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.canonicalSmallEtalePostcomp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DED.** The functor `j : X_étale ⟶ Y_étale` attached to a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
formal algebraic spaces over `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces and étale:
postcomposition of an étale scheme chart of `X_red` with the induced étale morphism of
reductions, which is the functor of Stacks 03LP at that morphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalSmallEtalePostcomp (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (het : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) f.hom hrep) :
    (canonicalReduction hX).SmallEtale ⥤ (canonicalReduction hY).SmallEtale
declarations.comment: the functor `j : X_étale ⟶ Y_étale`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.canonicalSmallEtalePostcomp_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DED.** The functor `j` is cocontinuous: a covering sieve of `jU` in `Y_étale`
pulls back to a covering sieve of `U` in `X_étale`.
declarations.statement:
instance canonicalSmallEtalePostcomp_isCocontinuous (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (het : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) f.hom hrep) :
    (canonicalSmallEtalePostcomp hX hY f hrep het).IsCocontinuous
      (canonicalReduction hX).smallEtaleTopology (canonicalReduction hY).smallEtaleTopology
declarations.comment: cocontinuity of `j`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.canonicalSmallEtalePostcomp_isContinuous
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0DED.** The functor `j` is continuous as well, so Sites 00XR applies to it.
declarations.statement:
instance canonicalSmallEtalePostcomp_isContinuous (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (het : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) f.hom hrep) :
    (canonicalSmallEtalePostcomp hX hY f hrep het).IsContinuous
      (canonicalReduction hX).smallEtaleTopology (canonicalReduction hY).smallEtaleTopology
declarations.comment: continuity of `j`, which is what makes Sites 00XR applicable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.canonicalSmallToposMorphism_pushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DED.** The morphism of topoi `f_small` of Stacks 0DEC, part (3), is the morphism
of topoi that Sites 00XO attaches to the cocontinuous functor `j`: its direct image is the
direct image of `j`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalSmallToposMorphism_pushforwardIso
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (het : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) f.hom hrep) :
    ((canonicalReduction hX).smallToposMorphism (canonicalReduction hY) f).pushforward ≅
      (canonicalSmallEtalePostcomp hX hY f hrep het).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous
        (Type (u + 1)) (canonicalReduction hX).smallEtaleTopology
        (canonicalReduction hY).smallEtaleTopology
declarations.comment:
`f_small` is the morphism of topoi that Sites 00XO attaches to `j`, identified on
  direct images

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.canonicalSmallToposMorphism_inverseImageObjObjIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DED**, the consequence of continuity of `j` recorded by Sites 00XR: the inverse
image of `f_small` is restriction along `j`, so a section of `f_small^{-1} G` over an étale
chart `U` of `X_red` is a section of `G` over the chart `jU` of `Y_red`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalSmallToposMorphism_inverseImageObjObjIso
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (het : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) f.hom hrep)
    (G : Sheaf (canonicalReduction hY).smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)))
    (U : (canonicalReduction hX).SmallEtale) :
    (((canonicalReduction hX).smallToposMorphism (canonicalReduction hY) f).inverseImage.obj
        G).obj.obj (Opposite.op U) ≅
      G.obj.obj (Opposite.op ((canonicalSmallEtalePostcomp hX hY f hrep het).obj U))
declarations.comment:
the formula on sections which Sites 00XR gives for `j`, continuous as well as
  cocontinuous

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.Reduction.isEtale_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DED**, the content of the proof. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of formal algebraic
spaces over `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces and étale. Then the induced morphism
of reductions `X_red ⟶ Y_red` is an étale morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`.

The fibre product `X ×_Y Y_red` is a reduction of `X` and every comparison morphism
`X_red ⟶ X ×_Y Y_red` over `X` is an isomorphism — this is Stacks 0GB7, applicable because an
étale morphism is smooth — so the morphism of reductions is, up to that isomorphism, the second
projection of the fibre product. That projection is a base change of `f`, hence étale after
every further base change along a scheme-valued point of `Y_red`; étaleness being étale local on
the source and target, it satisfies the every-étale-chart condition of Stacks 03MJ, which
descends to the value universe of the algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_map (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (RX : Reduction B S hS X) (RY : Reduction B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (het : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) f.hom hrep) :
    Space.IsEtale B S hS (RX.map RY f).hom
declarations.comment:
étaleness of the induced morphism of reductions, which is the content of the
  proof; read against given reductions, which Stacks 0AIN supplies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.Reduction.smallEtalePostcomp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DED.** The functor `j : X_étale ⟶ Y_étale` attached to a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
formal algebraic spaces over `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces and étale:
postcomposition of an étale scheme chart of `X_red` with the induced étale morphism of
reductions, which is the functor of Stacks 03LP at that morphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallEtalePostcomp (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (RX : Reduction B S hS X)
    (RY : Reduction B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (het : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) f.hom hrep) :
    RX.SmallEtale ⥤ RY.SmallEtale
declarations.comment:
the functor `j : X_étale ⟶ Y_étale`; read against given reductions, which
  Stacks 0AIN supplies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.Reduction.smallEtalePostcomp_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DED.** The functor `j` is cocontinuous: a covering sieve of `jU` in `Y_étale`
pulls back to a covering sieve of `U` in `X_étale`.
declarations.statement:
instance smallEtalePostcomp_isCocontinuous (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (RX : Reduction B S hS X)
    (RY : Reduction B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (het : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) f.hom hrep) :
    (smallEtalePostcomp hX hY RX RY f hrep het).IsCocontinuous RX.smallEtaleTopology
      RY.smallEtaleTopology
declarations.comment:
cocontinuity of `j`; read against given reductions, which Stacks 0AIN
  supplies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.Reduction.smallEtalePostcomp_isContinuous
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0DED.** The functor `j` is continuous as well, so Sites 00XR applies to it.
declarations.statement:
instance smallEtalePostcomp_isContinuous (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (RX : Reduction B S hS X)
    (RY : Reduction B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (het : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) f.hom hrep) :
    (smallEtalePostcomp hX hY RX RY f hrep het).IsContinuous RX.smallEtaleTopology
      RY.smallEtaleTopology
declarations.comment:
continuity of `j`, which is what makes Sites 00XR applicable; read against
  given reductions, which Stacks 0AIN supplies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.Reduction.smallToposMorphism_pushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DED.** The morphism of topoi `f_small` of Stacks 0DEC, part (3), is the morphism
of topoi that Sites 00XO attaches to the cocontinuous functor `j`: its direct image is the
direct image of `j`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallToposMorphism_pushforwardIso (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (RX : Reduction B S hS X)
    (RY : Reduction B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (het : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) f.hom hrep) :
    (RX.smallToposMorphism RY f).pushforward ≅
      (smallEtalePostcomp hX hY RX RY f hrep het).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous
        (Type (u + 1)) RX.smallEtaleTopology RY.smallEtaleTopology
declarations.comment:
`f_small` is the morphism of topoi that Sites 00XO attaches to `j`, identified on
  direct images; read against given reductions, which Stacks 0AIN supplies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.Reduction.smallToposMorphism_inverseImageObjObjIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DED**, the consequence of continuity of `j` recorded by Sites 00XR: the inverse
image of `f_small` is restriction along `j`, so a section of `f_small^{-1} G` over an étale
chart `U` of `X_red` is a section of `G` over the chart `jU` of `Y_red`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallToposMorphism_inverseImageObjObjIso
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (RX : Reduction B S hS X) (RY : Reduction B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (het : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) f.hom hrep)
    (G : Sheaf RY.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1))) (U : RX.SmallEtale) :
    ((RX.smallToposMorphism RY f).inverseImage.obj G).obj.obj (Opposite.op U) ≅
      G.obj.obj (Opposite.op ((smallEtalePostcomp hX hY RX RY f hrep het).obj U))
declarations.comment:
the formula on sections which Sites 00XR gives for `j`, continuous as well as
  cocontinuous; read against given reductions, which Stacks 0AIN supplies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.AffineEtaleFormalCharts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEE**, the category on the right-hand side: the morphisms `φ : U ⟶ X` of formal
algebraic spaces with `U` an affine formal algebraic space and `φ` representable by algebraic
spaces and étale, with the morphisms of fppf sheaves over `X` between them.
declarations.statement: abbrev AffineEtaleFormalCharts (X : FppfSheaf B S hS)
declarations.comment: the category of the morphisms satisfying (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.reductionAffineEtaleComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEE**, the comparison functor into the affine étale site of `X`. Let `X` be an
affine formal algebraic space over `S` whose reduction is the sheaf represented by an object
`V` of the site with affine underlying scheme, by a morphism `i`. By Stacks 0DEA the affine
étale site of `X` is the affine étale site of its reduction, that is of `V`, and this is the
functor to it from the category of the morphisms `φ : U ⟶ X` with `U` an affine formal
algebraic space and `φ` representable by algebraic spaces and étale, sending `φ` to
`U ×_X X_red`.

The reduction is carried as data, with its affineness, rather than chosen from Stacks 0AIN;
for an affine formal algebraic space the reduction is an affine scheme, which is why the datum
is not a restriction. Stacks 0DEE asserts that this functor is an equivalence; the
quasi-inverse is not constructed here.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def reductionAffineEtaleComparison {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hV : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V))
    (i : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj V ⟶ X)
    (_hred : IsReduction B S hS X
      ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj V) i) :
    AffineEtaleFormalCharts B S hS X ⥤ Space.AffineEtale B S hS (yoneda.obj V)
declarations.comment: the comparison functor from the category of the morphisms satisfying (1) and (2) to the affine étale site of `X`, carrying the reduction of `X` and its affineness as data rather than chosen from Stacks 0AIN; the functor is not shown to be an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.affineEtaleEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEE.** Let `X` be an affine formal algebraic space over `S`. Then
`X_{affine, étale}` — the affine étale site of the reduction of `X`, in the sense of Stacks
0DEA part (3), at an arbitrary reduction datum — is equivalent to the category whose objects
are the morphisms `φ : U ⟶ X` of formal algebraic spaces such that

1. `U` is an affine formal algebraic space,
2. `φ` is representable by algebraic spaces and étale.

The functor is the source's, `(U ⟶ X) ↦ U ×_X X_red`: it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.reductionAffineEtaleComparison`, read backwards and composed
with the identification of `X_{affine, étale}` with the affine étale site of the Yoneda
presheaf of the chosen affine reduction chart. Full faithfulness is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.full_affineEtaleComparison` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.faithful_affineEtaleComparison`, both out of the unique
extension of a morphism along a representable thickening; essential surjectivity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.essSurj_affineEtaleComparison`, whose quasi-inverse is the
dependent product `U_{W, q}` and whose affineness is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_liftAlong_of_affine`. The source's
omitted "verification that the constructions are mutually inverse to each other" is therefore
supplied.

The reduction datum is a parameter, not a weakening: `X_{affine, étale}` is defined, in Stacks
0DEA, only for a formal algebraic space with a given reduction, and the datum exists for every
affine formal algebraic space by Stacks 0AIN — in the shape used here by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.nonempty_affineReductionChart`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def affineEtaleEquivalence (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (R : Reduction B S hS X) : R.AffineEtale ≌ AffineEtaleFormalCharts B S hS X
declarations.comment: the equivalence of `X_affine,étale` with the category of the morphisms satisfying (1) and (2); fullness, faithfulness and essential surjectivity are all proved, and the affine étale site of Stacks 0DEA(3) is identified with the one the comparison functor targets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.reductionAffineEtaleComparison_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEE.** The comparison functor
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.reductionAffineEtaleComparison` of Stacks 0DEE is an equivalence
of categories: it is full, faithful and essentially surjective. Its target is the affine étale
site of `X`, which is identified with the site `X_{affine, étale}` of Stacks 0DEA part (3) by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.Reduction.affineEtaleIsoYonedaAffineReductionChart`; the
resulting equivalence stated with that site is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.affineEtaleEquivalence`.
declarations.statement:
theorem reductionAffineEtaleComparison_isEquivalence
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    (reductionAffineEtaleComparison' B S hS hX).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the comparison functor is an equivalence: it is full, faithful and essentially surjective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.reductionAffineEtaleComparison'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEE**, the comparison functor into the affine étale site of `X`. Let `X` be an
affine formal algebraic space over `S`. Its reduction `X_red` is the sheaf represented by an
object of the site with affine underlying scheme — this is Stacks 0AIN for an affine formal
algebraic space, in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.nonempty_affineReductionChart` — and by Stacks 0DEA the affine
étale site of `X` is the affine étale site of `X_red`. This is the functor to it from the
category of the morphisms `φ : U ⟶ X` with `U` an affine formal algebraic space and `φ`
representable by algebraic spaces and étale, sending `φ` to `U ×_X X_red`.

Nothing is carried as a hypothesis beyond `X` being an affine formal algebraic space: the
reduction and its affineness are constructed, and which reduction is chosen is immaterial by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.AffineReductionChart.iso`. Stacks 0DEE asserts that this functor
is an equivalence; that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.reductionAffineEtaleComparison_isEquivalence`, in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/Affine/EtaleSiteEquivalence.lean`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def reductionAffineEtaleComparison' {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    AffineEtaleFormalCharts B S hS X ⥤
      Space.AffineEtale B S hS (yoneda.obj (affineReductionChart B S hS hX).obj)
declarations.comment: the comparison functor from the category of the morphisms satisfying (1) and (2) to the affine étale site of `X`; that it is an equivalence is AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.reductionAffineEtaleComparison_isEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completionAffineEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEF**, the functor from the category of the `A`-algebras `B^∧ = lim B/JB` of its
items (1) and (2) to the *opposite* of an affine étale site, which is the direction in which
Stacks 0DEF identifies that category with `(X_{affine,étale})^{opp}`. It sends an étale ring map
`A → B` to the affine object `Spec (B ⧸ JB)` of the site, étale over `Spec (A ⧸ J)`, and a
continuous `A`-algebra homomorphism `B₁^∧ → B₂^∧` to the morphism `Spec (B₂ ⧸ JB₂) ⟶
Spec (B₁ ⧸ JB₁)` it induces on quotient stages.

The site is the affine étale site of the stage `Spec (A ⧸ J)`, which is the target of the
comparison functor `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.affineEtaleComparison` of Stacks 0DEE at the
affine object `Spec (A ⧸ J)` of the site and the stage inclusion `Spec (A ⧸ J) ⟶ Spf A`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def completionAffineEtale (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A)
    (J : WeakIdealOfDefinitionIndex A) :
    EtaleCompletion A ⥤ (Space.AffineEtale B S hS
      (yoneda.obj ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj (D.stage J))))ᵒᵖ
declarations.comment: the functor from the category of the completions `B^∧` of its items (1) and (2) to the opposite of an affine étale site, on objects the quotient stage `B^∧ ↦ Spec (B ⧸ JB)` and on morphisms the map of quotient stages a continuous `A`-algebra homomorphism of completions induces. The site is the affine étale site of the stage `Spec (A ⧸ J)`, the target of this library's Stacks 0DEE comparison functor at that affine object, rather than of the reduction of `Spf A`, which would have to be chosen from Stacks 0AIN. The functor is not shown to be an equivalence: the quasi-inverse would have to make `Spf B^∧ ⟶ Spf A` representable étale, which needs Stacks 0AKN and the locality on the target of the universe-lifted representability and étaleness conditions, neither of which this library carries

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.EtaleCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEF**, item (1): the datum naming an object of the category attached to a weakly
admissible topological ring `A`.  It is an étale ring map `A → B`; the `A`-algebra it names is
the completion `B^∧ = lim B/JB`, the limit being over the weak ideals of definition `J` of `A`,
see `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.EtaleCompletion.completion`.
declarations.statement: structure EtaleCompletion
declarations.comment: item (1), the objects: an `A`-algebra of the form `B^∧ = lim B/JB` for an étale ring map `A → B`, named here by that ring map together with its étaleness, the completion being `TopologicalRing.CompletionOver` of it. The equivalence with `(X_affine,étale)^opp` is not constructed: it needs Stacks 0DEE as an equivalence, which this library has only as a comparison functor, and Stacks 0AN8 as an equivalence, which this library has only in the ring-theoretic form `EtaleCompletion.etale_quotientMap`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.EtaleCompletion.Hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEF**, item (2): a morphism of the category, a continuous `A`-algebra
homomorphism `B₁^∧ → B₂^∧` between the completions named by two objects.  The `A`-algebra
structures are the canonical maps of Stacks 0AN6, so being an `A`-algebra homomorphism is the
displayed commuting triangle.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (Y Z : EtaleCompletion A)
declarations.comment: item (2), the morphisms: the continuous `A`-algebra homomorphisms between the objects, with the `A`-algebra structure of `B^∧` given by the canonical map `TopologicalRing.CompletionOver.canonicalMap`. The equivalence with `(X_affine,étale)^opp` is not constructed, for the reasons recorded on `EtaleCompletion`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.mcQuillanAffineEtaleEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEF.** Let `S` be a scheme contained in a big fppf site `B` and let
`X = Spf A` be a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space over `S`: `A` is a weakly admissible
topological ring presented over `S` by a quotient system `D` whose atlas lies in the site. Then
`(X_{affine,étale})^{opp}` — the opposite of the affine étale site of Stacks 0DEA part (3), at
an arbitrary reduction datum of `X` — is equivalent to the category whose

1. objects are the `A`-algebras `B^∧ = lim B/JB` for an étale ring map `A → B`, the limit being
   over the weak ideals of definition `J` of `A`, and
2. morphisms are the continuous `A`-algebra homomorphisms,

which is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.EtaleCompletion`.

This is the source's proof: combine Stacks 0DEE,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.affineEtaleEquivalence`, with Stacks 0AN8,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isEquivalence_etaleCompletionCharts`. The first identifies
`X_{affine,étale}` with the category of the affine formal algebraic spaces representable étale
over `X`, the second identifies that category with `(EtaleCompletion A)ᵒᵖ`; taking the opposite
of the composite moves the single opposite from the algebra side, where `Spf` being
contravariant puts it, to the geometric side, where Stacks 0DEF writes it.
declarations.statement:
def mcQuillanAffineEtaleEquivalence (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) (hD : D.HasLargeSite)
    (R : Reduction B S hS (formalSpectrum D)) :
    R.AffineEtaleᵒᵖ ≌ EtaleCompletion A
declarations.comment: the equivalence of `(X_affine,étale)^opp` with the category whose objects are the `A`-algebras `B^∧ = lim B/JB` for an étale ring map `A → B` (item (1)) and whose morphisms are the continuous `A`-algebra homomorphisms (item (2)), namely `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.EtaleCompletion`. It is the source's proof: Stacks 0DEE, `affineEtaleEquivalence`, composed with Stacks 0AN8, `isEquivalence_etaleCompletionCharts`, whose opposite is taken on the algebra side because `Spf` is contravariant; `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.leftOp` moves that one opposite to the geometric side, where the source writes it. The reduction datum is a parameter for the same reason as in Stacks 0DEE -- `X_affine,étale` of Stacks 0DEA(3) is defined only relative to one, and one exists by Stacks 0AIN -- and the quotient system `D` with its large-site condition is this library's spelling of `A` being a weakly admissible topological `S`-algebra whose `Spf` is an affine formal algebraic space, which is the source's hypothesis on `X`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.spacesEtaleComparison_isEquivalence'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEG.** The comparison functor from the category of the formal algebraic spaces
representable étale over a formal algebraic space `X` to `X_{spaces, étale}` is an equivalence
of categories.

Full faithfulness is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.bijective_spacesEtaleComparison_map` and
essential surjectivity is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.essSurj_spacesEtaleComparison`. Every
assertion of the source is proved: the sheaf `U_{V, ψ}` the source produces is constructed, in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/SpacesEtaleQuasiInverse.lean`, its fibre product with
`X_red` over `X` is identified with `V`, the source's omitted verification that
`U_{V, ψ} ⟶ X` is representable by algebraic spaces and étale is proved, in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/SpacesEtaleQuasiInverseRepresentable.lean`, and that
`U_{V, ψ}` is a formal algebraic space is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_liftAlong`.

The reduction of `X` is a parameter, not a weakening: `X_{spaces, étale}` is defined, in Stacks
0DEA, only for a formal algebraic space with a given reduction, and the datum exists for every
formal algebraic space by Stacks 0AIN.
declarations.comment:
the equivalence; full faithfulness and essential surjectivity are both proved,
  the latter from the source's assertion that `U_{V, ψ}` is a formal algebraic space, which is
  AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_liftAlong

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.spacesEtaleComparison_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The comparison functor from the category of the formal algebraic spaces representable étale
over a formal algebraic space `X` to `X_{spaces, étale}` is an equivalence of categories.

Two hypotheses are carried, and they are exactly the two verifications the source omits.
`hhom` is bijectivity on morphisms, which is the source's "we omit the verification that the
constructions are mutually inverse to each other": it amounts to lifting a morphism over `X`
along the thickening `X_red ⟶ X` against an étale target. `hess` is essential surjectivity,
which is the source's construction of the quasi-inverse `U_{V, ψ}` together with its "we omit
the verification that `U_{V, ψ} ⟶ X` is representable by algebraic spaces and étale". The
reduction of `X` is a given as well, which is no weakening: `X_{spaces, étale}` is defined, in
Stacks 0DEA, only for a formal algebraic space with a given reduction, and Stacks 0AIN supplies
one.
declarations.statement:
theorem spacesEtaleComparison_isEquivalence {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (R : Reduction B S hS X)
    (hhom : ∀ U U' : RepresentableEtaleFormalSpacesOver X,
      Function.Bijective fun f : U ⟶ U' ↦ (spacesEtaleComparison hX R).map f)
    (hess : ∀ V : R.SpacesEtale, ∃ U : RepresentableEtaleFormalSpacesOver X,
      Nonempty ((spacesEtaleComparison hX R).obj U ≅ V)) :
    (spacesEtaleComparison hX R).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
the equivalence; bijectivity on morphisms and essential surjectivity — the two
  verifications the source omits — are hypotheses, and the equivalence is read against a given
  reduction of `X`, which Stacks 0AIN supplies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.bijective_spacesEtaleComparison_map
declarations.doc:
The comparison functor is bijective on morphisms: for `φ : U ⟶ X` and
`φ' : U' ⟶ X` representable by algebraic spaces and étale, with `U` and `U'` formal algebraic
spaces, the morphisms `U ⟶ U'` over `X` correspond bijectively to the morphisms
`U_red ⟶ U'_red` over `X_red`.

This is the source's "we omit the verification that the constructions are mutually inverse to
each other", on the side that needs the lifting of a morphism along the thickening
`U_red ⟶ U`: a morphism of reductions over `X_red` is, by the fibre-product description
`U'_red = U' ×_X X_red` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isPullback_inclusion_liftSheafMap_map`, the same thing as a
morphism `U_red ⟶ U'` over `X`, and such a morphism extends uniquely to `U ⟶ U'` over `X` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.existsUnique_hom_of_isRepresentableThickening`. In both
directions the morphism of reductions is recovered from the extension by the characterisation
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.Reduction.eq_map`, so no naturality has to be checked.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_spacesEtaleComparison_map {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (R : Reduction B S hS X)
    (U U' : RepresentableEtaleFormalSpacesOver X) :
    Function.Bijective fun f : U ⟶ U' ↦ (spacesEtaleComparison hX R).map f
declarations.comment:
bijectivity on morphisms: the source's 'we omit the verification that the
  constructions are mutually inverse to each other'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.faithful_spacesEtaleComparison
declarations.doc: The comparison functor is faithful.
declarations.comment: faithfulness of the comparison functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.full_spacesEtaleComparison
declarations.doc: The comparison functor is full.
declarations.comment: fullness of the comparison functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.spacesEtaleQuasiInverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEG.** The quasi-inverse of the proof, at an object `ψ : V ⟶ X_red` of
`X_{spaces, étale}`: the fppf sheaf `U_{V, ψ}` whose sections over `T` are the pairs `(a, b)`
with `a : T ⟶ X` a morphism of formal algebraic spaces and
`b : T ×_{a, X} X_red ⟶ V` a morphism over `X_red`.

This is the functor the source writes down, as an fppf sheaf. That it is a sheaf is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSheaf_liftAlongPresheaf`.
declarations.statement:
def spacesEtaleQuasiInverse {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (R : Reduction B S hS X)
    (V : R.SpacesEtale) : FppfSheaf B S hS
declarations.comment:
the quasi-inverse `U_{V, ψ}` of the proof, as an fppf sheaf; that
  `U_{V, ψ} ⟶ X` is representable by algebraic spaces and étale is proved in
  StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/SpacesEtaleQuasiInverseRepresentable.lean, that
  `U_{V, ψ}` is a formal algebraic space is not, see the implementation notes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.spacesEtaleQuasiInverseBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEG.** The transformation `U_{V, ψ} ⟶ X`, `(a, b) ↦ a`, which the source claims
defines an object of the category of formal algebraic spaces representable étale over `X`.
declarations.statement:
def spacesEtaleQuasiInverseBase {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (R : Reduction B S hS X)
    (V : R.SpacesEtale) : spacesEtaleQuasiInverse B S hS R V ⟶ X
declarations.comment: the transformation `U_{V, ψ} ⟶ X`, `(a, b) ↦ a`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isPullback_spacesEtaleQuasiInverseSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEG.** `V` is the fibre product `U_{V, ψ} ×_X X_red`.

Since the comparison functor of Stacks 0DEG sends `φ : U ⟶ X` to `U ×_X X_red` — which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isPullback_inclusion_liftSheafMap_map` — this says that the
comparison functor applied to the quasi-inverse at `(V, ψ)` returns `(V, ψ)`. It is the half of
the source's "the constructions are mutually inverse to each other" that does not need the
lifting of morphisms along the thickening `X_red ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_spacesEtaleQuasiInverseSection {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (R : Reduction B S hS X) (V : R.SpacesEtale) :
    IsPullback (spacesEtaleQuasiInverseSection B S hS R V)
      (liftSheafMap B S hS V.obj.hom) (spacesEtaleQuasiInverseBase B S hS R V) R.inclusion
declarations.comment:
the quasi-inverse is a right inverse: `U_{V, ψ} ×_X X_red = V` over `X_red`,
  which is one half of the source's 'the constructions are mutually inverse to each other'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.spacesEtaleQuasiInverseFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEG.** The quasi-inverse as a functor, which is what the source produces: an
object `ψ : V ⟶ X_red` of `X_{spaces, étale}` goes to the formal-space-shaped sheaf
`U_{V, ψ}` with its morphism to `X`, and a morphism of `X_{spaces, étale}` goes to the
morphism over `X` obtained by postcomposition on the second component.

It lands in the slice `Over X` rather than in the category of Stacks 0DEG for a reason of import
order only. Both of the source's assertions about its values are proved: that the structure
morphism is representable by algebraic spaces and étale is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRepresentableEtale_spacesEtaleQuasiInverseBase`, and that
`U_{V, ψ}` is a formal algebraic space is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_liftAlong`, which lives further down the
import order, in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/LiftAlongAffineBase.lean`. The
equivalence assembled from them is there as well,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.spacesEtaleComparison_isEquivalence`. See the module
documentation.
declarations.statement:
def spacesEtaleQuasiInverseFunctor {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (R : Reduction B S hS X) :
    R.SpacesEtale ⥤ Over X
declarations.comment:
the quasi-inverse as a functor into the slice over `X` — the source's 'thus we
  obtain our functor `(V, ψ) ↦ (U_{V, ψ} ⟶ X)` in the other direction'. That its values lie in
  the subcategory of the formal algebraic spaces representable étale over `X` is proved, in both
  of the source's assertions: `isRepresentableEtale_spacesEtaleQuasiInverseBase` here and
  `isFormalAlgebraicSpace_liftAlong` further down the import order; the codomain restriction and
  the equivalence assembled from them are `spacesEtaleComparison_isEquivalence`. The slice is an
  import-order artefact, not a missing step

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRepresentableEtale_spacesEtaleQuasiInverseBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEG.** The structure morphism `U_{V, ψ} ⟶ X` of the quasi-inverse of the proof is
representable by algebraic spaces and étale. This is one of the two verifications the source
omits — "we omit the verification that `U_{V, ψ} ⟶ X` is representable by algebraic spaces and
étale" — and it is proved here outright.
declarations.comment: the omitted verification that `U_{V, ψ} ⟶ X` is representable by algebraic spaces and étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.affineEtaleReductionEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEH.** Let `S` be a scheme and `X` a formal algebraic space over `S`. Then
`X_{affine, étale}` is equivalent to the category whose objects are the morphisms `φ : U ⟶ X`
of formal algebraic spaces with `U` an affine formal algebraic space and `φ` representable by
algebraic spaces and étale; the equivalence is the functor `U ↦ U_red`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.affineEtaleReductionFunctor`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isStructureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEJ.** Every formal algebraic space has a structure sheaf: a sheaf of topological
rings `𝒪_X` on its small étale site `X_étale` such that `𝒪_X(U_red) = lim Γ(U_λ, 𝒪_{U_λ})` as
topological rings, canonically, for every affine formal algebraic space `U` with a morphism
`U ⟶ X` representable by algebraic spaces and étale, and every colimit presentation
`U = colim U_λ` of `U` as in Stacks 0AI7 (`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsStructureSheaf`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isStructureSheaf {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    ∃ O : Sheaf (canonicalSmallEtaleTopology hX) TopCommRingCat.{u + 1}, IsStructureSheaf hX O

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_not_enough_sections
declarations.doc:
The structure sheaf of a formal algebraic space does not always have enough sections. There
is an affine formal algebraic space `X` which is not McQuillan (it fails condition (4) of Stacks
0AIC) and whose points are not separated by regular functions, in the sense of Stacks 0CBD:
* for every presentation `X = colim X_λ` by affine thickenings as in Stacks 0AI7, the ring
  `lim Γ(X_λ, O_{X_λ})` of regular functions is a field, every stage `X_λ` has infinitely many
  points (they are the points of `X`, see
  `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.pointsULiftEquivStage`), and each regular function vanishes
  either at all points of a stage or at none, so it separates no two points;
* `X` has infinitely many points, and its reduction `X_red` is represented by a scheme of the
  site with infinitely many points.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_not_enough_sections :
    ∃ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (X : FppfSheaf B S hS),
      IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X ∧
      ¬ HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS X ∧
      (∀ (I : Type (u + 1)) [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
        (D : I ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS),
        (∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (f : i ⟶ j),
          Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (D.map f))) →
        Nonempty (X ≅ colimit (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
          Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))) →
        IsField (sectionDiagram B S hS D ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}).sections ∧
        (∀ i : I, Infinite ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).obj (D.obj i))) ∧
        ∀ (f : (sectionDiagram B S hS D ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}).sections) (i : I)
          (x y : (BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).obj (D.obj i)),
          x ∈ ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).obj (D.obj i)).basicOpen (f.1 (op i)) ↔
            y ∈ ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).obj (D.obj i)).basicOpen (f.1 (op i))) ∧
      Infinite (Space.pointsULift.{u + 1} B S hS X.obj) ∧
      ∃ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (ι : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj T ⟶ X),
        IsReduction B S hS X ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj T) ι ∧
        Infinite ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completedCechComplex_homology_isZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEL.**  Let `X = Spf A` be a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space, with
`J₀ ⊇ J₁ ⊇ ⋯` a countable fundamental system of weak ideals of definition of `A`, and let
`{Spf B^∧ ⟶ Spf A}` be a covering in the affine étale site, so that `A → B` is faithfully flat.
Then `Ȟⁿ({Spf B^∧ ⟶ Spf A}, 𝒪_X) = 0` for `n > 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem completedCechComplex_homology_isZero [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B] (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    IsZero ((completedCechComplex B J hJ).homology (n + 1))
declarations.comment: the computation half of the proof: for a covering of `X = Spf A` by one affine étale chart `Spf B^∧` the Čech cohomology of `𝒪_X` vanishes in every positive degree. The site-theoretic half, the reduction of `Hⁿ(X_étale, 𝒪_X)` to these Čech complexes along Stacks 03F9, 03OZ, 0DEE and 0DEF, is not carried: this library does have the étale sites of a formal algebraic space, `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.SmallEtale` and its siblings of Stacks 0DEA, and Stacks 0DEE as an equivalence, AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.affineEtaleEquivalence, but no structure sheaf on an étale site; Stacks 0DEF is formalized only as the ring-theoretic category of the completions `B^∧`. Stated for an arbitrary antitone sequence of ideals and an arbitrary faithfully flat `A`-algebra, which generalizes the source's weakly admissible `A` and étale covering `A → B`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_completedCechComplex_homology_isZero_of_isCountablyIndexed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEL** with the hypotheses of the source.  A countably indexed affine formal
algebraic space `X` is the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible topological ring `A` carrying
a countable antitone fundamental system `J₀ ⊇ J₁ ⊇ ⋯` of weak ideals of definition, and for
every covering `{Spf B^∧ ⟶ Spf A}` of `X` by one affine étale chart, in the sense of Stacks
0DEF and with `Spf B^∧ ⟶ Spf A` surjective, the Čech complex of `𝒪_X` for that covering has no
cohomology in positive Čech degrees.

Affineness of `X` is not assumed: it is part of the conclusion, `X` being exhibited as a formal
spectrum.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_completedCechComplex_homology_isZero_of_isCountablyIndexed
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hc : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X) :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A) (_ : IsTopologicalRing A)
      (_ : IsLinearTopology A A) (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
      (Q : QuotientSystem B S hS A) (J : ℕ → Ideal A) (hJ : Antitone J),
      (∀ k, TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition (J k)) ∧
        (nhds (0 : A)).HasBasis (fun _ : ℕ ↦ True) (fun k ↦ (J k : Set A)) ∧
        Nonempty (X ≅ formalSpectrum Q) ∧
        ∀ (Y : EtaleCompletion A) (E : QuotientSystem B S hS Y.completion)
          (g : ContinuousHom Q E), g.toRingHom = Y.structureMap →
          IsSurjective B S hS (formalSpectrumMap hA g) → ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
            letI : Algebra A Y.carrier := Y.str.toAlgebra
            IsZero ((completedCechComplex Y.carrier J hJ).homology (n + 1))
declarations.comment: the covering-level content with the source's own hypotheses: a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space and a surjective affine étale chart of it, in place of the antitone sequence of ideals and the faithfully flat algebra of `completedCechComplex_homology_isZero`. The conclusion is still the vanishing of the Čech cohomology of the covering, not of `Hⁿ(X_étale, 𝒪_X)`: this library has no structure sheaf on the étale site of a formal algebraic space: Stacks 0DEE is an equivalence here, AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.affineEtaleEquivalence, but Stacks 0DEF is formalized only as the ring-theoretic category of the completions `B^∧`, so no object of the affine étale site is known to be of the form `Spf B^∧` and the sections of `𝒪_X` are undefined

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.subsingleton_sheafH_countablyIndexedStructureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEL.** Let `X` be a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space over `S`, and
let `X_red` be a reduction of `X`. Then the structure sheaf `𝒪_X` has no higher cohomology on
`X_étale`: `Hⁿ(X_étale, 𝒪_X) = 0` for `n > 0`.

Only the countable presentation of `X` is used, not the set-theoretic condition which makes `X`
an affine formal algebraic space, so the statement is given for a countably indexed sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_countablyIndexedStructureSheaf (hc : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X)
    (R : Reduction B S hS X) [HasExt.{x} (Sheaf R.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H
      ((sheafCompose _ Space.topCommRingToAddCommGrp).obj
        (countablyIndexedStructureSheaf hc R)) n)
declarations.comment: at an arbitrary reduction `X_red` of `X`, which Stacks 0DEA reads `X_étale` against

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.subsingleton_sheafH_canonicalStructureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEL.** If `X` is a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space over `S`, then
`Hⁿ(X_étale, 𝒪_X) = 0` for `n > 0`, where `X_étale` is the small étale site of Stacks 0DEA at the
reduction of `X` given by Stacks 0AIN, and `𝒪_X` is the structure sheaf of `X` on it.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_canonicalStructureSheaf (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hc : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X)
    [HasExt.{x} (Sheaf (canonicalSmallEtaleTopology
      (isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS hX)) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H
      ((sheafCompose _ Space.topCommRingToAddCommGrp).obj
        (countablyIndexedStructureSheaf hc
          (canonicalReduction
            (isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS hX)))) n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_nonempty_abelian_quasicoherentModules_completionAlongIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEM.** Let `A` be a Noetherian domain which is complete for a principal ideal
`I = (π)` with `π` neither zero nor a unit, and let `X = Spf(A)` be the completion of `Spec A`
along `V(I)`, over any base scheme `S` of any big fppf site. Then `X` is a Noetherian affine
formal algebraic space, and the category of quasi-coherent modules on `X` (Stacks 06WG) is not
abelian: it admits no abelian structure at all.

Formal Spaces, Remark 0DEM, says that for almost any Noetherian affine formal algebraic space the
natural category of quasi-coherent modules is not abelian, referring to Examples, Section 0ALF;
the content of that section is the identification of these modules with the complete
`A`-modules (`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.quasicoherentModulesCompletionEquiv`) together with
the non-abelianness of the latter (Stacks 07JR), and this statement is that content for every
such `A`, of which the section's `ℤ_p` is one.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_nonempty_abelian_quasicoherentModules_completionAlongIdeal
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [NoZeroDivisors A] (f : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
    (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (I : Ideal A) (hAc : IsAdicComplete I A) (π : A)
    (hIπ : I = Ideal.span {π}) (hπ : π ≠ 0) (hπu : ¬ IsUnit π) :
    IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (completionAlongIdeal B S hS f hA I) ∧
      IsNoetherian B S hS (completionAlongIdeal B S hS f hA I) ∧
      ¬ Nonempty (Abelian (FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u} B S hS
        (completionFibred B S hS f hA I).p
        (isFiberedInGroupoids_completionFibred B S hS f hA I)))
declarations.comment: the content of Examples, Section 0ALF: for every Noetherian domain `A` complete for a principal ideal `(π)` with `π ≠ 0` not a unit, `Spf(A)` is a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space whose quasi-coherent modules do not form an abelian category

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.SitePointStalkSheafify.kFlat_of_stalks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEN, part (2), with no extra hypothesis.** On a ringed site whose underlying site
has enough points, a complex of `O`-modules whose stalk at every point is a K-flat complex of
modules over the stalk of `O` is itself K-flat.

This is `Stacks.Sheaves.KFlatStalkCriterion.kFlat_of_stalks` with its
`Stacks.Sheaves.KFlatStalkCriterion.StalkTensorData` argument supplied by `stalkTensorData`.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlat_of_stalks (hJ : J.HasConservativeFamily.{u})
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O)) ℤ)
    (hK : ∀ Ψ : J.Point.{u},
      CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} (Stacks.Sheaves.KFlatStalkCriterion.stalkComplex O Ψ K)) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat O K
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.KFlatStalkCriterion.kFlatStalk_of_kFlat_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEN, part (1).**  On a ringed site, a K-flat complex of `O`-modules has K-flat
stalk complex at every point of the site.

This is `Stacks.Sheaves.KFlatStalkCriterion.kFlatStalk_of_kFlat_of_stalkRetract` with its one
remaining obligation discharged by `stalkRetractFinitelyPresented`, so the hypotheses are
exactly those of the source.  Part (2), the converse under the hypothesis that the site has
enough points, is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.SitePointStalkSheafify.kFlat_of_stalks`.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlatStalk_of_kFlat_unconditional (Φ : J.Point.{u})
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O)) ℤ)
    (hK : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat O K) :
    CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} (stalkComplex O Φ K)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.KFlatPullbackMorphismOfSites.kFlat_pullbackComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEP.**  Let `f : (Sh(C), O) ⟶ (Sh(C'), O')` be a morphism of ringed topoi whose
underlying functor of the sites is a morphism of sites, and suppose the site `C` has a
conservative family of points.  Then the degreewise pullback along `f` of a K-flat complex of
`O'`-modules is a K-flat complex of `O`-modules.

The proof is the source's.  K-flatness of `f^*K` is tested at the points of `C` by part (2) of
Stacks 0DEN, which applies because `C` has a conservative family of points.  At a point `Φ` of
`C` the stalk complex of `f^*K` is the extension of scalars, along a map `O'_Ψ ⟶ O_Φ` of stalk
rings, of the stalk complex of `K` at the point `Ψ = f ∘ Φ` of `C'` produced by part (2) of
Stacks 00YA; that is `stalkComplexIso`, which is Stacks 05V5 at the level of complexes, built
from Stacks 05V1 for the inverse image and the stalkwise formula for the extension of scalars
along `f⁻¹O' ⟶ O`.  The stalk complexes of `K` are K-flat by part (1) of Stacks 0DEN on the
target, and extension of scalars preserves K-flatness by Stacks 06Y1.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlat_pullbackComplex (hX : X.J.HasConservativeFamily.{u})
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) ℤ)
    (hK : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat Y.O K) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat X.O ((KFlatPullback.pullbackComplex f).obj K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.StalkBaseChangeOfToposHom.kFlat_pullbackComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEP.**  Let `f : (Sh(C), O) ⟶ (Sh(C'), O')` be a morphism of ringed topoi and
suppose the site `C` has a conservative family of points.  Then the degreewise pullback along
`f` of a K-flat complex of `O'`-modules is a K-flat complex of `O`-modules.

The proof is the source's.  K-flatness of `f^*K` is tested at the points of `C` by part (2) of
Stacks 0DEN, which applies because `C` has a conservative family of points.  At a point `Φ` of
`C` the stalk complex of `f^*K` is the extension of scalars, along the map `O'_Ψ ⟶ O_Φ` of stalk
rings, of the stalk complex of `K` at the point `Ψ = f ∘ Φ` of `C'` produced by part (2) of
Stacks 00YA; that is `stalkComplexIso`, which is Stacks 05V5 at the level of complexes.  The
stalk complexes of `K` are K-flat by part (1) of Stacks 0DEN on the target, and extension of
scalars preserves K-flatness by Stacks 06Y1.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlat_pullbackComplex (hX : X.J.HasConservativeFamily.{u})
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)) ℤ)
    (hK : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat Y.O K) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat X.O ((KFlatPullbackOfToposHom.pullbackComplex f).obj K)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isCoveringOver_delta
declarations.doc:

declarations.statement:
theorem isCoveringOver_delta (hK : IsHypercovering J K) (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)) :
    IsCoveringOver J (K.δ i)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isCoveringOver_terminalFrom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DEQ, part (1).** Every level of a hypercovering of `X` is a
covering of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoveringOver_terminalFrom (hK : IsHypercovering J K) (n : ℕ) :
    IsCoveringOver J (terminal.from (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)))
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsHypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DER.** An augmented simplicial object is a `P`-hypercovering when its
degree-zero augmentation, its canonical degree-one morphism to `U₀ ×_X U₀`, and all of its higher
matching morphisms belong to `P`.
declarations.statement:
structure MorphismProperty.IsHypercovering {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasPullbacks C]
    (P : MorphismProperty C) (A : SimplicialObject.Augmented C) : Prop
declarations.comment: p_hypercovering

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsHypercovering.face_mem
declarations.doc: Every face map in positive degree of a `P`-hypercovering belongs to `P`.
declarations.statement:
lemma face_mem (P : MorphismProperty C) [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [P.IsMultiplicative]
    {A : SimplicialObject.Augmented C}
    (hA : MorphismProperty.IsHypercovering P A) (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)) :
    P (A.left.δ i)
declarations.comment: faces_in_p

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsHypercovering.hom_app
declarations.doc:
Every level of a `P`-hypercovering maps to its augmentation point by a morphism in `P`.

This is the `levels_in_p` assertion of **Stacks Project, Tag 0DER**.
declarations.statement:
lemma hom_app [P.IsMultiplicative] [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (hA : MorphismProperty.IsHypercovering P A) (n : ℕ) :
    P (A.hom.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n)))
declarations.comment: levels_in_p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_proper_isPHCovering
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0DES.** A proper surjection of schemes is a ph covering.

declarations.name: Stacks.Topologies.Fppf.etaleFiniteLocallyFreeDominates
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DET.** An fppf covering `{S_i ⟶ S}` is refined by an fppf covering
`{V_a ⟶ S}` whose members factor as `V_a ⟶ S'_a ⟶ S` with `{S'_a ⟶ S}` an étale covering and
`V_a ⟶ S'_a` surjective finite locally free.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isSheaf_sectionsPresheafOfModules_baseOverTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DT on each of the five big sites of `S`.**  The pullback-sections presheaf of
modules of a quasi-coherent module `F` on `S` is a sheaf for each of the five localized
topologies, with no hypothesis.

Each of the five topologies is coarser than the fppf one, so this is the fppf statement
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isSheaf_sectionsPresheafOfModules` — whose hypothesis is
discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.fpqcDescentOfQuasicoherentHoms` — read through
`CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.of_le`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_sectionsPresheafOfModules_baseOverTopology (τ : SiteKind)
    (F : S.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (baseOverTopology B S hS τ)
      (sectionsPresheafOfModules B S hS F).presheaf
declarations.comment: clause (1) only: 𝓕ᵃ satisfies the sheaf condition for fppf and a fortiori étale coverings; 𝓕 on S_étale is the associated module of a quasi-coherent module on the scheme S, the source's first reduction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedSheafIsoPiPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEW, clause (2).**  On `(Sch/S)_étale` the associated module `𝓕ᵃ` of a
quasi-coherent module is the inverse image `π_S^*𝓕` of its associated module on `S_étale`, along
the morphism of ringed sites `π_S : ((Sch/S)_étale, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_étale, 𝒪)`.
declarations.comment: clause (2) only: 𝓕ᵃ = π_S^*𝓕 on (Sch/S)_étale, with 𝓕 on S_étale the associated module of a quasi-coherent module on the scheme S as in the source's first reduction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedSheafIsoAPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEW, clause (3).**  On `(Sch/S)_fppf` the associated module `𝓕ᵃ` of a
quasi-coherent module is the inverse image `a_S^*𝓕` of its associated module on `S_étale`, along
the morphism of ringed sites `a_S : ((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_étale, 𝒪)`.
declarations.statement:
public def baseAssociatedSheafIsoAPullback :
    (SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (aStructureMap B S hS)).obj
        (smallEtaleAssociatedSheaf B S hS F) ≅
      baseAssociatedSheaf B S hS F .fppf
declarations.comment: clause (3) only: 𝓕ᵃ = a_S^*𝓕 on (Sch/S)_fppf, with 𝓕 on S_étale the associated module of a quasi-coherent module on the scheme S as in the source's first reduction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.pushforward_baseAssociatedSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEW, clause (6), first half.**  The direct image along
`ε_S : ((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪) ⟶ ((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)` of the associated module `𝓕ᵃ = a_S^*𝓕` is the
associated module `𝓕ᵃ = π_S^*𝓕` of the big `τ`-site; at `τ = étale` this is
`ε_{S,*}a_S^*𝓕 = π_S^*𝓕`.

Both sides are the presheaf `(f : T → S) ↦ Γ(T, f⁺𝓕)` of Stacks 03DS with its two sheaf
conditions, and the direct image along the identity functor is restriction of sections along
it.
declarations.comment: clause (6), first half, as documented above

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.pushforward_smallEtaleAssociatedSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEW, clause (6), second half.**  The direct image along
`a_S : ((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_étale, 𝒪_S)` of the associated module `𝓕ᵃ = a_S^*𝓕` is `𝓕`
itself, read on the small étale site as its own associated module: `a_{S,*}a_S^*𝓕 = 𝓕`.

Both sides are the presheaf `(f : T → S) ↦ Γ(T, f⁺𝓕)` of Stacks 03DS, the right-hand side
restricted along the inclusion of the small étale site, and the direct image is exactly that
restriction.
declarations.comment: clause (6), second half, as documented above

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isZero_rightDerived_epsilonPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEW, clause (7), first half.**  The higher direct images along
`ε_S : ((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪) ⟶ ((Sch/S)_étale, 𝒪)` of the associated module `𝓕ᵃ = a_S^*𝓕` vanish:
`R^p ε_{S,*}(a_S^*𝓕) = 0` for `p > 0`.

Every object of the big site is covered étale-locally by objects with affine total space, and
there the fppf cohomology of `𝓕ᵃ` vanishes in positive degrees by [Stacks, Tag 03P2]; so the
module-valued criterion
`Stacks.Cohomology.ModuleDirectImageOnACover.isZero_rightDerived_pushforward_of_presieve`
applies.
declarations.comment: clause (7), first half, as documented above

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isZero_rightDerived_aPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEW, clause (7), second half.**  The higher direct images along
`a_S : ((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_étale, 𝒪_S)` of the associated module `𝓕ᵃ = a_S^*𝓕` vanish:
`R^p a_{S,*}(a_S^*𝓕) = 0` for `p > 0`.

Every object of the small étale site is covered by its affine objects (Stacks 04HR), and over an
object of the big site with affine total space the fppf cohomology of `𝓕ᵃ` vanishes in positive
degrees by [Stacks, Tag 03P2].
declarations.comment: clause (7), second half, as documented above

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleBigEtaleQuasicoherentEquivalence'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEW, clause (4).**  The rule `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` is an equivalence between the
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules on `S_étale` and the quasi-coherent modules on
`((Sch/S)_étale, 𝒪)`.

The source's proof of this clause cites Descent, Proposition 03DX twice, and both citations are
theorems of this library.  The small-étale one is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.quasicoherentIsEssImageAssociatedModule`; the big-site one at
`τ = étale` is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseQuasicoherentIsEssImageAssociatedModule`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/BaseEssentialSurjectivity.lean`).
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallEtaleBigEtaleQuasicoherentEquivalence'
    (BE : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (BF : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hE : BE.Contains S) (hF : BF.Contains S) :
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        (SmallEtale.structureSheaf BE S hE)).FullSubcategory ≌
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        (FibredSite.baseRingStructureSheaf BF S hF .etale)).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment: clause (4): 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ is an equivalence between QCoh(S_étale, 𝒪) and QCoh((Sch/S)_étale, 𝒪)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleBigFppfQuasicoherentEquivalence'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEW, clause (5).**  The rule `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` is an equivalence between the
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules on `S_étale` and the quasi-coherent modules on
`((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)`.

The source's proof of this clause cites Descent, Proposition 03DX twice, and both citations are
theorems of this library.  The small-étale one is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.quasicoherentIsEssImageAssociatedModule`; the big-site one, at
`τ = fppf`, is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.quasicoherentIsEssImageAssociatedModule'`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/EffectiveGlueAgreementTransport.lean`
`:512`).  The equivalence used below is the `τ`-indexed one, whose essential surjectivity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseQuasicoherentIsEssImageAssociatedModule`; that theorem is
proved by reducing the `τ` case to this `fppf` one.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallEtaleBigFppfQuasicoherentEquivalence'
    (BE : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (BF : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hE : BE.Contains S) (hF : BF.Contains S) :
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        (SmallEtale.structureSheaf BE S hE)).FullSubcategory ≌
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        (FibredSite.baseRingStructureSheaf BF S hF .fppf)).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment: clause (5): 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ is an equivalence between QCoh(S_étale, 𝒪) and QCoh((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.rightAcyclic_epsilonPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEX, first half.**  The canonical map
`π_S^*𝓕 = ε_{S,*}(a_S^*𝓕) ⟶ Rε_{S,*}(a_S^*𝓕)` is an isomorphism, that is, `a_S^*𝓕` is right
acyclic for `ε_{S,*}`.

This is the criterion of [Stacks, Tag 015C] applied to clauses (6) and (7) of
[Stacks, Tag 0DEW]: clause (6) identifies the source of the map with `π_S^*𝓕`
(`pushforward_baseAssociatedSheaf`, an equality), and clause (7) supplies the vanishing of the
higher direct images, which is what right acyclicity amounts to for a left exact functor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rightAcyclic_epsilonPushforward :
    (SheafOfModules.pushforward (F := 𝟭 (BigFppfOver B S hS))
        (epsilonStructureMap B S hS .etale)).rightAcyclic
      (baseAssociatedSheaf B S hS F .fppf)
declarations.comment: first half, as documented above

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.rightAcyclic_aPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEX, second half.**  The canonical map
`𝓕 = a_{S,*}(a_S^*𝓕) ⟶ Ra_{S,*}(a_S^*𝓕)` is an isomorphism, that is, `a_S^*𝓕` is right acyclic
for `a_{S,*}`.

Clause (6) of [Stacks, Tag 0DEW] identifies the source of the map with `𝓕` itself
(`pushforward_smallEtaleAssociatedSheaf`, an equality), and clause (7) supplies the vanishing of
the higher direct images.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rightAcyclic_aPushforward :
    (SheafOfModules.pushforward (F := smallEtaleToFppf B S hS)
        (aStructureMap B S hS)).rightAcyclic
      (baseAssociatedSheaf B S hS F .fppf)
declarations.comment: second half, as documented above

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isSyntomic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEY.** A syntomic morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is locally of finite
presentation.

Both properties are the condition of Tag 03MJ on every commuting square of étale charts, so the
statement is the scheme-level implication of [Stacks Project, Tag 01UK] quantified over the
charts.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isSyntomic {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hf : IsSyntomic B S hS f) : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_of_isSyntomic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DEZ.** A syntomic morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is flat.

Both properties are the condition of Tag 03MJ on every commuting square of étale charts, so the
statement is the scheme-level implication of [Stacks Project, Tag 01UL] quantified over the
charts.
declarations.statement: theorem isFlat_of_isSyntomic {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : IsSyntomic B S hS f) : IsFlat B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyOpen_of_isSyntomic
declarations.doc:
A syntomic morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is universally open in the sense of
Stacks 03Z2.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyOpen_of_isSyntomic
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsSyntomic B S hS f) : UniversallyOpen B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtaleCovering_of_isZariskiCovering
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0DF1.** Every Zariski covering of algebraic spaces is an étale covering.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.inclusionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF2.** Composition with `f` regards an algebraic space étale over `Y` as an
object of the big étale site of `X`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev inclusionFunctor :
    Space.SpacesEtale T.fppfSite S T.fppf_mem Y ⥤ Over X
declarations.comment: the inclusion functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.inclusionFunctor_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF2.** The inclusion of the spaces-étale site of `Y` into the big étale site of
`X` is cocontinuous.
declarations.statement:
instance inclusionFunctor_isCocontinuous :
    (inclusionFunctor T f).IsCocontinuous
      (Space.SpacesEtale.topology T.fppfSite S T.fppf_mem Y) (T.bigEtaleTopology X)
declarations.comment: cocontinuity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.smallToBigEtaleMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF2.** The morphism of topoi from the spaces-étale topos of `Y` to the big
étale topos of `X` induced by the inclusion functor. Its inverse image is restriction of
sheaves along the inclusion, so its sections are computed by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous_obj_obj_obj`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallToBigEtaleMorphism :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (Space.SpacesEtale.topology T.fppfSite S T.fppf_mem Y) (Type (u + 1)))
      (Sheaf (T.bigEtaleTopology X) (Type (u + 1)))
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.lowerShriek
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0DF2.** The left adjoint of restriction along the inclusion functor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev lowerShriek :
    Sheaf (Space.SpacesEtale.topology T.fppfSite S T.fppf_mem Y) (Type (u + 1)) ⥤
      Sheaf (T.bigEtaleTopology X) (Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: the lower-shriek functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.lowerShriek_preservesPullbacks
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0DF2.** Lower shriek preserves fibre products.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance lowerShriek_preservesPullbacks :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan (lowerShriek T f)
declarations.comment: lower shriek preserves fibre products

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.lowerShriek_preservesEqualizers
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0DF2.** Lower shriek preserves equalizers.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance lowerShriek_preservesEqualizers :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair (lowerShriek T f)
declarations.comment: lower shriek preserves equalizers

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous_obj_obj_obj
registrations.comment: the inverse-image formula

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
registrations.comment: existence of lower shriek

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.inclusion_isMorphismOfSites
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF3.** The full inclusion of the spaces-étale site of `X` into the big étale
site of `X` is a morphism of sites in the reverse direction.
declarations.statement:
theorem inclusion_isMorphismOfSites :
    (Space.SpacesEtale.inclusion T.fppfSite S T.fppf_mem X).IsMorphismOfSites
      (Space.SpacesEtale.topology T.fppfSite S T.fppf_mem X) (T.bigEtaleTopology X)
declarations.comment: the morphism of sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.inclusionFunctorIdIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF3.** The inclusion of the spaces-étale site of `X` is canonically the functor
of Tag 0DF2 for the identity morphism of `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inclusionFunctorIdIso :
    inclusionFunctor T (𝟙 X) ≅ Space.SpacesEtale.inclusion T.fppfSite S T.fppf_mem X
declarations.comment: identification with the identity case of 0DF2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.bigToSmallEtaleMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF3.** The morphism of topoi from the big étale topos of `X` to its small étale
topos, induced by the inclusion of the spaces-étale site as a morphism of sites.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bigToSmallEtaleMorphism :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (T.bigEtaleTopology X) (Type (u + 1)))
      (Sheaf (Space.SpacesEtale.topology T.fppfSite S T.fppf_mem X) (Type (u + 1)))
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.bigToSmall_comp_smallToBig_pushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF3.** Composing the morphism of topoi induced by the inclusion with the
small-to-big morphism `i_X` gives the identity on the small étale topos, canonically up to
natural isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bigToSmall_comp_smallToBig_pushforwardIso :
    ((bigToSmallEtaleMorphism T X).comp (smallToBigEtaleMorphism T (𝟙 X))).pushforward ≅
      𝟭 (Sheaf (Space.SpacesEtale.topology T.fppfSite S T.fppf_mem X) (Type (u + 1)))
declarations.comment: the retraction identity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.smallToBig_inverseImageIso_bigToSmall_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF3.** The inverse image of the small-to-big morphism `i_X` is the direct image
of the big-to-small morphism of sites: both restrict a big étale sheaf to the objects étale
over `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallToBig_inverseImageIso_bigToSmall_pushforward :
    (smallToBigEtaleMorphism T (𝟙 X)).inverseImage ≅
      (bigToSmallEtaleMorphism T X).pushforward
declarations.comment: the inverse-image identification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SpacesEtale.hasPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF3.** The spaces-étale site of `X` has fibre products: it is the full
subcategory of the slice over `X` cut out by a base-change stable property of morphisms, so a
fibre product of algebraic spaces étale over `X` is again étale over `X`.
declarations.statement: instance hasPullbacks : HasPullbacks (SpacesEtale B S hS X)
declarations.comment: fibre products in the small site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SpacesEtale.hasTerminal
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0DF3.** The spaces-étale site of `X` has a final object, the identity of `X`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance hasTerminal : HasTerminal (SpacesEtale B S hS X)
declarations.comment: the final object of the small site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SpacesEtale.inclusion_preservesTerminalShape
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF3.** The final object of the spaces-étale site of `X` remains final in the
slice over `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance inclusion_preservesTerminalShape :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete PEmpty.{1}) (inclusion B S hS X)
declarations.comment: the inclusion preserves the final object

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SpacesEtale.inclusion_preservesPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF3.** The inclusion of the spaces-étale site of `X` into the slice over `X`
preserves fibre products.
declarations.statement:
instance inclusion_preservesPullbacks :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan (inclusion B S hS X)
declarations.comment: the inclusion preserves fibre products

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous_obj_obj_obj
registrations.comment: the section rule for inverse image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.bigToSmallEtaleMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF3.** The morphism of topoi from the big étale topos of `X` to its small étale
topos, induced by the inclusion of the spaces-étale site as a morphism of sites.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bigToSmallEtaleMorphism :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (T.bigEtaleTopology X) (Type (u + 1)))
      (Sheaf (Space.SpacesEtale.topology T.fppfSite S T.fppf_mem X) (Type (u + 1)))
declarations.comment: its pushforward is the restriction to the small étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.bigEtaleMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF5.** The morphism of big étale topoi induced by a morphism of algebraic
spaces: its direct image is the cocontinuous pushforward along composition with `f` and its
inverse image is the continuous pushforward along the same functor, so sections of the
inverse image are given by `CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous_obj_obj_obj`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bigEtaleMorphism :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (T.bigEtaleTopology Y) (Type (u + 1)))
      (Sheaf (T.bigEtaleTopology X) (Type (u + 1)))
declarations.comment: the morphism of big étale topoi and its inverse-image formula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.bigEtaleLowerShriek_preservesPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF5.** The left adjoint of the inverse image of
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.bigEtaleMorphism` preserves fibre products.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance bigEtaleLowerShriek_preservesPullbacks :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan
      ((Over.map f).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
        (T.bigEtaleTopology Y) (T.bigEtaleTopology X))
declarations.comment: lower shriek preserves fibre products

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.bigEtaleLowerShriek_preservesEqualizers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DF5.** The left adjoint of the inverse image of
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSpaceSite.bigEtaleMorphism` preserves equalizers.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance bigEtaleLowerShriek_preservesEqualizers :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair
      ((Over.map f).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
        (T.bigEtaleTopology Y) (T.bigEtaleTopology X))
