declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isBounded_and_isPseudoCoherent_iff_boundedCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI1, second equivalence, via Stacks 08E8.** On a Noetherian scheme an object of
`D(𝒪_X)` is bounded and pseudo-coherent if and only if it lies in `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`, that is,
if and only if it is bounded and all of its cohomology sheaves are coherent.

Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical_iff_isBounded_and_isPseudoCoherent` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isNoetherian_of_finitePresentation_over_field` this identifies the objects of
`D(𝒪_X)` perfect relative to a field with `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical_iff_boundedCoherent`.

Stacks 08E8 cuts `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)` out inside `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, and both sides here
imply quasi-coherence of the cohomology sheaves: on the left it is Stacks 08E5 for a pseudo-coherent
object,
`AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasicoherentDerived_of_isPseudoCoherent`, and on the right it is Stacks
01BW, `isQuasicoherent_of_isCoherent`, applied degreewise.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isBounded_and_isPseudoCoherent_iff_boundedCoherent (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsNoetherian X] (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)) :
    (DerivedCategoryB.IsBounded E ∧ RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent E) ↔
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
        (fun M : OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace => M.IsCoherent) E
declarations.comment: bounded pseudo-coherent objects are the bounded coherent ones

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical_iff_isBounded_and_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI1, first equivalence, at the genuine derived tensor product.** Let `k` be a field
and let `X` be a scheme of finite presentation over `k`. An object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` is perfect
relative to `Spec k` — read at the derived tensor product of Stacks 06YU on each open subspace of
`(X, f⁻¹𝒪_{Spec k})`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily` — if and only if it
is bounded and pseudo-coherent.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfectRelativeTo_iff_isBounded_and_isPseudoCoherent` at the
canonical family, whose underived operation *is* `- ⊗_{f⁻¹𝒪_{Spec k}} -` by `rfl`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical_iff_isBounded_and_isPseudoCoherent (k : Type u)
    [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    [QuasiCompact f] (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)) :
    f.IsPerfectRelativeTo
        (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
          (RingedSpace.inverseImage (Spec (.of k)).toRingedSpace f.base)) E ↔
      (DerivedCategoryB.IsBounded E ∧ RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent E)
declarations.comment:
first equivalence: at the 06YU derived tensor product, relative perfectness over a field is
  boundedness and pseudo-coherence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical_iff_boundedCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI1.** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a scheme of finite presentation over `k`.
An object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` is `Spec k`-perfect if and only if it lies in `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`, that is,
if and only if it is bounded with coherent cohomology sheaves.

This is the example in one statement: relative perfectness is read at the derived tensor product
of Stacks 06YU, and the cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent by Stacks 08E5 and 01BW. It is the
composite of
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical_iff_isBounded_and_isPseudoCoherent` with
`AlgebraicGeometry.isBounded_and_isPseudoCoherent_iff_boundedCoherent`, the scheme being
Noetherian by `AlgebraicGeometry.isNoetherian_of_finitePresentation_over_field`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical_iff_boundedCoherent (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)) :
    f.IsPerfectRelativeTo
        (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
          (RingedSpace.inverseImage (Spec (.of k)).toRingedSpace f.base)) E ↔
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
        (fun M : OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace => M.IsCoherent) E
declarations.comment: the `Spec k`-perfect objects are exactly `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPerfectRelativeTo_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI2.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes which is flat and locally of finite
presentation, and let `E` be an object of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules all of whose
cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent. The following are equivalent:

1. `E` is `S`-perfect;
2. for every affine open `U ⊆ X` mapping into an affine open `V ⊆ S`, the complex `RΓ(U, E)` is
   `𝒪_S(V)`-perfect;
3. there are an affine open covering `S = ⋃ V i` and, for each `i`, an affine open covering
   `f⁻¹(V i) = ⋃ U i j` such that `RΓ(U i j, E)` is `𝒪_S(V i)`-perfect.

`S`-perfectness is read at the derived tensor product of Stacks 06YU on the open subspaces of
`(X, f⁻¹𝒪_S)`, and `𝒪_S(V)`-perfectness of `RΓ(U, E)` is Stacks 0DHS for the chart ring map
`f.appLE V U e`, which is flat and of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPerfectRelativeTo_tfae [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsPerfectRelativeTo f
          (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
            (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base)) E,
        ∀ (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (V : S.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
          (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V), SectionsRelativelyPerfect f E hV hU e,
        ∃ (ι : Type u) (V : ι → S.affineOpens),
          (⨆ i, (V i : S.Opens)) = ⊤ ∧
            ∀ i, ∃ (κ : Type u) (U : κ → X.affineOpens) (hle : ∀ j, (U j).1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (V i).1),
              (⨆ j, (U j : X.Opens)) = f ⁻¹ᵁ (V i).1 ∧
                ∀ j, SectionsRelativelyPerfect f E (V i).2 (U j).2 (hle j)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_derivedSections_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI2, the pseudo-coherence clause.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and
let `E` be an object of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules all of whose cohomology sheaves are
quasi-coherent. Then the following are equivalent:

1. `E` is a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)`;
2. for every affine open `U ⊆ X` whose image lies in an affine open `V ⊆ S`, the complex of
   `Γ(X, U)`-modules `RΓ(U, E)` is pseudo-coherent;
3. there are an affine open covering of `S` and, over each of its members `V i`, an affine open
   covering of `f ⁻¹ᵁ V i` such that `RΓ(U, E)` is pseudo-coherent for each member `U` of the
   latter.

This is the first of the two clauses of relative perfectness, with the part of the source's
proof that concerns it: pseudo-coherence of `E` is the pseudo-coherence over `Γ(X, U)` of
`RΓ(U, E)`, by Stacks 08E7 and the affine presentation of `E|_U` of Stacks 06Z0, and the
condition is local on `X`. Together with the second clause, locally finite Tor dimension over
`f^{-1}𝒪_S`, this is assembled into Stacks 0DI2 in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPerfectRelativeTo_tfae`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pseudoCoherent_derivedSections_tfae (f : X ⟶ S)
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent) :
    List.TFAE
      [RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E,
        ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → ∀ (V : S.Opens), IsAffineOpen V → U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V →
          StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent ((derivedSectionsUnbounded X U).obj E),
        ∃ (ι : Type u) (V : ι → S.affineOpens),
          (⨆ i, (V i : S.Opens)) = ⊤ ∧
            ∀ i, ∃ (κ : Type u) (U : κ → X.affineOpens),
              (⨆ j, (U j : X.Opens)) = f ⁻¹ᵁ (V i).1 ∧
                ∀ j, StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
                  ((derivedSectionsUnbounded X (U j).1).obj E)]
declarations.comment: the pseudo-coherence clause

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_affineCovering_sectionsRelativelyPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI2**, the implication (2) ⟹ (3): if `RΓ(U, E)` is `Γ(S, V)`-perfect for every affine
open `U ⊆ X` mapping into an affine open `V ⊆ S`, then there are an affine open covering of `S`
and, over each of its members `V`, an affine open covering of `f⁻¹(V)` on whose members the
condition holds.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_affineCovering_sectionsRelativelyPerfect [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (h : ∀ (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (V : S.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
      (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V), SectionsRelativelyPerfect f E hV hU e) :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (V : ι → S.affineOpens),
      (⨆ i, (V i : S.Opens)) = ⊤ ∧
        ∀ i, ∃ (κ : Type u) (U : κ → X.affineOpens) (hle : ∀ j, (U j).1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (V i).1),
          (⨆ j, (U j : X.Opens)) = f ⁻¹ᵁ (V i).1 ∧
            ∀ j, SectionsRelativelyPerfect f E (V i).2 (U j).2 (hle j)
declarations.comment: the implication (2) implies (3), at the source's own module-side condition and for BOTH of its conjuncts at once: if the complex of sections over every affine open U of X mapping into an affine open V of S is O_S(V)-perfect, then there are an affine open covering of S and, over each member V, an affine open covering of the preimage of V on whose members the same condition holds. The whole three-way equivalence is AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPerfectRelativeTo_tfae

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.chartHasFiniteTorDimension_of_locallyHasFiniteTorDimension
declarations.doc:
**The implication (1) ⟹ (2) of the Tor-dimension clause of Stacks 0DI2.** If `E` locally has
finite Tor dimension over `f⁻¹𝒪_S`, then for every affine open `U ⊆ X` the restriction `E|_U` has
finite Tor dimension over `f⁻¹𝒪_S`.

The three steps are: the certificate-carrying predicate at the canonical family is the pinned one
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_canonicalCertificate_iff`, which is
`Iff.rfl`); locally finite Tor dimension is inherited by `X|_U`
(`Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_derivedRestrictModules`); and on
`X|_U`, which is quasi-compact because `U` is affine, locally finite Tor dimension is finite Tor
dimension (`locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_iff_hasFiniteTorDimension` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineRelativeTorAmplitude`).

**The certificate family is named, not quantified.** Unlike the two implications *into* condition
(1) of `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_of_forall_chart` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_of_exists_affineCovering`, this
implication is not available for an arbitrary family: the premise is tested against the
certificates at the members of some covering and the conclusion against the certificate at `U`,
and a family carries no relation between its members, so at an arbitrary family the two sides
measure Tor amplitude against unrelated operations. It is stated at the genuine derived tensor
product of Stacks 06YU, which is what the source means; a consumer holding another family with
the same underived halves may use
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_iff_of_tensor_eq`.

**Affineness is used only through quasi-compactness**, so the statement holds verbatim for a
quasi-compact open; it is stated for an affine open because that is the chart condition of the
source. The affine open `V ⊆ S` that clause (2) asks the chart to map into does not appear,
because the sheaf-side condition does not refer to it; its module-side counterpart
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.SectionsRelativelyPerfect` does.
declarations.statement:
theorem chartHasFiniteTorDimension_of_locallyHasFiniteTorDimension
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace))
    (h : RingedSpace.LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension
      (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base)
      (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base))
      ((derivedScalarRestriction f).obj E))
    (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens
      (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base).carrier)
    (hU : IsAffineOpen (X := X) U) :
    ChartHasFiniteTorDimension f
      (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base)) E U
declarations.comment: the Tor-dimension clause, the implication (1) implies (2): if E locally has finite Tor dimension over f^{-1}O_S then its restriction to every affine open U of X has finite Tor dimension over f^{-1}O_S, for the derived tensor product of Stacks 06YU. The whole three-way equivalence, at the source's module-side conditions, is AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPerfectRelativeTo_tfae

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI3.** Strict fullness of the `S`-perfect objects, at the derived tensor product
of Stacks 06YU.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isPerfectRelativeTo`, which
holds for an arbitrary certificate family, read at the canonical one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical :
    (isPerfectRelativeTo f
      (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base))).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms
declarations.comment: the strict fullness clause, at the genuine derived tensor product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isSaturated_isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI3.** Saturation of the `S`-perfect objects, at the derived tensor product of
Stacks 06YU: a direct summand of an `S`-perfect object is `S`-perfect.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isSaturated_isPerfectRelativeTo`, which holds for an
arbitrary certificate family, read at the canonical one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSaturated_isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical :
    (isPerfectRelativeTo f
      (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base))).IsSaturated
declarations.comment: the saturation clause, at the genuine derived tensor product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isTriangulated_isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI3.** For a flat, locally finitely presented morphism `f : X ⟶ S` of schemes, the
`S`-perfect objects of `D(𝒪_X)` — read at the derived tensor product of Stacks 06YU on each open
subspace of `(X, f^{-1}𝒪_S)`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily` — form a
*triangulated* subcategory: the property contains the zero object, is stable under all shifts,
and is closed under extensions.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isTriangulated_isPerfectRelativeTo` at the canonical
family: there each `- ⊗^{L} ℱ[0]` commutes with the shift and is exact, these being fields of the
derived tensor product, and finite Tor dimension restricts to smaller opens by Tag 09U8 at the
inclusion of one open subspace in another.

The other two assertions of Stacks 0DI3 — strict fullness and saturation — hold for an arbitrary
certificate family, and are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isPerfectRelativeTo` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isSaturated_isPerfectRelativeTo`; at the canonical family they are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isSaturated_isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isTriangulated_isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical :
    (isPerfectRelativeTo f
      (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base))).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the triangulated clause, at the genuine derived tensor product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isSaturated_and_isTriangulated_isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI3.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes which is flat and locally of finite
presentation. The `S`-perfect objects of `D(𝒪_X)`, read at the derived tensor product of
Stacks 06YU on each open subspace of `(X, f^{-1}𝒪_S)`, form a strictly full, saturated,
triangulated subcategory of `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSaturated_and_isTriangulated_isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical :
    (isPerfectRelativeTo f
        (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
          (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base))).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
      (isPerfectRelativeTo f
        (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
          (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base))).IsSaturated ∧
      (isPerfectRelativeTo f
        (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
          (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base))).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment:
the whole statement: for f flat and locally of finite presentation, the S-perfect
objects of D(O_X) form a strictly full, saturated, triangulated subcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPerfectRelativeTo_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
For a flat, locally finitely presented morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S`, every perfect object
of `D(𝒪_X)` is perfect relative to `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPerfectRelativeTo_of_isPerfect
    (hamp : FlatRepresentativeBounds f D) (hflat : ScalarRestrictionFlat f)
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)) (hE : RingedSpace.IsPerfect E) :
    f.IsPerfectRelativeTo D E
declarations.comment: a perfect object is perfect relative to the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPerfectRelativeTo_derivedTensor
declarations.doc:
For a flat, locally finitely presented morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S`, the derived tensor
product of a perfect object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)` with an `S`-perfect object `M` is perfect relative
to `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPerfectRelativeTo_derivedTensor
    (hrestricts : RingedSpace.FiniteTorDimensionRestricts
      (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base) D)
    (hind : StrictlyPerfectInduction.{u + 1, u})
    (hcl : Stacks.Cohomology.PseudoCoherentTensor.ComplexLevel.{u})
    (K M : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace))
    (Θ : ∀ (V : TopologicalSpace.Opens
          (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base).carrier)
        (W : TopologicalSpace.Opens X.toRingedSpace.carrier), (∀ x, x ∈ V → x ∈ W) →
      DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} (X.toRingedSpace.restrict W.isOpenEmbedding)) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u}
          ((RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base).restrict V.isOpenEmbedding)))
    (ΘcommShift : ∀ V W h, (Θ V W h).CommShift ℤ)
    (Θtriangulated : ∀ V W h, letI := ΘcommShift V W h; (Θ V W h).IsTriangulated)
    (Θunit : ∀ V W h, (Θ V W h).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (OXMod.{u, u} (X.toRingedSpace.restrict W.isOpenEmbedding)) 0).obj
          (structureModule (X.toRingedSpace.restrict W.isOpenEmbedding))) ≅
      (RingedSpace.derivedRestrictModules
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base) V).obj
          ((derivedScalarRestriction f).obj M))
    (Θtensor : ∀ (V W h) (A : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)),
      (Θ V W h).obj ((RingedSpace.derivedRestrictModules X.toRingedSpace W).obj A) ≅
        (RingedSpace.derivedRestrictModules
          (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base) V).obj
            ((derivedScalarRestriction f).obj
          (((Stacks.Cohomology.PseudoCoherentTensor.derivedTensorProduct
            X.toRingedSpace).tensor.obj A).obj M)))
    (hK : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} K)
    (hM : f.IsPerfectRelativeTo D M) :
    f.IsPerfectRelativeTo D
      (((Stacks.Cohomology.PseudoCoherentTensor.derivedTensorProduct
        X.toRingedSpace).tensor.obj K).obj M)
declarations.comment: tensoring an S-perfect object with a perfect object

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isRelativelyPerfect_of_isPerfect_and_derivedTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI4.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes which is flat and locally of finite
presentation. A perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` is `S`-perfect. If `K, M ∈ D(𝒪_X)`, then
`K ⊗^{L}_{𝒪_X} M` is `S`-perfect if `K` is perfect and `M` is `S`-perfect.

Here `S`-perfect is Stacks 0DI0, `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsRelativelyPerfect`, and the
derived tensor product is the one of Stacks 06YU.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyPerfect_of_isPerfect_and_derivedTensor :
    (∀ E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace),
        RingedSpace.IsPerfect E → f.IsRelativelyPerfect E) ∧
      ∀ K M : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace),
        RingedSpace.IsPerfect K → f.IsRelativelyPerfect M →
          f.IsRelativelyPerfect
            (((Stacks.Cohomology.PseudoCoherentTensor.derivedTensorProduct
              X.toRingedSpace).tensor.obj K).obj M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherent_derivedPullback_of_isPerfectRelativeTo
declarations.doc:
**The pseudo-coherence conjunct of Stacks 0DI5.** For `f : X ⟶ S` flat and locally of finite
presentation, `g : S' ⟶ S` arbitrary, `X' = S' ×_S X` with projection `g' : X' ⟶ X`, and `K` an
`S`-perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`, the derived pullback `L(g')^*K` is pseudo-coherent.

Only the pseudo-coherence conjunct of `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsPerfectRelativeTo` is used,
so the family of derived tensor products on the inverse-image ringed space plays no role and is
left arbitrary.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherent_derivedPullback_of_isPerfectRelativeTo
    {X S S' X' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S')
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (_hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (D : ∀ U : TopologicalSpace.Opens
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base).carrier,
      RingedSpace.CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.{u + 1, u}
        ((RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base).restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))
    (K : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace))
    (hK : f.IsPerfectRelativeTo D K) :
    RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X'.toRingedSpace)
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj K)
declarations.comment: the pseudo-coherence conjunct of the conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isRelativelyPerfect_derivedPullback_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI5.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes which is flat and locally of finite
presentation, let `g : S' ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, and let `X'` with `g' : X' ⟶ X` and
`f' : X' ⟶ S'` be a fibre product `S' ×_S X`. If `K` in `D(𝒪_X)` is `S`-perfect, then `L(g')^*K`
is `S'`-perfect.

Relative perfectness is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsRelativelyPerfect`, Stacks 0DI0 at the
derived tensor product of Stacks 06YU, on both sides. `Flat f'` and
`LocallyOfFinitePresentation f'`, which the conclusion needs in order to be stated, are the base
changes of the corresponding properties of `f` along `g`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRelativelyPerfect_derivedPullback_of_isPullback
    {X S S' X' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
    (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (K : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)) :
    haveI : Flat f' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @Flat) hpb inferInstance
    haveI : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f' :=
      MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @LocallyOfFinitePresentation) hpb inferInstance
    f.IsRelativelyPerfect K →
      f'.IsRelativelyPerfect
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
          g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPerfectRelativeTo_derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI5.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat and locally of finite presentation, `g : S' ⟶ S` a
morphism of schemes, and `X'` with `g' : X' ⟶ X`, `f' : X' ⟶ S'` the base change of `f` along `g`.
If `K` in `D(𝒪_X)` is `S`-perfect, then `L(g')^*K` is `S'`-perfect.

Relative perfectness is read at the derived tensor product of Stacks 06YU on the open subspaces
of the inverse-image ringed spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectRelativeTo_derivedPullback [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g) (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : f.IsPerfectRelativeTo
      (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base)) K) :
    haveI : Flat f' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @Flat) hpb (inferInstance : Flat f)
    haveI : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f' :=
      MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @LocallyOfFinitePresentation) hpb
        (inferInstance : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f)
    f'.IsPerfectRelativeTo
      (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage S'.toRingedSpace f'.base))
      ((derivedPullback g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDescentSituation
declarations.doc:
The relative descent situation: a directed inverse limit of
quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes with affine transition maps, together with a flat
morphism of finite presentation over a fixed stage.
declarations.statement: structure RelativeDescentSituation (I : Type v) [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDescentSituation.homDescent_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_locallyHasFiniteTorDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI7.** In Situation 0DI6, let `K₀` and `L₀` be objects of `D(𝒪_{X₀})` with `K₀`
pseudo-coherent and `L₀` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_{X₀})` of locally finite Tor dimension as an object of
`D((X₀ ⟶ S₀)⁻¹𝒪_{S₀})`. Then
`colim_i Hom_{D(𝒪_{Xᵢ})}(Lf_{i0}^*K₀, Lf_{i0}^*L₀) ⟶ Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(Lf₀^*K₀, Lf₀^*L₀)`
is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem homDescent_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_locallyHasFiniteTorDimension
    (hK₀ : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := D.X₀.left.toRingedSpace) K₀)
    (hL₀qc : ∀ n : ℤ,
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor D.X₀.left.Modules n).obj L₀).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hL₀tor : RingedSpace.LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension
      (RingedSpace.inverseImage (D.descent.system.obj (op D.descent.base)).toRingedSpace
        D.X₀.hom.base)
      (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily _)
      ((Scheme.Hom.derivedScalarRestriction D.X₀.hom).obj L₀)) :
    D.HomDescent K₀ L₀

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffinePerfectDescent.exists_isPerfectRelativeTo_stage
declarations.doc:
**The affine case of the essential-surjectivity half of Stacks 0DI8.** Let `R₀` be a ring,
let `i ↦ Rᵢ` be a filtered diagram of `R₀`-algebras with colimit `R`, and let `A₀` be a flat
`R₀`-algebra of finite presentation. Put `A = R ⊗_{R₀} A₀` and `Aᵢ = Rᵢ ⊗_{R₀} A₀`. Then every
object of `D(𝒪_{Spec A})` perfect relative to `Spec R` is, for some stage `i`, the derived
pullback along `Spec(Aᵢ → A)` of an object of `D(𝒪_{Spec Aᵢ})` perfect relative to `Spec Rᵢ`.

Relative perfectness is Stacks 0DI0 at the canonical certificate family on both sides. The
object has quasi-coherent cohomology by Stacks 08E5, so Stacks 06Z0 presents it as the derived
sheafification of a complex of `A`-modules; `isPerfectRelativeTo_tildeObj_iff` makes that complex
perfect relative to `R`; Stacks 0DHX descends it to a stage; and `derivedPullbackTildeObjIso`,
the affine comparison square of Stacks 08DW, identifies the derived pullback of the
sheafification at that stage with the sheafification of the derived extension of scalars.

Stacks 0DI8 itself is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDescentSituation.isPerfectRelativeTo_colimit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfectRelativeTo_stage
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u}
      (Spec (CommRingCat.of (c.pt ⊗[R₀] A₀))).toRingedSpace))
    (hE : (specMap c.pt (c.pt ⊗[R₀] A₀)).IsPerfectRelativeTo
      (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily _) E) :
    ∃ (i : I) (Ei : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u}
        (Spec (CommRingCat.of (PseudoCoherence.stageAlgebra F A₀ i))).toRingedSpace)),
      (specMap (F.obj i) (PseudoCoherence.stageAlgebra F A₀ i)).IsPerfectRelativeTo
          (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily _) Ei ∧
        Nonempty ((derivedPullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (PseudoCoherence.stageToLimitMap c A₀ i))).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Ei ≅ E)
declarations.comment: essential surjectivity only, and only in the affine case of the filtered system of rings of Stacks 0DHX. Full faithfulness (Stacks 0DI7) is not reproved, and nothing is proved for a general Situation 0DI6; see the implementation notes.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDescentSituation.isPerfectRelativeTo_colimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI8.** In Situation 0DI6 the category of `S`-perfect objects of `D(𝒪_X)` is the
colimit of the categories of `Sᵢ`-perfect objects of `D(𝒪_{Xᵢ})`: the transition functors
`Lf_{ji}^*` and the comparison functors `Lfᵢ^*` carry relatively perfect objects to relatively
perfect objects, the comparison out of the colimit is fully faithful, and it is essentially
surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectRelativeTo_colimit :
    (∀ {i j : D.LaterIndex} (h : i.1 ≤ j.1)
        (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} (D.schemeAt i).toRingedSpace)),
        D.IsPerfectAt i E →
          D.IsPerfectAt j ((derivedPullback (D.transition h).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E)) ∧
      (∀ (i : D.LaterIndex) (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} (D.schemeAt i).toRingedSpace)),
        D.IsPerfectAt i E →
          letI : Flat D.X₀.hom := D.flat
          letI : LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.X₀.hom :=
            D.finitePresentation.locallyOfFinitePresentation
          D.structureMapLimit.IsPerfectRelativeTo D.canonicalLimitCertificates
            ((derivedPullback (D.projection i).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E)) ∧
      (∀ (i : D.LaterIndex) (K L : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} (D.schemeAt i).toRingedSpace)),
        D.IsPerfectAt i K → D.IsPerfectAt i L → D.HomDescentAt i K L) ∧
      D.PerfectEssentiallySurjectiveCanonical

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isRelativelyPerfect_iff_isLocallyBoundedFlatFinitePresentation_and_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI9.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes.

1. If `f` is flat and locally of finite presentation (so that Definition 0DI0 applies), an object
   `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` is `S`-perfect exactly when it satisfies Lieblich's condition (A): locally on
   `X`, `E` is quasi-isomorphic to a finite complex of `S`-flat, finitely presented
   `𝒪_X`-modules.
2. If `f` is locally of finite type, condition (B) — `E` is pseudo-coherent relative to `S` and
   locally has finite Tor dimension as an object of `D(f⁻¹𝒪_S)` — defines a strictly full
   triangulated subcategory of `D(𝒪_X)`.
3. Condition (B) is the natural generalisation of Definition 0DI0: when `f` is flat and locally of
   finite presentation, (B) holds exactly for the `S`-perfect objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyPerfect_iff_isLocallyBoundedFlatFinitePresentation_and_isTriangulated :
    (∀ [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
        (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)),
      f.IsRelativelyPerfect E ↔ f.IsLocallyBoundedFlatFinitePresentation E) ∧
    (∀ [LocallyOfFiniteType f],
      f.isPseudoCoherentOfLocallyFiniteTorDimensionOver.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
        f.isPseudoCoherentOfLocallyFiniteTorDimensionOver.IsTriangulated) ∧
    (∀ [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
        (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)),
      f.isPseudoCoherentOfLocallyFiniteTorDimensionOver E ↔ f.IsRelativelyPerfect E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isPseudoCoherentOfFiniteTorDimensionRelativeTo
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI9, condition (B).** For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` which is only assumed
locally of finite type, the objects of `D(𝒪_X)` satisfying condition (B) form a *strictly full*
subcategory: both clauses are invariant under isomorphism in `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isPseudoCoherentOfFiniteTorDimensionRelativeTo :
    (isPseudoCoherentOfFiniteTorDimensionRelativeTo f D).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms
declarations.comment: condition (B) defines a triangulated subcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isTriangulated_isPseudoCoherentOfFiniteTorDimensionRelativeTo
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DI9, condition (B).** For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` which is only assumed
locally of finite type — neither flat nor locally of finite presentation — the objects of
`D(𝒪_X)` that are pseudo-coherent relative to `S` and of locally finite Tor dimension in
`D(f⁻¹𝒪_S)` form a *triangulated* subcategory: the property contains the zero object, is stable
under all shifts, and is closed under extensions.

Both clauses are triangulated subcategories separately — relative pseudo-coherence by Stacks
09UL, finite Tor dimension by Stacks 08CJ — and their intersection is one again. Exactness of
each `- ⊗^{L} ℱ[0]` and locality of finite Tor dimension are hypotheses, both of them properties
of the genuine derived tensor product that an arbitrary certificate need not have.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isTriangulated_isPseudoCoherentOfFiniteTorDimensionRelativeTo :
    (isPseudoCoherentOfFiniteTorDimensionRelativeTo f D).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: condition (B) defines a triangulated subcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DIB.** The standing data of Grothendieck's existence theorem in its
derived form: an inverse system of rings with surjective, locally nilpotent transitions, a
proper flat scheme of finite presentation over the inverse-limit ring, and a compatible system
of pseudo-coherent objects on its base changes.
declarations.statement: public structure DerivedExistenceSituation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.isDerivedLimit_coherator_obj
declarations.doc:
**The displayed equality of [Stacks, Tag 0DIC]**: `Rlim_{D_QCoh(𝒪_X)}(Kₙ)` and
`DQ_X(Rlim_{D(𝒪_X)} Kₙ)` agree. Precisely, if `K` is a derived limit of an inverse system `(Kₙ)`
in `D(𝒪_X)` then `DQ_X(K)` is a derived limit of the system `(DQ_X(Kₙ))` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`; the
existence of the product of the images is part of the conclusion.

This is the source's reason for the equality: `DQ_X` is a right adjoint, so it commutes with
products, and it is exact because the adjunction `ι ⊣ DQ_X` is triangulated, so it carries the
derived-limit triangle of `(Kₙ)` to the derived-limit triangle of `(DQ_X(Kₙ))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_coherator_obj (adj : quasiCoherentι X ⊣ DQ) [DQ.CommShift ℤ]
    [adj.IsTriangulated] (L : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ => L.obj ⟨n⟩] (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : IsDerivedLimit L K) :
    ∃ h : HasProduct fun n : ℕ => DQ.obj (L.obj ⟨n⟩),
      @IsDerivedLimit (quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) _ _ _ _ _ _ (L ⋙ DQ) h (DQ.obj K)
declarations.comment: the displayed equality only; the coherator of Stacks 0CR0 is an argument, as in Stacks 0CSA and 0CR2, and the tower is an arbitrary inverse system in D(O_X) rather than the system Ri_n,* K_n of Situation 0DIB, which this library cannot yet form at the locally small model the coherator lives at

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.limitObject_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DIC.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0DIB] consider
`K = R lim_{D_QCoh(𝒪_X)}(Kₙ) = DQ_X(R lim_{D(𝒪_X)} Kₙ)`. Then `K` is in `D^-_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.

Here `R lim_{D(𝒪_X)} Kₙ` is a chosen derived limit
(`AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.derivedLimit`) of the system
`(R(iₙ)_* Kₙ)` whose transition maps are the adjoints of the `φₙ`, and `DQ_X` is the coherator of
[Stacks, Tag 0CR0]. The three conjuncts are:

* the displayed equality: `DQ_X(R lim_{D(𝒪_X)} Kₙ)` is a derived limit `R lim_{D_QCoh(𝒪_X)}(Kₙ)`
  of the system in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`;
* `K`, read at the model of the situation
  (`AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.limitObject`), has
  quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves;
* `K` is bounded above.

The proof is the source's, see the module documentation and that of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Flatness/GrothendieckExistence/DerivedLimitObject.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem limitObject_spec :
    (∃ _ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ => S.qcohTower.obj (op n),
      IsDerivedLimit S.qcohTower S.coheratorLimit) ∧
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard
      (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u, u} S.X.left.toRingedSpace)
    (∀ j : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ j).obj S.limitObject).IsQuasicoherent) ∧
      ∃ c : ℤ, S.limitObject.IsLE c

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.isPseudoCoherent_cohomology_and_isIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DID].** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0DIB] let `K` be as in
[Stacks, Tag 0DIC]. For any perfect object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` the cohomology
`M = RΓ(X, K ⊗^L E)` is a pseudo-coherent object of `D(A)` and there is a canonical isomorphism
`RΓ(X_n, K_n ⊗^L E|_{X_n}) = M ⊗^L_A A_n` in `D(A_n)`, where `E|_{X_n}` is the derived pullback
of `E` to `X_n`.

Here `K` is `AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.limitObject`, `M`
is `AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.cohomology`, and the
canonical isomorphism is the base change map `M ⊗^L_A A_n ⟶ RΓ(X_n, K_n ⊗^L E|_{X_n})` adjoint to
the canonical map `M ⟶ RΓ(X_n, K_n ⊗^L E|_{X_n})`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.cohomologyMap`): pull back
along `X_n ⟶ X`, identify `(K ⊗^L E)|_{X_n} = K|_{X_n} ⊗^L E|_{X_n}`, and apply the canonical map
`K|_{X_n} ⟶ K_n`.

The proof is the source's. `RΓ(X, - ⊗^L E)` carries the derived-limit triangle of
`K = DQ_X(R lim K_n)` to a triangle presenting `M` as `R lim M_n` for `M_n = RΓ(X_n, K_n ⊗^L E_n)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.exists_distTriang_cohomology`);
the `M_n` are pseudo-coherent ([Stacks, Tag 0CSD]) with `M_{n+1} ⊗^L A_n = M_n` by flat base
change; and [Stacks, Tag 0CQF] concludes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_cohomology_and_isIso
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := S.X.left.toRingedSpace) E) :
    StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent (S.cohomology E) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (StacksDraft.DerivedInverseLimit.derivedBaseChangeComparison.{u, u, u}
        (limit.π S.system (op n)).hom (S.cohomologyMap E n))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.isPseudoCoherent_limitObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DIE.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0DIB] let `K` be as in
[Stacks, Tag 0DIC]. Then `K` is pseudo-coherent on `X`.

Here `K = DQ_X(R lim Kₙ)` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.limitObject`, an object of
`D(𝒪_X)` at the model at which the `Kₙ` are given. By [Stacks, Tag 0DID] (its first assertion,
`DerivedExistenceSituation.isPseudoCoherent_cohomology_and_isIso`)
`RΓ(X, K ⊗^𝐋 E)` is pseudo-coherent for every perfect `E`; [Stacks, Tag 0GES] (which is
[Stacks, Tags 0CSH and 0CSL] together, `X` being separated and of finite presentation over `A`
and `K` lying in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` by [Stacks, Tag 0DIC]) makes `K` pseudo-coherent relative to `A`,
and [Stacks, Tag 09UU] (for schemes, [Stacks, Tag 0DII]) turns that into pseudo-coherence on `X`,
`X` being flat and of finite presentation over `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_limitObject (S : DerivedExistenceSituation.{u}) :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u, u} S.X.left.toRingedSpace)
    RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := S.X.left.toRingedSpace) S.limitObject

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.isIso_derivedBaseChangeComparison_derivedSections
declarations.doc:
In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0DIB] let `K` be as in [Stacks, Tag 0DIC]. For any quasi-compact
open `U ⊆ X` we have `RΓ(U, K) ⊗^𝐋_A Aₙ = RΓ(Uₙ, Kₙ)` in `D(Aₙ)`, where `Uₙ = U ∩ Xₙ`.

Here `K` is `AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.limitObject`,
`RΓ(U, K)` is the `A`-linear derived global sections of `K|_U`, `RΓ(Uₙ, Kₙ)` the `Aₙ`-linear
derived global sections of `Kₙ|_{Uₙ}`, and the identification is the canonical map
`RΓ(U, K) ⊗^𝐋_A Aₙ ⟶ RΓ(Uₙ, Kₙ)`: the adjoint of
`AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.openRestrictionMap`, which pulls
derived sections back along `Uₙ ⟶ U` and applies the canonical map `K|_{Xₙ} ⟶ Kₙ` adjoint to the
projection `K ⟶ R(iₙ)_* Kₙ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedBaseChangeComparison_derivedSections (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S.X.left)) :
    IsIso (derivedBaseChangeComparison (limit.π S.system (op n)).hom
      (S.openRestrictionMap U n S.limitObject (S.restrictionMap n)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GrothendieckExistence.DerivedExistenceSituation.exists_isPseudoCoherent_derivedPullback_iso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DIG], Grothendieck's existence theorem in its derived form.** In Situation
[Stacks, Tag 0DIB] there is a pseudo-coherent `K ∈ D(𝒪_X)` together with isomorphisms
`βₙ : K ⊗ᴸ_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_{Xₙ} = L(iₙ)^* K ≅ Kₙ` compatible with the maps `φₙ`: the composite
`L(jₙ)^* L(iₙ₊₁)^* K ≅ L(iₙ)^* K ⟶ Kₙ` of the composition isomorphism with `βₙ` is
`L(jₙ)^* βₙ₊₁` followed by `φₙ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPseudoCoherent_derivedPullback_iso :
    ∃ K : DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u, u} S.X.left.toRingedSpace),
      RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := S.X.left.toRingedSpace) K ∧
        ∃ β : ∀ n : ℕ, (derivedPullback (S.levelInclusion n)).obj K ≅ S.K n,
          ∀ n : ℕ,
            (Stacks.DerivedPullback.Composition.derivedPullbackCompIsoCanonical
                (S.levelTransition n) (S.levelInclusion (n + 1))).hom.app K ≫
              eqToHom (congrArg (fun t : (schemeAt S.system S.X n).toRingedSpace ⟶
                  S.X.left.toRingedSpace => (derivedPullback t).obj K)
                (S.levelTransition_comp_levelInclusion n)) ≫ (β n).hom =
            (derivedPullback (S.levelTransition n)).map (β (n + 1)).hom ≫ S.φ n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherent_iff_of_flat_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DII, the case of schemes.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism of schemes locally of
finite presentation and let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)`. Then `E` is pseudo-coherent relative to
`Y` in the sense of Stacks 09UI if and only if `E` is pseudo-coherent on `X` in the sheaf-level
sense of Stacks 08CB.
declarations.comment: the case of schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_forall_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DII in a fixed degree, by étale localization.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite presentation, let `E` be an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and let `m` be an integer.  Then `E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `Y` if and
only if, on every commuting square of affine étale scheme charts `U` of `X` and `V` of `Y` over
`f`, the complex `RΓ(U, E)` is `m`-pseudo-coherent over the ring `𝒪_X(U)`.

Relative `m`-pseudo-coherence is by definition the relative condition on those same squares, so
the two sides differ square by square only, and on one square the equivalence is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativePseudoCoherence_chart_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_forall_chart
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f) (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X hX) (m : ℤ) :
    IsRelativelyPseudoCoherentFrom B S hS X hX f
        (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS hfp) E m ↔
      ∀ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y)
          (g : (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj V),
          yoneda.map g ≫ V.obj.hom = U.obj.hom ≫ f →
          IsAffine (chartScheme U) → IsAffine (chartScheme V) →
        StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherentFrom
          (chartDerivedSections B S hS X hX U E) m
declarations.comment: the fixed-degree etale-chart localization: relative m-pseudo-coherence over Y is m-pseudo-coherence of RGamma(U, E) over O_X(U) on every square of affine etale charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_iff_forall_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DII by étale localization.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` which is locally of finite presentation and let `E` be an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.  Then `E` is pseudo-coherent relative to `Y` if and only if, on every commuting
square of affine étale scheme charts `U` of `X` and `V` of `Y` over `f`, the complex `RΓ(U, E)`
is pseudo-coherent over the ring `𝒪_X(U)` — the target playing no role.

This is the all-degrees clause of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativePseudoCoherence_chart_iff` on each of the squares that relative
pseudo-coherence of Stacks 0CSY is tested on; see "What is proved, and what the right-hand side
says" in the module docstring for the sense in which the right-hand side is the absolute
condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_iff_forall_chart
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f) (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X hX) :
    IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent B S hS X hX f
        (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS hfp) E ↔
      ∀ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y)
          (g : (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj V),
          yoneda.map g ≫ V.obj.hom = U.obj.hom ≫ f →
          IsAffine (chartScheme U) → IsAffine (chartScheme V) →
        StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
          (chartDerivedSections B S hS X hX U E)
declarations.comment: the etale-chart localization: pseudo-coherence relative to Y is pseudo-coherence of RGamma(U, E) over O_X(U) on every square of affine etale charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_iff_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
flat and locally of finite presentation.  Let `E` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.  Then `E` is
pseudo-coherent relative to `Y` if and only if `E` is pseudo-coherent on `X`, the latter read on
the small étale ringed site of `X`.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_iff_isPseudoCoherent_of_chartDictionary` at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartPseudoCoherenceDictionaryFrom_holds` in every degree.  It is not the
fixed-degree statement above read degree by degree: the all-degrees clause of Stacks 08FT (3) asks
for one complex which is `m`-pseudo-coherent for every `m`, and the quantifier swap happens on the
site side, inside that theorem.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_iff_isPseudoCoherent (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f.hom) (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 f.hom
        (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS hfp) E ↔
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPseudoCoherent E.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DerivedExistenceSystem
declarations.doc:
The standing data of Grothendieck's existence theorem for algebraic spaces in its derived
form: an inverse system of rings `(Aₙ)` with surjective transitions whose kernels are locally
nilpotent, an algebraic space `X` proper, flat and of finite presentation over `A = lim Aₙ`, and
pseudo-coherent objects `Kₙ` of `D(𝒪_{Xₙ})` on the infinitesimal base changes
`Xₙ = X ×_{Spec A} Spec Aₙ`, with maps `Liₙ^* Kₙ₊₁ ⟶ Kₙ` that are isomorphisms, `Liₙ^*` being
the derived pullback along `Xₙ ⟶ Xₙ₊₁` constructed in `transitionDerivedPullback`.
declarations.statement: structure DerivedExistenceSystem
declarations.comment: the situation as stated, with the derived pullback along each Xₙ → Xₙ₊₁ constructed by Stacks 06YY; its fields are the data and hypotheses of the source, together with a big fppf site containing Spec A and every Spec Aₙ in which the algebraic spaces are taken

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DerivedExistenceSystem.derivedLimit_isBoundedAbove
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0DIK the inclusion `D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` has a right adjoint `DQ_X` and the
tower `(Rjₙ,* Kₙ)` has a derived limit `L = R lim_{D(𝒪_X)} Kₙ`. For every coherator `DQ_X` and
every such `L`, `K = DQ_X(L)` is a derived limit of the tower in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` whose cohomology
sheaves vanish above some degree. Every derived limit of the tower in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` lies in
`D⁻_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedLimit_isBoundedAbove :
    (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι.IsLeftAdjoint ∧
    (∃ L, IsDerivedLimit D.toSeparated.spaceTower L) ∧
    (∀ (DQ : spaceDerivedCategory D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left ⥤
        (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase
          D.X.left).FullSubcategory)
      (_ : (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι ⊣ DQ)
      (L : spaceDerivedCategory D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left),
      IsDerivedLimit D.toSeparated.spaceTower L →
        (∃ _ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ => D.toSeparated.quasicoherentTower.obj ⟨n⟩,
          IsDerivedLimit D.toSeparated.quasicoherentTower (DQ.obj L)) ∧
        ∃ c : ℤ, SpaceCohomologyVanishesAbove D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase
          D.X.left c ((spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase
            D.X.left).ι.obj (DQ.obj L))) ∧
    ∀ (_ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ => D.toSeparated.quasicoherentTower.obj ⟨n⟩)
      (K : (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase
        D.X.left).FullSubcategory),
      IsDerivedLimit D.toSeparated.quasicoherentTower K →
        ∃ c : ℤ, SpaceCohomologyVanishesAbove D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase
          D.X.left c ((spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase
            D.X.left).ι.obj K)
declarations.comment: K = R lim_{D_QCoh} K_n = DQ_X(R lim_{D(O_X)} K_n) lies in D^-_QCoh(O_X), for every choice of coherator and of derived limits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DerivedExistenceSystem.isPseudoCoherent_and_isIso_stageTensorSectionsBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DIM].** In Situation 0DIK let `K = DQ_X(R lim Kₙ)` be the object of
[Stacks, Tag 0DIL] and `E` a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`. Then `M = RΓ(X, E ⊗^L K)` is a
pseudo-coherent object of `D(A)`, and for every `n` the canonical map
`cₙ : M ⊗^L_A Aₙ ⟶ RΓ(Xₙ, Lpₙ^*E ⊗^L Kₙ)` (the base change map of `RΓ`, then Stacks 07A4 and
`Lpₙ^*E ⊗^L τₙ`, with `τₙ : Lpₙ^*K ⟶ Kₙ` adjoint to the projection) is an isomorphism in
`D(Aₙ)`. Here `K` is `D.quasicoherentLimit`, with `R lim Kₙ = D.derivedLimit` and `DQ_X` the
right adjoint `D.coherator` of the inclusion `D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_and_isIso_stageTensorSectionsBaseChange (D : DerivedExistenceSystem.{u})
    (E : spaceDerivedCategory D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left)
    (hE : spaceIsPerfect D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left E) :
    StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
        ((D.toSeparated.limitTensorSections E).obj ((spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B (limitBase D.system)
          D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι.obj D.toSeparated.quasicoherentLimit)) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (D.toSeparated.stageTensorSectionsBaseChange D.toSeparated.coherator
        D.toSeparated.coheratorAdjunction E n)
declarations.comment: the full statement: for every perfect E, M = RΓ(X, E ⊗^L K) is pseudo-coherent and the canonical map M ⊗^L_A Aₙ ⟶ RΓ(Xₙ, Lpₙ^*E ⊗^L Kₙ) is an isomorphism in D(Aₙ) for every n. D is Situation 0DIK (DerivedExistenceSystem), whose fields are only the situation's data and hypotheses: the rings Aₙ with surjective transitions with locally nilpotent kernels, the fppf site containing Spec A and every Spec Aₙ, X proper, flat and of finite presentation over A, the pseudo-coherent Kₙ, and the comparison isomorphisms Liₙ^* Kₙ₊₁ ≅ Kₙ; no result is a field. K = DQ_X(R lim Kₙ) is the object of 0DIL, built from the coherator (the right adjoint of D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)) and a derived limit, both constructed and not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DerivedExistenceSystem.isPseudoCoherentOnLimit_quasicoherentDerivedLimit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DIN].** In Situation 0DIK the inclusion `ι : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` has a right
adjoint `DQ_X` and the tower `(Rjₙ,* Kₙ)` has a derived limit `L = R lim_{D(𝒪_X)} Kₙ`. For every
coherator `adj : ι ⊣ DQ_X` and every such `L`, the object `K = DQ_X(L)` is a derived limit
`R lim_{D_QCoh(𝒪_X)} Kₙ` of the tower in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and is pseudo-coherent on `X`. Moreover every
derived limit of the tower in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is pseudo-coherent on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentOnLimit_quasicoherentDerivedLimit (D : DerivedExistenceSystem.{u}) :
    (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι.IsLeftAdjoint ∧
    (∃ L, IsDerivedLimit D.toSeparated.spaceTower L) ∧
    (∀ (DQ : spaceDerivedCategory D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left ⥤
        (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase
          D.X.left).FullSubcategory)
      (_ : (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι ⊣ DQ)
      (L : spaceDerivedCategory D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left),
      IsDerivedLimit D.toSeparated.spaceTower L →
        (∃ _ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ => D.toSeparated.quasicoherentTower.obj ⟨n⟩,
          IsDerivedLimit D.toSeparated.quasicoherentTower (DQ.obj L)) ∧
        D.IsPseudoCoherentOnLimit
          ((spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι.obj
            (DQ.obj L))) ∧
    ∀ (_ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ => D.toSeparated.quasicoherentTower.obj ⟨n⟩)
      (K : (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase
        D.X.left).FullSubcategory),
      IsDerivedLimit D.toSeparated.quasicoherentTower K →
        D.IsPseudoCoherentOnLimit
          ((spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι.obj
            K)
declarations.comment: the full statement: a coherator DQ_X and a derived limit R lim_{D(O_X)} K_n exist, and for every such choice K = DQ_X(R lim_{D(O_X)} K_n) is a derived limit R lim_{D_QCoh} K_n and is pseudo-coherent on X; every derived limit of the tower in D_QCoh(O_X) is pseudo-coherent on X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DerivedExistenceSystem.isIso_etaleSectionsBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0DIK let `K = DQ_X(R lim Kₙ)` be the object of [Stacks, Tag 0DIL]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SeparatedDerivedExistenceSystem.quasicoherentLimit` of
`D.toSeparated`, for the coherator `DQ_X`
right adjoint to `D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)`). For every étale `j : U ⟶ X` with `U`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated and every `n`, the canonical map
`RΓ(U, K) ⊗^L_A Aₙ ⟶ RΓ(Uₙ, Kₙ)` in `D(Aₙ)`, with `Uₙ = U ×_X Xₙ` (the base change map of `RΓ`
along `Spec Aₙ ⟶ Spec A`, then `RΓ(Uₙ, -)` of `τₙ|_{Uₙ}`, with `τₙ : Lpₙ^*K ⟶ Kₙ` adjoint to the
projection), is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_etaleSectionsBaseChangeMap (D : DerivedExistenceSystem.{u})
    {U : AlgebraicSpaces D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase} (j : U ⟶ D.X.left)
    (hj : IsEtale D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase j.hom)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase U.1)
    (hUqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase
      D.B.contains_terminal U.1) (n : ℕ) :
    IsIso (D.toSeparated.etaleSectionsBaseChangeMap j D.toSeparated.coherator
      D.toSeparated.coheratorAdjunction n)
declarations.comment: in Situation 0DIK with K = DQ_X(R lim K_n) as in 0DIL: for every étale U → X with U qcqs and every n, the canonical map RΓ(U, K) ⊗^L_A A_n → RΓ(U_n, K_n) is an isomorphism in D(A_n), U_n = U ×_X X_n; the full statement, with 0CRW and 0DIM proved in the library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DerivedExistenceSystem.exists_isPseudoCoherent_stageDerivedPullback_iso
declarations.doc:
**The derived Grothendieck existence theorem.** In Situation 0DIK there is a
pseudo-coherent `K` in `D(𝒪_X)` with `Kₙ = K ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_{Xₙ}` for all `n`, compatibly with the
maps `φₙ`: isomorphisms `ψₙ : Ljₙ^* K ≅ Kₙ` (`Ljₙ^*` the derived pullback along `jₙ : Xₙ ⟶ X`) with
`ψₙ = (Ljₙ^* ≅ Liₙ^* Ljₙ₊₁^*) ≫ Liₙ^* ψₙ₊₁ ≫ φₙ`, where `Ljₙ^* ≅ Liₙ^* Ljₙ₊₁^*` is the composition
isomorphism of derived pullbacks along `iₙ ≫ jₙ₊₁ = jₙ`.

Proof as in the source: `K = DQ_X(R lim Kₙ)` is pseudo-coherent by [Stacks, Tag 0DIN] (from both
halves of [Stacks, Tag 0DIM]), and the maps `τₙ : Ljₙ^* K ⟶ Kₙ` are isomorphisms by
[Stacks, Tag 0DIP] over affine `U` étale over `X`, compatible with the `φₙ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPseudoCoherent_stageDerivedPullback_iso (D : DerivedExistenceSystem.{u}) :
    ∃ (K : D.limitDerivedCategory) (ψ : ∀ n : ℕ, (D.stageDerivedPullback n).obj K ≅ D.K n),
      D.IsPseudoCoherentOnLimit K ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, (ψ n).hom = (D.stageDerivedPullbackCompIso n).inv.app K ≫
          (transitionDerivedPullback D.system D.B D.containsLimitBase D.containsBaseAt D.X n).map
            (ψ (n + 1)).hom ≫ D.φ n
declarations.comment: the full statement in Situation 0DIK with no further hypotheses: a pseudo-coherent K on X with isomorphisms Lj_n^* K = K_n for all n, compatible with the phi_n through the composition isomorphism of derived pullbacks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SupportedDerivedExistenceSystem
declarations.doc:
**The data of the generalized derived existence theorem (Stacks 0DIR, `X` flat).** An inverse
system of rings `(Aₙ)` with surjective transitions whose kernels are locally nilpotent, an
algebraic space `X` separated, flat and of finite presentation over `A = lim Aₙ`, and
pseudo-coherent `Kₙ ∈ D(𝒪_{Xₙ})` with isomorphisms `Liₙ^* Kₙ₊₁ ≅ Kₙ`, each `Kₙ` supported on a
closed subset `Zₙ` of `|Xₙ|` proper over `Spec Aₙ`.
declarations.statement: structure SupportedDerivedExistenceSystem extends SeparatedDerivedExistenceSystem.{u}
declarations.comment: the setting of the corrected remark: A = lim A_n with surjective transitions and locally nilpotent kernels, X separated, flat and of finite presentation over A, K_n pseudo-coherent on X_n supported on a closed subset proper over A_n, phi_n isomorphisms; flatness is necessary, see the errata entry 0DIR(flatness dropped)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SupportedDerivedExistenceSystem.exists_isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_stageDerivedPullback_iso_isProperOver_supportOfSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Grothendieck's existence theorem in its derived form, with supports proper over the base
(Stacks 0DIR, `X` flat over `A`, the per-degree support clause).** There is `K ∈ D(𝒪_X)`,
pseudo-coherent relative to `A`, with isomorphisms `ψₙ : Ljₙ^* K ≅ Kₙ` such that
`ψₙ = (Ljₙ^* ≅ Liₙ^* Ljₙ₊₁^*) ≫ Liₙ^* ψₙ₊₁ ≫ φₙ`, and such that for every `i` the support of the
cohomology sheaf `Hⁱ(K)` lies in a closed subset of `|X|` proper over `Spec A`. The source's
clause that the whole of `K` is supported on one closed subset proper over `A` fails (see the
module `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Deformations.DerivedExistenceSupported`); this is
the per-degree form, which holds.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_stageDerivedPullback_iso_isProperOver_supportOfSheaf :
    ∃ (K : D.limitDerivedCategory)
      (ψ : ∀ n : ℕ, (D.stageDerivedPullback n).obj K ≅ D.K n)
      (hK : QcohDerived D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left K),
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1
          D.X.left.2 D.X.hom.hom
          (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation D.B (limitBase D.system)
            D.containsLimitBase D.finitePresentation.1) ⟨K, hK⟩ ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, (ψ n).hom = (D.stageDerivedPullbackCompIso n).inv.app K ≫
          (transitionDerivedPullback D.system D.B D.containsLimitBase D.containsBaseAt D.X n).map
            (ψ (n + 1)).hom ≫ D.φ n) ∧
        ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ (T : Set (points D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1))
          (hT : IsClosed T),
          IsProperOver D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.2
              (schemeSpace (limitBaseObject D.system D.B D.containsLimitBase)).2 D.X.hom.hom
              (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation D.B (limitBase D.system)
                D.containsLimitBase D.finitePresentation.1) T hT ∧
            supportOfSheaf D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1
              ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
                (smallEtaleRingedSite D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1
                  D.X.left.2).O)).obj
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} D.B (limitBase D.system)
                  D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1 D.X.left.2) i).obj K)) ⊆ T
declarations.comment: corrected form, X flat: K pseudo-coherent relative to A, Lj_n^* K = K_n compatibly with the phi_n, and each cohomology sheaf of K supported on a closed subset proper over A; the one-subset support clause and the case of non-flat X are false (errata 0DIR)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RelativeDerivedExistenceSystem.exists_isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_stageDerivedPullback_iso_isProperOver_supportOfSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The generalized derived existence theorem for the data of Stacks 0DIR, `X` flat over `A`,
with the per-degree support clause.** Let `(Aₙ)`, `X` separated and of finite presentation over
`A = lim Aₙ`, and `Kₙ ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_{Xₙ})` pseudo-coherent relative to `Aₙ`, supported on closed
subsets of `|Xₙ|` proper over `Aₙ`, with isomorphisms `φₙ : Liₙ^* Kₙ₊₁ ≅ Kₙ`, be as in the
remark, and let `X` be flat over `A`. Then there is `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, pseudo-coherent relative
to `A`, with isomorphisms `ψₙ : Ljₙ^* K ≅ Kₙ` such that
`ψₙ = (Ljₙ^* ≅ Liₙ^* Ljₙ₊₁^*) ≫ Liₙ^* ψₙ₊₁ ≫ φₙ`, and such that for every `i` the support of
`Hⁱ(K)` lies in a closed subset of `|X|` proper over `Spec A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_stageDerivedPullback_iso_isProperOver_supportOfSheaf
    (hflat : IsFlat D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.hom.hom) :
    ∃ (K : (D.toSupported hflat).limitDerivedCategory)
      (ψ : ∀ n : ℕ, ((D.toSupported hflat).stageDerivedPullback n).obj K ≅ D.K n)
      (hK : QcohDerived D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left K),
      IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1
          D.X.left.2 D.X.hom.hom
          (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation D.B (limitBase D.system)
            D.containsLimitBase D.finitePresentation.1) ⟨K, hK⟩ ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, (ψ n).hom = ((D.toSupported hflat).stageDerivedPullbackCompIso n).inv.app K ≫
          (transitionDerivedPullback D.system D.B D.containsLimitBase D.containsBaseAt D.X n).map
            (ψ (n + 1)).hom ≫ D.φ n) ∧
        ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ (T : Set (points D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1))
          (hT : IsClosed T),
          IsProperOver D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.2
              (schemeSpace (limitBaseObject D.system D.B D.containsLimitBase)).2 D.X.hom.hom
              (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation D.B (limitBase D.system)
                D.containsLimitBase D.finitePresentation.1) T hT ∧
            supportOfSheaf D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1
              ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
                (smallEtaleRingedSite D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1
                  D.X.left.2).O)).obj
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} D.B (limitBase D.system)
                  D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1 D.X.left.2) i).obj K)) ⊆ T
declarations.comment: corrected form on the remark's own data (X separated, of finite presentation, K_n pseudo-coherent relative to A_n, supported on closed subsets proper over A_n) with X flat: K pseudo-coherent relative to A, Lj_n^* K = K_n compatibly, each cohomology sheaf of K supported on a closed subset proper over A; flatness is necessary and one closed subset for all of K fails (errata 0DIR)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.DerivedExistenceNotFlat.not_forall_exists_isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_stageDerivedPullback_iso
declarations.doc:
**The generalization of the derived existence theorem proposed in Stacks 0DIR is false
without flatness.** There is a system satisfying all of its hypotheses — `Aₙ = 𝔽₂ ⊕ 𝔽₂ⁿ`,
`X = Spec A/(f)` closed in `Spec A`, `Kₙ = 𝒪_{Xₙ}` — admitting no `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`
pseudo-coherent relative to `A` with `Ljₙ^* K ≅ Kₙ` for every `n` (not even for `n = 0`, and
with no compatibility asked of the isomorphisms).
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_exists_isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_stageDerivedPullback_iso :
    ¬ ∀ D : RelativeDerivedExistenceSystem.{0},
      ∃ (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{0}
          (ringedToposStructureRingSheaf D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left)))
        (hK : QcohDerived D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left K),
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1
            D.X.left.2 D.X.hom.hom
            (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation D.B (limitBase D.system)
              D.containsLimitBase D.finitePresentation.1) ⟨K, hK⟩ ∧
          ∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty ((smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback D.B (limitBase D.system)
            D.containsLimitBase (spaceProjection D.system D.B D.containsLimitBase
              D.containsBaseAt D.X n)).obj K ≅ D.K n)
declarations.comment: refutation of the remark with X separated and of finite presentation, not flat: X = Spec A/(f), K_n = O_{X_n} admits no K pseudo-coherent relative to A with Lj_n^* K = K_n (errata entry 0DIR(flatness dropped))

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.DerivedExistenceSupportNotProper.not_forall_exists_isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_isProperOver_cohomologySupportedOn
declarations.doc:
**The support clause of the generalized derived existence theorem proposed in Stacks 0DIR is
false.** There is a system satisfying all of its hypotheses, with `X` moreover flat over `A` —
`A = ℤ_2`, `X = 𝔸¹_A`, `Kₙ = ⊕ᵢ 𝒪_{Xₙ}/(x - 2^{i+1})[2i]`, each `Kₙ` supported on `V(x)`, finite
over `Aₙ` — for which no `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` pseudo-coherent relative to `A` with `Ljₙ^* K ≅ Kₙ`
for every `n` (with no compatibility asked of the isomorphisms) is supported on a closed subset
of `|X|` proper over `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_exists_isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_isProperOver_cohomologySupportedOn :
    ¬ ∀ D : SupportedDerivedExistenceSystem.{0},
      ∃ (K : D.limitDerivedCategory)
        (hK : QcohDerived D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left K),
        IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1
            D.X.left.2 D.X.hom.hom
            (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation D.B (limitBase D.system)
              D.containsLimitBase D.finitePresentation.1) ⟨K, hK⟩ ∧
          (∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty ((D.stageDerivedPullback n).obj K ≅ D.K n)) ∧
          ∃ (T : Set (points D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1))
            (hT : _root_.IsClosed T),
            IsProperOver D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.2
                (schemeSpace (limitBaseObject D.system D.B D.containsLimitBase)).2 D.X.hom.hom
                (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation D.B (limitBase D.system)
                  D.containsLimitBase D.finitePresentation.1) T hT ∧
              ∀ i : ℤ, supportOfSheaf D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1
                ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
                  (smallEtaleRingedSite D.B (limitBase D.system) D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1
                    D.X.left.2).O)).obj
                  ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Space.Modules.{0, 0} D.B (limitBase D.system)
                    D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1 D.X.left.2) i).obj K)) ⊆ T
declarations.comment: refutation of the clause that K is supported on one closed subset proper over A: A = Z_2, X = A^1_A, K_n = sum_i O_{X_n}/(x - 2^{i+1})[2i] (errata entry 0DIR(support of K))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.ComplexLifting.exists_liftedComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DIT.** A bounded-above flat lifting exists for a bounded-above complex and a
bounded-above graded flat family whose given maps form a map of complexes after extension of
scalars. The ambient module universe contains the site and the ring sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_liftedComplex [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w z}]
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w z}] {O O₀ : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}} (f : O ⟶ O₀)
    (hf : Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective f)
    (G : GradedDifferential
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O)))
    (K₀ : CochainComplex
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O₀)) ℤ)
    (g : ∀ n, G.X n ⟶
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars (ringSheafMap f)).obj (K₀.X n))
    (hGflat : ∀ n, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (G.X n))
    (hGbounded : ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, N ≤ n → IsZero (G.X n))
    (hKbounded : ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, N ≤ n → IsZero (K₀.homology n))
    (hG₀ : BaseChangeTo f G K₀ g) :
    Nonempty (LiftedComplex f G K₀ g)

declarations.name: Deformation.ComplexLift.unit_comp_curvature
declarations.doc:
The curvature computes the square of the lifted differential: pulled back to the lift and
followed by the ideal inclusion it is `d ∘ d`. This is the identification of `ω` with the
curvature class, read on the complex representing it.
declarations.statement:
theorem unit_comp_curvature (n : ℤ) :
    L.baseChange.unit n ≫ (restrict f).map (curvature T n) ≫ T.emb (n + 1 + 1) =
      L.F.d n ≫ L.F.d (n + 1)
declarations.comment:
variant: the curvature d ∘ d of the lifted differential, the complex-level
map; the tag is Deformation.ComplexLift.tensorOmegaMinus

declarations.name: Deformation.ComplexLift.obstructionMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DIU.** The canonical map `ω(K₀) : K₀ ⟶ (K₀ ⊗^L_{O₀} I)[2]` attached to a
square-zero extension of sheaves of rings with ideal sheaf `I`. It is the curvature of the
lifted differential of a bounded above flat lift of `K₀`, transported along the
quasi-isomorphism identifying the reduction of that lift with `K₀`.
declarations.statement:
def obstructionMap {L : FlatLift f K₀} (T : IdealKernel S L) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj K₀ ⟶ (D.functor.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K₀))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧
declarations.comment: variant: at a supplied derived ideal tensor datum D; the tag is Deformation.ComplexLift.tensorOmegaMinus, the map K₀ ⟶ (K₀ ⊗^L I)[2]

declarations.name: Deformation.ComplexLift.obstructionMap_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DIU.** Naturality of `ω`: for a map `φ : K₀ ⟶ L₀` of bounded above complexes
covered by a morphism of flat lifts, the square formed by `ω(K₀)`, `ω(L₀)` and the maps induced
by `φ` commutes.
declarations.statement:
theorem obstructionMap_natural :
    DerivedCategory.Q.map φ ≫ obstructionMap D TM =
      obstructionMap D TL ≫
        (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (SheafMod O₀)) (2 : ℤ)).map
          (D.functor.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map φ))
declarations.comment:
variant: naturality of ω along a morphism of flat lifts at a supplied derived ideal
tensor datum D; the tag is Deformation.ComplexLift.tensorOmegaMinus_natural

declarations.name: Deformation.ComplexLift.obstructionMap_eq_of_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DIU.** Two flat lifts of the same complex joined by a morphism of lifts over the
identity give the same map `ω(K₀)`. Together with the existence of a lift receiving maps from
any two, this is the independence of `ω` of the lift, hence its canonicality.
declarations.statement:
theorem obstructionMap_eq_of_hom {L M : FlatLift f K₀} (h : FlatLiftHom L M (𝟙 K₀))
    (TL : IdealKernel S L) (TM : IdealKernel S M)
    (hemb : ∀ n : ℤ, (restrict f).map (((idealTensorFunctor O₀ I).map h.red).f n) ≫
      TM.emb n = TL.emb n ≫ h.hom n) :
    obstructionMap D TL = obstructionMap D TM
declarations.comment:
variant: independence of the flat lift at a supplied derived ideal tensor datum D;
the tag is Deformation.ComplexLift.tensorOmegaMinus

declarations.name: Deformation.ComplexLift.tensorOmega
declarations.doc:
**The map `ω(K₀) : K₀ ⟶ (K₀ ⊗^L_{O₀} I)[2]` of a bounded above complex.** It is the curvature
class of a bounded above flat lift of `K₀` (Tag 0DIT), read through the canonical identification
of the ideal part of the lift with the kernel of its reduction; by
`Deformation.ComplexLift.tensorObstruction_eq_of_lift` it does not depend on the lift.
declarations.statement:
def tensorOmega (hf : Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective f) (S : SquareZeroIdeal f I)
    (K₀ : CochainComplex (SheafMod O₀) ℤ)
    (hK : ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, N ≤ n → IsZero (K₀.homology n)) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj K₀ ⟶
      ((derivedTensorRight.{d} I).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K₀))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧
declarations.comment: the canonical map ω(K₀) : K₀ ⟶ (K₀ ⊗^L I)[2], on a bounded above complex

declarations.name: Deformation.ComplexLift.tensorOmega_natural_derived
declarations.doc:
**Naturality of `ω` along an arbitrary morphism of `D(O₀)`** between bounded above
complexes: such a morphism is a roof `K₀ ⟶ M ⟵ L₀` of maps of complexes with the second leg a
quasi-isomorphism, and `ω` is natural along both legs.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorOmega_natural_derived (hf : Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective f) (S : SquareZeroIdeal f I)
    {K₀ L₀ : CochainComplex (SheafMod O₀) ℤ}
    (hK : ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, N ≤ n → IsZero (K₀.homology n))
    (hL : ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, N ≤ n → IsZero (L₀.homology n))
    (ψ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj K₀ ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj L₀) :
    ψ ≫ tensorOmega.{v, u, w, d} hf S L₀ hL =
      tensorOmega.{v, u, w, d} hf S K₀ hK ≫
        (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (SheafMod O₀)) (2 : ℤ)).map
          ((derivedTensorRight.{d} I).map ψ)
declarations.comment: naturality of ω, on bounded above complexes

declarations.name: Deformation.ComplexLift.tensorOmegaObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DIU.** Let `f : O ⟶ O₀` be a surjection of sheaves of commutative rings on a site
whose kernel is an ideal sheaf `I` of square zero (`S`). For every object `K₀` of `D⁻(O₀)` --
an object of `D(O₀)` whose cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently large degrees -- this is the
canonical map

`ω(K₀) : K₀ ⟶ (K₀ ⊗^L_{O₀} I)[2]`

in `D(O₀)`: it is `Deformation.ComplexLift.tensorOmega` on a complex representing `K₀`, the
curvature of the lifted differential of a bounded above flat lift.
declarations.statement:
def tensorOmegaObj (hf : Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective f) (S : SquareZeroIdeal f I)
    (X : DerivedCategory (SheafMod O₀))
    (hX : ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, N ≤ n →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafMod O₀) n).obj X)) :
    X ⟶ ((derivedTensorRight.{d} I).obj X)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧
declarations.comment:
the canonical map ω(K₀) : K₀ ⟶ (K₀ ⊗^L I)[2], on an object with bounded above
cohomology

declarations.name: Deformation.ComplexLift.tensorOmegaObj_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DIU, naturality of `ω`.** For every map `ψ : K₀ ⟶ L₀` in `D⁻(O₀)` the square

`ω(L₀) ∘ ψ = (ψ ⊗^L I)[2] ∘ ω(K₀)`

commutes.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorOmegaObj_natural (hf : Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective f) (S : SquareZeroIdeal f I)
    {X Y : DerivedCategory (SheafMod O₀)}
    (hX : ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, N ≤ n →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafMod O₀) n).obj X))
    (hY : ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, N ≤ n →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafMod O₀) n).obj Y))
    (ψ : X ⟶ Y) :
    ψ ≫ tensorOmegaObj.{v, u, w, d} hf S Y hY =
      tensorOmegaObj.{v, u, w, d} hf S X hX ≫
        (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (SheafMod O₀)) (2 : ℤ)).map
          ((derivedTensorRight.{d} I).map ψ)
declarations.comment: naturality of ω, on objects with bounded above cohomology

declarations.name: Deformation.ComplexLift.tensorOmegaMinus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DIU.** Let `f : O ⟶ O₀` be a surjection of sheaves of commutative rings on a site
whose kernel is an ideal sheaf `I` of square zero (`S`). For every object `K₀` of `D⁻(O₀)` there
is a canonical map

`ω(K₀) : K₀ ⟶ (K₀ ⊗^L_{O₀} I)[2]`

in `D(O₀)`, where `- ⊗^L_{O₀} I` is `Deformation.ComplexLift.derivedTensorRight I`. On a complex
representing `K₀` it is the curvature `d ∘ d` of the lifted differential of a bounded above flat
lift; its naturality is `Deformation.ComplexLift.tensorOmegaMinus_natural`.
declarations.comment: the canonical map ω(K₀) : K₀ ⟶ (K₀ ⊗^L I)[2] for every K₀ in D⁻(O₀)

declarations.name: Deformation.ComplexLift.tensorOmegaMinus_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DIU, naturality of `ω`.** For every map `ψ : K₀ ⟶ L₀` in `D⁻(O₀)` the square

`ω(L₀) ∘ ψ = (ψ ⊗^L I)[2] ∘ ω(K₀)`

in `D(O₀)` commutes.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorOmegaMinus_natural (hf : Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective f) (S : SquareZeroIdeal f I)
    {K₀ L₀ : DerivedCategory.Minus (SheafMod O₀)} (ψ : K₀.obj ⟶ L₀.obj) :
    ψ ≫ tensorOmegaMinus.{v, u, w, d} hf S L₀ =
      tensorOmegaMinus.{v, u, w, d} hf S K₀ ≫
        (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (SheafMod O₀)) (2 : ℤ)).map
          ((derivedTensorRight.{d} I).map ψ)
declarations.comment: naturality of ω along every map K₀ ⟶ L₀ in D⁻(O₀)

declarations.name: Deformation.ComplexLift.emb_coherence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DIU, coherence of the kernel identifications.** A morphism of flat lifts carries
the identification of the ideal part of the source to that of the target. This is the hypothesis
`hemb` of `Deformation.ComplexLift.obstructionMap_natural` and of
`Deformation.ComplexLift.obstructionMap_eq_of_hom`, and it holds for *every* pair of
identifications, because both are normalized by the same pure-tensor formula
`Deformation.ComplexLift.IdealKernel.emb_tmul`.
declarations.statement:
theorem emb_coherence (hf : Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective f)
    {L : FlatLift f K₀} {M : FlatLift f L₀} {φ : K₀ ⟶ L₀} (h : FlatLiftHom L M φ)
    (TL : IdealKernel S L) (TM : IdealKernel S M) (n : ℤ) :
    (restrict f).map (((idealTensorFunctor O₀ I).map h.red).f n) ≫ TM.emb n =
