            (ModuleCat.{u} (Localization.AtPrime (q.under R))) 0).obj
              (ModuleCat.of (Localization.AtPrime (q.under R))
                (q.under R).ResidueField))))) :
    HasTorAmplitude derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars
        ((algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime q)).comp
          (algebraMap R A))).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((totalDerivedExtensionScalars
          (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime q))).functor.obj K))
      (a - (d : ℤ)) b

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDual_of_isHomotopyColimit_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DJI.** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space, let `(Kₙ)` be a system of **perfect**
objects of `D(O_X)` and let `K = hocolim Kₙ`. Then for every object `E` of `D(O_X)`

`RSheafHom(K, E) = R lim (E ⊗^L_{O_X} Kₙ^∨)`.

The source uses the perfectness of the `Kₙ` to invoke the third assertion of Stacks 08DQ, which
is `isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfect`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDual_of_isHomotopyColimit_of_isPerfect
    (F : ℕ ⥤ DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    (E : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    (hperf : ∀ n : ℕ, (ringedSite Rc).IsPerfect (F.obj n))
    {K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)} (hK : IsHomotopyColimit F K) :
    IsDerivedLimit (tensorDerivedDualSystem Rc F E)
      (((derivedSheafHom Rc).flip.obj E).obj (op K))
declarations.comment: the whole tag: for a system of perfect objects `Kₙ` of `D(O_X)` with `K = hocolim Kₙ` and every `E` in `D(O_X)`, the identity `RSheafHom(K, E) = R lim (E ⊗^L_{O_X} Kₙ^∨)`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.hasTorAmplitudeCanonical_derivedModuleFiber_canonical
declarations.doc:
If an object `E` of `D(O)` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` for the derived tensor product of the
ringed site, then for every point `Φ` of the site its derived stalk `E_Φ` has Tor amplitude in
`[a, b]` as an object of `D(O_Φ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitudeCanonical_derivedModuleFiber_canonical
    (E : RingedSite.DerivedModules.{u, w, w, d} Y) (a b : ℤ)
    (hamp : HasTorAmplitude
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct.{u, w, d} Y) E a b)
    (Φ : Y.J.Point.{w}) :
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{d}
        (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.commRingSheafToRingSheaf.{w, u, w} Y.O)) := hd
    StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonical
      ((Φ.presheafFiber (A := CommRingCat.{w})).obj Y.O.obj)
      ((Stacks.derivedModuleFiber Φ Y.O).obj E) a b
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.hasTorAmplitude_canonical_of_forall_derivedModuleFiber
declarations.doc:
On a ringed site whose underlying site has a conservative family of points, an object `E`
of `D(O)` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` for the derived tensor product of the site as soon as its
derived stalk at every point of the site does.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_canonical_of_forall_derivedModuleFiber
    (E : RingedSite.DerivedModules.{u, w, w, d} Y) (a b : ℤ)
    (hY : Y.J.HasConservativeFamily.{w})
    (hE : ∀ Φ : Y.J.Point.{w},
      letI : HasDerivedCategory.{d}
          (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.commRingSheafToRingSheaf.{w, u, w} Y.O)) := hd
      StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonical
        ((Φ.presheafFiber (A := CommRingCat.{w})).obj Y.O.obj)
        ((Stacks.derivedModuleFiber Φ Y.O).obj E) a b) :
    HasTorAmplitude (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct.{u, w, d} Y) E a b
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineDerivedPushforward_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DJK.** Derived direct image under a morphism of affine schemes
preserves quasi-coherent cohomology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineDerivedPushforward_isQuasicoherent
    (R S : CommRingCat.{u}) (φ : R ⟶ S)
    (Rf : DerivedCategory (Spec S).Modules ⥤ DerivedCategory (Spec R).Modules)
    (α : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Spec.map φ)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ Rf)
    [Rf.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (Spec S).Modules (.up ℤ))]
    (K : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory (Spec S)) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec R).ringCatSheaf)
      (Rf.obj K.obj)
declarations.comment: pushforward route

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineDerivedPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DJK.** The affine associated-sheaf/derived-pushforward square
commutes naturally: derived direct image corresponds to restriction of scalars.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def affineDerivedPushforwardIso
    (R S : CommRingCat.{u}) (φ : R ⟶ S)
    (Rf : DerivedCategory (Spec S).Modules ⥤ DerivedCategory (Spec R).Modules)
    (α : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Spec.map φ)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ Rf)
    [Rf.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (Spec S).Modules (.up ℤ))] :
    affineTildeQuasicoherent S ⋙ affineDerivedPushforwardQuasicoherent R S φ Rf α ≅
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ.hom).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ affineTildeQuasicoherent R
declarations.comment: commutativity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTildeCompDerivedQuasicoherentPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DJK.** Let `φ : R ⟶ S` and let `f = Spec φ : Spec S ⟶ Spec R`. Then the square
`D(S) ⟶ D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec S}) ⟶^{Rf_*} D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`,
`D(S) ⟶^{restriction of scalars} D(R) ⟶ D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`
commutes: derived direct image along a morphism of affine schemes corresponds, under derived
sheafification, to derived restriction of scalars.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTildeCompIso_of_comparisonSquare` with its hypothesis `hsq`
discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedQuasicoherentComparisonSquare`, the commuting square of
[Stacks, Tag 08D7]. It is also the first assertion of [Stacks, Tag 0A9F].

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.SupportedGeneration.exists_dga_equivalence_quasiCoherentSupported
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DJL].** *"Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let
`T ⊂ X` be a closed subset such that `X ∖ T` is quasi-compact. The analogue of Theorem 09M5 holds
for `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)`."* That is: there is a differential graded algebra `(E, d)` with only a
finite number of nonzero cohomology groups `H^i(E)` such that `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` is equivalent to
`D(E, d)`. The derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules is taken at an arbitrary model `h`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dga_equivalence_quasiCoherentSupported (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hTc : IsCompact (Tᶜ : Set X))
    [h : HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)] :
    ∃ E : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{0, u} ℤ, {i : ℤ | Nontrivial (E.Cohomology i)}.Finite ∧
      Nonempty (@Stacks.Duality.QuasiCoherentSupportedDerivedCategory X T h ≌
        DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory.{0, u, u} E)

declarations.name: Stacks.PseudoCoherentHocolim.isPseudoCoherent_iff_exists_perfect_hocolim
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DJN].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let `K` be an
object of `D(𝒪_X)`. The following are equivalent:
1. `K` is pseudo-coherent;
2. `K = hocolim Kₙ` where each `Kₙ` is perfect and `τ_{≥ -n} Kₙ ⟶ τ_{≥ -n} K` is an
   isomorphism for all `n`.

Here `K = hocolim Kₙ` is `CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.IsHomotopyColimitWith F K c` (Definition
090Z, recording the coprojections `cₙ : Kₙ ⟶ K`), the map `τ_{≥ -n} Kₙ ⟶ τ_{≥ -n} K` is the
truncation of the coprojection `cₙ`, and the derived category is an arbitrary model of `D(𝒪_X)`.
The system is indexed by `n = 0, 1, 2, …`, as in Definition 090Z; a system `K₁ ⟶ K₂ ⟶ ⋯` indexed
from `1` as in the source's proof is the case `Kₙ ↦ Kₙ₊₁`, which satisfies the condition at `n`
because it does at `n + 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_iff_exists_perfect_hocolim [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) :
    @RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent X.toRingedSpace h K ↔
      ∃ (F : ℕ ⥤ DerivedCategory X.Modules) (_ : HasCoproduct F.obj) (c : ∀ n, F.obj n ⟶ K),
        (∀ n, @Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect X.toRingedSpace h (F.obj n)) ∧
        IsHomotopyColimitWith F K c ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE (-(n : ℤ))).map (c n))

declarations.name: Stacks.PseudoCoherentHocolim.isPseudoCoherent_iff_exists_supported_perfect_hocolim
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DJP].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let `T ⊆ X` be
a closed subset with `X \ T` quasi-compact and let `K ∈ D(𝒪_X)` be supported on `T`. Then `K` is
pseudo-coherent if and only if `K = hocolim Kₙ` for a system `F` of perfect objects `Kₙ`, each
supported on `T`, such that `τ_{≥ -n} Kₙ ⟶ τ_{≥ -n} K` is an isomorphism for every `n`; here
`c n : Kₙ ⟶ K` are the coprojections of the homotopy colimit. The derived category is an
arbitrary model of `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_iff_exists_supported_perfect_hocolim (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [h : HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules]
    (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact Tᶜ) (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : @Stacks.Cohomology.PushforwardRestriction.CohomologySupportedOn _ X.ringCatSheaf h T K) :
    @RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent X.toRingedSpace h K ↔
      ∃ (F : ℕ ⥤ DerivedCategory X.Modules) (_ : HasCoproduct F.obj) (c : ∀ n, F.obj n ⟶ K),
        (∀ n, @Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect X.toRingedSpace h (F.obj n)) ∧
        (∀ n, @Stacks.Cohomology.PushforwardRestriction.CohomologySupportedOn _ X.ringCatSheaf h
          T (F.obj n)) ∧
        IsHomotopyColimitWith F K c ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE (-(n : ℤ))).map (c n))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectPushforward.isPerfect_derivedPushforward_derivedTensorProductFunctor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DJQ].** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme and `f : X ⟶ S` a morphism of schemes
which is locally of finite type. Let `E` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` and let `𝒢` be a bounded
complex of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, flat over `S`, with support proper over `S`
(`Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectPushforward.FlatProperSupportComplex`). Then
`Rf_*(E ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} 𝒢)` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_S)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedPushforward_derivedTensorProductFunctor [IsNoetherian S]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (G : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace) ℤ)
    (hG : FlatProperSupportComplex f G) :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard
      (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.Modules X.toRingedSpace.sheaf)
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (OXMod.{u, u} S.toRingedSpace)
    ∀ E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace),
      RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E →
        RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := S.toRingedSpace)
          ((derivedPushforwardOX f).obj
            (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj E).obj
              (DerivedCategory.Q.obj G)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectInternalHomPushforward.isPerfect_derivedPushforward_derivedSheafHom_of_flatProperSupport
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DJR].**  Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme, `f : X ⟶ S` a morphism locally of
finite type, `E` a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` and `𝒢` a bounded complex of coherent
`𝒪_X`-modules, flat over `S`, with support proper over `S`.  Then `Rf_*RSheafHom(E, 𝒢)` is a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_S)`, with `Rf_*` the derived direct image
`Stacks.Cohomology.ProperSupportPerfection.derivedPushforwardOX f`.

The source's proof: `E^∨` is perfect and `RSheafHom(E, 𝒢) ≅ E^∨ ⊗^L 𝒢` by [Stacks, Tag 08DQ]
(`derivedSheafHomObjIsoDualTensor`), and [Stacks, Tag 0DJQ] applies to `(E^∨, 𝒢)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedPushforward_derivedSheafHom_of_flatProperSupport [IsNoetherian S]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace))
    (G : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace) ℤ)
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) (hG : FlatProperSupportComplex f G) :
    RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := S.toRingedSpace)
      ((derivedPushforwardOX f).obj (derivedSheafHomObj (X := X) E G))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeExtCanonical.exists_baseChange_relativeExt_iso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DJS]: formation of the complex `L` of [Stacks, Tag 08IF] (B) is compatible
with base change.** Let `S` be Noetherian, `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite type,
`E ∈ D^-_{Coh}(𝒪_X)` and `𝒢` a bounded complex of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, flat over `S`, with
support proper over `S`, and let `L` be the pseudo-coherent complex of (B). For every cartesian
square of schemes with `g' : X' ⟶ X`, `f' : X' ⟶ S'`, `g : S' ⟶ S` there are isomorphisms

`Ext^i_{𝒪_{S'}}(Lg^*L, ℱ') ≅ Ext^i_{𝒪_{X'}}(L(g')^*E, (g')^*𝒢 ⊗_{𝒪_{X'}} (f')^*ℱ')`

for quasi-coherent `ℱ'` on `S'`, with `(g')^*𝒢` the ordinary termwise pullback of `𝒢`, which are
functorial in `ℱ'` and compatible with the boundary maps of short exact sequences. They are
canonical: they are the ones induced by an identification
`Hom(Lg^*L, N) ≃ Hom(L(g')^*E, L(f')^*N ⊗^L (g')^*𝒢)` natural in `N ∈ D^+_{QCoh}(𝒪_{S'})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_baseChange_relativeExt_iso :
    ∃ β : ∀ (i : ℤ) (F' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S'.toRingedSpace)),
        F'.IsQuasicoherent →
        (baseExtGroup (baseChangedRepresentative f E hE G hG g) F' i ≃+
          relativeExtGroup f'
            ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackTensor.pullbackComplex g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj G)
            (baseChangedSource E g') F' i),
      (∀ (i : ℤ) (F F' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S'.toRingedSpace))
          (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (hF' : F'.IsQuasicoherent) (v : F ⟶ F')
          (z : baseExtGroup (baseChangedRepresentative f E hE G hG g) F i),
        β i F' hF' (baseExtMap _ i v z) =
          relativeExtMap f'
            ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackTensor.pullbackComplex g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj G)
            (baseChangedSource E g') i v (β i F hF z)) ∧
      (∀ (A : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S'.toRingedSpace)))
          (hA : A.ShortExact) (h₁ : A.X₁.IsQuasicoherent) (h₃ : A.X₃.IsQuasicoherent)
          (n m : ℤ) (h : 1 + n = m)
          (z : baseExtGroup (baseChangedRepresentative f E hE G hG g) A.X₃ n),
        β m A.X₁ h₁ (baseExtBoundaryMap _ hA n m h z) =
          relativeExtBoundaryMap (baseChangedSource E g')
            (isBoundedFlatOver_total_pullback hsq hG) hA n m h (β n A.X₃ h₃ z)) ∧
      ∃ θ : ShiftedHom.NaturalHomEquiv (𝟭 (DStd S'))
          (pullbackTensorDerivedFunctor (isBoundedFlatOver_total_pullback hsq hG))
          (baseChangedRepresentative f E hE G hG g)
          (baseChangedSource E g') (plusQCohDerived S'),
        ∀ (i : ℤ) (F' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S'.toRingedSpace))
          (hF' : F'.IsQuasicoherent),
          β i F' hF' = extIsoOfIdentification (isBoundedFlatOver_total_pullback hsq hG)
            (θ.toIdentification (plusQCohDerived_biprod S')) i F' hF'
declarations.comment: base change

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeExtCanonical.exists_iso_pseudoCoherentRepresentative
declarations.doc:
**The pseudo-coherent complex `L` representing relative `Ext` is canonical.**
Let `S` be Noetherian, `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite type, `E ∈ D^-_{Coh}(𝒪_X)` and `𝒢` a bounded
complex of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, flat over `S`, with support proper over `S`; let `L` be the
pseudo-coherent complex `pseudoCoherentRepresentative f E hE G hG`, with its identification
`θ_N : Hom(L, N) ≃ Hom(E, Lf^*N ⊗^L 𝒢)`, natural in `N ∈ D^+_{QCoh}(𝒪_S)`, and the
isomorphisms `Ext^i_{𝒪_S}(L, ℱ) ≅ Ext^i_{𝒪_X}(E, 𝒢 ⊗ f^*ℱ)` it induces. Then these are
functorial in quasi-coherent `ℱ` and compatible with boundary maps, and for every `L'` with
quasi-coherent cohomology and every identification
`θ'_N : Hom(L', N) ≃ Hom(E, Lf^*N ⊗^L 𝒢)` natural in `N ∈ D^+_{QCoh}(𝒪_S)` there is an
isomorphism `φ : L' ≅ L` with `θ'(φ ∘ x) = θ(x)` for all such `N` and `x : L ⟶ N`; in particular
`φ` carries the `Ext`-isomorphisms induced by `θ'` to those of `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_pseudoCoherentRepresentative (E : DStd X) (hE : IsBoundedAboveCoherent E)
    (G : CochainComplex (TModules X.toRingedSpace) ℤ)
    (hG : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectPushforward.FlatProperSupportComplex f G) :
    IsPseudoCoherentObject (pseudoCoherentRepresentative f E hE G hG) ∧
    (∀ (i : ℤ) (F F' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace))
        (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (hF' : F'.IsQuasicoherent) (v : F ⟶ F')
        (z : baseExtGroup (pseudoCoherentRepresentative f E hE G hG) F i),
      extIsoOfIdentification (isBoundedFlatOver_of_flatProperSupportComplex hG)
          ((pseudoCoherentRepresentativeHomEquiv f E hE G hG).toIdentification
            (plusQCohDerived_biprod S)) i F' hF'
          (baseExtMap (pseudoCoherentRepresentative f E hE G hG) i v z) =
        relativeExtMap f G E i v
          (extIsoOfIdentification (isBoundedFlatOver_of_flatProperSupportComplex hG)
            ((pseudoCoherentRepresentativeHomEquiv f E hE G hG).toIdentification
              (plusQCohDerived_biprod S)) i F hF z)) ∧
    (∀ (A : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace)))
        (hA : A.ShortExact) (h₁ : A.X₁.IsQuasicoherent) (h₃ : A.X₃.IsQuasicoherent)
        (n m : ℤ) (h : 1 + n = m)
        (z : baseExtGroup (pseudoCoherentRepresentative f E hE G hG) A.X₃ n),
      extIsoOfIdentification (isBoundedFlatOver_of_flatProperSupportComplex hG)
          ((pseudoCoherentRepresentativeHomEquiv f E hE G hG).toIdentification
            (plusQCohDerived_biprod S)) m A.X₁ h₁
          (baseExtBoundaryMap (pseudoCoherentRepresentative f E hE G hG) hA n m h z) =
        relativeExtBoundaryMap E (isBoundedFlatOver_of_flatProperSupportComplex hG) hA n m h
          (extIsoOfIdentification (isBoundedFlatOver_of_flatProperSupportComplex hG)
            ((pseudoCoherentRepresentativeHomEquiv f E hE G hG).toIdentification
              (plusQCohDerived_biprod S)) n A.X₃ h₃ z)) ∧
    ∀ (L' : DStd S) (_ : qcohDerived S L')
      (θ' : ShiftedHom.NaturalHomEquiv (𝟭 (DStd S))
        (pullbackTensorDerivedFunctor (isBoundedFlatOver_of_flatProperSupportComplex hG)) L' E
        (plusQCohDerived S)),
      ∃ φ : L' ≅ pseudoCoherentRepresentative f E hE G hG,
        (∀ (N : DStd S) (hN : plusQCohDerived S N)
            (x : pseudoCoherentRepresentative f E hE G hG ⟶ N),
          θ'.equiv N hN (φ.hom ≫ x) =
            (pseudoCoherentRepresentativeHomEquiv f E hE G hG).equiv N hN x) ∧
        ∀ (i : ℤ) (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace))
          (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent)
          (z : baseExtGroup (pseudoCoherentRepresentative f E hE G hG) F i),
          extIsoOfIdentification (isBoundedFlatOver_of_flatProperSupportComplex hG)
              (θ'.toIdentification (plusQCohDerived_biprod S)) i F hF (φ.hom ≫ z) =
            extIsoOfIdentification (isBoundedFlatOver_of_flatProperSupportComplex hG)
              ((pseudoCoherentRepresentativeHomEquiv f E hE G hG).toIdentification
                (plusQCohDerived_biprod S)) i F hF z
declarations.comment: canonical

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativelyPerfectProperPushforward.isPerfect_derivedPushforward_and_isIso_derivedBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DJT].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes which is flat, proper and of
finite presentation, and let `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` be `S`-perfect. Then `Rf_*E` is a perfect object of
`D(𝒪_S)` and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change: for every cartesian square
`X' = X ×_S S'` the base change map `Lg^*Rf_*E ⟶ Rf'_*L(g')^*E` of [Stacks, Tag 08HY] is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedPushforward_and_isIso_derivedBaseChangeMap {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (E : DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace))
    (hE : f.IsPerfectRelativeTo
      (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily.{u + 1, u} _) E) :
    IsPerfect (X := S.toRingedSpace) ((derivedPushforwardModules f).obj E) ∧
      ∀ {X' S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
        (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g),
        IsIso (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeMap g'.toLRSHom.toShHom
          f'.toLRSHom.toShHom f.toLRSHom.toShHom g.toLRSHom.toShHom (comp_toShHom_of_comm sq.w)
          E)
declarations.comment: f flat, proper and locally of finite presentation (finite presentation, as IsProper gives quasi-compact and quasi-separated) over an arbitrary base, E S-perfect: Rf_*E is perfect, and for every cartesian square X' = X ×_S S' the base change map Lg^*Rf_*E → Rf'_*L(g')^*E of Tag 08HY is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDerivedHomDual.exists_isPseudoCoherent_pushforward_sheafHom_iso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DJU].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and `E, K ∈ D(𝒪_X)`. Assume
`S` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, `f` is proper, flat and of finite presentation, `E` is
`S`-perfect and `K` is pseudo-coherent. Then there is a pseudo-coherent `L ∈ D(𝒪_S)` with

`Rf_* R𝓗om(K, E) ≅ R𝓗om(L, 𝒪_S)`,

and the same holds after arbitrary base change: for every cartesian square
`g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g` with `g : S' ⟶ S`,

`Rf'_* R𝓗om(L(g')^*K, L(g')^*E) ≅ R𝓗om(Lg^*L, 𝒪_{S'})`.

The derived categories are read at the standard model `CategoryTheory.HasDerivedCategory.standard`
(`DStd`), at which the derived direct image `pushStd`, the derived pullback `pullStd`, the derived
internal Hom `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom` and the structure sheaf in degree zero
`unitObj` are taken; "of finite presentation" is `LocallyOfFinitePresentation` together with the
quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness that properness contains. `L = hocolim Lₙ` for the
duals `Lₙ = (Rf_* R𝓗om(Kₙ, E))^∨` of an approximation `K = hocolim Kₙ` by perfect objects; see
`exists_construction_isPseudoCoherent`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPseudoCoherent_pushforward_sheafHom_iso [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    [IsProper f] [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (E K : DStd X) (hE : IsRelPerfect f E)
    (hK : IsPseudoCoherentStd K) :
    ∃ L : DStd S, IsPseudoCoherentStd L ∧
      Nonempty ((pushStd f).obj (((derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op K)).obj E) ≅
        ((derivedSheafHom S.sheaf).obj (op L)).obj (unitObj S)) ∧
      ∀ {X' S' : Scheme.{u}} (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S), IsPullback g' f' f g →
        Nonempty ((pushStd f').obj (((derivedSheafHom X'.sheaf).obj
            (op ((pullStd g').obj K))).obj ((pullStd g').obj E)) ≅
          ((derivedSheafHom S'.sheaf).obj (op ((pullStd g).obj L))).obj (unitObj S'))

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isPseudoCoherent_of_derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Pseudo-coherence descends along a finite-order thickening of schemes.** Let `i : X ⟶ X'` be
a closed immersion whose kernel ideal sheaf is nilpotent and let `K'` be an object of `D(𝒪_{X'})`
such that `K = Li^*K'` is pseudo-coherent. Then `K'` is pseudo-coherent.

Pseudo-coherence of `K'` is a local condition on `X'`, so it is enough to produce it over an
affine open `U` of `X'`. Over the chart `Spec Γ(X', U)` the thickening becomes `Spec` of the
surjection `i.app U`, whose kernel is nilpotent because a power of the kernel ideal sheaf
vanishes; the hypothesis travels to that chart because derived pullback preserves
pseudo-coherence and the two ways around the square `Spec Γ(X', U) ← Spec Γ(X, i⁻¹U)` over `i`
agree. The affine case then applies, and its conclusion comes back to `U` along
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.isoSpec`, again by preservation of pseudo-coherence under derived
pullback, this time along the inverse.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_of_derivedPullback {X X' : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ X')
    (hi : IsFiniteOrderThickening i)
    (K' : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X'.toRingedSpace))
    (hK : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace)
      ((derivedPullback i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj K')) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X'.toRingedSpace) K'
declarations.comment: the whole statement, unconditionally: pseudo-coherence of K' in D(𝒪_{X'}) from pseudo-coherence of Li^*K', for a finite-order thickening i : X ⟶ X' of schemes, at the standard derived category

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isQuasicoherent_homology_of_isPseudoCoherent_derivedPullback_specMap
declarations.doc:
**The quasi-coherence half of [Stacks, Tag 0DJX] in the affine case.** Let `f : R ⟶ S` be a
surjection of commutative rings with nilpotent kernel, so that `i = Spec f` is a finite-order
thickening, and let `A` be an object of `D(𝒪_{Spec R})` whose derived pullback `Li^*A` is
pseudo-coherent. Then every cohomology sheaf of `A` is quasi-coherent, that is, `A` lies in
`D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`.

This is the first paragraph of the source's proof. The dévissage is on the kernel ideal
`I = ker f`: writing `P` for the property of an `R`-module `N` that `Ñ[0] ⊗ᴸ_{𝒪_{Spec R}} A` has
quasi-coherent cohomology, `Stacks.Thickenings.prop_of_isNilpotent_of_smul_eq_bot` reduces `P` for
every module — in particular for `R` itself, where the unit of the derived tensor product
identifies `𝒪_{Spec R}[0] ⊗ᴸ A` with `A` — to `P` for a module annihilated by `I`.

*The inductive step.* `P` is stable under extensions: a short exact sequence of `R`-modules
becomes a short exact sequence of `𝒪_{Spec R}`-modules, `M ↦ M̃` being exact
(`AlgebraicGeometry.tilde.preservesFiniteLimits`), hence a distinguished triangle
(`CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.singleTriangle_distinguished`); the derived tensor
product is exact in its left variable, so tensoring with `A` keeps the triangle distinguished;
and the quasi-coherent modules form a weak Serre subcategory ([Stacks, Tag 01LA]), so the middle
vertex of a distinguished triangle whose outer vertices lie in `D_QCoh` lies in `D_QCoh`.

*The base case.* A module `N` annihilated by `I` is the restriction of scalars of an `S`-module
`M` (`Stacks.Thickenings.exists_restrictScalars_iso_of_smul_eq_bot`), and then
`Ñ ≅ i_*(M̃)` (`Stacks.Descent.restrictScalarsCompTildeIso`). The projection formula for the
closed embedding `i`, in the form
`exists_iso_derivedPushforward_derivedTensor_obj`, produces `D` in `D(𝒪_{Spec S})` with
`i_*(M̃)[0] ⊗ᴸ_{𝒪_{Spec R}} A ≅ Ri_*D` and `D ≅ M̃[0] ⊗ᴸ_{𝒪_{Spec S}} Li^*A`; the second
factor of the latter is in `D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec S})` by [Stacks, Tag 08E5], the first because `M̃` is
quasi-coherent, so `D` is by [Stacks, Tag 08DX] in the form
`isQuasicoherent_homology_specDerivedTensor`, and `Ri_*D` is by [Stacks, Tag 08D5].

Note that `i_* = Ri_*` here, which is `derivedPushforwardQIsoOfIsClosedEmbedding`, and that no
identification of the isomorphism with the canonical projection-formula morphism of
[Stacks, Tag 0B53] is needed: only membership in `D_QCoh` is transported.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherent_homology_of_isPseudoCoherent_derivedPullback_specMap
    (hf : Function.Surjective f.hom) (hnil : IsNilpotent (RingHom.ker f.hom))
    (A : DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} (Spec R).toRingedSpace))
    (hA : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := (Spec S).toRingedSpace)
      ((derivedPullback (Spec.map f).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj A)) :
    ∀ n : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Spec R).Modules n).obj A).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the quasi-coherence of the cohomology, in the affine case

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isPseudoCoherent_of_isPullback_of_isFiniteOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
**The pseudo-coherence conjunct of Stacks 0DJY.** In a cartesian diagram of schemes with
`i : X ⟶ X'`, `f : X ⟶ Y`, `f' : X' ⟶ Y'` and `j : Y ⟶ Y'`, with `j` a finite-order thickening,
an object `E'` of `D(𝒪_{X'})` whose derived pullback `Li^*E'` is pseudo-coherent is itself
pseudo-coherent.

A base change of a finite-order thickening is a finite-order thickening (Stacks 09ZU), so `i` is
one, and the conclusion is Stacks 0DJX. Neither flatness nor local finite presentation of `f'` is
used, and the family of derived tensor products plays no role, so neither appears.

This is the first of the two conjuncts of the conclusion of Stacks 0DJY. The second, locally
finite Tor dimension over `f'^{-1}𝒪_{Y'}`, is not proved here; its local content is
`Stacks.Thickenings.hasTorAmplitudeCanonical_derivedStalk_of_isPullback` above, and what is
missing between the two is recorded in the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherent_of_isPullback_of_isFiniteOrderThickening
    {X X' Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ X') (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (j : Y ⟶ Y')
    (hpb : IsPullback i f f' j) (hj : IsFiniteOrderThickening j)
    (E' : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X'.toRingedSpace))
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace)
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E')) :
    RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X'.toRingedSpace) E'
declarations.comment: the pseudo-coherence conjunct of the conclusion; the Tor-dimension conjunct is not proved — see the implementation notes of this module

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.isRelativelyPerfect_of_isPullback_of_isFiniteOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DJY at the canonical derived tensor products.** Consider a cartesian diagram of
schemes with `i : X ⟶ X'`, `f : X ⟶ Y`, `f' : X' ⟶ Y'` and `j : Y ⟶ Y'`, in which `f'` is flat and
locally of finite presentation and `j` is a finite-order thickening. Let `E'` be an object of
`D(𝒪_{X'})`. If `E = Li^*E'` is `Y`-perfect, then `E'` is `Y'`-perfect, relative perfectness being
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsRelativelyPerfect` — Stacks 0DI0 read at the canonical derived
tensor products — on both sides.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRelativelyPerfect_of_isPullback_of_isFiniteOrderThickening
    {X X' Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} {i : X ⟶ X'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {j : Y ⟶ Y'}
    (hpb : IsPullback i f f' j) (hj : IsFiniteOrderThickening j)
    [Flat f'] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f']
    (E' : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X'.toRingedSpace)) :
    haveI : Flat f := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @Flat) hpb inferInstance
    haveI : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f :=
      MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @LocallyOfFinitePresentation) hpb inferInstance
    f.IsRelativelyPerfect
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
          i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E') →
      f'.IsRelativelyPerfect E'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_finset_affineOpens_mvPolynomial_surjective_chartHom_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**The covering step of Stacks 0DJZ.** Let `R` be a ring and let `f : X ⟶ Spec R` be
universally closed and locally of finite type. Then finitely many affine opens cover `X`, and over
each the sections are a quotient of a polynomial algebra `R[x_1, …, x_d]` in finitely many
variables, compatibly with the structure map that `f` induces.

The source's proof of Stacks 0DJZ opens with this: *choose a finite affine open covering
`X = U_1 ∪ … ∪ U_n`; for each `i` we can choose a closed immersion `U_i → 𝐀^{d_i}_S`*. For an
affine `U_i`, giving a closed immersion into `𝐀^{d_i}_S` over `S` is the same as giving a
surjection `R[x_1, …, x_{d_i}] ⟶ Γ(X, U_i)` of `R`-algebras, and the surjection is the form the
fibrewise criterion of Stacks 0DJH consumes, so it is the form exported here.

Quasi-compactness of `X` comes from universal closedness of `f`: the import
`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.UniversallyClosed` carries an instance making a universally
closed morphism quasi-compact, and `Spec R` is quasi-compact, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace` applies. Properness is not asked
for; universal closedness and local finite type are all the source's proof of this step uses, and
they are also the hypotheses under which the sibling module
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Perfect.RelativelyPerfectJacobsonSpecialization` proves the
specialization step.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finset_affineOpens_mvPolynomial_surjective_chartHom_of_universallyClosed
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [UniversallyClosed f] :
    ∃ s : Finset X.affineOpens, (⨆ V ∈ s, (V : X.Opens)) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ V ∈ s, ∃ (d : ℕ) (ψ : MvPolynomial (Fin d) R →+* Γ(X, V.1)),
        Function.Surjective ψ ∧ ψ.comp MvPolynomial.C = chartHom f V.1
declarations.comment: the covering step with which the proof opens: for `f : X ⟶ Spec R` universally closed and locally of finite type, finitely many affine opens cover `X` and the sections over each are a quotient of a polynomial algebra over `R` in finitely many variables

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPerfectRelativeTo_of_isPerfectRelativeTo_closedFibre_of_genuine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DJZ.** Let `R` be a ring and `I` an ideal contained in its Jacobson radical; set
`S = Spec R` and `S₀ = Spec (R/I)`. Let `f : X ⟶ S` be proper, flat and locally of finite
presentation and let `X₀ = S₀ ×_S X`. Let `E` be a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)`. If the
derived restriction `E₀` of `E` to `X₀` is `S₀`-perfect, then `E` is `S`-perfect.

Relative perfectness is read at families of certified derived tensor products on the open
subspaces of the inverse-image ringed spaces, pinned to the tensor product of sheaves of modules,
which is the tensor product of the source's definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectRelativeTo_of_isPerfectRelativeTo_closedFibre_of_genuine [IsProper f] [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (hI : I ≤ (⊥ : Ideal R).jacobson)
    (D : ∀ U : TopologicalSpace.Opens
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).toRingedSpace f.base).carrier,
      RingedSpace.CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.{u + 1, u}
        ((RingedSpace.inverseImage (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).toRingedSpace f.base).restrict
          U.isOpenEmbedding))
    (hD : IsGenuineRelativeTensorFamily f D)
    (D₀ : ∀ U : TopologicalSpace.Opens
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage (Spec (CommRingCat.of (R ⧸ I))).toRingedSpace
          (closedFibreToBase f I).base).carrier,
      RingedSpace.CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.{u + 1, u}
        ((RingedSpace.inverseImage (Spec (CommRingCat.of (R ⧸ I))).toRingedSpace
          (closedFibreToBase f I).base).restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))
    (hD₀ : IsGenuineRelativeTensorFamily (closedFibreToBase f I) D₀)
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace))
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E)
    (hE₀ : (closedFibreToBase f I).IsPerfectRelativeTo D₀
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        (closedFibreToTotal f I).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E)) :
    f.IsPerfectRelativeTo D E

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical_of_closedFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DJZ at the canonical derived tensor products.** Let `R` be a ring and `I` an ideal
contained in its Jacobson radical; set `S = Spec R` and `S₀ = Spec (R/I)`. Let `f : X ⟶ S` be
proper, flat and locally of finite presentation and let `X₀ = S₀ ×_S X`. Let `E` be a
pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)`. If the derived restriction `E₀` of `E` to `X₀` is
`S₀`-perfect, then `E` is `S`-perfect, relative perfectness being read at the canonical derived
tensor products on both sides.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectRelativeTo_canonical_of_closedFibre [IsProper f] [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (hI : I ≤ (⊥ : Ideal R).jacobson)
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace))
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E)
    (hE₀ : (closedFibreToBase f I).IsPerfectRelativeTo
      (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage (Spec (CommRingCat.of (R ⧸ I))).toRingedSpace
          (closedFibreToBase f I).base))
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        (closedFibreToTotal f I).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E)) :
    f.IsPerfectRelativeTo
      (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).toRingedSpace f.base)) E

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_specializes_mem_range_pullback_snd_quotientMk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DJZ, the specialization step.** Let `I` be an ideal of `R` contained in the
Jacobson radical, let `f : X ⟶ Spec R` be universally closed and let
`X₀ = Spec (R/I) ×_{Spec R} X`. Then every point of `X` specializes to a point lying in the
image of `X₀ ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_specializes_mem_range_pullback_snd_quotientMk
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
    [UniversallyClosed f] {I : Ideal R} (hI : I ≤ (⊥ : Ideal R).jacobson) (x : X) :
    ∃ x₀ : X, x ⤳ x₀ ∧ x₀ ∈
      Set.range (pullback.snd (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) f).base
declarations.comment: the specialization step of the proof: universal closedness of `f` and `I` inside the Jacobson radical force every point of `X` to specialize to a point of `X₀ = Spec (R/I) ×_{Spec R} X`

declarations.name: torAmplitude_tfae_henselization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DK0, conditions (1)--(3).** The tor amplitude of a
complex over a henselization with extended residue field is the same whether
it is measured over the original local ring, the henselization with unchanged
residue field, or the extended-residue-field henselization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torAmplitude_tfae_henselization
    (Msh : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u uh ush w} Rsh) ℤ) (a b : ℤ) :
    List.TFAE
      [StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R Rsh)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj Msh)) a b,
       StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap Rh Rsh)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj Msh)) a b,
       StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
         (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Msh) a b]
declarations.comment: conditions (1)--(3)

declarations.name: torAmplitude_tfae_baseChange_henselization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DK0, conditions (1)--(5).** If the complex over the
extended-residue-field henselization is obtained from a complex over `Rh` by
base change, the preceding three conditions are also equivalent to tor
amplitude of the original complex over `R` and over `Rh`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torAmplitude_tfae_baseChange_henselization
    (Mh : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u uh ush w} Rh) ℤ) (a b : ℤ) :
    let Msh := (CochainComplex.extendScalarsLarge.{max u w, uh, ush}
      (algebraMap Rh Rsh)).obj Mh
    List.TFAE
      [StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R Rsh)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj Msh)) a b,
       StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap Rh Rsh)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj Msh)) a b,
       StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
         (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Msh) a b,
       StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R Rh)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj Mh)) a b,
       StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
         (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Mh) a b]
declarations.comment: conditions (1)--(5)

declarations.name: torAmplitude_tfae_iteratedBaseChange_henselization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DK0, conditions (1)--(6).** If the complex over `Rh`
is itself obtained by base change from `R`, all five conditions after base
change are equivalent to tor amplitude of the original complex over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torAmplitude_tfae_iteratedBaseChange_henselization
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u uh ush w} R) ℤ) (a b : ℤ) :
    let Mh := (CochainComplex.extendScalarsLarge.{max ush w, u, uh}
      (algebraMap R Rh)).obj M
    let Msh := (CochainComplex.extendScalarsLarge.{max u w, uh, ush}
      (algebraMap Rh Rsh)).obj Mh
    List.TFAE
      [StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R Rsh)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj Msh)) a b,
       StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap Rh Rsh)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj Msh)) a b,
       StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
         (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Msh) a b,
       StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R Rh)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj Mh)) a b,
       StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
         (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Mh) a b,
       StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeCanonicalLift
         (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) a b]
declarations.comment: conditions (1)--(6)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalkPushforwardIsoOfIsClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK1.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`
and let `z` be a geometric point of `Z` with image `x` in `X`. Then `(i_*F)_x = F_z` for every
sheaf of sets `F` on the small étale site of `Z`, naturally in `F`.
declarations.statement:
def stalkPushforwardIsoOfIsClosedImmersion (hci : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom)
    (z : GeometricPoint B S hS Z.1) :
    (smallToposMorphism B S hS i).pushforward ⋙
        sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) (Type (u + 1)) ⋙
          stalkSetFunctor (geometricPointMap i.hom z) ≅
      sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Z.1) (Type (u + 1)) ⋙
        stalkSetFunctor z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_geometricLifts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK3, finiteness of the index set.** A geometric point of the target of a finite
morphism of algebraic spaces has finitely many lifts, so the product in the statement is a
finite one.

The field spectrum of `y` is affine, so testing `π` against the section `y` produces an affine
scheme `V`, a finite morphism `V ⟶ Spec κ(y)` and a pullback square exhibiting `V` as the base
change of `X`. A lift of `y` therefore determines a section of that finite morphism, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.finite_lifts_of_isFinite` makes those finite in number; the assignment is
injective because the Yoneda embedding and the functor to schemes are faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_geometricLifts (hπ : IsFinite B S hS π.hom)
    (y : GeometricPoint B S hS Y.1) :
    Finite (GeometricLifts B S hS π y)
declarations.comment: the lifts `x₁, …, xₙ` of `y` are finite in number

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalkPushforwardToProduct
declarations.doc:
**The comparison map of Stacks 0DK3.** For a finite morphism `π : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic
spaces and a geometric point `y` of `Y`, the stalk at `y` of the direct image of a sheaf of
sets `F` on `X_étale` maps canonically to the product of the stalks of `F` over the lifts of
`y`, the component at a lift being
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalkPushforwardComponent`.

Stacks 0DK3 asserts that this map is bijective. That assertion is not proved for this map; it
is proved for the comparison map `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.presheafFiberCompToPi`
as `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_presheafFiberCompToPi_of_isFinite`. What is proved about
this map is its construction and its naturality in the sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def stalkPushforwardToProduct (y : GeometricPoint B S hS Y.1)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) (Type (u + 1))) :
    stalkSet y ((smallToposMorphism B S hS π).pushforward.obj F).obj →
      (∀ v : GeometricLifts B S hS π y,
        stalkSet (geometricLiftPoint B S hS π y v) F.obj)
declarations.comment: the canonical map `(π_*F)_y ⟶ ∏ᵢ F_{xᵢ}` over the lifts of `y`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalkPushforwardToProduct_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK3 is natural in the sheaf.** The comparison map commutes with the stalk maps
induced by a morphism of sheaves of sets on `X_étale`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkPushforwardToProduct_natural (y : GeometricPoint B S hS Y.1)
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) (Type (u + 1))} (α : F ⟶ G)
    (z : stalkSet y ((smallToposMorphism B S hS π).pushforward.obj F).obj)
    (v : GeometricLifts B S hS π y) :
    stalkPushforwardToProduct B S hS π y G
        (stalkSetMap y ((smallToposMorphism B S hS π).pushforward.map α).hom z) v =
      stalkSetMap (geometricLiftPoint B S hS π y v) α.hom
        (stalkPushforwardToProduct B S hS π y F z v)
declarations.comment: naturality of the comparison map in the sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.geometricLiftsEquivOfIsPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK3: the index set of the product is unchanged by base change.** For a
cartesian square

```
X' --i--> X
|         |
f'        π
↓         ↓
V --g---> Y
```

of algebraic spaces over `S` and a geometric point `v` of `V`, the lifts of `v` along `f'`
are the lifts along `π` of the image of `v` in `Y`, the bijection sending a lift to its image
under `i`.

This is the step with which the source's proof of Stacks 0DK3 begins, specialized to the
index set: it replaces `Y` by an étale neighbourhood `(V, v)` of `y` and `X` by `X ×_Y V`, and
the product over the lifts is the same product before and after exactly because of this
bijection. Nothing is assumed of the four arrows beyond the square being cartesian, so neither
finiteness of `π` nor étaleness of `g` is needed; the lifts of a geometric point are sections
over its field spectrum, and sections over one object of the site of a cartesian square of
algebraic spaces form a cartesian square of sets.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def geometricLiftsEquivOfIsPullback {X' V : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    {i : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ V} {g : V ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback i f' π g)
    (v : GeometricPoint B S hS V.1) :
    GeometricLifts B S hS f' v ≃ GeometricLifts B S hS π (geometricPointMap g.hom v)
declarations.comment: the lifts of `y` are the lifts of `v` along the base change of `π`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_presheafFiberCompToPi_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK3.** Let `π : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of algebraic spaces and `y` a geometric
point of `Y` with lifts `x₁, …, xₙ` in `X`. For every sheaf of sets `F` on `X_étale` the stalk of
the direct image `π_*F` at `y` is the product `∏ᵢ F_{xᵢ}`: the canonical map
`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.presheafFiberCompToPi`, sending the germ at `y` of a
section of `F` over a base-changed chart `V ×_Y X` to the family of its germs at the lifts, is
bijective.

The direct image is that along base change of étale charts (`π` is representable, being finite,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativelyRepresentable_hom_of_isFinite`),
which is the direct image of the morphism of small étale topoi of Stacks 03G2, part (3)
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleRingedToposHom_representable`); sheaves are valued in an
arbitrary universe containing `Type u`, the universe of the fibres of the points
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleSitePoint` at which stalks are taken.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_presheafFiberCompToPi_of_isFinite (hπ : IsFinite B S hS π.hom)
    (y : GeometricPoint B S hS Y.1)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) (Type (max u w))) :
    Function.Bijective (GrothendieckTopology.Point.presheafFiberCompToPi.{u, w, u, u + 1, u, u + 1}
      (smallBaseChange B S hS π (relativelyRepresentable_hom_of_isFinite B S hS π hπ))
      (etaleSitePoint B S hS Y.1 y Y.2)
      (fun v => etaleSitePoint B S hS X.1 (geometricLiftPoint B S hS π y v) X.2)
      (geometricFiberBaseChangeIso B S hS π (relativelyRepresentable_hom_of_isFinite B S hS π hπ) y)
      F.obj)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleRingedToposHomOfSharp
declarations.doc:
**The morphism of ringed topoi of Stacks 04G0**, `f : (Sh(Z_étale), ℬ) ⟶ (Sh(X_étale), 𝒜)`:
its underlying morphism of topoi is that of Stacks 03G2, part (3), and its structure map is `φ`.

No hypothesis on `i` enters, so this is equally the morphism of ringed topoi of Stacks 0DK4,
whose datum is the same `(i, φ)` in the same direction, with `i` finite instead of a closed
immersion.
declarations.comment: the morphism of ringed topoi determined by `π`, `𝒜`, `ℬ` and `φ`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tensorPushforwardMap
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map of Stacks 04G0**, `𝓕 ⊗_𝒜 f_*𝓖 ⟶ f_*(f^*𝓕 ⊗_ℬ 𝓖)`: the adjoint
transpose of `f^*(𝓕 ⊗_𝒜 f_*𝓖) = f^*𝓕 ⊗_ℬ f^*f_*𝓖 ⟶ f^*𝓕 ⊗_ℬ 𝓖`, built from the identity of
`f^*𝓕` and the adjunction map `f^*f_*𝓖 ⟶ 𝓖`.

No hypothesis on `i` enters, so this is equally the canonical map of Stacks 0DK4, which is the
adjoint transpose of the same comparison for the same datum with `i` finite.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorPushforwardMap (i : Z ⟶ X)
    {𝒜 : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) CommRingCat.{u}}
    {ℬ : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Z.1) CommRingCat.{u}}
    (φ : 𝒜 ⟶ (pushforwardCommRingFunctor.{u, u, u, u + 1, u, u + 1}
      (smallToposMorphismTypeU B S hS i)).obj ℬ)
    (𝓕 : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
      (smallEtaleRingedToposOfRings B S hS X 𝒜).O))
    (𝓖 : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
      (smallEtaleRingedToposOfRings B S hS Z ℬ).O)) :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u + 1, u, u, u, u} 𝒜).obj 𝓕).obj
      ((pushforwardModules (smallEtaleRingedToposHomOfSharp B S hS i φ)).obj 𝓖) ⟶
      (pushforwardModules (smallEtaleRingedToposHomOfSharp B S hS i φ)).obj
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u + 1, u, u, u, u} ℬ).obj
          (((smallEtaleRingedToposHomOfSharp B S hS i φ).pullbackModules).obj 𝓕)).obj 𝓖)
declarations.comment: the canonical map `𝓖 ⊗_ℬ f_*𝓕 ⟶ f_*(f^*𝓖 ⊗_𝒜 𝓕)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_tensorPushforwardMap_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK4.** Let `π : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, `𝒜` a
sheaf of rings on `X_étale`, `ℬ` a sheaf of rings on `Y_étale` and `φ : ℬ ⟶ π_*𝒜` a
homomorphism of sheaves of rings, with associated morphism of ringed topoi
`f = (π, φ) : (Sh(X_étale), 𝒜) ⟶ (Sh(Y_étale), ℬ)`. For every sheaf of `𝒜`-modules `𝓕` and every
sheaf of `ℬ`-modules `𝓖` the canonical map `𝓖 ⊗_ℬ f_*𝓕 ⟶ f_*(f^*𝓖 ⊗_𝒜 𝓕)` is an
isomorphism.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_derivedProjectionFormulaMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK5, the invertibility clause**, reduced to the derived adjunction of Stacks 07A6:
the canonical map `Rf_*M ⊗^L_{𝒪_D} K ⟶ Rf_*(M ⊗^L_{𝒪_C} Lf^*K)` of Equation 21.50.0.1 is an
isomorphism once the counit of `Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` is invertible at `M` and its unit is invertible at
`Rf_*M ⊗^L_{𝒪_D} K`.

Writing the canonical map through the unit, `projectionFormulaMap_eq_unit_comp`, it becomes

`Rf_*M ⊗^L K --η--> Rf_*Lf^*(Rf_*M ⊗^L K) --Rf_*(t)--> Rf_*(Lf^*Rf_*M ⊗^L Lf^*K)
   --Rf_*(ε ⊗ 1)--> Rf_*(M ⊗^L Lf^*K)`,

whose middle factor is the comparison of Stacks 07A4 and so invertible with no hypothesis, and
whose two outer factors are `hη` and `hε`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedProjectionFormulaMap
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)))
    (hε : IsIso ((derivedAdjunction f hmos).counit.app M))
    (hη : IsIso ((derivedAdjunction f hmos).unit.app
      ((Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.O)).obj
        ((derivedPushforward f).obj M, K)))) :
    IsIso (projectionFormulaMap f hmos M K)
declarations.comment: the invertibility clause, for a morphism of ringed topoi arising from a morphism of sites at a single universe, which is what the derived pullback tensor comparison of 07A4 requires — the small étale ringed topos of an algebraic space does not satisfy this — and given the counit of 07A6 at `M` and its unit at `Rf_*M ⊗^L K`, which is what finiteness of `π` is used for

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedProjectionFormulaIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK5** as an isomorphism `Rf_*M ⊗^L_{𝒪_D} K ≅ Rf_*(M ⊗^L_{𝒪_C} Lf^*K)`, with the
tensor factors in the order Equation 21.50.0.1 of Stacks 0B56 is written in; the forward map is
the canonical one, not an unspecified isomorphism of objects.
declarations.statement:
def derivedProjectionFormulaIso
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)))
    (hε : IsIso ((derivedAdjunction f hmos).counit.app M))
    (hη : IsIso ((derivedAdjunction f hmos).unit.app
      ((Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.O)).obj
        ((derivedPushforward f).obj M, K)))) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.O).obj ((derivedPushforward f).obj M)).obj K ≅
      (derivedPushforward f).obj
        (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.O).obj M).obj ((derivedPullback f).obj K))
declarations.comment: the isomorphism, for a morphism of ringed topoi arising from a morphism of sites at a single universe, which is what the derived pullback tensor comparison of 07A4 requires — the small étale ringed topos of an algebraic space does not satisfy this — and given the counit of 07A6 at `M` and its unit at `Rf_*M ⊗^L K`, which is what finiteness of `π` is used for; the tensor factors in the order of Equation 21.50.0.1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedProjectionFormulaIsoSourceOrder
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK5 in the order the source writes it**,
`K ⊗^L_{𝒪_D} Rf_*M ≅ Rf_*(Lf^*K ⊗^L_{𝒪_C} M)`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedProjectionFormulaIso` read through the commutativity
constraint of the derived tensor product (Stacks 0FPT) on each side: on `D(𝒪_D)` to transpose the
source, and inside `Rf_*` on `D(𝒪_C)` to transpose the target. No hypothesis is added.
declarations.statement:
def derivedProjectionFormulaIsoSourceOrder
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)))
    (hε : IsIso ((derivedAdjunction f hmos).counit.app M))
    (hη : IsIso ((derivedAdjunction f hmos).unit.app
      ((Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.O)).obj
        ((derivedPushforward f).obj M, K)))) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.O).obj K).obj ((derivedPushforward f).obj M) ≅
      (derivedPushforward f).obj
        (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.O).obj ((derivedPullback f).obj K)).obj M)
declarations.comment: the isomorphism in the source's order of tensor factors, for a morphism of ringed topoi arising from a morphism of sites at a single universe, which is what the derived pullback tensor comparison of 07A4 requires — the small étale ringed topos of an algebraic space does not satisfy this — and given the counit of 07A6 at `M` and its unit at `Rf_*M ⊗^L K`, which is what finiteness of `π` is used for

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_derivedTensorPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK5.** Let `π : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, `𝒜` a
sheaf of rings on `X_étale`, `ℬ` a sheaf of rings on `Y_étale` and `φ : ℬ ⟶ π_*𝒜` a homomorphism
of sheaves of rings, with associated morphism of ringed topoi
`f = (π, φ) : (Sh(X_étale), 𝒜) ⟶ (Sh(Y_étale), ℬ)`. Then for every `K ∈ D(ℬ)` and `M ∈ D(𝒜)`

`K ⊗^L_ℬ Rf_*M ≅ Rf_*(Lf^*K ⊗^L_𝒜 M)` in `D(ℬ)`.

`K` is represented by a K-flat complex with flat terms (Stacks 06YS) and `M` by any complex;
on such representatives the isomorphism is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedTensorPushforwardIsoOfKFlat`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_derivedTensorPushforwardIso (hπ : IsFinite B S hS π.hom)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf ℬ)))
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf 𝒜))) :
    Nonempty (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor
        (smallEtaleRingedToposOfRings B S hS Y ℬ).toRingedSite).obj K).obj
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPushforward.derivedPushforward
          (X := smallEtaleRingedToposOfRings B S hS X 𝒜)
          (Y := smallEtaleRingedToposOfRings B S hS Y ℬ)
          (ringedToposHomOfSharp B S hS π φ)).obj M) ≅
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPushforward.derivedPushforward
          (X := smallEtaleRingedToposOfRings B S hS X 𝒜)
          (Y := smallEtaleRingedToposOfRings B S hS Y ℬ)
          (ringedToposHomOfSharp B S hS π φ)).obj
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor
          (smallEtaleRingedToposOfRings B S hS X 𝒜).toRingedSite).obj
            ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedPullback
              (ringedToposHomOfSharp B S hS π φ)).obj K)).obj M))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.holds_of_affine_of_cechLocal
declarations.doc:
A Čech-local property of objects of the big fppf site over `X` can be
checked on affine objects flat and locally of finite presentation over `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem holds_of_affine_of_cechLocal
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (T : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSpaceSite S) (X : T.Spaces)
    (P : Over X → Prop)
    (hcech : ∀ (E : Covering (Over X)),
      AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSpaceOver.IsCovering T X E →
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.2.I₀)
        (c : WidePullbackCone (fun k : Fin (n + 1) => E.2.f (i k))),
        IsLimit c → P c.pt) → P E.1)
    (haffine : ∀ U : Over X,
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAffineSpace T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem U.left.1 →
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlat T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem U.hom.hom →
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem
        U.hom.hom → P U) :
    P (Over.mk (𝟙 X))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_relativeDerivedAssociatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK7, part (2).**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes and let `E` be an object
of `D(f⁻¹𝒪_Y)`.  Then `E` locally has finite Tor dimension if and only if `ε^*E` locally has
finite Tor dimension as an object of `D(ε⁻¹f⁻¹𝒪_Y)`, in the sense of Stacks 08FZ (3), for any
families of derived tensor products on the slices of the two sites.

Both conditions are read at the points of `X`.  An open covering of `X` with an interval on each
member gives, on any object `W` of the small étale site, the covering by the objects mapping into
one of the members, which is the pullback to `W` of the image of the open covering, a covering
because the inclusion of the small Zariski site is cover-preserving.  An étale covering of `X`
with an interval on each member gives the open covering of `X` by the images of the members,
open because the members are étale over `X`, every point of an image having its geometric point
lift to the member.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_relativeDerivedAssociatedModule
    (TU : ∀ U : (Scheme.Hom.inverseImageRingedSite f).C,
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u, u, u, d}
        ((Scheme.Hom.inverseImageRingedSite f).over U))
    (TW : ∀ W : (relativeRingedTopos B X hX f).toRingedSite.C,
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u + 1, u, u, e}
        ((relativeRingedTopos B X hX f).toRingedSite.over W))
    (E : RingedSite.DerivedModules.{u, u, u, d} (Scheme.Hom.inverseImageRingedSite f)) :
    LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension TU E ↔
      LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension TW ((relativeDerivedAssociatedModule B X hX f).obj E)
declarations.comment: part (2), with `ε⁻¹f⁻¹𝒪_Y` for `f_small⁻¹𝒪_{Y_étale}`; see the implementation notes of the module of part (1). The form with `f_small⁻¹𝒪_{Y_étale}` itself is, in `AlgebraicGeometry.Space`, `locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_derivedScalarRestriction_iff_representedZariskiDerivedPullback`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.hasTorAmplitude_relativeDerivedAssociatedModule_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK7, part (1).**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes and let `E` be an
object of `D(f⁻¹𝒪_Y)`.  Then `E` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` if and only if `ε^*E` has Tor
amplitude in `[a, b]` as an object of `D(ε⁻¹f⁻¹𝒪_Y)`.

Both sides are read at the stalks by Stacks 0DJJ: on the small Zariski site of `X` at the points
of `X`, a conservative family, and on the small étale site at the geometric points of `X` at the
points of `X`, a conservative family too
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isConservativeFamilyOfPoints_geometricSitePoints`).  At the point `x` the
two stalks agree, by Stacks 05V5 for `ε`
(`hasTorAmplitudeCanonical_derivedModuleFiber_relativeDerivedAssociatedModule_iff`).
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_relativeDerivedAssociatedModule_iff
    (E : RingedSite.DerivedModules.{u, u, u, d} (Scheme.Hom.inverseImageRingedSite f))
    (a b : ℤ) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.HasTorAmplitude T E a b ↔
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.HasTorAmplitude T'
        ((relativeDerivedAssociatedModule B X hX f).obj E) a b
declarations.comment: part (1), with `ε⁻¹f⁻¹𝒪_Y` for `f_small⁻¹𝒪_{Y_étale}`; see the implementation notes. The form with `f_small⁻¹𝒪_{Y_étale}` itself is, in `AlgebraicGeometry.Space`, `hasTorAmplitude_derivedScalarRestriction_iff_representedZariskiDerivedPullback`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_derivedScalarRestriction_iff_representedZariskiDerivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK7, part (2).**  Let `g₀ : X ⟶ Y` be the morphism of schemes underlying a
morphism `g` of the big fppf site and `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)`.  Then `E` read in `D(g₀⁻¹𝒪_Y)` locally has
finite Tor dimension if and only if `ε^*E` read in `D(g_{small}⁻¹𝒪_{Y_étale})` locally has
finite Tor dimension, for any family of derived tensor products on the slices.

As in part (1), `g_{small}⁻¹𝒪_{Y_étale}` is the inverse image of the structure sheaf of
`yoneda.obj T'` on the small étale site of `yoneda.obj T`, which is that of `X` by Stacks 04M0.
Both conditions are read at the points: an open cover of `X` with a Tor-amplitude interval on
each member gives the étale covers by the charts mapping into the members, and an étale cover of
the identity chart gives the open cover of `X` by the images of its members.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyHasFiniteTorDimension_derivedScalarRestriction_iff_representedZariskiDerivedPullback
    (Tfam : ∀ U : (inverseImageRingedSite B S hS (representedSpaceMap B S hS g)).C,
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct
        ((inverseImageRingedSite B S hS (representedSpaceMap B S hS g)).over U))
    (E : DerivedCategory (representedSchemeRepresentedZariskiRingedToposHom B S hS T).Modules) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage
          (representedSchemeRepresentedZariskiRingedToposHom B S hS T').toRingedSpace
          ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g).base)
        ((Scheme.Hom.derivedScalarRestriction ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g)).obj E) ↔
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.LocallyHasFiniteTorDimension Tfam
        ((derivedScalarRestriction B S hS (representedSpaceMap B S hS g)).obj
          ((representedZariskiDerivedPullback B S hS T).obj E))
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTorAmplitude_derivedScalarRestriction_iff_representedZariskiDerivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK7, part (1).**  Let `g₀ : X ⟶ Y` be the morphism of schemes underlying a
morphism `g` of the big fppf site, `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` and `ε^*E` its pullback to the small étale site.
Then `E` read in `D(g₀⁻¹𝒪_Y)` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` if and only if `ε^*E` read in
`D(g_{small}⁻¹𝒪_{Y_étale})` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`.

The small étale site of `X` is the small étale site of the algebraic space `yoneda.obj T`
(Stacks 04M0), on which `g_{small}⁻¹𝒪_{Y_étale}` is the inverse image of the structure sheaf of
`yoneda.obj T'` along `yoneda.map g` — the sheaf the source names.  An earlier form used
`ε⁻¹g₀⁻¹𝒪_Y` instead; identifying the two needs `g₀ ∘ ε_X = ε_Y ∘ g_{small}` and Stacks 070S, so
that form was not the statement of the source.  The proof is the source's, at the stalks.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_derivedScalarRestriction_iff_representedZariskiDerivedPullback
    (Tet : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct
      (inverseImageRingedSite B S hS (representedSpaceMap B S hS g)))
    (E : DerivedCategory (representedSchemeRepresentedZariskiRingedToposHom B S hS T).Modules)
    (a b : ℤ) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude
        (RingedSpace.inverseImage
          (representedSchemeRepresentedZariskiRingedToposHom B S hS T').toRingedSpace
          ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g).base)
        ((Scheme.Hom.derivedScalarRestriction ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g)).obj E) a b ↔
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.HasTorAmplitude Tet
        ((derivedScalarRestriction B S hS (representedSpaceMap B S hS g)).obj
          ((representedZariskiDerivedPullback B S hS T).obj E)) a b
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_differentialGradedAlgebra_equivalence_of_supported
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK8.** *Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
algebraic space over `S` and let `T ⊆ |X|` be a closed subset such that `|X| ∖ T` is
quasi-compact. Then there exists a differential graded algebra `(E, d)` with only a finite number
of nonzero cohomology groups `H^i(E)` such that `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` is equivalent to `D(E, d)`.*

This is the analogue of Stacks 09MC for `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)`, the full subcategory
`(AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedSupportedOn X T).FullSubcategory` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`
of the objects whose cohomology sheaves are supported on `T`; for `T = |X|` it is Stacks 09MC.
`E` is the endomorphism differential graded algebra of a K-injective complex representing a
perfect generator of `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` (Stacks 0AEC), formed on the equi-universe model of the
small étale ringed site of `X`, so that its carrier and `D(E, d)` live in the universe of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_differentialGradedAlgebra_equivalence_of_supported
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact Tᶜ) :
    ∃ E : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{0, u} ℤ, {i : ℤ | Nontrivial (E.Cohomology i)}.Finite ∧
      Nonempty ((quasicoherentDerivedSupportedOn X T).FullSubcategory ≌
        DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory.{0, u, u} E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_equivalence_derivedTensor_complexHomBimodule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DK9.** *Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over a ring
`R`, and let `K` and `L` be K-injective complexes of `𝒪_X`-modules corresponding to perfect
generators of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, with `A = Hom_{Comp^dg(𝒪_X)}(K, K)` and
`B = Hom_{Comp^dg(𝒪_X)}(L, L)`. Set `Ω = Hom_{Comp^dg(𝒪_X)}(K, L)` and
`Ω' = Hom_{Comp^dg(𝒪_X)}(L, K)`. Then `Ω` is a differential graded `B^opp ⊗_R A`-module and `Ω'`
a differential graded `A^opp ⊗_R B`-module, and the equivalence
`D(A, d) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(B, d)` is given by `- ⊗_A^𝐋 Ω'`, and its quasi-inverse by
`- ⊗_B^𝐋 Ω`.*

The bimodules are `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.complexHomBimodule`: `Ω' = Hom(L, K)` is a
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule A B` (left `A`-action by postcomposition, right `B`-action by
precomposition) and `Ω = Hom(K, L)` a `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule B A`. The equivalences
`D(A, d) ≌ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `D(B, d) ≌ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` are those of the proof of Stacks 09MC,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dgaQuasicoherentEquivalence`. The conclusion is an equivalence
`D(A, d) ≌ D(B, d)` whose functor is `- ⊗_A^𝐋 Ω'` and whose inverse is `- ⊗_B^𝐋 Ω`, isomorphic
to the composite `D(A, d) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(B, d)` and to its quasi-inverse: the situation of
Stacks 09ST.

`X` is over `R` through the ring map `ψ : R ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`; `K` and `L` are complexes on the
equi-universe model of the small étale site of `X`, corresponding through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modelEquivalence` to perfect generators `P` and `Q` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_equivalence_derivedTensor_complexHomBimodule
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (K L : CochainComplex (RingedSite.ModO.{u, u, u, u} (modelSite X)) ℤ)
    [(RingedSite.liftComplex.{u, u, u, u, u} (modelSite X) K).IsKInjective]
    [(RingedSite.liftComplex.{u, u, u, u, u} (modelSite X) L).IsKInjective]
    (P Q : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hP : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect P)
    (hQ : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect Q)
    (hgenP : ∀ E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2,
      IsZero E.obj ↔ ∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (P⟦n⟧ ⟶ E.obj))
    (hgenQ : ∀ E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2,
      IsZero E.obj ↔ ∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (Q⟦n⟧ ⟶ E.obj))
    (eP : (modelEquivalence X).inverse.obj
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (RingedSite.liftComplex.{u, u, u, u, u} (modelSite X) K) :
        DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (modelSite X).O))) ≅ P)
    (eQ : (modelEquivalence X).inverse.obj
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (RingedSite.liftComplex.{u, u, u, u, u} (modelSite X) L) :
        DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (modelSite X).O))) ≅ Q) :
    letI := modelLinear X ψ
    letI := modelScalarSections X ψ
    ∃ e : DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory.{u, u, u}
          (RingedSite.Rep.{u, u, u, u, u, u} (modelSite X) R K).algebra ≌
        DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory.{u, u, u}
          (RingedSite.Rep.{u, u, u, u, u, u} (modelSite X) R L).algebra,
      e.functor = DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor
          (RingedSite.complexHomBimodule.{u, u, u, u, u} (modelSite X) R K L) ∧
      e.inverse = DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor
          (RingedSite.complexHomBimodule.{u, u, u, u, u} (modelSite X) R L K) ∧
      Nonempty (e.functor ≅
        ((dgaQuasicoherentEquivalence X ψ K
            (isRelativelyCompactGenerator_model hqc hqs K P hP hgenP eP)).trans
          (dgaQuasicoherentEquivalence X ψ L
            (isRelativelyCompactGenerator_model hqc hqs L Q hQ hgenQ eQ)).symm).functor) ∧
      Nonempty (e.inverse ≅
        ((dgaQuasicoherentEquivalence X ψ K
            (isRelativelyCompactGenerator_model hqc hqs K P hP hgenP eP)).trans
          (dgaQuasicoherentEquivalence X ψ L
            (isRelativelyCompactGenerator_model hqc hqs L Q hQ hgenQ eQ)).symm).inverse)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPseudoCoherent_iff_exists_isHomotopyColimitWith
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DKB.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
algebraic space over `S` and let `K ∈ D(𝒪_X)`.  The following are equivalent:
1. `K` is pseudo-coherent;
2. `K = hocolim Kₙ` where `Kₙ` is perfect and `τ_{≥-n}Kₙ ⟶ τ_{≥-n}K` is an isomorphism for all
   `n`.

The model of `D(𝒪_X)` is arbitrary.  The system is `F : ℕ ⥤ D(𝒪_X)`, indexed from `0`, its
member `F.obj n` being the source's `K_{n+1}`; so the truncation condition at index `n` is in
degree `-(n + 1)`.  The maps `Kₙ ⟶ K` are the coprojections `c n` of the derived colimit
(`CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.IsHomotopyColimitWith`), whose direct sum `⊕ Kₙ` exists because
the `𝒪_X`-modules form a Grothendieck abelian category.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_iff_exists_isHomotopyColimitWith
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)]
    (K : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)) :
    haveI := hasColimitsOfShape_discrete_nat_derivedCategory_modules B S hS X hX
    (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X hX).IsPseudoCoherent K ↔
      ∃ (F : ℕ ⥤ DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)) (c : ∀ n, F.obj n ⟶ K),
        (∀ n, (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X hX).IsPerfect (F.obj n)) ∧
          (∀ n : ℕ,
            IsIso ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE (-((n : ℤ) + 1))).map (c n))) ∧
            IsHomotopyColimitWith F K c

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PerfectApproximation.isPseudoCoherent_iff_exists_isHomotopyColimitWith
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DKC].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let `T ⊆ X`
be a closed subset such that `X \ T` is quasi-compact, and let `K ∈ D(𝒪_X)` be supported on `T`.
The following are equivalent:
1. `K` is pseudo-coherent;
2. `K = hocolim Kₙ` where `Kₙ` is perfect, supported on `T`, and `τ_{≥-n}Kₙ ⟶ τ_{≥-n}K` is an
   isomorphism for all `n`.

The system is `F : ℕ ⥤ D(𝒪_X)`, indexed from `0`, its member `F.obj n` being the source's
`K_{n+1}`; so the truncation condition at index `n` is in degree `-(n + 1)`. The maps
`Kₙ ⟶ K` are the coprojections `c n` of the derived colimit
(`CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.IsHomotopyColimitWith`). The same statement is
[Stacks, Tag 0DJP].
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_iff_exists_isHomotopyColimitWith [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact Tᶜ)
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PushforwardRestriction.CohomologySupportedOn X.ringCatSheaf T K) :
    RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) K ↔
      ∃ (F : ℕ ⥤ DerivedCategory X.Modules) (c : ∀ n, F.obj n ⟶ K),
        (∀ n, IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) (F.obj n)) ∧
          (∀ n, Stacks.Cohomology.PushforwardRestriction.CohomologySupportedOn X.ringCatSheaf T
            (F.obj n)) ∧
            (∀ n : ℕ,
              IsIso ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE (-((n : ℤ) + 1))).map (c n))) ∧
              IsHomotopyColimitWith F K c

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTorAmplitude_derivedScalarRestriction_smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DKD (1).** Let `X' → X`, `Y' → Y` be a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over
`S` with `X` and `Y'` Tor independent over `Y`. If `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`
as a complex of `f⁻¹𝒪_Y`-modules, then `L(g')^*E` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` as a complex
of `f'⁻¹𝒪_{Y'}`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_derivedScalarRestriction_smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback
    (htor : TorIndependent X.2 Y'.2 Y.2 f.hom g.hom)
    (T : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct (inverseImageRingedSite B S hS f))
    (T' : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct (inverseImageRingedSite B S hS f'))
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)) (a b : ℤ)
    (hE : HasTorAmplitude T ((derivedScalarRestriction B S hS f).obj E) a b) :
    HasTorAmplitude T' ((derivedScalarRestriction B S hS f').obj
      ((smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback B S hS g').obj E)) a b
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_smallEtaleDerivedModulePullbackComparison_of_isFlatOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DKD (2).** For a cartesian square of algebraic spaces with `X` and `Y'` Tor
independent over `Y`, and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝒢` flat over `Y` (Stacks 05VV), the
canonical comparison `L(g')^*𝒢 ⟶ (g')^*𝒢` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleDerivedModulePullbackComparison_of_isFlatOver

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_smallEtaleDerivedModulePullbackComparison_of_ringedToposHom_isFlatOver
declarations.doc:

`𝒪_X`-module `𝒢` flat over `Y` — flat as an `f⁻¹𝒪_Y`-module, Stacks 08M5 — the canonical

    (hG : RingedToposHom.IsFlatOver (X := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X)
