declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPseudoCoherent_of_derivedPullback_of_isFiniteOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DL3.** Let `S` be a scheme and let `i : Z ⟶ X'` be a finite-order thickening of
algebraic spaces over `S`. Let `K'` be an object of `D(𝒪_{X'})` such that `K = Li^*K'` is
pseudo-coherent. Then `K'` is pseudo-coherent.

The thickening is the inclusion `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.subspaceInclusion` of a closed subspace
`Z` of `X'` which is a finite-order thickening (Stacks 05ZK), `Li^*` is the derived pullback of
Stacks 06YY along it, and pseudo-coherence is Stacks 08FT on the small étale ringed sites.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_of_derivedPullback_of_isFiniteOrderThickening
    {X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X'.1)
    (hZ : IsFiniteOrderThickening B S hS X' Z.1)
    (K' : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X'.1 X'.2))
    (hK :
      haveI := hasLeftDerivedFunctor_smallEtaleModulePullbackOnHomotopy B S hS
        (subspaceInclusion B S hS X' Z)
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Z.1.toFunctor Z.2.1).IsPseudoCoherent
        ((smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X' Z)).obj K')) :
    (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X'.1 X'.2).IsPseudoCoherent K'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPerfectRelativeToCanonical_of_pull_of_isThickeningHom
declarations.doc:
Consider a cartesian square
```
X --i--> X'
|f       |f'
v        v
Y --j--> Y'
```
of algebraic spaces over `S`. Assume `f'` is flat and locally of finite presentation and `j` is
a finite-order thickening: `j` is an isomorphism onto its range, which is a finite-order
thickening of `Y'` (Stacks 05ZK). Let `E' ∈ D(𝒪_{X'})`. If `E = Li^*E'` is `Y`-perfect
(Stacks 0DKN), then `E'` is `Y'`-perfect.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectRelativeToCanonical_of_pull_of_isThickeningHom
    {X X' Y Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {i : X ⟶ X'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {j : Y ⟶ Y'}
    (hpb : IsPullback i f f' j) (hj : IsThickeningHom B S hS j)
    (hjfin : IsFiniteOrderThickening B S hS Y' (Subfunctor.range j.hom))
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f'.hom) (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f'.hom)
    (E' : derivedModules B S hS X')
    (hE : IsPerfectRelativeToCanonical B S hS f
      ((isFlat_isStableUnderBaseChange B S hS).of_isPullback hpb hflat)
      ((isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_isStableUnderBaseChange B S hS).of_isPullback hpb
        hlfp)
      (((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackData B S hS).pull i).obj E')) :
    IsPerfectRelativeToCanonical B S hS f' hflat hlfp E'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativelyPerfect_of_isRelativelyPerfect_closedFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DL5.** Let `(R, I)` be a ring with an ideal contained in its Jacobson radical, let
`𝒮 = Spec R` and `𝒮₀ = Spec (R/I)`, and let `f : X ⟶ 𝒮` be a proper and flat morphism of
algebraic spaces, locally of finite presentation (hence of finite presentation, `f` being proper).
Let `X₀ = 𝒮₀ ×_𝒮 X`, with projections `i : X₀ ⟶ X` and `f₀ : X₀ ⟶ 𝒮₀`. If a pseudo-coherent object
`E` of `D(𝒪_X)` has `𝒮₀`-perfect derived restriction `Li^*E` to `X₀`, then `E` is `𝒮`-perfect.

On an affine étale chart `Spec A ⟶ X`, presented by `d` variables over `R`, `E` is `ε^*(P~)` for a
bounded above complex `P` of finite free `A`-modules, and `Li^*E` is `ε^*((P ⊗_R R/I)~)` on the
closed fibre of the chart. One interval `[a, b]` bounds the Tor amplitude of the geometric stalks
of `Li^*E` on the quasi-compact `X₀`, and then `[a - d, b]` bounds those of `E` over the stalks of
`f⁻¹𝒪_𝒮` (`hasTorAmplitudeCanonical_geometricStalk_of_closedFibre`); a uniform bound at the
geometric stalks gives locally finite Tor dimension (Stacks 0DJJ, 04K5).

`X₀` is the fibre product in the category of algebraic spaces; flatness and local finite
presentation of `f₀`, the preconditions of `𝒮₀`-perfectness (Stacks 0DKN), are those of `f` by base
change.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyPerfect_of_isRelativelyPerfect_closedFibre
    (hI : I ≤ (⊥ : Ideal R).jacobson) (i : X₀ ⟶ X)
    (hpb : IsPullback i f₀ f (representedSpaceMap B S hS (quotientSpecMap B S hS hR gR I hR₀)))
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS f.hom) (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f.hom)
    (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hE : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPseudoCoherent E)
    (hE₀ : haveI := hasLeftDerivedFunctor_smallEtaleModulePullbackOnHomotopy B S hS i
      IsRelativelyPerfect B S hS f₀ (isFlat_snd_of_isPullback B S hS hpb hflat)
        (isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_snd_of_isPullback B S hS hpb hlfp)
        ((smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback B S hS i).obj E)) :
    IsRelativelyPerfect B S hS f hflat hlfp E

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPerfectRelativeTo_of_isPerfectRelativeTo_closedFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DL5.** Let `(R, I)` be a ring with an ideal contained in its Jacobson radical, let
`𝒮 = Spec R` and `𝒮₀ = Spec (R/I)`, let `f : X ⟶ 𝒮` be a proper, flat, locally finitely
presented morphism of algebraic spaces and let `X₀ = 𝒮₀ ×_𝒮 X`. A pseudo-coherent object `E` of
`D(𝒪_X)` whose derived restriction to `X₀` is `𝒮₀`-perfect is `𝒮`-perfect.

The pseudo-coherence clause of the conclusion is the hypothesis on `E`. For the Tor clause,
properness makes `|X| → |𝒮|` closed and the ideal `I` lying in the Jacobson radical makes every
nonempty closed subset of `|𝒮|` meet `|𝒮₀|`, so every point of `|X|` specializes into the closed
fibre; from there the bound is `hTor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectRelativeTo_of_isPerfectRelativeTo_closedFibre (i : X₀ ⟶ X) (j : 𝒮₀ ⟶ 𝒮)
    [(smallEtaleModulePullbackOnHomotopy B S hS i).HasLeftDerivedFunctor
      (smallEtaleModuleQuasiIso B S hS X)]
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f.hom) (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hflat₀ : IsFlat B S hS f₀.hom) (hlfp₀ : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f₀.hom)
    (T : ∀ U : (inverseImageRingedSite B S hS f).C,
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u + 1, u, u, e}
        ((inverseImageRingedSite B S hS f).over U))
    (T₀ : ∀ U : (inverseImageRingedSite B S hS f₀).C,
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u + 1, u, u, e}
        ((inverseImageRingedSite B S hS f₀).over U))
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {I : Ideal R} (hI : I ≤ (⊥ : Ideal R).jacobson)
    (eR : points B S hS 𝒮.1 ≃ₜ PrimeSpectrum R)
    (hj : Set.range (pointsMap B S hS 𝒮₀.1 j.hom) =
      eR ⁻¹' PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set R))
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS f.hom) (_hpb : IsPullback i f₀ f j)
    (hTor : LocallyFiniteTorDimensionFromClosedFibre B S hS f f₀ i j hflat₀ hlfp₀ T T₀)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hE : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPseudoCoherent E)
    (hE₀ : IsPerfectRelativeTo B S hS f₀ hflat₀ hlfp₀ T₀
      ((smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback B S hS i).obj E)) :
    IsPerfectRelativeTo B S hS f hflat hlfp T E
declarations.comment: the pseudo-coherence clause and the specialization step; Tor clause carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedPushoutEssentialImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DL7.** Let `S` be a scheme and let
```
X  --i-->  X'
|          |
f          f'
v          v
Y  --j-->  Y'
```
be a pushout in the category of algebraic spaces over `S` as in Stacks 07VX, with `i` a
thickening and `f` affine. Then the essential image of the functor
`D(𝒪_{Y'}) ⥤ D(𝒪_Y) ×_{D(𝒪_X)} D(𝒪_{X'})`, `M' ↦ (Lj^* M', L(f')^* M', can)`, given by derived
pullback, contains every triple `(M, K', α)` with `M ∈ D(𝒪_Y)` and `K' ∈ D(𝒪_{X'})`
pseudo-coherent: for every isomorphism `α : Lf^* M ≅ Li^* K'` there are `M' ∈ D(𝒪_{Y'})` and
isomorphisms `a : Lj^* M' ≅ M` and `b : L(f')^* M' ≅ K'` with `Li^* b` equal to `α ∘ Lf^* a`
through the 2-cell `Lf^* Lj^* ≅ Li^* L(f')^*` (Stacks 0D6D). This holds at any models of the four
derived categories; the statement is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DerivedPushoutEssentialImage`.

The proof is the source's: the fibre `M'` of the glueing map
`Rj_* M ⊕ Rf'_* K' ⟶ Rj_* Rf_* Li^* K'`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedPushoutEssentialImage_of_derivedPushoutGlueingIsIso`), the
isomorphism step checked on the affine étale charts of `Y'`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedPushoutGlueingIsIso_of_onAffineChart`), where the base change
of the square is a represented affine square whose rings form a fibre product along a surjection
with nil kernel (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedPushoutEssentialImage_of_representedAffine`), and
on which the step is the ring-level statement
(`MilnorPatching.isIso_homEquiv_symm_of_isPullback_of_distinguished_glueingMap_derivedExtension`)
carried to the algebraic spaces along the derived associated-module functors
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pushoutGlueingIsIsoStepOnRepresentedAffine`).
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPushoutEssentialImage :
    DerivedPushoutEssentialImage.{w₁, w₂, w₃, w₄, u} B S hS

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SimplicialSpacesEtaleSite.negativeExt_eq_zero_and_exact_derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
Let `a : U → X` be an fppf hypercovering of an algebraic space and `K, E` objects of
`D_{QCoh}(𝒪_X)` with `Ext^i_{U_n}(La_n^*K, La_n^*E) = 0` for `i < 0` and all `n`. Then
(1) `Ext^i_X(K, E) = 0` for `i < 0`, and (2) the sequence
`0 ⟶ Hom_X(K, E) ⟶ Hom_{U_0}(La_0^*K, La_0^*E) ⟶ Hom_{U_1}(La_1^*K, La_1^*E)` is exact, where the
first map is `La_0^*` and the second the difference of the pullbacks along the two faces.
declarations.statement:
theorem negativeExt_eq_zero_and_exact_derivedPullback
    {K E : @DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
      (spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem X).O)) _ _
      (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)}
    (hK : (@DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB _ _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
          (spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem X).O))) K)
    (hE : (@DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB _ _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
          (spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem X).O))) E)
    (hvan : ∀ (n : SimplexCategory) (i : ℤ), i < 0 →
      ∀ g : (derivedPullback
          (X := spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem (U.obj (op n)))
          (Y := spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem X)
          (spacesEtaleRingedToposHom (a.app (op n)))).obj K ⟶
        ((derivedPullback (X := spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem (U.obj (op n)))
          (Y := spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem X)
          (spacesEtaleRingedToposHom (a.app (op n)))).obj E)⟦i⟧, g = 0) :
    (∀ (i : ℤ), i < 0 → ∀ g : K ⟶ E⟦i⟧, g = 0) ∧
      Function.Injective (fun g : K ⟶ E ↦
        (derivedPullback (X := spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem (U.obj (op ⦋0⦌)))
          (Y := spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem X)
          (spacesEtaleRingedToposHom (a.app (op ⦋0⦌)))).map g) ∧
      Function.Exact (fun g : K ⟶ E ↦
        (derivedPullback (X := spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem (U.obj (op ⦋0⦌)))
          (Y := spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem X)
          (spacesEtaleRingedToposHom (a.app (op ⦋0⦌)))).map g)
        (fun ψ ↦ augmentationFaceTransport a 0 ψ - augmentationFaceTransport a 1 ψ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SimplicialSpacesEtaleSite.exists_derivedPullback_degreeZero_iso_compatible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DLA: gluing quasi-coherent derived descent data along an fppf hypercovering.** Let
`a : U → X` be an fppf hypercovering of an algebraic space `X`, `K₀ ∈ D_{QCoh}(𝒪_{U_0})` and
`α : L(f_{δ¹₁})^* K₀ ≅ L(f_{δ¹₀})^* K₀` an isomorphism satisfying the cocycle condition (on `U_2`,
through the canonical identifications of the composite face maps). Set
`K_n = L(f_{τⁿₙ})^* K₀` with `τⁿₙ : ⦋0⦌ → ⦋n⦌, 0 ↦ n`, and assume `Ext^i(K_n, K_n) = 0` for
`i < 0`. Then there are `K ∈ D_{QCoh}(𝒪_X)` and an isomorphism `e : La_0^* K ≅ K₀` compatible with
`α`: `L(f_{δ¹₁})^* e ≫ α = θ₁ ≫ θ₀⁻¹ ≫ L(f_{δ¹₀})^* e`, where
`θ_i : L(f_{δ¹ᵢ})^* La_0^* ≅ La_1^*` are the canonical isomorphisms (`a_0 ∘ f_{δ¹ᵢ} = a_1`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedPullback_degreeZero_iso_compatible
    (h : IsHypercoveringAugmentation T.pretopologyBigFppfPretopology U a)
    (K₀ : @DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
      (spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem (U.obj (op ⦋0⦌))).O)) _ _
      (HasDerivedCategory.standard _))
    (hK₀ : @DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB _ _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
          (spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem (U.obj (op ⦋0⦌))).O)) K₀)
    (α : (derivedPullback (spacesEtaleRingedToposHom
        (U.map (SimplexCategory.δ (1 : Fin 2)).op))).obj K₀ ≅
      (derivedPullback (spacesEtaleRingedToposHom
        (U.map (SimplexCategory.δ (0 : Fin 2)).op))).obj K₀)
    (hα : SpacesEtaleDerivedCocycle U K₀ α)
    (hExt : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), i < 0 →
      ∀ g : (derivedPullback (spacesEtaleRingedToposHom
          (U.map (SimplexCategory.const ⦋0⦌ ⦋n⦌ (Fin.last n)).op))).obj K₀ ⟶
        (shiftFunctor (@DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u + 1}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            (spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem (U.obj (op ⦋n⦌))).O)) _ _
          (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)) i).obj
          ((derivedPullback (spacesEtaleRingedToposHom
            (U.map (SimplexCategory.const ⦋0⦌ ⦋n⦌ (Fin.last n)).op))).obj K₀), g = 0) :
    ∃ K : @DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem X).O)) _ _
        (HasDerivedCategory.standard _),
      @DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB _ _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            (spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem X).O)) K ∧
      ∃ e : (derivedPullback (X := spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem
          (U.obj (op ⦋0⦌))) (Y := spacesEtaleRingedTopos T.schemeSite S T.scheme_mem X)
          (spacesEtaleRingedToposHom (a.app (op ⦋0⦌)))).obj K ≅ K₀,
        (derivedPullback (spacesEtaleRingedToposHom (U.map (SimplexCategory.δ (1 : Fin 2)).op))).map
            e.hom ≫ α.hom =
          ((augmentationTransitionDerivedIso a (SimplexCategory.δ (1 : Fin 2))).hom.app K ≫
            (augmentationTransitionDerivedIso a (SimplexCategory.δ (0 : Fin 2))).inv.app K) ≫
            (derivedPullback (spacesEtaleRingedToposHom
              (U.map (SimplexCategory.δ (0 : Fin 2)).op))).map e.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_negativeExtLocus_and_vanishing_and_representable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DLC.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is proper,
flat and of finite presentation, and let `K`, `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` with `K` pseudo-coherent and `E`
`Y`-perfect (Stacks 0DKN). For a point `y : Spec(k) ⟶ Y` with values in a field write `K_y`, `E_y`
for the pullbacks to the fibre `X_y`.
1. There is an open `W ⊆ Y` characterized by: `y ∈ |W|` if and only if
   `Ext^i_{𝒪_{X_y}}(K_y, E_y) = 0` for `i < 0`
   (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsNegativeExtLocus`).
2. For such a `W` and every algebraic space `V` over `Y` whose morphism to `Y` factors through `W`,
   `Ext^i_{𝒪_{X_V}}(K_V, E_V) = 0` for `i < 0`, where `X_V` is the base change of `X` and `K_V`,
   `E_V` are the derived pullbacks of `K` and `E` to `X_V`.
3. For such a `W`, the functor `V ↦ Hom_{𝒪_{X_V}}(K_V, E_V)` on the schemes over `W` is
   representable by an algebraic space affine and of finite presentation over `W` (in particular
   it is a sheaf).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_negativeExtLocus_and_vanishing_and_representable
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hproper : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f.hom) (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (K E : derivedModules B S hS X) (hK : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPseudoCoherent K)
    (hE : IsPerfectRelativeToCanonical B S hS f hflat hfp.1 E) :
    (∃ W : OpenSubspaces B S hS Y.1, IsNegativeExtLocus f K E W) ∧
      (∀ W : OpenSubspaces B S hS Y.1, IsNegativeExtLocus f K E W →
        ∀ V : Over Y, (∃ g : V.left ⟶ openSubspaceAsSpace B S hS W,
            g ≫ openSubspaceImmersion B S hS W = V.hom) →
        ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 →
          Subsingleton (((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackData B S hS).pull (overProjection f V)).obj K ⟶
            (((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackData B S hS).pull (overProjection f V)).obj E)⟦i⟧)) ∧
      (∀ W : OpenSubspaces B S hS Y.1, IsNegativeExtLocus f K E W →
        IsAffineFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOver (openSubspaceAsSpace B S hS W)
          (relativeDerivedHomOverOpen f K E W))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.conditions_negativeSelfExt_selfHom_overBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DLD.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is proper,
flat and of finite presentation, and let `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)`. Assume that `E` is `Y`-perfect
(Stacks 0DKN) and that `Ext^i_{𝒪_{X_y}}(E_y, E_y) = 0` for `i < 0` at every point
`y : Spec(k) ⟶ Y` with values in a field, `E_y` the derived pullback to the fibre `X_y`. Then
* (a) both conditions hold for `X_V ⟶ V` and `E_V` after every base change `V ⟶ Y`;
* (b) `Ext^i_{𝒪_{X_V}}(E_V, E_V) = 0` for `i < 0` and every algebraic space `V` over `Y`;
* (c) `V ↦ Hom_{𝒪_{X_V}}(E_V, E_V)` is representable by an algebraic space affine and of finite
  presentation over `Y`.
Here `X_V` is the base change of `X` and `E_V` the derived pullback of `E` to `X_V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conditions_negativeSelfExt_selfHom_overBaseChange (E : derivedModules B S hS D.X)
    (h1 : IsPerfectRelativeToCanonical B S hS D.f D.flat D.finitePresentation.1 E)
    (h2 : HasNoNegativeFieldFibreExt D.f E) :
    (∀ V : Over D.Y,
      IsPerfectRelativeToCanonical B S hS (overInclusion D.f V) (D.overInclusion_isFlat V)
          (D.overInclusion_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation V)
          (((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackData B S hS).pull (overProjection D.f V)).obj E) ∧
        HasNoNegativeFieldFibreExt (overInclusion D.f V)
          (((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackData B S hS).pull (overProjection D.f V)).obj E)) ∧
      (∀ (V : Over D.Y) (i : ℤ), i < 0 →
        Subsingleton
          (((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackData B S hS).pull (overProjection D.f V)).obj E ⟶
            (((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackData B S hS).pull (overProjection D.f V)).obj E)⟦i⟧)) ∧
      IsAffineFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOver D.Y (relativeDerivedHom D.f E E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DLE, the standing data.**  A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S`
which is proper, flat and of finite presentation: the relative algebraic space whose relatively
perfect complexes the category `Complexes_{X/Y}` classifies.

It is the standing datum `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation` of Stacks 08KB, which
assumes only finite presentation, together with the two further hypotheses of Stacks 0DLE.
declarations.statement:
structure ComplexesSituation (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    extends CoherentSituation B S hS
declarations.comment:
the standing situation: a proper, flat, finitely presented morphism of algebraic
spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DLE, the objects.**  An object of `Complexes_{X/Y}`: a scheme `T` of the site over
`Y` together with an object of `D(𝒪_{X_T})` satisfying conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks
0DLD.
declarations.statement: structure ComplexesObject (D : ComplexesSituation B S hS)
declarations.comment: objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DLE, the morphisms.**  A morphism of `Complexes_{X/Y}`: a morphism `h : T ⟶ T'` of
test schemes over `Y` together with an isomorphism `L(X_h)^*E' ⟶ E` of `D(𝒪_{X_T})`.
declarations.statement: structure ComplexesHom {D : ComplexesSituation B S hS} (A A' : ComplexesObject D)
declarations.comment: morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.complexesCategory
declarations.doc:
**The category `Complexes_{X/Y}` of Stacks 0DLE.**  The category structure on the objects
whose hom-sets are `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesHom`, whose identity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesHom.id` and whose composition is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesHom.comp`.
declarations.statement: def complexesCategory : Category.{u + 1} (ComplexesObject D)
declarations.comment:
the category structure on the objects: the hom-sets are the
pairs (h, φ), with the identity and the composition the tag designates

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.complexesProjection
declarations.doc:
**The projection of `Complexes_{X/Y}` to the test schemes over `Y` of Stacks 0DLE**,
`(T, g, E) ↦ (T, g)`: it forgets the complex and keeps the base map of a morphism.
declarations.comment: the functor (T, g, E) ↦ (T, g) to the test schemes over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.complexesFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The functor `p : Complexes_{X/Y} ⥤ (Sch/S)_fppf` of Stacks 0DLE**, `(T, g, E) ↦ T`: the
projection to the test schemes over `Y` followed by forgetting the morphism to `Y`.
declarations.comment: the functor p : Complexes_{X/B} ⥤ (Sch/S)_fppf, (T, g, E) ↦ T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.isGroupoid_fiber_complexesFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The fibre categories of `p : Complexes_{X/Y} ⥤ (Sch/S)_fppf` are groupoids**, as Stacks
0DLE asserts.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGroupoid_fiber_complexesFunctor (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) :
    IsGroupoid ((complexesFunctor D).Fiber T)
declarations.comment: the fibre categories of p over the schemes T are groupoids

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.complexesCategory_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DLE in full.**  `Complexes_{X/Y}` is a category whose objects are the triples
`(T, g, E)` of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesObject` — a scheme `T` over `S`, a morphism
`g : T ⟶ Y` and an object `E` of `D(𝒪_{X_T})` satisfying conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks
0DLD — and whose morphisms are the pairs `(h, φ)` of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesHom`,
with the identity and the composition the tag designates; the rule `(T, g, E) ↦ T` is a functor
`p` to `(Sch/S)_fppf`, and its fibre categories are groupoids.

The conjuncts are: the hom-sets, the identity, the composition, the two clauses saying that `p`
is the designated rule, and that the fibre categories of `p` are groupoids.  That the objects
and the morphisms are the designated data is the definition of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesObject` and `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesHom`, and that
the category laws hold is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.complexesCategory`, whose
existence is asserted by the statement being about it.
declarations.statement:
theorem complexesCategory_spec :
    letI : Category.{u + 1} (ComplexesObject D) := complexesCategory D
    (∀ A A' : ComplexesObject D, (A ⟶ A') = ComplexesHom A A') ∧
      (∀ A : ComplexesObject D, (𝟙 A : ComplexesHom A A) = ComplexesHom.id A) ∧
      (∀ {A A' A'' : ComplexesObject D} (m : ComplexesHom A A') (n : ComplexesHom A' A''),
        ((m ≫ n : A ⟶ A'') : ComplexesHom A A'') = ComplexesHom.comp m n) ∧
      (∀ A : ComplexesObject D, (complexesFunctor D).obj A = A.T.left) ∧
      (∀ {A A' : ComplexesObject D} (m : ComplexesHom A A'),
        (complexesFunctor D).map (m : A ⟶ A') = m.base.left) ∧
      ∀ T : BigFppfOver B S hS, IsGroupoid ((complexesFunctor D).Fiber T)
declarations.comment:
the whole statement: the category Complexes_{X/B} of the triples (T, g, E) and the
pairs (h, φ), with the designated identity and composition, the functor p : (T, g, E) ↦ T to
(Sch/S)_fppf, and its fibre categories being groupoids

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.complexesFunctor_isFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DLF.**  In Situation 0DLE the functor `p : Complexes_{X/B} ⥤ (Sch/S)_fppf`,
`(T, g, E) ↦ T`, is fibred in groupoids: every morphism `h : T ⟶ T'` of schemes over `S` lifts
at every object `(T', g', E')`, to `(T, g' ∘ h, L(h')^*E') ⟶ (T', g', E')` with the identity as
comparison of complexes, and fill-ins exist and are unique.

The lift is an object because both conditions of Stacks 0DLD survive pullback
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.relativelyPerfectBaseChange` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.hasNoNegativeFibreExt_pull`); the fill-in is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.fillIn`.
declarations.statement:
theorem complexesFunctor_isFiberedInGroupoids :
    letI : Category.{u + 1} (ComplexesObject D) := complexesCategory D
    (complexesFunctor D).IsFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.comment:
the functor p : Complexes_{X/B} ⥤ (Sch/S)_fppf, (T, g, E) ↦ T, is fibred in
groupoids

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.complexes_hasRepresentableDiagonal_proved
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DLG.** In Situation 0DLE (`f : X ⟶ Y` proper, flat and of finite presentation),
the diagonal `Δ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 × 𝒳` of `𝒳 = Complexes_{X/Y}` is representable by algebraic spaces:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.complexes_hasRepresentableDiagonal` with Stacks 0DLC,
parts (1) and (3), discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem complexes_hasRepresentableDiagonal_proved :
    Stack.HasRepresentableDiagonal B S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.mk (complexesBasedCategory D)
        (complexesFunctor_isFiberedInGroupoids D))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.complexesFunctor_isStackInGroupoids_proved
declarations.doc:
In a `Complexes` situation `D` over `S`, the category `Complexes_{X/Y}` fibred in groupoids
over `(Sch/S)_fppf` is a stack in groupoids.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.complexesToBase
declarations.doc:
**The projection to the base.**  The rule `(T, g, E) ↦ (T, g)` which forgets the complex is
a 1-morphism `Complexes_{X/B} ⟶ 𝒮_B` of categories over the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement:
def complexesToBase (D : ComplexesSituation B S hS) :
    complexesBasedCategory D ⥤ᵇ baseBasedCategory D.Y
declarations.comment: the 1-morphism Complexes_{X/B} → 𝒮_B, (T, g, E) ↦ (T, g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.baseChangeSquare_isTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**The square

`Complexes_{X'/B'} ⟶ Complexes_{X/B}`, `𝒮_{B'} ⟶ 𝒮_B`

is a 2-fibre product.**  That is, `Complexes_{X'/B'}`, with the base-change functor and the
projection which forgets the complex, is a 2-fibre product of the projection
`Complexes_{X/B} ⟶ 𝒮_B` with the morphism `𝒮_{B'} ⟶ 𝒮_B` induced by `g : B' ⟶ B`.
declarations.statement:
def baseChangeSquare_isTwoFibreProduct (g : Y' ⟶ D.Y) :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.finiteDimensional_tangentSpace_infinitesimalAutomorphisms_complexes
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0DLE (`f : X ⟶ Y` proper, flat and of finite presentation, the `B` of the source
being `Y`), assume that `S` is locally Noetherian and `Y ⟶ S` is locally of finite presentation.
Let `k` be a field of finite type over `S`, presented as in Stacks Section 07T2 through an affine
open `Spec Λ ⊆ S` with `Λ → k` finite, and let `x₀` be an object of `𝒳 = Complexes_{X/Y}` over
`Spec k`. Then `𝒳` satisfies (RS), so that the predeformation category `𝓕_{𝒳,k,x₀}` is a
deformation category and the spaces of Stacks Section 07WY are defined, and the tangent space
`T𝓕_{𝒳,k,x₀}` (`Deformation.Artin.tangentSpaceModuleOfSatisfiesRS`) and the infinitesimal
automorphisms `Inf(𝓕_{𝒳,k,x₀})` (`Deformation.Artin.infinitesimalAutomorphismModuleOfSatisfiesRS`,
at every object over `k` and every choice of pushforwards) are finite dimensional over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_tangentSpace_infinitesimalAutomorphisms_complexes
    (D : ComplexesSituation B S hS) [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (hY : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (terminal.from D.Y.obj))
    {Λ k : Type u} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k] [Module.Finite Λ k]
    (iΛ : Spec (.of Λ) ⟶ S) (hiΛ : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion iΛ)
    (x₀ : ComplexesObject D)
    (hx₀ : (complexesFunctor D ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x₀ =
      Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ)) :
    SatisfiesRS B S hS (complexesFunctor D) (complexesFunctor_isFiberedInGroupoids D) ∧
      ∀ hRS : SatisfiesRS B S hS (complexesFunctor D) (complexesFunctor_isFiberedInGroupoids D),
        FiniteDimensional k (tangentSpaceModuleOfSatisfiesRS B S hS (complexesFunctor D)
            (complexesFunctor_isFiberedInGroupoids D) hRS iΛ x₀ hx₀
            (locallyOfFiniteType_specMap_comp_of_isOpenImmersion iΛ hiΛ)
            (quasiCompact_of_spec_field _)) ∧
          ∀ x P, FiniteDimensional k (infinitesimalAutomorphismModuleOfSatisfiesRS B S hS
            (complexesFunctor D) (complexesFunctor_isFiberedInGroupoids D) hRS iΛ x₀ hx₀
            (locallyOfFiniteType_specMap_comp_of_isOpenImmersion iΛ hiΛ)
            (quasiCompact_of_spec_field _) x P)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_flatLocus_of_isSurjectiveChart
declarations.doc:
For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces locally of finite presentation and a module
which is quasi-coherent and of finite type on the small étale site of `X`, the relative flat locus
is open in the point space of `X` as soon as the weakly associated points of the scheme of one
surjective étale chart of `Y` are locally finite there.

Condition (3) of the source asks that the weakly associated points of `Y` be locally finite in
`|Y|`; the source's proof reads it as local finiteness on a surjective étale scheme chart, which can
be stronger when `Y` is not decent.  With (3) on `|Y|` the statement is false:
`Stacks.Examples.NonOpenFlatLocusWeaklyAssociated.exists_not_isOpen_flatLocus`
exhibits a target with two weakly associated points over which the flat locus is not open.  The
chart reading is therefore the correction of the statement, recorded in `errata.md`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_flatLocus_of_isSurjectiveChart (f : X.1 ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hqc : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F)
    (V₀ : SmallEtale B S hS Y) (hV₀ : IsSurjectiveChart B S hS V₀)
    (h₀ : ∀ v : etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀,
      ∃ W : (etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀).Opens, v ∈ W ∧
        (Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints (etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀) ∩
          (W : Set (etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀))).Finite) :
    IsOpen (flatLocus B S hS X.2 f F)
declarations.comment: openness of the locus U, at the Stacks erratum: condition (3) of the source, local finiteness of the weakly associated points of Y in |Y|, is replaced by local finiteness of the weakly associated points of the scheme of one surjective etale chart of Y, which is how the source's proof reads it and which implies (3). The tag as published, with (3) on |Y|, is false, refuted (with a target which is not decent) by the theorem Stacks.Examples.NonOpenFlatLocusWeaklyAssociated.exists_not_isOpen_flatLocus of StacksFrontier/Examples/Flatness/NonOpenFlatLocusWeaklyAssociated.lean. Conditions (1) and (2) are the source's: f locally of finite presentation, the module quasi-coherent of finite type on the small etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenSubspace_flatLocusOpenSubspace_of_isSurjectiveChart
declarations.doc:
For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces locally of finite presentation and a module
which is quasi-coherent and of finite type on the small étale site of `X`, the relative flat locus
cuts out an open subspace of `X` as soon as the weakly associated points of the scheme of one
surjective étale chart of `Y` are locally finite there.

Condition (3) of the source asks that the weakly associated points of `Y` be locally finite in
`|Y|`; the source's proof reads it as local finiteness on a surjective étale scheme chart, which can
be stronger when `Y` is not decent.  With (3) on `|Y|` the statement is false:
`Stacks.Examples.NonOpenFlatLocusWeaklyAssociated.exists_not_isOpen_flatLocus`
exhibits a target with two weakly associated points over which the flat locus is not open.  The
chart reading is therefore the correction of the statement, recorded in `errata.md`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenSubspace_flatLocusOpenSubspace_of_isSurjectiveChart (f : X.1 ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hqc : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F)
    (V₀ : SmallEtale B S hS Y) (hV₀ : IsSurjectiveChart B S hS V₀)
    (h₀ : ∀ v : etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀,
      ∃ W : (etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀).Opens, v ∈ W ∧
        (Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints (etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀) ∩
          (W : Set (etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀))).Finite) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS (flatLocusOpenSubspace B S hS X.2 f F)
declarations.comment: the locus U cuts out an open subspace of X in the sense of Tag 03BZ, at the Stacks erratum: condition (3) of the source, local finiteness of the weakly associated points of Y in |Y|, is replaced by local finiteness of the weakly associated points of the scheme of one surjective etale chart of Y, which is how the source's proof reads it and which implies (3). The tag as published, with (3) on |Y|, is false, refuted (with a target which is not decent) by the theorem Stacks.Examples.NonOpenFlatLocusWeaklyAssociated.exists_not_isOpen_flatLocus of StacksFrontier/Examples/Flatness/NonOpenFlatLocusWeaklyAssociated.lean

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatLocus
declarations.doc:
The relative flat locus of a module on an algebraic space: the set of points `x` of the
source such that some commuting square of étale scheme charts through `x` witnesses flatness of
the restricted module over the target chart.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def flatLocus (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) : Set (points B S hS X)
declarations.comment: the locus U of the statement: the points of the source at which the module is flat over the target, which is Tag 05VV (1), i.e. clause (1) of Tag 05VU

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentationOnCharts_flatLocusRestrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DLR: `F|_U` is an `𝒪_U`-module of finite presentation.**  For a morphism of
algebraic spaces locally of finite presentation, a module quasi-coherent of finite type on the
small étale site and a target whose weakly associated points are locally finite on the scheme of
one surjective étale chart, the module `F|_U` on the open subspace
`U = {x ∈ |X| : F flat at x over Y}` is of finite presentation.

Conditions (1) and (2) are the source's own; condition (3), local finiteness of the weakly
associated points of `Y` in `|Y|`, is replaced by local finiteness on one *surjective* étale
scheme chart, as the source's proof reads it.  This is the correction of Stacks 0DLR recorded in
`errata.md`: with (3) on `|Y|` the statement is false,
`Stacks.Examples.NonOpenFlatLocusWeaklyAssociated.exists_not_isOpen_flatLocus`.
The every-chart reading the proof consumes is derived from it by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasLocallyFiniteWeaklyAssociatedPointsOnCharts_of_isSurjectiveChart`.

The conclusion is read on the étale scheme charts of `U`, as every property of a module on an
algebraic space is in this development.  The proof is the source's: the condition is étale local,
so it is enough to read it on one chart of `U` surjective on points, and such a chart may be
chosen to lie over a chart of `Y` (Tag 02X1), where the scheme-level theorem Stacks 05IK applies;
the passage back to every chart is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentation_restrictToChartScheme_of_isSurjective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentationOnCharts_flatLocusRestrict (f : Xs ⟶ Ys)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Xs.1 Xs.2) [hqc : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F) (V₀ : SmallEtale B S hS Ys.1)
    (hV₀ : IsSurjectiveChart B S hS V₀)
    (h₀ : ∀ v : etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀,
      ∃ W : (etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀).Opens, v ∈ W ∧
        (Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints (etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀) ∩
          (W : Set (etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀))).Finite) :
    IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS
      (flatLocusSpace B S hS f F
        (isOpenSubspace_flatLocusOpenSubspace_of_isSurjectiveChart B S hS Xs f.hom F hf hqc hft
          V₀ hV₀ h₀)).2
      (flatLocusRestrict B S hS f F
        (isOpenSubspace_flatLocusOpenSubspace_of_isSurjectiveChart B S hS Xs f.hom F hf hqc hft
          V₀ hV₀ h₀))
declarations.comment: F|_U is an O_U-module of finite presentation, for U the open subspace cut out by the flat locus, at the Stacks erratum: condition (3) of the source, local finiteness of the weakly associated points of Y in |Y|, is replaced by local finiteness of the weakly associated points of the scheme of one surjective etale chart of Y, which is how the source's proof reads it and which implies (3). The tag as published, with (3) on |Y|, is false, refuted (with a target which is not decent) by the theorem Stacks.Examples.NonOpenFlatLocusWeaklyAssociated.exists_not_isOpen_flatLocus of StacksFrontier/Examples/Flatness/NonOpenFlatLocusWeaklyAssociated.lean. The module is quasi-coherent of finite type on the small etale site; the conclusion is read on the etale scheme charts of U, as every property of a module on an algebraic space is in this development

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOver_flatLocusRestrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DLR: `F|_U` is flat over `Y`.**  For a morphism of algebraic spaces locally of
finite presentation, a module quasi-coherent of finite type on the small étale site and a target
whose weakly associated points are locally finite on the scheme of one surjective étale chart,
the module `F|_U` on the open subspace `U = {x ∈ |X| : F flat at x over Y}` is flat over `Y` along
the composite `U ⟶ X ⟶ Y`, in the sense of Tag 05VV.

Conditions (1) and (2) are the source's own; condition (3) is replaced by local finiteness of the
weakly associated points on one *surjective* étale scheme chart of the target, as the source's
proof reads it, which is the correction of Stacks 0DLR recorded in `errata.md` (with (3) on `|Y|`
the statement is false,
`Stacks.Examples.NonOpenFlatLocusWeaklyAssociated.exists_not_isOpen_flatLocus`).

On a commuting square of étale scheme charts of `U ⟶ Y`, the chart of `U` is a chart of `X` whose
points all lie in the relative flat locus, so the square witnesses flatness at each of them by
Stacks 05VU.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOver_flatLocusRestrict (f : Xs ⟶ Ys) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Xs.1 Xs.2)
    [hqc : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F) (V₀ : SmallEtale B S hS Ys.1)
    (hV₀ : IsSurjectiveChart B S hS V₀)
    (h₀ : ∀ v : etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀,
      ∃ W : (etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀).Opens, v ∈ W ∧
        (Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints (etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀) ∩
          (W : Set (etaleChartScheme B S hS V₀))).Finite) :
    IsFlatOver B S hS
      (flatLocusSpace B S hS f F
        (isOpenSubspace_flatLocusOpenSubspace_of_isSurjectiveChart B S hS Xs f.hom F hf hqc hft
          V₀ hV₀ h₀)).2
      ((flatLocusSpaceι B S hS f F
        (isOpenSubspace_flatLocusOpenSubspace_of_isSurjectiveChart B S hS Xs f.hom F hf hqc hft
          V₀ hV₀ h₀)).hom ≫ f.hom)
      (flatLocusRestrict B S hS f F
        (isOpenSubspace_flatLocusOpenSubspace_of_isSurjectiveChart B S hS Xs f.hom F hf hqc hft
          V₀ hV₀ h₀))
declarations.comment: F|_U is flat over Y along the composite U -> X -> Y, for U the open subspace cut out by the flat locus, at the Stacks erratum: condition (3) of the source, local finiteness of the weakly associated points of Y in |Y|, is replaced by local finiteness of the weakly associated points of the scheme of one surjective etale chart of Y, which is how the source's proof reads it and which implies (3). The tag as published, with (3) on |Y|, is false, refuted (with a target which is not decent) by the theorem Stacks.Examples.NonOpenFlatLocusWeaklyAssociated.exists_not_isOpen_flatLocus of StacksFrontier/Examples/Flatness/NonOpenFlatLocusWeaklyAssociated.lean. Flatness of a module on an algebraic space over the target is Tag 05VV, read on the commuting squares of etale scheme charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSmooth_quotientStackModelToBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DLS.** Let `X ⟶ Y` be a smooth morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `G` be a
group algebraic space over `Y` which is flat and locally of finite presentation over `Y`, and let
`G` act on `X` over `Y`. Then the quotient stack `[X/G]` is smooth over `Y`: for every algebraic
stack `𝒳` equivalent over the big fppf site to `[X/G]`, the canonical morphism `[X/G] ⟶ Y` of
Stacks 044R, read on `𝒳`, is a smooth 1-morphism of algebraic stacks in the sense of
Stacks 075U.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_quotientStackModelToBase
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (G X : Over Y.obj) [GrpObj G] [ModObj G X]
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G.left) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X.left)
    (hXsmooth : Space.IsSmooth B S hS X.hom)
    (hGflat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.hom)
    (hGlfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.hom)
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (e : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (quotientStack (actionGroupoid B S hS Y G X hG hX)).p 𝒳.val.val.p) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS
      (quotientStackModelToBase.{u, w} B S hS Y G X hG hX 𝒳 e)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation.coherentRelativeDiagonal_affine_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**The diagonal of `Coh_{X/B}` over `B` is affine and of finite presentation** (Stacks 0DLY).
The relative diagonal of the projection `Coh_{X/B} ⟶ 𝒮_B` is representable by algebraic spaces,
and every algebraic space representing one of its base changes along a scheme-valued point over
`U` is affine and of finite presentation over `U`: that base change is the isomorphism sheaf of
two objects over one point of `B`
(`exists_isAlgebraicSpace_isomPresheaf_affineFinitePresentation`).
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentRelativeDiagonal_affine_finitePresentation :
    ∃ _hrep : Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
        (Stack.relativeDiagonalBasedFunctor B S hS (coherentCFG D) (baseCFG D.Y)
          (coherentToBase D.categoryData)),
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
          (Stack.twoFibreProduct B S hS (baseCFG D.Y) (coherentCFG D) (coherentCFG D)
            (coherentToBase D.categoryData) (coherentToBase D.categoryData)).val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ (Stack.twoFibreProduct B S hS (baseCFG D.Y) (coherentCFG D) (coherentCFG D)
            (coherentToBase D.categoryData) (coherentToBase D.categoryData)).val.p =
          Over.map U.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) (coherentCFG D).val.p
            (Stack.twoFibreProduct B S hS (baseCFG D.Y) (coherentCFG D) (coherentCFG D)
              (coherentToBase D.categoryData) (coherentToBase D.categoryData)).val.p y
            (Stack.relativeDiagonalBasedFunctor B S hS (coherentCFG D) (baseCFG D.Y)
              (coherentToBase D.categoryData)).toFunctor)
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        IsAffineHom B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom ∧
          IsFinitePresentation B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation.isFiberedQuasiSeparated_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_toBaseCFG
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a morphism of algebraic spaces of finite presentation. Then the morphism
`Coh_{X/B} ⟶ B` is quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation.

Quasi-separatedness is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsFiberedQuasiSeparated`, Stacks 04YW for a
1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids; local finite presentation is part (1) of Stacks 06Q2
for the induced 1-morphism of small models (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.smallHomsModelMap`), the
hom types of `Coh_{X/B}` lying one universe above those of the site. See the implementation notes
of the file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiberedQuasiSeparated_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_toBaseCFG
    (D : CoherentSituation B S hS) :
    Stack.IsFiberedQuasiSeparated.{u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS D.toBaseCFG ∧
      letI := locallySmall_coherentCFG D
      letI := locallySmall_baseCFG D.Y
      Stack.HasPropertyOnEverySmoothDiagram B S hS
        (fun _ _ h => Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS h)
        (Stack.smallHomsModelMap D.toBaseCFG)
declarations.comment: quasi-separated as Stacks 04YW for a 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids; locally of finite presentation as Stacks 06Q2 (1) for the small models, Coh_{X/B} having its hom types one universe above the site

declarations.name: StacksDraft.CoherentGenericFibre.exists_submodule_finite_flat_isLocalizedModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DM0, on an affine chart over a valuation ring.**  Let `R` be a valuation ring, `A`
an `R`-algebra and `A_K` the localization of `A` at the nonzero elements of `R`, that is, the
chart of the generic fibre.  Let `N` be an `A_K`-module of finite type, the coherent module on
the generic fibre.  Then there is an `A`-submodule `M` of `N` which is of finite type over `A`,
flat over `R`, and whose generic fibre is `N`, in that `N` is the localization of `M` at the
nonzero elements of `R`.

This is the chart-wise content of the source's proof: `M` is generated over `A` by a finite
`A_K`-generating family of `N`, it is flat over `R` because it is torsion free and `R` is a
valuation ring (Stacks 0539), and its generic fibre is all of `N` because denominators can be
cleared.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_submodule_finite_flat_isLocalizedModule [IsDomain R] [ValuationRing R]
    [Module.Finite AK N] :
    ∃ M : Submodule A N, Module.Finite A M ∧ Module.Flat R M ∧
      IsLocalizedModule R⁰ (LinearMap.restrictScalars R M.subtype)
declarations.comment: the affine-chart case: over a valuation ring a module of finite type on the chart of the generic fibre is the generic fibre of a module of finite type on the chart which is flat over the valuation ring, its flatness being Stacks 0539 and its generic fibre being identified by a localization; the base-change reduction of the first step, the gluing of the chart-wise extensions over Stacks 0829, the proper support, the finite presentation of Stacks 0DLR, and hence the statement for the 1-morphism Cohstack_{X/B} -> B in the sense of Stacks 0CLK are not covered

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation.fiberedValuativeExistence_toBaseCFG
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a morphism of algebraic spaces which is proper and of finite presentation.
Then `Coh_{X/B} ⟶ B` satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion (Stacks 0CLK): every
2-commutative square with left edge `Spec K ⟶ Spec R`, for a valuation ring `R` with fraction field
`K`, admits a dotted arrow after an extension `K'/K` and passage to a valuation ring `R' ⊂ K'`
dominating `R` — here already with `K' = K` and `R' = R`.

The criterion is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FiberedValuativeExistence`, the data of Stacks 0CLK
for a 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids; it agrees with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ValuativeCriterion.Existence` on 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.valuativeCriterionExistence_iff_fiberedValuativeExistence`.
declarations.statement:
theorem CoherentSituation.fiberedValuativeExistence_toBaseCFG (D : CoherentSituation B S hS)
    (hp : IsProper B S hS D.f.hom) :
    Stack.FiberedValuativeExistence.{u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS D.toBaseCFG

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.diagonal_quotSitePresheafToBase
declarations.doc:
The diagonal of `Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ B` is a closed immersion. If `F` is of finite type, then the
diagonal is a closed immersion of finite presentation.

The diagonal is that of the Quot presheaf of `Type (u + 1)` over the base, and being a closed
immersion (of finite presentation) is representability by closed immersions of schemes (locally
of finite presentation), read through `CategoryTheory.uliftYoneda`.
declarations.statement:
theorem diagonal_quotSitePresheafToBase :
    IsClosedImmersionULift.{u + 1} B S hS (pullback.diagonal D.quotSitePresheafToBase) ∧
      (SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.F →
        (closedImmersionFinitePresentation (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS)).relative
          uliftYoneda.{u + 1} (pullback.diagonal D.quotSitePresheafToBase))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.isLocallyOfFinitePresentationULift_quotSitePresheafToBase
declarations.doc:
If `F` is of finite presentation, then `Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ B` is locally of finite presentation:
the morphism of schemes underlying every commuting square of étale charts of the Quot presheaf over
`B` is locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentationULift_quotSitePresheafToBase
    (hF : D.F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentationULift.{u + 1} B S hS D.quotSitePresheafToBase
declarations.comment: the finite-presentation clause: if F is of finite presentation, Quot_{F/X/B} → B is locally of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.isSeparatedULift_and_imp_isLocallyOfFinitePresentationULift_quotSitePresheafToBase
declarations.doc:
The morphism `Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ B` is separated, and if `F` is of finite presentation it is also
locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparatedULift_and_imp_isLocallyOfFinitePresentationULift_quotSitePresheafToBase :
    IsSeparatedULift.{u + 1} B S hS D.quotSitePresheafToBase ∧
      (D.F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite →
        IsLocallyOfFinitePresentationULift.{u + 1} B S hS D.quotSitePresheafToBase)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.isSeparatedULift_quotSitePresheafToBase
registrations.comment: the separation clause: the diagonal of Quot over B is a closed immersion

declarations.name: StacksDraft.GenericFibre.existsUnique_submodule_flat_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DM4, on an affine chart over a valuation ring.**  Let `R` be a valuation ring, `A`
an `R`-algebra, `M` a finite `A`-module and `M_K` the generic fibre of `M`, that is, its
localization at the nonzero elements of `R`.  Let `P` be the kernel of a prescribed quotient of
`M_K`, an `A`-submodule saturated for the nonzero elements of `R`.  Then there is exactly one
`A`-submodule `L` of `M` such that `M / L` is flat over `R` and finite over `A` and the generic
fibre of `L` is `P`; it is the generic kernel `{x ∈ M | ι x ∈ P}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_submodule_flat_quotient [ValuationRing R] [Module.Finite A M]
    (hP : ∀ (s : R) {y : MK}, s ≠ 0 → s • y ∈ P → y ∈ P) :
    ∃! L : Submodule A M, (Module.Flat R (M ⧸ L) ∧ Module.Finite A (M ⧸ L)) ∧
      Submodule.localized₀ R⁰ (ι.restrictScalars R) (L.restrictScalars R)
        = P.restrictScalars R
declarations.comment: the affine-chart case: over a valuation ring a quotient of the generic fibre of a finite module extends uniquely to a quotient flat over the valuation ring and finite over the chart, the extension being the generic-kernel quotient and its flatness Stacks 0539; the etale gluing of Stacks 03M3, the proper support, and the finite presentation of Stacks 0DLR are not covered

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSitePresheafModel.valuativeCriterionExistence_toBase
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a morphism of algebraic spaces which is proper and of finite
presentation, and let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type.  Then
`Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ B` satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion (Stacks 03IX): for
every model of the Quot presheaf, its canonical morphism to `B` has it.  Here the Quot situation
`D` (Stacks 09TR) records `f`, its finite presentation and the quasi-coherent module `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem QuotSitePresheafModel.valuativeCriterionExistence_toBase (D : QuotSituation B S hS)
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS D.f.hom) (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite D.F)
    (N : QuotSitePresheafModel D) : ValuativeCriterion.Existence N.toBase

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.diagonal_hilbertPresheafToBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DM6.** The diagonal of `Hilb_{X/Y} ⟶ Y` is a closed immersion of finite
presentation, for `f : X ⟶ Y` of finite presentation.

The Hilbert presheaf takes values in `Type (u + 1)`, closed subspaces being recorded as
subfunctors, so its diagonal is read through `CategoryTheory.uliftYoneda`: it is representable by
closed immersions of schemes locally of finite presentation.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HilbertPresheafModel.isSeparated_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_toBase
declarations.doc:
For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` which is separated and of finite
presentation, the morphism `Hilb_{X/Y} ⟶ Y` from the Hilbert functor of Stacks 0CZY to the base
— read on the canonical model of the Hilbert presheaf in the universe of the site — is separated
and locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem HilbertPresheafModel.isSeparated_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_toBase
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom) :
    IsSeparated B S hS (HilbertPresheafModel.canonical f).toBase ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (HilbertPresheafModel.canonical f).toBase

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.valuativeCriterionExistence_hilbertPresheafModel_toBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DM8.**  For a morphism `f : X ⟶ B` of algebraic spaces over `S` which is proper as
well as of finite presentation, `Hilb_{X/B} ⟶ B` satisfies the existence part of the valuative
criterion of Morphisms of Spaces, Definition 03IX: every model of the Hilbert presheaf has it for
its canonical morphism to `B`.

This is the source's deduction from Quot, Lemma 0D00 and Lemma 0DM4, both of which are carried as
hypotheses because neither is in the library.  Lemma 0DM4 is `N` together with `hex`: a model of
the Quot presheaf of a situation on `f` whose morphism to `B` satisfies the existence part.
Lemma 0D00 is `e` together with `he`: an isomorphism of the Hilbert presheaf with that Quot
presheaf, compatible with the two canonical morphisms to `B`.  The source's hypotheses that `f`
be proper and of finite presentation are recorded as `_hproper` and `_hfp`; the deduction itself
does not consume them, since they enter through Lemma 0DM4, which is carried.  The content
delivered is the transport: the Quot model is a model of the Hilbert presheaf through `e` with the
same morphism to `B`, and the existence part is independent of the model.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuativeCriterionExistence_hilbertPresheafModel_toBase {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (D : QuotSituation B S hS) (f : X ⟶ D.Y)
    (_hproper : IsProper B S hS f.hom) (_hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (N : QuotSitePresheafModel D) (hex : ValuativeCriterion.Existence N.toBase)
    (e : hilbertPresheaf f ≅ D.quotSitePresheaf)
    (he : e.hom ≫ D.quotSitePresheafToBase = hilbertPresheafToBase f)
    (M : HilbertPresheafModel f) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Existence M.toBase
declarations.comment: the existence part of the valuative criterion for `Hilb_{X/B} ⟶ B`, for any model of the Hilbert presheaf. WARNING, stated plainly: given the carried `e`, `he` (Lemma 0D00) the carried `hex` (Lemma 0DM4 for `Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ B`) is INTER-DERIVABLE with the conclusion, the identification making the transport run both ways, so this statement's content is the transport and the model-independence, not the criterion. The unconditional results are the ones to cite

declarations.name: StacksDraft.GenericFibre.existsUnique_submodule_structureSheaf_flat_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DM8 on an affine chart over a valuation ring.**  Let `R` be a valuation ring, `A`
an `R`-algebra — the ring of an affine chart of `X` — and `A_K` the generic fibre of `A`, that is,
its localization at the nonzero elements of `R`.  Let `P` be an ideal of `A_K` saturated for the
nonzero elements of `R`, that is, the ideal of a closed subscheme of the generic fibre.  Then
there is exactly one ideal `L` of `A` such that `A / L` is flat over `R` and the generic fibre of
`L` is `P`: the closed subscheme of the generic fibre extends uniquely to a closed subscheme of
the chart flat over the valuation ring, and the extension is cut out by the generic kernel
`{x ∈ A | ι x ∈ P}`.

This is the case `F = 𝒪_X` of the chart-wise construction of Lemma 0DM4 — the case Stacks 0DM8
uses, via the identification `Hilb_{X/B} = Quot_{𝒪_X/X/B}` of Quot, Lemma 0D00, under which a
family classified by `Hilb_{X/B}` is the quotient of the structure sheaf by the ideal of a closed
subspace.  It is stated with no finiteness condition on the quotient, which for an ideal of `A` is
automatic, so its uniqueness clause is stronger than that of
`StacksDraft.GenericFibre.existsUnique_submodule_flat_quotient`; flatness over `R` comes from
torsion freeness, which is Stacks 0539.

The gluing of these chart-wise extensions, the properness of the support of the glued extension
and its finite presentation are not proved — see the implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Quot/QuotValuativeAffineChart.lean` — so this does not discharge
the hypothesis `hex` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.valuativeCriterionExistence_hilbertPresheafModel_toBase`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_submodule_structureSheaf_flat_quotient
    (hP : ∀ (s : R) {y : AK}, s ≠ 0 → s • y ∈ P → y ∈ P) :
    ∃! L : Submodule A A, Module.Flat R (A ⧸ L) ∧
      Submodule.localized₀ R⁰ (ι.restrictScalars R) (L.restrictScalars R)
        = P.restrictScalars R
declarations.comment: the affine-chart case over a valuation ring: a closed subscheme of the generic fibre of an affine chart extends uniquely to one flat over the valuation ring, the extension being the generic-kernel ideal; the etale gluing, the proper support and the finite presentation of the glued extension, and hence the valuative criterion itself, are not covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HilbertPresheafModel.valuativeCriterionExistence_toBase
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is proper
as well as of finite presentation.  Then `Hilb_{X/Y} ⟶ Y` satisfies the existence part of the
valuative criterion (Stacks 03IX): for every model of the Hilbert presheaf of `f`, its canonical
morphism to `Y` has it.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.picardRelativeDiagonal_affine_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is flat, proper and of finite
presentation (finite presentation is part of the standing data `D`). The diagonal of
`Picardstack_{X/B}` over `B` is affine and of finite presentation: the relative diagonal of the
structure morphism `Picardstack_{X/B} ⟶ 𝒮_B` is representable by algebraic spaces (Stacks 02ZW),
and every algebraic space representing one of its base changes along a scheme-valued point over
`U` is affine and of finite presentation over `U` (Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB).
declarations.statement:
theorem picardRelativeDiagonal_affine_finitePresentation
    (D : CoherentSituation B S hS) (hflat : IsFlat B S hS D.f.hom)
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS D.f.hom) :
    letI π := picardToBase (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) D.toPicardSituation
    ∃ _hrep : Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
        (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS _ _ π).hom,
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (z : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
          (Stack.twoFibreProduct B S hS (baseCFG D.Y) _ _ π.hom π.hom).val.obj)
        (_hz : z ⋙ (Stack.twoFibreProduct B S hS (baseCFG D.Y) _ _ π.hom π.hom).val.p =
          Over.map U.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom)
            (picardCFG (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) D.toPicardSituation).val.p
            (Stack.twoFibreProduct B S hS (baseCFG D.Y) _ _ π.hom π.hom).val.p z
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor
              (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS _ _ π)))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        IsAffineHom B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom ∧
          IsFinitePresentation B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardOverBase.quasiSeparated_limitPreservingOnObjects_picardToBase
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is flat, proper and of finite
presentation. Then the structure morphism `Picardstack_{X/B} ⟶ 𝒮_B` is quasi-separated, i.e. its
relative diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces, quasi-compact and quasi-separated
(Stacks 04YW, 04XB), and locally of finite presentation in the sense of categories fibred in
groupoids, i.e. limit preserving on objects (Stacks 06CU; for a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks
this is local finite presentation, Stacks 0CMY).
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiSeparated_limitPreservingOnObjects_picardToBase
    (s : PicardSituation B S hS) (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS s.f.hom)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS s.f.hom) (hproper : IsProper B S hS s.f.hom) :
    (∃ _ : Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
        (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS _ _
          (picardToBase (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s)).hom,
      Stack.IsQuasiCompact B S hS
          (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS _ _
            (picardToBase (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s)) ∧
        Stack.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS
          (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS _ _
            (picardToBase (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s))) ∧
      BigFppfOver.IsLimitPreservingOnObjects.{u, u, u} B S hS _ _
        (picardToBase (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s)
declarations.comment: quasi-separated: the relative diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces, quasi-compact and quasi-separated; locally of finite presentation: limit preserving on objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_genericFibre_eq
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a valuation ring with fraction field `K`, and let `X` be an algebraic space over
`R` whose structure morphism `X → Spec R` is smooth. For every effective Cartier divisor
`D ⊆ X_K` there is an effective Cartier divisor `D' ⊆ X` with `D'_K = D`.

Here `X_K` is the base change of `X` along `Spec K → Spec R`, that is the restriction of `X`
along `CategoryTheory.OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict`, and `D'_K` is the base change of the
closed subspace `D'`, `CategoryTheory.OverShriek.relocalizeRestrictSubfunctor`, a closed subspace
of `X_K`. The divisor `D'` is the scheme-theoretic image of `D → X_K → X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_genericFibre_eq
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [ValuationRing R]
    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hR : B.Contains (Spec (.of R))) (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K)))
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of R)) hR)
    (hX : Space.IsSmooth B (Spec (.of R)) hR (Space.toBaseSiteMap B (Spec (.of R)) hR X.1))
    (D : Space.ClosedSubspaces B (Spec (.of K)) hK
      ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (Space.specAlgebraMapHom B R K hR hK)).obj X.1))
    (hD : Space.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B (Spec (.of K)) hK
      ⟨(OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (Space.specAlgebraMapHom B R K hR hK)).obj X.1,
        isAlgebraicSpace_relocalizeRestrict B (Spec (.of K)) (Spec (.of R)) hK hR
          (Space.specAlgebraMapHom B R K hR hK) X.1 X.2⟩ D) :
    ∃ D' : Space.ClosedSubspaces B (Spec (.of R)) hR X.1,
      Space.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B (Spec (.of R)) hR X D' ∧
        OverShriek.relocalizeRestrictSubfunctor (Space.specAlgebraMapHom B R K hR hK) D'.1 =
          D.1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.isGerbeOver_toPicardFunctorBased
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0D25 — a morphism `f : X ⟶ B` of algebraic spaces over `S` —
the morphism `Picardstack_{X/B} ⟶ Pic_{X/B}`, sending an object `(U, b, L)` to the element of
`Pic_{X/B}(U, b)` named by the class of `L`, turns the Picard stack into a gerbe over the Picard
functor: it satisfies the two conditions of Stacks 06P2 (conditions (2)(a) and (2)(b) of
Stacks 06P1) over the big fppf site of `S`, which is the condition of Stacks 06QC.

The section's assumptions on `f` (flat, proper, of finite presentation, with
`𝒪_T ≅ f_{T,*}𝒪_{X_T}` for every `T`) are not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGerbeOver_toPicardFunctorBased :
    IsGerbeOver (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) s.picardFunctorBasedCategory.p
      s.toPicardFunctorBased.toFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.isImmersion_and_isQuasiCompact_diagonal_of_iso_picardFunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is flat, proper and of
finite presentation, such that `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T,*}𝒪_{X_T}` is an isomorphism for every scheme `T`
over `B`, and let `p : H ⟶ B` be an algebraic space over `B` whose functor of points over `B` is
identified (`c`) with the relative Picard functor `Pic_{X/B}` (such an `H` exists by Stacks 0D2C,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpaceOver_picardFunctor`). Then the diagonal `H ⟶ H ×_B H` of
`Pic_{X/B}` over `B` is a quasi-compact immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isImmersion_and_isQuasiCompact_diagonal_of_iso_picardFunctor
    {s : PicardSituation B S hS} (hflat : IsFlat B S hS s.f.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS s.f.hom) (hproper : IsProper B S hS s.f.hom)
    (h : s.StructureSheafMapIso) {H : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {p : H ⟶ s.base}
    (c : spacePointsOver p ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} ≅ s.picardFunctor) :
    IsImmersion B S hS (pullback.diagonal p.hom) ∧
      IsQuasiCompact B S hS (pullback.diagonal p.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeCurvesMorphismsEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMK, the identification `Mor_B(T, B-Curves) = Mor(T, Curves)`.** For a morphism
`f : T → A` of algebraic spaces, the category of morphisms over `(Sch/A)` from `T` to the stack
`A-Curves` is equivalent to the category of morphisms over the big fppf site from `T` to the stack
of curves, by forgetting the morphisms of the bases to `A`.
declarations.comment: the identification of Mor_B(T, B-Curves) with Mor(T, Curves)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curvesMorphismsEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMK, `Mor(T, Curves)` is the category of families of curves over `T`.** For an
algebraic space `T`, the category of morphisms over the big fppf site from `T` (read as the
category `(Sch/T)` of schemes with a morphism to `T`) to the stack of curves is equivalent to the
category of families of curves over `T`: morphisms of algebraic spaces `X ⟶ T` which are flat,
proper, of finite presentation and of relative dimension at most one, with the isomorphisms over
`T` as morphisms. A family `X ⟶ T` corresponds to the morphism sending `U ⟶ T` to the family of
curves `U ×_T X ⟶ U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def curvesMorphismsEquivalence (T : AlgebraicSpaces B integerBase hZ) :
    (schemesOverSpaceBased B hZ T ⥤ᵇ (curvesFiberedCategory B hZ).val) ≌
      CurveFamilyOnSpace B integerBase hZ T
declarations.comment: Mor(T, Curves) is the category of families of curves over the algebraic space T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeCurvesMorphismsCurveFamilyEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMK.** For a morphism `f : T ⟶ A` of algebraic spaces, the category
`Mor_A(T, A-Curves)` of morphisms over `(Sch/A)` from `T` to the stack `A-Curves` is equivalent to
`Mor(T, Curves)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.relativeCurvesMorphismsEquivalence`), and both are the
category of families of curves over `T`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeCurvesMorphismsCurveFamilyEquivalence
    {T A : AlgebraicSpaces B integerBase hZ} (f : T ⟶ A) :
    (schemesOverSpaceBasedOver B hZ f ⥤ᵇ curvesOverSpaceBased B hZ A) ≌
      CurveFamilyOnSpace B integerBase hZ T
declarations.comment: Mor_B(T, B-Curves) = Mor(T, Curves) is the category of families of curves over T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_compl_denseAffineOpen'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DML.** Let `S` be a scheme and let `X` be a regular Noetherian
separated algebraic space over `S`.  Let `U ⊆ X` be a dense affine open subspace, presented by
an open immersion `u : h_W ⟶ X` whose source has affine underlying scheme and whose set of
points is dense.  Then there is an effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ X` with `U = X ∖ D`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_compl_denseAffineOpen` with
both of its inputs supplied: the reduced induced form of Stacks 0BCW on a scheme by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_vanishingIdeal_compl_denseAffineOpen`, and the
implication (2) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 083C by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_hasEffectiveCartierEtaleCover`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_compl_denseAffineOpen'
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hsep : IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    (hnoeth : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1)
    (hreg : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular T))
    (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (hWaff : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W))
    (u : yoneda.obj W ⟶ X.1) (hu : IsOpenImmersion B S hS u)
    (hudense : Dense (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj W) u))) :
    ∃ D : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1,
      IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D ∧
        Set.range (pointsMap B S hS D.1.toFunctor D.1.ι) =
          (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj W) u))ᶜ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_iso_differenceDivisorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DMM.**  Let `S` be a scheme and let `X` be a regular Noetherian
separated algebraic space over `S`.  Then every invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L` is isomorphic to
`𝒪_X(D - D') = 𝒪_X(D) ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_X(D')^{⊗ -1}` for effective Cartier divisors `D, D' ⊆ X`.

Following the source: choose a dense affine open subspace `U ⊆ X` on which `L` is trivial
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_denseAffineOpenChart_bijective_smul`); its complement is an
effective Cartier divisor `D₀` by Stacks 0DML; the trivialization `𝒪_U ≅ L|_U` extends to a
monomorphism `𝓘_{D₀}^{n} ⟶ L` for some `n > 0` by Stacks 07UM
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_mono_idealPowModule_of_iso`), and `𝓘_{D₀}^{n}` is the ideal
sheaf of the effective Cartier divisor `n D₀` (Stacks 083U, 083V).  Twisting by `𝒪_X(n D₀)`
gives a regular global section of `L ⊗ 𝒪_X(n D₀)`, which is `𝒪_X(D)` for an effective Cartier
divisor `D` by Stacks 0847, part (2); so `L ≅ 𝒪_X(D - n D₀)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isEffectiveCartierDivisor_iso_differenceDivisorSheaf
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (separated : IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    (noetherian : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1)
    (regular : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular T))
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf B S hS X))
    (invertible : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS X)
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS X).property L) :
    ∃ (D D' : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (cD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D)
      (cD' : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor B S hS X D'),
      Nonempty (L ≅ differenceDivisorSheaf B S hS X D D' cD cD')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isClosedSubspace_isAlteration
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper surjective morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` with
`Y` integral. Then `f` restricts to an alteration on some integral closed subspace of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isClosedSubspace_isAlteration (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hYint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hp : IsProper B S hS f) (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) :
    ∃ Z : Subfunctor X, IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z ∧
      IsIntegralSpace B S hS Z.toFunctor ∧ IsAlteration B S hS (Z.ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGeometricallyReducedAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMQ, part (1).** An algebraic space `X` over a field `k` is *geometrically
reduced at* a point `x` of `X` when the étale local ring of `X` at every geometric point
above `x` is geometrically reduced as a `k`-algebra.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsGeometricallyReducedAt (k : Type u) [Field k] (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
    (x : points B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1): at a point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGeometricallyReduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMQ, part (2).** An algebraic space over a field `k` is *geometrically
reduced* when it is geometrically reduced at every one of its points.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsGeometricallyReduced (k : Type u) [Field k] (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2): over the field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGeometricallyReducedAt_iff_exists_etaleChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMR, conditions (1) and (2).** An algebraic space over a field `k` is
geometrically reduced at a point `x` exactly when *some* étale neighbourhood `(U, u) → (X, x)`
with `U` a scheme is geometrically reduced at `u`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyReducedAt_iff_exists_etaleChart
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) (x : points B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) :
    IsGeometricallyReducedAt k B hk X hX x ↔
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
        IsEtale B (Spec (.of k)) hk a ∧
          ∃ p : FieldValuedPoint B (Spec (.of k)) hk (yoneda.obj U),
            pointsMap B (Spec (.of k)) hk (yoneda.obj U) a
                (p.class B (Spec (.of k)) hk (yoneda.obj U)) = x ∧
              _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsGeometricallyReducedAt (B.inclusion.map U.hom)
                (schemePoint B (Spec (.of k)) hk U p)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2): some étale neighbourhood

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGeometricallyReducedAt_iff_forall_etaleChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMR, conditions (1) and (3).** An algebraic space over a field `k` is
geometrically reduced at a point `x` exactly when *every* étale neighbourhood `(U, u) → (X, x)`
with `U` a scheme is geometrically reduced at `u`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyReducedAt_iff_forall_etaleChart
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) (x : points B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) :
    IsGeometricallyReducedAt k B hk X hX x ↔
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
        IsEtale B (Spec (.of k)) hk a →
          ∀ p : FieldValuedPoint B (Spec (.of k)) hk (yoneda.obj U),
            pointsMap B (Spec (.of k)) hk (yoneda.obj U) a
                (p.class B (Spec (.of k)) hk (yoneda.obj U)) = x →
              _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsGeometricallyReducedAt (B.inclusion.map U.hom)
                (schemePoint B (Spec (.of k)) hk U p)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (3): every étale neighbourhood

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGeometricallyReduced_iff_exists_surjective_etaleChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMS, conditions (1) and (2).** An algebraic space over a field `k` is
geometrically reduced exactly when *some* surjective étale morphism `U → X` with `U` a scheme
has `U` geometrically reduced over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyReduced_iff_exists_surjective_etaleChart
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) :
    IsGeometricallyReduced k B hk X hX ↔
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
        IsSurjective B (Spec (.of k)) hk a ∧ IsEtale B (Spec (.of k)) hk a ∧
          _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyReduced (B.inclusion.map U.hom)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2): some surjective étale chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGeometricallyReduced_iff_forall_etaleChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMS, conditions (1) and (3).** An algebraic space over a field `k` is
geometrically reduced exactly when *every* étale morphism `U → X` with `U` a scheme has `U`
geometrically reduced over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyReduced_iff_forall_etaleChart
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) :
    IsGeometricallyReduced k B hk X hX ↔
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
        IsEtale B (Spec (.of k)) hk a →
          _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyReduced (B.inclusion.map U.hom)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (3): every étale chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGeometricallyIrreducible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMU.** An algebraic space over a field `k` is *geometrically irreducible* when
the space of points of its base change to every field extension of `k` is irreducible — in
particular nonempty.
declarations.statement: def IsGeometricallyIrreducible (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGeometricallyIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMW.** An algebraic space over a field `k` is *geometrically integral* when its
base change to every field extension of `k` is an integral algebraic space.
