declarations.statement: def IsGeometricallyIntegral (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGeometricallyIntegral_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMX.** A decent algebraic space over a field `k` is geometrically integral over
`k` exactly when it is geometrically reduced and geometrically irreducible over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyIntegral_iff (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
    (hdecent : IsDecentSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) :
    IsGeometricallyIntegral B k hk X ↔
      IsGeometricallyReduced k B hk X hX ∧ IsGeometricallyIrreducible B k hk X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_connectedComponents_points_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMY, part (2), the number of factors.**  The point space of a proper algebraic
space over a field has finitely many connected components, so that the product decomposition of
its global regular functions is a finite product.

Properness makes `X` quasi-compact and locally Noetherian through Tags 04ZL and 04ZK, and
Tag 04ZF then makes `|X|` a Noetherian topological space;  a Noetherian space has finitely many
connected components.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_connectedComponents_points_of_isProper (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of k)) hS f) :
    Finite (ConnectedComponents (points B (Spec (.of k)) hS X))
declarations.comment: part (2): the product is finite, there being one factor for each of the finitely many connected components of the point space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isField_componentFunctions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMY, part (3).**  For a reduced algebraic space, each factor of a componentwise
factorization of its global regular functions is a field:  the factor is an Artinian local ring
by the factorization and reduced by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReduced_componentFunctions`, and a reduced Artinian local ring is a
field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isField_componentFunctions
    (hred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of k)) hS X
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced T))
    (fac : ComponentwiseArtinianFactorization k B hS X)
    (c : ConnectedComponents (points B (Spec (.of k)) hS X)) :
    IsField (componentFunctions B (Spec (.of k)) hS X c)
declarations.comment: part (3): the factors of a reduced space are fields

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_componentwiseArtinianFactorization_of_isProper_of_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMY, part (2).**  The global regular functions `A` of a proper algebraic space over
a field `k` split as the product, over the connected components of the point space `|X|`, of the
rings of functions on the étale charts lying in each component, each factor an Artinian local
`k`-algebra, the splitting being simultaneous restriction to the components; there are finitely
many components (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_connectedComponents_points_of_isProper`), so the
product is finite.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_componentwiseArtinianFactorization_of_isQuasiCompactSpace`
with its remaining hypothesis, artinianness of `A`, supplied by part (1):
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isArtinianRing_globalFunctions_of_isProper_of_field`.
Quasi-compactness and local Noetherianity of `X` come from properness (Tags 04ZL and 04ZK).
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_componentwiseArtinianFactorization_of_isProper_of_field
    (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of k)) hS f) :
    Nonempty (ComponentwiseArtinianFactorization k B hS X)
declarations.comment: part (2): A is the product, over the connected components of |X|, of Artinian local k-algebras, the splitting being restriction to the components

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.moduleFinite_componentFunctions_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMY, part (3), finiteness of the factors.**  Each factor of a componentwise
factorization of the global regular functions of a proper algebraic space over a field `k` is
finite dimensional over `k` — so that, `X` being reduced, each factor is a field
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isField_componentFunctions`) finite over `k`.

The global functions are finite dimensional by part (1), the factorization makes the product of
the factors `k`-linearly isomorphic to them, and projection onto a factor is a surjective
`k`-linear map.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleFinite_componentFunctions_of_isProper (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of k)) hS f)
    (fac : ComponentwiseArtinianFactorization k B hS X)
    (c : ConnectedComponents (points B (Spec (.of k)) hS X)) :
    @Module.Finite k (componentFunctions B (Spec (.of k)) hS X c) _ _
      (@Algebra.toModule k (componentFunctions B (Spec (.of k)) hS X c) _ _
        (fac.factorAlgebra c))
declarations.comment: part (3): the factors are finite over the base field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_componentwiseArtinianFactorization_isField_finite_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMY, part (3).**  Let `X` be a reduced proper algebraic space over a field `k`.
Then `A = H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` is a product of fields, each a finite extension of `k`: there is a
componentwise factorization of `A` (part (2)), and each of its factors is a field
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isField_componentFunctions`, the factor being reduced by Tag 0BGS and
Artinian local) which is finite dimensional over `k`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.moduleFinite_componentFunctions_of_isProper`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_componentwiseArtinianFactorization_isField_finite_of_isProper
    (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of k)) hS f)
    (hred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of k)) hS X
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced T)) :
    ∃ fac : ComponentwiseArtinianFactorization k B hS X,
      ∀ c : ConnectedComponents (points B (Spec (.of k)) hS X),
        IsField (componentFunctions B (Spec (.of k)) hS X c) ∧
          @Module.Finite k (componentFunctions B (Spec (.of k)) hS X c) _ _
            (@Algebra.toModule k (componentFunctions B (Spec (.of k)) hS X c) _ _
              (fac.factorAlgebra c))
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparable_componentFunctions_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMY, part (4).**  For a proper *geometrically* reduced algebraic space `X` over a
field `k`, each factor `k_i` of the global regular functions `A = ∏ k_i` is a finite separable
field extension of `k`:  for every componentwise factorization of `A` (part (2)) and every
connected component `c` of `|X|`, the factor at `c` is a field, finite over `k` and separable
over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparable_componentFunctions_of_isProper (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of k)) hS f)
    (hgr : IsGeometricallyReduced k B hS X hX)
    (fac : ComponentwiseArtinianFactorization k B hS X)
    (c : ConnectedComponents (points B (Spec (.of k)) hS X)) :
    IsField (componentFunctions B (Spec (.of k)) hS X c) ∧
      @Module.Finite k (componentFunctions B (Spec (.of k)) hS X c) _ _
        (@Algebra.toModule k (componentFunctions B (Spec (.of k)) hS X c) _ _
          (fac.factorAlgebra c)) ∧
      @Algebra.IsSeparable k (componentFunctions B (Spec (.of k)) hS X c) _ _
        (fac.factorAlgebra c)
declarations.comment: part (4): if X is geometrically reduced, each factor k_i is finite separable over k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.irreducibleSpace_primeSpectrum_globalFunctions_tensorProduct_of_isGeometricallyConnected
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMY, part (5).**  For a proper geometrically connected algebraic space `X` over a
field `k`, the ring `A = H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` of global regular functions is geometrically irreducible
over `k`:  the spectrum of `A ⊗_k K` is irreducible for every field extension `K/k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem irreducibleSpace_primeSpectrum_globalFunctions_tensorProduct_of_isGeometricallyConnected
    (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of k)) hS f) (hconn : IsGeometricallyConnected B k hS X) :
    ∀ (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra k K],
      IrreducibleSpace (PrimeSpectrum (globalFunctions B (Spec (.of k)) hS X ⊗[k] K))
declarations.comment: part (5): if X is geometrically connected, A is geometrically irreducible over k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.irreducibleSpace_primeSpectrum_globalFunctions_tensorProduct_of_isGeometricallyIrreducible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMY, part (6).**  For a proper geometrically irreducible algebraic space `X` over
a field `k`, the ring `A = H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` of global regular functions is geometrically irreducible
over `k`.

As in the source, this is part (5): every base change of `X` has an irreducible, hence
connected, point space.
declarations.statement:
theorem irreducibleSpace_primeSpectrum_globalFunctions_tensorProduct_of_isGeometricallyIrreducible
    (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of k)) hS f) (hirr : IsGeometricallyIrreducible B k hS X) :
    ∀ (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra k K],
      IrreducibleSpace (PrimeSpectrum (globalFunctions B (Spec (.of k)) hS X ⊗[k] K))
declarations.comment: part (6): if X is geometrically irreducible, A is geometrically irreducible over k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_baseToGlobalFunctions_of_isGeometricallyConnected
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMY, part (7), in its corrected form.**  For a proper geometrically reduced and
geometrically connected algebraic space `X` over a field `k`, the canonical homomorphism
`k ⟶ H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` is bijective: `A = k`.

The source prints "geometrically reduced and connected".  With mere connectedness the clause is
false: `X = Spec ℚ(i)` over `k = ℚ` is proper, geometrically reduced and connected, yet
`A = ℚ(i) ≠ ℚ`.  The source's proof uses geometric irreducibility of `A`, which it obtains from
part (5), whose hypothesis is geometric connectedness; this is the hypothesis stated here, and
the wording of the scheme version, Tag 0BUG (7).  Recorded in `errata.md`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_baseToGlobalFunctions_of_isGeometricallyConnected
    (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of k)) hS f) (hgr : IsGeometricallyReduced k B hS X hX)
    (hconn : IsGeometricallyConnected B k hS X) :
    Function.Bijective (baseToGlobalFunctions k B hS X)
declarations.comment: part (7), corrected form: if X is geometrically reduced and geometrically connected, A = k (the printed 'connected' is false: Spec Q(i) over Q)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_baseToGlobalFunctions_of_isGeometricallyIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMY, part (8).**  For a proper geometrically integral algebraic space `X` over a
field `k`, the canonical homomorphism `k ⟶ H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` is bijective:  `A = k`.

As in the source, this is part (7):  a geometrically integral algebraic space is geometrically
reduced and geometrically connected.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_baseToGlobalFunctions_of_isGeometricallyIntegral
    (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of k)) hS f) (hint : IsGeometricallyIntegral B k hS X) :
    Function.Bijective (baseToGlobalFunctions k B hS X)
declarations.comment: part (8): if X is geometrically integral, A = k

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.moduleFinite_globalFunctions_of_isProper
registrations.comment: part (1): A is finite over the base, here any Noetherian ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isTrivial_of_nontrivial_sections_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DMZ.**  Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a proper integral algebraic space over `k`
and let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module.  If `H⁰(X, L)` and `H⁰(X, L^{⊗ -1})` are both
nonzero then `L ≅ 𝒪_X`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isTrivial_of_nontrivial_sections` with its hypothesis that
`H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` be a field discharged from properness and integrality by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isField_globalFunctions_of_isProper_of_isIntegralSpace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTrivial_of_nontrivial_sections_of_isProper
    (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of k)) hS f)
    (hint : IsIntegralSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS X)
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (modulesRingSheaf B (Spec (.of k)) hS X hX))
    [IsInvertible (structureSheaf B (Spec (.of k)) hS X hX).obj
      (structureRingPresheaf_isSheaf B (Spec (.of k)) hS X hX) L]
    (hL : Nontrivial L.sections)
    (hLinv : Nontrivial (tensorPower (structureSheaf B (Spec (.of k)) hS X hX).obj
      (structureRingPresheaf_isSheaf B (Spec (.of k)) hS X hX) L (-1)).sections) :
    IsTrivial (structureSheaf B (Spec (.of k)) hS X hX).obj
      (structureRingPresheaf_isSheaf B (Spec (.of k)) hS X hX) L

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eulerCharacteristic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DN1.** The Euler characteristic of a coherent module `F` on a proper algebraic
space `X` over a field `k`: the alternating sum `∑ᵢ (-1)ⁱ dim_k Hⁱ(X, F)` of the dimensions over
`k` of the cohomology modules of `F` on the small étale site of `X`.
declarations.statement:
def eulerCharacteristic (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseObject k B hk))
    (_hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of k)) hk f)
    (F : Modules.{u, max (u + 1) w} B (Spec (.of k)) hk X hX)
    [IsCoherent B (Spec (.of k)) hk X hX F] : ℤ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eulerCharacteristic_add_of_shortExact_of_outer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DN2.** Let `k` be a field, `X` a proper algebraic space over `k` and
`0 ⟶ F₁ ⟶ F₂ ⟶ F₃ ⟶ 0` a short exact sequence of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules. Then
`χ(X, F₂) = χ(X, F₁) + χ(X, F₃)`.

`X` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, being proper over `Spec k`, so by Stacks 072C there is
`N` beyond which the cohomology of every coherent module vanishes; below `N` the cohomology of
`F₁` and `F₃` is finite-dimensional by Stacks 08AS; and the long exact sequence with
rank-nullity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finsum_alternating_finrank_cohomologyOverBase_add_of_shortExact_of_outer`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eulerCharacteristic_add_of_shortExact_of_outer
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseObject k B hk)) (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of k)) hk f)
    {S : ShortComplex (Modules.{u, max (u + 1) w} B (Spec (.of k)) hk X hX)} (hS : S.ShortExact)
    [IsCoherent B (Spec (.of k)) hk X hX S.X₁] [IsCoherent B (Spec (.of k)) hk X hX S.X₂]
    [IsCoherent B (Spec (.of k)) hk X hX S.X₃] :
    eulerCharacteristic.{u, w} k B hk X hX f hf S.X₂ =
      eulerCharacteristic.{u, w} k B hk X hX f hf S.X₁ +
        eulerCharacteristic.{u, w} k B hk X hX f hf S.X₃

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eulerCharacteristic_add_of_shortExact_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DN2.**  Let `k` be a field, `X` a proper algebraic space over `k` and
`0 ⟶ F₁ ⟶ F₂ ⟶ F₃ ⟶ 0` a short exact sequence of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules.  Then
`χ(X, F₂) = χ(X, F₁) + χ(X, F₃)`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eulerCharacteristic_add_of_shortExact_of_outer`: the long exact
sequence of cohomology and rank-nullity, with the finiteness of Stacks 08AS and the uniform
vanishing of Stacks 072C, for `X` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, being proper over
`Spec k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eulerCharacteristic_add_of_shortExact_of_isProper
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseObject k B hk)) (hf : IsProper B (Spec (.of k)) hk f)
    {S : ShortComplex (Modules.{u, max (u + 1) w} B (Spec (.of k)) hk X hX)} (hS : S.ShortExact)
    [IsCoherent B (Spec (.of k)) hk X hX S.X₁] [IsCoherent B (Spec (.of k)) hk X hX S.X₂]
    [IsCoherent B (Spec (.of k)) hk X hX S.X₃] :
    eulerCharacteristic.{u, w} k B hk X hX f hf S.X₂ =
      eulerCharacteristic.{u, w} k B hk X hX f hf S.X₁ +
        eulerCharacteristic.{u, w} k B hk X hX f hf S.X₃

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isTwistedEulerNumericalPolynomial_of_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DN4.**  Let `k` be a field, `X` a proper algebraic space over `k`, `F` a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module and `L₁, …, L_r` invertible `𝒪_X`-modules.  For every closed subspace `i : Z ⟶ X`
with `F ≅ i_*𝒢` for a coherent `𝒪_Z`-module `𝒢`, the twisted Euler characteristics
`χ(X, F ⊗ L₁^{⊗ n₁} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ L_r^{⊗ n_r})` are the values at the integral tuples of a rational
polynomial which is zero or of total degree at most `dim Z`.  Taking `Z` to be the
scheme-theoretic support of `F` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTwistedEulerPolynomialOfDegreeLE_coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTwistedEulerNumericalPolynomial_of_isCoherent
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B (Spec (.of k)) hk X.1 X.2)
    (hF : IsCoherent B (Spec (.of k)) hk X.1 X.2 F)
    (L : Fin r → Modules.{u, u} B (Spec (.of k)) hk X.1 X.2)
    [∀ j, Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structurePresheaf B (Spec (.of k)) hk X.1)
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B (Spec (.of k)) hk X.1 X.2).O)).property (L j)] :
    @IsTwistedEulerNumericalPolynomial.{u, w} k _ B hk X r f hf F L _
      (isCoherent_twistedModuleUlift_of_isProper.{u, w} k B hk X f hf L F hF)
declarations.comment: for every closed subspace Z with F = i_*G, G coherent; the scheme-theoretic support is the smallest such Z (Stacks 07U0), and the bound at it is hasTwistedEulerPolynomialOfDegreeLE_coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTwistedEulerPolynomialOfDegreeLE_coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DN4.**  Let `k` be a field, `X` a proper algebraic space over `k`, `F` a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module and `L₁, …, L_r` invertible `𝒪_X`-modules.  The map
`(n₁, …, n_r) ↦ χ(X, F ⊗ L₁^{⊗ n₁} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ L_r^{⊗ n_r})` is the restriction to the integral tuples
of a rational polynomial which is zero or of total degree at most the dimension of the
scheme-theoretic support of `F`.  It is numerical, its values being integers
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_intCast_eq_eval_of_representsTwistedEuler`), and unique
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_of_representsTwistedEuler`); when the support is empty it is `0`.

`F` is the direct image of a coherent module on its scheme-theoretic support (Stacks 07U0 and
07UG), and `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isTwistedEulerNumericalPolynomial_of_isCoherent` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTwistedEulerPolynomialOfDegreeLE_coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B (Spec (.of k)) hk X.1 X.2) [hF : IsCoherent B (Spec (.of k)) hk X.1 X.2 F]
    (L : Fin r → Modules.{u, u} B (Spec (.of k)) hk X.1 X.2)
    [∀ j, Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structurePresheaf B (Spec (.of k)) hk X.1)
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B (Spec (.of k)) hk X.1 X.2).O)).property (L j)] :
    @HasTwistedEulerPolynomialOfDegreeLE.{u, w} k _ B hk X r f hf F L _
      (isCoherent_twistedModuleUlift_of_isProper.{u, w} k B hk X f hf L F hF)
      (dimension B (Spec (.of k)) hk
        (closedSubspaceToSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X
          (coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport B (Spec (.of k)) hk X F)).1
        (closedSubspaceToSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X
          (coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport B (Spec (.of k)) hk X F)).2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTwistedEulerPolynomialOfDegreeLE_fin_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DN4 in the case `r = 0`.**  With no invertible modules to twist by, the function
on `ℤ ^ 0` is the constant `χ(X, F)`, so it is represented by a constant polynomial, whose total
degree is `0`; and `0` is at most the dimension of the closed subspace `Z` carrying `F` as soon
as `Z` has a point, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.zero_le_dimension`.  Taking `Z` to be the scheme
theoretic support of `F` gives the source's statement for `r = 0`.

The point of `Z` is the one hypothesis beyond the source's, and it is the empty-support case
that it excludes: a space with no points has dimension `⊥`, the bound then forces the
representing polynomial to be `0`, hence `χ(X, F) = 0`, and that needs an empty scheme theoretic
support to force `F ≅ 0`, which this library does not provide.  The closed immersion `i`, the
module `G` and the isomorphism `F ≅ i_*G` are the source's hypotheses, carried so that the
statement is the one of the tag; the constant polynomial does not use them.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTwistedEulerPolynomialOfDegreeLE_fin_zero
    (Z : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of k)) hk) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (_hi : IsClosedImmersion B (Spec (.of k)) hk i.hom)
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B (Spec (.of k)) hk Z.1 Z.2)
    (_hG : IsCoherent B (Spec (.of k)) hk Z.1 Z.2 G)
    (_hF : F ≅ (modulePushforward B (Spec (.of k)) hk i).obj G)
    (z : points B (Spec (.of k)) hk Z.1) :
    HasTwistedEulerPolynomialOfDegreeLE.{u, w} k B hk X f hf F L
      (dimension B (Spec (.of k)) hk Z.1 Z.2)
declarations.comment:
the case r = 0 of no invertible modules: the constant function χ(X, F) is
represented by a constant polynomial, of total degree 0, which is at most the dimension of the
closed subspace carrying F whenever that subspace has a point.  The empty-support case, and
every case with invertible modules present, is not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_valuationRing_extension_lift_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DN5.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a flat 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` and let
`g : Spec A ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism out of the spectrum of a valuation ring `A`, presented as an
object `V` of the big fppf site of `S` with an isomorphism `e` of its underlying scheme with
`Spec A`. If the closed point of `Spec A` — presented by a field-valued point `p` of the
algebraic space `V` represents — is carried by `g` to a point of `|𝒴|` in the image of
`|𝒳| ⟶ |𝒴|`, then there are an extension of valuation rings `ι : A ⟶ A'`, an object `V'` of the
site with an isomorphism `e'` of its underlying scheme with `Spec A'` over `Spec ι`, and a
1-morphism `Spec A' ⟶ 𝒳` whose composite with `f` is 2-isomorphic to `Spec A' ⟶ Spec A ⟶ 𝒴`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_valuationRing_extension_lift_of_isFlat
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (e : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V ≅ Spec (.of A))
    (g : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS V ⟶ 𝒴)
    (p : Space.FieldValuedPoint B S hS (yoneda.obj V))
    (hp : e.hom ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map p.value
      (IsLocalRing.closedPoint p.carrier)) = IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)
    (himage : ∃ x : points B S hS 𝒳, pointsMap B S hS f x =
      pointsMap B S hS g (spacePointMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V)
        (schemeFibredCategory B S hS V) (schemeRepChart B S hS V)
        (p.class B S hS (yoneda.obj V)))) :
    ∃ (A' : Type u) (_ : CommRing A') (_ : IsDomain A') (_ : ValuationRing A') (ι : A →+* A'),
      ValuationRing.IsExtension ι ∧
      ∃ (V' : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (e' : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V' ≅ Spec (.of A'))
        (j : V' ⟶ V) (lift : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS V' ⟶ 𝒳),
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map j ≫ e.hom =
            e'.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ι) ∧
          Nonempty (lift ≫ f ≅ schemeStackMap.{u, w} B S hS j ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasProperty_of_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `P` be smooth local on the source-and-target, with fppf local restriction to algebraic
spaces, and let `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` be surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. If the base
change `𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` of `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` along `g` has `P`, then `f` has `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProperty_of_baseChange
    (P : MorphismProperty ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
    (hP : Space.IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    [hlocal : (spaceProperty B S hS P).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)]
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hgsurj : IsSurjective B S hS g)
    (hgflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hglfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g)
    (hbase : HasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram B S hS P
      (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f).fst.hom) :
    HasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram B S hS P f.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSmooth_of_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DN7.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` and let
`g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` be surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. If the base change
`𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` of `f` along `g` is smooth, then so is `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_of_baseChange
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hgs : Stack.IsSurjective B S hS g)
    (hgflat : IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hglfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g)
    (hbase : IsSmooth B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f).fst) :
    IsSmooth B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSurjective_and_isSmooth_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DN8.** Let `π : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`. If `𝒳` is a
gerbe over `𝒴`, then `π` is surjective and smooth.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentPushforwardSituation.cohPushforward
declarations.doc:
Let `B` be an algebraic space and let `π : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-finite
morphism of algebraic spaces which are separated and of finite presentation over `B`.  Then `π_*`
induces a morphism `Coh_{X/B} ⟶ Coh_{Y/B}`: the 1-morphism of categories over the big fppf site
sending an object `(T, ℱ)` to `(T, π_{T,*}ℱ)` and a morphism `(h, φ)`, with `φ : X_h^*ℱ' ⟶ ℱ`, to
`(h, θ_h ≫ π_{T,*}φ)`, where `θ_h : Y_h^*π_{T',*}ℱ' ⟶ π_{T,*}X_h^*ℱ'` is the base change map.
declarations.statement:
def cohPushforward :
    coherentBasedCategory D.source.categoryData ⥤ᵇ coherentBasedCategory D.target.categoryData

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_of_comp_isProper_of_isSeparated_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
Let `π : X ⟶ Y` and `pY : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`. If the composite
`X ⟶ Z` is proper, `pY` is separated and `π` is locally quasi-finite, then `π` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_of_comp_isProper_of_isSeparated_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (π : X ⟶ Y) (pY : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hXZ : IsProper B S hS (π ≫ pY)) (hpY : IsSeparated B S hS pY)
    (hπ : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS π) :
    IsFinite B S hS π
declarations.comment: the reduction of the proof to the finite case: a locally quasi-finite morphism whose source is proper and whose target is separated over the base is finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentation_of_comp_isProper_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
Let `π : X ⟶ Y` and `pY : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`. If the composite
`X ⟶ Z` is locally of finite presentation and proper and `pY` is locally of finite type and
separated, then `π` is of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_of_comp_isProper_of_isSeparated
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (π : X ⟶ Y) (pY : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hXZfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (π ≫ pY))
    (hXZ : IsProper B S hS (π ≫ pY)) (hpYft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS pY)
    (hpY : IsSeparated B S hS pY) :
    IsFinitePresentation B S hS π
declarations.comment: the finite presentation of π in the reduction to the finite case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_comp_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_comp_isProper_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
Let `i : W ⟶ X`, `π : X ⟶ Y` and `pY : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`. If
`i` and `π` are locally quasi-finite, the composite `W ⟶ Z` is proper and `pY` is separated, then
`i ≫ π` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_comp_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_comp_isProper_of_isSeparated
    {W : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS W)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (i : W ⟶ X) (π : X ⟶ Y) (pY : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hi : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS i) (hπ : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS π)
    (hWZ : IsProper B S hS (i ≫ π ≫ pY)) (hpY : IsSeparated B S hS pY) :
    IsFinite B S hS (i ≫ π)
declarations.comment: the finiteness of the composite Z ⟶ X_T ⟶ Y_T in the first paragraph of the proof, the composite being locally quasi-finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation.isOpenSubspace_supportFactorizationLocus
declarations.doc:
For an object `(T, g, F)` of `Coh_{Y/B}` the locus in `T` above which `Supp(F)` lands in
the open subspace `X_T ⊆ Y_T` is an open subspace of `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenSubspace_supportFactorizationLocus (hπ : π ≫ D.f = bX)
    (hopen : IsOpenImmersion B S hS π.hom) (obj : CoherentObject D)
    (hU : IsClosed (D.support obj.T obj.F)) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS (supportFactorizationLocus D hπ obj hU)
declarations.comment: an ingredient only: the open locus of the source's hint, namely the locus in T above which Supp(F) lands in X_T. The conclusion itself is not stated, the 1-morphism Coh_{X/B} ⟶ Coh_{Y/B} of 0DN9 not being constructed in this development

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation.factorsThrough_supportFactorizationLocus_iff
declarations.doc:
A morphism `T' ⟶ T` from an algebraic space factors through the locus exactly when the
base change of `Supp(F)` to `T'` lands in `X_T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsThrough_supportFactorizationLocus_iff (hπ : π ≫ D.f = bX)
    (hopen : IsOpenImmersion B S hS π.hom) (obj : CoherentObject D)
    (hU : IsClosed (D.support obj.T obj.F))
    {T' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hT' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS T')
    (g : T' ⟶ ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).obj obj.T.left).1) :
    (∃ l : T' ⟶ (supportFactorizationLocus D hπ obj hU).toFunctor,
        l ≫ (supportFactorizationLocus D hπ obj hU).ι = g) ↔
      ∃ l : pullback ((supportSubspace D obj hU).ι ≫ (D.projection obj.T).hom) g ⟶
          (baseChangeSpace bX obj.T).1,
        l ≫ (baseChangeOfMap D hπ obj.T).hom =
          pullback.fst ((supportSubspace D obj hU).ι ≫ (D.projection obj.T).hom) g ≫
            (supportSubspace D obj hU).ι
declarations.comment: an ingredient only: the universal property of that locus, a test object factoring through it exactly when the base change of Supp(F) lands in X_T. The residues are the 1-morphism of 0DN9 and the algebraicity of Coh of 09DS

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_and_isOpenImmersion_cohPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DNA.**  Let `B` be an algebraic space and let `π : X ⟶ Y` be an open immersion of
algebraic spaces which are separated and of finite presentation over `B`, the structure morphism
of `X` being `π ≫ f` for the structure morphism `f : Y ⟶ B`.  Then the morphism
`Coh_{X/B} ⟶ Coh_{Y/B}` of Stacks 0DN9,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentPushforwardSituation.cohPushforward`, is an open immersion: it
is representable by algebraic spaces, and every algebraic space representing its base change
along a scheme-valued point of `Coh_{Y/B}` is an open subspace of that scheme (Stacks 04XB at open
immersions), which together are Stacks 04YL (1).

The morphism is fully faithful because `π_{T,*}` is, `π_T` being an open immersion; its essential
image over a test scheme `T` is the objects `(T, G)` with `Supp(G) ⊆ |X_T|`; and over every
scheme-valued point `(T₀, G)` of `Coh_{Y/B}` that condition is cut out by the open subscheme on
`{t ∈ |T₀| : Supp(G) ∩ |Y_t| ⊆ |X_t|}`, the locus of the source's hint.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_and_isOpenImmersion_cohPushforward
    {A X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (π : X ⟶ Y) (f : Y ⟶ A)
    (hopen : IsOpenImmersion B S hS π.hom)
    (hsepX : IsSeparated B S hS (π ≫ f).hom) (hfpX : IsFinitePresentation B S hS (π ≫ f).hom)
    (hsepY : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom) (hfpY : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom) :
    let D := CoherentPushforwardSituation.ofIsOpenImmersion π f hopen hsepX hfpX hsepY hfpY
    Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
        (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom D.cohPushforward :
          coherentCFG D.source ⟶ coherentCFG D.target).hom ∧
      Stack.IsOpenImmersion B S hS
        (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom D.cohPushforward :
          coherentCFG D.source ⟶ coherentCFG D.target)
declarations.comment: the whole statement: for an open immersion π : X → Y of algebraic spaces separated and of finite presentation over B, the morphism Cohstack_{X/B} → Cohstack_{Y/B} of Tag 0DN9 is representable by algebraic spaces and an open immersion in the sense of Tag 04XB, which together are representability by open immersions (Tag 04YL (1))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_and_isClosedImmersion_cohPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DNB.**  Let `B` be an algebraic space and let `π : X ⟶ Y` be a closed immersion of
algebraic spaces which are separated and of finite presentation over `B`, the structure morphism
of `X` being `π ≫ f` for the structure morphism `f : Y ⟶ B`.  Then the morphism
`Coh_{X/B} ⟶ Coh_{Y/B}` of Stacks 0DN9,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentPushforwardSituation.cohPushforward`, is a closed immersion: it
is representable by algebraic spaces, and every algebraic space representing its base change
along a scheme-valued point of `Coh_{Y/B}` is a closed subspace of that scheme (Stacks 04XB at
closed immersions), which together are Stacks 04YL (2).

The proof is the source's.  The morphism is fully faithful because `π_{T,*}` is, `π_T` being a
closed immersion (Stacks 04CJ); its essential image over a test scheme `T` is the objects
`(T, G)` with `G` a direct image along `π_T`, which is the vanishing of the inclusion
`ker(G ⟶ π_{T,*}π_T^*G) ⟶ G`, and that vanishing after base change is cut out by a closed
subspace of `T` by Stacks 083M.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_and_isClosedImmersion_cohPushforward
    {A X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (π : X ⟶ Y) (f : Y ⟶ A)
    (hclosed : IsClosedImmersion B S hS π.hom)
    (hsepX : IsSeparated B S hS (π ≫ f).hom) (hfpX : IsFinitePresentation B S hS (π ≫ f).hom)
    (hsepY : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom) (hfpY : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom) :
    let D := CoherentPushforwardSituation.ofIsClosedImmersion π f hclosed hsepX hfpX hsepY hfpY
    Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
        (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom D.cohPushforward :
          coherentCFG D.source ⟶ coherentCFG D.target).hom ∧
      Stack.IsClosedImmersion B S hS
        (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom D.cohPushforward :
          coherentCFG D.source ⟶ coherentCFG D.target)
declarations.comment: the whole statement: for a closed immersion π : X → Y of algebraic spaces separated and of finite presentation over B, the morphism Cohstack_{X/B} → Cohstack_{Y/B} of Tag 0DN9 is representable by algebraic spaces and a closed immersion in the sense of Tag 04XB, which together are representability by closed immersions (Tag 04YL (2))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NumericalSituation.numericalDirectImage
declarations.doc:
For an object `(T, 𝓕)` of `Coh_{X/B}` and `i ∈ I`, the object
`K_i = Rf_{T,*}(E_{i,T} ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_{X_T}} 𝓕)` of `D(𝒪_T)`, where `f_T : X_T ⟶ T` is the projection of
the base change and `E_{i,T}` the derived pullback of `E_i` to `X_T`.
declarations.statement:
def numericalDirectImage (i : N.I) :
    DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (testSpace A).1 (testSpace A).2)
declarations.comment: the object `K_i = Rf_{T,*}(E_{i,T} ⊗^𝐋 𝓕)` of `D(𝒪_T)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NumericalSituation.numericalEuler
declarations.doc:
The function `χ_i : |T| → ℤ` whose value at a point `t` of `T` is the Euler characteristic
`χ(K_i ⊗^𝐋 κ(t)) = ∑ (-1)^n dim H^n(K_i ⊗^𝐋 κ(t))` of the derived fibre of `K_i` at `t`.
declarations.statement: def numericalEuler (i : N.I) : points B S hS (testSpace A).1 → ℤ
declarations.comment: the function `χ_i : |T| → ℤ`, `t ↦ χ(K_i ⊗^𝐋 κ(t))`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NumericalSituation.numericalSubstack
declarations.doc:
The substack `Coh^P_{X/B} ⊆ Coh_{X/B}`: the full subcategory of `Coh_{X/B}` on the objects
`(T, 𝓕)` with `χ_i(t) = P(i)` for all `i ∈ I` and all `t ∈ |T|`.
declarations.statement: abbrev numericalSubstack : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the substack `Coh^P_{X/B} ⊆ Coh_{X/B}` cut out by `χ_i(t) = P(i)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NumericalSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DNC, the standing data.**  Over a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces of
finite presentation: separatedness of `f`, a set `I`, a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` for each
`i ∈ I`, and the prescribed numerical invariants `P : I → ℤ`.
declarations.statement: structure NumericalSituation
declarations.comment:
the standing data: separatedness of the relative space, the index set, the family
of perfect objects of `D(𝒪_X)`, and the prescribed numerical invariants

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NumericalSituation.isAlgebraicStack_and_numericalSubstackι_isFlatClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0DNC the substack `Coh^P_{X/B}` of `Coh_{X/B}` cut out by `χ_i = P(i)` is an
algebraic stack, and its inclusion into `Coh_{X/B}` is a flat closed immersion: representable by
algebraic spaces, a closed immersion and flat (Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB).
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_and_numericalSubstackι_isFlatClosedImmersion :
    Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS
        (D.conditionCFG N.HasNumericalInvariants N.hasNumericalInvariants_inherited).val ∧
      Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
        (D.conditionι N.HasNumericalInvariants N.hasNumericalInvariants_inherited).hom ∧
      Stack.IsClosedImmersion B S hS
        (D.conditionι N.HasNumericalInvariants N.hasNumericalInvariants_inherited) ∧
      Stack.IsFlat B S hS
        (D.conditionι N.HasNumericalInvariants N.hasNumericalInvariants_inherited)
declarations.comment: Coh^P_{X/B} is algebraic and Coh^P_{X/B} -> Coh_{X/B} is a flat closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NumericalSituation.numericalSubstackι_isOpenAndClosedImmersion_of_finite
declarations.doc:
If `I` is finite, `Coh^P_{X/B}` is an open and closed substack of `Coh_{X/B}`: its inclusion
is representable by algebraic spaces, an open immersion and a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem numericalSubstackι_isOpenAndClosedImmersion_of_finite [Finite N.I] :
    Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
        (D.conditionι N.HasNumericalInvariants N.hasNumericalInvariants_inherited).hom ∧
      Stack.IsOpenImmersion B S hS
        (D.conditionι N.HasNumericalInvariants N.hasNumericalInvariants_inherited) ∧
      Stack.IsClosedImmersion B S hS
        (D.conditionι N.HasNumericalInvariants N.hasNumericalInvariants_inherited)
declarations.comment: the case I finite: Coh^P_{X/B} is an open and closed substack of Coh_{X/B}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NumericalSituation.numericalSubstackι_isOpenAndClosedImmersion_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
If `B` is locally Noetherian (`hB`) and `I` is arbitrary, `Coh^P_{X/B}` is an open and closed
substack of `Coh_{X/B}`: its inclusion is representable by algebraic spaces, an open immersion and
a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem numericalSubstackι_isOpenAndClosedImmersion_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    (hB : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS D.Y.1) :
    Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
        (D.conditionι N.HasNumericalInvariants N.hasNumericalInvariants_inherited).hom ∧
      Stack.IsOpenImmersion B S hS
        (D.conditionι N.HasNumericalInvariants N.hasNumericalInvariants_inherited) ∧
      Stack.IsClosedImmersion B S hS
        (D.conditionι N.HasNumericalInvariants N.hasNumericalInvariants_inherited)
declarations.comment: the case B locally Noetherian: Coh^P_{X/B} is an open and closed substack of Coh_{X/B}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NumericalSituation.isClopen_setOf_chi_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DNE, the open-and-closed clause, at the level of the locus in `|T|`.**  For an
object `(T, 𝓕)` of `Coh_{X/B}` and an index `i`, the subset of `|T|` on which the numerical
invariant `χ_i` takes the prescribed value `P i` is open and closed: `χ_i` is locally constant by
Stacks 0D1Z (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyConstant_of_isEtaleLocallyDerivedFibreChi`), and
the fibres of a locally constant function are open and closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClopen_setOf_chi_eq (c : ChiData B S hS D N) (A : CoherentObject D) (i : N.I) :
    IsClopen {t : testPoints B S hS D A | c.chi A i t = N.P i}
declarations.comment:
the open-and-closed clause only, at the level of the locus in |T| cut out by the
condition chi_i = P i; Coh_{X/B} is no category here, so no substack claim is made

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NumericalSituation.isOpenAndClosedCondition_ofDerivedTensorPowerProducts
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a separated morphism of finite presentation of algebraic spaces,
`E_1, …, E_r` perfect objects of `D(𝒪_X)` and `P : ℤ^{⊕ r} ⟶ ℤ`.  Then the subcategory
`Coh^P_{X/B} ⊆ Coh_{X/B}` of the objects `(T, 𝓕)` with
`χ(X_t, (E_1^{⊗ n_1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ E_r^{⊗ n_r})_t ⊗^𝐋 𝓕_t) = P(n)` for all `n ∈ ℤ^{⊕ r}` and all
`t ∈ T` is an open and closed substack.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenAndClosedCondition_ofDerivedTensorPowerProducts (hf : IsSeparated B S hS D.f.hom)
    {r : ℕ}
    (E : Fin r → @DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS D.X.1 D.X.2) _ _
      (HasDerivedCategory.standard _))
    (hE : ∀ j, letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (Modules.{u, u} B S hS D.X.1 D.X.2)
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS D.X.1 D.X.2).IsPerfect (E j))
    (P : (Fin r → ℤ) → ℤ) :
    IsOpenAndClosedCondition D (ofDerivedTensorPowerProducts hf E hE P).HasNumericalInvariants

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation.exists_hilbertPolynomialι_obj_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
An object `(T ⟶ B, 𝓕)` of `Coh_{X/B}` lies in `Coh^P_{X/B} = Coh^{P, L}_{X/B}` (is the image of
an object of it) exactly when `P(n) = χ(X_t, 𝓕_t ⊗_{𝒪_{X_t}} L_t^{⊗ n})` for every `n ∈ ℤ` and
every `t ∈ T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hilbertPolynomialι_obj_eq_iff (A : CoherentObject D) :
    (∃ X, (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (D.hilbertPolynomialι L P)).obj X = A) ↔
      ∀ (n : ℤ) (t : A.testScheme), P n = CoherentObject.twistedEuler L A t n
declarations.comment:
an object `(T ⟶ B, 𝓕)` of `Coh_{X/B}` lies in `Coh^P_{X/B}` iff
`P(n) = χ(X_t, 𝓕_t ⊗ L_t^{⊗ n})` for all `n ∈ ℤ` and `t ∈ T`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation.hilbertPolynomialι_isOpenAndClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
`Coh^P_{X/B} ⊆ Coh_{X/B}` is an open and closed substack: the inclusion
`Coh^{P, L}_{X/B} ⟶ Coh_{X/B}` is representable by algebraic spaces, an open immersion and a closed
immersion (Stacks 0DNE for `I = ℤ` and `E_n = L^{⊗ n}`).
declarations.statement:
theorem hilbertPolynomialι_isOpenAndClosedImmersion :
    Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (D.hilbertPolynomialι L P).hom ∧
      Stack.IsOpenImmersion B S hS (D.hilbertPolynomialι L P) ∧
      Stack.IsClosedImmersion B S hS (D.hilbertPolynomialι L P)
declarations.comment: `Coh^P_{X/B} = Coh^{P,L}_{X/B} ⊂ Coh_{X/B}` is an open and closed substack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation.isAlgebraicStack_hilbertPolynomialCFG
declarations.doc:
For a separated morphism `f : X ⟶ B` of finite presentation, `Coh^{P, L}_{X/B}` is an algebraic
stack: `Coh_{X/B}` is algebraic (Stacks 09DS, with Grothendieck's existence theorem Stacks 0CXB),
and the inclusion of `Coh^{P, L}_{X/B}` is representable by algebraic spaces (Stacks 05UM).
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_hilbertPolynomialCFG (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS D.f.hom) :
    Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (D.hilbertPolynomialCFG L P).val
declarations.comment:
for `f : X ⟶ B` separated and of finite presentation, `Coh^P_{X/B}` is an
algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentSituation.hilbertPolynomialLocus_decomposition
declarations.doc:
The disjoint union decomposition `Coh_{X/B} = ∐_P Coh^P_{X/B}`, read on each object
`A = (T, 𝓕)` of `Coh_{X/B}`: the loci of the functions `P : ℤ → ℤ`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentObject.hilbertPolynomialLocus`) are open and closed in `T`,
pairwise disjoint, and those of the numerical polynomials cover `T` (Stacks 0DN4); a morphism
`A' ⟶ A` of `Coh_{X/B}` has its source in `Coh^{P, L}_{X/B}` exactly when its map of test schemes
lands in the locus of `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hilbertPolynomialLocus_decomposition (A : CoherentObject D) :
    (∀ P : ℤ → ℤ, IsClopen (A.hilbertPolynomialLocus L P)) ∧
      (⋃ P : {P : ℤ → ℤ // ∃ p : Polynomial ℚ, ∀ m : ℤ, p.eval (m : ℚ) = (P m : ℚ)},
        A.hilbertPolynomialLocus L P.1) = Set.univ ∧
      Pairwise (fun P Q : ℤ → ℤ =>
        Disjoint (A.hilbertPolynomialLocus L P) (A.hilbertPolynomialLocus L Q)) ∧
      ∀ (P : ℤ → ℤ) (A' : CoherentObject D) (φ : CoherentHom A' A),
        CoherentObject.HasHilbertPolynomial L P A' ↔
          Set.range φ.baseScheme ⊆ A.hilbertPolynomialLocus L P
declarations.comment:
`Coh_{X/B} = ∐_{P numerical polynomial} Coh^P_{X/B}` is a disjoint union
decomposition, read on each object `(T, 𝓕)`: the loci of the numerical polynomials are open and
closed, pairwise disjoint, cover `T`, and the locus of `P` cuts out `Coh^P_{X/B}`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NumericalSituation.ofInvertibleTwists
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DNF, the specialisation of Situation 0DNC.**  Over a separated morphism
`f : X ⟶ B` of algebraic spaces of finite presentation, an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L` and a
map `P : ℤ → ℤ`, the standing data of Stacks 0DNC with index set `I = ℤ` and with the family
`n ↦ L^{⊗ n}` of perfect objects of `D(𝒪_X)`.  This is the datum relative to which the source's
`Coh^P_{X/B} = Coh^{P,L}_{X/B}` is formed.

Perfectness of the twists `L^{⊗ n}` is the hypothesis `perfect`: the source takes it for granted
for an invertible module, and this development has no route to it on the small étale ringed site
of an algebraic space.  Nothing here asserts that the resulting substack is open and closed —
that is Lemma 0DNE, which is absent — nor that `P` is a numerical polynomial, which the source
assumes but which no clause of the specialisation uses.
declarations.statement:
def NumericalSituation.ofInvertibleTwists (separated : IsSeparated B S hS D.f.hom)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS D.X.1 D.X.2)
    [hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structurePresheaf B S hS D.X.1)
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS D.X.1 D.X.2).O)).property L]
    (perfect : ∀ n : ℤ, (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS D.X.1 D.X.2).IsPerfect
      (invertibleTwistObject B S hS D.X.1 D.X.2 L n))
    (P : ℤ → ℤ) : NumericalSituation.{u, 0, u} B S hS D
declarations.comment:
the substack as the specialisation of Situation 0DNC to the index set `ℤ` and the
family `n ↦ L^{⊗ n}`; perfectness of those twists is a hypothesis, and openness and closedness
(Lemma 0DNE) and the disjoint union decomposition are not established

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsPrescribedTwistedEuler
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DNF, the membership condition.**  An object `(T ⟶ B, 𝓕)` of `Coh_{X/B}` lies in
`Coh^P_{X/B} = Coh^{P,L}_{X/B}` exactly when

`P(n) = χ(X_t, 𝓕_t ⊗_{𝒪_{X_t}} L_t^{⊗ n})`

holds for every `n ∈ ℤ` and every `t ∈ T`.  Here `ι` is the type of points of the test scheme and
`χ t n` is the Euler characteristic above.  That family is *given*: the Euler characteristic of a
perfect object on an algebraic space cannot be constructed in this development, for the reason
recorded in the implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Quot/NumericalInvariants.lean`, and the same device is used by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtaleLocallyDerivedFibreChi`.
declarations.statement: def IsPrescribedTwistedEuler {ι : Type v} (P : ℤ → ℤ) (χ : ι → ℤ → ℤ) : Prop
declarations.comment:
the membership condition `P(n) = χ(X_t, 𝓕_t ⊗ L_t^{⊗ n})`, stated for a given
family of fibrewise twisted Euler characteristics, which this development cannot construct

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.liftedValuativeCriterionExistence_picardToBase
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is proper, of finite
presentation and smooth. Then the structure morphism `Picardstack_{X/B} ⟶ B` satisfies the
existence part of the valuative criterion (Stacks 0CLK).
declarations.statement:
theorem liftedValuativeCriterionExistence_picardToBase (s : PicardSituation B S hS)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS s.f.hom) (hproper : IsProper B S hS s.f.hom)
    (hsmooth : IsSmooth B S hS s.f.hom) :
    Stack.LiftedValuativeCriterion.Existence.{u, u + 1} B S hS
      (picardToBase (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.picardInertiaEquivalenceOverMultiplicativeGroupProduct
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, and assume that
for every scheme `T` over `B` the structure map `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T}` of the base change
`f_T : X_T ⟶ T` is an isomorphism.  Then the inertia stack of the Picard stack
`Picardstack_{X/B}` of Section 0372 is equal to `𝐆_{m, S} ×_S Picardstack_{X/B}`: this is an
equivalence of the two over `(Sch/S)_fppf`, which is the identity on the
`Picardstack_{X/B}`-factor and sends a point `(L, α)` of the inertia over `T` to the point of
`𝐆_{m, S}(T) = H^0(T, 𝒪_T^*)` that the automorphism `α` of `L` is multiplication by.

The hypothesis `h` reads the source's `f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T} ≅ 𝒪_T`, as in Stacks 0375, as the
canonical map `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T}` being an isomorphism for every test scheme over the base.
The category `Picardstack_{X/B}` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.picardCategoryData`, with the
comparisons of inverse images of Stacks 03LU given by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence`. The standing assumptions of the section that
`f` be flat, proper and of finite presentation are not needed.

"Equal" is read as an equivalence *over the site*
(`CategoryTheory.StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver`), and the product is the 2-fibre product
`CategoryTheory.inertiaPresheafProduct` of the category of elements of `𝐆_{m, S}` with
`Picardstack_{X/B}` over the site.
declarations.statement:
def picardInertiaEquivalenceOverMultiplicativeGroupProduct (s : PicardSituation B S hS)
    (h : s.StructureSheafMapIso) :
    letI : Category.{u + 1} (PicardObject s) :=
      (picardCategoryData (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s).category
    StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (relativeInertiaStruct
        (picardCategoryData (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s).siteProjection
        (picardCategoryData (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s).siteProjection)
      (inertiaPresheafProductStruct
        (picardCategoryData (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s).siteProjection
        (multiplicativeGroupPresheaf B S hS))
declarations.comment: the inertia stack of the Picard stack is 𝐆_{m,S} ×_S Picardstack_{X/B}, as categories over the big fppf site, when 𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T,*}𝒪_{X_T} is an isomorphism for every scheme T over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.isQuasiSeparated_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_represents_picardFunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a flat, proper morphism of finite presentation of algebraic spaces, and
let `p : H ⟶ B` be an algebraic space over `B` whose functor of points over `B` is identified
(`c`) with the relative Picard functor `Pic_{X/B}`. Then `p` is quasi-separated and locally of
finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_represents_picardFunctor
    (c : spacePointsOver p ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} ≅ s.picardFunctor)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS s.f.hom) (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS s.f.hom)
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS s.f.hom) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS p.hom ∧ Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS p.hom
declarations.comment: Stated for every algebraic space representing Pic_{X/B}, i.e. with an identification c of its points over B with Pic_{X/B}, since Section 0DMD presupposes that Pic_{X/B} is an algebraic space (Stacks 0D2C); with Pic_{X/B} itself as that space this is the lemma as printed. The cohomological-flatness condition O_T -> f_{T,*}O_{X_T} iso of the section is dropped: f flat, proper and of finite presentation suffices.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardSituation.isSeparated_of_represents_picardFunctor_of_hasIntegralGeometricFibres
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a flat, proper morphism of finite presentation of algebraic spaces with
`𝒪_T ≅ f_{T,*}𝒪_{X_T}` for every scheme `T` over `B`, whose geometric fibres are integral, and
let `p : H ⟶ B` be an algebraic space over `B` whose functor of points over `B` is identified
(`c`) with the relative Picard functor `Pic_{X/B}`. Then `p` is separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_represents_picardFunctor_of_hasIntegralGeometricFibres
    (c : spacePointsOver p ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} ≅ s.picardFunctor)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS s.f.hom) (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS s.f.hom)
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS s.f.hom) (hstein : s.StructureSheafMapIso)
    (hgeom : HasIntegralGeometricFibres B S hS s.f.hom) :
    IsSeparated B S hS p.hom
declarations.comment: Stated for every algebraic space representing Pic_{X/B}, i.e. with an identification c of its points over B with Pic_{X/B}, since Section 0DMD presupposes that Pic_{X/B} is an algebraic space (Stacks 0D2C); with Pic_{X/B} itself as that space this is the lemma as printed.

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleExternalTensor.isInvertibleModule_externalTensor
declarations.doc: The external tensor product of two invertible modules is invertible.
declarations.statement:
instance isInvertibleModule_externalTensor (L : X.Modules) (N : Y.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] [IsInvertibleModule Y N] :
    IsInvertibleModule (pullback f g) (externalTensor f g L N)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleExternalTensor.isAmple_externalTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0DNK.** Let `S` be a quasi-separated scheme, let `X` and `Y` be schemes over
`S`, let `L` be an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module and `N` an ample invertible `𝒪_Y`-module. Then
`pr₁^* L ⊗_{𝒪_{X ×_S Y}} pr₂^* N` is an ample invertible module on `X ×_S Y`.

Invertibility is the instance `Stacks.AmpleExternalTensor.isInvertibleModule_externalTensor`,
which the statement of ampleness already presupposes. Ampleness is the composite of the two
halves proved above: the absolute case
`Stacks.AmpleExternalTensor.isAmple_externalTensor_of_isAffine`, taken at the terminal scheme
`Spec ℤ`, which is affine, and the descent
`Stacks.AmpleExternalTensor.isAmple_externalTensor_of_isAmple_absolute` along the quasi-compact
immersion `X ×_S Y ⟶ X ×_{Spec ℤ} Y`, which is where quasi-separatedness of `S` is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_externalTensor [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (hL : IsAmple X L) (hN : IsAmple Y N) :
    IsAmple (pullback f g) (externalTensor f g L N)
declarations.comment:
the whole lemma: for `S` quasi-separated, `X` and `Y` schemes over `S`, `L` ample
invertible on `X` and `N` ample invertible on `Y`, the external tensor product
`pr₁^* L ⊗ pr₂^* N` is ample on `X ×_S Y`. Invertibility of that module, the other half of the
tag's conclusion, is the instance `isInvertibleModule_externalTensor` of this file, which the
statement uses. No hypothesis beyond the tag's own.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.picardFirstOrderSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DNM.** Let `S` be a scheme and let `X ⊂ X'` be a first-order
thickening of algebraic spaces over `S` with ideal sheaf `𝓘`. Then there is a canonical exact
sequence

`0 → H⁰(X,𝓘) → H⁰(X',𝒪*_{X'}) → H⁰(X,𝒪*_X) → H¹(X,𝓘) → Pic(X') → Pic(X) → H²(X,𝓘) → ⋯`

which continues in every degree.

It is the long exact cohomology sequence of
`0 → 𝓘 → 𝒪*_{X'} → 𝒪*_X → 0` on the common small étale site, with the two degree-one unit
cohomology groups read as Picard groups by Tag 040E.
declarations.statement: def picardFirstOrderSequence : PicardFirstOrderSequence B S hS hG

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.injective_twoFibreInfProj
declarations.doc:
**Exactness of the six-term sequence of Stacks 0DNN at `Inf_w(M)`**: an infinitesimal
automorphism of the trivial deformation of `w` is determined by its two components.  Each
component is read off through the comparison of the trivial deformation of the component with
the image of the trivial deformation of `w`, and that comparison is invertible because the
lifts form a category fibred in groupoids; a morphism of the `2`-fibre product is determined
by its two components.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_twoFibreInfProj (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (toS : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
    (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A)))
    {𝒳 : Type v₁} [Category.{w₁} 𝒳] {𝒵 : Type v₂} [Category.{w₂} 𝒵]
    {𝒴 : Type v₃} [Category.{w₃} 𝒴]
    (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (p𝒵 : 𝒵 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (P : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (Q : 𝒵 ⥤ 𝒴)
    (hP : P ⋙ p𝒴 = p𝒳) (hQ : Q ⋙ p𝒴 = p𝒵)
    (h𝒳 : p𝒳.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (h𝒵 : p𝒵.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (h𝒴 : p𝒴.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (w : TwoFibreProductOver p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q)
    (hw : (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q).obj w = algebraOver A B S hS toS hA)
    (InfW : InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData A B S hS toS hA
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) w hw
        (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ))
    (InfX : InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData A B S hS toS hA p𝒳 w.x (w.hx.trans hw) h𝒳)
    (InfZ : InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData A B S hS toS hA p𝒵 w.y (w.hy.trans hw) h𝒵)
    (M : SiteModule A B) :
    Function.Injective (LinearMap.prod
        (infLinearMapOfOneMorphism A B S hS toS hA
            (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) p𝒳 (TwoFibreProductOver.fst p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴
              P Q) TwoFibreProductOver.fst_comp_eq w hw (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳
              p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ) h𝒳
            InfW InfX M)
        (infLinearMapOfOneMorphism A B S hS toS hA
            (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) p𝒵 (TwoFibreProductOver.snd p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴
              P Q) TwoFibreProductOver.snd_comp_eq w hw (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳
              p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ) h𝒵
            InfW InfZ M))
declarations.comment: exactness of the six-term sequence at Inf_w(M), i.e. injectivity of Inf_w(M) → Inf_x(M) ⊕ Inf_z(M), which is what exactness of 0 → Inf_w(M) → ⋯ says (see exact_zero_iff_injective). Also constructed in this module, and used to state that map, are the four functoriality maps of Remark 07YA out of the 2-fibre product and out of 𝒳 (infLinearMapOfOneMorphism, tangentLinearMapOfOneMorphism) and the zeros of Inf_x(M) and T_x(M) (autEquiv_zero, liftEquiv_zero). The sequence with all five of its maps and the exactness at all five of its places is Deformation.Artin.twoFibre_sixTermExact in StacksFrontier.Deformation.Artin.Infinitesimal.TwoFibreInfExact.

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.twoFibreInfSideMap
declarations.doc:
**The `𝒵`-side map `Inf_z(M) ⟶ Inf_y(M)` of the six-term sequence of Stacks 0DNN**: the
map induced by `q` on infinitesimal automorphisms, followed by the identification of the
invariants of `q z` with those of `y = p x` along the comparison isomorphism of `w`.
declarations.statement:
public def twoFibreInfSideMap
    (InfZ : InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData A B S hS toS hA p𝒵 w.y
      (twoFibreSndOver A B S hS toS hA w hw) h𝒵)
    (InfY' : InfinitesimalAutomorphismFunctorData A B S hS toS hA p𝒴 (P.obj w.x)
      (twoFibreFstImageOver A B S hS toS hA hP w hw) h𝒴)
    (M : SiteModule A B) : InfZ.functor.obj M →ₗ[A] InfY'.functor.obj M
declarations.comment: the map `Inf_z(M) → Inf_y(M)` of the six-term sequence -- the map of Remark 07YA induced by q, followed by the transport along the comparison isomorphism of w. The sequence and its exactness are Deformation.Artin.twoFibre_sixTermExact.

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.twoFibreTangentSideMap
declarations.doc:
**The `𝒵`-side map `T_z(M) ⟶ T_y(M)` of the six-term sequence of Stacks 0DNN**: the map
induced by `q` on tangent spaces, followed by the identification of the invariants of `q z`
with those of `y = p x` along the comparison isomorphism of `w`.
declarations.statement:
public def twoFibreTangentSideMap
    (TZ : TangentFunctorData A B S hS toS hA p𝒵 w.y (twoFibreSndOver A B S hS toS hA w hw))
    (TY : TangentFunctorData A B S hS toS hA p𝒴 (P.obj w.x)
      (twoFibreFstImageOver A B S hS toS hA hP w hw))
    (M : SiteModule A B) : TZ.functor.obj M →ₗ[A] TY.functor.obj M
declarations.comment: the map `T_z(M) → T_y(M)` of the six-term sequence -- the map of Remark 07YA induced by q, followed by the transport along the comparison isomorphism of w. The sequence and its exactness are Deformation.Artin.twoFibre_sixTermExact.

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.boundaryLinearMap
declarations.doc: **The boundary map `δ : Inf_y(M) ⟶ T_w(M)` of Stacks 0DNN, as an `A`-linear map.**
declarations.statement:
public def boundaryLinearMap (M : SiteModule A B) :
    InfY.functor.obj M →ₗ[A] TW.functor.obj M
declarations.comment: the boundary map `δ : Inf_y(M) → T_w(M)` of the six-term sequence, as an A-linear map: an automorphism α of the trivial deformation y' of y = p x over A[M] is sent to the deformation (x', z', p x' → y' --α--> y' → q z') of w, exactly as in the source. The sequence and its exactness at all five places are Deformation.Artin.twoFibre_sixTermExact.

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.tangentProj_twoFibreBoundaryMap_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The six-term sequence of Stacks 0DNN is a complex at `T_w(M)`**: the boundary map
followed by the pair of projections to the tangent spaces of `x` and of `z` is zero, because
the two components of `δ(α)` are the trivial deformations.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tangentProj_twoFibreBoundaryMap_eq_zero
    (TX : TangentFunctorData A B S hS toS hA p𝒳 w.x (twoFibreFstOver A B S hS toS hA w hw))
    (TZ : TangentFunctorData A B S hS toS hA p𝒵 w.y (twoFibreSndOver A B S hS toS hA w hw))
    (M : SiteModule A B) (α : InfY.functor.obj M) :
    LinearMap.prod
        (tangentLinearMapOfOneMorphism A B S hS toS hA
          (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) p𝒳
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) TwoFibreProductOver.fst_comp_eq w hw TW TX
          h𝒳 M)
        (tangentLinearMapOfOneMorphism A B S hS toS hA
          (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) p𝒵
          (TwoFibreProductOver.snd p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) TwoFibreProductOver.snd_comp_eq w hw TW TZ
          h𝒵 M)
        (boundaryLinearMap A B S hS toS hA hP hQ h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 w hw InfY TW M α) = 0
declarations.comment: one inclusion of exactness at T_w(M): the composite Inf_y(M) → T_w(M) → T_x(M) ⊕ T_z(M) of the six-term sequence is zero, the two components of δ(α) being by construction the trivial deformations of x and of z. The exactness assertion itself is Deformation.Artin.exact_boundary_tangentProj, and the whole sequence is Deformation.Artin.twoFibre_sixTermExact.

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.twoFibre_sixTermExact_of_satisfiesRSStar
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DNN.** Let `P : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `Q : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` be `1`-morphisms of categories fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`, and assume `𝒳`, `𝒴`, `𝒵` satisfy (RS\*). Let `w` be an
object of `𝒲 = 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒵` over `Spec A`, with components `x`, `z` and `y = P x`. For every
`A`-module `M` the six-term sequence

`0 ⟶ Inf_w(M) ⟶ Inf_x(M) ⊕ Inf_z(M) ⟶ Inf_y(M) --δ--> T_w(M) ⟶ T_x(M) ⊕ T_z(M) ⟶ T_y(M)`

of `A`-modules is exact. Here `Inf_?` and `T_?` are the `A`-linear functors that (RS\*)
produces (Stacks 07Y9), for `w` through (RS\*) for `𝒲` (Stacks 0CXQ); the horizontal maps
are those of Remark 07YA and `δ` is `Deformation.Artin.boundaryLinearMap`. Exactness is
stated as injectivity of the first map together with four `Function.Exact`s.
declarations.statement:
public theorem twoFibre_sixTermExact_of_satisfiesRSStar
    (hRS𝒳 : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS p𝒳 h𝒳) (hRS𝒵 : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS p𝒵 h𝒵)
    (hRS𝒴 : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS p𝒴 h𝒴) (M : SiteModule A B) :
    Function.Injective (LinearMap.prod (infLinearMapOfOneMorphism A B S hS toS hA
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) p𝒳 (TwoFibreProductOver.fst p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q)
      TwoFibreProductOver.fst_comp_eq w hw (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳
      h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ) h𝒳 (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) w hw
      (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ)
      (twoFibreProductOver_satisfiesRSStar B S hS p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒵 P Q h𝒳 h𝒴 h𝒵 hP hQ hRS𝒳 hRS𝒴 hRS𝒵))
      (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA p𝒳 w.x (twoFibreFstOver A B S hS toS hA w
      hw) h𝒳 hRS𝒳) M) (infLinearMapOfOneMorphism A B S hS toS hA
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) p𝒵 (TwoFibreProductOver.snd p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q)
      TwoFibreProductOver.snd_comp_eq w hw (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳
      h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ) h𝒵 (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) w hw
      (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ)
      (twoFibreProductOver_satisfiesRSStar B S hS p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒵 P Q h𝒳 h𝒴 h𝒵 hP hQ hRS𝒳 hRS𝒴 hRS𝒵))
      (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA p𝒵 w.y (twoFibreSndOver A B S hS toS hA w
      hw) h𝒵 hRS𝒵) M)) ∧ Function.Exact (LinearMap.prod (infLinearMapOfOneMorphism A B S hS toS hA
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) p𝒳 (TwoFibreProductOver.fst p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q)
      TwoFibreProductOver.fst_comp_eq w hw (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳
      h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ) h𝒳 (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) w hw
      (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ)
      (twoFibreProductOver_satisfiesRSStar B S hS p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒵 P Q h𝒳 h𝒴 h𝒵 hP hQ hRS𝒳 hRS𝒴 hRS𝒵))
      (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA p𝒳 w.x (twoFibreFstOver A B S hS toS hA w
      hw) h𝒳 hRS𝒳) M) (infLinearMapOfOneMorphism A B S hS toS hA
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) p𝒵 (TwoFibreProductOver.snd p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q)
      TwoFibreProductOver.snd_comp_eq w hw (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳
      h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ) h𝒵 (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) w hw
      (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ)
      (twoFibreProductOver_satisfiesRSStar B S hS p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒵 P Q h𝒳 h𝒴 h𝒵 hP hQ hRS𝒳 hRS𝒴 hRS𝒵))
      (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA p𝒵 w.y (twoFibreSndOver A B S hS toS hA w
      hw) h𝒵 hRS𝒵) M)) (LinearMap.coprod (infLinearMapOfOneMorphism A B S hS toS hA p𝒳 p𝒴 P hP w.x
      (twoFibreFstOver A B S hS toS hA w hw) h𝒳 h𝒴 (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA
      p𝒳 w.x (twoFibreFstOver A B S hS toS hA w hw) h𝒳 hRS𝒳) (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S
      hS toS hA p𝒴 (P.obj w.x) (twoFibreFstImageOver A B S hS toS hA hP w hw) h𝒴 hRS𝒴) M)
      (-(twoFibreInfSideMap A B S hS toS hA hP hQ h𝒵 h𝒴 w hw (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S
      hS toS hA p𝒵 w.y (twoFibreSndOver A B S hS toS hA w hw) h𝒵 hRS𝒵)
      (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA p𝒴 (P.obj w.x) (twoFibreFstImageOver A B S
      hS toS hA hP w hw) h𝒴 hRS𝒴) M))) ∧ Function.Exact (LinearMap.coprod (infLinearMapOfOneMorphism
      A B S hS toS hA p𝒳 p𝒴 P hP w.x (twoFibreFstOver A B S hS toS hA w hw) h𝒳 h𝒴
      (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA p𝒳 w.x (twoFibreFstOver A B S hS toS hA w
      hw) h𝒳 hRS𝒳) (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA p𝒴 (P.obj w.x)
      (twoFibreFstImageOver A B S hS toS hA hP w hw) h𝒴 hRS𝒴) M) (-(twoFibreInfSideMap A B S hS toS
      hA hP hQ h𝒵 h𝒴 w hw (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA p𝒵 w.y (twoFibreSndOver
      A B S hS toS hA w hw) h𝒵 hRS𝒵) (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA p𝒴 (P.obj
      w.x) (twoFibreFstImageOver A B S hS toS hA hP w hw) h𝒴 hRS𝒴) M))) (boundaryLinearMap A B S hS
      toS hA hP hQ h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 w hw (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA p𝒴 (P.obj w.x)
      (twoFibreFstImageOver A B S hS toS hA hP w hw) h𝒴 hRS𝒴) (tangentFunctor A B S hS toS hA
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) w hw
      (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ)
      (twoFibreProductOver_satisfiesRSStar B S hS p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒵 P Q h𝒳 h𝒴 h𝒵 hP hQ hRS𝒳 hRS𝒴 hRS𝒵)) M) ∧
      Function.Exact (boundaryLinearMap A B S hS toS hA hP hQ h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 w hw
      (infinitesimalAutomorphismFunctor A B S hS toS hA p𝒴 (P.obj w.x) (twoFibreFstImageOver A B S
      hS toS hA hP w hw) h𝒴 hRS𝒴) (tangentFunctor A B S hS toS hA
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) w hw
      (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ)
      (twoFibreProductOver_satisfiesRSStar B S hS p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒵 P Q h𝒳 h𝒴 h𝒵 hP hQ hRS𝒳 hRS𝒴 hRS𝒵)) M)
      (LinearMap.prod (tangentLinearMapOfOneMorphism A B S hS toS hA
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) p𝒳 (TwoFibreProductOver.fst p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q)
      TwoFibreProductOver.fst_comp_eq w hw (tangentFunctor A B S hS toS hA
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) w hw
      (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ)
      (twoFibreProductOver_satisfiesRSStar B S hS p𝒳 p𝒴 p𝒵 P Q h𝒳 h𝒴 h𝒵 hP hQ hRS𝒳 hRS𝒴 hRS𝒵))
      (tangentFunctor A B S hS toS hA p𝒳 w.x (twoFibreFstOver A B S hS toS hA w hw) h𝒳 hRS𝒳) h𝒳 M)
      (tangentLinearMapOfOneMorphism A B S hS toS hA (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴
      P Q) p𝒵 (TwoFibreProductOver.snd p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) TwoFibreProductOver.snd_comp_eq w hw
      (tangentFunctor A B S hS toS hA (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q) w hw
      (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids p𝒳 p𝒵 p𝒴 P Q h𝒳 h𝒵 h𝒴 hP hQ)
