    D.pushforwardQuotient' I.comparison T K ∈
      D.targetSituation'.properlySupportedQuotients T
declarations.comment: the direct image of a quotient of the Quot functor is one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotPushforwardSituation.quotFunctorMap'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DP1.**  The morphism of Quot functors `Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{π_*F/Y/B}` induced by
the direct image: over a test scheme it sends a quotient `F_T ⟶ Q` to `G_T ⟶ π_{T,*}Q`.

Naturality is the compatibility of the direct image with pullback along a morphism of test
schemes, part (b) of the proof of Stacks 0DN9.
declarations.statement:
def quotFunctorMap' (I : AffinePushforwardQuotInputs' D) :
    D.sourceSituation.quotFunctor ⟶ D.targetSituation'.quotFunctor
declarations.comment: the induced morphism of Quot functors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotPushforwardSituation.isOpenImmersion_pushforwardQuotModelMap
declarations.doc:
Let `B` be an algebraic space, let `π : X ⟶ Y` be an affine open immersion of algebraic spaces
which are separated and of finite presentation over `B`, and let `F` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module.  Then the morphism `Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{π_*F/Y/B}` of Stacks 0DP1 is an open
immersion.

The morphism is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotPushforwardSituation.pushforwardQuotFunctorMap`,
read on the Quot presheaves of the site
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotPushforwardSituation.pushforwardQuotSitePresheafMap_app`) and then in
their canonical models in the universe of the site, where being an open immersion of algebraic
spaces is defined (Stacks 02YU).
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_pushforwardQuotModelMap (base X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (π : X ⟶ Y) (structureX : X ⟶ base) (structureY : Y ⟶ base)
    (comp : π ≫ structureY = structureX) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hπ : IsOpenImmersion B S hS π.hom)
    (haff : IsAffineHom B S hS π.hom) (hsepX : IsSeparated B S hS structureX.hom)
    (hsepY : IsSeparated B S hS structureY.hom)
    (hfpX : IsFinitePresentation B S hS structureX.hom)
    (hfpY : IsFinitePresentation B S hS structureY.hom) :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS (ofAffineOpenImmersion base X Y π structureX structureY comp F hF hπ
      haff hsepX hsepY hfpX hfpY).pushforwardQuotModelMap

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotOpenImmersionSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DP3, the standing data.**  An open immersion `j : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces which
are separated and of finite presentation over an algebraic space `B`, together with a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-module `G`: the data along which the direct image induces a morphism
`Quot_{j^*G/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{G/Y/B}`.
declarations.statement:
structure QuotOpenImmersionSituation (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S)
declarations.comment: the standing data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotOpenImmersionSituation.directImageQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DP3, the direct image of a quotient.**  The quotient `G_T ⟶ j_{T,*}(F_T/K)` of
`G_T`, recorded — as the quotients themselves are — by its kernel.
declarations.comment: the direct image of a quotient, recorded by its kernel

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotOpenImmersionSituation.directImageQuotient_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DP3.**  The direct image of a quotient in `Quot_{F/X/B}(T)` lies in
`Quot_{G/Y/B}(T)`: the quotient of `G_T` by it is `j_{T,*}(F_T/K)`, which is quasi-coherent, of
finite presentation, flat over `T` and has support proper over `T` because `F_T/K` is, this being
the morphism of stacks `Coh_{X/B} ⟶ Coh_{Y/B}` of Stacks 0DN9.
declarations.statement:
theorem directImageQuotient_mem (I : QuotDirectImageInputs D) (T : SchemesOver D.base)
    (K : Subobject (D.sourceSituation.baseChangeModule T))
    (hK : K ∈ D.sourceSituation.properlySupportedQuotients T) :
    D.directImageQuotient I.projections T K ∈
      D.targetSituation.properlySupportedQuotients T
declarations.comment: the direct image of a quotient of the Quot functor is one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotOpenImmersionSituation.quotFunctorMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DP3, the morphism of Quot functors.**  The morphism
`Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{G/Y/B}` induced by the direct image: over a test scheme it sends a quotient
`F_T ⟶ Q` to `G_T ⟶ j_{T,*}Q`.  This is the morphism the source constructs; that it is an open
immersion is the half of the statement whose proof the source omits, and is not proved here.

Naturality is the compatibility of the direct image with pullback along a morphism of test
schemes, part (b) of the proof of Stacks 0DN9.
declarations.statement:
def quotFunctorMap (I : QuotDirectImageInputs D) :
    D.sourceSituation.quotFunctor ⟶ D.targetSituation.quotFunctor
declarations.comment: the morphism of Quot functors the source constructs, not its being open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotOpenSubspaceSituation.isOpenImmersion_quotSitePresheafModelMap
declarations.doc:
Let `B` be an algebraic space, let `j : X ⟶ Y` be an open immersion of algebraic spaces which
are separated and of finite presentation over `B`, let `G` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-module and set
`F = j^*G`.  Then the morphism `Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{G/Y/B}`, sending a quotient `F_T ⟶ Q` to
`G_T ⟶ j_{T,*}Q`, is an open immersion of spaces over `B`.

The Quot functors are read in their canonical models in the universe of the site
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.quotSitePresheafModel`); for arbitrary models this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotOpenSubspaceSituation.isOpenImmersion_quotModelMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_quotSitePresheafModelMap :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS
        (D.quotModelMap D.sourceSituation.quotSitePresheafModel
          D.targetSituation.quotSitePresheafModel) ∧
      D.quotModelMap D.sourceSituation.quotSitePresheafModel
          D.targetSituation.quotSitePresheafModel ≫ D.targetSituation.quotSitePresheafModel.toBase =
        D.sourceSituation.quotSitePresheafModel.toBase

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotOpenSubspaceSituation.isOpenImmersion_quotSitePresheafModelMap_ofOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
Let `B` be an algebraic space, let `j : X ⟶ Y` be an open immersion of algebraic spaces which
are separated and of finite presentation over `B`, let `G` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-module and set
`F = j^*G`.  Then the morphism `Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{G/Y/B}`, sending a quotient `F_T ⟶ Q` to
`G_T ⟶ j_{T,*}Q`, is an open immersion of spaces over `B`.

The situation `D` is assembled from the hypotheses by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotOpenSubspaceSituation.ofOpenImmersion`.  Its source Quot situation
`D.sourceSituation` is `F/X/B` of Stacks 09TR with `F = (modulePullback B S hS j).obj G`, the
inverse image `j^*G` (quasi-coherent by Stacks 03GA), and its target Quot situation
`D.targetSituation` is `G/Y/B`.  The Quot functors are read in their canonical models in the
universe of the site (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.quotSitePresheafModel`), where being
an open immersion of algebraic spaces is defined (Stacks 02YU); for arbitrary models this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotOpenSubspaceSituation.isOpenImmersion_quotModelMap`.  Over a test
scheme the morphism takes a quotient to its direct image
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotOpenSubspaceSituation.familyEquiv_quotModelMap`), and the second
conjunct says it is a morphism over `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_quotSitePresheafModelMap_ofOpenImmersion
    (base X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (j : X ⟶ Y)
    (structureX : X ⟶ base) (structureY : Y ⟶ base) (comp : j ≫ structureY = structureX)
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (quasicoherent : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (openImmersion : IsOpenImmersion B S hS j.hom)
    (separatedX : IsSeparated B S hS structureX.hom)
    (separatedY : IsSeparated B S hS structureY.hom)
    (finitePresentationX : IsFinitePresentation B S hS structureX.hom)
    (finitePresentationY : IsFinitePresentation B S hS structureY.hom) :
    let D := ofOpenImmersion base X Y j structureX structureY comp G quasicoherent openImmersion
      separatedX separatedY finitePresentationX finitePresentationY
    D.sourceSituation.F = (modulePullback B S hS j).obj G ∧
      IsOpenImmersion B S hS D.quotSitePresheafModelMap ∧
      D.quotSitePresheafModelMap ≫ D.targetSituation.quotSitePresheafModel.toBase =
        D.sourceSituation.quotSitePresheafModel.toBase

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotPushforwardSituation.isIso_pushforwardQuotFunctorMap_ofIsClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
Let `B` be an algebraic space, let `π : X ⟶ Y` be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces
which are separated and of finite presentation over `B`, and let `F` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module. Then the morphism `Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{π_*F/Y/B}` of Stacks 0DP1 is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pushforwardQuotFunctorMap_ofIsClosedImmersion (base X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (π : X ⟶ Y) (hπ : IsClosedImmersion B S hS π.hom) (structureX : X ⟶ base)
    (structureY : Y ⟶ base) (comp : π ≫ structureY = structureX)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (quasicoherent : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (separatedX : IsSeparated B S hS structureX.hom)
    (separatedY : IsSeparated B S hS structureY.hom)
    (finitePresentationX : IsFinitePresentation B S hS structureX.hom)
    (finitePresentationY : IsFinitePresentation B S hS structureY.hom) :
    IsIso (ofIsClosedImmersion base X Y π hπ structureX structureY comp F quasicoherent
      separatedX separatedY finitePresentationX finitePresentationY).pushforwardQuotFunctorMap
declarations.comment: the direct image along a closed immersion `π : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces separated and of finite presentation over `B` gives an isomorphism `Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{π_*F/Y/B}` for every quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.relative_closedImmersionOver_quotientInclusion
declarations.doc:
Let `φ : F ⟶ G` be a surjection of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules. The canonical transformation
`Quot_{G/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{F/X/B}` of functors on the test schemes over `B`, sending a quotient
`G_T ⟶ Q` to the quotient `F_T ⟶ G_T ⟶ Q`, is a closed immersion: it is representable by closed
immersions of test schemes.

The Quot functors take values in `Type (u + 1)`, so representability is read through
`CategoryTheory.uliftYoneda`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_closedImmersionOver_quotientInclusion :
    D.closedImmersionOver.relative uliftYoneda.{u + 1} (D.quotientInclusion (hG := hG) φ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.numericalQuot
declarations.doc:
**The fibre product `Quot^P_{F/X/B} = Quot_{F/X/B} ×_{Coh_{X/B}} Coh^P_{X/B}`**, as a category
over the big fppf site of `S`: an object over a scheme `U` is a member `F_T ⟶ 𝒬` of
`Quot_{F/X/B}` over `U`, an object of `Coh^P_{X/B}` over `U` and a vertical isomorphism of their
images in `Coh_{X/B}`.
declarations.statement: def numericalQuot : BasedCategory.{u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)
declarations.comment: the fibre product Quot^P = Quot_{F/X/B} ×_{Coh_{X/B}} Coh^P_{X/B}, as the 2-fibre product over the site of Stacks 0040 of the morphism Quot ⟶ Coh and the inclusion Coh^P ⟶ Coh

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.numericalQuotSubspace
declarations.doc:
**`Quot^P_{F/X/B}`**, as the subfunctor of the Quot presheaf it is: the
quotients `F_T ⟶ 𝒬` whose object `(T, 𝒬)` of `Coh_{X/B}` has `χ(K_i ⊗^𝐋 κ(t)) = P(i)` for all
`i ∈ I` and `t ∈ |T|`, where `K_i = Rf_{T,*}(E_{i,T} ⊗^𝐋 𝒬)`.  It is a subfunctor because the
numerical invariants are compatible with pullback
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NumericalSituation.numericalEuler_eq_of_hom`, from Stacks 0A1P).
declarations.statement: def numericalQuotSubspace : Subfunctor D.quotSitePresheaf
declarations.comment: Quot^P_{F/X/B} as the subfunctor of Quot_{F/X/B} of the quotients whose object of Coh_{X/B} lies in Coh^P_{X/B}; it is the fibre product numericalQuot by mem_numericalQuotSubspace_iff_exists_numericalQuot

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.numericalQuotToQuot_fullyFaithful_and_mem_numericalQuotSubspace_iff
declarations.doc:
The fibre product
`Quot^P_{F/X/B} = Quot_{F/X/B} ×_{Coh_{X/B}} Coh^P_{X/B}` of the remark
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.numericalQuot`) is the subfunctor
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.numericalQuotSubspace` of `Quot_{F/X/B}`: its projection to
`Quot_{F/X/B}` is fully faithful, and a quotient `F_T ⟶ 𝒬` lifts to it exactly when it lies in
the subfunctor.
declarations.statement:
theorem numericalQuotToQuot_fullyFaithful_and_mem_numericalQuotSubspace_iff :
    (D.numericalQuotToQuot N).toFunctor.Full ∧ (D.numericalQuotToQuot N).toFunctor.Faithful ∧
      ∀ {T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ} (x : D.quotSitePresheaf.obj T),
        x ∈ (D.numericalQuotSubspace N).obj T ↔
          ∃ P : D.NumericalQuotObjects N, P.x = QuotFamilyOver.toQuotObjects x
declarations.comment: the fibre product Quot_{F/X/B} x_{Coh_{X/B}} Coh^P_{X/B} is the subfunctor numericalQuotSubspace: the left vertical arrow is fully faithful with that essential image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.relative_closedImmersion_flat_numericalQuotSubspace_ι
declarations.doc:
**`Quot^P_{F/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{F/X/B}` is a flat closed immersion**: its base change
to every scheme of the site is a flat closed immersion.  It is the base change of the flat closed
immersion `Coh^P_{X/B} ⟶ Coh_{X/B}` of Lemma 0DND, the functions `χ_i` being compatible with
pullback and locally constant (Stacks 0A1P, 0D1Z).
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_closedImmersion_flat_numericalQuotSubspace_ι :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.{u} ⊓ @Flat.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative uliftYoneda.{u + 1}
        (D.numericalQuotSubspace N).ι
declarations.comment: the left vertical arrow Quot^P -> Quot is a flat closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.relative_openImmersion_closedImmersion_numericalQuotSubspace_ι_of_finite
declarations.doc:
**For a finite index set, `Quot^P_{F/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{F/X/B}` is an open and closed
immersion.**
declarations.comment: the left vertical arrow is an open and closed immersion if I is finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.relative_openImmersion_closedImmersion_numericalQuotSubspace_ι_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**For `B` locally Noetherian, `Quot^P_{F/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{F/X/B}` is an open and
closed immersion**, however large the index set: every object of `Coh_{X/B}` is étale locally
pulled back from one over a Noetherian test scheme, on which the locus where every `χ_i` takes
its prescribed value is an intersection of unions of connected components, hence open.
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_openImmersion_closedImmersion_numericalQuotSubspace_ι_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    (hB : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS D.Y.1) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion.{u} ⊓
        @_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative uliftYoneda.{u + 1}
        (D.numericalQuotSubspace N).ι
declarations.comment: the left vertical arrow is an open and closed immersion if B is locally Noetherian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.isAlgebraicSpace_subfunctorModel_numericalQuotSubspace
declarations.doc:
**`Quot^P_{F/X/B}` is an algebraic space**, for `F` étale-locally generated by
fewer than `μ` sections with `μ` below the cutoff of the site (for instance `F` of finite type):
every model of `Quot^P_{F/X/B}` in the universe of the site is an algebraic space.  It maps to a
model of `Quot_{F/X/B}`, an algebraic space by Stacks 09TU, by a flat closed immersion.  For an
arbitrary quasi-coherent `F` the assertion fails on the size-bounded site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_subfunctorModel_numericalQuotSubspace
    (hF : ∃ μ < B.cutoff, IsEtaleLocallyGeneratedBelow B S hS μ D.F)
    (F : D.SubfunctorModel (D.numericalQuotSubspace N)) : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F.presheaf
declarations.comment: Quot^P_{F/X/B} is an algebraic space, for F etale-locally generated by fewer than mu sections with mu below the cutoff of the site (every F of finite type)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.relative_openImmersion_closedImmersion_hilbertPolynomialQuot_ι
declarations.doc:
**For `I = ℤ` and `E_i = 𝓛^{⊗ i}`, `Quot^{P, 𝓛}_{F/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{F/X/B}` is an open and
closed immersion.**  For an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `𝓛` and `P : ℤ → ℤ`, the subfunctor
`Quot^{P, 𝓛}_{F/X/B}` of the quotients `F_T ⟶ 𝒬` with `P(n) = χ(X_t, 𝒬_t ⊗ 𝓛_t^{⊗ n})` for all
`n ∈ ℤ` and `t ∈ |T|` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.hilbertPolynomialQuot`, the
condition of Example 0DNF) is an open and closed subfunctor: it is the base change of the open and
closed substack `Coh^{P, 𝓛}_{X/B}`.
declarations.comment: the left vertical arrow is an open and closed immersion if I = Z and E_i = L^{(x) i} for an invertible L; this is Quot^{P,L}, cut out by P(n) = chi(X_t, Q_t (x) L_t^n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.cohObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DP6, the object part of the morphism `Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ Coh_{X/B}`.**  A `T`-point
`F_T ⟶ 𝒬` of the Quot functor, recorded by its kernel `K`, goes to the object `(T, F_T/K)` of
`Coh_{X/B}`: the four conditions an object of `Coh_{X/B}` over `T` satisfies — quasi-coherence,
finite presentation, flatness over `T` and proper support over `T` — are the four conditions
cutting `Quot_{F/X/B}(T)` out of the subobjects of `F_T`.
declarations.statement:
def cohObject (T : SchemesOver D.Y) (K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T))
    (hK : K ∈ D.properlySupportedQuotients T) : CoherentObject D.toCoherentSituation
declarations.comment: the object part of the morphism Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ Coh_{X/B}: a quotient F_T ⟶ Q in Quot_{F/X/B}(T) goes to the object Q of Coh_{X/B} over T. The action on morphisms of test schemes is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.cohHom`. The functor laws hold for the OBJECT part (`cohObject_quotientPullback_id`, `cohObject_quotientPullback_comp`) but are NOT established for the module comparisons, Coh_{X/B} not being a category in this development; and the fibre product Quot^P = Quot ×_{Coh} Coh^P of the remark is NOT formed: Coh^P_{X/B} is not constructed anywhere in this development, only the standing data of Situation 0DNC. See the module docstring for the full accounting

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.cohHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DP6, the action of the morphism `Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ Coh_{X/B}` on morphisms of test
schemes.**  A morphism `h : T' ⟶ T` of test schemes over `B` and a member `K` of
`Quot_{F/X/B}(T)` give a morphism of `Coh_{X/B}` from the object attached to the inverse image
of `K` to the object attached to `K`: its base map is `h` itself, and its module comparison is
the identification of the inverse image of `F_T/K` with the quotient of `F_{T'}` by the
pulled-back kernel.
declarations.statement:
def cohHom {T' T : SchemesOver D.Y}
    (h : T' ⟶ T)
    {K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T)} (hK : K ∈ D.properlySupportedQuotients T) :
    CoherentHom
      (D.cohObject T' (D.quotientPullback h K)
        (D.quotientPullback_mem_properlySupportedQuotients h K hK))
      (D.cohObject T K hK)
declarations.comment: the action of the morphism Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ Coh_{X/B} on morphisms of test schemes, whose object part is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.cohObject`: the base map is h itself, so the morphism lies over the identity of the schemes over B, and the module comparison is the one of Tag 03LU identifying the inverse image of F_T/K with the quotient of F_{T'} by the pulled-back kernel. No hypothesis is carried: the preservation under inverse image of finite presentation (Properties of Spaces, Section 05VR) is the theorem `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.pullbackPreservesFinitePresentation`. The functor laws for the module comparisons are NOT established and the fibre product Quot^P of the remark is NOT formed; see the module docstring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.quotToCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DP6, the morphism `Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ Coh_{X/B}`.**  The rule sending an element
`F_T ⟶ 𝒬` of `Quot_{F/X/B}(T)` to the object `𝒬` of `Coh_{X/B}` over `T`, and a morphism of test
schemes along which one quotient pulls back to another to the morphism of `Coh_{X/B}` with that
base map identifying the inverse image of the one quotient with the other, is a 1-morphism of
categories over the big fppf site: it respects identities and composition, by the coherences of
the comparisons of inverse images of Stacks 03LU, and it does not change the underlying test
scheme.
declarations.statement:
def quotToCoherent :
    D.quotBasedCategory ⥤ᵇ coherentBasedCategory D.toCoherentSituation.categoryData
declarations.comment: the morphism Quot_{F/X/B} ⟶ Coh_{X/B} sending F_T ⟶ Q to the object Q over T, as a 1-morphism of categories over the big fppf site (functor laws included)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPrescribedTwistedEuler_iff_shift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DP7, the final statement, at the level of membership conditions.**  Tensoring with
an invertible module `L` replaces the twisted Euler characteristics `n ↦ χ(X_t, 𝓕_t ⊗ L_t^{⊗ n})`
of `𝓕` by their shift `n ↦ χ(X_t, 𝓕_t ⊗ L_t^{⊗ (n + 1)})`, which is the hypothesis `twist`.  The
condition cutting out `Quot^P_{𝓕/X/B}` is then the condition cutting out
`Quot^{P'}_{𝓕 ⊗ L/X/B}` for `P'(t) = P(t + 1)`.

The isomorphism `Quot_{𝓕/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{𝓕 ⊗ L/X/B}` of the first statement of the source is not
constructed here, and neither are the two open and closed substacks it is claimed to restrict
to.
declarations.comment:
the final statement at the level of membership conditions: the condition for `P`
and `𝓕` is the condition for `P'(t) = P(t + 1)` and `𝓕 ⊗ L`.  The isomorphism
`Quot_{𝓕/X/B} ⟶ Quot_{𝓕 ⊗ L/X/B}` itself is not constructed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.quotSitePresheafTensorInvertibleIso_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DP7.**  Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a morphism of algebraic spaces of finite presentation,
`F` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and `L` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module.  Tensoring with `L` is an
isomorphism of Quot functors
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.quotSitePresheafTensorInvertibleIso :
Quot_{F/X/B} ≅ Quot_{F ⊗ L/X/B}`; precisely:

* it lies over `B`;
* it sends a quotient `F_T ⟶ Q` over `T` to a quotient of `(F ⊗ L)_T` with quotient module
  `Q ⊗ L_T`;
* for every `P : ℤ → ℤ` it carries `Quot^P_{F/X/B}` onto `Quot^{P'}_{F ⊗ L/X/B}`, where
  `P'(n) = P(n + 1)`: a quotient lies in `Quot^P_{F/X/B}` exactly when its image lies in
  `Quot^{P'}_{F ⊗ L/X/B}`, membership being that the object of `Coh_{X/B}` the quotient gives has
  Hilbert polynomial `P`, respectively `P'`, with respect to `L` (Stacks 0DNF).
declarations.statement:
theorem quotSitePresheafTensorInvertibleIso_spec :
    (D.quotSitePresheafTensorInvertibleIso L).hom ≫
        (D.tensorInvertible L).quotSitePresheafToBase = D.quotSitePresheafToBase ∧
      (∀ {T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ} (x : D.quotSitePresheaf.obj T),
        Nonempty ((D.tensorInvertible L).quotientModule _
            ((D.quotSitePresheafTensorInvertibleIso L).hom.app T x).subobject ≅
          moduleTensor B S hS (D.space _) (D.quotientModule _ x.subobject)
            (D.baseChangeInvertible L _))) ∧
      ∀ (P : ℤ → ℤ) {T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ} (x : D.quotSitePresheaf.obj T),
        letI : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
            (structurePresheaf B S hS (D.tensorInvertible L).toCoherentSituation.X.1)
            ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS
              (D.tensorInvertible L).toCoherentSituation.X.1
              (D.tensorInvertible L).toCoherentSituation.X.2).O)).property L := hL
        letI : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
            (structurePresheaf B S hS D.toCoherentSituation.X.1)
            ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS
              D.toCoherentSituation.X.1 D.toCoherentSituation.X.2).O)).property L := hL
        (((D.quotSitePresheafTensorInvertibleIso L).hom.app T x).cohObject.HasHilbertPolynomial L
            (fun n ↦ P (n + 1)) ↔
          x.cohObject.HasHilbertPolynomial L P)
declarations.comment:
the isomorphism `Quot_{F/X/B} ≅ Quot_{F ⊗ L/X/B}` given by tensoring with `L`, and
its restriction to `Quot^P ≅ Quot^{P'}` for `P'(t) = P(t + 1)`, membership read on the actual
twisted Euler characteristics `χ(X_t, Q_t ⊗ L_t^{⊗ n})`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPrescribedTwistedEuler_iff_reindexMul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DP8, at the level of membership conditions.**  Replacing `L` by `L^{⊗ n}` replaces
the twisted Euler characteristics `m ↦ χ(X_t, 𝓕_t ⊗ L_t^{⊗ m})` by `m ↦ χ(X_t, 𝓕_t ⊗ L_t^{⊗ n m})`,
which is the hypothesis `twist`.  For `n ≠ 0` the condition cutting out `Quot^{P,L}_{𝓕/X/B}` is
then the condition cutting out `Quot^{P',L^{⊗ n}}_{𝓕/X/B}` for `P'(t) = P(n t)`: this is the
source's equality of the two substacks, read on their defining conditions.

The hypotheses `hP` and `hχ` say that `P` and each `χ t` are numerical polynomials, represented by
the rational polynomials `p` and `q t`.  They are not removable: for a general `P` the right-hand
condition constrains only the values of `P` at the multiples of `n`.
declarations.comment:
the equality `Quot^{P,L} = Quot^{P',L^{⊗ n}}` with `P'(t) = P(n t)`, read on the
two membership conditions, for `n ≠ 0` and numerical-polynomial invariants; the substacks
themselves are not constructed in this development

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.setOf_hasHilbertPolynomial_invertibleTensorPower_eq
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a morphism of algebraic spaces of finite presentation, `F` a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, `L` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module, `P : ℤ → ℤ` a numerical polynomial
(at every integer, the value of a rational polynomial) and `n` a nonzero integer.  Then

`Quot^{P, L}_{F/X/B} = Quot^{P', L^{⊗ n}}_{F/X/B}`,  where `P'(t) = P(n t)`:

over every scheme `T` of the site, a quotient `F_T ⟶ Q` in `Quot_{F/X/B}(T)` satisfies
`P(m) = χ(X_t, Q_t ⊗ L_t^{⊗ m})` for all `t ∈ T` and `m ∈ ℤ` exactly when it satisfies
`P(n m) = χ(X_t, Q_t ⊗ (L^{⊗ n})_t^{⊗ m})` for all `t ∈ T` and `m ∈ ℤ`, these being the twisted
Euler characteristics `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CoherentObject.twistedEuler` of the object of
`Coh_{X/B}` the quotient gives.
declarations.statement:
theorem setOf_hasHilbertPolynomial_invertibleTensorPower_eq {P : ℤ → ℤ}
    (hP : ∃ p : Polynomial ℚ, ∀ m : ℤ, p.eval (m : ℚ) = (P m : ℚ)) {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0)
    (T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ) :
    letI : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
        (structurePresheaf B S hS D.toCoherentSituation.X.1)
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS
          D.toCoherentSituation.X.1 D.toCoherentSituation.X.2).O)).property L := hL
    letI := isInvertible_invertibleTensorPower B S hS D.toCoherentSituation.X.1
      D.toCoherentSituation.X.2 L n
    {x : D.quotSitePresheaf.obj T | x.cohObject.HasHilbertPolynomial L P} =
      {x : D.quotSitePresheaf.obj T | x.cohObject.HasHilbertPolynomial
        (invertibleTensorPower B S hS D.toCoherentSituation.X.1 D.toCoherentSituation.X.2 L n)
        (fun m => P (n * m))}
declarations.comment:
the equality `Quot^{P,L} = Quot^{P',L^{⊗ n}}` with `P'(t) = P(n t)`, for `n ≠ 0` and
`P` a numerical polynomial, compared on the sections over every scheme of the site, membership
read on the actual twisted Euler characteristics `χ(X_t, Q_t ⊗ L_t^{⊗ m})`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveQuot.isProperAlgebraicSpaceOver_hilbertSubfunctor_quotSituation
declarations.doc:
Let `n ≥ 0`, `r ≥ 1` and `P ∈ ℚ[t]`.  The algebraic space `Quot^P_{𝒪^{⊕ r}_{ℙⁿ_ℤ}/ℙⁿ_ℤ/ℤ}`
parametrizing quotients of `𝒪^{⊕ r}_{ℙⁿ_ℤ}` with Hilbert polynomial `P` is proper over `Spec ℤ`:
the subfunctor of the Quot presheaf (Stacks 09TR) of `𝒪^{⊕ r}/ℙⁿ_ℤ/ℤ` of the quotients which,
read on `ℙⁿ_T`, have Hilbert polynomial `P` on every fibre is an algebraic space proper over
`Spec ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperAlgebraicSpaceOver_hilbertSubfunctor_quotSituation (hr : 1 ≤ r)
    (P : Polynomial ℚ) :
    (quotSituation B n r).IsProperAlgebraicSpaceOver
      (hilbertSubfunctor (quotSituationFrame B n r) P)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveQuotOverSpace.isProperAlgebraicSpaceOver_hilbertPolynomialQuot_productSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `Y` be an algebraic space, `X = Y × ℙⁿ_ℤ`, `𝓛` the pullback of `𝒪_{ℙⁿ}(1)` to `X` and `F`
an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation.  For a numerical polynomial `P : ℤ → ℤ` (the function of a
rational polynomial `p`), the algebraic space `Quot^P_{F/X/Y}` parametrizing quotients of `F`
having Hilbert polynomial `P` with respect to `𝓛` is proper over `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperAlgebraicSpaceOver_hilbertPolynomialQuot_productSpace
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B integerBase B.contains_integerBase)
    (F : Space.Modules.{u, u} B integerBase B.contains_integerBase (productSpace n Y).1
      (productSpace n Y).2) (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F)
    {P : ℤ → ℤ} {p : Polynomial ℚ} (hP : ∀ m : ℤ, p.eval (m : ℚ) = (P m : ℚ)) :
    (situation n Y F (@SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite
        _ _ _ _ F hF)).IsProperAlgebraicSpaceOver
      ((situation n Y F (@SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite
          _ _ _ _ F hF)).hilbertPolynomialQuot
        (twistingModule (situationFrame n Y F
          (@SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite _ _ _ _ F hF)))
        (hL := isInvertible_twistingModule (situationFrame n Y F
          (@SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite _ _ _ _ F hF))) P)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.isProperAlgebraicSpaceOver_hilbertPolynomialQuot_of_isRelativelyAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DPC.**  Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a proper morphism of finite presentation of algebraic
spaces (over `Spec ℤ`), `F` a finitely presented `𝒪_X`-module, `L` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module
ample on `X/B` (Stacks 0D31) and `P` a numerical polynomial.  Then the algebraic space
`Quot^P_{F/X/B}` parametrizing quotients of `F` having Hilbert polynomial `P` with respect to `L`
is proper over `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperAlgebraicSpaceOver_hilbertPolynomialQuot_of_isRelativelyAmple
    (D : QuotSituation B integerBase B.contains_integerBase)
    (hf : IsProper B integerBase B.contains_integerBase D.f.hom)
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite D.F)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B integerBase B.contains_integerBase D.X.1 D.X.2)
    [hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structurePresheaf B integerBase
      B.contains_integerBase D.X.1)
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B integerBase B.contains_integerBase D.X.1 D.X.2).O)).property L]
    (hamp : IsRelativelyAmple B integerBase B.contains_integerBase D.f L)
    {P : ℤ → ℤ} {p : Polynomial ℚ} (hP : ∀ m : ℤ, p.eval (m : ℚ) = (P m : ℚ)) :
    D.IsProperAlgebraicSpaceOver (D.hilbertPolynomialQuot L P)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.exists_model_isSeparated_isFinitePresentation_hilbertPolynomialQuot
declarations.doc:
Let `F/X/B` be a Quot situation over `Spec ℤ` (Stacks 09TR): `f : X ⟶ B` a morphism of finite
presentation of algebraic spaces and `F` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module.  If `f` is separated, `F`
is of finite presentation, `L` is an invertible `𝒪_X`-module ample on `X/B` (Stacks 0D31) and `P`
is a numerical polynomial, then `Quot^P_{F/X/B}` (the quotients of `F` having Hilbert polynomial
`P` with respect to `L`) has a model `M` in the universe of the site, identified with it over `B`,
which is an algebraic space whose morphism to `B` is separated and of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_model_isSeparated_isFinitePresentation_hilbertPolynomialQuot
    (D : QuotSituation B integerBase B.contains_integerBase)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B integerBase B.contains_integerBase D.f.hom)
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite D.F)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B integerBase B.contains_integerBase D.X.1 D.X.2)
    [hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
      (structurePresheaf B integerBase B.contains_integerBase D.X.1)
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B integerBase B.contains_integerBase D.X.1 D.X.2).O)).property L]
    (hamp : IsRelativelyAmple B integerBase B.contains_integerBase D.f L)
    {P : ℤ → ℤ} {p : Polynomial ℚ} (hP : ∀ m : ℤ, p.eval (m : ℚ) = (P m : ℚ)) :
    ∃ M : D.SubfunctorModel (D.hilbertPolynomialQuot L P),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B integerBase B.contains_integerBase M.presheaf ∧
        IsSeparated B integerBase B.contains_integerBase M.toBase ∧
        IsFinitePresentation B integerBase B.contains_integerBase M.toBase

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hilbertPresheafMap
declarations.doc:
An open immersion `π : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `A` induces a
morphism of Hilbert functors `Hilb_{X/A} ⟶ Hilb_{Y/A}`, sending a family of closed subspaces of
`X_T` to its image in `Y_T`.
declarations.statement: def hilbertPresheafMap : hilbertPresheaf bX ⟶ hilbertPresheaf bY
declarations.comment: the induced morphism of Hilbert functors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenImmersion_hilbertModelMap
declarations.doc:
The morphism of Hilbert functors induced by an open immersion `π : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic
spaces over `A`, with `Y` separated over `A`, is an open immersion, read in any models of the two
Hilbert functors.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_hilbertModelMap (MX : HilbertPresheafModel bX)
    (MY : HilbertPresheafModel bY) :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS (hilbertModelMap hπ hopen hsep MX MY)
declarations.comment: the induced morphism is an open immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenImmersion_hilbertModelMap_canonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DPE.** Let `π : X ⟶ Y` be an open immersion of algebraic spaces over an algebraic
space `A`, with `Y` separated over `A`. Then `π` induces an open immersion
`Hilb_{X/A} ⟶ Hilb_{Y/A}` of Hilbert functors: the morphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hilbertPresheafMap`, sending a family `Z ⊆ X_T` to its image in `Y_T`,
read in the canonical models `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HilbertPresheafModel.canonical` of the two
Hilbert functors, is an open immersion. Nothing is assumed about the models: they exist for every
morphism of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_hilbertModelMap_canonical (hπ : π ≫ bY = bX)
    (hopen : IsOpenImmersion B S hS π.hom) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS bY.hom) :
    IsOpenImmersion B S hS (hilbertModelMap hπ hopen hsep (HilbertPresheafModel.canonical bX)
      (HilbertPresheafModel.canonical bY))
declarations.comment: the induced morphism of the canonical Hilbert functors is an open immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hilbertPresheafMapOfClosed
declarations.doc:
A closed immersion `π : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `A` induces a
morphism of Hilbert functors `Hilb_{X/A} ⟶ Hilb_{Y/A}`, sending a family of closed subspaces of
`X_T` to its image in `Y_T`.
declarations.statement: def hilbertPresheafMapOfClosed : hilbertPresheaf bX ⟶ hilbertPresheaf bY
declarations.comment: the induced morphism of Hilbert functors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mono_hilbertModelMapOfClosed
declarations.doc:
The morphism of Hilbert functors induced by a closed immersion over the base is a
monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_hilbertModelMapOfClosed (MX : HilbertPresheafModel bX)
    (MY : HilbertPresheafModel bY) :
    Mono (hilbertModelMapOfClosed hπ hclosed MX MY)
declarations.comment: the induced morphism is a monomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_hilbertModelMapOfClosed
declarations.doc:
Let `π : X ⟶ Y` be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces over an algebraic space `A`, with
`Y` of finite presentation over `A`. Then the morphism of Hilbert functors
`Hilb_{X/A} ⟶ Hilb_{Y/A}` that `π` induces is a closed immersion, read in any models of the two
Hilbert functors.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_hilbertModelMapOfClosed (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS bY.hom)
    (MX : HilbertPresheafModel bX) (MY : HilbertPresheafModel bY) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS (hilbertModelMapOfClosed hπ hclosed MX MY)
declarations.comment: the induced morphism is a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_hilbertModelMapOfClosed_canonical
declarations.doc:
Let `π : X ⟶ Y` be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces over an algebraic space `A`, with
`Y` of finite presentation over `A`. Then `π` induces a closed immersion
`Hilb_{X/A} ⟶ Hilb_{Y/A}` of Hilbert functors: the morphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hilbertPresheafMapOfClosed`, sending a family `Z ⊆ X_T` to its image in
`Y_T`, read in the canonical models `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HilbertPresheafModel.canonical` of
the two Hilbert functors, is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_hilbertModelMapOfClosed_canonical
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS bY.hom) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS (hilbertModelMapOfClosed hπ hclosed
      (HilbertPresheafModel.canonical bX) (HilbertPresheafModel.canonical bY))
declarations.comment: the induced morphism of the canonical Hilbert functors is a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HilbertEulerData.numericalHilbertFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DPG.** The functor `Hilb^P_{X/Y}`: it sends a test scheme `T` over `Y` to the set
of families classified by `Hilb_{X/Y}` over `T` whose fibrewise invariants are the prescribed
`P`, and a morphism of test schemes to base change of those families, which is well defined by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HilbertEulerData.isPrescribed_baseChange`.

This is the source's `Hilb^P_{X/Y} = Quot^P_{𝒪_X/X/Y}`, formed directly as the subfunctor of the
Hilbert functor that the fibre product of Remark 0DP6 computes; that fibre product itself is not
available here, since `Coh^P_{X/Y}` is not constructed in this development.
declarations.statement: def numericalHilbertFunctor : (SchemesOverPresheaf B S hS Y)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the definition of `Hilb^P_{X/Y}`, as the subfunctor of `Hilb_{X/Y}` of families whose fibrewise invariants are the prescribed ones; the fibre product `Quot_{𝒪_X/X/Y} ×_{Coh_{X/Y}} Coh^P_{X/Y}` of Remark 0DP6 and the identification `Hilb_{X/Y} = Quot_{𝒪_X/X/Y}` of Lemma 0D00 are not available in this development

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HilbertEulerData.numericalHilbertInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DPG.** The morphism `Hilb^P_{X/Y} ⟶ Hilb_{X/Y}`: a family with the prescribed
invariants is in particular a family.  The source asserts that this morphism is a flat closed
immersion, and an open and closed immersion in three listed cases; neither assertion is proved
here, both resting on Lemmas 0DND and 0DNE, which are absent.  What is proved is that it is a
monomorphism, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HilbertEulerData.mono_numericalHilbertInclusion`.
declarations.statement: def numericalHilbertInclusion : χd.numericalHilbertFunctor P ⟶ hilbertFunctor f
declarations.comment: the morphism `Hilb^P_{X/Y} ⟶ Hilb_{X/Y}`, proved to be a monomorphism; that it is a flat closed immersion, and an open and closed immersion for `I` finite, `Y` locally Noetherian, or `I = ℤ` with `E i = L^{⊗ i}`, rests on Lemmas 0DND and 0DNE and is not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.numericalHilbertSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
`Hilb^P_{X/B} = Quot^P_{𝒪_X/X/B}`: the subfunctor of the Hilbert presheaf of the families
`Z ⊆ X_T` whose object `(T, 𝒪_Z)` of `Coh_{X/B}` lies in `Coh^P_{X/B}`: for every `i ∈ I` and
every point `t` of `T`, `χ(K_i ⊗^𝐋 κ(t)) = P(i)` with `K_i = Rf_{T,*}(E_{i,T} ⊗^𝐋 𝒪_Z)`.  It is
the subfunctor that the fibre product `Quot_{𝒪_X/X/B} ×_{Coh_{X/B}} Coh^P_{X/B}` of Stacks 0DP6
cuts out of `Hilb_{X/B}` through Stacks 0D00
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_numericalHilbertSubfunctor_iff_exists_numericalQuot`), and a
subfunctor because the `χ_i` are compatible with pullback (Stacks 0A1P).
declarations.statement: def numericalHilbertSubfunctor : Subfunctor (hilbertPresheaf f)
declarations.comment: the definition of `Hilb^P_{X/B}` as the subfunctor of `Hilb_{X/B}` corresponding to `Quot^P_{𝒪_X/X/B} = Quot_{𝒪_X/X/B} ×_{Coh_{X/B}} Coh^P_{X/B}`, for the actual invariants `χ(K_i ⊗^𝐋 κ(t))` of Situation 0DNC

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_numericalHilbertSubfunctor_iff_exists_numericalQuot
declarations.doc:
A family `Z ⊆ X_T` lies in `Hilb^P_{X/B}` exactly when its quotient `𝒪_{X_T} ⟶ 𝒪_Z`, the
section of `Quot_{𝒪_X/X/B}` over `T` it corresponds to under `Hilb_{X/B} = Quot_{𝒪_X/X/B}`
(Stacks 0D00), lifts to the 2-fibre product
`Quot^P_{𝒪_X/X/B} = Quot_{𝒪_X/X/B} ×_{Coh_{X/B}} Coh^P_{X/B}` of Stacks 0DP6
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotSituation.numericalQuot`).
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_numericalHilbertSubfunctor_iff_exists_numericalQuot {T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ}
    (x : (hilbertPresheaf f).obj T) :
    x ∈ (numericalHilbertSubfunctor f hf N).obj T ↔
      ∃ P : (structureSheafQuotSituation f hf).NumericalQuotObjects N,
        P.x = ((hilbertPresheafIsoQuotSitePresheaf f hf).hom.app T x).toQuotObjects
declarations.comment: `Hilb^P_{X/B} = Quot^P_{𝒪_X/X/B}`: a family lies in `Hilb^P_{X/B}` exactly when its quotient, through `Hilb_{X/B} = Quot_{𝒪_X/X/B}` (0D00), lifts to the 2-fibre product `Quot_{𝒪_X/X/B} ×_{Coh_{X/B}} Coh^P_{X/B}` of 0DP6

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relative_closedImmersion_flat_numericalHilbertSubfunctor_ι
declarations.doc:
`Hilb^P_{X/B} ⟶ Hilb_{X/B}` is a flat closed immersion: its inclusion is representable
by morphisms of schemes which are flat closed immersions.  This is the base change of
`Coh^P_{X/B} ⟶ Coh_{X/B}`, a flat closed immersion by Stacks 0DND.
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_closedImmersion_flat_numericalHilbertSubfunctor_ι :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.{u} ⊓ @Flat.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative uliftYoneda.{u + 1}
        (numericalHilbertSubfunctor f hf N).ι
declarations.comment: `Hilb^P_{X/B} ⟶ Hilb_{X/B}` is a flat closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relative_openImmersion_closedImmersion_numericalHilbertSubfunctor_ι_of_finite
declarations.doc: If `I` is finite, then `Hilb^P_{X/B} ⟶ Hilb_{X/B}` is an open and closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_openImmersion_closedImmersion_numericalHilbertSubfunctor_ι_of_finite
    [Finite N.I] :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion.{u} ⊓
        @_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative uliftYoneda.{u + 1}
        (numericalHilbertSubfunctor f hf N).ι
declarations.comment: for `I` finite, `Hilb^P_{X/B} ⟶ Hilb_{X/B}` is an open and closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relative_openImmersion_closedImmersion_numericalHilbertSubfunctor_ι_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
If every scheme étale over `B` is locally Noetherian (Stacks 03E2), then
`Hilb^P_{X/B} ⟶ Hilb_{X/B}` is an open and closed immersion, whatever the index set.
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_openImmersion_closedImmersion_numericalHilbertSubfunctor_ι_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y.1) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion.{u} ⊓
        @_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative uliftYoneda.{u + 1}
        (numericalHilbertSubfunctor f hf N).ι
declarations.comment: for `B` locally Noetherian, `Hilb^P_{X/B} ⟶ Hilb_{X/B}` is an open and closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hilbertPolynomialHilbertSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
`Hilb^{P, 𝓛}_{X/B}`: the case `I = ℤ`, `E_n = 𝓛^{⊗ n}` for an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `𝓛`,
the subfunctor of the Hilbert presheaf of the families `Z ⊆ X_T` whose object `(T, 𝒪_Z)` lies in
`Coh^{P, 𝓛}_{X/B}` of Stacks 0DNF: `P(n) = χ(X_t, 𝒪_{Z_t} ⊗ 𝓛_t^{⊗ n})` for every `n ∈ ℤ` and
every point `t` of `T`.  It is the inverse image of `Quot^{P, 𝓛}_{𝒪_X/X/B}` under
`Hilb_{X/B} = Quot_{𝒪_X/X/B}` (Stacks 0D00).
declarations.statement: alias hilbertPolynomialHilbertSubfunctor
declarations.comment: the notation `Hilb^{P, L}_{X/B}` for the case `I = ℤ`, `E_n = L^{⊗ n}`: the families `Z ⊆ X_T` with `P(n) = χ(X_t, 𝒪_{Z_t} ⊗ L_t^{⊗ n})` for all `n` and `t`, the inverse image of `Quot^{P, L}_{𝒪_X/X/B}` under `Hilb_{X/B} = Quot_{𝒪_X/X/B}`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relative_openImmersion_closedImmersion_hilbertPolynomialHilbertSubfunctor_ι
declarations.doc:
In the case `I = ℤ`, `E_n = 𝓛^{⊗ n}`, `Hilb^{P, 𝓛}_{X/B} ⟶ Hilb_{X/B}` is an open and
closed immersion, the base change of the open and closed substack `Coh^{P, 𝓛}_{X/B} ⊆ Coh_{X/B}`
of Stacks 0DNF.
declarations.comment: for `I = ℤ` and `E_n = L^{⊗ n}`, `Hilb^{P, L}_{X/B} ⟶ Hilb_{X/B}` is an open and closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_hilbertPolynomialHilbert_isProper
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of finite presentation of algebraic spaces (over
`Spec ℤ`), `L` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module ample on `X/Y` (Stacks 0D31) and `P` a numerical
polynomial. Then the algebraic space `Hilb^P_{X/Y}` parametrizing closed subschemes
having Hilbert polynomial `P` with respect to `L` is proper over `Y`: the subfunctor
`Hilb^{P, L}_{X/Y}` of the Hilbert presheaf has a model `M` in the universe of the site,
identified with it over `Y`, which is an algebraic space whose morphism to `Y` is proper.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hilbertPolynomialHilbert_isProper
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B integerBase B.contains_integerBase} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hprop : IsProper B integerBase B.contains_integerBase f.hom)
    (hf : IsFinitePresentation B integerBase B.contains_integerBase f.hom)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B integerBase B.contains_integerBase X.1 X.2)
    [hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
      (structurePresheaf B integerBase B.contains_integerBase X.1)
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B integerBase B.contains_integerBase X.1 X.2).O)).property L]
    (hamp : IsRelativelyAmple B integerBase B.contains_integerBase f L)
    {P : ℤ → ℤ} {p : Polynomial ℚ} (hP : ∀ m : ℤ, p.eval (m : ℚ) = (P m : ℚ)) :
    ∃ (M : (BigFppfOver B integerBase B.contains_integerBase)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (e : M ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} ≅ (hilbertPolynomialHilbert f hf L P).toFunctor)
      (q : M ⟶ Y.obj),
      Functor.whiskerRight q uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} =
          e.hom ≫ (hilbertPolynomialHilbert f hf L P).ι ≫ hilbertPresheafToBase f ∧
        IsAlgebraicSpace B integerBase B.contains_integerBase M ∧
        IsProper B integerBase B.contains_integerBase q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_hilbertPolynomialHilbert_isSeparated_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a separated morphism of finite presentation of algebraic spaces (over
`Spec ℤ`), `L` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module ample on `X/Y` (Stacks 0D31) and `P` a numerical
polynomial. Then the algebraic space `Hilb^P_{X/Y}` parametrizing closed subschemes having Hilbert
polynomial `P` with respect to `L` is separated and of finite presentation over `Y`: the subfunctor
`Hilb^{P, L}_{X/Y}` of the Hilbert presheaf has a model `M` in the universe of the site, identified
with it over `Y`, which is an algebraic space whose morphism to `Y` is separated and of finite
presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hilbertPolynomialHilbert_isSeparated_isFinitePresentation
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B integerBase B.contains_integerBase} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B integerBase B.contains_integerBase f.hom)
    (hf : IsFinitePresentation B integerBase B.contains_integerBase f.hom)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B integerBase B.contains_integerBase X.1 X.2)
    [hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
      (structurePresheaf B integerBase B.contains_integerBase X.1)
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B integerBase B.contains_integerBase X.1 X.2).O)).property L]
    (hamp : IsRelativelyAmple B integerBase B.contains_integerBase f L)
    {P : ℤ → ℤ} {p : Polynomial ℚ} (hP : ∀ m : ℤ, p.eval (m : ℚ) = (P m : ℚ)) :
    ∃ (M : (BigFppfOver B integerBase B.contains_integerBase)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (e : M ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} ≅ (hilbertPolynomialHilbert f hf L P).toFunctor)
      (q : M ⟶ Y.obj),
      Functor.whiskerRight q uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} =
          e.hom ≫ (hilbertPolynomialHilbert f hf L P).ι ≫ hilbertPresheafToBase f ∧
        IsAlgebraicSpace B integerBase B.contains_integerBase M ∧
        IsSeparated B integerBase B.contains_integerBase q ∧
        IsFinitePresentation B integerBase B.contains_integerBase q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmooth_picardStructureMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DPJ: the Picard stack is smooth in relative dimension `≤ 1`.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is flat, proper, of finite presentation (a field of the
standing datum `D`) and of relative dimension `≤ 1`. Then the structure morphism
`Picardstack_{X/Y} ⟶ Y` is smooth, as a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks; the Picard stack is
algebraic by Stacks 0D04.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_picardStructureMorphism (D : CoherentSituation B S hS)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS D.f.hom) (hproper : IsProper B S hS D.f.hom)
    (hd : HasRelativeDimensionLE 1 B S hS D.f.hom) :
    Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS
      (picardStructureMorphism D (isAlgebraicStack_picardCFG.{u, w} D hflat hproper))
declarations.comment: the full statement: f flat (hflat), proper (hproper), of finite presentation (the field of D) and of relative dimension ≤ 1 (hd); Picardstack_{X/B} → B is smooth; the algebraicity of Picardstack_{X/B} is Stacks 0D04, proved, not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpaceOver_and_isSmooth_picardFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The Picard functor is smooth in relative dimension `≤ 1`.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S` which is flat, of finite presentation and proper, with
`𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T,*}𝒪_{X_T}` an isomorphism for every scheme `T` over `Y` (the standing assumptions of
Section 0DMD), and of relative dimension `≤ 1`. Then `Pic_{X/Y}` is an algebraic space over `Y`
(Stacks 0D2C) and `Pic_{X/Y} ⟶ Y` is smooth: every algebraic space `H` with a morphism
`p : H ⟶ Y` whose functor of points over `Y` is identified with `Pic_{X/Y}` has `p` smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpaceOver_and_isSmooth_picardFunctor {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f.hom) (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (hstr : (PicardSituation.mk X Y f).StructureSheafMapIso)
    (hd : HasRelativeDimensionLE 1 B S hS f.hom) :
    IsAlgebraicSpaceOver (PicardSituation.mk X Y f).picardFunctor ∧
      ∀ (H : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (p : H ⟶ Y),
        Nonempty (spacePointsOver p ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} ≅
          (PicardSituation.mk X Y f).picardFunctor) →
        IsSmooth B S hS p.hom
declarations.comment: the full statement, in the setting of Section 0DMD: f flat (hflat), of finite presentation (hfp), proper (hproper), O_T -> f_{T,*}O_{X_T} an isomorphism for every T (hstr), of relative dimension ≤ 1 (hd); the conclusion contains that Pic_{X/B} is an algebraic space over B (Stacks 0D2C) and that its morphism to B is smooth, for every algebraic space representing it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.diagonal_relativeHomProjection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DPM.** The diagonal of `Mor_B(Y, X) ⟶ B` is a closed immersion of finite
presentation, for `Y ⟶ B` flat, proper and of finite presentation and `X ⟶ B` separated and of
finite presentation: it is representable by closed immersions of schemes locally of finite
presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem diagonal_relativeHomProjection (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS x)
    (hxfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS x) (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS z)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS z) (hproper : IsProper B S hS z) :
    (closedImmersionFinitePresentation (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS)).presheaf
      (pullback.diagonal (relativeHomProjection B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relativeHomProjection_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DPN.** Let `Q` be an algebraic space, `z : Z ⟶ Q` flat, proper and of finite
presentation and `x : X ⟶ Q` separated and of finite presentation, all algebraic spaces over `S`.
Then the projection `Mor_Q(Z, X) ⟶ Q` of the relative morphism functor is separated (its diagonal
is a closed immersion, Stacks 0DPM) and locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relativeHomProjection_unconditional
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS x) (hxfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS x)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS z) (hflat : IsFlat B S hS z)
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS z) :
    IsSeparated B S hS (relativeHomProjection B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ) ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (relativeHomProjection B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isomSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DPP,** the subfunctor `Isom_Q(Z, X) ⊆ Mor_Q(Z, X)` of relative isomorphisms: its
sections over a scheme `T` are the pairs `(a, b)` of Stacks 05Y1 at `T` whose morphism of base
changes `Z_T ⟶ X_T` is an isomorphism.

This is a subfunctor because the restriction maps of `Mor_Q(Z, X)` are restriction of pairs
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeHomSections_map`) and a restriction of a relative isomorphism
is a relative isomorphism.
declarations.statement: def isomSubfunctor : Subfunctor (relativeHom B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ)
declarations.comment: the subfunctor Isom_B(Y, X) of Mor_B(Y, X) of isomorphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenSubspace_isomSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DPP.** With `Z ⟶ Q` flat, proper and of finite presentation and `X ⟶ Q` proper,
the subfunctor `Isom_Q(Z, X) ⊆ Mor_Q(Z, X)` of relative isomorphisms is an open subspace.

This is the isomorphism locus of Stacks 05XD applied to the universal relative morphism, the
pair corresponding to the identity of `Mor_Q(Z, X)` under the bijection of Stacks 05Y3: the
source of that morphism is flat, locally of finite presentation and universally closed over
`Mor_Q(Z, X)` and its target is separated, locally of finite type and closed over
`Mor_Q(Z, X)`, both being base changes. A morphism from a scheme `T` factors through the locus
exactly when the base change of the universal morphism along it is an isomorphism, which is the
condition cutting out `Isom_Q(Z, X)`, so the locus *is* `Isom_Q(Z, X)`.

The algebraicity `hM` of `Mor_Q(Z, X)` is an explicit hypothesis: it is Stacks 0D1C, the standing
fact of the source's section, and the conclusion cannot do without it, because an open subspace
is in particular an algebraic space and the finite presentation and separatedness hypotheses on
`x` of the source's section enter the statement only through it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenSubspace_isomSubfunctor (hzfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS z)
    (hzflat : IsFlat B S hS z) (hzproper : IsProper B S hS z) (hxproper : IsProper B S hS x)
    (hM : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (relativeHom B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ)) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS (isomSubfunctor B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ)
declarations.comment: openness of the subfunctor of isomorphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenSubspace_isomSubfunctor_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
Let `Q` be an algebraic space and `z : Z ⟶ Q`, `x : X ⟶ Q` morphisms of algebraic spaces over
`S` with `z` flat, proper and of finite presentation and `x` proper and of finite presentation (in
particular separated, as in the standing data of Stacks 0DPL). Then the subfunctor
`Isom_Q(Z, X) ⊆ Mor_Q(Z, X)` of isomorphisms is an open subspace.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenSubspace_isomSubfunctor_of_isFinitePresentation
    (hx_fp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS x) (hx_proper : IsProper B S hS x)
    (hz_fp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS z) (hz_flat : IsFlat B S hS z)
    (hz_proper : IsProper B S hS z) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS (isomSubfunctor B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ)
declarations.comment: the subfunctor Isom_B(Y, X) of Mor_B(Y, X) of isomorphisms is an open subspace, for Y ⟶ B flat, proper and of finite presentation and X ⟶ B proper and of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.numericalRelativeHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DPQ,** the subfunctor `Mor^P_Q(Z, X) ⊆ Mor_Q(Z, X)`: its sections over a scheme `T`
are the pairs `(a, b)` of Stacks 05Y1 at `T` whose graph, a point of `Hilb_{Z ×_Q X / Q}` over
`T` by Stacks 0D1A, has the prescribed invariants.  Since the graph transformation is the
inclusion `Mor_Q(Z, X) ⊆ Hilb_{Z ×_Q X / Q}` of Stacks 0D1B, this is the intersection
`Mor_Q(Z, X) ∩ Hilb^P_{Z ×_Q X / Q}` of the source, formed as an inverse image.

This is a subfunctor because the restriction maps of `Mor_Q(Z, X)` go to base change of graphs
and the condition on the invariants is stable under base change.
declarations.statement: def numericalRelativeHom : Subfunctor (relativeHom B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ)
declarations.comment: the definition of `Mor^P_B(Y, X)` as the subfunctor of `Mor_B(Y, X)` of relative morphisms whose graph has the prescribed invariants, with the open subspace of a test scheme that tests the source's open immersion for a finite index set; that `Mor^P_B(Y, X) ⟶ Mor_B(Y, X)` is a flat closed immersion rests on Lemmas 0DND and 0DNE, which are assertions about a morphism of algebraic stacks and are unavailable in this development, and is not stated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.numericalSituationRelativeHom
declarations.doc:
The subfunctor `Mor^P_Q(Z, X) = Mor_Q(Z, X) ∩ Hilb^P_{Z ×_Q X / Q}`. For the standing data `N`
of Situation 0DNC on `Z ×_Q X ⟶ Q` (a set `I`, perfect objects `E_i` of `D(𝒪_{Z ×_Q X})` and
`P : I → ℤ`), the subfunctor of `Mor_Q(Z, X)` of the relative morphisms over `T` whose graph `W`, a
point of `Hilb_{Z ×_Q X / Q}` by Stacks 0D1A and 0D1B, lies in `Hilb^P_{Z ×_Q X / Q}` of Stacks
0DPG: `χ(K_i ⊗^𝐋 κ(t)) = P(i)` for `K_i = Rf_{T,*}(E_{i,T} ⊗^𝐋 𝒪_W)`, every `i ∈ I` and every point
`t` of `T`.
declarations.statement: abbrev numericalSituationRelativeHom : Subfunctor (relativeHom B S hS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ)
declarations.comment: the definition `Mor^P_B(Y, X) = Mor_B(Y, X) ∩ Hilb^P_{Y ×_B X/B}`, for the numerical invariants `χ(K_i ⊗^𝐋 κ(t))` of Situation 0DNC on `Y ×_B X ⟶ B`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_and_isClosedImmersion_numericalSituationRelativeHom_ι
declarations.doc: The morphism `Mor^P_Q(Z, X) ⟶ Mor_Q(Z, X)` is a flat closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_and_isClosedImmersion_numericalSituationRelativeHom_ι :
    IsFlat B S hS (numericalSituationRelativeHom B S hS hsep hx_fp hfp hflat hproper N).ι ∧
      IsClosedImmersion B S hS
        (numericalSituationRelativeHom B S hS hsep hx_fp hfp hflat hproper N).ι
declarations.comment: `Mor^P_B(Y, X) ⟶ Mor_B(Y, X)` is a flat closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenImmersion_and_isClosedImmersion_numericalSituationRelativeHom_ι
declarations.doc: For `I` finite the morphism `Mor^P_Q(Z, X) ⟶ Mor_Q(Z, X)` is an open and closed immersion.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_and_isFinitePresentation_relativeHomHilbertPolynomial
declarations.doc:
Let `Q` be an algebraic space over `Spec ℤ`, `z : Z ⟶ Q` flat, proper and of finite
presentation, `x : X ⟶ Q` separated and of finite presentation, `N` an invertible module ample on
`Z/Q` and `L` an invertible module ample on `X/Q` (Stacks 0D31), and `P` a numerical polynomial.
Then for `ℳ = pr₁^*N ⊗ pr₂^*L` on `Z ×_Q X` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.graphAmbientTensor`),
`Mor^{P, ℳ}_Q(Z, X)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeHomHilbertPolynomial`) is an algebraic
space and its morphism to `Q` is separated and of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_and_isFinitePresentation_relativeHomHilbertPolynomial
    {Z X Q : (BigFppfOver B integerBase ℤS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {z : Z ⟶ Q} {x : X ⟶ Q}
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B integerBase ℤS Z) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B integerBase ℤS X)
    (hQ : IsAlgebraicSpace B integerBase ℤS Q)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B integerBase ℤS x) (hxfp : IsFinitePresentation B integerBase ℤS x)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B integerBase ℤS z) (hflat : IsFlat B integerBase ℤS z)
    (hproper : IsProper B integerBase ℤS z)
    (N : Modules.{u, u} B integerBase ℤS Z hZ)
    [hNi : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structurePresheaf B integerBase ℤS Z)
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B integerBase ℤS Z hZ).O)).property N]
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B integerBase ℤS X hX)
    [hLi : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structurePresheaf B integerBase ℤS X)
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B integerBase ℤS X hX).O)).property L]
    (hN : IsRelativelyAmple B integerBase ℤS
      (ObjectProperty.homMk z : (⟨Z, hZ⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B integerBase ℤS) ⟶ ⟨Q, hQ⟩) N)
    (hL : IsRelativelyAmple B integerBase ℤS
      (ObjectProperty.homMk x : (⟨X, hX⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B integerBase ℤS) ⟶ ⟨Q, hQ⟩) L)
    {P : ℤ → ℤ} {p : Polynomial ℚ} (hP : ∀ m : ℤ, p.eval (m : ℚ) = (P m : ℚ)) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B integerBase ℤS (relativeHomHilbertPolynomial hZ hX hQ hsep hxfp hfp hflat
        hproper (graphAmbientTensor z x hZ hX hQ N L) P).toFunctor ∧
      IsSeparated B integerBase ℤS ((relativeHomHilbertPolynomial hZ hX hQ hsep hxfp hfp hflat
        hproper (graphAmbientTensor z x hZ hX hQ N L) P).ι ≫
          relativeHomProjection B integerBase ℤS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ) ∧
      IsFinitePresentation B integerBase ℤS ((relativeHomHilbertPolynomial hZ hX hQ hsep hxfp hfp
        hflat hproper (graphAmbientTensor z x hZ hX hQ N L) P).ι ≫
          relativeHomProjection B integerBase ℤS Z X Q z x hZ hX hQ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.diagonal_polarizedStackUnconditional_isSeparated_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DPT.** The diagonal `Δ : 𝒫olarized ⟶ 𝒫olarized × 𝒫olarized` of the stack of
polarized proper flat families of finite presentation, over the big fppf site of a terminal base
scheme, is separated and of finite presentation, both read as in Properties of Stacks,
Section 04XB: `Δ` is representable by algebraic spaces (Stacks 0D42), and every algebraic space
representing its base change along a scheme-valued point over a scheme `U` is separated (Stacks
03HL) and of finite presentation (Stacks 03XP, part (3)) over `U`, read over the base (Stacks
04SG).
declarations.statement:
theorem diagonal_polarizedStackUnconditional_isSeparated_isFinitePresentation :
    Stack.HasRepresentableDiagonal B S hS (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT) ∧
      Stack.IsSeparated B S hS
        (Stack.diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT)) ∧
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.product (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT)
            (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT)).val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ (CatFiberedInGroupoids.product (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT)
            (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT)).val.p = Over.map U.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT).val.p
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.product (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT)
              (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT)).val.p y
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor
              (Stack.diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT))))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.IsFinitePresentation B S hS
          (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ComplexesSituation.complexesIsom_finitePresentation_and_affine_overQuasiCompactNegativeExtLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DPW, corrected: the diagonal of `Complexes_{X/B}` over `B` is quasi-affine and of
finite presentation.**  Let `f : X ⟶ B` be proper, flat and of finite presentation
(Situation 0DLE), and let `x = (T, E)`, `y = (T, E')` be objects of `Complexes_{X/B}` over the
same scheme `T` and the same morphism `T ⟶ B`, so that `E`, `E'` are `B`-perfect objects of
`D(𝒪_{X_T})` with vanishing negative self-Exts on the fibres; the base change of the diagonal of
`Complexes_{X/B}` over `B` along the `T`-point `(x, y)` of `Complexes_{X/B} ×_B Complexes_{X/B}`
is `Isom(x, y)`.  Then:

1. the presheaf `Isom(x, y)` on `(Sch/T)` is the relative derived Isom functor
   `T' ↦ Isom(E_{T'}, E'_{T'})` of `X_T ⟶ T`;
2. it is an algebraic space of finite presentation over `T`: the diagonal of `Complexes_{X/B}`
   over `B` is representable by algebraic spaces and of finite presentation;
3. the opens `W(E, E')` and `W(E', E)` of `T` of Stacks 0DLC, part (1), exist;
4. for these opens (`W(E, E')`: the field points `y` of `T` with `Ext^i(E_y, E'_y) = 0` for
   `i < 0`, and symmetrically), the inclusion of `W(E, E') ∩ W(E', E)` into `T` is
   quasi-compact, and `Isom(x, y)` factors through this open and is affine and of finite
   presentation over it.

**This is the corrected form of Stacks 0DPW**, not the statement as written.  The source asserts
that the diagonal is affine and of finite presentation; the "affine" part is false (its proof
applies Stacks 0DLC, part (3), as if `W(E, E')` were all of `T`): for `X = P¹` over `A²_k`,
`E = [O(-2) --s--> O]` with `s = a(x² - y²) + bxy` and `E' = E ⊗ O(2)`, `Isom(E, E')` is empty
over the origin and has a section over `A² ∖ 0`, so it is not affine over `A²`.
declarations.statement:
theorem complexesIsom_finitePresentation_and_affine_overQuasiCompactNegativeExtLocus :
    Nonempty ((complexesFunctor D).isomPresheaf ⟨A, rfl⟩ ⟨sameTest A E' h₁ h₂, rfl⟩ ≅
      (overSchemeTest A.T.left).op ⋙ relativeDerivedIsomFunctor (D.projection A.T) A.E E') ∧
    IsFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOver ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).obj A.T.left)
      (relativeDerivedIsomFunctor (D.projection A.T) A.E E') ∧
    (∃ W₁ : OpenSubspaces B S hS ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).obj A.T.left).1,
      IsNegativeExtLocus (D.projection A.T) A.E E' W₁) ∧
    (∃ W₂ : OpenSubspaces B S hS ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).obj A.T.left).1,
      IsNegativeExtLocus (D.projection A.T) E' A.E W₂) ∧
    ∀ (W₁ W₂ : OpenSubspaces B S hS ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).obj A.T.left).1),
      IsNegativeExtLocus (D.projection A.T) A.E E' W₁ →
      IsNegativeExtLocus (D.projection A.T) E' A.E W₂ →
      IsQuasiCompact B S hS (openSubspaceImmersion B S hS ⟨W₁.1 ⊓ W₂.1,
          isOpenSubspace_inf B S hS ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).obj A.T.left).2 W₁.1 W₂.1
            W₁.2 W₂.2⟩).hom ∧
      (∀ T' : SchemesOver ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).obj A.T.left),
        Nonempty ((relativeDerivedIsomFunctor (D.projection A.T) A.E E').obj (op T')) →
          ∃ t : (schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).obj T'.left ⟶ openSubspaceAsSpace B S hS ⟨W₁.1 ⊓ W₂.1,
          isOpenSubspace_inf B S hS ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).obj A.T.left).2 W₁.1 W₂.1
            W₁.2 W₂.2⟩,
            t ≫ openSubspaceImmersion B S hS ⟨W₁.1 ⊓ W₂.1,
          isOpenSubspace_inf B S hS ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).obj A.T.left).2 W₁.1 W₂.1
            W₁.2 W₂.2⟩ = T'.hom) ∧
      IsAffineFinitePresentationAlgebraicSpaceOver (openSubspaceAsSpace B S hS ⟨W₁.1 ⊓ W₂.1,
          isOpenSubspace_inf B S hS ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).obj A.T.left).2 W₁.1 W₂.1
            W₁.2 W₂.2⟩)
        ((CostructuredArrow.map (S := schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS)
          (openSubspaceImmersion B S hS ⟨W₁.1 ⊓ W₂.1,
          isOpenSubspace_inf B S hS ((schemeSpaceFunctor B S hS).obj A.T.left).2 W₁.1 W₂.1
            W₁.2 W₂.2⟩)).op ⋙
          relativeDerivedIsomFunctor (D.projection A.T) A.E E')
declarations.comment: Corrected statement (Stacks erratum): the source asserts that the diagonal of Complexes_{X/B} over B is affine and of finite presentation; the 'affine' part is false (counterexample: X = P^1 over A^2_k with complexes E = [O(-2) -s-> O], s = a(x^2 - y^2) + bxy, and E' = E ⊗ O(2), for which Isom(E, E') is empty over the origin and has a section over A^2 minus the origin, so is not affine over A^2). Formalized: the diagonal over B is representable by algebraic spaces and of finite presentation, and for (T, E), (T, E') the functor Isom(E, E') factors through the open W(E, E') ∩ W(E', E) of 0DLC, whose inclusion into T is quasi-compact, and is affine and of finite presentation over it; so the diagonal is quasi-affine and of finite presentation.

declarations.comment: open immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedImmersion_polarizedCurvesToPolarized_unconditional
declarations.doc: The projection `PolarizedCurves ⟶ 𝒫olarized` is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_polarizedCurvesToPolarized_unconditional :
    Stack.IsClosedImmersion B integerBase hZ (polarizedCurvesToPolarizedUnconditionalUp B hZ)
declarations.comment: closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSmooth_and_isSurjective_polarizedCurvesToCurves
declarations.doc:
The projection `PolarizedCurves ⟶ 𝒞urves` is smooth and surjective.

The 1-morphism is `AlgebraicGeometry.polarizedCurvesToCurvesAlgebraicOfPolarized`, the projection
of the 2-fibre product `PolarizedCurves = 𝒞urves ×_{𝒮paces'_{fp, flat, proper}} 𝒫olarized` of
Stacks 0DPY, read in the 2-category of algebraic stacks of Stacks 03YP; smoothness is Stacks 075U
and surjectivity is Stacks 04ZS.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_and_isSurjective_polarizedCurvesToCurves :
    Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B integerBase hZ
        (polarizedCurvesToCurvesAlgebraicOfPolarized B hZ
          (polarizedCurvesToCurves_isAlgebraic_smooth_surjective.{w, u} B hZ).2.1.1
          (curvesFiberedCategory_isAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B hZ)) ∧
      Stack.IsSurjective B integerBase hZ
        (polarizedCurvesToCurvesAlgebraicOfPolarized B hZ
          (polarizedCurvesToCurves_isAlgebraic_smooth_surjective.{w, u} B hZ).2.1.1
          (curvesFiberedCategory_isAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B hZ))

declarations.name: numberOfBranches_eq_of_isLocalization_smooth
declarations.doc:
A local homomorphism of local rings which is a localization of a smooth ring map preserves
the number of geometric branches. If its residue-field extension is purely inseparable, it also
preserves the number of branches.

The source's two rings carry independent universes, together with their henselizations and
strict henselizations: `A`, `Aʰ`, `Aˢʰ` in one and `B`, `Bʰ`, `Bˢʰ` in the other, and the two
separable closures in two more. The universe work is done by
`StacksDraft.henselization_tensorProduct_at_unique_prime` and
`StacksDraft.strictHenselization_tensorProduct_at_induced_prime`, the source-strength forms of
tags 08HU and 08HV, and by the ind-étale layer they are built on, which lets the branch-counting
lemmas above be stated with the base and its henselization in independent universes.
declarations.statement:
theorem numberOfBranches_eq_of_isLocalization_smooth
    (A Ah Ash : Type uA) (B Bh Bsh : Type uB) (kAsep : Type vA) (kBsep : Type vB)
    [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (hsm : ∃ (C : Type uC) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra A C) (_ : Algebra C B)
      (_ : IsScalarTower A C B) (S : Submonoid C),
        Algebra.Smooth A C ∧ IsLocalization S B)
    [CommRing Ah] [IsLocalRing Ah] [Algebra A Ah]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) Ah]
    [CommRing Bh] [IsLocalRing Bh] [Algebra B Bh]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization B (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) Bh]
    [Field kAsep] [Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) kAsep]
    [IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) kAsep]
    [CommRing Ash] [IsLocalRing Ash] [Algebra A Ash]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization A kAsep Ash]
    [Field kBsep] [Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) kBsep]
    [IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) kBsep]
    [CommRing Bsh] [IsLocalRing Bsh] [Algebra B Bsh]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization B kBsep Bsh] :
    numberOfGeometricBranches A kAsep Ash = numberOfGeometricBranches B kBsep Bsh ∧
      ((IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map (algebraMap A B)).IsPurelyInseparable →
        numberOfBranches A Ah = numberOfBranches B Bh)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.numberOfGeometricBranches_eq_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DQ2.** A smooth morphism of schemes preserves the number of geometric
branches at a point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem numberOfGeometricBranches_eq_of_smooth {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Smooth f]
    (x : X) :
    numberOfGeometricBranches X x = numberOfGeometricBranches S (f.base x)
declarations.comment: geometric_branches

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.numberOfBranches_eq_of_smooth_of_isPurelyInseparable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DQ2.** A smooth morphism of schemes preserves the number of branches
at a point whose residue field is a purely inseparable extension of the residue field of its
image.
declarations.statement:
public theorem numberOfBranches_eq_of_smooth_of_isPurelyInseparable {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [Smooth f] (x : X)
    (h : (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.IsPurelyInseparable) :
    numberOfBranches X x = numberOfBranches S (f.base x)
declarations.comment: branches_purely_inseparable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.minimalPrimeCount_iff_componentCount
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DQ3, conditions (1) and (2).** A point of a presheaf on the big fppf site has
minimal-prime count `n` on its étale scheme charts exactly when it has irreducible-component
count `n` on them: the two counts agree at each chart point separately.
declarations.statement:
theorem minimalPrimeCount_iff_componentCount (x : points B S hS F) (n : ℕ) :
    HasMinimalPrimeCount B S hS x n ↔ HasComponentCount B S hS x n
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.componentCount_iff_branchCount
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DQ3, conditions (2) and (3).** A point of a presheaf on the big fppf site has
irreducible-component count `n` on its étale scheme charts exactly when it has branch count `n`
on them.

No algebraicity hypothesis is needed: both directions only use that an étale neighbourhood of a
point of a chart above `x` is refined by an open subscheme of a chart above `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem componentCount_iff_branchCount (x : points B S hS F) (n : ℕ) :
    HasComponentCount B S hS x n ↔ HasBranchCount B S hS x n
declarations.comment: conditions (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.branchCount_iff_geometricBranchCount
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DQ3, conditions (3) and (4).** A point of an algebraic space has branch count `n`
on its étale scheme charts exactly when every chart has exactly `n` geometric branches at every
point above it.
declarations.statement:
theorem branchCount_iff_geometricBranchCount (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (x : points B S hS F) (n : ℕ) :
    HasBranchCount B S hS x n ↔ HasGeometricBranchCount B S hS x n
declarations.comment: conditions (3) and (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.geometricBranchCount_iff_etaleLocalRingMinimalPrimeCount
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DQ3, conditions (4) and (5).** Every étale scheme chart of an algebraic space has
exactly `n` geometric branches at every point above `x` exactly when the étale local ring at
every geometric point above `x` has exactly `n` minimal primes.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricBranchCount_iff_etaleLocalRingMinimalPrimeCount
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (x : points B S hS F) (n : ℕ) :
    HasGeometricBranchCount B S hS x n ↔
      HasEtaleLocalRingMinimalPrimeCount B S hS x n
declarations.comment: conditions (4) and (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.numberOfGeometricBranches
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DQ4.** The number of geometric branches of an algebraic space at a point: the
natural number satisfying the equivalent conditions of Tag 0DQ3 if there is one, and `⊤`
otherwise.
declarations.statement: def numberOfGeometricBranches (x : points B S hS F) : ℕ∞

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.numberOfGeometricBranches_eq_nat_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DQ4.** A finite value of the number of geometric branches of an algebraic space at
a point is exactly the value appearing in the equivalent conditions of Tag 0DQ3.
declarations.statement:
theorem numberOfGeometricBranches_eq_nat_iff (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (x : points B S hS F) (n : ℕ) :
    numberOfGeometricBranches B S hS x = (n : ℕ∞) ↔ HasGeometricBranchCount B S hS x n
declarations.comment: finite value

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.numberOfGeometricBranches_eq_top_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DQ4.** The number of geometric branches of an algebraic space at a point is
infinite exactly when no natural number satisfies the equivalent conditions of Tag 0DQ3.
declarations.statement:
theorem numberOfGeometricBranches_eq_top_iff (x : points B S hS F) :
    numberOfGeometricBranches B S hS x = ⊤ ↔
      ∀ n : ℕ, ¬ HasGeometricBranchCount B S hS x n
declarations.comment: infinite value

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.forall_existsUnique_minimalPrimes_iff_forall_existsUnique_component
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DQ6, conditions (1) and (2).** The local ring of every elementary étale
neighbourhood of `x` at its distinguished point has a unique minimal prime exactly when exactly
one irreducible component of every such neighbourhood passes through its distinguished point.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_existsUnique_minimalPrimes_iff_forall_existsUnique_component :
    (∀ U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX x,
        ∃! q : Ideal (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point),
          q ∈ minimalPrimes (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point)) ↔
      ∀ U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX x,
        ∃! Z : irreducibleComponents U.scheme.left.1,
          U.point ∈ (Z : Set U.scheme.left.1)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.forall_existsUnique_component_iff_forall_isUnibranchAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DQ6, conditions (2) and (3).** Exactly one irreducible component of every
elementary étale neighbourhood of `x` passes through its distinguished point exactly when the
