    (h𝒯Irreducible : @IrreducibleSpace _ (pointTopology B S hS 𝒯.val))
    (h𝒳QuasiSeparated : IsQuasiSeparatedAbs.{u, w, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    {P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj} (hP : IsSchemeTheoreticImage f P) :
    ∀ t : points B S hS 𝒯.val.val 𝒯.val.property,
      dimension B S hS 𝒯 h𝒯 ≤
        closedSubstackDimension B S hS 𝒳 P hP.1 hP.isAlgebraicStack h𝒳 +
          relativeStackDimensionAt.{u, w} B S hS f hf h𝒯 h𝒳 t
declarations.comment: the inequality clause, for every f (no quasi-compactness), under the hypotheses of the statement in the Stacks Project other than quasi-compactness of f. The equality clause needs f quasi-compact and is registered on AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.dimension_le_add_and_exists_isOpen_dense_eq_add_relativeStackDimensionAt_of_isQuasiCompactMorphism; without quasi-compactness it is refuted by AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.not_forall_dimension_le_add_and_exists_isOpen_dense_eq

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.classifyingStack_multiplicativeGroup_dimension_lt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DS5**, the example `[Spec k/𝐆_m] ⟶ Spec k`. Let `k` be a field. The classifying
stack `[Spec k/𝐆_m]` is an algebraic stack, of which a model `𝒬` in the 2-category of algebraic
stacks over `Spec k` exists; and for every such model, the structure morphism `f : 𝒬 ⟶ Spec k`
satisfies the hypotheses of Stacks 0DS4 — it is quasi-compact and locally of finite type, `𝒬` and
`Spec k` are Jacobson, pseudo-catenary and locally Noetherian, `|𝒬|` is irreducible and `Spec k` is
quasi-separated — its scheme theoretic image is all of `Spec k`, of dimension `0`, while
`dim 𝒬 = -1`, so that `dim 𝒬 < dim 𝒵`; and the fibre dimension `dim_t(𝒬_{f(t)})` of Stacks 0DRL is
`-1 < 0` at every point `t` of `𝒬`.
declarations.statement:
theorem classifyingStack_multiplicativeGroup_dimension_lt :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C (Spec (.of k)) hk
        (classifyingStack C hk (multiplicativeGroupOverField C hk)).val ∧
      (∃ 𝒬 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} C (Spec (.of k)) hk, Nonempty
        (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (classifyingStack C hk (multiplicativeGroupOverField C hk)).val.p 𝒬.val.val.p)) ∧
      ∀ (𝒬 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} C (Spec (.of k)) hk)
        (_e : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (classifyingStack C hk (multiplicativeGroupOverField C hk)).val.p 𝒬.val.val.p),
        ∃ (h𝒯 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} C (Spec (.of k)) hk 𝒬)
          (h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} C (Spec (.of k)) hk (specFieldStack.{u, w} C hk))
          (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFiniteType C (Spec (.of k)) hk (toSpecFieldStack C hk 𝒬))
          (hP : IsSchemeTheoreticImage (toSpecFieldStack C hk 𝒬) ⊤),
          IsQuasiCompactMorphism C (Spec (.of k)) hk (toSpecFieldStack C hk 𝒬) ∧
          AlgebraicStacks.IsJacobson C (Spec (.of k)) hk 𝒬 ∧
          AlgebraicStacks.IsJacobson C (Spec (.of k)) hk (specFieldStack.{u, w} C hk) ∧
          AlgebraicStacks.IsPseudoCatenary C (Spec (.of k)) hk 𝒬 ∧
          AlgebraicStacks.IsPseudoCatenary C (Spec (.of k)) hk (specFieldStack.{u, w} C hk) ∧
          @IrreducibleSpace _ (pointTopology C (Spec (.of k)) hk 𝒬.val) ∧
          IsQuasiSeparatedAbs.{u, w, w} C (Spec (.of k)) hk (specFieldStack.{u, w} C hk) ∧
          closedSubstackDimension C (Spec (.of k)) hk (specFieldStack.{u, w} C hk) ⊤ hP.1
            hP.isAlgebraicStack h𝒳 = 0 ∧
          dimension C (Spec (.of k)) hk 𝒬 h𝒯 = ((-1 : ℤ) : EInt) ∧
          dimension C (Spec (.of k)) hk 𝒬 h𝒯 <
            closedSubstackDimension C (Spec (.of k)) hk (specFieldStack.{u, w} C hk) ⊤ hP.1
              hP.isAlgebraicStack h𝒳 ∧
          ∀ t : points C (Spec (.of k)) hk 𝒬.val.val 𝒬.val.property,
            relativeStackDimensionAt.{u, w} C (Spec (.of k)) hk (toSpecFieldStack C hk 𝒬) hf h𝒯
                h𝒳 t =
              ((-1 : ℤ) : EInt)
declarations.comment: the example [Spec k/G_m] → Spec k: it need not be that dim T ≥ dim Z, the fibres having negative dimension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiDMAbs_and_zero_le_dimensionAtPoint_fieldFibreStackSquare
declarations.doc:
Let `f : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳` be a quasi-DM 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`, locally of finite type,
and let `p` be a field-valued point of `𝒳` with field spectrum `Spec k`. Then the fibre
`𝒯 ×_𝒳 Spec k` of `f` over `p` is a quasi-DM algebraic stack (Stacks 050D, part (6)), and hence has
non-negative dimension at every one of its points; so, when it is nonempty, its dimension of Stacks
0AFP is non-negative.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDMAbs_and_zero_le_dimensionAtPoint_fieldFibreStackSquare
    {𝒯 𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hqdm : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS f)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val.val) :
    IsQuasiDMAbs.{u, w, w} B S hS (fieldFibreStackSquare B S hS f p).pt ∧
      (∀ x : points B S hS (fieldFibreStackSquare B S hS f p).pt.val.val
          (fieldFibreStackSquare B S hS f p).pt.val.property,
        0 ≤ dimensionAtPoint B S hS (fieldFibreStackSquare B S hS f p).pt
          (isLocallyNoetherianStack_fieldFibreStackSquare.{u, w} B S hS f hf p) x) ∧
      (Nonempty (points B S hS (fieldFibreStackSquare B S hS f p).pt.val.val
          (fieldFibreStackSquare B S hS f p).pt.val.property) →
        0 ≤ dimension B S hS (fieldFibreStackSquare B S hS f p).pt
          (isLocallyNoetherianStack_fieldFibreStackSquare.{u, w} B S hS f hf p))
declarations.comment: the fibres of a quasi-DM 1-morphism are quasi-DM algebraic stacks, hence of non-negative dimension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.zero_le_relativeStackDimensionAt_and_closedSubstackDimension_le_dimension
declarations.doc:
Let `f : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳` be a quasi-compact, locally of finite type 1-morphism of Jacobson,
pseudo-catenary, locally Noetherian algebraic stacks over `S`, whose source is irreducible and
whose target is quasi-separated, and let `𝒵 ↪ 𝒳`, cut out by `P`, be the scheme theoretic image of
`f` — the situation of Stacks 0DS4. If `f` is moreover quasi-DM, then its fibres have non-negative
dimension, `dim_t(𝒯_{f(t)}) ≥ 0` at every `t ∈ |𝒯|`, and Stacks 0DS4 then gives `dim 𝒵 ≤ dim 𝒯`.
declarations.statement:
theorem zero_le_relativeStackDimensionAt_and_closedSubstackDimension_le_dimension
    {𝒯 𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hfQC : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hDM : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS f)
    (h𝒯 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒯)
    (h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (h𝒯Jacobson : AlgebraicStacks.IsJacobson B S hS 𝒯)
    (h𝒳Jacobson : AlgebraicStacks.IsJacobson B S hS 𝒳)
    (h𝒯Catenary : AlgebraicStacks.IsPseudoCatenary B S hS 𝒯)
    (h𝒳Catenary : AlgebraicStacks.IsPseudoCatenary B S hS 𝒳)
    (h𝒯Irreducible : @IrreducibleSpace _ (pointTopology B S hS 𝒯.val))
    (h𝒳QuasiSeparated : IsQuasiSeparatedAbs.{u, w, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    {P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj} (hP : IsSchemeTheoreticImage f P) :
    (∀ t : points B S hS 𝒯.val.val 𝒯.val.property,
        0 ≤ relativeStackDimensionAt B S hS f hf h𝒯 h𝒳 t) ∧
      closedSubstackDimension B S hS 𝒳 P hP.1 hP.isAlgebraicStack h𝒳 ≤
        dimension B S hS 𝒯 h𝒯
declarations.comment: in the quasi-DM case the lemma implies dim T ≥ dim Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.closedSubstackDimension_le_dimension_of_isQuasiCompactMorphism
declarations.doc:
**The inequality of Stacks 0DS6.** For a quasi-compact, locally of finite type, quasi-DM
1-morphism `f : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳` of Jacobson, pseudo-catenary, locally Noetherian algebraic stacks over
`S`, with `|𝒯|` irreducible and `𝒳` quasi-separated, and `P` cutting out the scheme theoretic
image `𝒵` of `f`, one has `dim(𝒵) ≤ dim(𝒯)`.

At a point of the nonempty open subset of `|𝒯|` on which
`dim(𝒯) = dim(𝒵) + dim_t(𝒯_{f(t)})` (Stacks 0DS4 for a quasi-compact `f`), the fibre dimension
is non-negative because `f` is quasi-DM.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedSubstackDimension_le_dimension_of_isQuasiCompactMorphism
    {𝒯 𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hfQC : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hDM : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS f)
    (h𝒯 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒯)
    (h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (h𝒯Jacobson : AlgebraicStacks.IsJacobson B S hS 𝒯)
    (h𝒳Jacobson : AlgebraicStacks.IsJacobson B S hS 𝒳)
    (h𝒯Catenary : AlgebraicStacks.IsPseudoCatenary B S hS 𝒯)
    (h𝒳Catenary : AlgebraicStacks.IsPseudoCatenary B S hS 𝒳)
    (h𝒯Irreducible : @IrreducibleSpace _ (pointTopology B S hS 𝒯.val))
    (h𝒳QuasiSeparated : IsQuasiSeparatedAbs.{u, w, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    {P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj} (hP : IsSchemeTheoreticImage f P) :
    closedSubstackDimension B S hS 𝒳 P hP.1 hP.isAlgebraicStack h𝒳 ≤ dimension B S hS 𝒯 h𝒯
declarations.comment: the first clause, dim Z ≤ dim T, under exactly the hypotheses of the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.closedSubstackDimension_le_dimension_and_xor_relativeDimension_pos_of_ne_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DS6**, for `𝒯` of finite dimension. Let `f : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳` be a quasi-compact, locally of
finite type 1-morphism of Jacobson, pseudo-catenary, locally Noetherian algebraic stacks over `S`
which is quasi-DM, whose source is irreducible and whose target is quasi-separated, and let
`𝒵 ↪ 𝒳`, cut out by `P`, be the scheme theoretic image of `f`. Suppose `dim(𝒯) ≠ ∞`. Then
`dim(𝒵) ≤ dim(𝒯)`, and exactly one of the following holds: (1) `dim_t(𝒯_{f(t)}) > 0` at every
finite type point `t ∈ |𝒯|`, in which case `dim(𝒵) < dim(𝒯)`; or (2) `dim(𝒯) = dim(𝒵)`.

**Erratum.** The source states the lemma without the hypothesis `dim(𝒯) ≠ ∞`, and as written
it is false when `dim(𝒯) = dim(𝒵) = ∞`. Let `N` be Nagata's Noetherian ring of infinite dimension
(Stacks, Examples, Tag 02JC), let `D = N⟨X⟩` be the localization of `N[X]` at the monic
polynomials, and let `f : 𝔸¹_D ⟶ Spec D` be the projection.
* Every hypothesis holds. `N` is regular, its local rings being localizations of polynomial rings,
  so `D` is a Noetherian regular domain, hence Cohen–Macaulay and universally catenary
  (Stacks 00NM), and `D[s]` is as well. `D` is Jacobson by J. W. Brewer and W. J. Heinzer,
  *R Noetherian implies R⟨X⟩ is a Hilbert ring*, J. Algebra 67 (1980) 204–209,
  doi:10.1016/0021-8693(80)90317-8; so is `D[s]`, being of finite type over `D`. `𝔸¹_D` is
  irreducible, `f` is affine, hence quasi-compact and representable, hence quasi-DM, and of finite
  type, and `Spec D` is affine, hence quasi-separated.
* Both alternatives hold. `f` is faithfully flat, so its scheme theoretic image is `Spec D`. Every
  fibre is an affine line over a field, so `dim_t(𝒯_{f(t)}) = 1 > 0` everywhere. The primes
  `p_i N[X]` contain no monic polynomial and have unbounded height, so
  `dim(𝒯) = dim(𝒵) = ∞`. Thus (1) and (2) hold together, and (1) does not force
  `dim(𝒵) < dim(𝒯)`.

This counterexample is machine-checked:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.not_forall_xor_relativeDimension_pos`, in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/DimensionSchemeTheoreticImageCounterexample0DS6.lean`,
proves that the statement below without `h𝒯Finite` is false, every hypothesis of the source
(quasi-compactness of `f` included) being proved for this `f`.

Infinite-dimensional Noetherian Hilbert domains were first constructed by K. Fujita, *Infinite
dimensional Noetherian Hilbert domains*, Hiroshima Math. J. 5 (1975) 181–185,
doi:10.32917/hmj/1206136627. The source's arithmetic presupposes finiteness: Stacks 0DS4, from
which it derives this lemma, is stated as `dim_t(𝒯_{f(t)}) ≥ dim 𝒯 - dim 𝒵`, and the proof as
`dim_t(𝒯_{f(t)}) = dim_t 𝒯 - dim_{f(t)} 𝒵`, differences that are undefined when both dimensions
are infinite; Stacks 0DRT, on which Stacks 0DRX rests, assumes finite dimension explicitly. With
no finiteness hypothesis, what holds is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.closedSubstackDimension_le_dimension_and_xor_relativeDimension_pos`:
`dim(𝒵) ≤ dim(𝒯)` and `Xor ((1) ∧ dim(𝒵) < dim(𝒯)) (2)`.

The proof: Stacks 0DS4 for a quasi-compact `f` gives `dim(𝒯) ≤ dim(𝒵) + dim_t(𝒯_{f(t)})` at
every point, with equality on a nonempty open subset `W` of `|𝒯|`; the fibre dimensions are
non-negative integers because `f` is quasi-DM. The open `W` contains a finite type point `t`,
`𝒯` being Jacobson (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isFiniteTypePoint_mem_of_isOpen`). Under (1)
the fibre dimension at `t` is a positive integer, so `dim(𝒵) < dim(𝒯)` because `dim(𝒯)` is finite
— it is neither `∞`, by hypothesis, nor `-∞`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.dimensionAtPoint_ne_bot`; hence (1) excludes (2). If (2) fails, then
(1) holds by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.closedSubstackDimension_le_dimension_and_xor_relativeDimension_pos`.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedSubstackDimension_le_dimension_and_xor_relativeDimension_pos_of_ne_top
    {𝒯 𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒯 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hfQC : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hDM : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS f)
    (h𝒯 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒯)
    (h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (h𝒯Jacobson : AlgebraicStacks.IsJacobson B S hS 𝒯)
    (h𝒳Jacobson : AlgebraicStacks.IsJacobson B S hS 𝒳)
    (h𝒯Catenary : AlgebraicStacks.IsPseudoCatenary B S hS 𝒯)
    (h𝒳Catenary : AlgebraicStacks.IsPseudoCatenary B S hS 𝒳)
    (h𝒯Irreducible : @IrreducibleSpace _ (pointTopology B S hS 𝒯.val))
    (h𝒳QuasiSeparated : IsQuasiSeparatedAbs.{u, w, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    {P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj} (hP : IsSchemeTheoreticImage f P)
    (h𝒯Finite : dimension B S hS 𝒯 h𝒯 ≠ ⊤) :
    closedSubstackDimension B S hS 𝒳 P hP.1 hP.isAlgebraicStack h𝒳 ≤ dimension B S hS 𝒯 h𝒯 ∧
      Xor (∀ t, IsFiniteTypePoint.{u, w} B S hS 𝒯 t →
            0 < relativeStackDimensionAt B S hS f hf h𝒯 h𝒳 t)
        (dimension B S hS 𝒯 h𝒯 =
          closedSubstackDimension B S hS 𝒳 P hP.1 hP.isAlgebraicStack h𝒳) ∧
      ((∀ t, IsFiniteTypePoint.{u, w} B S hS 𝒯 t →
            0 < relativeStackDimensionAt B S hS f hf h𝒯 h𝒳 t) →
        closedSubstackDimension B S hS 𝒳 P hP.1 hP.isAlgebraicStack h𝒳 <
          dimension B S hS 𝒯 h𝒯)
declarations.comment: the exactly-one form under the added hypothesis that dim T is finite; erratum: false as written when dim T = dim Z = infinity, machine-checked as AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.not_forall_xor_relativeDimension_pos (the affine line over N<X>, N Nagata's ring; Fujita 1975, Brewer-Heinzer 1980), see the docstring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ringKrullDim_relation_eq_add_ringKrullDim_sourceFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DS8**, the dimension formula. For a smooth 1-morphism `f : U ⟶ 𝒳` from a scheme to
a locally Noetherian algebraic stack and a presented self-intersection `R = U ×_𝒳 U` with source
morphism `s`, the dimension of `𝒪_{R, r}` at a geometric point `r` is the sum of the dimension
of `𝒪_{U, s(r)}` and the dimension of the fibre `𝒪_{R_{s(r)}, r}`.

The morphism `s` is smooth, hence flat, so `𝒪_{U, s(r)} ⟶ 𝒪_{R, r}` is a flat local
homomorphism of Noetherian local rings and Stacks 00ON applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_relation_eq_add_ringKrullDim_sourceFibre
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f) (hsq : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct sq)
    (h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (hR : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS R)
    (r : Space.GeometricPoint B S hS R) :
    ringKrullDim (Space.etaleLocalRing B S hS R r) =
      ringKrullDim (chartEtaleLocalRing B S hS U f sq R eU eR r) +
        ringKrullDim (sourceFibreEtaleLocalRing B S hS U f sq R eU eR hR r)
declarations.comment: the dimension formula for the source projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ringKrullDim_chart_add_relation_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DS8.** The identity
`dim(𝒪_{U,s(r)}) - dim(𝒪_{R_u,r}) = 2 dim(𝒪_{U,s(r)}) - dim(𝒪_{R,r})`, recorded in the
subtraction-free form obtained by adding `dim(𝒪_{R_u,r}) + dim(𝒪_{R,r})` to both sides, which is
equivalent to it wherever the three dimensions are finite — in particular here, all three rings
being Noetherian local.

The invariant `2 dim(𝒪_{U,s(r)}) - dim(𝒪_{R,r})` of Stacks 0DSA is thus computed by the source
fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_chart_add_relation_eq
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f) (hsq : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct sq)
    (h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (hR : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS R)
    (r : Space.GeometricPoint B S hS R) :
    ringKrullDim (chartEtaleLocalRing B S hS U f sq R eU eR r) +
        ringKrullDim (Space.etaleLocalRing B S hS R r) =
      ringKrullDim (chartEtaleLocalRing B S hS U f sq R eU eR r) +
          ringKrullDim (chartEtaleLocalRing B S hS U f sq R eU eR r) +
        ringKrullDim (sourceFibreEtaleLocalRing B S hS U f sq R eU eR hR r)
declarations.comment: the dimension-difference identity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasLocalRingDimensionAtEveryChart_of_hasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DS9, condition (1) implies condition (2).** If some scheme of the site carries a
smooth 1-morphism to a locally Noetherian algebraic stack `𝒳` and a finite type point above the
finite type point `x ∈ |𝒳|` at which the invariant of Stacks 0DSA is `d`, then every such
configuration measures it to be `d`.

This is the chart independence of the invariant,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasChartInvariant_congr_of_isFiniteTypePoint`, read through the
restatement of the two conditions in terms of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasChartInvariant`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocalRingDimensionAtEveryChart_of_hasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.property)
    (hx : IsFiniteTypePoint.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 x) (d : ℤ)
    (hd : HasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 h𝒳 x hx d) :
    HasLocalRingDimensionAtEveryChart.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 h𝒳 x hx d
declarations.comment: condition (1) implies condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart_iff_hasLocalRingDimensionAtEveryChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DS9.** For a locally Noetherian algebraic stack `𝒳`, a finite type point
`x ∈ |𝒳|` and an integer `d`, the two conditions

1. there *exists* a scheme `U` of the site, a smooth 1-morphism `U ⟶ 𝒳` and a finite type point
   `u ∈ U` above `x` with `2 dim(𝒪_{U,ū}) - dim(𝒪_{R, e(ū)}) = d`, where `R = U ×_𝒳 U`, and
2. *every* such `U`, smooth 1-morphism and finite type point above `x` satisfies that identity

are equivalent. Condition (1) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart`,
which is also the definition of Stacks 0DSA, and condition (2) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasLocalRingDimensionAtEveryChart`.

Condition (2) implies condition (1) because the range of the two quantifiers is nonempty, by
**Stacks 06FX**. The converse is the chart independence of the invariant, which is the content of
the source's proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart_iff_hasLocalRingDimensionAtEveryChart
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.property)
    (hx : IsFiniteTypePoint.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 x) (d : ℤ) :
    HasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 h𝒳 x hx d ↔
      HasLocalRingDimensionAtEveryChart.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 h𝒳 x hx d
declarations.comment: the equivalence of the two conditions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart_of_hasLocalRingDimensionAtEveryChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DS9, condition (2) implies condition (1).** If every smooth chart of a locally
Noetherian algebraic stack `𝒳` carrying a finite type point above `x` measures the invariant of
Stacks 0DSA to be `d`, then some one does — because, by **Stacks 06FX**, there is one.

This direction of the equivalence is exactly the non-emptiness of the range of the two
quantifiers, supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_smoothChart_presentation_of_isFiniteTypePoint`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart_of_hasLocalRingDimensionAtEveryChart
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.property)
    (hx : IsFiniteTypePoint.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 x) (d : ℤ)
    (h : HasLocalRingDimensionAtEveryChart.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 h𝒳 x hx d) :
    HasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 h𝒳 x hx d
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies condition (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelationLocalRingDimension_transport_twoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**The invariant of Stacks 0DSA does not depend on the presented self-intersection.** Let a
smooth chart `g : V ⟶ 𝒳` be given, and let its self-intersection be presented twice over — by a
2-fibre product square `T` for the cospan `(g, g)`, an algebraic space `Q` presenting its apex
through `eQ` and a mediating morphism `δ`, and by `T'`, `Q'`, `eQ'`, `δ'`. Then at one and the
same point `ν` of the chart the two presentations measure the invariant to be the same integer.

The point of the chart does *not* move: the comparison of the two presentations is an
isomorphism `Q ≅ Q'` of the two representing presheaves of the relation, which carries the
diagonal image of `ν` for the first presentation to the diagonal image of `ν` for the second and
leaves `ν` alone. The chart dimension entering the invariant is read at `ν` itself
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelationLocalRingDimension_diagonal_iff`), so it is untouched, and
the dimension of the relation is unchanged under an isomorphism of presheaves
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension_pointsMap_of_isIso`).

This is one half of the presentation quantifier of condition (2) of **Stacks 0DS9**; the other
half, the comparison equivalence of the chart, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelationLocalRingDimension_transport_equivalence`, and the two are
combined in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.forall_hasRelationLocalRingDimension_transport_presentation`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRelationLocalRingDimension_transport_twoFibreProduct
    (δ : Bicategory.TwoCommSq.PreHom (selfIntersectionDiagonalSquare B S hS V g) T)
    (δ' : Bicategory.TwoCommSq.PreHom (selfIntersectionDiagonalSquare B S hS V g) T')
    (ν : Space.points B S hS (yoneda.obj V)) (d : ℤ) :
    HasRelationLocalRingDimension B S hS V g T Q eV eQ
        (Space.pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V)
          (selfIntersectionDiagonalMap B S hS V g T Q eV eQ δ) ν) d ↔
      HasRelationLocalRingDimension B S hS V g T' Q' eV eQ'
        (Space.pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V)
          (selfIntersectionDiagonalMap B S hS V g T' Q' eV eQ' δ') ν) d
declarations.comment: the invariant of the two conditions does not depend on the presented self-intersection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_iff_forall_geometricPoint_hasChartLocalRingDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DS9, for the choice of geometric point.** The existential and the universal
condition over the geometric points above a point `ρ` of the relation are equivalent: some
geometric point above `ρ` measures the invariant to be `d` exactly when every one does.

Forward this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasChartLocalRingDimension_iff_hasRelationLocalRingDimension`; backward
it is the existence of a geometric point above `ρ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iff_forall_geometricPoint_hasChartLocalRingDimension
    (hR : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS R) (ρ : Space.points B S hS R) (d : ℤ) :
    (∃ r : Space.GeometricPoint B S hS R, r.LiesOver ρ ∧
        HasChartLocalRingDimension B S hS U f sq R eU eR r d) ↔
      ∀ r : Space.GeometricPoint B S hS R, r.LiesOver ρ →
        HasChartLocalRingDimension B S hS U f sq R eU eR r d
declarations.comment: the two conditions, over the geometric point above a point of the relation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_hasChartLocalRingDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DS9, well-definedness of the invariant.** At a geometric point of a presented
self-intersection of a smooth chart of a locally Noetherian algebraic stack the invariant
`2 dim(𝒪_{U,s(r)}) - dim(𝒪_{R,r})` of Stacks 0DSA is realized by an integer: both local rings are
Noetherian local rings, so Krull's height theorem makes both dimensions finite.

This is what lets the conditions of Stacks 0DS9 be read at a `d ∈ ℤ`; the integer is unique by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasChartLocalRingDimension_unique`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hasChartLocalRingDimension
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f) (hsq : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct sq)
    (h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (hR : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS R)
    (r : Space.GeometricPoint B S hS R) :
    ∃ d : ℤ, HasChartLocalRingDimension B S hS U f sq R eU eR r d
declarations.comment: the invariant of the two conditions is a well-defined integer at a smooth chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasLocalRingDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSA.** The dimension of the local ring of a locally Noetherian algebraic stack `𝒳`
at a finite type point `x ∈ |𝒳|` *is* the integer `d` when condition (1) of Stacks 0DS9 holds:
some scheme `U` of the site carries a smooth 1-morphism `f : U ⟶ 𝒳` and a finite type point `u`
of `U` above `x` at which a presented self-intersection `R = U ×_𝒳 U`, with diagonal `e`, has
`2 dim(𝒪_{U,ū}) - dim(𝒪_{R, e(ū)}) = d`.

The source phrases the dimension as a relation between `x` and `d ∈ ℤ`, not as a function of `x`,
and so does this: the value is pinned down by Stacks 0DS9, whose independence of the chart is not
available here. Negative values occur (Stacks 0DS5), whence `ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
def HasLocalRingDimension (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (_h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.property)
    (_hx : IsFiniteTypePoint.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 x) (d : ℤ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart_iff_of_versalCogroupoid
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSB.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack, locally of finite type over a locally
Noetherian scheme `S` (Situation 0DQU), and let `x₀ : Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` be a morphism, `k` a field of
finite type over `S`, with `Spec Λ ⊆ S` an affine open through which `Spec k ⟶ S` factors with
`Λ → k` finite (Section 07T2). Represent `𝓕_{𝒳,k,x₀}` as in Remark 0DR3 by a cogroupoid
`(A, B, s, t, c)` of Noetherian complete local `Λ`-algebras with residue field `k`: a versal formal
object `ξ` over `A` and a representable presentation `P` on `𝒞^_Λ` with objects `P.objects = A`,
arrows `P.arrows = B`, source and target `s = P.source`, `t = P.target` and comultiplication
`c = P.comultiplication`, whose restriction to `𝒞_Λ` is the groupoid in functors
`(A|_{𝒞_Λ}, A|_{𝒞_Λ} ×_{ξ, 𝓕, ξ} A|_{𝒞_Λ})` of `ξ` (this is the representation produced by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_versalCogroupoid_predeformationCategory`). Then the dimension of
the local ring of `𝒳` at the point of `x₀` (Stacks 0DSA, the single integer of Stacks 0DS9) is
`2 dim A - dim B`: an integer `d` satisfies condition (1) of Stacks 0DS9
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart`) at that point exactly when
`d = 2 dim A - dim B`.

Every such representation is allowed, so the statement holds for all of them; the two dimensions
are finite and are recorded as natural numbers before the difference is taken, as in Stacks
0DSA.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart_iff_of_versalCogroupoid (D : VersalSituation.{u, w})
    {Λ k : Type u} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k] [Module.Finite Λ k]
    (iΛ : Spec (.of Λ) ⟶ D.S) (hiΛ : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion iΛ)
    (x₀ : D.𝒳.val.val.obj)
    (hx₀ : (D.𝒳.val.val.p ⋙ Over.post D.B.inclusion).obj x₀ =
      Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ))
    (hfinite : LocallyOfFiniteType (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ) ∧
      QuasiCompact (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ)) :
    let C := Deformation.Artin.predeformationCategory iΛ
      (D.𝒳.val.val.p ⋙ Over.post D.B.inclusion) x₀ hx₀
    letI := C.category
    let hp := Deformation.Artin.predeformationCategory_isPredeformationCategory
      D.B D.hS iΛ D.𝒳.val.val.p x₀ hx₀ D.𝒳.val.property
    ∀ (ξ : Deformation.FormalObject C.projection) (_ : Deformation.IsVersal hp.cofibered ξ)
      (P : Deformation.RepresentablePresentation.{_, u, u}
        (Deformation.CompleteLocalAlgCat.{u, u, u} Λ k)),
      P.objects = ξ.base →
      Nonempty (Deformation.versalGroupoid C.projection hp ξ ≅
        Deformation.GroupoidInFunctors.restrict P.groupoidInFunctors
          Deformation.artinianToComplete) →
      ∃ m n : ℕ, ringKrullDim P.objects = m ∧ ringKrullDim P.arrows = n ∧
        ∀ d : ℤ, HasLocalRingDimensionAtSomeChart D.B D.S D.hS D.𝒳
          (isLocallyNoetherianStack_of_versalSituation D) (objectPoint D.B D.S D.hS iΛ x₀ hx₀)
          (isFiniteTypePoint_objectPoint D iΛ hiΛ x₀ hx₀ hfinite) d ↔
            d = 2 * (m : ℤ) - (n : ℤ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nodalLocus_isGreatest
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DSC.** For a morphism of schemes which is flat and locally of finite
presentation there is a maximal open subscheme of its source on which it is at-worst-nodal of
relative dimension one: the restriction of the morphism to `nodalLocus f` is at-worst-nodal of
relative dimension one, and every open subscheme with that property is contained in
`nodalLocus f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nodalLocus_isGreatest {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] :
    IsGreatest {U : X.Opens | IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne (U.ι ≫ f)} (nodalLocus f)
declarations.comment: the maximal open subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nodalLocus_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DSC.** Formation of the maximal at-worst-nodal open subscheme
commutes with arbitrary base change: in a cartesian square with right edge a flat morphism `f`
locally of finite presentation and base edge `g`, the nodal locus of the base change `f'` of `f`
is the inverse image of the nodal locus of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nodalLocus_baseChange {X' X S' S : Scheme.{u}} (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (f : X ⟶ S)
    (g : S' ⟶ S) (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] :
    nodalLocus f' = g' ⁻¹ᵁ nodalLocus f
declarations.comment: compatibility with base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSE.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is *at-worst-nodal of
relative dimension one* when every commuting square of étale scheme charts induces a
scheme morphism which is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_isStableUnderBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSF.** Being at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one is preserved by base
change of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_isStableUnderBaseChange (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
      (fun ⦃F G : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : F ⟶ G) =>
        IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne B S hS f.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSG.** Eight criteria for a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` to be
at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one: the condition may be tested after base change to
every scheme or to every affine scheme, on one surjective étale chart of the target, on the
composite with one surjective étale chart of the source, in every or in one surjective
commuting square of étale charts, or over a pair of Zariski coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_tfae (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne B S hS f,
      ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Y),
        IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne B S hS (Limits.pullback.snd f g),
      ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Y),
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
          IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne B S hS (Limits.pullback.snd f g),
      ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
        IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧
          IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne B S hS (Limits.pullback.snd f g),
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
        IsSurjective B S hS p ∧ IsEtale B S hS p ∧
          IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne B S hS (p ≫ f),
      ∀ (U V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X) (q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y) (a : U ⟶ V),
        IsEtale B S hS p → IsEtale B S hS q → p ≫ f = yoneda.map a ≫ q →
          AlgebraicGeometry.IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne
            ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map a),
      ∃ (U V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X) (q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y) (a : U ⟶ V),
        IsEtale B S hS p ∧ IsEtale B S hS q ∧ IsSurjective B S hS p ∧
          p ≫ f = yoneda.map a ≫ q ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne
            ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map a),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (Yopen : I → Subfunctor Y) (J : I → Type u)
        (Xopen : ∀ i, J i → Subfunctor (Limits.pullback f (Yopen i).ι)),
        IsZariskiCover B S hS I Yopen ∧ (∀ i, IsZariskiCover B S hS (J i) (Xopen i)) ∧
          ∀ i j, IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne B S hS
            ((Xopen i j).ι ≫ Limits.pullback.snd f (Yopen i).ι)
    ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isGreatest_isNodalOpen_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSH.** Let `S` be a scheme and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` which is flat and locally of finite presentation. Then there is a maximal open
subspace `X' ⊆ X` such that the restriction of `f` to `X'` is at-worst-nodal of relative
dimension one, and formation of `X'` commutes with arbitrary base change.

The maximal open subspace is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nodalOpenSubspace`; it is an open
subspace on which the restriction of `f` is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one, and it
contains every open subspace with that property, which is the content of the `IsGreatest`
assertion. The second assertion is that for an arbitrary morphism `g : Y' ⟶ Y` of algebraic
spaces over `S`, the locus of the base change `X ×_Y Y' ⟶ Y'` of `f` along `g` is the inverse
image of the locus of `f` under the projection to `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGreatest_isNodalOpen_baseChange {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f) (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    IsGreatest {W : Subfunctor X | IsNodalOpen B S hS f W} (nodalOpenSubspace B S hS f) ∧
      ∀ Y' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y' →
        ∀ g : Y' ⟶ Y, nodalOpenSubspace B S hS (pullback.snd f g) =
          (nodalOpenSubspace B S hS f).preimage (pullback.fst f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyQuasiFinite_iff_at_identity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSI.** A group algebraic space locally of finite type over its base is locally
quasi-finite exactly when it is quasi-finite at the identity point over every point of the
base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_iff_at_identity (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bs hBs)
    (hG : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.obj.X.hom) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS G.obj.X.hom ↔
      ∀ b : points B S hS Bs,
        IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS G.obj.X.hom
          (pointsMap B S hS Bs (MonObj.one (X := G.obj.X)).left b)
declarations.comment: the locally quasi-finite characterization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_iff_at_identity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSI.** A group algebraic space locally of finite type over its base is unramified
exactly when it is unramified at the identity point over every point of the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_iff_at_identity (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bs hBs)
    (hG : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.obj.X.hom) :
    IsUnramified B S hS G.obj.X.hom ↔
      ∀ b : points B S hS Bs,
        IsUnramifiedAt B S hS G.obj.X.hom
          (pointsMap B S hS Bs (MonObj.one (X := G.obj.X)).left b)
declarations.comment: the unramified characterization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSJ, the locally quasi-finite case.** The *locally quasi-finite base locus* of a
group algebraic space: the union of all open subspaces of the base over which it is locally
quasi-finite.
declarations.statement: def locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bs hBs) : Subfunctor Bs
declarations.comment: the locally quasi-finite base locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.le_locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSJ, maximality in the locally quasi-finite case.** Every open subspace of the
base over which a group algebraic space is locally quasi-finite is contained in its locally
quasi-finite base locus: it is a member of the family that locus is the supremum of.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bs hBs)
    {U : Subfunctor Bs} (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U)
    (hGU : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (pullback.snd G.obj.X.hom U.ι)) :
    U ≤ locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus B S hS G
declarations.comment: maximality of the locally quasi-finite base locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenSubspace_locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSJ, openness in the locally quasi-finite case.** The locally quasi-finite base
locus of a group algebraic space locally of finite type over its base is an open subspace.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenSubspace_locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bs hBs)
    (hG : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.obj.X.hom) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS (locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus B S hS G)
declarations.comment: openness of the locally quasi-finite base locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyQuasiFinite_locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSJ, the locally quasi-finite case.** A group algebraic space locally of finite
type over its base is locally quasi-finite over its locally quasi-finite base locus.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus
    (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bs hBs)
    (hG : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.obj.X.hom) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS
      (pullback.snd G.obj.X.hom (locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus B S hS G).ι)
declarations.comment: local quasi-finiteness over the locally quasi-finite base locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSJ, base change in the locally quasi-finite case.** Forming the locally
quasi-finite base locus of a group algebraic space locally of finite type commutes with
arbitrary base change of algebraic spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus_preimage (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bs hBs)
    (hG : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.obj.X.hom)
    {Bt : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hBt : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bt) (f : Bt ⟶ Bs) :
    locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus B S hS (GroupAlgebraicSpace.baseChange B S hS hBt f G) =
      (locallyQuasiFiniteBaseLocus B S hS G).preimage f
declarations.comment: base change of the locally quasi-finite base locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.unramifiedBaseLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSJ, the unramified case.** The *unramified base locus* of a group algebraic
space: the union of all open subspaces of the base over which it is unramified.
declarations.statement: def unramifiedBaseLocus (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bs hBs) : Subfunctor Bs
declarations.comment: the unramified base locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.le_unramifiedBaseLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSJ, maximality in the unramified case.** Every open subspace of the base over
which a group algebraic space is unramified is contained in its unramified base locus: it is a
member of the family that locus is the supremum of.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_unramifiedBaseLocus (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bs hBs)
    {U : Subfunctor Bs} (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U)
    (hGU : IsUnramified B S hS (pullback.snd G.obj.X.hom U.ι)) :
    U ≤ unramifiedBaseLocus B S hS G
declarations.comment: maximality of the unramified base locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenSubspace_unramifiedBaseLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSJ, openness in the unramified case.** The unramified base locus of a group
algebraic space is an open subspace.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenSubspace_unramifiedBaseLocus (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bs hBs) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS (unramifiedBaseLocus B S hS G)
declarations.comment: openness of the unramified base locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_unramifiedBaseLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSJ, the unramified case.** A group algebraic space is unramified over its
unramified base locus.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_unramifiedBaseLocus (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bs hBs) :
    IsUnramified B S hS (pullback.snd G.obj.X.hom (unramifiedBaseLocus B S hS G).ι)
declarations.comment: unramifiedness over the unramified base locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.unramifiedBaseLocus_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSJ, base change in the unramified case.** Forming the unramified base locus of a
group algebraic space locally of finite type commutes with arbitrary base change of algebraic
spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem unramifiedBaseLocus_preimage (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bs hBs)
    (hG : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS G.obj.X.hom)
    {Bt : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hBt : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Bt) (f : Bt ⟶ Bs) :
    unramifiedBaseLocus B S hS (GroupAlgebraicSpace.baseChange B S hS hBt f G) =
      (unramifiedBaseLocus B S hS G).preimage f
declarations.comment: base change of the unramified base locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_of_isPseudoTorsor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSK.** A pseudo-torsor under an unramified group algebraic space is unramified
over the base, provided it is locally of finite type over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_of_isPseudoTorsor (𝒞 : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : 𝒞.Contains S) {B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B) (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB) (X : Over B)
    [ModObj G.obj.X X] (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS X.left)
    (hXFiniteType : IsLocallyOfFiniteType 𝒞 S hS X.hom)
    (hG : IsUnramified 𝒞 S hS G.obj.X.hom) (hPseudo : IsPseudoTorsor G.obj.X X) :
    IsUnramified 𝒞 S hS X.hom
declarations.comment: the unramified case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_isPseudoTorsor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSK.** A pseudo-torsor under a locally quasi-finite group algebraic space is
locally quasi-finite over the base, provided it is locally of finite type over the base.

The shear map identifies the second projection of `X ×_B X` with that of `G ×_B X`, which is a
base change of `G ⟶ B`, so the projection is locally quasi-finite; that is the only use of the
torsor structure, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_pullbackSnd` is the rest
of the argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_isPseudoTorsor (𝒞 : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : 𝒞.Contains S) {B : (BigFppfOver 𝒞 S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B) (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB) (X : Over B)
    [ModObj G.obj.X X] (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS X.left)
    (hXFiniteType : IsLocallyOfFiniteType 𝒞 S hS X.hom)
    (hG : IsLocallyQuasiFinite 𝒞 S hS G.obj.X.hom) (hPseudo : IsPseudoTorsor G.obj.X X) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite 𝒞 S hS X.hom
declarations.comment: the locally quasi-finite case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.dmLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSM**, the Deligne–Mumford locus. The object property of an algebraic stack `𝒳`
cut out by the supremum of the object properties of its Deligne–Mumford open substacks; this is
the substack `𝒳''` of the source.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dmLocus (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj
declarations.comment: the DM locus, as the supremum of the DM open substacks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quasiDMLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSM**, the quasi-Deligne–Mumford locus. The object property of an algebraic stack
`𝒳` cut out by the supremum of the object properties of its quasi-Deligne–Mumford open
substacks; this is the substack `𝒳'` of the source.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasiDMLocus (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj
declarations.comment: the quasi-DM locus, as the supremum of the quasi-DM open substacks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.le_dmLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSM, maximality for the DM locus.** Every Deligne–Mumford open substack of `𝒳` is
contained in the Deligne–Mumford locus. This is the force of the word *largest* in the source,
and it holds with no hypothesis beyond those of the ambient site.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_dmLocus (U : OpenSubstack 𝒳)
    (hU : AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS hZ U.toAlgebraicStack) :
    U.property ≤ dmLocus B S hS hZ 𝒳
declarations.comment: maximality of the DM locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.le_quasiDMLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSM, maximality for the quasi-DM locus.** Every quasi-Deligne–Mumford open
substack of `𝒳` is contained in the quasi-Deligne–Mumford locus.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_quasiDMLocus (U : OpenSubstack 𝒳)
    (hU : AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS hZ U.toAlgebraicStack) :
    U.property ≤ quasiDMLocus B S hS hZ 𝒳
declarations.comment: maximality of the quasi-DM locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.dmLocus_le_quasiDMLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSM, the nesting `𝒳'' ⊆ 𝒳'`.** The Deligne–Mumford locus is contained in the
quasi-Deligne–Mumford locus, because a Deligne–Mumford open substack is quasi-Deligne–Mumford by
**Stacks 050E** (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDM_of_isDM`). This holds with
no further input.
declarations.statement:
theorem dmLocus_le_quasiDMLocus :
    dmLocus B S hS hZ 𝒳 ≤ quasiDMLocus B S hS hZ 𝒳
declarations.comment: the DM locus is contained in the quasi-DM locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_nested_largest_isAbsolutelyDM_openSubstacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSM.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack. There exist open substacks
`𝒳'' ⊆ 𝒳' ⊆ 𝒳` such that `𝒳''` is DM, `𝒳'` is quasi-DM, and these are the largest open
substacks with these properties.

Here `W''` is `𝒳''` and `W'` is `𝒳'`. DM and quasi-DM are the absolute notions of
**Stacks 050D**, parts (5) and (6), read over the terminal scheme `Spec ℤ`, which every big fppf
site contains (`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.contains_terminal`); containment of open substacks
is containment of their objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nested_largest_isAbsolutelyDM_openSubstacks :
    ∃ W' W'' : OpenSubstack 𝒳,
      W''.property ≤ W'.property ∧
      AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS B.contains_terminal W''.toAlgebraicStack ∧
      AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS B.contains_terminal W'.toAlgebraicStack ∧
      (∀ V : OpenSubstack 𝒳,
        AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS B.contains_terminal V.toAlgebraicStack →
          V.property ≤ W''.property) ∧
      ∀ V : OpenSubstack 𝒳,
        AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS B.contains_terminal V.toAlgebraicStack →
          V.property ≤ W'.property
declarations.comment: open substacks W'' ≤ W' of 𝒳 with W'' absolutely DM and W' absolutely quasi-DM (050D(5),(6)), each containing every absolutely DM, resp. absolutely quasi-DM, open substack of 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.dmLocus_apply_iff_isUnramifiedAutomorphismGroupSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSN, part (1).** A field-valued point of an algebraic stack lies in its
Deligne–Mumford locus exactly when its automorphism group algebraic space is unramified over
its field.

The objects of `𝒳` whose automorphism group algebraic space is unramified form an open substack,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.automorphismLocusSubstack`, open because the unramified base locus of
**Stacks 0DSJ** is, and Deligne–Mumford by the pseudo-torsor argument of **Stacks 0CL0** through
**Stacks 0DSK**; conversely an open substack is Deligne–Mumford only if the automorphism group
algebraic spaces of its objects, which are those computed in `𝒳`, are unramified.
declarations.statement:
theorem dmLocus_apply_iff_isUnramifiedAutomorphismGroupSpace
    (x : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val.val) :
    dmLocus B S hS hZ 𝒳 x.obj ↔ IsUnramifiedAutomorphismGroupSpace B S hS 𝒳 x
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quasiDMLocus_apply_iff_isLocallyQuasiFiniteAutomorphismGroupSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSN, part (2).** A field-valued point of an algebraic stack lies in its
quasi-Deligne–Mumford locus exactly when its automorphism group algebraic space is locally
quasi-finite over its field. The source says the proof is the same as for part (1), and it
is.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiDMLocus_apply_iff_isLocallyQuasiFiniteAutomorphismGroupSpace
    (x : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val.val) :
    quasiDMLocus B S hS hZ 𝒳 x.obj ↔
      IsLocallyQuasiFiniteAutomorphismGroupSpace B S hS 𝒳 x
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_and_isRelativelyFinitePresentation_diagonal_curves
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSQ.** The diagonal of the algebraic stack `Curves` over `Spec ℤ` is separated and
of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_and_isRelativelyFinitePresentation_diagonal_curves :
    Stack.IsSeparated B integerBase hZ
        (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B integerBase hZ
          (curvesAlgebraicStack B hZ
            (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, w} B hZ)).val
          (Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B integerBase hZ (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hZ)))).val
          (Stack.structureMorphism B integerBase hZ (curvesAlgebraicStack B hZ
            (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, w} B hZ))).hom) ∧
      Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsRelativelyFinitePresentation B integerBase hZ
        (Stack.AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B integerBase hZ
          (Stack.structureMorphism B integerBase hZ (curvesAlgebraicStack B hZ
            (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, w} B hZ))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiSeparated_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_curvesAlgebraicStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSS.** The morphism `Curves → Spec(ℤ)` of the algebraic stack of curves is
quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation.

Quasi-separatedness is the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of the diagonal, given by
the finite presentation of the diagonal in Stacks 0DSQ
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_and_isRelativelyFinitePresentation_diagonal_curves`); local
finite presentation is Stacks 0CMY applied to Stacks 0D55
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isLimitPreserving_curvesFiberedCategory_unconditional`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_curvesAlgebraicStack :
    Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B integerBase hZ
        (Stack.structureMorphism B integerBase hZ (curvesAlgebraicStack B hZ
          (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, w} B hZ))) ∧
      Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B integerBase hZ
        (Stack.structureMorphism B integerBase hZ (curvesAlgebraicStack B hZ
          (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, w} B hZ)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedImmersion_doublePointsToProjectiveLine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSU.** For three pairwise distinct points of the affine line, the three double
points `Spec(k[t]/(t - aᵢ)²)` form a closed subscheme of `P¹_k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_doublePointsToProjectiveLine (hpts : Function.Injective pts) :
    IsClosedImmersion (doublePointsToProjectiveLine k pts)
declarations.comment: the three double points form a closed subscheme of the projective line

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPushout_gluingScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSU.** Gluing two copies of `A¹_k` along the three double points gives the
spectrum of the equalizer of the two reduction maps `k[t] × k[t] ⇉ ∏ᵢ k[t]/(t - aᵢ)²`: the
functions on the affine part of the glued curve are the pairs of polynomials agreeing to first
order at the three points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPushout_gluingScheme (hpts : Function.Injective pts) :
    IsPushout (doublePointsToAffineLine k pts) (doublePointsToAffineLine k pts)
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (gluingSubringSnd pts)))
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (gluingSubringFst pts)))
declarations.comment: the two affine lines glue to the spectrum of the equalizer of the two reductions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gluedCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSU.** The curve `X` of the example: two copies of `P¹_k` glued along the closed
subscheme of the three double points `Spec(k[t]/(t - aᵢ)²)`, that is, the pushout of
`T ⟶ P¹_k` with itself.
declarations.statement: def gluedCurve : Scheme.{u}
declarations.comment: the curve obtained by gluing two projective lines along three double points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPushout_gluedCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSU.** The glued curve is the pushout of the two copies of `P¹_k` along the
three double points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPushout_gluedCurve :
    IsPushout (doublePointsToProjectiveLine k pts) (doublePointsToProjectiveLine k pts)
      (gluedCurveInl k pts hpts) (gluedCurveInr k pts hpts)
declarations.comment: the glued curve is the pushout of the two projective lines

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.epsTranslate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSU.** The automorphism of the equalizer diagram
`k[ε][t] × k[ε][t] ⇉ ∏ᵢ k[ε][t]/(t - aᵢ)²` over the dual numbers of a field of characteristic
`2` given by the substitution `t ↦ t + ε` on both coordinates.
declarations.statement: def epsTranslate : gluingSubring pts ≃+* gluingSubring pts
declarations.comment: the automorphism of the equalizer diagram sending t to t + epsilon

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.epsTranslate_ne_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSU.** The substitution `t ↦ t + ε` on the equalizer diagram is not the
identity.
declarations.statement: theorem epsTranslate_ne_one : epsTranslate k pts ≠ RingEquiv.refl _
declarations.comment: non-triviality of the automorphism sending t to t + epsilon

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.map_fst_epsTranslate
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0DSU.** The substitution `t ↦ t + ε` becomes the identity modulo `ε`.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_fst_epsTranslate (x : gluingSubring pts) :
    ((Polynomial.mapRingHom (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom k k k).toRingHom) (epsTranslate k pts x).1.1,
        (Polynomial.mapRingHom (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom k k k).toRingHom)
          (epsTranslate k pts x).1.2) =
      ((Polynomial.mapRingHom (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom k k k).toRingHom) x.1.1,
        (Polynomial.mapRingHom (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom k k k).toRingHom) x.1.2)
declarations.comment: the automorphism sending t to t + epsilon is the identity modulo epsilon

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineOpen_gluedCurveAffinePart
declarations.doc: **`U` is an affine open of the glued curve.**
declarations.statement: theorem isAffineOpen_gluedCurveAffinePart : IsAffineOpen (gluedCurveAffinePart k pts hpts)
declarations.comment: the affine open part U of X, the image of the two affine lines

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gluedCurveAffinePartSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The functions on `U` are the equalizer** `O_X(U) ⟶ k[t] × k[t] ⇉ ∏ᵢ k[t]/(t - aᵢ)²`: the
ring of sections of `X` over the affine part is the ring of pairs of polynomials agreeing to first
order at the three points.
declarations.statement:
def gluedCurveAffinePartSectionsEquiv :
    Γ(gluedCurve k pts hpts, gluedCurveAffinePart k pts hpts) ≃+* gluingSubring pts
declarations.comment: O_X(U) is the equalizer of k[t] × k[t] ⇉ ∏ k[t]/(t - a_i)²

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gluedCurveDualNumbersAut
declarations.doc:
**The automorphism `t ↦ t + ε` of the equalizer diagram extends to an automorphism of `X`
over `A = k[ε]`.** For `k` of characteristic `2`, the automorphism of
`X_A = X ×_{Spec k} Spec k[ε]` over `Spec k[ε]` which is the translation `t ↦ t + ε` on both
copies of `ℙ¹_{k[ε]}`.
declarations.statement:
def gluedCurveDualNumbersAut :
    Aut (Over.mk (pullback.snd (gluedCurveToBase k pts hpts) (dualNumbersToBase k)))
declarations.comment: the automorphism t ↦ t + ε extends to an automorphism of X over A = k[ε]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveLineXChart_comp_gluedCurveDualNumbersAut
declarations.doc:
**The automorphism of `X_A` restricts on the two affine lines `Spec k[ε][t]` to the
substitution `t ↦ t + ε`** of the equalizer diagram
`O(U_A) ⟶ k[ε][t] × k[ε][t] ⇉ ∏ᵢ k[ε][t]/(t - aᵢ)²`; on the equalizer itself this substitution is
`AlgebraicGeometry.epsTranslate`.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveLineXChart_comp_gluedCurveDualNumbersAut (b : Bool) :
    projectiveLineXChart (DualNumber k) ≫ gluedCurveDualNumbersComponent k pts hpts b ≫
        (gluedCurveDualNumbersAut k pts hpts).asIso.hom.left =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (translate (DualNumber.eps : DualNumber k)).toRingHom) ≫
        projectiveLineXChart (DualNumber k) ≫ gluedCurveDualNumbersComponent k pts hpts b
declarations.comment: the automorphism of X_A is the substitution t ↦ t + ε on the two affine lines

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.gluedCurveDualNumbersAut_ne_one
declarations.doc:
**The automorphism of `X_A` is not the identity**: it moves the `k[ε]`-point
`t = 0` of the first copy of `ℙ¹_{k[ε]}` to the point `t = ε`.
declarations.statement: theorem gluedCurveDualNumbersAut_ne_one : gluedCurveDualNumbersAut k pts hpts ≠ 1
declarations.comment: the automorphism of X over A is nontrivial

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_aut_gluedCurve
declarations.doc:
**The automorphism group of `X` over `k` is finite.** For `k` algebraically
closed and three distinct points, the group of automorphisms over `k` of the curve obtained by
gluing two copies of `ℙ¹_k` along the three double points `Spec(k[t]/(t - aᵢ)²)` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_aut_gluedCurve :
    Finite (Aut (Over.mk (gluedCurveToBase k pts hpts)))
declarations.comment: the automorphism group of X over k is finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_autFunctor_gluedCurve
declarations.doc: `Aut(X)(k)` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_autFunctor_gluedCurve :
    Finite ((Scheme.autFunctor (gluedCurveOver k pts hpts)).obj (op (pointOver k)))
declarations.comment: the automorphism group of X over k, the k-points of Aut(X), is finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.autFunctor_map_gluedCurveDualNumbersAut
declarations.doc:
The automorphism `t ↦ t + ε` of `X_{k[ε]}` restricts to the identity over the closed point
of `Spec k[ε]`: its image under `Aut(X)(k[ε]) ⟶ Aut(X)(k)` is the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem autFunctor_map_gluedCurveDualNumbersAut :
    (Scheme.autFunctor (gluedCurveOver k pts hpts)).map (dualNumbersClosedPoint k).op
      (gluedCurveDualNumbersAut k pts hpts) =
        (1 : Aut ((Over.pullback (pointOver k).hom).obj (gluedCurveOver k pts hpts)))
declarations.comment: the automorphism t ↦ t + ε becomes the identity modulo ε

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.not_exists_isReduced_represents_autFunctor_gluedCurve
declarations.doc:
**The automorphism group scheme of `X` is non-reduced.** For `k` algebraically closed of
characteristic `2` and three distinct points, no reduced scheme locally of finite type over `k`
represents the automorphism functor `T ↦ Aut_T(X_T)` of the curve `X` obtained by gluing two
copies of `ℙ¹_k` along the double points at the three points.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_exists_isReduced_represents_autFunctor_gluedCurve :
    ¬ ∃ (G : Over (Spec (.of k))) (_ : IsReduced G.left) (_ : LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom),
      Nonempty (yoneda.obj G ≅ Scheme.autFunctor (gluedCurveOver k pts hpts))
declarations.comment: Aut(X) is non-reduced

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GenusOne.autScheme_topologicalKrullDim_eq_one_of_genus_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DSV**, genus one. **The automorphism group scheme of a smooth proper
curve of genus one over an algebraically closed field has dimension one.** The automorphism
functor `T ↦ Aut_T(X ×_k T)` of `X` over `k` is representable by a scheme over `k`, and every
scheme representing it has dimension one.
declarations.statement:
theorem autScheme_topologicalKrullDim_eq_one_of_genus_eq_one
    (hg : genus f = 1) :
    (∃ G : Over (Spec (.of k)), Nonempty ((Scheme.autFunctor (Over.mk f)).RepresentableBy G)) ∧
      ∀ (G : Over (Spec (.of k))), (Scheme.autFunctor (Over.mk f)).RepresentableBy G →
        topologicalKrullDim G.left = 1
declarations.comment: genus one: the automorphism group scheme of a smooth proper genus one curve over an algebraically closed field exists and has dimension one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GenusZero.autFunctor_projectiveLine_representableBy_projectiveGeneralLinearTwo
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DSV**, genus zero. **`Aut(ℙ¹_k) = PGL_{2,k}` as functors.** The scheme
`PGL_{2,k}` represents the automorphism functor of the projective line over `k`, the point of
`PGL_{2,k}` given by an invertible matrix `M` over a `k`-algebra `A` corresponding to the Möbius
automorphism of `M`; and `PGL_{2,k}` has dimension three.
declarations.statement:
theorem autFunctor_projectiveLine_representableBy_projectiveGeneralLinearTwo :
    (∃ R : (Scheme.autFunctor (projectiveLineOver k)).RepresentableBy
        (projectiveGeneralLinearTwoScheme k),
      ∀ {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (h : Spec (.of A) ⟶ Spec (.of k))
        (M : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) A) (hM : IsUnit M.det),
        R.homEquiv (evaluationOver h M hM) = mobiusAutFunctor h M hM) ∧
      topologicalKrullDim (projectiveGeneralLinearTwoScheme k).left = 3
declarations.comment: genus zero: Aut(P^1_k) = PGL_{2,k} as functors, an invertible matrix acting by its Moebius map, and PGL_{2,k} has dimension three

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GenusZero.autScheme_topologicalKrullDim_eq_three_of_genus_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DSV**, genus zero. **The automorphism group scheme of a smooth proper
curve of genus zero over an algebraically closed field is `PGL_{2,k}` and has dimension three.**
The automorphism functor `T ↦ Aut_T(X ×_k T)` of `X` over `k` is represented by `PGL_{2,k}`, and
every scheme representing it has dimension three.
declarations.statement:
theorem autScheme_topologicalKrullDim_eq_three_of_genus_eq_zero (hg : genus f = 0) :
    Nonempty ((Scheme.autFunctor (Over.mk f)).RepresentableBy
        (projectiveGeneralLinearTwoScheme k)) ∧
      ∀ G : Over (Spec (.of k)), (Scheme.autFunctor (Over.mk f)).RepresentableBy G →
        topologicalKrullDim G.left = 3
declarations.comment: genus zero: the automorphism functor of a smooth proper genus zero curve over an algebraically closed field is represented by PGL_{2,k}, and every representing scheme has dimension three

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curvesSmall.exists_deligneMumfordLocus_unconditional
declarations.doc:
There exists an open substack `Curves^DM ⊂ Curves` of the algebraic stack of curves over
`Spec ℤ` such that

1. `Curves^DM` is the maximal open substack of `Curves` which is DM: it is Deligne–Mumford, and
   every Deligne–Mumford open substack of `Curves` is contained in it;
2. for a family of curves `X → S`, the classifying morphism `S → Curves` factors through
   `Curves^DM` if and only if the group algebraic space `Aut_S(X)` is unramified over `S`;
3. for a field-valued point `x : Spec k → Curves`, classifying a proper `X` of dimension `≤ 1`
   over `k`, the following are equivalent: `x` factors through `Curves^DM`; `Aut(X)` is
   geometrically reduced over `k` of dimension `0`; `Aut(X) → Spec k` is unramified.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_deligneMumfordLocus_unconditional :
    ∃ W : Stack.OpenSubstack (curvesAlgebraicStack B hZ
        (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, w} B hZ)),
      (Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyDM B integerBase hZ B.contains_terminal
          W.toAlgebraicStack ∧
        ∀ V : Stack.OpenSubstack (curvesAlgebraicStack B hZ
            (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, w} B hZ)),
          Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyDM B integerBase hZ B.contains_terminal
              V.toAlgebraicStack →
            V.property ≤ W.property) ∧
      (∀ F : CurveFamily B hZ,
        W.property (ShrinkHoms.toShrinkHoms F) ↔
          Space.IsUnramified B integerBase hZ (CurveFamily.autFunctorProjection F)) ∧
      ∀ x : Stack.FieldValuedPoint B integerBase hZ (curvesAlgebraicStack B hZ
          (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, w} B hZ)).val.val,
        List.TFAE
          [W.property x.obj,
            Space.IsGeometricallyReduced x.carrier B
                (Stack.contains_spectrum_fieldValuedPoint B integerBase hZ x)
                (Stack.automorphismGroupSpaceOverField B integerBase hZ _ x)
                (Stack.isAlgebraicSpace_automorphismGroupSpaceOverField B integerBase hZ _ x) ∧
              Space.dimension B (Spec (.of x.carrier))
                (Stack.contains_spectrum_fieldValuedPoint B integerBase hZ x)
                (Stack.automorphismGroupSpaceOverField B integerBase hZ _ x)
                (Stack.isAlgebraicSpace_automorphismGroupSpaceOverField B integerBase hZ _ x) = 0,
            Stack.IsUnramifiedAutomorphismGroupSpace B integerBase hZ
              (curvesAlgebraicStack B hZ
                (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, w} B hZ)) x]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nodalCurvesOpenSubstack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSY, part (1).** The open substack `Curves^{nodal}` of families of curves which are
at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one, together with the characterisation of its objects: an
object of the stack belongs to it exactly when the family of curves it classifies is
at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one.

The algebraic stack of curves is a hypothesis: `𝒳` is any algebraic stack over the big fppf site
of the integers whose objects are identified with families of curves by an equivalence `E` over
that site.

Part (2) of the source, the characterisation for a proper scheme over a field, is not asserted
here.

The definition carries `@[no_expose]`: its body names the private helpers that build the
substack, so it may not be exposed. Nothing downstream needs to unfold it — the
characterisation of its objects is the second component of the subtype.
declarations.statement:
def nodalCurvesOpenSubstack
    (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B integerBase hZ)
    (E : CurveFamily B hZ ≌ 𝒳.val.val.obj)
    (hE : E.functor ⋙ 𝒳.val.val.p = curvesProjectionOver B hZ) :
    {U : Stack.OpenSubstack 𝒳 //
      ∀ F : CurveFamily B hZ,
        U.property (E.functor.obj F) ↔
          Space.IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne B integerBase hZ F.toBase.hom}
declarations.comment: the open substack and part (1): the characterisation on every family of curves, given a presentation of the algebraic stack of curves. Part (2), the characterisation for a proper scheme over a field, is NOT asserted here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.classifying_factors_nodalCurvesOpenSubstack_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSY, part (1).** The classifying object of a family of curves lifts through the
inclusion of the nodal open substack exactly when the family is at-worst-nodal of relative
dimension one.

As for `AlgebraicGeometry.nodalCurvesOpenSubstack`, the algebraic stack of curves and its
identification with families of curves are hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem classifying_factors_nodalCurvesOpenSubstack_iff
    (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B integerBase hZ)
    (E : CurveFamily B hZ ≌ 𝒳.val.val.obj)
    (hE : E.functor ⋙ 𝒳.val.val.p = curvesProjectionOver B hZ)
    (F : CurveFamily B hZ) :
    (∃ Y : (nodalCurvesOpenSubstack B hZ 𝒳 E hE).1.property.FullSubcategory,
      Y.obj = E.functor.obj F) ↔
      Space.IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne B integerBase hZ F.toBase.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): the classifying morphism of a family factors through the nodal open substack iff the family is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one, given a presentation of the algebraic stack of curves. Part (2), the characterisation for a proper scheme over a field, is NOT asserted here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lifts_nodalCurves_curveFamilyOfProperOverField_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSY, part (2).** Let `k` be a field and let `X ⟶ Spec(k)` be a morphism of the big
fppf site of the integers which is proper and whose source has dimension at most one. The
classifying morphism `Spec(k) → Curves` of the attached family of curves factors through
`Curves^{nodal}` — that is, that family lifts through the inclusion of the strictly full
subcategory of families which are at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one — if and only if the
singularities of `X` are at worst nodal and `X` is equidimensional of dimension one.

The hypotheses are those of the source: `X` is proper over the field and of dimension at most
one. Nothing else is assumed; in particular this does not use the hypothesis
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.Bootstrap04S6Spaces` on which
`AlgebraicGeometry.nodalCurvesOpenSubstackUnconditional` — the open substack itself, part of the
same tag — is conditional, because factoring through the substack is tested by lifting the
classifying object through the inclusion, and that inclusion is constructed unconditionally.

"Equidimensional of dimension one" is read as the source's definition reads it: `X` is
equidimensional and every irreducible component of `X` has dimension one.
declarations.statement:
theorem lifts_nodalCurves_curveFamilyOfProperOverField_iff
    {T W : BigFppfOver B integerBase hZ} (g : T ⟶ W) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (hW : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).obj W = Spec (.of k))
    (hproper : IsProper ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).map g))
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).obj T) ≤ 1) :
    letI : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).obj T).Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
      ⟨(BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).map g ≫ eqToHom hW⟩
    ((∃ Y : (isNodalCurveFamily B hZ).FullSubcategory,
        Y.obj = curveFamilyOfProperOverFieldEqSpec B hZ g k hW hproper hdim) ↔
      (Stacks.Curves.HasAtWorstNodalSingularities k
          ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).obj T) ∧
        Equidimensional ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).obj T) ∧
        ∀ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).obj T),
          topologicalKrullDim Z = (1 : WithBot ℕ∞)))
declarations.comment: part (2): for a scheme X proper over a field k with dim(X) ≤ 1, the classifying morphism Spec(k) → Curves factors through Curves^{nodal} if and only if the singularities of X are at-worst-nodal and X is equidimensional of dimension 1. Factoring through the substack is lifting the classifying object through the inclusion of the strictly full subcategory of at-worst-nodal families, as in AlgebraicGeometry.lifts_nodalCurves_iff; no part of Tag 04S6 is assumed, and this declaration carries no hypothesis beyond the source's

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lifts_nodalCurvesInclusion_curveFamilyOfProperOverField_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSY, part (2).** Let `k` be a field and let `X ⟶ Spec(k)` be a morphism of the big
fppf site of the integers which is proper and whose source has dimension at most one. The
classifying morphism `Spec(k) → Curves` of the attached family of curves factors through the
open substack `Curves^{nodal}` if and only if the singularities of `X` are at worst nodal and
`X` is equidimensional of dimension one.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.lifts_nodalCurves_curveFamilyOfProperOverField_iff` with factoring
through `Curves^{nodal}` read as being in the image on objects of the 1-morphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.nodalCurvesInclusion`, so that the statement is about the same object as the
other registrations of the tag: the strictly full subcategory
`AlgebraicGeometry.nodalCurvesFiberedCategory` of the fibred category of families of curves,
whose inclusion is proved representable by algebraic spaces and an open immersion in
`AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_nodalCurvesInclusion` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_nodalCurvesInclusion`.

The hypotheses are those of the source: `X` is proper over the field and of dimension at most
one. Nothing else is assumed; in particular there is no algebraic stack `𝒳`, no equivalence
identifying it with the category of families of curves, and no part of Stacks 04S6.

"Equidimensional of dimension one" is read as the source's definition reads it: `X` is
equidimensional and every irreducible component of `X` has dimension one.
declarations.statement:
theorem lifts_nodalCurvesInclusion_curveFamilyOfProperOverField_iff
    {T W : BigFppfOver B integerBase hZ} (g : T ⟶ W) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (hW : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).obj W = Spec (.of k))
    (hproper : IsProper ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).map g))
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).obj T) ≤ 1) :
    letI : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).obj T).Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
      ⟨(BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).map g ≫ eqToHom hW⟩
    ((∃ Y : (nodalCurvesFiberedCategory B hZ).based.obj,
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (nodalCurvesInclusion B hZ)).obj Y =
          curveFamilyOfProperOverFieldEqSpec B hZ g k hW hproper hdim) ↔
      (Stacks.Curves.HasAtWorstNodalSingularities k
          ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).obj T) ∧
        Equidimensional ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).obj T) ∧
        ∀ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B integerBase hZ).obj T),
          topologicalKrullDim Z = (1 : WithBot ℕ∞)))
declarations.comment: part (2), stated through the inclusion 1-morphism AlgebraicGeometry.nodalCurvesInclusion of the open substack: for a scheme X proper over a field k with dim(X) ≤ 1, the classifying morphism Spec(k) → Curves factors through Curves^nodal if and only if the singularities of X are at-worst-nodal and X is equidimensional of dimension 1. Unconditional: no presentation of Curves as an algebraic stack (Tag 0D5A) and no part of Tag 04S6 is assumed, and this declaration carries no hypothesis beyond the source's

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNodalCurveFamily_of_hom
declarations.doc:
A family of curves mapping to an at-worst-nodal family of relative dimension one is itself
at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNodalCurveFamily_of_hom {F G : CurveFamily B hZ} (a : F ⟶ G)
    (hG : isNodalCurveFamily B hZ G) : isNodalCurveFamily B hZ F
declarations.comment: the open substack Curves^nodal, base-change clause: the at-worst-nodal condition is inherited along every morphism of families of curves, and a morphism of families is a cartesian square, so the subcategory is closed under base change. Unconditional: no presentation of Curves as an algebraic stack (Tag 0D5A) and no part of Tag 04S6 is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isNodalCurveFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSY.** The nodal condition cuts a *strictly* full subcategory out of the category
of families of curves: it is invariant under isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isNodalCurveFamily :
    (isNodalCurveFamily B hZ).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms
declarations.comment: the open substack Curves^nodal, strict-fullness clause: the at-worst-nodal condition is invariant under isomorphism of families of curves, so it cuts a strictly full subcategory out of Curves. Unconditional: no presentation of Curves as an algebraic stack (Tag 0D5A) and no part of Tag 04S6 is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nodalCurvesOpenSubstackUnconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSY, part (1).** The open substack `Curves^{nodal}` of families of curves which are
at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one, together with the characterisation of its objects: an
object of the stack belongs to it exactly when the family of curves it classifies is
at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.curvesOpenSubstackOfBaseLocus`, the method of Section 109.6, at the
locus `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_nodal_baseOpen`.

The algebraic stack of curves is a hypothesis: `𝒳` is any algebraic stack over the big fppf site
of the integers whose objects are identified with families of curves by an equivalence `E` over
that site. Nothing else is assumed; in particular no part of Stacks 04S6 is, the algebraic-stack
field of the substack coming from the unconditional Stacks 05UM.

Part (2) of the source, the characterisation for a proper scheme over a field, is not asserted
here.

The definition carries `@[no_expose]`: its body names the private helpers that build the
substack, so it may not be exposed. Nothing downstream needs to unfold it — the
characterisation of its objects is the second component of the subtype.
declarations.statement:
def nodalCurvesOpenSubstackUnconditional
    (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B integerBase hZ)
    (E : CurveFamily B hZ ≌ 𝒳.val.val.obj)
    (hE : E.functor ⋙ 𝒳.val.val.p = curvesProjectionOver B hZ) :
    {U : Stack.OpenSubstack 𝒳 //
      ∀ F : CurveFamily B hZ,
        U.property (E.functor.obj F) ↔
          Space.IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne B integerBase hZ F.toBase.hom}
declarations.comment: the open substack and part (1): the characterisation on every family of curves, given a presentation of the algebraic stack of curves. Part (2), the characterisation for a proper scheme over a field, is registered separately on `AlgebraicGeometry.lifts_nodalCurves_curveFamilyOfProperOverField_iff`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.classifying_factors_nodalCurvesOpenSubstack_iff_unconditional
declarations.doc:
