**Stacks 0DSY, part (1).** The classifying object of a family of curves lifts through the
inclusion of the nodal open substack exactly when the family is at-worst-nodal of relative
dimension one.

As for `AlgebraicGeometry.nodalCurvesOpenSubstackUnconditional`, the algebraic stack of curves
and its identification with families of curves are hypotheses, and nothing else is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem classifying_factors_nodalCurvesOpenSubstack_iff_unconditional
    (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B integerBase hZ)
    (E : CurveFamily B hZ ≌ 𝒳.val.val.obj)
    (hE : E.functor ⋙ 𝒳.val.val.p = curvesProjectionOver B hZ)
    (F : CurveFamily B hZ) :
    (∃ Y : (nodalCurvesOpenSubstackUnconditional B hZ 𝒳 E hE).1.property.FullSubcategory,
      Y.obj = E.functor.obj F) ↔
      Space.IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne B integerBase hZ F.toBase.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): the classifying morphism of a family factors through the nodal open substack iff the family is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one, given a presentation of the algebraic stack of curves. Part (2), the characterisation for a proper scheme over a field, is registered separately on `AlgebraicGeometry.lifts_nodalCurves_curveFamilyOfProperOverField_iff`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nodalCurvesFiberedCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSY.** The category `Curves^{nodal}` of families of curves which are at-worst-nodal
of relative dimension one, as an object of the 2-category of categories fibred in groupoids over
the big fppf site of `Spec(ℤ)`.
declarations.statement:
def nodalCurvesFiberedCategory :
    CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B integerBase hZ)
declarations.comment: the open substack Curves^nodal itself, as the strictly full subcategory of Curves spanned by the families which are at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one, read as an object of the 2-category of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of Spec(Z). Unconditional: no presentation of Curves as an algebraic stack (Tag 0D5A) and no part of Tag 04S6 is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nodalCurvesInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSY.** The inclusion `Curves^{nodal} ⊂ Curves`, as a 1-morphism of categories
fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `Spec(ℤ)`.
declarations.statement:
def nodalCurvesInclusion :
    nodalCurvesFiberedCategory B hZ ⟶ curvesFiberedCategory B hZ
declarations.comment: the inclusion Curves^nodal ⊂ Curves of the open substack, as a 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of Spec(Z). Unconditional: no presentation of Curves as an algebraic stack (Tag 0D5A) and no part of Tag 04S6 is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_nodalCurvesInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSY.** The inclusion `Curves^{nodal} ⊂ Curves` is representable by algebraic
spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_nodalCurvesInclusion :
    Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B integerBase hZ (nodalCurvesInclusion B hZ).hom
declarations.comment: the open substack Curves^nodal, representability clause: the inclusion Curves^nodal ⊂ Curves is representable by algebraic spaces. Unconditional: no presentation of Curves as an algebraic stack (Tag 0D5A) and no part of Tag 04S6 is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_nodalCurvesInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSY.** The inclusion `Curves^{nodal} ⊂ Curves` is an open immersion: every
algebraic space representing one of its base changes along a scheme-valued point of `Curves` has
open immersion structural morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_nodalCurvesInclusion :
    Stack.IsOpenImmersion B integerBase hZ (nodalCurvesInclusion B hZ)
declarations.comment: the open substack Curves^nodal, open-immersion clause: the inclusion Curves^nodal ⊂ Curves is an open immersion in the sense of Tag 04XB. Unconditional: no presentation of Curves as an algebraic stack (Tag 0D5A) and no part of Tag 04S6 is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lifts_nodalCurves_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSY, part (1).** A family of curves lifts through the inclusion
`Curves^{nodal} ⊂ Curves` exactly when it is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one.
declarations.statement:
theorem lifts_nodalCurves_iff (F : CurveFamily B hZ) :
    (∃ Y : (isNodalCurveFamily B hZ).FullSubcategory, Y.obj = F) ↔
      Space.IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne B integerBase hZ F.toBase.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): the classifying morphism of a family of curves factors through Curves^nodal -- that is, the family lifts through the inclusion of the strictly full subcategory -- if and only if the family is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one. Unconditional: no presentation of Curves as an algebraic stack (Tag 0D5A) and no part of Tag 04S6 is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lifts_nodalCurvesInclusion_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DSY, part (1).** The classifying morphism of a family of curves factors through
`Curves^{nodal}` exactly when the family is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one, where
factoring through `Curves^{nodal}` is being in the image on objects of the 1-morphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.nodalCurvesInclusion` itself.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.lifts_nodalCurves_iff` read through that 1-morphism, so that part (1)
is asserted about the very object whose inclusion is proved representable by algebraic spaces
and an open immersion in
`AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_nodalCurvesInclusion` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_nodalCurvesInclusion`.

The declaration carries no hypothesis beyond the site and its containing `Spec(ℤ)`: there is no
algebraic stack `𝒳` and no equivalence identifying it with the category of families of
curves.
declarations.statement:
theorem lifts_nodalCurvesInclusion_iff (F : CurveFamily B hZ) :
    (∃ Y : (nodalCurvesFiberedCategory B hZ).based.obj,
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (nodalCurvesInclusion B hZ)).obj Y = F) ↔
      Space.IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne B integerBase hZ F.toBase.hom
declarations.comment: part (1), stated through the inclusion 1-morphism AlgebraicGeometry.nodalCurvesInclusion of the open substack: a family of curves is in the image on objects of Curves^nodal ⟶ Curves if and only if it is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one. Unconditional: no presentation of Curves as an algebraic stack (Tag 0D5A) and no part of Tag 04S6 is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalenceRelation_of_unramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DT7.** An unramified pre-relation which is an equivalence relation on
points over every algebraically closed field, and whose reflexivity, symmetry, and composition
operations are represented by morphisms, is an equivalence relation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalenceRelation_of_unramified
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {R U : Over S} (j : PreRelation R U)
    [Unramified j.source.left] [Unramified j.target.left]
    (hpoints : ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
      (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S),
      (Function.Injective (fun r : Over.mk p ⟶ R ↦ r ≫ j) ∧
        Equivalence (j.Rel (T := Over.mk p))))
    (e : U ⟶ R)
    (he_target : e ≫ j.target = 𝟙 U)
    (he_source : e ≫ j.source = 𝟙 U)
    (i : R ⟶ R)
    (hi_target : i ≫ j.target = j.source)
    (hi_source : i ≫ j.source = j.target)
    (c : pullback j.source j.target ⟶ R)
    (hc_target : c ≫ j.target = pullback.fst j.source j.target ≫ j.target)
    (hc_source : c ≫ j.source = pullback.snd j.source j.target ≫ j.source) :
    IsEquivalenceRelation j.target j.source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Base-changing the object and arrow schemes of a groupoid scheme, and all its structure
maps, produces a groupoid scheme over the new base whose projections form a morphism of
groupoid schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_baseChange {S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : S' ⟶ S)
    (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S) : Nonempty (BaseChange f G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.etale_invariantRingMap
declarations.doc:
**The first conclusion of [Stacks Project, Tag 0DT9]: the map `C ⟶ C'` from the `R`-invariant
functions on `U` to the `R'`-invariant functions on `U'` is étale.**

The four hypotheses of the source are all present: that `U`, `R`, `U'`, `R'` are affine is the four
`IsAffine` instances; that `s`, `t`, `s'`, `t'` are finite locally free is the four
`IsFiniteLocallyFree` instances; the three cartesian squares are `hsource`, `htarget` and `hstab`;
and that `f : U' → U` is étale is `[Etale F.mapObjects.left]`.

Étaleness is checked point by point with the source-cover criterion
`AlgebraicGeometry.etale_of_forall_exists_etale_comp`, whose covering family is supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_etale_comp_invariantRingMap`. No finite presentation
hypothesis on `Spec C' ⟶ Spec C` is needed, which matters because local finite presentation is
itself part of the conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_invariantRingMap
    (hsource : IsPullback F.mapArrows.left G'.source.left G.source.left F.mapObjects.left)
    (htarget : IsPullback F.mapArrows.left G'.target.left G.target.left F.mapObjects.left)
    (hstab : IsPullback (stabilizerMap F).left (stabilizer G').hom (stabilizer G).hom
      F.mapObjects.left) :
    (invariantRingMap F).Etale
declarations.comment: the FIRST conclusion: the map C -> C' from the R-invariant functions on U to the R'-invariant functions on U' is etale. Together with isPullback_mapObjects, which is the second conclusion, this is the whole statement of the tag

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.isPullback_mapObjects
declarations.doc:
**The second conclusion of [Stacks Project, Tag 0DT9]: `U' = Spec C' ×_{Spec C} U`.**

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.isPullback_mapObjects_of_etale_invariantRingMap` with its
hypothesis `hC` discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.etale_invariantRingMap`, the first conclusion of the tag. The
cartesian `s'/s` square is not needed for the implication from the first conclusion to the second,
but it is a hypothesis of the first, so it appears here too.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_mapObjects
    (hsource : IsPullback F.mapArrows.left G'.source.left G.source.left F.mapObjects.left)
    (htarget : IsPullback F.mapArrows.left G'.target.left G.target.left F.mapObjects.left)
    (hstab : IsPullback (stabilizerMap F).left (stabilizer G').hom (stabilizer G).hom
      F.mapObjects.left) :
    IsPullback F.mapObjects.left (objectsToInvariantSpectrum G')
      (objectsToInvariantSpectrum G) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (invariantRingMap F)))
declarations.comment: the SECOND conclusion: U' is the fibre product of Spec C' and U over Spec C. Unconditional: the premise that C -> C' is etale is supplied by etale_invariantRingMap, the tag's first conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.baseChange
declarations.doc: Pull back a groupoid in algebraic spaces along a morphism of bases.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SplittingSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DTB.** The standing splitting situation for a groupoid scheme at
a point of its object scheme.
declarations.statement: structure SplittingSituation

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.exists_split_of_splittingSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DTC.**  In the splitting situation of Stacks 0DTB there are an
algebraic space `U'`, an étale morphism `g : U' ⟶ U` of algebraic spaces and a point
`u' : Spec κ(u) ⟶ U'` lying over `u : Spec κ(u) ⟶ U` such that the restriction `R' = R|_{U'}`
of `R` to `U'` is split over `u'`.

`U'` is the object space of the finite part `(R_s/U, e)_fin` of Stacks 04RU, `g` its étale
projection, `u'` the pair `(u, Z_u)` where `Z_u` is the open and closed piece of the fibre
`F_u = R ×_{s, U} Spec κ(u)` supported on the arrows underlying the points of the stabilizer
group scheme over `u`, and the splitting is the universal open `Z_univ` read inside `R|_{U'}`.
Being split is a condition on a point of `|U'|`, so it is asserted at the point of `|U'|` which
the morphism `u' : Spec κ(u) ⟶ U'` determines.

The standing hypothesis is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SplittingSituation`, Situation 0DTB, and not
the strictly stronger `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.StrongSplittingSituation` of Stacks 04RL: the
open `Z_u` is supported on the stabilizer, which is in general a proper subset of the arrows
with both endpoints at `u`.  So this is not a formal consequence of Stacks 03FM,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_stronglySplit_of_strongSplittingSituation`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_split_of_splittingSituation
    (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SplittingSituation.{u})
    (C : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : C.Contains D.S)
    (hU : C.Contains D.groupoid.objects.left)
    (hR : C.Contains D.groupoid.arrows.left)
    (hP : C.Contains (pullback D.groupoid.source D.groupoid.target).left)
    (hK : C.Contains (Spec (D.groupoid.objects.left.residueField D.u))) :
    ∃ (U' : AlgebraicSpaces C D.S hS)
      (g : U' ⟶ (D.groupoid.realization C hS hU hR hP).objects),
      IsEtale C D.S hS g.hom ∧
      ∃ v : U'.obj.obj (Opposite.op
          (schemeSiteObject C hS (X := residueOver D.groupoid D.u) hK)),
        (yonedaSchemePointEquiv C hS hU (Opposite.op
            (schemeSiteObject C hS (X := residueOver D.groupoid D.u) hK))
            (g.hom.app _ v)).left =
          D.groupoid.objects.left.fromSpecResidueField D.u ∧
        GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.IsSplitAt
          (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.restrict (D.groupoid.realization C hS hU hR hP)
            g).groupoid
          ((residueSectionValuedPoint D.groupoid C hS D.u hK U' v).class C D.S hS U'.obj)
declarations.comment: ALL FOUR ASSERTIONS, in Situation 0DTB: the algebraic space U', the etale morphism g : U' -> U, the point u' : Spec k(u) -> U' lying over u, and that the restriction R|_{U'} is SPLIT over u' -- all four PRODUCED, none assumed. The situation hypothesis is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SplittingSituation, which carries the 0DTB attribute, and NOT the stronger StrongSplittingSituation of Tag 04RL. Beyond Situation 0DTB the only hypotheses are that the big fppf site contains the base, object, arrow and composable-pair schemes and Spec k(u), which is this library's standing ambient requirement. The supporting open of the fibre is the stabilizer-supported one of SplittingSituation.exists_fiberOpens_stabilizer, a proper subset in general of the target-condition open that Tag 03FM uses

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.exists_etale_separated_scheme_split
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DTD.**

In the splitting situation of Stacks 0DTB, with the source in addition flat and locally of finite
presentation, there are a scheme `U'`, a separated étale morphism `g : U' ⟶ U`, and a point `u'`
of `U'` over `u` with `κ(u) = κ(u')`, such that the restriction `R' = R|_{U'}` is split over
`u'`.

The neighbourhood is `U' = (R_s/U, e)_{fin}`, the finite part of Stacks 04RU containing the
unit, with its étale projection; it is a scheme by Stacks 04RI part (2) and Stacks 04RR part
(4), and the projection is separated by Stacks 04RI part (1) and Stacks 04RR part (1).  The
point and the splitting are those of Stacks 0DTC, the point being recorded as a section over
`Spec κ(u)` whose image under `g` is the canonical morphism `Spec κ(u) ⟶ U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_separated_scheme_split
    (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SplittingSituation.{u})
    (C : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : C.Contains D.S)
    (hU : C.Contains D.groupoid.objects.left)
    (hR : C.Contains D.groupoid.arrows.left)
    (hP : C.Contains (pullback D.groupoid.source D.groupoid.target).left)
    (hK : C.Contains (Spec (D.groupoid.objects.left.residueField D.u)))
    (hflat : AlgebraicGeometry.Flat D.groupoid.source.left)
    (hfp : AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.groupoid.source.left) :
    ∃ (U' : AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpaces C D.S hS)
      (g : U' ⟶ (D.groupoid.realization C hS hU hR hP).objects),
      U'.obj.IsRepresentable ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtale C D.S hS g.hom ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparated C D.S hS g.hom ∧
      ∃ v : U'.obj.obj (Opposite.op
          (schemeSiteObject C hS (X := residueOver D.groupoid D.u) hK)),
        (yonedaSchemePointEquiv C hS hU (Opposite.op
            (schemeSiteObject C hS (X := residueOver D.groupoid D.u) hK))
            (g.hom.app _ v)).left =
          D.groupoid.objects.left.fromSpecResidueField D.u ∧
        IsSplitAt
          (restrict (D.groupoid.realization C hS hU hR hP) g).groupoid
          ((residueSectionValuedPoint D.groupoid C hS D.u hK U' v).class C D.S hS U'.obj)
declarations.comment:
in Situation 0DTB with the source flat and locally of finite presentation: U' is
a SCHEME (asserted as representability of the neighbourhood), U' ⟶ U is SEPARATED as well as
étale, and R|_{U'} is SPLIT over a Spec κ(u)-valued point of U' lying over u. The neighbourhood,
its point and the splitting are Stacks 0DTC, which this library proves as
`Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.exists_split_of_splittingSituation`; the scheme-ness and the
separatedness are Stacks 04RI and Stacks 04RR applied to the finite part (R_s/U, e)_fin, through
its identification with the neighbourhood recorded by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FinitePartUniversalOpen.objectsEquiv` and `objectProjection_spec`.
Splitting is Stacks 04RK part (2) for the restriction of the REALIZATION of the groupoid scheme,
as in this library's Stacks 0DTC and Stacks 04RX; the scheme-level
`Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.Splitting` is not used, the composition of the restricted
realization not being compared with the composition of
`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.restrict`. The residue-field clause κ(u) = κ(u') is the
section over Spec κ(u): a section of a representable U' is a point u' of U' over u together with
a retraction of the residue field map at u', and a retraction forces that map to be an
isomorphism by `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isIso_residueFieldMap_of_retraction`. Only flatness
and local finite presentation of the SOURCE are assumed, where the tag asks them of the target
too, so the hypotheses are weaker than the tag's. Beyond Situation 0DTB the remaining hypotheses
are that the big fppf site contains the base, object, arrow and composable-pair schemes and
Spec κ(u), this library's standing ambient requirement

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.exists_isAffine_isSplitAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DTE.**

In the splitting situation of Stacks 0DTB, with `s` and `t` in addition flat and locally of
finite presentation and with `U` affine, there are an affine scheme `U''`, an étale morphism
`U'' ⟶ U` and a point `u''` of `U''` over `u` with `κ(u) = κ(u'')`, such that the restriction of
`R` to `U''` is split over `u''`.

The étale neighbourhood `U'` of Stacks 0DTD is shrunk to an affine one: `U''` is an invariant
affine open of the object scheme of the splitting of `R' = R|_{U'}`, so `U'' ⟶ U'` is an open
immersion and the restriction of that splitting to `U''` is a splitting of `R'|_{U''}` over
`u''`.  The restriction is taken in two steps, as the restriction of `R'` to `U''`; its
identification with the restriction of `R` along the composite `U'' ⟶ U' ⟶ U` is
Stacks 04MW.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffine_isSplitAt
    (D : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SplittingSituation.{u})
    (C : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : C.Contains D.S)
    (hU : C.Contains D.groupoid.objects.left) (hR : C.Contains D.groupoid.arrows.left)
    (hP : C.Contains (pullback D.groupoid.source D.groupoid.target).left)
    (hK : C.Contains (Spec (D.groupoid.objects.left.residueField D.u)))
    [IsAffine D.groupoid.objects.left]
    [Flat D.groupoid.source.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.groupoid.source.left]
    [Flat D.groupoid.target.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.groupoid.target.left] :
    ∃ (U' : Over D.S) (g : U' ⟶ D.groupoid.objects)
      (R' : AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.Restriction D.groupoid g)
      (U'' : Over D.S) (j : U'' ⟶ R'.groupoid.objects) (u'' : U''.left),
      IsAffine U''.left ∧ IsOpenImmersion j.left ∧
      Etale (j ≫ R'.hom.mapObjects).left ∧
      (j ≫ R'.hom.mapObjects).left.base u'' = D.u ∧
      IsIso ((j ≫ R'.hom.mapObjects).left.residueFieldMap u'') ∧
      ∀ R'' : AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.Restriction R'.groupoid j,
        IsSplitAt R''.groupoid ((eqToHom R''.objects_eq.symm).left.base u'')
declarations.comment:
in Situation 0DTB with s, t flat and locally of finite presentation and U affine:
an affine scheme U'', an étale U'' ⟶ U and a point u'' over u with κ(u) = κ(u''), such that
R|_{U''} is SPLIT over u'' -- all of it PRODUCED: the neighbourhood, the point and the splitting
are conclusions of this theorem, never inputs to it. Splitting is Stacks 04RK part (2) read for a
groupoid scheme, stated in
this file as `Splitting`: an open subscheme P of the arrow scheme which (a) is a groupoid scheme
on the same object scheme, with composition the restriction of the ambient one, (b) has s|_P and
t|_P finite, and (c) contains the arrow underlying every point of the stabilizer group scheme
`AlgebraicGeometry.stabilizer` lying over the point; (a) and (b) are `OpenFiniteSubgroupoid`,
which carries the 04RK attribute, and (c) is the field `contains_stabilizer`. The situation
hypothesis is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SplittingSituation`, which carries the 0DTB attribute, and not the
stronger `StrongSplittingSituation` of Tag 04RL. R|_{U''} is covered in its two-step reading, as
the restriction to U'' of R' = R|_{U'} for the étale neighbourhood U' of Stacks 0DTD, rather
than as the restriction of R along the composite U'' ⟶ U' ⟶ U; the identification of the two is
Stacks 04MW, which this library has as the comparison diagram `doubleRestrictionDiagram` and not
as an identification of realizations. The conclusion is stronger than the tag in two respects:
U'' ⟶ U' is an open immersion, not merely étale, and the splitting is produced for EVERY
groupoid scheme realizing that restriction. Beyond Situation 0DTB the hypotheses are that the
big fppf site contains the base, object, arrow and composable-pair schemes and Spec κ(u), this
library's standing ambient requirement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientSheaf_isPullback_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTF.** The quotient sheaf of the base change of an invariant pre-relation along
`f : X' ⟶ X` is the fibre product of `X'` and the original quotient sheaf over `X`. The three
canonical maps are specified by their composites with the quotient projections.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientSheaf_isPullback_baseChange (j : PreRelation R U)
    (hX : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology site S hS) X)
    (hX' : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology site S hS) X')
    (φ : U.left ⟶ X) (f : X' ⟶ X) (hφ : IsInvariant j φ) :
    let j' := (baseChangedPreRelation j φ f hφ).val
    ∃ (qToX : quotientSheaf j ⟶ baseSheaf hX)
      (q'ToX' : quotientSheaf j' ⟶ baseSheaf hX')
      (q'ToQ : quotientSheaf j' ⟶ quotientSheaf j),
      (toQuotientSheaf j ≫ qToX.hom = φ) ∧
      (toQuotientSheaf j' ≫ q'ToX'.hom = pullback.fst f φ) ∧
      (toQuotientSheaf j' ≫ q'ToQ.hom = pullback.snd f φ ≫ toQuotientSheaf j) ∧
      IsPullback q'ToX' q'ToQ ⟨f⟩ qToX

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.baseChangeQuotientStackSquare_isTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTG, the 2-fibre product.** For a groupoid in algebraic spaces `(U, R, s, t, c)`
over an algebraic space `B` over a scheme `S` of a big fppf site, an `R`-invariant morphism
`φ : U ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `B` and a morphism `g : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over
`B`, the 2-commutative square

    [U'/R'] ---> [U/R]
      |            |
      v            v
     𝒮_{X'} ---> 𝒮_X

of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.baseChangeQuotientStackSquare` is a 2-fibre product (Stacks 003Q),
where `(U', R', s', t', c')` is the base change of Stacks 048G.

Its comparison 1-morphism is faithful by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.faithful_comparison`, locally essentially surjective on fibres by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.locallyEssSurjOnFibers_baseChangeQuotientStackComparison` and full by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.full_baseChangeQuotientStackComparison`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseChangeQuotientStackSquare_isTwoFibreProduct :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct
      (baseChangeQuotientStackSquare.{u, w} G XtoB X'toB g hg φ hφB hφ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.baseChangeQuotientStackSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTG, the displayed square.** For a groupoid in algebraic spaces `(U, R, s, t, c)`
over an algebraic space `B` over a scheme `S` of a big fppf site, an `R`-invariant morphism
`φ : U ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `B` and a morphism `g : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over
`B`, the square

    [U'/R'] ---> [U/R]
      |            |
      v            v
     𝒮_{X'} ---> 𝒮_X

of stacks in groupoids over the big fppf site 2-commutes, where `(U', R', s', t', c')` is the
base change of Stacks 048G. It is a 2-commutative diagram over the cospan in the sense of
Stacks 003O, with its filling 2-isomorphism an identity.

The further assertion of Stacks 0DTG, that this square is a 2-fibre product, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.baseChangeQuotientStackSquare_isTwoFibreProduct`; hence the qualifier on
the tag here.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseChangeQuotientStackSquare :
    let J := BigFppfOver.topology C S hS
    let Q : StackInGroupoids (BigFppfOver C S hS) J :=
      ⟨quotientStack (invariantTargetGroupoid G XtoB φ hφB hφ),
        isStackInGroupoids_quotientStack _⟩
    let SX : StackInGroupoids (BigFppfOver C S hS) J :=
      ⟨liftedFibredCategory X, isStackInGroupoids_liftedFibredCategory X⟩
    let SX' : StackInGroupoids (BigFppfOver C S hS) J :=
      ⟨liftedFibredCategory X', isStackInGroupoids_liftedFibredCategory X'⟩
    Bicategory.TwoCommSq
      (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom
        (liftedQuotientStackToBase (invariantTargetGroupoid G XtoB φ hφB hφ)) : Q ⟶ SX)
      (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom (liftedAssociatedMap g) : SX' ⟶ SX)
declarations.comment: the displayed square and its 2-commutativity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.residualGerbeMap
declarations.doc:
**The 1-morphism induced by `f` on residual gerbes, Stacks 0DTH.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a
1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`, let `P` cut out a substack `𝒵_x` of `𝒳` and let `Q` cut
out a substack `𝒵_y` of `𝒴`. If `f` carries every object of `𝒳` with the property `P` to an
object of `𝒴` with the property `Q`, then it induces a 1-morphism `𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒵_y`, namely the lift
through the full subcategory `𝒵_y` of the underlying functor of `𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`.

In the application `P` and `Q` are the residual gerbes of `𝒳` at `x` and of `𝒴` at its image,
and `hmem` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.map_mem_of_isResidualGerbeAt`.
declarations.statement:
def residualGerbeMap
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    {P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj} {Q : ObjectProperty 𝒴.val.val.obj}
    (hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P))
    (hQ : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒴 Q))
    (hmem : ∀ ξ : 𝒳.val.val.obj, P ξ → Q (f.hom.hom.toFunctor.obj ξ)) :
    fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 P hP ⟶ fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒴 Q hQ
declarations.comment: the 1-morphism induced between substacks whose objects f carries into one another

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.residualGerbeMap_comp_inclusion
declarations.doc:
**The commutative square of Stacks 0DTH.** The induced 1-morphism `𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒵_y` composed with
the inclusion of `𝒵_y` into `𝒴` is the inclusion of `𝒵_x` into `𝒳` composed with `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem residualGerbeMap_comp_inclusion
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    {P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj} {Q : ObjectProperty 𝒴.val.val.obj}
    (hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒳 P))
    (hQ : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒴 Q))
    (hmem : ∀ ξ : 𝒳.val.val.obj, P ξ → Q (f.hom.hom.toFunctor.obj ξ)) :
    residualGerbeMap B S hS f hP hQ hmem ≫ fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒴 Q hQ =
      fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 P hP ≫ f
declarations.comment: the commutativity of the square for that 1-morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.residualGerbeMap_comp_inclusion_of_isResidualGerbeAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTH.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`, let `x` be a
point of `𝒳` and let `y` be its image under `f`. Assume the residual gerbes of `𝒳` at `x` and of
`𝒴` at `y` exist, cut out by the object properties `P` and `Q` respectively, in the sense of the
specification `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt` of Stacks 06MT. Then `f` induces a
commutative square: the 1-morphism `residualGerbeMap` from the residual gerbe at `x` to the
residual gerbe at `y`, composed with the inclusion of the latter, is the inclusion of the former
composed with `f`.

That `f` carries the residual gerbe at `x` into the one at `y` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.map_mem_of_isResidualGerbeAt`, the source's argument through Stacks 06MQ;
it uses the bootstrap theorem Stacks 04S6 part (3) for the representability by algebraic spaces
of the inclusion of the residual gerbe at `y` that the source takes from Stacks 04Y5.
declarations.statement:
theorem residualGerbeMap_comp_inclusion_of_isResidualGerbeAt
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒳.property))
    (y : points B S hS 𝒴.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒴.property))
    (hxy : pointsMap B S hS 𝒳.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒳.property)
      (Classical.choose 𝒴.property) f.hom.hom x = y)
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj) (Q : ObjectProperty 𝒴.val.val.obj)
    (hx : IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x P) (hy : IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒴 y Q) :
    residualGerbeMap B S hS f hx.2.choose hy.2.choose
        (map_mem_of_isResidualGerbeAt B S hS f x y hxy hx hy) ≫
        fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒴 Q hy.2.choose =
      fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 P hx.2.choose ≫ f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalenceOver_residualGerbeMap_of_hasSelfProductEquivalenceAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTI.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`, let `x` be a
point of `|𝒳|` and let the object properties `P` of `𝒳` and `Q` of `𝒴` be residual gerbes of `𝒳`
at `x` and of `𝒴` at the image of `x`, in the sense of the specification
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt` of **Stacks 06MT**. If there is a 1-morphism from the
algebraic stack of the spectrum of a field to `𝒳` in the equivalence class of `x` whose
self-product comparison over `𝒳` and over `𝒴` is an equivalence, then the 1-morphism
`𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒵_y` induced by `f` --- the **Stacks 0DTH** map
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.residualGerbeMap` --- is an isomorphism: an equivalence over the big
fppf site of `S`.

The proof is the source's. Full faithfulness of `𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`, the source's first two
paragraphs, is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.full_and_faithful_comp_of_hasSelfProductEquivalenceAt`.
The concluding sentence is taken through **Stacks 06MQ**: the **Stacks 0DTH** square commutes on
the nose, so cancelling the faithful inclusion `𝒵_y ⟶ 𝒴` makes `𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒵_y` fully faithful, hence
a monomorphism by the implication (2) ⟹ (1) of **Stacks 04ZZ** once it is known representable by
algebraic spaces. The residual gerbe `𝒵_y` is reduced, locally Noetherian and one-point by its
specification, so it is covered by the spectrum of a field by the implication (1) ⟹ (2) of
**Stacks 06MP**, and `|𝒵_x|` is nonempty by its own specification, which rules out the empty
alternative of Stacks 06MQ.

The representability of `𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒵_y`, and of the inclusion `𝒵_y ⟶ 𝒴` behind the Stacks 0DTH map,
is what the source takes from Stacks 04Y5; the library has the implication (2) ⟹ (3) of
Stacks 04Y5 from the bootstrap theorem Stacks 04S6 part (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalenceOver_residualGerbeMap_of_hasSelfProductEquivalenceAt
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj) (Q : ObjectProperty 𝒴.val.val.obj)
    (hx : IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x P)
    (hy : IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒴 (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS f x) Q)
    (hself : HasSelfProductEquivalenceAt B S hS f x) :
    Nonempty (Functor.IsEquivalenceOver
      (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 P hx.2.choose).val.val.p
      (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒴 Q hy.2.choose).val.val.p
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor
        (residualGerbeMap B S hS f hx.2.choose hy.2.choose
          (map_mem_of_isResidualGerbeAt B S hS f x _ rfl hx hy)).hom))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isQuasiCompactFieldValuedPoint_iff_forall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTK.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` and let `x` be a point of `𝒳`. Some
morphism `Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` in the equivalence class of `x` is quasi-compact if and only if every
morphism `Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` in the equivalence class of `x` is quasi-compact.

Two field-valued representatives of `x` admit a common refinement (**Stacks 04XF**), and the
arrow to each of them carries quasi-compactness from the refinement and to it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isQuasiCompactFieldValuedPoint_iff_forall (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids) :
    (∃ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val.val,
        pointClass B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids p = x ∧
          IsQuasiCompactFieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val p) ↔
      ∀ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val.val,
        pointClass B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids p = x →
          IsQuasiCompactFieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_isQuasiCompactMorphism_fst
declarations.doc:
Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` and let
`g : W ⟶ 𝒴` be surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, where `W` is an algebraic
space. If the base change `W ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ W` of `f` along `g` is quasi-compact, then `f` is
quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_isQuasiCompactMorphism_fst
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    {W : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS W)
    (g : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS W hW ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hgsurj : IsSurjective B S hS g)
    (hgflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hglfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hbase : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS P.fst) :
    IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fiber_lift_of_universallyInjective
declarations.doc:
Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a universally injective 1-morphism of algebraic stacks and `y : Spec k ⟶ 𝒴`
a morphism with `k` algebraically closed. If `y` is in the image of `|𝒳| → |𝒴|`, then there is
`x : Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` with `y = f ∘ x`: an object `x` of the fibre of `𝒳` over the base of `y` whose
image under `f` is isomorphic to `y` in that fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fiber_lift_of_universallyInjective
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.UniversallyInjective B S hS f)
    (y : AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒴.val.val)
    [IsAlgClosed y.carrier]
    (hy : AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.pointClass B S hS 𝒴.val.val
      𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids y ∈
        Set.range (AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.pointsMap B S hS 𝒳.val.val
          𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids 𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids f.hom.hom)) :
    ∃ x : 𝒳.val.val.p.Fiber y.base,
      Nonempty
        (((Functor.fiberMap 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p
          f.hom.hom.toFunctor f.hom.hom.w y.base).obj x) ≅
          (⟨y.obj, y.over⟩ : 𝒴.val.val.p.Fiber y.base))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyInjective_iff_affineBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTN.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` is universally
injective if and only if for every affine scheme `U` of the big fppf site over `S` and every
1-morphism from the algebraic stack it represents to `𝒴`, the base change of `f` is universally
injective.

The base change is an arbitrary 2-fibre product of the cospan, as in **Stacks 0CI2** itself, so
neither side depends on a chosen model.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_iff_affineBaseChange (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    UniversallyInjective B S hS f ↔
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS), IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) →
        ∀ (g : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U ⟶ 𝒴) (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f),
          Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P → UniversallyInjective B S hS P.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyInjective_of_fppfCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTP.** Universal injectivity of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` can be
checked after base change along a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented 1-morphism from
the stack of an algebraic space onto its target.

Only surjectivity of the cover is used; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyInjective_of_isSurjective_baseChange`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_of_fppfCover
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (W : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS W)
    (g : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS W hW ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hgSurj : IsSurjective B S hS g)
    (_hgFlat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS g)
    (_hgLfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g)
    (hgf : UniversallyInjective B S hS
      (AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProductSquare B S hS g f).fst) :
    UniversallyInjective B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universalHomeomorphism_of_fppfCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTQ.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` and let
`g : 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒴` be a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented 1-morphism from the stack of an
algebraic space. If the base change `𝒲 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒲` of `f` along `g` is a universal
homeomorphism, then so is `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalHomeomorphism_of_fppfCover {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (W : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS W)
    (g : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS W hW ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hgSurj : IsSurjective B S hS g)
    (hgFlat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hgLfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g)
    (hgf : UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS
      (AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProductSquare B S hS g f).fst) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentable_pointAutomorphismSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTS.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` and let `x : Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` be a
field-valued point with automorphism group algebraic space `G_x = Isom_𝒳(x, x)` over `Spec k`.
Then `G_x` is a scheme if one of the following holds: the diagonal `Δ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 × 𝒳` is
quasi-separated, `Δ` is locally separated, `𝒳` is quasi-DM, the inertia projection
`I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is quasi-separated, `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is locally separated, or `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is locally
quasi-finite.

Products are over `S` (Properties of Stacks, Section 04XA), the properties of `Δ` and of
`I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` are taken in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB, quasi-DM is the absolute
notion of Stacks 050D (over `Spec ℤ`), and "is a scheme" is representability of the presheaf
`G_x` on the big fppf site of `Spec k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_pointAutomorphismSpace (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (x : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val.val)
    (h : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val) ∨
      IsLocallySeparated B S hS (diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val) ∨
      AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS B.contains_terminal 𝒳 ∨
      IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳).hom ∨
      IsLocallySeparated B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳).hom ∨
      IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳).hom) :
    (pointAutomorphismSpace B S hS 𝒳.val x).IsRepresentable
declarations.comment: the automorphism group algebraic space of a field-valued point is a scheme under any of the six conditions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_pointAutomorphismSpace_iff_forall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTT.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack, let `q ∈ |𝒳|` be a point and let `P` be a
property of algebraic spaces over fields which is invariant under ground field extensions. Then
the automorphism group algebraic space `G_x/k` has `P` for *some* field-valued representative
`x : Spec k → 𝒳` of `q` if and only if it has `P` for *every* field-valued representative.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pointAutomorphismSpace_iff_forall
    (q : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids)
    (P : ∀ U : BigFppfOver B S hS, ((BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) → Prop)
    (hP : IsInvariantUnderGroundFieldExtension B S hS P) :
    (∃ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val.val,
        pointClass B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids p = q ∧
        P p.base (pointAutomorphismSpace B S hS 𝒳.val p)) ↔
      ∀ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val.val,
        pointClass B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids p = q →
        P p.base (pointAutomorphismSpace B S hS 𝒳.val p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AutomorphismGroupHasProperty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTU.** Let `P` be a property of algebraic spaces over fields and let `q` be a point
of `|𝒳|` for an algebraic stack `𝒳`. The *automorphism group of `𝒳` at `q` has `P`* when the
automorphism group algebraic space `G_x/k = Isom_𝒳(x, x)` has `P` for every field-valued
representative `x : Spec k → 𝒳` of `q`.

This is condition (2) of Stacks 0DTT, so it makes no choice of representative. When `P` is
invariant under ground field extensions
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsInvariantUnderGroundFieldExtension`) it agrees with condition (1) of
Stacks 0DTT by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.automorphismGroupHasProperty_iff_exists`, and it is
decided by any single representative by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.automorphismGroupHasProperty_iff_of_representative`; that is what makes
the phrase well posed, and it is the content of Remark 0DTU.
declarations.statement:
def AutomorphismGroupHasProperty
    (P : ∀ U : BigFppfOver B S hS, ((BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) → Prop)
    (q : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids) : Prop
declarations.comment: the definition: the automorphism group of a stack at a point has P when the automorphism group algebraic space of every field-valued representative has P

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.automorphismGroupHasProperty_iff_of_representative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTU: the phrase is well posed.** For a property `P` of algebraic spaces over fields
which is invariant under ground field extensions, the statement that the automorphism group of
`𝒳` at `q` has `P` is decided by an arbitrary single field-valued representative `p` of `q`:
it holds exactly when the automorphism group algebraic space `G_p` has `P`. In particular the
answer does not depend on which representative of `q` one reads it at, which is what licenses
the phrase "the automorphism group of `𝒳` at `q` has `P`" of Remark 0DTU.
declarations.statement:
theorem automorphismGroupHasProperty_iff_of_representative
    (P : ∀ U : BigFppfOver B S hS, ((BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) → Prop)
    (hP : IsInvariantUnderGroundFieldExtension B S hS P)
    {q : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids}
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val.val)
    (hp : pointClass B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids p = q) :
    AutomorphismGroupHasProperty B S hS P q ↔
      P p.base (pointAutomorphismSpace B S hS 𝒳.val p)
declarations.comment: the phrase is well posed: for a property invariant under ground field extensions, an arbitrary single field-valued representative decides it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inducesIsomorphismAt_iff_forall_representatives
declarations.doc:
A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks induces an isomorphism between automorphism groups at a
point of `|𝒳|` exactly when it does so at *every* object lying above *every* field-valued
representative of that point: one pullback of one representative above each object of the big
site already decides it, because in a category fibred in groupoids any two lifts of the same
morphism of the base are isomorphic over an identity.

This is Stacks 0DTV for the lifts of one field-valued representative. Passing between two
representatives of the same point is a descent statement, proved for the automorphism group
algebraic spaces in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isIso_pointAutomorphismSpaceMap_iff_forall`: the map of
automorphism group algebraic spaces over a field extension is a base change, and being an
isomorphism is fpqc local on the target (Stacks 041Y).
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.InducesIsomorphismAt` quantifies over *all* field-valued
representatives, which is condition (2) of Stacks 0DTV and so never weaker than the notion of
Stacks 0DTW.
declarations.statement:
theorem inducesIsomorphismAt_iff_forall_representatives (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (q : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids) :
    InducesIsomorphismAt B S hS f q ↔
      ∀ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val.val,
        pointClass B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids p = q →
          InducesIsomorphismAtObject B S hS f p.obj
declarations.comment: for the lifts of one field-valued representative: some lift, hence any lift

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isIso_pointAutomorphismSpaceMap_iff_forall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTV.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks and let `x` be a point
of `|𝒳|`. The map `G_x ⟶ G_y` of automorphism group algebraic spaces, where `y = f ∘ x`, is an
isomorphism for *some* field-valued representative `x : Spec k → 𝒳` of the point if and only if
it is an isomorphism for *every* such representative.

Two representatives of one point admit a common refinement. Over a field extension the map of
automorphism group algebraic spaces is a base change of the map below, and being an isomorphism
is fpqc local on the target (**Stacks 041Y**), so it passes both ways between a representative
and a refinement.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isIso_pointAutomorphismSpaceMap_iff_forall (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (q : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids) :
    (∃ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val.val,
        pointClass B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids p = q ∧
          IsIso (pointAutomorphismSpaceMap B S hS f p)) ↔
      ∀ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val.val,
        pointClass B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids p = q →
          IsIso (pointAutomorphismSpaceMap B S hS f p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.InducesIsomorphismAt
declarations.doc:
A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks *induces an isomorphism between automorphism
groups at a point* `q` of `|𝒳|` and at `f(q)` — in the literature, `f` is *stabilizer
preserving*, or *fixed-point reflecting*, at `q` — when for every field-valued representative `p`
of `q` and every object of the big site the morphism of automorphism group algebraic spaces of
`p` has a pullback of `p` at which it is bijective on sections.

By `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inducesIsomorphismAt_iff_forall_representatives` one such pullback
per object of the site is enough: the condition then holds at every object lying above every
representative of `q`, which is the content of Stacks 0DTV for the representatives of a fixed
field-valued point.
declarations.statement:
def InducesIsomorphismAt (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (q : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids) : Prop
declarations.comment: f induces an isomorphism between automorphism groups at a point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_diagonal_of_isSeparated_sourceTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTY, part (1).** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `S` with
`s` and `t` flat and locally of finite presentation, and let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack equivalent
over the site to its quotient stack `[U/R]`. If `(t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_S U` is separated, then the
diagonal of `𝒳` is separated in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_diagonal_of_isSeparated_sourceTarget
    (hequiv : Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (quotientStack G).p 𝒳.val.val.p))
    (_hsFlat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htFlat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.target.hom)
    (_hsLfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htLfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.target.hom)
    (hj : Space.IsSeparated B S hS (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.sourceTarget G).hom) :
    Stack.IsSeparated B S hS (diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val)
declarations.comment: part (1): a separated relation gives a separated diagonal, the diagonal being the one over the base scheme of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_diagonal_of_isSeparated_spaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTY, part (2).** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `S` with
`s` and `t` flat and locally of finite presentation, and let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack equivalent
over the site to its quotient stack `[U/R]`. If `U` and `R` are separated, then the diagonal of `𝒳`
is separated in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_diagonal_of_isSeparated_spaces
    (hequiv : Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (quotientStack G).p 𝒳.val.val.p))
    (_hsFlat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htFlat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.target.hom)
    (_hsLfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htLfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.target.hom)
    (_hU : Space.IsSeparated B S hS G.objectsToBase.hom)
    (hR : Space.IsSeparated B S hS G.arrowsToBase.hom) :
    Stack.IsSeparated B S hS (diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val)
declarations.comment: part (2): separated object and arrow spaces give a separated diagonal, the diagonal being the one over the base scheme of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_sourceTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTY, part (3).** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `S` with
`s` and `t` flat and locally of finite presentation, and let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack equivalent
over the site to its quotient stack `[U/R]`. If `(t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_S U` is locally quasi-finite, then
`𝒳` is quasi-DM.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_sourceTarget
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hequiv : Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (quotientStack G).p 𝒳.val.val.p))
    (_hsFlat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htFlat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.target.hom)
    (_hsLfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htLfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.target.hom)
    (hj : Space.IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS
      (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.sourceTarget G).hom) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (3): a locally quasi-finite relation gives a quasi-DM quotient

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_source_target
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTY, part (4).** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `S` with
`s` and `t` flat and locally of finite presentation, and let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack equivalent
over the site to its quotient stack `[U/R]`. If `s` and `t` are locally quasi-finite, then `𝒳` is
quasi-DM.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_source_target
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hequiv : Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (quotientStack G).p 𝒳.val.val.p))
    (_hsFlat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htFlat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.target.hom)
    (_hsLfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htLfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.target.hom)
    (hs : Space.IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_ht : Space.IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS G.target.hom) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (4): a locally quasi-finite source and target give a quasi-DM quotient

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparatedOver_of_isProper_sourceTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTY, part (5).** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `S` with
`s` and `t` flat and locally of finite presentation, and let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack equivalent
over the site to its quotient stack `[U/R]`. If `(t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_S U` is proper, then `𝒳` is
separated over the base scheme of the site (Stacks 050D, part (3)).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparatedOver_of_isProper_sourceTarget
    (hequiv : Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (quotientStack G).p 𝒳.val.val.p))
    (_hsFlat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htFlat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.target.hom)
    (_hsLfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htLfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.target.hom)
    (hj : Space.IsProper B S hS (GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.sourceTarget G).hom) :
    IsSeparatedOver.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (5): a proper relation gives a quotient separated over the base scheme `S` (Stacks 050D part (3)), the source's `separated` for an algebraic stack over `S`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparatedOver_of_isProper_source_target
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTY, part (6).** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `S` with
`s` and `t` flat and locally of finite presentation, and let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack equivalent
over the site to its quotient stack `[U/R]`. If `s` and `t` are proper and `U` is separated, then
`𝒳` is separated over the base scheme of the site (Stacks 050D, part (3)).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparatedOver_of_isProper_source_target
    (hequiv : Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (quotientStack G).p 𝒳.val.val.p))
    (_hsFlat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htFlat : Space.IsFlat B S hS G.target.hom)
    (_hsLfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htLfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS G.target.hom)
    (hs : Space.IsProper B S hS G.source.hom)
    (_ht : Space.IsProper B S hS G.target.hom)
    (hU : Space.IsSeparated B S hS G.objectsToBase.hom) :
    IsSeparatedOver.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (6): a proper source and target over a separated object space give a quotient separated over the base scheme `S` (Stacks 050D part (3)), the source's `separated` for an algebraic stack over `S`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.equivalence_sourceTargetRel_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTZ.** For a groupoid in algebraic spaces `(U, R, s, t, c)` the image of
`|R| → |U| × |U|` is an equivalence relation on the points of the object space: the pair of
points related by a point of the arrow space is its target and its source, and the arrows over
each test scheme form a groupoid.

No hypothesis on the source and target maps is needed; the flatness and local finite presentation
of Stacks 0DTZ enter only through the algebraicity of the quotient stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem equivalence_sourceTargetRel_points (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    Equivalence (Function.SourceTargetRel
      (Space.pointsMap C S hS G.arrows.obj G.source.hom)
      (Space.pointsMap C S hS G.arrows.obj G.target.hom))
declarations.comment: the image of |R| in |U| x |U| is an equivalence relation, with no hypothesis on the source and target maps

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.pointMap_eq_iff_sourceTargetRel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTZ.** Two points of the object space of a groupoid in algebraic spaces have the
same image in the points of the quotient stack exactly when they lie in the image of
`|R| → |U| × |U|`, that is exactly when some point of the arrow space has the first as its target
and the second as its source.

No hypothesis on the source and target maps is needed; the flatness and local finite presentation
of Stacks 0DTZ enter only through the algebraicity of the quotient stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointMap_eq_iff_sourceTargetRel
    (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (first second : Space.points C S hS G.objects.obj) :
    quotientStackPointMap G first = quotientStackPointMap G second ↔
      Function.SourceTargetRel
        (Space.pointsMap C S hS G.arrows.obj G.source.hom)
        (Space.pointsMap C S hS G.arrows.obj G.target.hom)
        first second
declarations.comment: the fibres of |U| -> |[U/R]| are the classes of the image of |R|, with no hypothesis on the source and target maps

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.surjective_quotientStackPointMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTZ.** Every point of the quotient stack `[U/R]` of a groupoid in
algebraic spaces is the image of a point of the object space `U`.

No hypothesis on the groupoid is needed: a point of `|[U/R]|` is represented by an object over
the spectrum of a field, the projection is surjective on objects by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjectiveOnObjects_quotientStackProjection`, and the resulting
object of the object space over a field extension is dominated by a field-valued point of `U`
whose image therefore has a common refinement with the chosen representative.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_quotientStackPointMap (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    Function.Surjective (quotientStackPointMap G)
declarations.comment: |U| surjects onto the points of the quotient stack, with no hypothesis on the source and target maps

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_quotientPointsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DTZ.** The points of the quotient stack of a groupoid in algebraic spaces are the
quotient of the points of the object space by the image of `|R| → |U| × |U|`: there is an
equivalence of the quotient set with `|[U/R]|` carrying the class of a point of `|U|` to its
image under the canonical map, so the identification is the canonical one and not merely a
bijection of underlying sets.

No hypothesis on the source and target maps is needed; the flatness and local finite presentation
of Stacks 0DTZ enter only through the algebraicity of the quotient stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quotientPointsEquiv (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B) :
    ∃ e : Quotient (arrowSetoid G) ≃
        points C S hS (quotientStack G) (isFiberedInGroupoids_quotientStack G),
      ∀ x : Space.points C S hS G.objects.obj,
        e (Quotient.mk _ x) = quotientStackPointMap G x
declarations.comment: |[U/R]| is the quotient of |U| by that equivalence relation, with no hypothesis on the source and target maps

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSheaf_of_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU1, algebraicity of the quotient.** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in
algebraic spaces over an algebraic space `Y` whose object space is flat and locally of finite
presentation over `Y` and whose pre-relation `(t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_Y U` is an open immersion.  Then
the quotient sheaf `U/R` of Stacks 044J is an algebraic space over `S`.

The pre-relation is an equivalence relation and `s` and `t` are flat and locally of finite
presentation, so Stacks 04S6, condition (1), applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSheaf_of_isOpenImmersion
    (hflat : IsFlat C S hS G.objectsToBase.hom)
    (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.objectsToBase.hom)
    (hopen : IsOpenImmersion C S hS (groupoidPreRelation G).left) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS (quotientSheaf (groupoidPreRelation G)).obj
declarations.comment: algebraicity of the quotient U/R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtale_quotientSheafToBase_of_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU1, étaleness of the quotient over the base.** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a
groupoid in algebraic spaces over an algebraic space `Y` whose object space is flat and locally
of finite presentation over `Y` and whose pre-relation `(t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_Y U` is an open
immersion.  Then the canonical morphism `U/R ⟶ Y` of Stacks 044J is étale.

Algebraicity of the quotient,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSheaf_of_isOpenImmersion`, is what Stacks 06PG
needs in order to give the three properties of the covering map `U ⟶ U/R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_quotientSheafToBase_of_isOpenImmersion
    (hflat : IsFlat C S hS G.objectsToBase.hom)
    (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.objectsToBase.hom)
    (hopen : IsOpenImmersion C S hS (groupoidPreRelation G).left) :
    IsEtale C S hS (quotientSheafToBase Y.property.isSheaf (groupoidPreRelation G)).hom
declarations.comment: étaleness of the structural morphism U/R → Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackToQuotientSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU1, the canonical comparison `[U/R] ⟶ U/R`.** Under the hypotheses of Stacks 0DU1
the quotient sheaf is an algebraic space
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSheaf_of_isOpenImmersion`), so the quotient
projection `U ⟶ U/R` is an invariant morphism to an algebraic space, and it descends to a
1-morphism from the quotient stack to the category fibred in sets of `U/R`.

This is the comparison asserted by the equality `X = [U/R] = U/R` of the source.  It is a real
construction — the descent of Stacks 044R applied to the quotient projection — and not a choice
out of an existence statement; `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackToQuotientSheaf_unique`
shows it is the only 1-morphism restricting along the projection to the quotient map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quotientStackToQuotientSheaf :
    quotientStack G ⥤ᵇ
      (fibredCategory C S hS (quotientSheafSpace G hflat hlfp hopen).obj).val
declarations.comment: the canonical comparison [U/R] → U/R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackProjection_comp_quotientStackToQuotientSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU1.** The canonical comparison composed with the projection `U ⟶ [U/R]` of
Stacks 044R is the 1-morphism that Stacks 0458 attaches to the quotient map `U ⟶ U/R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientStackProjection_comp_quotientStackToQuotientSheaf :
    BasedFunctor.comp (quotientStackProjection G)
        (quotientStackToQuotientSheaf G hflat hlfp hopen) =
      (associatedMap C S hS (Space.toQuotientSheaf (Space.groupoidPreRelation G))).1.hom
declarations.comment: the comparison composed with the quotient projection is the map attached to U → U/R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackToQuotientSheaf_comp_toBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU1.** The canonical comparison is a morphism over the base: composed with the
1-morphism attached to the structural morphism `U/R ⟶ Y` it is the structure arrow
`[U/R] ⟶ Y` of Stacks 044R.

Both sides restrict along the projection to the structure morphism `U ⟶ Y` of the object space,
and by Stacks 0DUH a 1-morphism from the quotient stack to an algebraic space is determined by
that restriction.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientStackToQuotientSheaf_comp_toBase :
    BasedFunctor.comp (quotientStackToQuotientSheaf G hflat hlfp hopen)
        (associatedMap C S hS (quotientSheafToBaseSpace G hflat hlfp hopen).hom).1.hom =
      quotientStackToBase G
declarations.comment: the comparison is compatible with the structural morphisms to the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicSpace_and_equivalenceOver_and_isEtale_of_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU1.** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over an algebraic
space `Y` whose object space `U` is flat and locally of finite presentation over `Y` and whose
pre-relation `(t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_Y U` is an open immersion.  Then `X = [U/R] = U/R` is an algebraic
space and `X ⟶ Y` is étale: the quotient sheaf `U/R` of Stacks 044J is an algebraic space, the
canonical comparison `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackToQuotientSheaf` from the quotient
stack `[U/R]` to it is an equivalence over the big fppf site, and the structural morphism
`U/R ⟶ Y` is étale.

The three clauses are `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSheaf_of_isOpenImmersion`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_equivalenceOver_quotientStackToQuotientSheaf` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtale_quotientSheafToBase_of_isOpenImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_and_equivalenceOver_and_isEtale_of_isOpenImmersion :
    IsAlgebraicSpace C S hS (Space.quotientSheaf (Space.groupoidPreRelation G)).obj ∧
      Nonempty { e : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver (quotientStack G).p
          (fibredCategory C S hS (quotientSheafSpace G hflat hlfp hopen).obj).val.p //
        e.hom.functor = (quotientStackToQuotientSheaf G hflat hlfp hopen).toFunctor } ∧
      Space.IsEtale C S hS
        (Space.quotientSheafToBase Y.property.isSheaf (Space.groupoidPreRelation G)).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_representable_surjective_etale_quotientStackMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU2.** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces (here over an
algebraic space `A` over `S`, which contains the case of a groupoid over `S`) with `s`, `t` flat
and locally of finite presentation, and let `P ⊆ R` be an open subspace such that
`(U, P, s|_P, t|_P, c|_P)` is a groupoid in algebraic spaces; that is, let `φ : G ⟶ H` be a
morphism of groupoids in algebraic spaces whose map on objects is an isomorphism and whose map on
arrows is an open immersion. Then `[U/P]` and `[U/R]` are algebraic stacks, and
`[φ] : [U/P] ⟶ [U/R]` is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective and étale, the last two in
the sense of Stacks 03YK.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_representable_surjective_etale_quotientStackMap
    {G H : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS A} (φ : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.Hom G H)
    (hopen : Space.IsOpenImmersion C S hS φ.toGroupoidHom.mapArrows)
    (hobj : IsIso φ.toGroupoidHom.mapObjects)
    (hsflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS H.source.hom) (htflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS H.target.hom)
    (hslfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS H.source.hom)
    (htlfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS H.target.hom) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack G) ∧
      IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} C S hS (quotientStack H) ∧
      ∃ hrep : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces C S hS (quotientStackMap φ),
        HasRelativeProperty.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u} C S hS
          (Space.surjectiveMorphismProperty C S hS) (quotientStackMapCFGHom φ) hrep ∧
        HasRelativeProperty.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u} C S hS
          (Space.etaleMorphisms C S hS) (quotientStackMapCFGHom φ) hrep

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.exists_quasiSplitting_isAffine_isFinite_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU3, the groupoid of clause (3).**

Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid scheme over `S` with `U` affine and with `s` and `t` flat and
locally of finite presentation, and let `u` be a point of `U` over which the groupoid is
quasi-split in the sense of **Stacks 04RK**, part (3).  Then there is a groupoid scheme
`(U, P, s|_P, t|_P, c|_P)` together with a morphism into `(U, R, s, t, c)` which is an open
immersion on arrow schemes and the identity on object schemes, carrying the identity arrow at
`u`, whose *both* structure schemes are affine and whose source and target are finite, flat and
locally of finite presentation.

This is the groupoid scheme of clause (3) of **Stacks 0DU3**, with every property that clause
asserts of it: the source's proof takes `𝒰 = [U/P]` for exactly this `P`.  The properties are
asserted of one single groupoid scheme, as the tag asserts them.

The three conjuncts that are not re-derivations are the equality of object schemes, the open
immersion and the identity arrow: these are the three pieces of data a quasi-splitting *is*
(conditions (a) and (c) of Stacks 04RK), and they are listed so that the groupoid produced is
pinned to be the quasi-splitting at `u` rather than an unrelated groupoid.  Everything else is
derived: affineness of the object scheme from the equality, flatness and local finite
presentation of `s|_P` and `t|_P` from the open immersion composed with `s` and `t`, and
affineness of the arrow scheme from finiteness of `s|_P` over the affine object scheme — the
last being the step where an *open* subscheme of `R` is shown affine without `R` being used at
all.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quasiSplitting_isAffine_isFinite_flat [IsAffine G.objects.left]
    [Flat G.source.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.source.left]
    [Flat G.target.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.target.left]
    {u : G.objects.left} (h : IsQuasiSplitAt G u) :
    ∃ (G' : GroupoidScheme S) (φ : Hom G' G),
      G'.objects = G.objects ∧
      IsOpenImmersion φ.mapArrows.left ∧
      (∃ p : G'.arrows.left, φ.mapArrows.left.base p = G.identity.left.base u) ∧
      IsAffine G'.objects.left ∧ IsAffine G'.arrows.left ∧
      IsFinite G'.source.left ∧
      Flat G'.source.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation G'.source.left ∧
      IsFinite G'.target.left ∧
      Flat G'.target.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation G'.target.left
declarations.comment: the groupoid scheme of clause (3), with U and its arrow scheme affine and source and target finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, built from a quasi-splitting of Stacks 04RK. Clause (1), clause (2) and the identification of the stack with [U/R] in clause (3) are NOT covered: see the implementation notes for the three named obstructions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_etale_quotientStack_of_isQuasiDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU3.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` which is quasi-DM (Stacks 050D) with
separated diagonal `Δ_{𝒳/S}` (Stacks 04XB), and let `x ∈ |𝒳|`. Then there is a 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks `g : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` such that

1. some point of `|𝒰|` maps to `x`,
2. `g` is representable by algebraic spaces and étale,
3. `𝒰` is the quotient stack `[U/R]` of (the realization of) a groupoid scheme `(U, R, s, t, c)`
   with `U` and `R` affine and `s`, `t` finite, flat and locally of finite presentation: there is
   an equivalence over the site between that quotient stack and `𝒰`.

The parenthetical equivalent hypothesis of the source (`I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` locally quasi-finite and
separated) is Stacks 0CL0, parts (1) and (5).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_quotientStack_of_isQuasiDM (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hQ : AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS B.contains_terminal 𝒳)
    (hΔ : Stack.IsSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val
        (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS)))).val
        (structureMorphism B S hS 𝒳).hom))
    (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳) :
    ∃ (𝒰 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (g : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳),
      (∃ v, AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS g v = x) ∧
      (IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS g.hom.hom ∧ IsEtale B S hS g) ∧
      ∃ (G : GroupoidScheme S) (hU : B.Contains G.objects.left) (hR : B.Contains G.arrows.left)
        (hP : B.Contains (pullback G.source G.target).left),
        IsAffine G.objects.left ∧ IsAffine G.arrows.left ∧
        IsFinite G.source.left ∧ Flat G.source.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.source.left ∧
        IsFinite G.target.left ∧ Flat G.target.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.target.left ∧
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (quotientStack (G.realization B hS hU hR hP)).p 𝒰.val.val.p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_etale_quotientStack_inducesIsomorphismAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU4.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` which is quasi-DM (Stacks 050D) with
separated diagonal `Δ_{𝒳/S}` (Stacks 04XB), and let `x ∈ |𝒳|` be a point at which the automorphism
group of `𝒳` is finite (Remark 0DTU). Then there is a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks
`g : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` such that

1. some point `v ∈ |𝒰|` maps to `x` and `g` induces an isomorphism between the automorphism
   groups at `v` and `x` (Stacks 0DTW),
2. `g` is representable by algebraic spaces and étale,
3. `𝒰` is the quotient stack `[U/R]` of (the realization of) a groupoid scheme `(U, R, s, t, c)`
   with `U` and `R` affine and `s`, `t` finite, flat and locally of finite presentation: there is
   an equivalence over the site between that quotient stack and `𝒰`.

The parenthetical equivalent hypothesis of the source (`I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` locally quasi-finite and
separated) is Stacks 0CL0, parts (1) and (5).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_quotientStack_inducesIsomorphismAt (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hQ : AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS B.contains_terminal 𝒳)
    (hΔ : Stack.IsSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val
        (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS)))).val
        (structureMorphism B S hS 𝒳).hom))
    (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)
    (hAut : AutomorphismGroupHasProperty B S hS (IsFiniteOverBase B S hS) x) :
    ∃ (𝒰 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (g : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳),
      (∃ v, AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS g v = x ∧ InducesIsomorphismAt B S hS g v) ∧
      (IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS g.hom.hom ∧ IsEtale B S hS g) ∧
      ∃ (G : GroupoidScheme S) (hU : B.Contains G.objects.left) (hR : B.Contains G.arrows.left)
        (hP : B.Contains (pullback G.source G.target).left),
        IsAffine G.objects.left ∧ IsAffine G.arrows.left ∧
        IsFinite G.source.left ∧ Flat G.source.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.source.left ∧
        IsFinite G.target.left ∧ Flat G.target.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.target.left ∧
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (quotientStack (G.realization B hS hU hR hP)).p 𝒰.val.val.p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_etale_quotientStack_residualGerbeMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU5.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` which is quasi-DM (Stacks 050D) with
separated diagonal `Δ_{𝒳/S}` (Stacks 04XB), and let `x ∈ |𝒳|` be a point which can be represented
by a quasi-compact morphism from the spectrum of a field. Then there is a 1-morphism of algebraic
stacks `g : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` such that

1. some point `v ∈ |𝒰|` maps to `x`, the residual gerbes of `𝒰` at `v` and of `𝒳` at `x` exist,
   and the 1-morphism between them induced by `g` (Stacks 0DTH) is an isomorphism for every
   choice of them;
2. `g` is representable by algebraic spaces and étale;
3. `𝒰` is the quotient stack `[U/R]` of (the realization of) a groupoid scheme `(U, R, s, t, c)`
   with `U` and `R` affine and `s`, `t` finite, flat and locally of finite presentation: there is
   an equivalence over the site between that quotient stack and `𝒰`.

The parenthetical equivalent hypothesis of the source (`I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` locally quasi-finite and
separated) is Stacks 0CL0, parts (1) and (5). See the module documentation for the proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_quotientStack_residualGerbeMap (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hQ : AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM B S hS B.contains_terminal 𝒳)
    (hΔ : Stack.IsSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val
        (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS)))).val
        (structureMorphism B S hS 𝒳).hom))
    (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)
    (hqc : ∃ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val.val,
      pointClass B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids p = x ∧
        IsQuasiCompactFieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val p) :
    ∃ (𝒰 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (g : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳)
      (v : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒰),
      (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS g v = x ∧
        (∃ P : ObjectProperty 𝒰.val.val.obj, IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒰 v P) ∧
        (∃ Q : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj, IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x Q) ∧
        ∀ (P : ObjectProperty 𝒰.val.val.obj) (Q : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj)
          (hv : IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒰 v P)
          (hx : IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS g v) Q),
          Nonempty (Functor.IsEquivalenceOver
            (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒰 P hv.2.choose).val.val.p
            (fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒳 Q hx.2.choose).val.val.p
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor
              (residualGerbeMap B S hS g hv.2.choose hx.2.choose
                (map_mem_of_isResidualGerbeAt B S hS g v _ rfl hv hx)).hom))) ∧
      (IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS g.hom.hom ∧ IsEtale B S hS g) ∧
      ∃ (G : GroupoidScheme S) (hU : B.Contains G.objects.left) (hR : B.Contains G.arrows.left)
        (hP : B.Contains (pullback G.source G.target).left),
        IsAffine G.objects.left ∧ IsAffine G.arrows.left ∧
        IsFinite G.source.left ∧ Flat G.source.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.source.left ∧
        IsFinite G.target.left ∧ Flat G.target.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.target.left ∧
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (quotientStack (G.realization B hS hU hR hP)).p 𝒰.val.val.p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_inertiaPullbackComparison_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU7.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`. If the
canonical comparison `ℐ_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 ℐ_𝒴` of Stacks 06R5 is an isomorphism, then `f` is
representable by algebraic spaces.

The comparison makes `f` faithful
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.faithful_homFunctor_of_inertiaPullbackComparison_full`, condition (4)
of Stacks 04YY), and a faithful 1-morphism of algebraic stacks is representable by algebraic
spaces (Stacks 04Y5, the implication (2) ⟹ (3)).
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_inertiaPullbackComparison_isEquivalence
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : (CategoryTheory.inertiaPullbackComparison 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom)
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor_comp_p f.hom)).IsEquivalence) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HigherDiagonal.prop_isomMap_of_prop_relativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU8.** Let `x : T ⟶ 𝒳` have an algebraic space as source, and let `G ⟶ H` be the
pullback to `T` of the stabilizer comparison `ℐ_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 ℐ_𝒴`, that is, the map
`G = Isom_𝒳(x, x) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(f ∘ x, f ∘ x) = H` on automorphism spaces. Then `G ⟶ H` satisfies a
