condition of Stacks 04XB as soon as the relative diagonal `Δ_f` does, for an arbitrary property
`P` of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`: if `Δ_f` is unramified, étale, proper, … then so
is `G ⟶ H`.

The square `T ×_𝒳 T ⟶ 𝒳`, `T ×_𝒴 T ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳` over `Δ_f` is 2-cartesian, so `T ×_𝒳 T ⟶ T ×_𝒴 T`
is a base change of `Δ_f` (Stacks 050H), and `G ⟶ H` is a base change of that along the diagonal
of `T` (Stacks 0CPL, part (2)).
declarations.statement:
theorem prop_isomMap_of_prop_relativeDiagonal
    (x : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS T hT ⟶ 𝒳)
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hP : ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
        (AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProduct B S hS f f).val.val.obj)
      (_hy : y ⋙ (AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProduct B S hS f f).val.val.p = Over.map U.hom)
      (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.val.p
            (AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProduct B S hS f f).val.val.p y
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor
              (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom)))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        P (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
          ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩))) :
    ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (z : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
        (isomStack B S hS T hT (x ≫ f) (x ≫ f)).val.obj)
      (_hz : z ⋙ (isomStack B S hS T hT (x ≫ f) (x ≫ f)).val.p = Over.map U.hom)
      (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom)
            (isomStack B S hS T hT x x).val.p
            (isomStack B S hS T hT (x ≫ f) (x ≫ f)).val.p z
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (isomMap B S hS f T hT x x)))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        P (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
          ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inertiaPullbackComparison_isEquivalenceOver_iff_inducesIsomorphismAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DU9.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be an unramified 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`.
Then the canonical comparison `ℐ_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 ℐ_𝒴` of Stacks 06R5 is an isomorphism (an
equivalence over the big fppf site) if and only if `f` induces an isomorphism between the
automorphism groups at `x` and at `f(x)` (Stacks 0DTW) for every `x ∈ |𝒳|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem inertiaPullbackComparison_isEquivalenceOver_iff_inducesIsomorphismAt
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hu : IsUnramified B S hS f) :
    Nonempty (IsEquivalenceOver
      (RelativeInertia.toBase 𝒳.val.val.p)
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor (RelativeInertia.toBase 𝒴.val.val.p)
        𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p (RelativeInertia.π 𝒴.val.val.p)
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom))
      (inertiaPullbackComparison 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom)
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor_comp_p f.hom))) ↔
      ∀ q : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids,
        InducesIsomorphismAt B S hS f q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_openSubstack_isStabilizerPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUA.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` which is
representable by algebraic spaces and unramified, and assume the inertia `ℐ_𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴` is proper.
Then the set of `x ∈ |𝒳|` at which `f` induces an isomorphism between the automorphism groups
at `x` and at `f(x)` (**Stacks 0DTW**) is open; there is an open substack `𝒰 ⊆ 𝒳` with that set
of points (**Stacks 06FJ**); and for every open substack `𝒰 ⊆ 𝒳` with that set of points, the
canonical comparison `ℐ_𝒰 ⟶ 𝒰 ×_𝒴 ℐ_𝒴` of **Stacks 06R5** is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openSubstack_isStabilizerPreserving
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) (hu : IsUnramified B S hS f)
    (hI : AlgebraicStacks.IsProper B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒴)) :
    @IsOpen _ (pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val) (stabilizerPreservingLocus B S hS f) ∧
      (∃ U : OpenSubstack 𝒳, U.pointSet B S hS = stabilizerPreservingLocus B S hS f) ∧
        ∀ U : OpenSubstack 𝒳, U.pointSet B S hS = stabilizerPreservingLocus B S hS f →
          IsStabilizerPreserving B S hS (U.inclusion ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inducesIsomorphismAt_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUB, part (1).** In a 2-cartesian square of algebraic stacks with apex `𝒳'`,
first projection `f' : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴'` and second projection `𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳`, if `f` induces an isomorphism
between automorphism groups at the image `x` of a point `x'` of `|𝒳'|`, then `f'` induces an
isomorphism between automorphism groups at `x'`.

The hypothesis is the isomorphism at the single point `x` and nothing else; in particular `f` is
not assumed stabilizer preserving, which is the hypothesis of part (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem inducesIsomorphismAt_baseChange (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (x' : points B S hS P.pt.val.val P.pt.val.isFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hx : InducesIsomorphismAt B S hS f
      (pointsMap B S hS P.pt.val.val P.pt.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
        𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids P.snd.hom.hom x')) :
    InducesIsomorphismAt B S hS P.fst x'
declarations.comment: the automorphism groups at a point of a base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_inertiaPullbackComparison_isEquivalenceOver_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUB, part (2).** In a cartesian square of algebraic stacks, if the canonical
comparison from the inertia of `𝒳` to `𝒳 ×_𝒴 ℐ_𝒴` is an equivalence, then so is the
corresponding comparison for the base change of `f` along `g`.

The base change of `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` along `g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴` is the first projection of a 2-fibre product
`P` of the cospan `(g, f)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_inertiaPullbackComparison_isEquivalenceOver_baseChange
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hf : (CategoryTheory.inertiaPullbackComparison 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom)
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor_comp_p f.hom)).IsEquivalence) :
    Nonempty (CategoryTheory.IsEquivalenceOver
      (RelativeInertia.toBase P.pt.val.val.p)
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor (RelativeInertia.toBase 𝒴'.val.val.p)
        P.pt.val.val.p 𝒴'.val.val.p (RelativeInertia.π 𝒴'.val.val.p)
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor P.fst.hom))
      (CategoryTheory.inertiaPullbackComparison P.pt.val.val.p 𝒴'.val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor P.fst.hom)
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor_comp_p P.fst.hom)))
declarations.comment: the inertia map of a base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isoClassMk_eq_of_isoClassMk_eq_components
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUC.** Let `𝒳'` be the apex of a 2-cartesian square of algebraic stacks with
`f' : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴'` its first projection, over `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴`, and suppose `f`
induces an isomorphism between automorphism groups at every point of `|𝒳|` (Stacks 0DTW). Then
for every field `k` the map `Mor(Spec k, 𝒳') → Mor(Spec k, 𝒴') × Mor(Spec k, 𝒳)` is injective
on isomorphism classes.

A 1-morphism `Spec k ⟶ 𝒳'` is, by 2-Yoneda, an object of the fibre of `𝒳'` over an object `U`
of the big site with underlying scheme `Spec k`, and its isomorphism class is
`CategoryTheory.Functor.isoClassMk`; so this says that two such 1-morphisms with the same pair
of classes in `𝒴'` and in `𝒳` have the same class in `𝒳'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isoClassMk_eq_of_isoClassMk_eq_components (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hf : ∀ q : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids,
      InducesIsomorphismAt B S hS f q)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hU : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U ≅ Spec (.of k))
    (a b : P.pt.val.val.p.Fiber U)
    (hfst : Functor.isoClassMk 𝒴'.val.val.p
        ((Functor.fiberMap P.pt.val.val.p 𝒴'.val.val.p
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor P.fst.hom)
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor_comp_p P.fst.hom) U).obj a)
      = Functor.isoClassMk 𝒴'.val.val.p
        ((Functor.fiberMap P.pt.val.val.p 𝒴'.val.val.p
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor P.fst.hom)
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor_comp_p P.fst.hom) U).obj b))
    (hsnd : Functor.isoClassMk 𝒳.val.val.p
        ((Functor.fiberMap P.pt.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor P.snd.hom)
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor_comp_p P.snd.hom) U).obj a)
      = Functor.isoClassMk 𝒳.val.val.p
        ((Functor.fiberMap P.pt.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor P.snd.hom)
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor_comp_p P.snd.hom) U).obj b)) :
    Functor.isoClassMk P.pt.val.val.p a = Functor.isoClassMk P.pt.val.val.p b
declarations.comment: field-valued points of a base change, injective on isomorphism classes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_of_isEtale_of_inducesIsomorphismAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUD.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`. Assume `f`
is étale, that `f` induces an isomorphism between the automorphism groups at `x` and at `f(x)`
for every `x ∈ |𝒳|` (**Stacks 0DTW**), and that for every algebraically closed field `k` the
functor `Mor(Spec k, 𝒳) ⟶ Mor(Spec k, 𝒴)` is an equivalence. Then `f` is an isomorphism.

The proof is the source's. Fullness of the functors on geometric points is condition (3) of
**Stacks 0CPN**, so `f` is universally injective. Étale implies unramified (**Stacks 0CIW**), so
**Stacks 0DU9** makes `f` stabilizer preserving and **Stacks 0DU7** makes it representable by
algebraic spaces. Essential surjectivity on geometric points makes `f` surjective, and
**Stacks 05W5**, in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_of_isEtale_of_universallyInjective_of_isSurjective`,
concludes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_of_isEtale_of_inducesIsomorphismAt (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (he : IsEtale B S hS f)
    (hauto : ∀ x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳, InducesIsomorphismAt B S hS f x)
    (hfibre : ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (V : BigFppfOver B S hS),
      ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V ≅ Spec (.of k)) →
        (geometricFibreFunctor B S hS f V).IsEquivalence) :
    (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isWellNighAffine_etale_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUE.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` whose inertia projection
`I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is finite. Then there are a set `I` and, for `i ∈ I`, 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks
`g_i : 𝒳_i ⟶ 𝒳` such that

1. `|𝒳| = ⋃ |g_i|(|𝒳_i|)`,
2. `𝒳_i` is well-nigh affine (Stacks 0DUL),
3. `I_{𝒳_i} ⟶ 𝒳_i ×_𝒳 I_𝒳` is an isomorphism (equivalently, by Stacks 0DU9, `g_i` induces an
   isomorphism between automorphism groups at every point of `𝒳_i`),
4. `g_i` is representable by algebraic spaces, separated (Stacks 04YW) and étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isWellNighAffine_etale_cover (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hI : AlgebraicStacks.IsFinite B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳)) :
    ∃ (ι : Type (u + 1)) (𝒳ᵢ : ι → AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (g : ∀ i, 𝒳ᵢ i ⟶ 𝒳),
      (∀ x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳,
        ∃ (i : ι) (y : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS (𝒳ᵢ i)),
          AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (g i) y = x) ∧
      (∀ i, IsWellNighAffine.{u, w} B S hS (𝒳ᵢ i)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsStabilizerPreserving B S hS (g i) ∧
        ∀ q : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS (𝒳ᵢ i), InducesIsomorphismAt B S hS (g i) q) ∧
      (∀ i, IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (g i).hom.hom ∧
        AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS (g i) ∧ IsEtale B S hS (g i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsCategoricalModuliSpace
declarations.doc:
A 1-morphism from a category fibred in groupoids to the
category attached to an algebraic space `Y` is a *categorical moduli space* when every
1-morphism to the category attached to an algebraic space `W` factors through it by a unique
morphism `Y ⟶ W` of algebraic spaces, the factorization holding up to an invertible
2-morphism.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsCategoricalModuliSpace
    {𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ fibredCategory B S hS Y.obj) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpace
declarations.doc:
A categorical moduli space is *uniform* when every base change of it along a flat morphism
of algebraic spaces, given by any 2-fibre product of the cospan, is again a categorical moduli
space.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpace
    {𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ fibredCategory B S hS Y.obj) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsCategoricalModuliSpaceIn
declarations.doc:
The universal factorization property with the target algebraic spaces restricted to the full
subcategory selected by the object predicate `C`, which `Y` is required to meet.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsCategoricalModuliSpaceIn
    (C : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS → Prop)
    {𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ fibredCategory B S hS Y.obj) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpaceIn
declarations.doc:
A categorical moduli space in the full subcategory selected by
`C` is *uniform in* `C` when its base change along every flat morphism of that subcategory is
again a categorical moduli space in `C`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpaceIn
    (C : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS → Prop)
    {𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ fibredCategory B S hS Y.obj) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackHomEquivInvariant
declarations.doc:
For a groupoid in algebraic spaces `(U, R, s, t, c)` over an algebraic space `B` over a scheme
`S` of a big fppf site, and an algebraic space `Y` over `S`, the 1-morphisms `[U/R] ⟶ Y` of stacks
over the big fppf site are in 1-to-1 correspondence with the `R`-invariant morphisms `U ⟶ Y`, by
restriction along the projection `π : U ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 044R.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackHomEquivInvariant_spec
declarations.doc:
The correspondence is restriction along the projection: the 1-morphism `[U/R] ⟶ Y`
corresponding to an `R`-invariant morphism `φ : U ⟶ Y` restricts along the projection
`π : U ⟶ [U/R]` to the 1-morphism attached to `φ` by Stacks 0458.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientStackHomEquivInvariant_spec
    (f : quotientStack G ⥤ᵇ (fibredCategory C S hS Y.obj).val) :
    BasedFunctor.comp (quotientStackProjection G) f =
      (associatedMap C S hS (quotientStackHomEquivInvariant G Y f).val.hom).1.hom
declarations.comment: the correspondence is restriction along the projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStack_isCategoricalModuliSpace_iff_isCategoricalQuotient
declarations.doc:
Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over a terminal base, let
`j = (t, s)` be its pre-relation and let `f : [U/R] ⟶ Y` be a 1-morphism to the category attached
to an algebraic space `Y`. Then `f` is a categorical moduli space exactly when its restriction
`φ : U ⟶ Y` along the projection is a categorical quotient of `j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientStack_isCategoricalModuliSpace_iff_isCategoricalQuotient (hB : IsTerminal B)
    (hjt : (Space.PreRelation.target j).left = G.target)
    (hjs : (Space.PreRelation.source j).left = G.source)
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)
    (f : quotientStack G ⥤ᵇ (fibredCategory C S hS Y.obj).val) :
    IsBasedCategoricalModuliSpace Y f ↔
      Space.IsCategoricalQuotient j
        (Over.homMk (restrictedMorphism G f) (hB.hom_ext _ _) :
          (Over.mk G.objectsToBase : Over B) ⟶ Over.mk (hB.from Y))
declarations.comment: the non-uniform case, for a groupoid over the terminal base as in the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStack_isCategoricalModuliSpace_iff_isCategoricalQuotient_prodLift
declarations.doc:
Let `G` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over a terminal base and let `f : [U/R] ⟶ Y` be a
1-morphism to the category attached to an algebraic space `Y`. Then `f` is a categorical moduli
space exactly when its restriction `φ : U ⟶ Y` along the projection is a categorical quotient of
the pre-relation `prod.lift t s` of `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientStack_isCategoricalModuliSpace_iff_isCategoricalQuotient_prodLift
    (hB : IsTerminal B) (G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B)
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)
    (f : quotientStack G ⥤ᵇ (fibredCategory C S hS Y.obj).val) :
    IsBasedCategoricalModuliSpace Y f ↔
      Space.IsCategoricalQuotient
        (prod.lift (Over.homMk G.target G.target_over) (Over.homMk G.source G.source_over) :
          Space.PreRelation (Over.mk G.arrowsToBase) (Over.mk G.objectsToBase))
        (Over.homMk (restrictedMorphism G f) (hB.hom_ext _ _) :
          (Over.mk G.objectsToBase : Over B) ⟶ Over.mk (hB.from Y))
declarations.comment: the non-uniform case at the pre-relation (t, s) the groupoid cuts out

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStack_isCategoricalModuliSpaceIn_iff_isCategoricalQuotientIn
declarations.doc:
With the same data as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStack_isCategoricalModuliSpace_iff_isCategoricalQuotient` and a
full subcategory of the algebraic spaces, selected by a predicate `P` on objects and containing
the object and arrow spaces of the groupoid, `f` is a categorical moduli space in that
subcategory exactly when `φ` is a categorical quotient in it.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientStack_isCategoricalModuliSpaceIn_iff_isCategoricalQuotientIn (hB : IsTerminal B)
    (hjt : (Space.PreRelation.target j).left = G.target)
    (hjs : (Space.PreRelation.source j).left = G.source)
    (P : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS → Prop) (hR : P G.arrows) (hU : P G.objects)
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)
    (f : quotientStack G ⥤ᵇ (fibredCategory C S hS Y.obj).val) :
    IsBasedCategoricalModuliSpaceIn P Y f ↔
      Space.IsCategoricalQuotientIn (fun Z : Over B => P Z.left) j
        (Over.homMk (restrictedMorphism G f) (hB.hom_ext _ _) :
          (Over.mk G.objectsToBase : Over B) ⟶ Over.mk (hB.from Y))
declarations.comment: the non-uniform case in a full subcategory, for a groupoid over the terminal base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStack_isUniformCategoricalModuliSpace_iff_isUniformCategoricalQuotient
declarations.doc:
Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over a terminal base, let
`f : [U/R] ⟶ Y` be a 1-morphism to the category attached to an algebraic space `Y` and let
`φ : U ⟶ Y` be its restriction along the projection of Stacks 044R. Then `f` is a *uniform*
categorical moduli space exactly when `φ` is a *uniform* categorical quotient: for every flat
`a : Y' ⟶ Y`, the base change `Y' ×_Y [U/R] ⟶ Y'` of `f` is a categorical moduli space exactly when
the base-changed quotient map `U' ⟶ Y'` is a categorical quotient of the base-changed pre-relation
`(t', s')`, for `U' = Y' ×_Y U` and `R' = Y' ×_Y R`.

The base change is an arbitrary 2-fibre product of the cospan in the 2-category of stacks in
groupoids of Stacks 02ZK.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientStack_isUniformCategoricalModuliSpace_iff_isUniformCategoricalQuotient :
    (∀ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (a : Y' ⟶ Y), Space.IsFlat C S hS a.hom →
        ∀ P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq
            (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom (BasedFunctor.comp f (liftedFibredCategoryUp Y)) :
              quotientStackAsStack G ⟶ spaceAsStack Y)
            (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom (liftedAssociatedMap a) :
              spaceAsStack Y' ⟶ spaceAsStack Y),
          Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P →
            IsBasedCategoricalModuliSpace Y'
              (BasedFunctor.comp P.snd.hom (liftedFibredCategoryDown Y'))) ↔
      ∀ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (a : Y' ⟶ Y), Space.IsFlat C S hS a.hom →
        Space.IsCategoricalQuotient
          (baseChangeSituationPreRelation hB G (restrictedMorphism G f)
            (restrictedMorphism_isInvariant G f) a)
          (baseChangeSituationQuotientMap hB G (restrictedMorphism G f)
            (restrictedMorphism_isInvariant G f) a)
declarations.comment: the uniform case, for a groupoid over the terminal base as in the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStack_isUniformCategoricalModuliSpaceIn_iff_isUniformCategoricalQuotientIn
declarations.doc:
The uniform case in a full subcategory. With the same data as
`quotientStack_isUniformCategoricalModuliSpace_iff_isUniformCategoricalQuotient` and a full
subcategory of the algebraic spaces, selected by a predicate `Pr` on objects which contains the
object and arrow spaces of every base change of the groupoid: for every flat `a : Y' ⟶ Y`, the base
change `Y' ×_Y [U/R] ⟶ Y'` of `f` is a categorical moduli space in `Pr` exactly when the
base-changed quotient map `U' ⟶ Y'` is a categorical quotient in `Pr` of the base-changed
pre-relation `(t', s')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientStack_isUniformCategoricalModuliSpaceIn_iff_isUniformCategoricalQuotientIn
    (Pr : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS → Prop)
    (hR : ∀ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (a : Y' ⟶ Y),
      Pr (baseChangeSituationGroupoid hB G (restrictedMorphism G f)
        (restrictedMorphism_isInvariant G f) a).arrows)
    (hU : ∀ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (a : Y' ⟶ Y),
      Pr (baseChangeSituationGroupoid hB G (restrictedMorphism G f)
        (restrictedMorphism_isInvariant G f) a).objects) :
    (∀ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (a : Y' ⟶ Y), Space.IsFlat C S hS a.hom →
        ∀ P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq
            (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom (BasedFunctor.comp f (liftedFibredCategoryUp Y)) :
              quotientStackAsStack G ⟶ spaceAsStack Y)
            (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom (liftedAssociatedMap a) :
              spaceAsStack Y' ⟶ spaceAsStack Y),
          Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P →
            IsBasedCategoricalModuliSpaceIn Pr Y'
              (BasedFunctor.comp P.snd.hom (liftedFibredCategoryDown Y'))) ↔
      ∀ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS) (a : Y' ⟶ Y), Space.IsFlat C S hS a.hom →
        Space.IsCategoricalQuotientIn (fun Z : Over B => Pr Z.left)
          (baseChangeSituationPreRelation hB G (restrictedMorphism G f)
            (restrictedMorphism_isInvariant G f) a)
          (baseChangeSituationQuotientMap hB G (restrictedMorphism G f)
            (restrictedMorphism_isInvariant G f) a)
declarations.comment: variant: the uniform case in a full subcategory, over every flat Y' ⟶ Y and with the subcategory containing every base change of R and U; the tag is quotientStack_isUniformModuliSpaceIn_iff_isUniformQuotientIn_of_isClosedUnderLimitsOfShape

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStack_isUniformModuliSpaceIn_iff_isUniformQuotientIn_of_isClosedUnderLimitsOfShape
declarations.doc:
Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over a terminal base,
`f : [U/R] ⟶ Y` a 1-morphism to the category attached to an algebraic space `Y`, and `φ : U ⟶ Y`
its restriction along the projection of Stacks 044R. Let `Pr` be a full subcategory of the
algebraic spaces which is closed under fibre products and contains `R` and `U`. Then `f` is a
uniform categorical moduli space in `Pr` (Stacks 0DUG, part (4)) — `Y` lies in `Pr` and for every
flat `a : Y' ⟶ Y` with `Y'` in `Pr` the base change `Y' ×_Y [U/R] ⟶ Y'` is a categorical moduli
space in `Pr` — exactly when `φ` is a uniform categorical quotient in `Pr` (Stacks 048L, part (2))
— `R`, `U` and `Y` lie in `Pr` and for every flat `a : Y' ⟶ Y` with `Y'` in `Pr` the base-changed
quotient map `U' ⟶ Y'` is the categorical quotient in `Pr` of the base-changed pre-relation
`(t', s')`, for `U' = Y' ×_Y U` and `R' = Y' ×_Y R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientStack_isUniformModuliSpaceIn_iff_isUniformQuotientIn_of_isClosedUnderLimitsOfShape
    (Pr : ObjectProperty (AlgebraicSpaces C S hS)) [Pr.IsClosedUnderLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan]
    (hR : Pr G.arrows) (hU : Pr G.objects) :
    (Pr Y ∧ ∀ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS), Pr Y' → ∀ (a : Y' ⟶ Y), Space.IsFlat C S hS a.hom →
        ∀ P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq
            (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom (BasedFunctor.comp f (liftedFibredCategoryUp Y)) :
              quotientStackAsStack G ⟶ spaceAsStack Y)
            (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom (liftedAssociatedMap a) :
              spaceAsStack Y' ⟶ spaceAsStack Y),
          Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P →
            IsBasedCategoricalModuliSpaceIn Pr Y'
              (BasedFunctor.comp P.snd.hom (liftedFibredCategoryDown Y'))) ↔
      Pr G.arrows ∧ Pr G.objects ∧ Pr Y ∧
        ∀ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces C S hS), Pr Y' → ∀ (a : Y' ⟶ Y), Space.IsFlat C S hS a.hom →
          Space.IsCategoricalQuotientIn (fun Z : Over B => Pr Z.left)
            (baseChangeSituationPreRelation hB G (restrictedMorphism G f)
              (restrictedMorphism_isInvariant G f) a)
            (baseChangeSituationQuotientMap hB G (restrictedMorphism G f)
              (restrictedMorphism_isInvariant G f) a)
declarations.comment: uniform, in a full subcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUniformCategoricalModuliSpace_of_affineFlatBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUJ.** A 1-morphism from a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of
`S` to the category attached to an algebraic space `Y` is a *uniform* categorical moduli space as
soon as every base change of it along a flat morphism to `Y` from an affine scheme is a
categorical moduli space.

The source states this for a 1-morphism from an algebraic stack; nothing of `𝒳` beyond being
fibred in groupoids is used, so it is stated here at that generality.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniformCategoricalModuliSpace_of_affineFlatBaseChange
    {𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ fibredCategory B S hS Y.obj)
    (h : ∀ T : BigFppfOver B S hS, IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) →
      ∀ a : (schemeSpace T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ Y,
        Space.IsFlat B S hS a.hom →
          ∀ P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq (associatedMap B S hS a.hom).1 f,
            Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P →
              IsCategoricalModuliSpace B S hS
                (schemeSpace T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
                P.fst) :
    IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpace B S hS Y f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsWellNighAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUL.** An algebraic stack over `S` is *well-nigh affine* when there is an object `U`
of the big fppf site of `S` with affine underlying scheme and a 1-morphism from the algebraic
stack it represents to `𝒳` which is surjective, flat, finite and of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsWellNighAffine (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompactStack_of_isWellNighAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUM, the quasi-compactness assertion.** A well-nigh affine algebraic stack is
quasi-compact: the algebraic stack of the affine scheme that Stacks 0DUL provides is
quasi-compact, and it surjects onto `𝒳`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactStack_of_isWellNighAffine
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (h𝒳 : IsWellNighAffine.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) :
    IsQuasiCompactStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒳.property
declarations.comment: a well-nigh affine algebraic stack is quasi-compact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasAffineFiniteLocallyFreeGroupoidPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUM, condition (2).** An algebraic stack over `S` has an *affine finite locally
free groupoid presentation* when it is equivalent over the site to the quotient stack of a
groupoid scheme whose object and arrow schemes are affine objects of the site and whose source
and target are finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
abbrev HasAffineFiniteLocallyFreeGroupoidPresentation
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: condition (2): a presentation by an affine groupoid scheme with finite locally free source and target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_representedGroupoid_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUM, the quasi-DM assertion.** An algebraic stack equivalent over the site to the
quotient stack of a groupoid scheme of the site with finite locally free source and target is
quasi-DM.

This is Stacks 0DTY, part (4): finite local freeness makes the source and target flat, locally of
finite presentation and locally quasi-finite, and the cancellation of the source projection of
the square of the object space makes `(t, s)` locally quasi-finite. Affineness of the object and
arrow schemes is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiDM_of_representedGroupoid_isFiniteLocallyFree
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hs : Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map s))
    (ht : Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map t))
    (hequiv : Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (quotientStack (representedGroupoid B S hS s t c hG)).p 𝒳.val.val.p)) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳
declarations.comment: a well-nigh affine algebraic stack is quasi-DM, read off condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparatedOver_of_representedGroupoid_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUM, the separatedness assertion over the base scheme of the site.** An algebraic
stack equivalent over the site to the quotient stack of a groupoid scheme of the site with affine
object scheme and finite locally free source and target is separated over `S`.

This is Stacks 0DTY, part (6): finite local freeness makes the source and target flat, locally of
finite presentation and proper, the object scheme being affine makes the object space separated
over `S`, and the cancellation of the separated source projection of the square of the object
space makes `(t, s)` proper.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparatedOver_of_representedGroupoid_isFiniteLocallyFree
    (hU : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U))
    (hs : Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map s))
    (ht : Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map t))
    (hequiv : Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (quotientStack (representedGroupoid B S hS s t c hG)).p 𝒳.val.val.p)) :
    IsSeparatedOver.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: a well-nigh affine algebraic stack is separated over the base scheme of the site, read off condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAbsolutelySeparated_of_representedGroupoid_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUM, the separatedness assertion.** An algebraic stack equivalent over the site to
the quotient stack of a groupoid scheme of the site with affine object scheme and finite locally
free source and target is separated in the source's unqualified, absolute sense of Stacks 050D,
part (7), provided the algebraic stack of the base scheme of the site is separated.

Separatedness over the base scheme is the previous clause; the absolute notion is strictly
stronger, and `hBase` is the one further input Stacks 0DTY needs to reach it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelySeparated_of_representedGroupoid_isFiniteLocallyFree
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hBase : AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelySeparated.{u, w} B S hS hZ
      (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hS)))))
    (hU : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U))
    (hs : Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map s))
    (ht : Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map t))
    (hequiv : Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (quotientStack (representedGroupoid B S hS s t c hG)).p 𝒳.val.val.p)) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelySeparated.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳
declarations.comment: a well-nigh affine algebraic stack is separated in the source's unqualified (absolute) sense, read off condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isWellNighAffine_iff_and_isQuasiCompact_isQuasiDM_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUM.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S`. The following are equivalent:

1. `𝒳` is well-nigh affine (Stacks 0DUL);
2. there is a groupoid scheme `(U, R, s, t, c)` with `U` and `R` affine and `s, t : R ⟶ U`
   finite locally free such that `𝒳 = [U/R]`.

If they hold, then `𝒳` is quasi-compact, quasi-DM and separated, the last two in the absolute
sense of Stacks 050D, parts (6) and (7), that is over `Spec ℤ`.

The equivalence is `hasAffineFiniteLocallyFreeGroupoidPresentation_of_isWellNighAffine` and
`isWellNighAffine_of_hasAffineFiniteLocallyFreeGroupoidPresentation`; quasi-compactness is
`isQuasiCompactStack_of_isWellNighAffine`, quasi-DM is Stacks 0DTY (4) applied to the
presentation of (2), and separatedness is `isAbsolutelySeparated_of_isWellNighAffine`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWellNighAffine_iff_and_isQuasiCompact_isQuasiDM_isSeparated
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    (IsWellNighAffine.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 ↔
        HasAffineFiniteLocallyFreeGroupoidPresentation.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) ∧
      (IsWellNighAffine.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 →
        IsQuasiCompactStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒳.property ∧
          AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiDM.{u, w} B S hS (contains_terminalScheme B) 𝒳 ∧
            AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelySeparated.{u, w} B S hS (contains_terminalScheme B) 𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isWellNighAffine_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUN, clause (2).** If `𝒳` is a well-nigh affine algebraic stack over `S` and
`f : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳` is an affine 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`, then `𝒳'` is well-nigh
affine.

The affine scheme `U` presenting `𝒳` is read as a scheme-valued point of `𝒳`; the base change of
`f` along it is represented by an algebraic space over `U` whose structural morphism is affine, so
tested at `U` itself it is the projection of an affine scheme `W` of the site. The apex of the
base-change square is then the algebraic stack of `W`, and its projection to `𝒳'` is surjective,
flat, finite and of finite presentation because the presentation of `𝒳` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWellNighAffine_of_isAffineHom {𝒳 𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsAffineHom B S hS f)
    (h𝒳 : IsWellNighAffine.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) :
    IsWellNighAffine.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳'
declarations.comment: clause (2): the source of an affine 1-morphism of algebraic stacks whose target is well-nigh affine is well-nigh affine

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAffineSpace_of_isWellNighAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUN, clause (1).** A well-nigh affine algebraic stack over `S` which is an
algebraic space is affine: every algebraic space `F` representing it over the site is affine.

The affine scheme `U` presenting `𝒳` represents an algebraic stack as well, so Stacks 04SW turns
the presentation into a morphism `h_U ⟶ F` of algebraic spaces over `S`. It is surjective
because the presentation is surjective on points, finite because the presentation is finite in
the relative sense of Stacks 03YK, flat because the presentation is flat, and locally of finite
presentation because the presentation is of finite presentation; so it is a surjective finite
locally free chart of `F` by Stacks 0416, and the ring of invariant functions of its kernel
pair makes `F` affine by Stacks 03BM.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineSpace_of_isWellNighAffine (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : IsWellNighAffine.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (eF : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver 𝒳.val.val.p
      (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) :
    Space.IsAffineSpace B S hS F
declarations.comment: clause (1): a well-nigh affine algebraic stack which is an algebraic space is affine

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.existsUnique_comp_objectsToInvariantSpectrum
declarations.doc:
Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid scheme and let `C` be the ring of `R`-invariant
global functions on `U`. Every morphism `ψ : U ⟶ Spec C'` to an affine scheme which coequalizes
the target and the source maps factors uniquely through `φ : U ⟶ Spec C`. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.target_comp_objectsToInvariantSpectrum` this says that `φ` is a
categorical quotient of `(t, s)` in the category of affine schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_comp_objectsToInvariantSpectrum (C' : Type u) [CommRing C']
    (ψ : G.objects.left ⟶ Spec (.of C'))
    (hψ : G.target.left ≫ ψ = G.source.left ≫ ψ) :
    ∃! χ : Spec (.of (invariantRing G)) ⟶ Spec (.of C'),
      objectsToInvariantSpectrum G ≫ χ = ψ
declarations.comment: the construction of the moduli space and its universal property, at the groupoid presentation and for the quotient map of the object scheme: the invariant-ring quotient U -> M = Spec C is a categorical quotient in the category of affine schemes. The 1-morphism f : X -> M out of the quotient stack is NOT constructed, and none of the four assertions about f is proved: the passage from U -> M to f along Stacks 0DUH and Stacks 0DUI, and the implication (1) => (2) of Stacks 0DUM, are not available in the library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.existsUnique_comp_objects_hom_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Let `C ⟶ C'` be a flat ring map and let `G'` be the base change of the groupoid along it.
Then the structure morphism `U' ⟶ Spec C'` of the object scheme of `G'` has the universal property
of `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.existsUnique_comp_objectsToInvariantSpectrum`: every morphism
from `U'` to an affine scheme which coequalizes the target and the source maps of `G'` factors
uniquely through it.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_comp_objects_hom_of_flat [Module.Flat (invariantRing G) C']
    (C'' : Type u) [CommRing C''] (ψ : G'.groupoid.objects.left ⟶ Spec (.of C''))
    (hψ : G'.groupoid.target.left ≫ ψ = G'.groupoid.source.left ≫ ψ) :
    ∃! χ : Spec (.of C') ⟶ Spec (.of C''), G'.groupoid.objects.hom ≫ χ = ψ
declarations.comment: the word *uniform*, at the groupoid presentation and for the quotient map of the object scheme: after a flat base change C -> C' the structure morphism U' -> Spec C' of the base-changed groupoid is again a categorical quotient in the category of affine schemes, so the flat base change of M is again the moduli space. Stated for U' -> Spec C' and NOT for the base change of a 1-morphism f : X -> M, which is not constructed here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.universallyClosed_objectsToInvariantSpectrum
declarations.doc: The invariant quotient map `U ⟶ M = Spec C` is universally closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_objectsToInvariantSpectrum :
    UniversallyClosed (objectsToInvariantSpectrum G)
declarations.comment: part of assertion (d), at the groupoid presentation and for the quotient map of the object scheme: U -> M = Spec C is integral (Stacks 03BJ) and therefore universally closed (Stacks 01WM). That f : X -> M is a universal homeomorphism is NOT proved: neither the transport of universal closedness along the surjection U -> X (Stacks 0CQK), nor universal injectivity of f (Stacks 0DTN), nor surjectivity of |f| is covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isUniformCategoricalModuliSpaceIn_of_isWellNighAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUP.** Let the algebraic stack `𝒳` be well-nigh affine. There exists a uniform
categorical moduli space `f : 𝒳 ⟶ M` in the category of affine schemes. Moreover `f` is
separated, quasi-compact, and a universal homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isUniformCategoricalModuliSpaceIn_of_isWellNighAffine
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (h𝒳 : IsWellNighAffine.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) :
    ∃ (M : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
      (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS M.obj M.property),
      IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpaceIn B S hS (fun W => Space.IsAffineSpace B S hS W.obj) M
          f.hom ∧
        AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f ∧ IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f ∧
          UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isTwoFibreProduct_moduliSpace_of_isEtale_of_inducesIsomorphismAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUQ.** Let `h : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳` be a morphism of algebraic stacks. Assume `𝒳'` and `𝒳` are
well-nigh affine, `h` is étale, and `h` induces isomorphisms on automorphism groups (Stacks 0DTW).
Then there exists a cartesian diagram
```
𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳
↓     ↓
M' ⟶ M
```
where `M' ⟶ M` is étale and the vertical arrows are moduli spaces as constructed in Stacks 0DUP:
uniform categorical moduli spaces in affine schemes, separated, quasi-compact and universal
homeomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isTwoFibreProduct_moduliSpace_of_isEtale_of_inducesIsomorphismAt
    {𝒳 𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (h : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳)
    (h𝒳 : IsWellNighAffine.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (h𝒳' : IsWellNighAffine.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳')
    (he : IsEtale B S hS h)
    (hauto : ∀ q : points B S hS 𝒳'.val.val 𝒳'.val.isFiberedInGroupoids,
      InducesIsomorphismAt B S hS h q) :
    ∃ (M M' : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS (yoneda.obj M) (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS M))
      (f' : 𝒳' ⟶
        algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS (yoneda.obj M') (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS M'))
      (g : M' ⟶ M) (hcomm : f'.hom ≫ (associatedMap B S hS (yoneda.map g)).1 = h.hom ≫ f.hom),
      Etale ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g) ∧
      Nonempty (Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct
        (ChartBaseChange.moduliSquare h g f.hom f'.hom hcomm)) ∧
      (IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpaceIn B S hS (fun W => Space.IsAffineSpace B S hS W.obj)
          (schemeSpace M) f.hom ∧
        AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f ∧ IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f ∧
          UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f) ∧
      (IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpaceIn B S hS (fun W => Space.IsAffineSpace B S hS W.obj)
          (schemeSpace M') f'.hom ∧
        AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f' ∧ IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f' ∧
          UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUniformCategoricalModuliSpace_of_isWellNighAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUR.** Let `𝒳` be a well-nigh affine algebraic stack. The morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ M` of
Stacks 0DUP is a uniform categorical moduli space.

The first clause is the morphism of Stacks 0DUP with all the properties that lemma gives it, and
the conclusion of Stacks 0DUR. The second clause says the same of every 1-morphism to an algebraic
space which is a uniform categorical moduli space in the category of affine algebraic spaces, the
property by which Stacks 0DUP characterizes its morphism up to unique isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniformCategoricalModuliSpace_of_isWellNighAffine (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : IsWellNighAffine.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) :
    (∃ (M : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS M.obj M.property),
        IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpaceIn B S hS (fun W => Space.IsAffineSpace B S hS W.obj) M
            f.hom ∧
          AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f ∧ IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f ∧
          UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f ∧ IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpace B S hS M f.hom) ∧
      ∀ (M : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : 𝒳.val ⟶ fibredCategory B S hS M.obj),
        IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpaceIn B S hS (fun W => Space.IsAffineSpace B S hS W.obj)
          M f →
        IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpace B S hS M f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isTwoFibreProduct_moduliSpace_of_isEtale_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUS.** Let `h : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳` be a morphism of algebraic stacks. Assume `𝒳` is well-nigh
affine, `h` is étale, `h` is separated, and `h` induces isomorphisms on automorphism groups
(Stacks 0DTW). Then there exists a cartesian diagram
```
𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳
↓     ↓
M' ⟶ M
```
where `M' ⟶ M` is a separated étale morphism of schemes and `𝒳 ⟶ M` is the moduli space
constructed in Stacks 0DUP: a uniform categorical moduli space in affine schemes, separated,
quasi-compact and a universal homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isTwoFibreProduct_moduliSpace_of_isEtale_of_isSeparated
    {𝒳 𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (h : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳)
    (h𝒳 : IsWellNighAffine.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (he : IsEtale B S hS h) (hsep : AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS h)
    (hauto : ∀ q : points B S hS 𝒳'.val.val 𝒳'.val.isFiberedInGroupoids,
      InducesIsomorphismAt B S hS h q) :
    ∃ (M M' : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS (yoneda.obj M) (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS M))
      (f' : 𝒳' ⟶
        algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS (yoneda.obj M') (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS M'))
      (g : M' ⟶ M) (hcomm : f'.hom ≫ (associatedMap B S hS (yoneda.map g)).1 = h.hom ≫ f.hom),
      Etale ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g) ∧
      _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g) ∧
      Nonempty (Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct
        (ChartBaseChange.moduliSquare h g f.hom f'.hom hcomm)) ∧
      (IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpaceIn B S hS (fun W => Space.IsAffineSpace B S hS W.obj)
          ⟨yoneda.obj M, isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS M⟩ f.hom ∧
        AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f ∧ IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f ∧
          UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isUniformCategoricalModuliSpace_of_isFinite_inertia
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUT (Keel–Mori).** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack whose inertia `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is
finite. Then there exists a uniform categorical moduli space `f : 𝒳 ⟶ M`, and `f` is separated,
quasi-compact, and a universal homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isUniformCategoricalModuliSpace_of_isFinite_inertia
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hI : AlgebraicStacks.IsFinite B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳)) :
    ∃ (M : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS M.obj M.property),
      IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpace B S hS M f.hom ∧ AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f ∧
        IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f ∧ UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isTwoFibreProduct_keelMoriModuliSpace_of_isEtale_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUV.** Let `h : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks. Assume that the
inertia `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is finite, and that `h` is étale, separated, and induces isomorphisms between
automorphism groups at every point (Stacks 0DTW). Then there are moduli spaces `f : 𝒳 ⟶ M` and
`f' : 𝒳' ⟶ M'` as in Theorem 0DUT (uniform categorical moduli spaces which are separated,
quasi-compact and universal homeomorphisms) and a separated étale morphism `g : M' ⟶ M` of
algebraic spaces with `f' ≫ g = h ≫ f`, such that the square `𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳` over `g` is a 2-fibre
product.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isTwoFibreProduct_keelMoriModuliSpace_of_isEtale_of_isSeparated
    {𝒳 𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (h : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hI : AlgebraicStacks.IsFinite B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳))
    (he : IsEtale B S hS h) (hsep : AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS h)
    (hauto : ∀ q : points B S hS 𝒳'.val.val 𝒳'.val.isFiberedInGroupoids,
      InducesIsomorphismAt B S hS h q) :
    ∃ (M M' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
      (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS M.obj M.property)
      (f' : 𝒳' ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS M'.obj M'.property) (g : M' ⟶ M)
      (hcomm : f'.hom ≫ (associatedMap B S hS g.hom).1 = h.hom ≫ f.hom),
      Space.IsEtale B S hS g.hom ∧ Space.IsSeparated B S hS g.hom ∧
      Nonempty (Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct
        (⟨𝒳'.val, f'.hom, h.hom, eqToIso hcomm⟩ :
          Bicategory.TwoCommSq (associatedMap B S hS g.hom).1 f.hom)) ∧
      (IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpace B S hS M f.hom ∧ AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f ∧
        IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f ∧ UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f) ∧
      (IsUniformCategoricalModuliSpace B S hS M' f'.hom ∧ AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f' ∧
        IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f' ∧ UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isCategoricalModuliSpace_of_isFinite_inertia
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUX.** Let `p : 𝒳 ⟶ Y` be a 1-morphism from an algebraic stack to an algebraic
space such that the inertia `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is finite, `Y` is locally Noetherian and `p` is locally
of finite type, and let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ M` be a categorical moduli space (for instance the moduli
space of Stacks 0DUT). Then `p` factors as `f` followed by a unique morphism `M ⟶ Y`, up to a
2-isomorphism, and that morphism `M ⟶ Y` is locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isCategoricalModuliSpace_of_isFinite_inertia
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hI : AlgebraicStacks.IsFinite B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳))
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hY : Space.HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.obj (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (p : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Y.obj Y.property)
    (hp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS p)
    (M : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS M.obj M.property)
    (hf : IsCategoricalModuliSpace B S hS M f.hom) :
    (∃! q : M ⟶ Y, Nonempty (f.hom ≫ (associatedMap B S hS q.hom).1 ≅ p.hom)) ∧
      ∀ q : M ⟶ Y, Nonempty (f.hom ≫ (associatedMap B S hS q.hom).1 ≅ p.hom) →
        Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS q.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_and_isAbsolutelySeparated_of_isFinite_inertia
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUY.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack whose inertia `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is finite, and let
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ M` be a categorical moduli space — for instance the moduli space constructed in
Stacks 0DUT, which every categorical moduli space of `𝒳` is up to unique isomorphism. Then
1. if `𝒳` is quasi-separated, then `M` is quasi-separated;
2. if `𝒳` is separated, then `M` is separated.

Both properties are absolute, over the terminal scheme `Spec ℤ` (Stacks 050D parts (8), (7) and
Stacks 03BS parts (3), (1)). Part (3) of the source ("Add more here") asserts nothing.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_and_isAbsolutelySeparated_of_isFinite_inertia
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hI : AlgebraicStacks.IsFinite B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳))
    (M : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS M.obj M.property)
    (hf : IsCategoricalModuliSpace B S hS M f.hom) :
    (AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳 →
        Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ M.obj) ∧
      (AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelySeparated.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳 →
        Space.IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ M.obj)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_and_isAbsolutelySeparated_of_universalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUY.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ M` be a universal homeomorphism (Stacks 0CI7) from an algebraic
stack over `S` to an algebraic space over `S` — for instance the moduli space of the Keel–Mori
theorem (Stacks 0DUT) of an algebraic stack with finite inertia, which is a universal
homeomorphism. Then
1. if `𝒳` is quasi-separated, then `M` is quasi-separated;
2. if `𝒳` is separated, then `M` is separated.

Both properties are absolute (Stacks 050D parts (7), (8) and Stacks 03BS parts (1), (3)). Part (3)
of the source ("Add more here") asserts nothing.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_and_isAbsolutelySeparated_of_universalHomeomorphism
    {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {M : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hM : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS M) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS M hM)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f) :
    (AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳 →
        Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ M) ∧
      (AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelySeparated.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳 →
        Space.IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isProper_of_isCategoricalModuliSpace_of_isFinite_inertia
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DUZ.** Let `p : 𝒳 ⟶ Y` be a 1-morphism from an algebraic stack to an algebraic
space. Assume
1. `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is finite,
2. `p` is proper, and
3. `Y` is locally Noetherian.

Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ M` be a categorical moduli space — for instance the moduli space constructed in
Stacks 0DUT, which every categorical moduli space of `𝒳` is up to unique isomorphism. Then `p`
factors as `f` followed by a unique morphism `M ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces, up to a 2-isomorphism,
and `M ⟶ Y` is proper.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_isCategoricalModuliSpace_of_isFinite_inertia
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hI : AlgebraicStacks.IsFinite B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳))
    (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hY : Space.HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.obj (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (p : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Y.obj Y.property)
    (hp : AlgebraicStacks.IsProper B S hS p)
    (M : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS M.obj M.property)
    (hf : IsCategoricalModuliSpace B S hS M f.hom) :
    (∃! g : M ⟶ Y, Nonempty (f.hom ≫ (associatedMap B S hS g.hom).1 ≅ p.hom)) ∧
      ∀ g : M ⟶ Y, Nonempty (f.hom ≫ (associatedMap B S hS g.hom).1 ≅ p.hom) →
        Space.IsProper B S hS g.hom

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.isColimit_pushforwardStage_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DV2.** Let `I` be a directed set, let `(X_i, f_{i'i})` and `(S_i, h_{i'i})` be
inverse systems of schemes with affine transition morphisms, let `g_i : X_i ⟶ S_i` be a morphism
of the first system into the second with every `g_i` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let
`f_i : X ⟶ X_i` and `h_i : S ⟶ S_i` be the projections of limit cones over the two systems, let
`g : X ⟶ S` be the limit morphism, and let `𝓕` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of
`X`. Then

`R^p g_* 𝓕 = colim_{i ∈ I} h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *}(f_{i, *}𝓕)`:

the objects `h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *}(f_{i, *}𝓕)` with the maps induced by the transition maps
`ψ_{i'i}` of [Stacks, Tag 0EYM] satisfy the cocycle condition, the maps `ψ_i` of the same source
form a cocone on them, and that cocone is a colimit.

The counits present `𝓕 = colim_i f_i^{-1}f_{i, *}𝓕` by the colimit half of [Stacks, Tag 0EYN],
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isPullbackColimitPresentation_directImageSystem`; they are compatible with
the transition maps of `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.directImageSystem` by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.coneDirectImageCounit_cocone`, and [Stacks, Tag 0EYM],
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.isHigherDirectImageColimit`, applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isColimit_pushforwardStage_of_isLimit [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DX.map a)]
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DS.map a)]
    [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, QuasiCompact (γ.app i)] [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, QuasiSeparated (γ.app i)]
    (hcX : IsLimit cX) :
    (∀ {i j k : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j) (b : j ⟶ k),
        (systemPullbackComp DS Ab.{u + 1} a b).inv.app
              (((smallEtalePushforwardAb (γ.app k)).rightDerived p).obj
                ((directImageSystem DX Ab.{u + 1} cX 𝓕).obj k)) ≫
            (systemPullback DS Ab.{u + 1} a).map (pushforwardStageTransition cX 𝓕 γ p b) ≫
              pushforwardStageTransition cX 𝓕 γ p a =
          pushforwardStageTransition cX 𝓕 γ p (a ≫ b)) ∧
      (∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j),
          (conePullbackComp cS a).inv.app
                (((smallEtalePushforwardAb (γ.app j)).rightDerived p).obj
                  ((directImageSystem DX Ab.{u + 1} cX 𝓕).obj j)) ≫
              (smallEtalePullbackAb (cS.π.app i)).map (pushforwardStageTransition cX 𝓕 γ p a) ≫
                pushforwardStageLeg cX 𝓕 γ cS hcS p i =
            pushforwardStageLeg cX 𝓕 γ cS hcS p j) ∧
        IsHigherDirectImageColimit γ p cX cS hcS 𝓕 (directImageSystem DX Ab.{u + 1} cX 𝓕)
          (coneDirectImageCounit cX 𝓕)
declarations.comment: the colimit assertion for the canonical diagram and the canonical cocone, with the cocycle condition of the diagram and the cocone identity of its legs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteLocallyConstantAbelianSheafEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DV5, part (2).** For a connected scheme `X` with a geometric point
`x`, the finite locally constant sheaves of abelian groups on `X_étale` are equivalent to the
finite `π₁(X, x)`-modules, that is, to the finite abelian groups with a continuous action of the
étale fundamental group.

Part (1) of the tag is `AlgebraicGeometry.finiteLocallyConstantSetsEquivalence` and part (3) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheafEquivalence`.
declarations.comment: (2) finite locally constant sheaves of abelian groups are the finite π₁(X, x)-modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheafEquivalence
declarations.doc:
For a connected scheme `X` with a geometric point `x` and a finite ring `Λ`, the finite type
locally constant sheaves of `Λ`-modules on `X_étale` are equivalent to the finite `Λ`-modules
endowed with a commuting continuous action of `π₁(X, x)`.
declarations.statement:
public def finiteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheafEquivalence :
    ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
        (fun F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.2) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) ↦
          IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstant Λ (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.2) F) ≌
      FiniteTypeContinuousModule.{r, u + 1, u + 1} Λ (EtaleFundamentalGroup X.1 x)
declarations.comment: (3) finite type locally constant sheaves of Λ-modules, for Λ a finite ring, are the finite π₁(X, x)-modules with commuting Λ-module structure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteLocallyConstantSetsEquivalence
declarations.doc:
For a connected scheme `X` with a geometric point `x`, the equivalence between the finite
locally constant sheaves of sets on the small étale site of `X` and the finite sets with a
continuous action of the étale fundamental group `π₁(X, x)`. It is
`finiteLocallyConstantFiniteEtaleEquivalence` followed by
`finiteEtaleEquivalenceOfIsGaloisCategory` and the change of universe
`contActionUniverseEquivalence`.
declarations.comment: (1) finite locally constant sheaves of sets are the finite continuous π₁(X, x)-sets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteSmallEtaleToFiniteLocallyConstantBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DV6, the first leg of the sets case.** The inverse image of the
finite locally constant sheaf represented by a finite étale cover is the one represented by its
base change: the square of `AlgebraicGeometry.finiteSmallEtaleToFiniteLocallyConstant` against
base change on the site and inverse image on sheaves commutes.

The equivalence of Tag 0DV5 (1) between the finite locally constant sheaves of sets on
`X_étale` and the finite continuous `π₁(X, x)`-sets is the composite of two legs, the dictionary
of Tag 03RV with finite étale covers and the equivalence of Tag 0BND (1). This is the
compatibility of the first leg with pullbacks.
declarations.comment: the sets case, first leg: the dictionary of Stacks 03RV between the finite objects of the small etale site and the finite locally constant sheaves of sets commutes with pullback. The second leg, Stacks 0BND (3), is proved separately as AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteEtaleEquivalence_mapIso; the two legs are not composed here, which would need the comparison of AlgebraicGeometry.finiteSmallEtaleBaseChange with AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleBaseChange across AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleSiteEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_finiteLocallyConstantSetsEquivalence_pullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DV6 for sheaves of sets.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of connected
schemes and let `y` be a geometric point of `Y`, with image `x = f(y)`. Then the square

```
  finite locally constant sheaves of sets on X_étale  ──→  finite π₁(X, x)-sets
                        │                                          │
                     f^{-1}                                   restriction
                        ↓                                          ↓
  finite locally constant sheaves of sets on Y_étale  ──→  finite π₁(Y, y)-sets
```

commutes, where the horizontal arrows are the equivalence of Stacks Tag 0DV5 (1) and the right
vertical arrow reindexes the action along the homomorphism `π₁(Y, y) ⟶ π₁(X, x)` induced by
`f`.

The equivalence of Tag 0DV5 (1) is the composite of the dictionary of Tag 03RV with the finite
étale covers, the equivalence of Tag 0BND (1) and a change of universe. The first factor
commutes with pullback by
`AlgebraicGeometry.finiteLocallyConstantFiniteEtaleEquivalenceBaseChangeIso`, the second by
Tag 0BND (3), that is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteEtaleEquivalence_mapIso`, and the third
on the nose. Only the existence of the comparison is asserted, because Tag 0BND (3) is
available in that form.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_finiteLocallyConstantSetsEquivalence_pullbackIso
    [ConnectedSpace X.1] [ConnectedSpace Y.1] (y : GeometricPoint Y.1) :
    Nonempty ((finiteLocallyConstantSetsEquivalence B X (y.map f.hom)).functor ⋙
        ContAction.res FintypeCat.{u + 1} (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f.hom y) ≅
      finiteLocallyConstantSheafPullback B f ⋙
        (finiteLocallyConstantSetsEquivalence B Y y).functor)
declarations.comment: for sheaves of sets: the equivalence of Stacks 0DV5 (1) commutes with pullback, the action being reindexed along the induced homomorphism of fundamental groups

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_finiteLocallyConstantAbelianSheafEquivalence_pullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DV6 for sheaves of abelian groups.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of
connected schemes and let `y` be a geometric point of `Y`, with image `x = f(y)`. Then the square

```
  finite locally constant abelian sheaves on X_étale  ──→  finite π₁(X, x)-modules
                        │                                          │
                     f^{-1}                                   restriction
                        ↓                                          ↓
  finite locally constant abelian sheaves on Y_étale  ──→  finite π₁(Y, y)-modules
```

commutes, where the horizontal arrows are the equivalence of Stacks Tag 0DV5 (2), the left
vertical arrow is the inverse image of abelian sheaves
(`AlgebraicGeometry.finiteLocallyConstantAbelianSheafPullback_comp_ι`) and the right vertical
arrow reindexes the action along the homomorphism `π₁(Y, y) ⟶ π₁(X, x)` induced by `f`
(`CategoryTheory.ContinuousGAddCommGrp.resIsFinite_comp_ι`).

The equivalence of Tag 0DV5 (2) is the transport of commutative group objects along the
equivalence of Tag 0DV5 (1), and the only factor of that transport which depends on the latter is
`CategoryTheory.Functor.mapCommGrp` applied to it, so the sets case of Tag 0DV6 transports:
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.finiteLocallyConstantAbelianPullbackSquare`. Its two remaining inputs are
the compatibility of each dictionary with the two vertical arrows, and for the sheaf side that is
the identification of the inverse image of abelian sheaves with the inverse image of the
underlying sheaves of sets together with the induced group operations,
`Stacks.Sites.AbelianPullback.internalSheafPullbackSquare`. Only the existence of the comparison
is asserted, because the sets case is available in that form.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_finiteLocallyConstantAbelianSheafEquivalence_pullbackIso
    [ConnectedSpace X.1] [ConnectedSpace Y.1] (y : GeometricPoint Y.1) :
    Nonempty ((finiteLocallyConstantAbelianSheafEquivalence B X (y.map f.hom)).functor ⋙
        ContinuousGAddCommGrp.resIsFinite (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f.hom y) ≅
      finiteLocallyConstantAbelianSheafPullback B f ⋙
        (finiteLocallyConstantAbelianSheafEquivalence B Y y).functor)
declarations.comment: for sheaves of abelian groups: the equivalence of Stacks 0DV5 (2) commutes with pullback, the action being reindexed along the induced homomorphism of fundamental groups

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_finiteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheafEquivalence_pullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DV6 for sheaves of modules.** Let `Λ` be a finite ring, let
`f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of connected schemes and let `y` be a geometric point of `Y`, with
image `x = f(y)`. Then the square

```
  finite type locally constant Λ-module sheaves on X_étale  ──→  finite Λ-π₁(X, x)-modules
                        │                                                 │
                     f^{-1}                                          restriction
                        ↓                                                 ↓
  finite type locally constant Λ-module sheaves on Y_étale  ──→  finite Λ-π₁(Y, y)-modules
```

commutes, where the horizontal arrows are the equivalence of Stacks Tag 0DV5 (3), the left
vertical arrow is the inverse image of sheaves of `Λ`-modules
(`AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheafPullback_comp_ι`) and the right vertical
arrow reindexes the action along the homomorphism `π₁(Y, y) ⟶ π₁(X, x)` induced by `f`
(`Stacks.GroupCohomology.finiteTypeContinuousModuleRes_comp_ι` together with
`Stacks.GroupCohomology.continuousModuleRes_comp_ι`).

The equivalence of Tag 0DV5 (3) is the equivalence of Tag 0DV5 (2) read on additive functors out
of the one-object category of `Λ`, and the only factor of that reading which depends on the
latter is postcomposition with it, so the abelian case of Tag 0DV6 transports:
`CategoryTheory.scalarActionTransportSquare`. Only the existence of the comparison is asserted,
because the abelian case is available in that form.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_finiteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheafEquivalence_pullbackIso
    (y : GeometricPoint Y.1) :
    Nonempty ((finiteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheafEquivalence B X (y.map f.hom) Λ).functor ⋙
        finiteTypeContinuousModuleRes Λ (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f.hom y) ≅
      finiteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheafPullback B f Λ ⋙
        (finiteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheafEquivalence B Y y Λ).functor)
declarations.comment: for sheaves of modules over a finite ring: the equivalence of Stacks 0DV5 (3) commutes with pullback, the action being reindexed along the induced homomorphism of fundamental groups

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeLocallyConstantEquivContinuousModuleUnivPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DV6, for the equivalence of Tag 0GIY.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism
of irreducible, geometrically unibranch schemes, let `y` be a geometric point of `Y` and let `Λ`
be a ring. The equivalences of Tag 0GIY for `X` at `f(y)` and for `Y` at `y` are compatible with
pullback: the square

```
  finite type loc. const. Λ-module sheaves on X_étale  ──→  finite Λ-π₁(X, f(y))-modules
                      │                                               │
                   f^{-1}                                        restriction
                      ↓                                               ↓
  finite type loc. const. Λ-module sheaves on Y_étale  ──→  finite Λ-π₁(Y, y)-modules
```

commutes up to the natural isomorphism given here, the right-hand vertical arrow restricting the
action along the homomorphism `π₁(Y, y) ⟶ π₁(X, f(y))` of Tag 0BND (3).

The comparison sends the image of a section `s` over a pointed Galois cover `A` of `X` to the
image of the restriction of `f^{-1}s` to a pointed Galois cover of `Y` dominating `A ×_X Y`; it is
bijective because `f^{-1}` carries a trivialization of `F` over `A` to one of `f^{-1}F` over
`A ×_X Y`, compatibly with the sections.
declarations.statement:
public def finiteTypeLocallyConstantEquivContinuousModuleUnivPullbackIso :
    (finiteTypeLocallyConstantEquivContinuousModuleUniv X hX (y.map f) Λ).functor ⋙
        finiteTypeContinuousModuleRes Λ (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f y) ≅
      etaleFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModulePullback f Λ ⋙
        (finiteTypeLocallyConstantEquivContinuousModuleUniv Y hY y Λ).functor
declarations.comment: the square for the equivalence of Stacks 0GIY; the squares for the equivalences of Stacks 0DV5 are in BaseChangeRepresentable and BaseChangeEtaleSite

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isPrimePowerTorsion_nontrivial_sheafH_smallEtalePushforwardAb_of_isLimit

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_isPrimePowerTorsion_nontrivial_sheafH_iff_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DV7].** Let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let
`X = lim Xᵢ` be the limit of a directed system of `S`-schemes `ιᵢ : Xᵢ ⟶ S`, each finite étale of
constant degree `dᵢ` prime to `ℓ`, with structure morphism `g : X ⟶ S`. Then there is an
`ℓ`-power torsion sheaf `G` on `S_étale` with `Hⁿ(S, G) ≠ 0` if and only if there is an `ℓ`-power
torsion sheaf `F` on `X_étale` with `Hⁿ(X, F) ≠ 0`.

The source assumes that `ℓ` is prime and that `n > 0`; the proof uses neither.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPrimePowerTorsion_nontrivial_sheafH_iff_of_isLimit [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    [Nonempty I] [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [∀ i, IsFinite (ι i)]
    [∀ i, Etale (ι i)] (d : Iᵒᵖ → ℕ) [∀ i, Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (ι i) (d i)]
    {ℓ : ℕ} (hd : ∀ i, (d i).Coprime ℓ) (hc : IsLimit c) (n : ℕ) :
    (∃ G : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology S) Ab.{u + 1},
        Stacks.Torsion.IsPrimePowerTorsion (smallEtaleTopology S) ℓ G ∧
          Nontrivial (Sheaf.H.{u + 1} G n)) ↔
      ∃ F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology c.pt) Ab.{u + 1},
        Stacks.Torsion.IsPrimePowerTorsion (smallEtaleTopology c.pt) ℓ F ∧
          Nontrivial (Sheaf.H.{u + 1} F n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_sheafH_iff_of_isMaximalProPSubgroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DV8.** Let `ℓ` be a prime, `K` a field with separable closure `Kˢᵉᵖ`,
`H` a maximal pro-`ℓ` subgroup of `Gal(Kˢᵉᵖ/K)` and `L` its fixed field. Then
`Hⁿ_ét(Spec K, 𝓕)` vanishes for every `ℓ`-power torsion abelian sheaf `𝓕` on the small étale
site of `Spec K` if and only if `Hⁿ_ét(Spec L, ℤ/ℓℤ)` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_iff_of_isMaximalProPSubgroup (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (n : ℕ)
    (hH : IsMaximalProPSubgroup ℓ H)
    [HasExt (Sheaf (Spec (.of K)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})]
    [HasExt (Sheaf (Spec (.of (fixedField H))).smallEtaleTopology
      AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})] :
    (∀ 𝓕 : Sheaf (Spec (.of K)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v},
      Stacks.Torsion.IsPrimePowerTorsion _ ℓ 𝓕 → Subsingleton (Sheaf.H 𝓕 n)) ↔
      Subsingleton (Sheaf.H ((constantSheaf (Spec (.of (fixedField H))).smallEtaleTopology
        AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{max (u + 1) v} (ZMod ℓ))))
          n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tfae_subsingleton_sheafH_of_isMaximalProPSubgroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DV9.** Let `ℓ` be a prime, `K` a field with separable closure `Kˢᵉᵖ`,
`H` a maximal pro-`ℓ` subgroup of `Gal(Kˢᵉᵖ/K)` and `L` its fixed field. The following are
equivalent:
1. `H^q_ét(Spec K, 𝓕)` vanishes for every `q ≥ n` and every `ℓ`-power torsion abelian sheaf `𝓕`
   on the small étale site of `Spec K`;
2. `H^q_ét(Spec K, 𝓕)` vanishes for every `q ≥ n` and every abelian sheaf `𝓕` on the small étale
   site of `Spec K` killed by `ℓ`;
3. `Hⁿ_ét(Spec L, ℤ/ℓℤ)` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_subsingleton_sheafH_of_isMaximalProPSubgroup (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (n : ℕ)
    (hH : IsMaximalProPSubgroup ℓ H)
    [HasExt (Sheaf (Spec (.of K)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})]
    [HasExt (Sheaf (Spec (.of (fixedField H))).smallEtaleTopology
      AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})] :
    List.TFAE [
      ∀ q, n ≤ q → ∀ 𝓕 : Sheaf (Spec (.of K)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v},
        Stacks.Torsion.IsPrimePowerTorsion _ ℓ 𝓕 → Subsingleton (Sheaf.H 𝓕 q),
      ∀ q, n ≤ q → ∀ 𝓕 : Sheaf (Spec (.of K)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v},
        ℓ • 𝟙 𝓕 = 0 → Subsingleton (Sheaf.H 𝓕 q),
      Subsingleton (Sheaf.H ((constantSheaf (Spec (.of (fixedField H))).smallEtaleTopology
        AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{max (u + 1) v} (ZMod ℓ))))
          n)]
declarations.comment: both readings of `ℓ`-torsion: `ℓ`-power torsion (1) and killed by `ℓ` (2)
