declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.existsUnique_homEquiv_derivedCategory_of_isRightDerivedValueAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVC**: deriving adjoints between derived categories. Let `F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` be right
adjoint to `G : ℬ ⥤ 𝒜`, functors of abelian categories, let `K` be a complex of `𝒜` and `M` a
complex of `ℬ`, and let `RF`, resp. `LG`, be the right, resp. left, derived functor of
`K(𝒜) ⥤ K(ℬ) ⥤ D(ℬ)`, resp. `K(ℬ) ⥤ K(𝒜) ⥤ D(𝒜)`, with respect to the quasi-isomorphisms.
Assume `RF` is defined at `K`, with value `RF(K) = c.pt`, and `LG` is defined at `M`, with value
`LG(M) = d.pt` (Stacks 05S9). Then there is a unique bijection
`Hom_{D(ℬ)}(M, RF(K)) ≃ Hom_{D(𝒜)}(LG(M), K)` compatible with the fractions computing the two
sides: for every index `s : K ⟶ I` of the ind-object defining `RF(K)`, every index `t : P ⟶ M`
of the pro-object defining `LG(M)` and every pair of chain maps `f : P ⟶ F(I)`, `g : G(P) ⟶ I`
that are adjoint to one another in each degree, a morphism `ψ : M ⟶ RF(K)` satisfies
`Qh(t) ≫ ψ = Qh(f) ≫ (coprojection at s)` if and only if its image satisfies
`φ(ψ) ≫ Qh(s) = (projection at t) ≫ Qh(g)`.

The source's further assertion that this isomorphism is functorial in both variables is not part
of this statement: the bijection is named `CategoryTheory.Adjunction.derivedCategoryHomEquiv`, and
its naturality in `K` and in `M` is `derivedCategoryHomEquiv_comp_rightDerivedMap` and
`derivedCategoryHomEquiv_map_comp`, in the module
`StacksFrontier.CategoryTheory.Localization.DerivingAdjointsNaturality`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_homEquiv_derivedCategory_of_isRightDerivedValueAt
    {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} A]
    {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B] [Abelian B] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} B]
    {F : A ⥤ B} {G : B ⥤ A} [F.Additive] [G.Additive] (adj : G ⊣ F)
    (K : HomotopyCategory A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) (M : HomotopyCategory B (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    (c : Cocone (MorphismProperty.Under.forget
        (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ⊤ K ⋙
      Under.forget K ⋙ F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh))
    (hc : (F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).IsRightDerivedValueAt
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) K c)
    (d : Cone (MorphismProperty.Over.forget
        (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ⊤ M ⋙
      Over.forget M ⋙ G.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh))
    (hd : (G.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).IsLeftDerivedValueAt
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) M d) :
    ∃! φ : (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj M ⟶ c.pt) ≃ (d.pt ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh.obj K),
      ∀ (s : (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).Under ⊤ K)
        (t : (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).Over ⊤ M)
        (f : t.left.as ⟶ (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj s.right.as)
        (g : (G.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj t.left.as ⟶ s.right.as),
        (∀ n, f.f n = adj.homEquiv _ _ (g.f n)) →
        ∀ ψ : DerivedCategory.Qh.obj M ⟶ c.pt,
          DerivedCategory.Qh.map t.hom ≫ ψ =
              DerivedCategory.Qh.map
                ((HomotopyCategory.quotient B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f) ≫ c.ι.app s ↔
            φ ψ ≫ DerivedCategory.Qh.map s.hom =
              d.π.app t ≫ DerivedCategory.Qh.map
                ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map g)
declarations.comment:
the canonical isomorphism and its characterisation by fractions; functoriality is
`derivedCategoryHomEquiv_comp_rightDerivedMap` and `derivedCategoryHomEquiv_map_comp`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.derivedCategoryHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVC**: the canonical bijection `Hom_{D(ℬ)}(M, RF(K)) ≃ Hom_{D(𝒜)}(LG(M), K)` for
`F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` right adjoint to `G : ℬ ⥤ 𝒜`, a complex `K` of `𝒜` at which `RF` is defined, with
value `RF(K) = c.pt`, and a complex `M` of `ℬ` at which `LG` is defined, with value
`LG(M) = d.pt`. It is the unique bijection compatible with the fractions computing the two sides
(`derivedCategoryHomEquiv_spec`, `derivedCategoryHomEquiv_unique`), and it is natural in `K`
(`derivedCategoryHomEquiv_comp_rightDerivedMap`) and in `M`
(`derivedCategoryHomEquiv_map_comp`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedCategoryHomEquiv
    (hc : (F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).IsRightDerivedValueAt
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) K c)
    (hd : (G.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).IsLeftDerivedValueAt
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) M d) :
    (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj M ⟶ c.pt) ≃ (d.pt ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh.obj K)
declarations.comment:
the canonical isomorphism; its functoriality in both variables is
`derivedCategoryHomEquiv_comp_rightDerivedMap` and `derivedCategoryHomEquiv_map_comp`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.derivedCategoryHomEquiv_comp_rightDerivedMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVC**, functoriality in `K`. Let `κ : K ⟶ K'` be a morphism of complexes of `𝒜`
(in the homotopy category) such that `RF` is defined at `K` and at `K'`, and let
`RF(κ) : RF(K) ⟶ RF(K')` be the induced morphism between the values (Stacks 05SA). Then for every
`ψ : M ⟶ RF(K)` in `D(ℬ)`, `φ_{K',M}(ψ ≫ RF(κ)) = φ_{K,M}(ψ) ≫ κ` in `D(𝒜)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryHomEquiv_comp_rightDerivedMap
    (hc : (F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).IsRightDerivedValueAt
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) K c)
    (hc' : (F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).IsRightDerivedValueAt
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) K' c')
    (hd : (G.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).IsLeftDerivedValueAt
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) M d)
    (κ : K ⟶ K') (ψ : DerivedCategory.Qh.obj M ⟶ c.pt) :
    adj.derivedCategoryHomEquiv hc' hd
        (ψ ≫ rightDerivedMap (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
          (F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh) hc hc' κ) =
      adj.derivedCategoryHomEquiv hc hd ψ ≫ DerivedCategory.Qh.map κ
declarations.comment: functoriality in `K`, with respect to morphisms of `K(𝒜)`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.derivedCategoryHomEquiv_map_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVC**, functoriality in `M`. Let `γ : M' ⟶ M` be a morphism of complexes of `ℬ`
(in the homotopy category) such that `LG` is defined at `M'` and at `M`, and let
`LG(γ) : LG(M') ⟶ LG(M)` be the induced morphism between the values (Stacks 05SA). Then for every
`ψ : M ⟶ RF(K)` in `D(ℬ)`, `φ_{K,M'}(γ ≫ ψ) = LG(γ) ≫ φ_{K,M}(ψ)` in `D(𝒜)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryHomEquiv_map_comp
    (hc : (F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).IsRightDerivedValueAt
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) K c)
    (hd : (G.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).IsLeftDerivedValueAt
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) M d)
    (hd' : (G.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).IsLeftDerivedValueAt
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) M' d')
    (γ : M' ⟶ M) (ψ : DerivedCategory.Qh.obj M ⟶ c.pt) :
    adj.derivedCategoryHomEquiv hc hd' (DerivedCategory.Qh.map γ ≫ ψ) =
      leftDerivedMap (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso B (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
          (G.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh) hd' hd γ ≫
        adj.derivedCategoryHomEquiv hc hd ψ
declarations.comment: functoriality in `M`, with respect to morphisms of `K(ℬ)`

declarations.name: Stacks.ContinuousCohomology.continuousModuleCohomologyForgetIso
declarations.doc:
Continuous group cohomology of continuous discrete `R`-`G`-modules commutes, naturally in the
module, with forgetting the `R`-module structure.
declarations.statement:
def continuousModuleCohomologyForgetIso [IsTopologicalGroup G]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (Stacks.Injectives.ContinuousModule.{u, v, max u v w} R G)]

    cohomologyFunctor.{d, u, v, w} R G i ⋙
        forget₂ (ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w} ≅
      continuousModuleForget.{u, v, max u v w} R G ⋙
        continuousGroupCohomologyFunctor.{v, max u v w} G i

declarations.name: Stacks.ContinuousCohomology.extIsoCohomologyDualTensor
declarations.doc:
Let `G` be a topological group, `R` a commutative ring and `M`, `N` continuous discrete
`R`-`G`-modules. If `M` is finite projective as an `R`-module, then `Extⁱ(M, N)`, computed in the
category of continuous discrete `R`-`G`-modules, is the continuous group cohomology
`Hⁱ(G, Mᵛ ⊗_R N)` of the diagonal action on `Mᵛ ⊗_R N`, `R`-linearly and in every degree.
declarations.statement:
def extIsoCohomologyDualTensor
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (Stacks.Injectives.ContinuousModule.{u, v, max u v w} R G)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (ModuleCat.{max u v w} R)]
    (N : Stacks.Injectives.ContinuousModule.{u, v, max u v w} R G) (i : ℕ) :
    Ext.{max u v w} M N i ≃ₗ[R]
      (cohomologyFunctor.{d, u, v, w} R G i).obj
        (dualTensorContinuousModule.{u, v, max u v w} R G M N)
declarations.comment: R-linear, in every degree; the `Ext`-universe smallness (hasExt_continuousModule) and themodel of the derived category are free instance arguments

declarations.name: Stacks.ContinuousCohomology.finite_cohomologyFunctor_one
declarations.doc:
Let `G` be a topological group, `k` a field and `V` a `k`-`G`-module, that is a `k`-module with
a continuous action of `G` for the discrete topology on `V`. If `G` is topologically finitely
generated, so that some finite subset generates a dense subgroup, and `V` is finite dimensional
over `k`, then the first continuous cohomology group `H¹(G, V)` is finite dimensional over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_cohomologyFunctor_one
    (hG : ∃ S : Finset G, Dense ((Subgroup.closure (S : Set G) : Subgroup G) : Set G))
    (V : Stacks.Injectives.ContinuousModule.{u, v, max u v w} k G)
    [Module.Finite k V.obj.obj.V] :
    Module.Finite k ((cohomologyFunctor.{d, u, v, w} k G 1).obj V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPushout_elementaryDistinguishedSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVI.** An elementary distinguished square is a pushout square in the category
of algebraic spaces over the base scheme: the target is glued from the open subspace and the
étale morphism along their fibre product.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPushout_elementaryDistinguishedSquare
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {W V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS W) (U : Subfunctor W) (f : V ⟶ W)
    (h : IsElementaryDistinguishedSquare B S hS hW U f) :
    IsPushout
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd U.ι f) :
        AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS
            (ObjectProperty.homMk U.ι :
              (⟨U.toFunctor, h.isOpenSubspace.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ ⟨W, hW⟩)
            (ObjectProperty.homMk f :
              (⟨V, h.isAlgebraicSpace⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ ⟨W, hW⟩) ⟶
          ⟨V, h.isAlgebraicSpace⟩)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst U.ι f) :
        _ ⟶ (⟨U.toFunctor, h.isOpenSubspace.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
      (ObjectProperty.homMk f :
        (⟨V, h.isAlgebraicSpace⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ ⟨W, hW⟩)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk U.ι :
        (⟨U.toFunctor, h.isOpenSubspace.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ ⟨W, hW⟩)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_pushout_isElementaryDistinguishedSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVJ.** Let `V` and `U` be algebraic spaces over `S`, let `V'` be an open
subspace of `V` and let `f' : V' ⟶ U` be a separated étale morphism. Then there is an algebraic
space `W` over `S` together with an open subspace of `W` isomorphic to `U` and a morphism
`V ⟶ W` forming an elementary distinguished square, and the resulting square is a pushout of
`V ← V' → U` in the category of algebraic spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pushout_isElementaryDistinguishedSquare
    (U V : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (V' : Subfunctor V.obj)
    (hV' : IsOpenSubspace B S hS V') (f' : V'.toFunctor ⟶ U.obj)
    (hf' : IsEtale B S hS f') (hf'sep : IsSeparated B S hS f') :
    ∃ (W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (Uw : Subfunctor W.obj) (e : U.obj ≅ Uw.toFunctor)
      (f : V ⟶ W),
      IsElementaryDistinguishedSquare B S hS W.property Uw f.hom ∧
        IsPushout
          (ObjectProperty.homMk V'.ι :
            (⟨V'.toFunctor, hV'.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ V)
          (ObjectProperty.homMk f' :
            (⟨V'.toFunctor, hV'.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ U)
          f (ObjectProperty.homMk (e.hom ≫ Uw.ι) : U ⟶ W)

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveModule.Family.satisfiesRS_projection
declarations.doc:
Finite projective modules over Artinian local algebras satisfy the Rim–Schlessinger
condition: a cospan whose second base morphism is surjective is covered by the Milnor patch of
the two modules over the fibre product of the base algebras.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Family.satisfiesRS_projection
    (𝓕 : FiniteProjectiveModule.Family.{u, w, t} (Λ := Λ) (k := k)) :
    letI := 𝓕.category
    SatisfiesRS 𝓕.projection
declarations.comment: Rim-Schlessinger condition

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveModule.isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory
declarations.doc: Deformations of a finite-dimensional vector space form a deformation category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory
    (V : Type t) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V] :
    let 𝓕 : FiniteProjectiveModule.Family.{u, w, t} (Λ := Λ) (k := k) :=
      FiniteProjectiveModule.family (Λ := Λ) (k := k)
    letI := 𝓕.category
    IsDeformationCategory
      (objectsOverFunctor 𝓕.projection
        (FiniteProjectiveModule.specialFiber (Λ := Λ) (k := k) V))
declarations.comment: deformation category

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveModule.subsingleton_tangentSpace
declarations.doc:
The tangent space of the deformation category of a finite-dimensional vector space has at
most one element: it is the zero vector space.
declarations.statement:
public theorem subsingleton_tangentSpace
    (V : Type t) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V] :
    let 𝓖 := FiniteProjectiveModule.family.{u, w, t} (Λ := Λ) (k := k)
    letI := 𝓖.category
    let p := objectsOverFunctor 𝓖.projection (specialFiber (Λ := Λ) (k := k) V)
    let 𝓕 := BasedCategory.ofFunctor p
    let hD := isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory (Λ := Λ) V
    let hS2 := Artin.schlessingerConditionS2_isomorphismClasses_of_isDeformationCategory 𝓕 hD
    letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory 𝓕.p) := ⟨hD.predeformation⟩
    letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2
      (Functor.Elements.π (isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered))) := ⟨hS2⟩
    let T := artinianTangentSpace Λ k (isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered)
    letI : AddCommGroup T := associatedTangentSpaceAddCommGroupUnlifted 𝓕
    letI : Module k T := associatedTangentSpaceModuleUnlifted 𝓕
    Subsingleton T
declarations.comment: tangent_space_zero

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveModule.finiteDimensional_tangentSpace

The tangent space of the deformation category of a finite-dimensional vector space is

public theorem finiteDimensional_tangentSpace
    (V : Type t) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V] :

    letI := 𝓖.category

    let 𝓕 := BasedCategory.ofFunctor p

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveModule.infinitesimalAutomorphismsEquivEnd
declarations.doc:
Infinitesimal automorphisms of a finite-dimensional vector space are its
linear endomorphisms, with composition corresponding to addition.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def infinitesimalAutomorphismsEquivEnd
    {Λ : Type u} {k : Type w} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k]
    (V : Type t) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V] :
    let 𝓖 := FiniteProjectiveModule.family.{u, w, t} (Λ := Λ) (k := k)
    letI := 𝓖.category
    let p := objectsOverFunctor 𝓖.projection
      (specialFiber (Λ := Λ) (k := k) V)
    let hD := isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory (Λ := Λ) (k := k) V
    let hp : IsPredeformationCategory p := hD.predeformation
    ∀ {Aε : ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, w, w} Λ k}
      {x₀ : p.Fiber (residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k)}
      {xε : p.Fiber Aε}
      (g : residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k ⟶ Aε)
      (e : Aε ⟶ residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k)
      (hpair : IsCanonicalDualNumberPair g e)
      (i : x₀.1 ⟶ xε.1) (hi : p.IsHomLift g i),
      let iε : Aε ≃ₐ[Λ] DualNumber k :=
        Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec hpair)
      let M := xε.1.left
      let hbase : M.base = Aε := (𝓖.projection_obj xε.1.left).symm.trans xε.2
      let ε : M.base := (eqToHom hbase.symm).hom (iε.symm DualNumber.eps)
      let r := 𝓖.homEquiv M
        (specialFiber (Λ := Λ) (k := k) V) xε.1.hom
      { E : infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi ≃*
          Multiplicative (Module.End k V) //
        ∀ (γ : infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi) (m : M.carrier),
          let a := 𝓖.homEquiv M M γ.val.asIso.hom.val.left
          ∃ n : M.carrier,
            r.linear n = (Multiplicative.toAdd (E γ)) (r.linear m) ∧
              a.linear m = m + ε • n }
declarations.comment: infinitesimal_automorphisms

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveModule.exists_infinitesimalAutomorphismsLinearEquivEnd
declarations.doc:
The infinitesimal automorphism group of the deformations of `V` is the `k`-vector space
`Module.End k V`, and is in particular finite-dimensional. The `k`-structure is the one of
Stacks 06JV: its addition is composition of automorphisms, and multiplying by `c` scales the
infinitesimal coordinate, which on the formula `γ(m) = m + ε·n` reads
`(c · γ)(m) = m + ε·(cb · n)` for any element `cb` of the base reducing to `c`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_infinitesimalAutomorphismsLinearEquivEnd
    {Λ : Type u} {k : Type w} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k]
    (V : Type t) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V] :
    let 𝓖 := FiniteProjectiveModule.family.{u, w, t} (Λ := Λ) (k := k)
    letI := 𝓖.category
    let p := objectsOverFunctor 𝓖.projection
      (specialFiber (Λ := Λ) (k := k) V)
    let hD := isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory (Λ := Λ) (k := k) V
    let hp : IsPredeformationCategory p := hD.predeformation
    ∀ {Aε : ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, w, w} Λ k}
      {x₀ : p.Fiber (residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k)}
      {xε : p.Fiber Aε}
      (g : residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k ⟶ Aε)
      (e : Aε ⟶ residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k)
      (hpair : IsCanonicalDualNumberPair g e)
      (i : x₀.1 ⟶ xε.1) (hi : p.IsHomLift g i),
      let iε : Aε ≃ₐ[Λ] DualNumber k :=
        Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec hpair)
      let M := xε.1.left
      let hbase : M.base = Aε := (𝓖.projection_obj xε.1.left).symm.trans xε.2
      let ε : M.base := (eqToHom hbase.symm).hom (iε.symm DualNumber.eps)
      let r := 𝓖.homEquiv M
        (specialFiber (Λ := Λ) (k := k) V) xε.1.hom
      ∃ A : AddCommGroup (infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi),
        letI := A
        ∃ Mo : Module k (infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi),
          letI := Mo
          (∀ γ δ : infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi, γ + δ = γ * δ) ∧
          (∃ E : infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi ≃ₗ[k] Module.End k V,
            (∀ (γ : infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi) (m : M.carrier),
              ∃ n : M.carrier, r.linear n = E γ (r.linear m) ∧
                (𝓖.homEquiv M M γ.val.asIso.hom.val.left).linear m = m + ε • n) ∧
            ∀ (c : k) (cb : M.base), r.base.hom cb = c →
              ∀ (γ : infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi)
                (m n : M.carrier), r.linear n = E γ (r.linear m) →
                (𝓖.homEquiv M M γ.val.asIso.hom.val.left).linear m = m + ε • n →
                (𝓖.homEquiv M M (c • γ).val.asIso.hom.val.left).linear m =
                  m + ε • (cb • n)) ∧
          FiniteDimensional k (infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi)
declarations.comment: infinitesimal_automorphisms

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveRepresentation.satisfiesRS_projection
declarations.doc: Finite projective representations satisfy the Rim–Schlessinger condition.
declarations.comment: Rim-Schlessinger condition

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveRepresentation.isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory
declarations.doc: The deformations of a finite-dimensional representation form a deformation category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory
    {Λ : Type u} {k : Type w} {Γ : Type*}
    [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k] [Group Γ]
    (V : Type m) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V]
    (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V) :
    IsDeformationCategory
      (objectsOverFunctor
        (FiniteProjectiveRepresentation.projection.{u, w, w, m}
          (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Γ := Γ))
        (FiniteProjectiveRepresentation.specialFiber (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀))
declarations.comment: deformation category

declarations.name: Deformation.finiteDimensional_tangentSpace_representation
declarations.doc:
The tangent space of the deformation category of a finite-dimensional representation of a
finitely generated group is finite dimensional over `k`, for the canonical vector space structure
of Stacks 06IH.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_tangentSpace_representation (V : Type m) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    [Module.Finite k V] [Group.FG Γ] (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V) :
    let 𝓕 := BasedCategory.ofFunctor (deformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀)
    let ee := tangentSpaceEquivSelfExt (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀
    letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory 𝓕.p) := ⟨ee.1⟩
    letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2
      (Functor.Elements.π (isomorphismClasses 𝓕 ee.1.cofibered))) := ⟨ee.2.1⟩
    FiniteDimensional k (artinianTangentSpace Λ k (isomorphismClasses 𝓕 ee.1.cofibered))
declarations.comment: clause 5: `T Def_{V,ρ₀}` is finite dimensional over `k` when `Γ` is finitely generated, for the canonical vector space structure of Stacks 06IH. The hypothesis `Group.FG Γ` is what separates this from clause 4, which holds for every `Γ`

declarations.name: Deformation.infinitesimalAutomorphismsEquivH0
declarations.doc:
The infinitesimal automorphisms of the deformation category of a finite-dimensional
representation `ρ₀` are the degree-zero group cohomology of the conjugation action on its
endomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def infinitesimalAutomorphismsEquivH0
    (V : Type w) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V]
    (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V)
    {A₀ Aε : ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, w, w} Λ k}
    {x₀ : (deformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀).Fiber A₀}
    {xε : (deformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀).Fiber Aε}
    (g : A₀ ⟶ Aε) (e : Aε ⟶ A₀) (hpair : IsCanonicalDualNumberPair g e)
    (i : x₀.1 ⟶ xε.1)
    (hi : (deformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀).IsHomLift g i) :
    ↥(infinitesimalAutomorphisms
        (deformationCategoryProjection_isCofiberedInGroupoids (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀)
        g e hpair i hi) ≃*
      Multiplicative (groupCohomology (Rep.of (Representation.linHom ρ₀ ρ₀)) 0)
declarations.comment: clause 3: `Inf Def_{V,ρ₀} = H⁰(Γ, End_k(V))`, the infinitesimal automorphisms of the deformation category of a finite-dimensional representation `ρ₀` are the `Γ`-invariant `k`-endomorphisms of `V`, i.e. the `ψ` with `id + εψ` an automorphism of `V ⊗_k k[ε]`

declarations.name: Deformation.exists_infinitesimalAutomorphismsLinearEquivH0
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVT**, the finiteness clause for infinitesimal automorphisms, stated of
`Inf Def_{V,ρ₀}` itself: the group of infinitesimal automorphisms of the deformation category
of a finite-dimensional representation carries a `k`-vector space structure whose addition is
composition of automorphisms, for which the identification of clause 3 with `H⁰(Γ, End_k(V))`
is `k`-linear, and it is *always* finite dimensional over `k` — no hypothesis whatsoever on
the group `Γ`.

`Inf Def_{V,ρ₀}` is presented as a subgroup of the automorphism group of a dual-number
pushforward (`Deformation.infinitesimalAutomorphisms`), so it carries no `k`-module structure
to begin with and `FiniteDimensional k` does not even typecheck on it. The structure is
therefore produced here, exactly as in `Stacks 0DVQ`'s version of the same statement for
finite projective modules
(`Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveModule.exists_infinitesimalAutomorphismsLinearEquivEnd`),
and it is pinned: addition is composition, which fixes the additive group, and the `k`-linear
equivalence is required to be the group isomorphism
`Deformation.infinitesimalAutomorphismsEquivH0` of clause 3, which fixes the scalar action.
Compare Stacks 06JV (1), which puts the same structure on the tangent space at the identity of
the automorphism functor of a category cofibered in groupoids satisfying (RS).

Finite dimensionality is then `Deformation.finiteDimensional_groupCohomology_zero_linHom`
transported along that equivalence. This is in contrast with the tangent space, whose
finiteness needs `Γ` to be finitely generated
(`Deformation.finiteDimensional_tangentSpace_representation`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_infinitesimalAutomorphismsLinearEquivH0
    (V : Type w) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V]
    (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V)
    {A₀ Aε : ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, w, w} Λ k}
    {x₀ : (deformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀).Fiber A₀}
    {xε : (deformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀).Fiber Aε}
    (g : A₀ ⟶ Aε) (e : Aε ⟶ A₀) (hpair : IsCanonicalDualNumberPair g e)
    (i : x₀.1 ⟶ xε.1)
    (hi : (deformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀).IsHomLift g i) :
    ∃ A : AddCommGroup ↥(infinitesimalAutomorphisms
        (deformationCategoryProjection_isCofiberedInGroupoids (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀)
        g e hpair i hi),
      letI := A
      ∃ _ : Module k ↥(infinitesimalAutomorphisms
          (deformationCategoryProjection_isCofiberedInGroupoids (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀)
          g e hpair i hi),
        (∀ a b : ↥(infinitesimalAutomorphisms
            (deformationCategoryProjection_isCofiberedInGroupoids (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀)
            g e hpair i hi), a + b = a * b) ∧
        (∃ L : ↥(infinitesimalAutomorphisms
              (deformationCategoryProjection_isCofiberedInGroupoids (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀)
              g e hpair i hi) ≃ₗ[k]
            groupCohomology (Rep.of (Representation.linHom ρ₀ ρ₀)) 0,
          ∀ a, Multiplicative.ofAdd (L a) =
            infinitesimalAutomorphismsEquivH0 (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ g e hpair i hi a) ∧
        FiniteDimensional k ↥(infinitesimalAutomorphisms
          (deformationCategoryProjection_isCofiberedInGroupoids (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀)
          g e hpair i hi)
declarations.comment: clause 4: `Inf Def_{V,ρ₀}` is ALWAYS finite dimensional over `k`, with no hypothesis whatsoever on `Γ`. Stated of `Inf Def_{V,ρ₀}` itself, which is a subgroup of an automorphism group and so is given here the `k`-vector space structure the claim needs: addition is composition of automorphisms and the clause-3 identification with `H⁰(Γ, End_k(V))` is `k`-linear. Contrast clause 5, where `Γ` must be finitely generated

declarations.name: Deformation.selfExtEquivGroupCohomologyOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVT.** The first self-extension group over the group algebra of a
finite-dimensional representation `ρ₀` of `Γ` on `V` is the first group cohomology of the
conjugation action of `Γ` on `End_k(V)`:

`Ext¹_{k[Γ]}(V, V) = H¹(Γ, End_k(V))`.

The extension group is taken over the `k[Γ]`-module attached to `ρ₀`, which is the module over
which the tangent-space clause `Deformation.tangentSpaceEquivSelfExt` of the same tag is
stated. No hypothesis on `Γ` is needed.
declarations.statement:
def selfExtEquivGroupCohomologyOne (V : Type w) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    [Module.Finite k V] (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V) :
    Abelian.Ext
        ((Rep.equivalenceModuleMonoidAlgebra (k := k) (G := Γ)).functor.obj (Rep.of ρ₀))
        ((Rep.equivalenceModuleMonoidAlgebra (k := k) (G := Γ)).functor.obj (Rep.of ρ₀)) 1 ≃ₗ[k]
      (groupCohomology (Rep.of (Representation.linHom ρ₀ ρ₀)) 1 : Type w)
declarations.comment: clause 2: `Ext¹_{k[Γ]}(V, V) = H¹(Γ, End_k(V))` for the conjugation action of `Γ` on `End_k(V)`, over the `k[Γ]`-module attached to `ρ₀` by `Rep.equivalenceModuleMonoidAlgebra`, which is the module clause 1 states its `Ext¹` over. No hypothesis on `Γ`

declarations.name: Deformation.tangentSpaceEquivSelfExt
declarations.doc:
The canonical tangent space of a finite-dimensional representation deformation category
is linearly equivalent to its first self-Ext over the group algebra.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def tangentSpaceEquivSelfExt
    {Λ : Type u} {k : Type w} {Γ : Type*}
    [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k] [Group Γ]
    (V : Type m) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V]
    (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V) :
    let p := deformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀
    let 𝓕 := BasedCategory.ofFunctor p
    let M₀ := (Rep.equivalenceModuleMonoidAlgebra (k := k) (G := Γ)).functor.obj
      (Rep.of ρ₀)
    let E := Abelian.Ext M₀ M₀ 1
    Σ' (hpre : Deformation.IsPredeformationCategory 𝓕.p)
      (hS2 : Deformation.SchlessingerConditionS2
        (Functor.Elements.π
          (Deformation.isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hpre.cofibered))),
      letI : Fact (Deformation.IsPredeformationCategory 𝓕.p) := ⟨hpre⟩
      letI : Fact (Deformation.SchlessingerConditionS2
        (Functor.Elements.π
          (Deformation.isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hpre.cofibered))) := ⟨hS2⟩
      letI : AddCommGroup
        (Deformation.artinianTangentSpace Λ k
          (Deformation.isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hpre.cofibered)) :=
        Deformation.associatedTangentSpaceAddCommGroupUnlifted 𝓕
      letI : Module k
        (Deformation.artinianTangentSpace Λ k
          (Deformation.isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hpre.cofibered)) :=
        Deformation.associatedTangentSpaceModuleUnlifted 𝓕
      { L : Deformation.artinianTangentSpace Λ k
          (Deformation.isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hpre.cofibered) ≃ₗ[k] E //
        (∀ x : p.Fiber (Deformation.augmentedDualNumbers (Λ := Λ) (k := k)),
          ∃ (M : ModuleCat (MonoidAlgebra k Γ)) (f : M₀ ⟶ M) (g : M ⟶ M₀)
            (hfg : f ≫ g = 0),
            (ShortComplex.mk f g hfg).ShortExact ∧
              IsAssociatedSelfExtension V ρ₀ x M f g) ∧
        (∀ (x : p.Fiber (Deformation.augmentedDualNumbers (Λ := Λ) (k := k)))
          (M : ModuleCat (MonoidAlgebra k Γ)) (f : M₀ ⟶ M) (g : M ⟶ M₀)
          (hfg : f ≫ g = 0) (hexact : (ShortComplex.mk f g hfg).ShortExact),
          IsAssociatedSelfExtension V ρ₀ x M f g →
            L (Deformation.classOf 𝓕 hpre.cofibered x) = hexact.extClass) }
declarations.comment: clause 1: `T Def_{V,ρ₀} = Ext¹_{k[Γ]}(V, V)`, the tangent space of the deformation category of a finite-dimensional representation `ρ₀` is its first self-extension group over the group algebra. The identification of that `Ext¹` with `H¹(Γ, End_k(V))` is clause 2, `Deformation.selfExtEquivGroupCohomologyOne`

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveRepresentation.satisfiesRS_continuousProjection
declarations.doc:
Continuous finite projective representations of a topological group satisfy the
Rim–Schlessinger condition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem satisfiesRS_continuousProjection {Λ : Type u} {k : Type w} {Γ : Type*}
    [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k] [Group Γ] [TopologicalSpace Γ] :
    SatisfiesRS
      (continuousProjection.{u, v, w, max v m} (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Γ := Γ))
declarations.comment: Rim-Schlessinger condition

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveRepresentation.isDeformationCategory_continuousDeformationCategory
declarations.doc:
The deformations of a finite-dimensional continuous representation of a topological group
form a deformation category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDeformationCategory_continuousDeformationCategory {Λ : Type u} {k : Type w}
    {Γ : Type*} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k] [Group Γ] [TopologicalSpace Γ]
    (V : Type m) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V]
    (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V) (hρ₀ : IsContinuousRepresentation ρ₀) :
    IsDeformationCategory
      (objectsOverFunctor
        (continuousProjection.{u, w, w, m} (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Γ := Γ))
        (continuousSpecialFiber (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀))
declarations.comment: deformation category

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveRepresentation.finiteDimensional_continuousTangentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVW**, the tangent clause: for a topologically finitely generated topological
group `Γ` the tangent space of the deformation category of a finite-dimensional continuous
representation `ρ₀` is finite dimensional over `k`.

Topological finite generation enters through a dense finitely generated subgroup `H ≤ Γ`.
A continuous deformation is locally constant, so an `H`-equivariant map between two of them is
`Γ`-equivariant: the agreement locus is closed and contains `H`. Hence restriction of the
action to `H` is fully faithful, so its differential is an injective `k`-linear map from the
tangent space into the tangent space of the deformation category of `ρ₀|_H`, and the latter is
finite dimensional by Stacks 0DVT.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteDimensional_continuousTangentSpace
    (V : Type m) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V]
    (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V) (hρ₀ : IsContinuousRepresentation ρ₀)
    (hΓ : ∃ H : Subgroup Γ, Group.FG ↥H ∧ Dense (H : Set Γ)) :
    let 𝓕 := BasedCategory.ofFunctor (Deformation.objectsOverFunctor
      (continuousProjection.{u, w, w, m} (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Γ := Γ))
      (continuousSpecialFiber (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀))
    let hD := isDeformationCategory_continuousDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀
    letI : Fact (Deformation.IsPredeformationCategory 𝓕.p) := ⟨hD.predeformation⟩
    letI : Fact (Deformation.SchlessingerConditionS2 (Functor.Elements.π
        (Deformation.isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered))) :=
      ⟨Deformation.Artin.schlessingerConditionS2_isomorphismClasses_of_isDeformationCategory
        𝓕 hD⟩
    FiniteDimensional k (Deformation.artinianTangentSpace Λ k
      (Deformation.isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered))
declarations.comment: the tangent space is finite dimensional

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveRepresentation.localizedAutomorphismTangentLinearEquivH0
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVW**, the clause `Inf(Def_{V,ρ₀}) = H⁰(Γ, End_k(V))`, as `k`-vector spaces. For a
finite-dimensional continuous representation `ρ₀` of a topological group, the infinitesimal
automorphisms of the deformation category of Stacks 0D3K at a point `x`, in their natural
`k`-vector space structure of Stacks 06JX — the tangent space `T_{id_x} Aut(x)` of the
automorphism functor at the identity, whose addition is composition of automorphisms and whose
scalar multiplication is transport along `ε ↦ cε` — are `k`-linearly isomorphic to the
degree-zero cohomology `H⁰(Γ, End_k(V))` of the conjugation action.

The proof is that of Stacks 0DVT: an infinitesimal automorphism is an automorphism `id + εφ` of
the module of the pushforward of `x` to the dual numbers, for a unique `Γ`-equivariant `φ`, and
composing automorphisms adds the `φ`'s (`continuousAutEquivInvariants`). The pushforward along
`ε ↦ cε` is semilinear along a base map sending `ε` to an element of residue `c` times `ε`, so
transport along it turns `id + εφ` into `id + ε(cφ)`.
declarations.statement:
def localizedAutomorphismTangentLinearEquivH0 :
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup P
      (isDeformationCategory_continuousDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀).satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule P
      (isDeformationCategory_continuousDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀).satisfiesRS
    localizedAutomorphismFunctorTangent P ≃ₗ[k]
      groupCohomology (Rep.of (Representation.linHom ρ₀ ρ₀)) 0
declarations.comment: `Inf(Def_{V,ρ₀}) = H⁰(Γ, End_k(V))` as `k`-vector spaces, for the natural `k`-vector space structure of Stacks 06JX on `Inf`

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveRepresentation.finiteDimensional_continuousLocalizedAutomorphismTangent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVW**, the clause that `Inf(Def_{V,ρ₀})` is *always* finite dimensional, for its
natural `k`-vector space structure of Stacks 06JX: no hypothesis on `Γ` is needed, because
`Inf(Def_{V,ρ₀})` is `H⁰(Γ, End_k(V))` (`localizedAutomorphismTangentLinearEquivH0`), the
subspace of `Γ`-invariants of the finite-dimensional space `End_k(V)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_continuousLocalizedAutomorphismTangent :
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup P
      (isDeformationCategory_continuousDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀).satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule P
      (isDeformationCategory_continuousDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀).satisfiesRS
    FiniteDimensional k (localizedAutomorphismFunctorTangent P)
declarations.comment: `Inf(Def_{V,ρ₀})` is always finite dimensional, for the natural `k`-vector space structure of Stacks 06JX

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveRepresentation.continuousRepresentation_tangentSpace_and_infinitesimalAutomorphisms
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVW.** Let `ρ₀ : Γ → GL_k(V)` be a finite-dimensional continuous representation of
a topological group, and `Def_{V,ρ₀}` the deformation category of Stacks 0D3K. Then

* `T Def_{V,ρ₀} = H¹(Γ, End_k(V))`: the tangent space, in its natural `k`-vector space structure
  of Stacks 06IH, is `k`-linearly isomorphic to the first continuous cohomology of the dual
  tensor module `Vᵛ ⊗_k V`, whose representation is the conjugation action on `End_k(V)`;
* `Inf(Def_{V,ρ₀}) = H⁰(Γ, End_k(V))`: the infinitesimal automorphisms at any point `x`, in
  their natural `k`-vector space structure of Stacks 06JX (addition is composition, `c` acts by
  transport along `ε ↦ cε`), are `k`-linearly isomorphic to the degree-zero cohomology of the
  conjugation action;
* `Inf(Def_{V,ρ₀})` is always finite dimensional, for that structure;
* `T Def_{V,ρ₀}` is finite dimensional if `Γ` is topologically finitely generated, that is, has
  a dense finitely generated subgroup.

The four clauses are `tangentSpaceEquivContinuousCohomology`,
`localizedAutomorphismTangentLinearEquivH0`,
`finiteDimensional_continuousLocalizedAutomorphismTangent` and
`finiteDimensional_continuousTangentSpace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem continuousRepresentation_tangentSpace_and_infinitesimalAutomorphisms
    [IsTopologicalGroup Γ]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (Stacks.Injectives.ContinuousModule.{w, w, w} k Γ)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (ModuleCat.{w} k)]
    (V : Type w) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V]
    (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V) (hρ₀ : IsContinuousRepresentation ρ₀)
    {x : continuousDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀}
    (P : ChosenPushforwardsAt (continuousDeformationProjection (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀) x) :
    let 𝓕 := BasedCategory.ofFunctor (continuousDeformationProjection (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀)
    let hD := isDeformationCategory_continuousDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀
    letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory 𝓕.p) := ⟨hD.predeformation⟩
    letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2
        (Functor.Elements.π
          (isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered))) :=
      ⟨Deformation.Artin.schlessingerConditionS2_isomorphismClasses_of_isDeformationCategory
        𝓕 hD⟩
    letI := Stacks.ContinuousCohomology.hasExt_continuousModule.{w, w, w} k Γ
    let M := continuousModuleOfContinuousRepresentation V ρ₀ hρ₀
    letI : Module.Finite k (M.obj.obj.V : Type w) := inferInstanceAs (Module.Finite k V)
    letI : Module.Projective k (M.obj.obj.V : Type w) :=
      inferInstanceAs (Module.Projective k V)
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup P hD.satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule P hD.satisfiesRS
    Nonempty (Σ' _ : artinianTangentSpace Λ k
          (isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered) ≃ₗ[k]
        (Stacks.ContinuousCohomology.cohomologyFunctor.{d, w, w, w} k Γ 1).obj
          (Stacks.ContinuousCohomology.dualTensorContinuousModule k Γ M M),
      (Stacks.ContinuousCohomology.rep k Γ
        (Stacks.ContinuousCohomology.dualTensorContinuousModule k Γ M M)).Equiv
          (Representation.linHom ρ₀ ρ₀)) ∧
      Nonempty (localizedAutomorphismFunctorTangent P ≃ₗ[k]
        groupCohomology (Rep.of (Representation.linHom ρ₀ ρ₀)) 0) ∧
      FiniteDimensional k (localizedAutomorphismFunctorTangent P) ∧
      ((∃ H : Subgroup Γ, Group.FG ↥H ∧ Dense (H : Set Γ)) →
        FiniteDimensional k (artinianTangentSpace Λ k
          (isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered)))
declarations.comment: all four clauses: `T Def = H¹(Γ, End_k(V))`, `Inf(Def) = H⁰(Γ, End_k(V))` for the natural `k`-vector space structure of Stacks 06JX on `Inf`, `Inf(Def)` always finite dimensional, `T Def` finite dimensional for topologically finitely generated `Γ`

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveRepresentation.tangentSpaceEquivContinuousCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVW, the tangent clause.** For a finite-dimensional continuous representation
`ρ₀ : Γ → GL_k(V)` of a topological group, the tangent space of the deformation category of
Stacks 0D3K — in its natural `k`-vector space structure of Stacks 06IH — is the first
continuous cohomology `H¹(Γ, End_k(V))` of the conjugation action on the endomorphisms of `V`.

The coefficient module is the dual tensor module `Vᵛ ⊗_k V` of Stacks 0DVE, and the second
component of the statement identifies its representation equivariantly with
`Representation.linHom ρ₀ ρ₀`, the conjugation action on `End_k(V)`, so the cohomology on the
right is `H¹(Γ, End_k(V))`.

The proof is the one of Stacks 0DVT: `tangentSpaceEquivContinuousSelfExt` identifies the
tangent space with `Ext¹` of `V` by itself in continuous discrete modules, and Stacks 0DVE turns
that `Ext¹` into continuous cohomology of `Vᵛ ⊗_k V`.
declarations.statement:
def tangentSpaceEquivContinuousCohomology [IsTopologicalGroup Γ]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (Stacks.Injectives.ContinuousModule.{w, w, w} k Γ)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (ModuleCat.{w} k)]
    (V : Type w) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V]
    (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V) (hρ₀ : IsContinuousRepresentation ρ₀) :
    let 𝓕 := BasedCategory.ofFunctor (continuousDeformationProjection (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀)
    let hD := isDeformationCategory_continuousDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀
    letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory 𝓕.p) := ⟨hD.predeformation⟩
    letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2
        (Functor.Elements.π
          (isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered))) :=
      ⟨Deformation.Artin.schlessingerConditionS2_isomorphismClasses_of_isDeformationCategory
        𝓕 hD⟩
    letI := Stacks.ContinuousCohomology.hasExt_continuousModule.{w, w, w} k Γ
    let M := continuousModuleOfContinuousRepresentation V ρ₀ hρ₀
    letI : Module.Finite k (M.obj.obj.V : Type w) := inferInstanceAs (Module.Finite k V)
    letI : Module.Projective k (M.obj.obj.V : Type w) :=
      inferInstanceAs (Module.Projective k V)
    Σ' _ : artinianTangentSpace Λ k
          (isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered) ≃ₗ[k]
        (Stacks.ContinuousCohomology.cohomologyFunctor.{d, w, w, w} k Γ 1).obj
          (Stacks.ContinuousCohomology.dualTensorContinuousModule k Γ M M),
      (Stacks.ContinuousCohomology.rep k Γ
        (Stacks.ContinuousCohomology.dualTensorContinuousModule k Γ M M)).Equiv
          (Representation.linHom ρ₀ ρ₀)
declarations.comment: tangent_space

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.satisfiesRS_projection

The category of graded algebras finite projective in each degree satisfies the
Rim–Schlessinger condition.

    SatisfiesRS

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory
declarations.doc:
The deformations of a fixed graded `k`-algebra, finite-dimensional in each degree, form a
deformation category.

public theorem isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory
    {Λ : Type u} {k : Type w} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k]
    (P : Type (max w m)) [CommRing P] [Algebra k P]
    (grading : ℕ → Submodule k P) [GradedAlgebra grading]
    [∀ d, Module.Finite k (grading d)] :
    IsDeformationCategory

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.infinitesimalAutomorphismGroupEquivDegreeZeroDerivations
declarations.doc:
The infinitesimal automorphism group of the deformation category of a graded algebra is the
additive group of degree-preserving derivations.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def infinitesimalAutomorphismGroupEquivDegreeZeroDerivations
    {Λ : Type u} {k : Type w} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k]
    (P : Type (max w m)) [CommRing P] [Algebra k P]
    (grading : ℕ → Submodule k P) [GradedAlgebra grading]
    [∀ d, Module.Finite k (grading d)]
    {Aε : ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, w, w} Λ k}
    {x₀ : (objectsOverFunctor
      (ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.projection.{u, w, w, max w m} (Λ := Λ) (k := k))
      (specialFiber (Λ := Λ) P grading)).Fiber
        (residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k)}
    {xε : (objectsOverFunctor
      (ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.projection.{u, w, w, max w m} (Λ := Λ) (k := k))
      (specialFiber (Λ := Λ) P grading)).Fiber Aε}
    (g : residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k ⟶ Aε)
    (e : Aε ⟶ residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k)
    (hpair : IsCanonicalDualNumberPair g e)
    (i : x₀.1 ⟶ xε.1)
    (hi : (objectsOverFunctor
      (ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.projection.{u, w, w, max w m} (Λ := Λ) (k := k))
      (specialFiber (Λ := Λ) P grading)).IsHomLift g i) :
    infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup
      (isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory P grading).predeformation
      g e hpair i hi ≃*
      Multiplicative (degreeZeroDerivations grading)
declarations.comment: graded_inf_derivations

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.exists_module_finiteDimensional_infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DVZ, the infinitesimal automorphisms.** Let `P` be a graded algebra of finite type
over the field `k`, finite-dimensional in each degree. Then `Inf(Def_P)` is a finite-dimensional
`k`-vector space: at every lift `i : x₀ ⟶ xε` of the special fibre along a canonical dual-number
pair `k → Aε → k`, the infinitesimal automorphism group carries a `k`-vector-space structure

* whose addition is composition of infinitesimal automorphisms, and
* in which a scalar `c` acts by pushforward along `ε ↦ cε`: for every endomorphism `s` of `Aε`
  which is `ε ↦ cε` in a dual-number coordinate of `Aε` compatible with its residue field, and
  every arrow `j : xε ⟶ xε` over `s` fixing `i`, `c • a` is the pushforward of `a` along `j`,

which is the natural structure of Stacks 06JV / 06JX, and this vector space is finite
dimensional.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_module_finiteDimensional_infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup
    {Λ : Type u} {k : Type w} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k]
    (P : Type (max w m)) [CommRing P] [Algebra k P]
    (grading : ℕ → Submodule k P) [GradedAlgebra grading]
    [∀ d, Module.Finite k (grading d)] [Algebra.FiniteType k P]
    {Aε : ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, w, w} Λ k}
    {x₀ : (objectsOverFunctor
      (ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.projection.{u, w, w, max w m} (Λ := Λ) (k := k))
      (specialFiber (Λ := Λ) P grading)).Fiber (residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k)}
    {xε : (objectsOverFunctor
      (ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.projection.{u, w, w, max w m} (Λ := Λ) (k := k))
      (specialFiber (Λ := Λ) P grading)).Fiber Aε}
    (g : residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k ⟶ Aε)
    (e : Aε ⟶ residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k)
    (hpair : IsCanonicalDualNumberPair g e)
    (i : x₀.1 ⟶ xε.1)
    (hi : (objectsOverFunctor
      (ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.projection.{u, w, w, max w m} (Λ := Λ) (k := k))
      (specialFiber (Λ := Λ) P grading)).IsHomLift g i) :
    ∃ hA : AddCommGroup (infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup
        (isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory (Λ := Λ) P grading).predeformation
        g e hpair i hi),
      letI := hA
      ∃ hM : Module k (infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup
          (isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory (Λ := Λ) P grading).predeformation
          g e hpair i hi),
        letI := hM
        (∀ a b : infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup
          (isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory (Λ := Λ) P grading).predeformation
          g e hpair i hi, a + b = a * b) ∧
        (∀ (c : k) (s : Aε ⟶ Aε),
          (∃ φ : Aε ≃ₐ[Λ] DualNumber k,
            (∀ t : Aε, (φ t).1 = Aε.residueEquiv (IsLocalRing.residue Aε t)) ∧
            (∀ t : k, φ (s.hom (φ.symm (TrivSqZeroExt.inl t))) = TrivSqZeroExt.inl t) ∧
            φ (s.hom (φ.symm DualNumber.eps)) = c • DualNumber.eps) →
          ∀ (j : xε.1 ⟶ xε.1) (hj : (objectsOverFunctor
              (ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.projection.{u, w, w, max w m} (Λ := Λ) (k := k))
              (specialFiber (Λ := Λ) P grading)).IsHomLift s j),
            i ≫ j = i →
            ∀ a : infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup
                (isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory (Λ := Λ) P grading).predeformation
                g e hpair i hi,
              ∃ b : infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup
                  (isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory (Λ := Λ) P grading).predeformation
                  g e hpair i hi,
                b.val = pushforwardAutomorphismHom
                  (isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory (Λ := Λ) P
                    grading).predeformation.cofibered s j hj a.val ∧ c • a = b) ∧
        FiniteDimensional k (infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup
          (isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory (Λ := Λ) P grading).predeformation
          g e hpair i hi)
declarations.comment: graded_inf_finite: for P of finite type over k, Inf(Def_P) with its natural vector space structure (addition is composition; c acts by pushforward along eps -> c eps) is finite dimensional over k, at every lift x0 -> x_eps along a canonical dual-number pair

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.finiteDimensional_tangentSpace
declarations.doc:
**The tangent-space half of Stacks 0DVZ.** The tangent space of the deformation category of
a graded `k`-algebra which is finite-dimensional in each degree and of finite type over `k` is
finite-dimensional.

The proof is Stacks' own: choose a weighted graded presentation of `P`
(`GradedAlgebra.exists_weightedGradedPresentation`), attach to a lift of `P` over `k[V]` the
class in `W ⊗[k] V` of the vector of obstructions of the lifted relations, where `W` is the
cokernel of the graded Jacobian of the presentation
(`Deformation.Examples.ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.tangentRecord`), and feed that map, its
naturality and its injectivity to
`Deformation.finiteDimensional_artinianTangentSpace_of_natural_injection` through
`finiteDimensional_tangentSpace_of_gradedJacobian_natural_injection`. `W` is
finite-dimensional because each graded piece of `P` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_tangentSpace :
    letI p := objectsOverFunctor
      (ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.projection.{u, w, w, max w m} (Λ := Λ) (k := k))
      (specialFiber (Λ := Λ) P grading)
    letI 𝓕 := BasedCategory.ofFunctor p
    letI hD := isDeformationCategory_deformationCategory (Λ := Λ) P grading
    letI hS2 := Artin.schlessingerConditionS2_isomorphismClasses_of_isDeformationCategory 𝓕 hD
    letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory 𝓕.p) := ⟨hD.predeformation⟩
    letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2
      (Functor.Elements.π (isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered))) := ⟨hS2⟩
    letI T := artinianTangentSpace Λ k (isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hD.predeformation.cofibered)
    letI : AddCommGroup T := associatedTangentSpaceAddCommGroupUnlifted 𝓕
    letI : Module k T := associatedTangentSpaceModuleUnlifted 𝓕
    FiniteDimensional k T
declarations.comment: graded_tangent_finite

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.hasEnoughPoints_of_coversTop_of_exists_finite_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DW0**. Let `(C, J)` be a site and let `U : I → C` be a family of objects, indexed by
a `w`-small type, which covers the final object of the topos of sheaves on `C`: for every object
`W` of `C`, the sieve of morphisms `Z ⟶ W` whose source `Z` admits a morphism to some `U i` is a
covering sieve. Assume that each localized site `C/U i` satisfies the hypotheses of Deligne's
criterion Stacks 00YQ: fibre products exist in `C/U i`, and every covering sieve `S` of an object
`X` of `C/U i` admits a refinement by a finite covering, i.e. contains a finite family
`g k : Y k ⟶ X` which is again a covering of `X`. Then `(C, J)` has enough points.

The finiteness condition is needed only on the localizations, so a site none of whose coverings
admits a finite refinement can still have enough points, as soon as it is covered by objects whose
localizations are coherent in Deligne's sense.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasEnoughPoints_of_coversTop_of_exists_finite_refinement {C : Type u}
    [Category.{v} C] [LocallySmall.{w} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {I : Type*} [Small.{w} I]
    {U : I → C} [∀ i, HasPullbacks (Over (U i))] [∀ i, Small.{w} (Over (U i))] (hU : J.CoversTop U)
    (h :
      ∀ (i : I) ⦃X : Over (U i)⦄ (S : Sieve X),
        S ∈ (J.over (U i)) X →
          ∃ (ι : Type) (_ : Finite ι) (Y : ι → Over (U i)) (g : ∀ k, Y k ⟶ X),
            Sieve.ofArrows Y g ≤ S ∧ Sieve.ofArrows Y g ∈ (J.over (U i)) X) :
    HasEnoughPoints.{w} J
declarations.comment:
A site covered by objects whose localizations satisfy Deligne's criterion has
  enough points.

declarations.name: StacksDraft.InjectiveDimension.hasFiniteInjectiveDimension_iff_quotient_ext_vanishing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DW2.** For a bounded below complex with finite cohomology over a Noetherian ring,
finite injective dimension can be tested by uniform high-degree Ext vanishing against the
quotients by all ideals containing an ideal in the Jacobson radical.
declarations.statement:
public lemma hasFiniteInjectiveDimension_iff_quotient_ext_vanishing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal R))
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite R
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj K))) :
    HasFiniteInjectiveDimension (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj K) ↔
      ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (J : Ideal R), I ≤ J → ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
        Subsingleton
          (DerivedCategory.Ext
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj
              (ModuleCat.of R (Shrink.{v} (R ⧸ J))))
            (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj K) i)

declarations.name: Dualizing.isCohenMacaulayRing_of_dualizingModule

A Gorenstein ring is Cohen--Macaulay: its localization at every prime is a Cohen--Macaulay

    [IsNoetherianRing A] (hA : IsGorensteinRing A) : IsCohenMacaulayRing A

declarations.name: Dualizing.isGorensteinRing_iff_isInvertible_canonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DW9 (1)(a).** A Noetherian ring with a dualizing complex is
Gorenstein exactly when that complex is invertible, for the canonical derived tensor product
of [Stacks, Tag 0FNQ], which is available when the module universe is the ring's own.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGorensteinRing_iff_isInvertible_canonical
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K) :
    letI := (DerivedCategory.Invertible.derivedCategory_symmetricMonoidalCategory A).choose
    Dualizing.IsGorensteinRing A ↔ MonoidalCategory.IsInvertible K

declarations.name: Dualizing.isGorensteinRing_iff_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DW9 (1)(a)**, for a dualizing complex whose module universe is larger
than the ring's. A Noetherian ring with a dualizing complex is Gorenstein if and only if that
complex is invertible, the tensor product being the one transported along the coefficient
equivalence; invertibility does not depend on which of the two is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGorensteinRing_iff_isInvertible
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
    (hK : Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K) :
    letI := derivedCategoryMonoidal.{u, v} A
    IsGorensteinRing A ↔ MonoidalCategory.IsInvertible K
declarations.comment: (1)(a) at a larger module universe

declarations.name: Dualizing.isOpen_gorensteinLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DW9 (1)(c).** If a Noetherian ring admits a dualizing complex, then the
set of primes whose local ring is Gorenstein is open in the prime spectrum.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_gorensteinLocus
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A)) (hK : Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K) :
    IsOpen {p : PrimeSpectrum A |
      Dualizing.IsGorensteinLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)}

declarations.name: Dualizing.exists_isDualizingComplex_iff_regularModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DW9 (2).** A Noetherian Gorenstein ring has a dualizing complex if and
only if the ring itself, placed in degree zero, is a dualizing complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isDualizingComplex_iff_regularModule
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hA : IsGorensteinRing A) :
    (∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A), IsDualizingComplex K) ↔
      IsDualizingComplex
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of A A))

declarations.name: Dualizing.isGorensteinLocalRing_iff_isInvertible_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DW9 (1)(b).** The localization of a Noetherian
ring at a prime is Gorenstein if and only if the localization of a dualizing complex
is invertible in the derived category of the localized ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGorensteinLocalRing_iff_isInvertible_localization
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A))
    (hK : IsDualizingComplex K)
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] :
    let B := Localization.AtPrime p
    letI := derivedCategoryMonoidal.{u, v} B
    IsGorensteinLocalRing B ↔
      MonoidalCategory.IsInvertible
        ((StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.derivedExtensionScalars
          (algebraMap A B)).obj K)

declarations.name: Dualizing.isGorensteinRing_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
The target of a local complete intersection homomorphism from a Noetherian Gorenstein ring is
Gorenstein.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorensteinRing_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (f : A →+* B) (hf : f.IsLocalCompleteIntersection)
    (hA : IsGorensteinRing A) :
    letI := f.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra.FiniteType A B := hf.1
    letI : IsNoetherianRing B := Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing A B
    IsGorensteinRing B

declarations.name: Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_extendScalars_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a flat map of Noetherian commutative rings. If the induced map `A/I → B/IB`
is bijective and `IB` is contained in the Jacobson radical of `B`, then extending a dualizing
complex from `A` to `B` gives a dualizing complex over `B`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDualizingComplex_extendScalars_of_flat
    {A : Type u} {B : Type w} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [Module.Flat A B] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (I : Ideal A)
    (hquotient : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap A B)) (algebraMap A B)
        Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (hjacobson : I.map (algebraMap A B) ≤ Ring.jacobson B)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A))
    (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) :
    IsDualizingComplex
      ((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, w, v} (algebraMap A B)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)

declarations.name: Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DWD.** The derived base change of a dualizing complex
to the completion of a Noetherian ring along any ideal is a dualizing complex.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDualizingComplex_adicCompletion
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A))
    (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) :
    IsDualizingComplex
      (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, v}
        (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).mapDerivedCategory).obj K)
declarations.comment: ideal_adic_completion

declarations.name: Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_completion_henselization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DWD.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, let `I ⊆ A` be an ideal and let
`ω_A^•` be a dualizing complex. Then

1. `ω_A^• ⊗_A A^h` is a dualizing complex on the henselization `(A^h, I^h)` of the pair
   `(A, I)`,
2. `ω_A^• ⊗_A A^∧` is a dualizing complex on the `I`-adic completion `A^∧`, and
3. if `A` is local, then `ω_A^• ⊗_A A^h`, resp. `ω_A^• ⊗_A A^{sh}`, is a dualizing complex on
   the henselization, resp. a strict henselization, of `A`.

The conjuncts are `Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_henselizationPair`,
`Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_adicCompletion`, `Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_henselization` and
`Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_strictHenselization`, each of which carries the tag for its own
part. As there, part (3) for a strict henselization is stated for a henselization of `A` along
an arbitrary prescribed extension `κ(A) ⊆ L` of its residue field, which is a strict
henselization exactly when `L` is a separable algebraic closure of `κ(A)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingComplex_completion_henselization
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v w} A)) (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) :
    (∀ (Ah : Type w) [CommRing Ah] [Algebra A Ah]
        (hh : HenselianPair Ah (I.map (algebraMap A Ah)))
        (hι : ∀ (B : Type (max u w)) (_ : CommRing B) (J : Ideal B),
          HenselianPair B J →
            ∀ f : A →+* B, I ≤ J.comap f →
              ∃! g : Ah →+* B,
                g.comp (algebraMap A Ah) = f ∧ I.map (algebraMap A Ah) ≤ J.comap g),
        haveI : Module.Flat A Ah :=
          (flat_henselization_and_bijective_quotientMap A I Ah hh hι).1
        haveI : IsNoetherianRing Ah :=
          (henselization_isNoetherian_and_completion_equiv A I Ah hh hι).2.1
        IsDualizingComplex
          ((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, w, max u v w}
            (algebraMap A Ah)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)) ∧
    IsDualizingComplex
      ((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max u v w}
        (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).mapDerivedCategory.obj K) ∧
    ∀ [IsLocalRing A],
      (∀ (Ah : Type w) [CommRing Ah] [IsLocalRing Ah] [Algebra A Ah]
          [IsHenselization A (ResidueField A) Ah],
          haveI : Module.Flat A Ah := IsHenselization.flat (L := ResidueField A)
          haveI : IsNoetherianRing Ah :=
            isNoetherianRing_of_isHenselization (A := A) (B := Ah) (ResidueField A)
          IsDualizingComplex
            ((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, w, max u v w}
              (algebraMap A Ah)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)) ∧
      (∀ (L : Type t) [Field L] [Algebra (ResidueField A) L]
          (Ash : Type w) [CommRing Ash] [IsLocalRing Ash] [Algebra A Ash]
          [IsHenselization A L Ash],
          haveI : Module.Flat A Ash := IsHenselization.flat (L := L)
          haveI : IsNoetherianRing Ash :=
            isNoetherianRing_of_isHenselization (A := A) (B := Ash) L
          IsDualizingComplex
            ((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, w, max u v w}
              (algebraMap A Ash)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K))
declarations.comment: all three parts conjoined

declarations.name: Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_henselizationPair
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DWD, part (1).** The derived base change of a dualizing complex to
the henselization `A^h` of a pair `(A, I)` with `A` Noetherian is a dualizing complex.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDualizingComplex_henselizationPair
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (Ah : Type w) [CommRing Ah] [Algebra A Ah]
    (hh : HenselianPair Ah (I.map (algebraMap A Ah)))
    (hι : ∀ (B : Type (max u w)) (_ : CommRing B) (J : Ideal B),
      HenselianPair B J →
        ∀ f : A →+* B, I ≤ J.comap f →
          ∃! g : Ah →+* B,
            g.comp (algebraMap A Ah) = f ∧ I.map (algebraMap A Ah) ≤ J.comap g)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A)) (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) :
    haveI : Module.Flat A Ah :=
      (flat_henselization_and_bijective_quotientMap A I Ah hh hι).1
    haveI : IsNoetherianRing Ah :=
      (henselization_isNoetherian_and_completion_equiv A I Ah hh hι).2.1
    IsDualizingComplex
      ((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, w, v} (algebraMap A Ah)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)
declarations.comment: pair_henselization

declarations.name: Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_henselization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DWD, part (3), the henselization.** The derived base change of a
dualizing complex to the henselization `A^h` of a Noetherian local ring `A` is a dualizing
complex.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDualizingComplex_henselization
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {Ah : Type w} [CommRing Ah] [IsLocalRing Ah] [Algebra A Ah]
    [IsHenselization A (ResidueField A) Ah]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A)) (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) :
    haveI : Module.Flat A Ah := IsHenselization.flat (L := ResidueField A)
    haveI : IsNoetherianRing Ah :=
      isNoetherianRing_of_isHenselization (A := A) (B := Ah) (ResidueField A)
    IsDualizingComplex
      ((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, w, v} (algebraMap A Ah)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)
declarations.comment: local_henselization

declarations.name: Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_strictHenselization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DWD, part (3), the strict henselization.** The derived base change of
a dualizing complex to a henselization `A^{sh}` of a Noetherian local ring `A` along a
prescribed extension `κ ⊆ L` of its residue field — for `L` a separable algebraic closure of
`κ`, a strict henselization of `A` — is a dualizing complex.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDualizingComplex_strictHenselization
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (L : Type t) [Field L] [Algebra (ResidueField A) L]
    {Ash : Type w} [CommRing Ash] [IsLocalRing Ash] [Algebra A Ash]
    [IsHenselization A L Ash]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v w} A)) (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) :
    haveI : Module.Flat A Ash := IsHenselization.flat (L := L)
    haveI : IsNoetherianRing Ash :=
      isNoetherianRing_of_isHenselization (A := A) (B := Ash) L
    IsDualizingComplex
      ((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, w, max u v w}
        (algebraMap A Ash)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)
declarations.comment: local_strict_henselization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGorenstein_of_isRegular
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0DWG.** Every regular scheme is Gorenstein.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorenstein_of_isRegular (X : Scheme.{u}) (hX : IsRegular X) :
    IsGorenstein X

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule_invertible_iff_fibers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DWK**, part (1). For a quasi-finite flat homomorphism of Noetherian
rings, the relative dualizing module is invertible over the target if and only if the relative
dualizing module of the fibre `B ⊗_A κ(p)` over `κ(p)` is invertible for every prime `p` of the
base.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingModule_invertible_iff_fibers
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [Algebra.FiniteType A B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    [Module.Flat A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} A B) :
    Module.Invertible B (dualizingModule F) ↔
      ∀ (p : PrimeSpectrum A),
        letI : Algebra p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.Fiber B) :=
          Algebra.TensorProduct.leftAlgebra
        ∀ (G : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, max u v, max u w}
            p.asIdeal.ResidueField (p.asIdeal.Fiber B)),
          Module.Invertible (p.asIdeal.Fiber B) (dualizingModule G)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.relativeDualizingModuleData_isInvertible_iff_fibers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DWK**, part (2). For a quasi-finite flat morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of
Noetherian schemes, the relative dualizing module `ω_{Y/X}` of Tag 0BVG is an invertible
`𝒪_Y`-module if and only if the relative dualizing module `ω_{Y_x/x}` of the fibre
`Y_x → Spec κ(x)` is invertible for every point `x` of `X`. Both modules are the ones constructed
by `Stacks.Discriminant.relativeDualizingModuleData`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDualizingModuleData_isInvertible_iff_fibers :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace).property (relativeDualizingModuleData f).sheaf ↔
      ∀ x : X, Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (f.fiber x).presheaf
        (structureSheafRing (f.fiber x).toRingedSpace).property
          (relativeDualizingModuleData (f.fiberToSpecResidueField x)).sheaf
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModule_invertible_of_isGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DWL.** Let `k` be a field and let `B` be a global complete
intersection over `k` of dimension `0`. Then the relative dualizing module `ω_{B/k}` is an
invertible `B`-module.

The dualizing module is computed from an arbitrary finite-open factorization of `k → B`; the
choice is immaterial by `Stacks.Discriminant.dualizingModuleEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingModule_invertible_of_isGlobalCompleteIntersection
    {k : Type u} {B : Type v} [Field k] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} k B)
    (hB : IsGlobalCompleteIntersection k B) (hdim : ringKrullDim B = 0) :
    Module.Invertible B (dualizingModule F)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.nonempty_complementSheafCohomology_iso_localCohomologyModule
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DWR] (2), the isomorphisms above degree zero.** Let `R` be a ring and let
`I ⊆ R` be a finitely generated ideal. Set `X = Spec R`, `Z = V(I)` and `U = X ∖ Z`. Let `F` be
an `𝒪_U`-module and let `M` be an `R`-module with `F ≅ M̃|_U`. Then
`H^p(U, F) ≅ H^{p+1}_Z(M)` as `R`-modules for every `p ≥ 1`.

The isomorphism is transported along `F ≅ M̃|_U`, then
`complementSheafCohomologyTildeIso` passes to the cohomology over `U` of `M̃` on `X`, where
`Stacks.LocalCohomologySequence.nonempty_complementCohomologyBase_iso_localCohomologyModule` is
the comparison with local cohomology. The source only asserts that the two modules are
isomorphic, so the conclusion is nonemptiness of the type of isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_complementSheafCohomology_iso_localCohomologyModule (hI : I.FG)
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) (F : (complementZeroLocus R I : Scheme).Modules)
    (e : F ≅ complementTilde R I M) (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p) :
    Nonempty ((complementSheafCohomology R I p).obj F ≅
      localCohomologyModule R I hI M ((p + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ))
declarations.comment: higher_cohomology_comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.exists_module_iso_restrict_tilde
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DWR.** Every quasi-coherent module on the complement of the zero
locus of a finitely generated ideal in an affine spectrum is the restriction of the sheaf
associated to a module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_module_iso_restrict_tilde
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (_hI : I.FG)
    (F : (complementZeroLocus R I : Scheme).Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ∃ M : ModuleCat.{u} R,
      Nonempty
        (F ≅ ((tilde.functor (CommRingCat.of R)).obj M).restrict
          (complementZeroLocus R I).ι)
declarations.comment: extension

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.exact_lowDegreeSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0BK0, the low-degree sequence.** Let `I` be a finitely generated ideal of a
commutative ring `A`, let `U = Spec A \ V(I)`, let `M` be an `A`-module and let `F` be a sheaf of
modules on `U` identified with the restriction to `U` of the sheaf associated to `M`. Then the
four-term sequence
`0 ⟶ H⁰_I(M) ⟶ M ⟶ Γ(U, F) ⟶ H¹_I(M) ⟶ 0`
is exact: the map out of degree-zero local cohomology is injective, the sequence is exact at `M`
and at `Γ(U, F)`, and the connecting map onto `H¹_I(M)` is surjective.

Every ideal of a Noetherian ring is finitely generated, by `Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing`, so
this covers the Noetherian hypothesis of the source; and it does not assume `M` finite or `F`
coherent, which the source does.

The same four-term sequence is the first half of clause (2) of Stacks 0DWR, which assumes only
that `I` is finitely generated. The second half of that clause, the comparison
`H^p(U, F) ≅ H^{p+1}_I(M)` in degrees `p ≥ 1`, `A`-linearly and for the same `F` and `M`, is
`Stacks.LocalCohomology.nonempty_complementSheafCohomology_iso_localCohomologyModule`, under the
same hypothesis `I.FG`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_lowDegreeSequence (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (complementZeroLocus A I : Scheme).ringCatSheaf)
    (e : F ≅ complementTilde A I M) :
    Function.Injective (localCohomologyZeroToModule A I hI M).hom ∧
      Function.Exact (localCohomologyZeroToModule A I hI M)
        (restrictionToComplement (localizationTriangleData.{v} A I hI) M F e) ∧
      Function.Exact (restrictionToComplement (localizationTriangleData.{v} A I hI) M F e)
        (localizationBoundary (localizationTriangleData.{v} A I hI) M F e) ∧
      Function.Surjective (localizationBoundary (localizationTriangleData.{v} A I hI) M F e)
declarations.comment: low_degree_sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.iso_restrict_tilde_globalSectionsModule
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent module on the complement of `V(I)` is the restriction of the associated sheaf
of its global-sections `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem iso_restrict_tilde_globalSectionsModule
    (F : (complementZeroLocus R I : Scheme).Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Nonempty
      (F ≅ ((tilde.functor (CommRingCat.of R)).obj
        (complementGlobalSections R I F)).restrict
        (complementZeroLocus R I).ι)
declarations.comment: global_sections_choice

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.isZero_localCohomology_zero_globalSectionsModule
declarations.doc: The degree-zero local cohomology of the global-sections module vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_localCohomology_zero_globalSectionsModule
    (F : (complementZeroLocus R I : Scheme).Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsZero (localCohomologyModule R I hI (complementGlobalSections R I F) 0)
declarations.comment: global_sections_choice

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.isZero_localCohomology_one_globalSectionsModule
declarations.doc: The degree-one local cohomology of the global-sections module vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_localCohomology_one_globalSectionsModule
    (F : (complementZeroLocus R I : Scheme).Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsZero (localCohomologyModule R I hI (complementGlobalSections R I F) 1)
declarations.comment: global_sections_choice

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.isIso_homology_localCohomologyComparison_of_isIPowerTorsion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DWS.** For an `I`-power-torsion module `M`, the canonical map
`H^i_{V(I) ∩ V(J)}(M) ⟶ H^i_{V(J)}(M)` is an isomorphism in every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homology_localCohomologyComparison_of_isIPowerTorsion
    (I J : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (hJ : J.FG) (M : ModuleCat.{v} A)
    (hM : IsIPowerTorsion A M I) (i : ℤ) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) i).map
      (Stacks.Algebraization.localCohomologyComparison A (I ⊔ J) J
        (Submodule.FG.sup hI hJ) hJ le_sup_right
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).obj M)))

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.isIso_colimitPrincipalLocalCohomologyToModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DWT, degree zero.** Let `S` be a multiplicative subset of a commutative ring `A`
and let `M` be an `A`-module whose localization at `S` vanishes. Then the canonical map
`colim_{f ∈ S} H⁰_{V(f)}(M) ⟶ M` is an isomorphism.

The legs `H⁰_{V(f)}(M) ⟶ M` are injective, which gives injectivity on the filtered colimit; and
every `m ∈ M` is annihilated by some `f ∈ S`, hence restricts to zero on `Spec A ∖ V(f)` and so
lies in the image of the leg at `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimitPrincipalLocalCohomologyToModule (S : Submonoid A) (M : ModuleCat.{u} A)
    [Subsingleton (LocalizedModule S M)] :
    IsIso (colimitPrincipalLocalCohomologyToModule A S M)
declarations.comment: degree zero

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.isZero_colimitPrincipalLocalCohomologyOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DWT, degree one.** Let `S` be a multiplicative subset of a commutative ring `A` and
let `M` be an `A`-module whose localization at `S` vanishes. Then
`colim_{f ∈ S} H¹_{V(f)}(M) = 0`.

Every class in the system dies at a larger index, so every leg into the colimit is zero and the
identity of the colimit is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_colimitPrincipalLocalCohomologyOne (S : Submonoid A) (M : ModuleCat.{u} A)
    [Subsingleton (LocalizedModule S M)] :
    IsZero (colimit (principalLocalCohomologySystem A S M 1))
declarations.comment: degree one

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.range_localCohomologyAwayComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DWU, part (1).** The image of the comparison out of the colimit of the local
cohomology modules on the supports `V(I + (f))`, for `f` outside the prime `𝔭`, is the kernel of
localization at `𝔭`.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_localCohomologyAwayComparison
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I p : Ideal A) (hp : p.IsPrime) (hI : I.FG)
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) (i : ℤ) (_hi : 0 ≤ i) :
    LinearMap.range (localCohomologyAwayColimitData A I p hp hI M i).comparison.hom =
      LinearMap.ker (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.primeCompl
        (localCohomologyModule A I hI M i))
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyAwayComparison_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DWU, part (2).** If `Hⁱ⁻¹_{V(I)}(M)` vanishes after localization at the prime `𝔭`,
the comparison out of the colimit is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem localCohomologyAwayComparison_injective
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I p : Ideal A) (hp : p.IsPrime) (hI : I.FG)
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) (i : ℤ) (_hi : 0 ≤ i)
    (hvan : Subsingleton
      (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl (localCohomologyModule A I hI M (i - 1)))) :
    Function.Injective
      (localCohomologyAwayColimitData A I p hp hI M i).comparison.hom
declarations.comment: part (2)
