where its relative dimension `dim((A/𝔭)_𝔮)` is `dim(A/𝔭)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localStabilizationHypotheses_iff (I : Ideal A) (s d : ℤ)
    (omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{w} A)) :
    LocalStabilizationHypotheses (M := M) I s d omega ↔
      (I ≠ ⊤ ∧ StabilizationHypotheses (M := M) I (maximalIdeal A) s d omega)
declarations.comment: the hypotheses, identified with those of Stacks 0EFI at J = 𝔪

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.zeroLocus_stabilizingIdeal_maximalIdeal_inter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DXM.** The ideal that Stacks 0EFI selects at `J = 𝔪` meets `V(I)` in the closed
point only, which is the first clause of the conclusion of the lemma.
declarations.statement:
public theorem zeroLocus_stabilizingIdeal_maximalIdeal_inter (I : Ideal A) (s d : ℤ)
    (omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{w} A))
    (H : LocalStabilizationHypotheses (M := M) I s d omega) :
    PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus
          ((stabilizingIdeal I (maximalIdeal A) s d omega
            H.toStabilizationHypotheses : Ideal A) : Set A) ∩
        PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) = {closedPoint A}
declarations.comment: the ideal J₀, with V(J₀) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_stabilization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DXM.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring, let `I ⊂ A` be an ideal, let `M` be
a finite `A`-module and let `s` and `d` be integers. Under hypotheses (1)–(4) of the lemma there
is an ideal `J₀` with `V(J₀) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}` such that for every ideal `J ⊆ J₀` with
`V(J) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}` the comparison `RΓ_{J₀}(M) → RΓ_J(M)` induces an isomorphism in cohomology
in degrees `≤ s`, and one power of `J₀ I` annihilates all of those cohomology modules.

This is `Stacks.Algebraization.exists_stabilization_of_exists` with its hypothesis discharged by
`Stacks.Algebraization.exists_isStabilizingData_maximalIdeal`. Taking `J = J₀` gives the
annihilation of `H^i_{J₀}(M)` by a power of `J₀ I`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_stabilization (I : Ideal A) (s d : ℤ)
    (omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (H : LocalStabilizationHypotheses (M := M) I s d omega) :
    ∃ J₀ : Ideal A, ∃ n : ℕ,
      PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J₀ : Set A) ∩ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) =
          {closedPoint A} ∧
        ∀ J : Ideal A, ∀ hJ : J ≤ J₀,
          PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) ∩ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) =
            {closedPoint A} →
          ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ s →
            IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).map
                (localCohomologyComparison A J₀ J J₀.fg_of_isNoetherianRing
                  J.fg_of_isNoetherianRing hJ
                  ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
                    (ModuleCat.of A M)))) ∧
              (J₀ * I) ^ n ≤ Module.annihilator A
                ↥((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj
                  ((Dualizing.localCohomologyFunctor A J J.fg_of_isNoetherianRing).obj
                    ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
                      (ModuleCat.of A M))).obj)
declarations.comment: the conclusion: an ideal J₀ and one exponent n such that every J ⊆ J₀ with V(J) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪} has RΓ_{J₀}(M) → RΓ_J(M) an isomorphism on cohomology in degrees ≤ s and (J₀ I) ^ n annihilating those modules

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_stabilization_finite_localCohomologyModule_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DXN.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring, `I ⊂ A` an ideal, `M` a finite
`A`-module and `s`, `d` integers. Assume (1) `A` has a dualizing complex, (2') every prime
`𝔭 ∈ V(I)` other than `𝔪` has `depth(M_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > s`, (3) every prime `𝔭 ∉ V(I)` with
`V(𝔭) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}` has `dim(A/𝔭) ≤ d`, and (4) every prime `𝔭 ∉ V(I)` with
`V(𝔭) ∩ V(I) ≠ {𝔪}` has `depth(M_𝔭) ≥ s` or `depth(M_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > d + s`. Then there is an
ideal `J₀` with `V(J₀) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}` such that for every `J ⊆ J₀` with `V(J) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}` the
map `RΓ_{J₀}(M) → RΓ_J(M)` is an isomorphism on cohomology in degrees `≤ s` and one power of
`J₀ I` annihilates those cohomology modules (the conclusion of Stacks 0DXM), and moreover
`H^i_{J₀}(M)` is a finite `A`-module for every `i ≤ s`.

Hypotheses (1), (3), (4) and the source's standing assumption `I ≠ A` (without which
`V(J₀) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}` is unattainable) are `LocalStabilizationHypotheses`; (2') is
`DepthAddDimGtAtMaximalIdeal`. The integers `s` and `d` are arbitrary. For `s < 0` the
finiteness is the vanishing of local cohomology in negative degrees; for `d < 0` the hypotheses
force `I` to be nilpotent (`LocalStabilizationHypotheses.mem_zeroLocus_of_neg`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_stabilization_finite_localCohomologyModule_maximalIdeal
    (I : Ideal A) (s d : ℤ) (omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (H : LocalStabilizationHypotheses (M := M) I s d omega)
    (h2 : DepthAddDimGtAtMaximalIdeal (M := M) I s) :
    ∃ J₀ : Ideal A, ∃ n : ℕ,
      PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J₀ : Set A) ∩ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) =
          {closedPoint A} ∧
        (∀ J : Ideal A, ∀ hJ : J ≤ J₀,
          PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) ∩ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) =
            {closedPoint A} →
          ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ s →
            IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).map
                (localCohomologyComparison A J₀ J J₀.fg_of_isNoetherianRing
                  J.fg_of_isNoetherianRing hJ
                  ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
                    (ModuleCat.of A M)))) ∧
              (J₀ * I) ^ n ≤ Module.annihilator A
                ↥((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj
                  ((Dualizing.localCohomologyFunctor A J J.fg_of_isNoetherianRing).obj
                    ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
                      (ModuleCat.of A M))).obj)) ∧
        ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ s →
          Module.Finite A
            (localCohomologyModule A J₀ J₀.fg_of_isNoetherianRing (ModuleCat.of A M) i)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.depthAddDimGtOnZeroLocus_maximalIdeal_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DXN.** Hypothesis (2') of the lemma is hypothesis (2') of Stacks 0EFJ at
`J = 𝔪`, for every ideal `I`.

This biconditional is the content of the source's proof, which reads "this is a special case of
Lemma 0EFJ": at `J = 𝔪` the set `V(𝔪) ∩ V(I)` is the single point `𝔪`, so a prime of `V(I)`
lies outside it exactly when it differs from `𝔪`, and the only specialization of it available
in `V(𝔪) ∩ V(I)` is `𝔪` itself, where `dim((A/𝔭)_𝔪)` is `dim(A/𝔭)`.

That reading of `V(𝔪) ∩ V(I)` uses `𝔪 ∈ V(I)`, the source's standing assumption that `I` is
proper. It is not needed for the equivalence itself: for `I = A` the locus `V(I)` is empty, so
both conditions quantify over nothing.
declarations.comment: hypothesis (2') is hypothesis (2') of Stacks 0EFJ at J = 𝔪, for every ideal I

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.finite_localCohomologyModule_stabilizingIdeal_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DXN.** Under hypotheses (1), (3), (4) of Stacks 0DXM together with hypothesis
(2') in place of its empty hypothesis (2), the local cohomology of `M` supported in the ideal
`J₀` that Stacks 0DXM selects is a finite `A`-module in every degree `i ≤ s`.

This is Stacks 0EFJ at `J = 𝔪`. The annihilation of `H^i_{J₀}(M)` by a power of `J₀ I` for
`i ≤ s` is a clause of the conclusion of Stacks 0DXM and is carried as a hypothesis, as it is in
Stacks 0EFJ.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finite_localCohomologyModule_stabilizingIdeal_maximalIdeal
    (h2 : DepthAddDimGtAtMaximalIdeal (M := M) I s) (hs : 0 ≤ s)
    (hann : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ j : ℤ, j ≤ s →
      ((stabilizingIdeal I (maximalIdeal A) s d omega H.toStabilizationHypotheses * I) ^ n
        : Ideal A) ≤ Module.annihilator A
        (localCohomologyModule A
          (stabilizingIdeal I (maximalIdeal A) s d omega H.toStabilizationHypotheses)
          (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing
            (stabilizingIdeal I (maximalIdeal A) s d omega H.toStabilizationHypotheses))
          (ModuleCat.of A M) j))
    (i : ℤ) (hi : i ≤ s) :
    Module.Finite A
      (localCohomologyModule A
        (stabilizingIdeal I (maximalIdeal A) s d omega H.toStabilizationHypotheses)
        (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing
          (stabilizingIdeal I (maximalIdeal A) s d omega H.toStabilizationHypotheses))
        (ModuleCat.of A M) i)
declarations.comment: H^i_{J₀}(M) is a finite A-module for i ≤ s, given the annihilation clause of Stacks 0DXM and 0 ≤ s

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.finite_localCohomologyModule_stabilizingIdeal_maximalIdeal_of_exists
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DXN.** The same finiteness, with the annihilation clause of Stacks 0DXM proved
from Stacks 0EFI.

The hypotheses are then exactly those of Stacks 0DXM with its empty hypothesis (2) replaced by
(2'), together with `0 ≤ s` and the hypothesis `0 ≤ d` that Stacks 0EFI needs and the source
of Stacks 0DXM uses silently; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finite_localCohomologyModule_stabilizingIdeal_maximalIdeal_of_exists
    (h2 : DepthAddDimGtAtMaximalIdeal (M := M) I s) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (hd : 0 ≤ d)
    (i : ℤ) (hi : i ≤ s) :
    Module.Finite A
      (localCohomologyModule A
        (stabilizingIdeal I (maximalIdeal A) s d omega H.toStabilizationHypotheses)
        (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing
          (stabilizingIdeal I (maximalIdeal A) s d omega H.toStabilizationHypotheses))
        (ModuleCat.of A M) i)
declarations.comment: H^i_{J₀}(M) is a finite A-module for i ≤ s, for 0 ≤ s and 0 ≤ d

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_isLocalAlgebraizationIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DXP.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring, let `I ⊆ A` be a proper ideal, let
`M` be a finite `A`-module and let `s` and `d` be integers. Assume `A` is `I`-adically complete
with a dualizing complex, that `cd(A, I) ≤ d`, and that every prime `𝔭 ∉ V(I)` with
`V(𝔭) ∩ V(I) ≠ {𝔪}` has `depth(M_𝔭) ≥ s` or `depth(M_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > d + s`. Then there is an
ideal `J₀` with `V(J₀) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}` such that for every ideal `J ⊆ J₀` with
`V(J) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}` the canonical map

`RΓ_J(M) ⟶ RΓ_𝔪(M)^∧`

is an isomorphism on cohomology in all degrees `≤ s`.

This is the source's own proof: the case `s < 0` is
`Stacks.Algebraization.isLocalAlgebraizationIdeal_of_lt_zero`, and for `0 ≤ s` the statement is
the case `J = 𝔪` of Stacks 0EFL, by
`Stacks.Algebraization.LocalAlgebraizationHypotheses.toAlgebraizationHypotheses` on the
hypotheses and `Stacks.Algebraization.isLocalAlgebraizationIdeal_of_isAlgebraizationIdeal` on
the conclusion.

Condition (5) of Stacks 0EFL is stated against a dimension function on `Spec(A)`, which the
statement of Stacks 0DXP does not mention. No such datum is assumed here: hypothesis (1)
provides a dualizing complex, and the dimension function attached to one by Stacks 0A7Z is
`Dualizing.dualizingDimensionFunctionOfArbitraryUniverse`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isLocalAlgebraizationIdeal (I : Ideal A) (s d : ℤ)
    (omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (H : LocalAlgebraizationHypotheses (M := M) I s d omega) :
    ∃ J₀ : Ideal A, IsLocalAlgebraizationIdeal (M := M) I H.ne_top s J₀
declarations.comment: existence of J₀

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.coherentFormalAlgebraization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DXQ.**  Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring which has a dualizing complex and
is complete with respect to an ideal `I`.  Set `X = Spec A`, `Y = V(I)` and `U = X ∖ {𝔪}`, and
let `ℱ` be a coherent sheaf on `U`.  Assume

1. `cd(A, I) ≤ d`, and
2. for any `x ∈ X ∖ Y` whose closure in `X` meets `U ∩ Y`,
   `depth(ℱ_x) ≥ s` or `depth(ℱ_x) + dim(closure of x) > d + s`,

Then there is an open `V₀ ⊆ U` containing `U ∩ Y` such that for any open `V ⊆ V₀` containing
`U ∩ Y` the map

`H^i(V, ℱ) ⟶ lim_n H^i(U, ℱ/Iⁿℱ)`

is an isomorphism for `i < s`.  If in addition `depth(ℱ_x) + dim(closure of x) > s` for all
`x ∈ U ∩ Y`, then these cohomology groups are finite `A`-modules.

Concretely: there is a finite `A`-module `M` with `ℱ ≅ M̃|_U` and `ℱ/Iⁿℱ ≅ (M/IⁿM)~|_U` as
towers, and an ideal `J₀` with `V(J₀) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}` — that is, the open
`V₀ = X ∖ V(J₀) ⊆ U` containing `U ∩ Y` — such that for every ideal `J ⊆ J₀` with
`V(J) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}` — that is, for every open `V = X ∖ V(J) ⊆ V₀` containing `U ∩ Y` — and every
degree `i < s`, the canonical map `H^i(V, M̃) ⟶ lim_n H^i(U, (M/IⁿM)~)` is an isomorphism, and
`H^i(V, M̃)` is a finite `A`-module whenever the extra depth bound holds.

Both groups of that map are identified with the source's own, so that nothing is left to the
reader:

* `H^i(V, M̃)` is `H^i(V, ℱ|_V)`, the cohomology on `V` of the sheaf `ℱ` itself, by the conjunct
  built from `Stacks.Algebraization.openCohomologyBaseRestrictIso`;
* the tower `n ↦ H^i(U, (M/IⁿM)~)` whose limit the map lands in is the tower
  `n ↦ H^i(U, ℱ/Iⁿℱ)`, transition maps included, by the conjunct built from
  `Stacks.Algebraization.quotientSystemOpenCohomologyNatIso`.  An isomorphism of towers is
  stronger than the isomorphism of limits it induces, so this pins the right-hand side without
  either limit having to be formed again.

The division of the two clauses is the source's.  The comparison is asserted under assumptions
(1) and (2) alone; the extra bound `depth(ℱ_x) + dim(closure of x) > s` on `U ∩ Y` appears only
as the hypothesis of the finiteness clause, where the source puts it ("If in addition …").  One
ideal `J₀` serves both, by the case distinction carried out in
`Stacks.Algebraization.PuncturedNeighbourhood.comparison_and_finiteness`.

Nothing beyond the hypotheses of the theorem is assumed.  The module `M` is produced by Stacks
0BK0 (1), the ideal `J₀` by Stacks 0DXP and Stacks 0DXN, the stabilizing data of Stacks 0EFI and
the bound `0 ≤ d` from assumption (1), and the localization triangle data of the degree-zero case
from a finite generating family of `J`.  Properness of `I` — the source's standing `𝔪 ∈ V(I)`,
without which `V(I)` is empty — is derived too, not assumed: over a local ring `I = A` would make
`A` `⊤`-adically Hausdorff, hence zero.

The two cohomology groups of the conclusion are named through the presentation `ℱ ≅ M̃|_U` and
the tower isomorphism `ℱ/Iⁿℱ ≅ (M/IⁿM)~|_U`, both of which the statement exhibits; this is the
reading the source itself uses, its proof opening with the choice of such an `M`.  The statement
also carries out that reading, exhibiting each of the two groups of the comparison map as the
corresponding group of `ℱ` — see the two conjuncts described above.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentFormalAlgebraization (I : Ideal A) (s d : ℤ)
    (omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete I A)
    (hdualizing : Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex omega)
    (hcd : Stacks.LocalCohomology.cohomologicalDimension A I
      (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing I) ≤ d)
    (F : (complementZeroLocus A (maximalIdeal A) : Scheme).Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (h2 : StalkDepthOrDimensionBound I F s d) :
    ∃ M : ModuleCat.{u} A, Module.Finite A M ∧
      Nonempty (F ≅ ((tilde.functor (CommRingCat.of A)).obj M).restrict
        (complementZeroLocus A (maximalIdeal A)).ι) ∧
      Nonempty (quotientSystemNearVanishing A I (maximalIdeal A) F ≅
        (adicQuotientModuleSystem A I M ⋙ tilde.functor (CommRingCat.of A)) ⋙
          Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (complementZeroLocus A (maximalIdeal A)).ι) ∧
      (∀ i : ℕ, Nonempty (quotientSystemNearVanishing A I (maximalIdeal A) F ⋙
          openCohomologyBaseFunctor A (complementZeroLocus A (maximalIdeal A)) i ≅
        adicQuotientModuleSystem A I M ⋙
          complementCohomologyBaseFunctor (A := CommRingCat.of A) (maximalIdeal A) i)) ∧
      ∃ J₀ : Ideal A,
        PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J₀ : Set A) ∩ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) =
            {closedPoint A} ∧
          ∀ J : Ideal A, J ≤ J₀ →
            ∀ hV : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) ∩ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) =
              {closedPoint A},
            ∀ i : ℕ, (i : ℤ) < s →
              IsIso (PuncturedNeighbourhood.neighbourhoodToPuncturedLimit I J M hV i) ∧
                Nonempty (openCohomologyBase A (complementZeroLocus A J)
                    ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor
                      ((Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).homOfLE
                        (le_complementZeroLocus_maximalIdeal
                          (PuncturedNeighbourhood.le_maximalIdeal_of_zeroLocus_inter hV)))).obj F)
                      i ≅
                  complementCohomologyBase (A := CommRingCat.of A) J M i) ∧
                (StalkDepthAddDimGt I F s →
                  Module.Finite A
                    (complementCohomologyBase (A := CommRingCat.of A) J M i))

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.PuncturedNeighbourhood.exists_ideal_finite_neighbourhoodCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DXQ, the finiteness clause.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring which has a
dualizing complex and is `I`-adically complete, let `M` be a finite `A`-module, and assume
assumptions (1) and (2) of the theorem together with
`depth(M_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > s` for every prime `𝔭 ∈ V(I)` other than `𝔪` — the theorem's extra
finiteness assumption, read at the points of `U ∩ Y`. Then there is an ideal `J₀` with
`V(J₀) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}`, that is an open `V₀ = Spec A ∖ V(J₀)` of the punctured spectrum containing
`U ∩ V(I)`, such that for every `J ⊆ J₀` with `V(J) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}` — that is, for every open
`V = Spec A ∖ V(J)` inside `V₀` containing `U ∩ V(I)` — the `A`-module `H^i(V, M̃)` is finite in
every degree `i < s`.

Nothing beyond the hypotheses of the theorem is assumed: the stabilizing data of Stacks 0EFI is
constructed, not assumed, from assumption (1); see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_ideal_finite_neighbourhoodCohomology (I : Ideal A) (s d : ℤ)
    (omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (H : Hypotheses (M := M) I s d omega)
    (hdepth : DepthAddDimGtAtMaximalIdeal (M := M) I s) :
    ∃ J₀ : Ideal A,
      PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J₀ : Set A) ∩ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) =
          {closedPoint A} ∧
        ∀ J : Ideal A, J ≤ J₀ →
          PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) ∩ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) =
            {closedPoint A} →
          ∀ i : ℕ, (i : ℤ) < s → Module.Finite A (neighbourhoodCohomology (M := M) J i)
declarations.comment: finiteness of H^i(V, ℱ) for i < s, with ℱ = M̃|_U

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.PuncturedNeighbourhood.finite_neighbourhoodCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DXQ, the finiteness clause.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring which has a
dualizing complex and is `I`-adically complete, let `M` be a finite `A`-module, and assume
assumptions (1) and (2) of the theorem together with
`depth(M_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > s` for every prime `𝔭 ∈ V(I)` other than `𝔪` — the theorem's extra
finiteness assumption, read at the points of `U ∩ Y`. Then there is an ideal `J₀` with
`V(J₀) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}`, that is an open `V₀ = Spec A ∖ V(J₀)` of the punctured spectrum containing
`U ∩ V(I)`, such that for every `J ⊆ J₀` with `V(J) ∩ V(I) = {𝔪}` — that is, for every open
`V = Spec A ∖ V(J)` inside `V₀` containing `U ∩ V(I)` — the `A`-module `H^i(V, M̃)` is finite in
every degree `i < s`.

This is `exists_ideal_finite_neighbourhoodCohomology`; the existence statement of Stacks 0EFI
is not needed as a hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finite_neighbourhoodCohomology (I : Ideal A) (s d : ℤ)
    (omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (H : Hypotheses (M := M) I s d omega)
    (hdepth : DepthAddDimGtAtMaximalIdeal (M := M) I s) :
    ∃ J₀ : Ideal A,
      PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J₀ : Set A) ∩ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) =
          {closedPoint A} ∧
        ∀ J : Ideal A, J ≤ J₀ →
          PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) ∩ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) =
            {closedPoint A} →
          ∀ i : ℕ, (i : ℤ) < s → Module.Finite A (neighbourhoodCohomology (M := M) J i)
declarations.comment: finiteness of H^i(V, ℱ) for i < s, with ℱ = M̃|_U

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.mono_comparisonMap_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DXR, the injectivity half.** The canonical map from the sections of a coherent
module `ℱ` on the punctured spectrum `U = Spec(A) ∖ {𝔪}` defined near `U ∩ V(I)` to the
compatible families of sections of `ℱ / Iⁿ ℱ` on all of `U` is injective. No hypothesis beyond
`A` Noetherian and `ℱ` coherent is used: neither completeness, nor the dualizing complex, nor
the dimension bound at the associated points.

The surjectivity half, and with it the whole of the source's conclusion — the map is an
isomorphism and both of its sides are finite `A`-modules — is
`Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonModuleMap_and_finite_maximalIdeal` of
`PuncturedSpectrumFormalSectionsWhole.lean`, at the source's own hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mono_comparisonMap_maximalIdeal [F.IsCoherent] :
    Mono (comparisonMap A I (maximalIdeal A) F)
declarations.comment: the injectivity half of the displayed map, proved with none of the source's hypotheses beyond Noetherian and coherent; the surjectivity half and the finiteness of the two modules hold at the source's own hypotheses, by `Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonModuleMap_and_finite_maximalIdeal`

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.mono_comparisonModuleMap_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DXR, the `A`-module structures and the `A`-linearity of the displayed map.** The
source states its conclusion as an isomorphism *of finite `A`-modules*, so the two sides carry
`A`-module structures and the map between them is `A`-linear. The two sides of
`Stacks.Algebraization.comparisonMap` are a colimit and a limit of groups of sections, hence
abelian groups; the `A`-module structures are
`Stacks.Algebraization.sectionsNearVanishingColimit` and
`Stacks.Algebraization.formalSectionsLimit`, obtained from the multiplication by `A` on
sections induced by `A ⟶ Γ(U, 𝒪_U)`, and the displayed map is `A`-linear for them, by
`Stacks.Algebraization.comparisonMap_comp_smul`. The statement below is that this `A`-linear
map — whose underlying map of abelian groups is the tag's map, by
`Stacks.Algebraization.forget₂_comparisonModuleMap` — is injective, that is, that the
injectivity half holds in the category of `A`-modules.

The source's surjectivity half and the finiteness of the two `A`-modules are supplied, for this
same `A`-linear map and at the source's own hypotheses, by
`Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonModuleMap_and_finite_maximalIdeal` of
`PuncturedSpectrumFormalSectionsWhole.lean`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mono_comparisonModuleMap_maximalIdeal [F.IsCoherent] :
    Mono (comparisonModuleMap A I (maximalIdeal A) F)
declarations.comment: the two sides of the displayed map are A-modules and the map is A-linear, and injective as a map of A-modules; its underlying map of abelian groups is the tag's map, by forget₂_comparisonModuleMap. The surjectivity half and the finiteness of the two A-modules hold at the source's own hypotheses, by `Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonModuleMap_and_finite_maximalIdeal`

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonModuleMap_and_finite_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DXR.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring which has a dualizing complex and is
complete with respect to an ideal `I`. Put `X = Spec(A)`, `Y = V(I)` and `U = X ∖ {𝔪}`, and let
`ℱ` be a coherent module on `U` such that every associated point `x ∈ U` of `ℱ` satisfies
`dim(closure {x}) > cd(A, I) + 1`, the closure being taken in `X`. Then the canonical map

`colim_V H⁰(V, ℱ) ⟶ lim_n H⁰(U, ℱ / Iⁿ ℱ)`,

the colimit being over the opens `V ⊆ U` containing `U ∩ Y`, is an isomorphism of finite
`A`-modules.

The two sides are the `A`-modules `Stacks.Algebraization.sectionsNearVanishingColimit` and
`Stacks.Algebraization.formalSectionsLimit`; the map is
`Stacks.Algebraization.comparisonModuleMap`, whose underlying map of abelian groups is
`Stacks.Algebraization.comparisonMap` by
`Stacks.Algebraization.forget₂_comparisonModuleMap`. The source's dimension hypothesis is stated
with `dim(closure {x}) = dim(A/𝔭)`, exactly as the source states it.

The proof is the source's: apply Stacks 0DXQ with `s = 1`, getting the finiteness too. Stacks
0BK0 (1) presents `ℱ` as `M̃|_U` for a finite `A`-module `M`; the associated points of `M̃|_U` are
the associated primes of `M`, so the dimension hypothesis becomes the hypothesis of Stacks 0DXP,
which supplies an ideal `J₀`, and of the finiteness clause of Stacks 0DXQ, which supplies an
ideal `J₁`. At `J = J₀ ∩ J₁` both apply: the canonical map `H¹_J(M) ⟶ lim_n H¹_J(M/IⁿM)` is onto
by Stacks 0DXP together with the pinned form of Stacks 0DXJ, so the four-term diagram chase makes
the comparison at the neighbourhood `X ∖ V(J)` onto; the displayed map is injective with no
hypothesis beyond Noetherian and coherent, hence an isomorphism; and the colimit is a quotient of
`H⁰(X ∖ V(J), ℱ)`, which is finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_comparisonModuleMap_and_finite_maximalIdeal
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete I A)
    (hdualizing : ∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K)
    (F : (complementZeroLocus A (maximalIdeal A) : Scheme).Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hdim : ∀ x : (complementZeroLocus A (maximalIdeal A) : Scheme),
      x ∈ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints F →
      ((cohomologicalDimension A I I.fg_of_isNoetherianRing + 1 : ℤ) : EInt) <
        krullDimToEInt (ringKrullDim (A ⧸ x.1.asIdeal))) :
    IsIso (comparisonModuleMap A I (maximalIdeal A) F) ∧
      Module.Finite A (sectionsNearVanishingColimit A I (maximalIdeal A) F) ∧
        Module.Finite A (formalSectionsLimit A I (maximalIdeal A) F)
declarations.comment: the whole statement: the displayed map colim_V H⁰(V, ℱ) ⟶ lim_n H⁰(U, ℱ/Iⁿℱ) is an isomorphism of A-modules, and both of its two sides are finite A-modules

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.restrictedTildeSystem_isCoherentAdicSystem
declarations.doc:
A finite module model gives a coherent adic system on the punctured
spectrum.
declarations.statement:
public theorem restrictedTildeSystem_isCoherentAdicSystem
    (M : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} S.A) (hM : IsFiniteModuleModel S M) :
    Stacks.Coherent.IsCoherentAdicSystem (Stacks.Algebraization.idealOnOpen S)
      (restrictedTildeSystem S M)
declarations.comment: forward implication

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_finiteModuleModel
declarations.doc:
Every coherent adic system on `U` has a finite module model, compatible
with the whole inverse-system structure.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finiteModuleModel
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (Stacks.Algebraization.idealOnOpen S)) :
    ∃ M : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} S.A,
      ∃ hM : IsFiniteModuleModel S M,
        Nonempty (coherentAdicSystemOfFiniteModuleModel S M hM ≅ F)
declarations.comment: converse

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.canonicallyExtends_and_isCompletion_of_depthDim
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DXU].**  In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0EHC] let `(ℱₙ)` be an object of
`Coh(U, I𝒪_U)`.  Assume

1. `A` is local and `𝔞 = 𝔪` is the maximal ideal,
2. `A` has a dualizing complex,
3. `I = (f)` is principal for a nonzerodivisor `f`,
4. each `ℱₙ` is finite locally free over `𝒪_U/fⁿ𝒪_U`,
5. `depth((A/f)_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > 1` for every `𝔭 ∈ V(f)` other than `𝔪`, and
6. `depth(A_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > 3` for every `𝔭 ∉ V(f)` with `V(𝔭) ∩ V(f) ≠ {𝔪}`.

Then `(ℱₙ)` extends canonically to `X = Spec(A)`; in particular, if `A` is `I`-adically complete
then `(ℱₙ)` is the completion of a coherent `𝒪_U`-module.

The proof is the source's.  Conditions (b) and (c) of the Mittag-Leffler criterion
[Stacks, Tag 0EHH] come from hypotheses (3), (4) and (5); condition (a) is the finite length of
the image of `H¹(U, ℱₙ) ⟶ H¹(U, ℱ₁)`, which [Stacks, Tag 0BK0] (2) and [Stacks, Tag 0EIR] turn
into the finite length of the image of `H²_𝔪(Mₙ) ⟶ H²_𝔪(M₁)` for `Mₙ = H⁰(U, ℱₙ)`, and which
local duality — in the shape that reads a vanishing of `Ext` back as a vanishing of local
cohomology — reduces to the finite length of the image of
`Ext^{-2}_A(M₁, ω) ⟶ Ext^{-2}_A(Mₙ, ω)`.  That last statement is where hypotheses (2), (4), (5)
and (6) are spent, over the localizations `A_𝔮` at the primes `𝔮 ∈ V(f) ∖ {𝔪}`.  The normalized
dualizing complex the computation needs is produced from hypothesis (2) by
`Dualizing.exists_isNormalizedDualizingComplex_shift`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicallyExtends_and_isCompletion_of_depthDim
    (S : AlgebraizationSituation.{u}) [IsLocalRing S.A] (ha : S.a = maximalIdeal S.A)
    (omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S.A))
    (homega : Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex (A := S.A) (K := omega))
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (idealOnOpen S)) (f : S.A)
    (hI : S.I = Ideal.span {f}) (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors S.A)
    (hfree : IsFiniteLocallyFreeAdic (idealOnOpen S) F)
    (h5 : DepthDimOnDivisor f) (h6 : DepthDimOffDivisor f) :
    CanonicallyExtends S F ∧
      (IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) S.A →
        (completionFunctor S.U.toScheme (S.Yι.ker.comap S.U.ι)).essImage
          (kerComapSystem S F))

declarations.name: Stacks.RingTheory.AssociatedPrimes.associatedPrimes_quotient_span_singleton_pow_succ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DXU (the associated-primes step).** For a nonzerodivisor `f` of a
commutative ring `A`, the associated primes of `A ⧸ fⁿ⁺¹A` are those of `A ⧸ fA`.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedPrimes_quotient_span_singleton_pow_succ (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) (n : ℕ) :
    associatedPrimes A (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f ^ (n + 1)}) =
      associatedPrimes A (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f})
declarations.comment: the step of the proof asserting that the associated primes of A/fⁿA agree with those of A/fA, for f a nonzerodivisor

declarations.name: Stacks.RingTheory.PrincipalDivisorDepth.mem_of_depth_add_ringKrullDim_le_three
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DXU (hypothesis (6) confines the support to `V(f)`).** Let `f` be an
element of a local ring `A` satisfying hypothesis (6), and let `𝔮` be a prime containing `f` and
different from the maximal ideal.  Then every prime `𝔭 ⊆ 𝔮` with
`depth(A_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) ≤ 3` contains `f`.

This is the source's "condition (6) tells us these primes are contained in `V(f)`", used twice:
for `dim(A/𝔮) = 2` with the primes of `depth(A_𝔭) + dim((A/𝔭)_𝔮) ≤ 1` supporting
`H^{-1}(ω^•_{A_𝔮})`, and for `dim(A/𝔮) = 1` with the primes of
`depth(A_𝔭) + dim((A/𝔭)_𝔮) ≤ 2` supporting `H^{-2}(ω^•_{A_𝔮})`.  In both cases
`dim(A/𝔭) = dim((A/𝔭)_𝔮) + dim(A/𝔮)`, so the two support conditions read
`depth(A_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) ≤ 3`, which is the single bound used here; `𝔮` itself is the point of
`V(𝔭) ∩ V(f)` other than `𝔪` that lets (6) apply.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_of_depth_add_ringKrullDim_le_three [IsLocalRing A] {f : A}
    (h6 : DepthDimOffDivisor f) {q p : PrimeSpectrum A} (hfq : f ∈ q.asIdeal)
    (hqm : q ≠ closedPoint A) (hpq : p.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal)
    (hle : (Module.depth A[p] (maximalIdeal A[p]) A[p] : WithBot ℕ∞) +
        ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p.asIdeal) ≤ 3) :
    f ∈ p.asIdeal
declarations.comment: the step of the proof deducing from hypothesis (6) that a prime below a point of V(f) other than the closed point, whose depth plus dimension is at most 3, contains f — the source's 'condition (6) tells us these primes are contained in V(f)'

declarations.name: Stacks.RingTheory.PrincipalDivisorDepth.exists_mulPowQuotSMulTop_eq_zero_of_depthDimOffDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DXU (the vanishing for `n` large enough).** Let `f` be an element of
a local ring `A` satisfying hypothesis (6), let `𝔮` be a prime containing `f` and different from
the maximal ideal, and let `N` be a finite `A`-module every prime of whose support lies below
`𝔮` and has `depth(A_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) ≤ 3`.  Then the maps `fⁿ : N ⧸ fN → N ⧸ f^{n+1}N` vanish for
all large `n`.

This is the conclusion of both of the source's two remaining cases.  There `N` is
`H^{-1}(ω^•_{A_𝔮})` when `dim(A/𝔮) = 2` and `H^{-2}(ω^•_{A_𝔮})` when `dim(A/𝔮) = 1`, each a
finite module whose support [Stacks, Tag 0DWZ] describes by a depth-plus-dimension bound; the
hypothesis (6) step `mem_of_depth_add_ringKrullDim_le_three` puts that support inside `V(f)`,
which makes `f` nilpotent on `N`, and the source's "thus the desired vanishing for `n` large
enough" is the vanishing below.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mulPowQuotSMulTop_eq_zero_of_depthDimOffDivisor [IsLocalRing A] {f : A}
    (h6 : DepthDimOffDivisor f) {q : PrimeSpectrum A} (hfq : f ∈ q.asIdeal)
    (hqm : q ≠ closedPoint A) (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module.Finite A N]
    (hsupp : ∀ p ∈ Module.support A N, p.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal ∧
      (Module.depth A[p] (maximalIdeal A[p]) A[p] : WithBot ℕ∞) +
        ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p.asIdeal) ≤ 3) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n, c ≤ n → mulPowQuotSMulTop f N n = 0
declarations.comment: the step of the proof concluding, for a finite module whose support hypothesis (6) places in V(f), that multiplication by fⁿ from N/fN to N/f^(n+1)N vanishes for all large n — the source's 'thus the desired vanishing for n large enough', in both the dim(A/q) = 2 and the dim(A/q) = 1 case

declarations.name: Stacks.RingTheory.PrincipalDivisorDepth.one_le_depth_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DXU (`depth(A_𝔮) ≥ 1` because `f` is a nonzerodivisor).** For `f` a
nonzerodivisor of a Noetherian ring `A` and `𝔮` a prime containing `f`, the local ring `A_𝔮` has
depth at least one.

This is the source's "`H^0(ω^•_{A_𝔮}) = 0` because `depth(A_𝔮) ≥ 1` as `f` is a
nonzerodivisor", the input to the case `dim(A/𝔮) = 2`: the image of `f` in `A_𝔮` lies in the
maximal ideal and is still a nonzerodivisor, so it is a regular sequence of length one, and
[Stacks, Tag 090R] gives `depth(A_𝔮) = depth(A_𝔮/fA_𝔮) + 1 ≥ 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem one_le_depth_localization [IsNoetherianRing A] {f : A} (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A)
    {q : PrimeSpectrum A} (hfq : f ∈ q.asIdeal) :
    1 ≤ Module.depth A[q] (maximalIdeal A[q]) A[q]
declarations.comment: the step of the proof asserting that A_q has depth at least 1 for a prime q containing the nonzerodivisor f, which is what makes H^0 of the dualizing complex of A_q vanish in the case dim(A/q) = 2

declarations.name: Stacks.RingTheory.PrincipalDivisorDepth.two_le_depth_localization_of_depthDimOnDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DXU (`depth(A_𝔮) ≥ 2` when `dim(A/𝔮) = 1`).** Let `f` be a
nonzerodivisor of a Noetherian local ring `A` satisfying hypothesis (5), and let `𝔮` be a prime
containing `f`, different from the maximal ideal, with `dim(A/𝔮) = 1`.  Then `A_𝔮` has depth at
least two.

This is the source's "if `dim(A/𝔮) = 1`, then condition (5) combined with the fact that `f` is a
nonzerodivisor insures that `A_𝔮` has depth at least `2`", which is what makes both
`H^0(ω^•_{A_𝔮})` and `H^{-1}(ω^•_{A_𝔮})` vanish in that case.  Hypothesis (5) at `𝔮` reads
`depth((A/fA)_𝔮) + 1 > 1`, so `(A/fA)_𝔮 = A_𝔮/fA_𝔮` has depth at least one, and
[Stacks, Tag 090R] adds the one coming from the nonzerodivisor `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem two_le_depth_localization_of_depthDimOnDivisor [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    {f : A} (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) (h5 : DepthDimOnDivisor f) {q : PrimeSpectrum A}
    (hfq : f ∈ q.asIdeal) (hqm : q ≠ closedPoint A)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (A ⧸ q.asIdeal) = 1) :
    2 ≤ Module.depth A[q] (maximalIdeal A[q]) A[q]
declarations.comment: the step of the proof asserting that A_q has depth at least 2 when dim(A/q) = 1, deduced from hypothesis (5) at q together with f being a nonzerodivisor

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.CompleteNormalDomain.satisfiesAssumptions_and_isCompletion_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeAdic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DXV.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a complete Noetherian normal local domain of
dimension at least four and let `f ∈ 𝔪` be nonzero. Then the algebraization situation with
`𝔞 = 𝔪` and `I = (f)` satisfies assumptions (1), (2), (3), (5) and (6) of [Stacks, Tag 0DXU]:
`𝔞` is the maximal ideal, `A` has a dualizing complex, `I` is generated by the nonzerodivisor `f`,
and the two depth-dimension inequalities hold off the closed point. Thus vector bundles on the
formal completion of the punctured spectrum `U` along `U ∩ V(f)` can be algebraized: every object
`(ℱₙ)` of `Coh(U, f𝒪_U)` whose terms are finite locally free over the infinitesimal neighbourhoods
of `U ∩ V(f)` extends to `X` and is the completion of a coherent `𝒪_U`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem satisfiesAssumptions_and_isCompletion_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeAdic (A : Type u)
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal A) A]
    [IsDomain A] [IsIntegrallyClosed A] (hdim : (4 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim A) (f : A)
    (hfm : f ∈ maximalIdeal A) (hf : f ≠ 0) :
    ((completeNormalSituation A f hfm).a = maximalIdeal A ∧
      (∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K) ∧
      ((completeNormalSituation A f hfm).I = Ideal.span {f} ∧ IsSMulRegular A f) ∧
      (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, f ∈ p.asIdeal →
        p.asIdeal ≠ maximalIdeal A →
        (1 : WithBot ℕ∞) <
          (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
            (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
            (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p.asIdeal (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f})) : WithBot ℕ∞) +
            ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p.asIdeal)) ∧
      (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
        ({q : PrimeSpectrum A | p.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal} ∩
          {q : PrimeSpectrum A | f ∈ q.asIdeal}) ≠
          {⟨maximalIdeal A, (maximalIdeal.isMaximal A).isPrime⟩} →
        (3 : WithBot ℕ∞) <
          (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
            (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
            (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) : WithBot ℕ∞) +
            ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p.asIdeal))) ∧
    ∀ F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (idealOnOpen (completeNormalSituation A f hfm)),
      IsFiniteLocallyFreeAdic (idealOnOpen (completeNormalSituation A f hfm)) F →
        ExtendsToX (completeNormalSituation A f hfm)
            (toKerSystem (completeNormalSituation A f hfm) F) ∧
          (completionFunctor (completeNormalSituation A f hfm).U.toScheme
            ((completeNormalSituation A f hfm).Yι.ker.comap
              (completeNormalSituation A f hfm).U.ι)).essImage
            (toKerSystem (completeNormalSituation A f hfm) F)
declarations.comment: assumptions (1), (2), (3), (5) and (6) of Lemma 0DXU hold, and every object of Coh(U, f O_U) with finite locally free terms (a vector bundle on the formal completion of U along U ∩ V(f)) extends to X and is the completion of a coherent O_U-module, by Lemma 0EJ9

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.canonicallyExtends_and_isCompletion_of_principal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DXW].** Let `S` be the standing situation of [Stacks, Tag 0EHC] and let
`(F_n)` be an object of `Coh(U, I𝒪_U)`. Assume

1. `I = (f)` is principal with `f` a nonzerodivisor of `A`,
2. every `F_n` is a finite locally free `𝒪_U/Iⁿ𝒪_U`-module, and
3. `H¹_𝔞(A/fA)` and `H²_𝔞(A/fA)` are finite `A`-modules.

Then `(F_n)` extends canonically to `X = Spec(A)`; and if moreover `A` is `f`-adically complete,
`(F_n)` is the completion of a coherent `𝒪_U`-module.

Hypothesis (2) is used at the stalks, where a finite locally free `𝒪_U/Iⁿ𝒪_U`-module is a finite
free module over the local ring modulo the `n`-th power of the stalk of `I𝒪_U`; that is
`Stacks.Algebraization.HasFiniteFreeStalks`.

The three conditions (a), (b), (c) of the Mittag-Leffler criterion [Stacks, Tag 0EHH] come from
`Stacks.Algebraization.canonicallyExtends_of_principal_shortExactSequences`, whose two
hypotheses are discharged here: the short exact sequences
`0 → F_n → F_{n+1} → F_1 → 0` by
`Stacks.Algebraization.hasPrincipalShortExactSequences_of_nonzerodivisor`, and the finiteness of
`H⁰(U, F₁)` and `H¹(U, F₁)` by
`Stacks.Algebraization.finite_openCohomology_of_hasFiniteFreeStalks`. The second clause follows
from the first along the chain of [Stacks, Tag 0EIL].
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicallyExtends_and_isCompletion_of_principal
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (idealOnOpen S)) {f : S.A}
    (hI : S.I = Ideal.span {f}) (hnzd : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors S.A)
    (hH1 : Module.Finite S.A (specialFibreLocalCohomology S f 1))
    (hH2 : Module.Finite S.A (specialFibreLocalCohomology S f 2))
    (hfree : HasFiniteFreeStalks S F) :
    CanonicallyExtends S F ∧
      (IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) S.A →
        (completionFunctor S.U.toScheme (S.Yι.ker.comap S.U.ι)).essImage
          (kerComapSystem S F))

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.canonicallyExtends_of_principal_shortExactSequences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DXW, first clause.** Let `S` be an algebraization situation whose ideal
`I` is the principal ideal generated by `f ∈ A`, and let `(F_n)` be a coherent `I`-adic system on
the open complement `U`. If the system has the short exact sequences
`0 → F_n → F_{n+1} → F_1 → 0` of the source's proof, and if `H⁰(U, F_1)` and `H¹(U, F_1)` are
finite `A`-modules, then `(F_n)` extends canonically to `X = Spec(A)`.

The three hypotheses (a), (b), (c) of the Mittag-Leffler criterion Stacks 0EHH are proved here:
(b) from the degree-zero half of Stacks 0EHA, (a) from Stacks 0BLC, and (c) by the source's
induction on the short exact sequences.

The source's hypotheses (2) and (3) are replaced by the two consequences its proof uses. Finite
local freeness of `F_n` over `𝒪_U/f^n𝒪_U` and the nonzerodivisor property of `f` are used only
to produce the short exact sequences `0 → F_n → F_{n+1} → F_1 → 0`, which is the hypothesis `h`;
and the finiteness of `H¹_𝔞(A/fA)` and `H²_𝔞(A/fA)` is used only to produce the finiteness of
`H⁰(U, F_1)` and `H¹(U, F_1)`, by Local Cohomology 0BK0 and 0BLT, which are the hypotheses `h0`
and `h1`. Neither derivation is carried out here.

The source's second clause, algebraizability over an `I`-adically complete `A`, is
`Stacks.Algebraization.isCompletionNearClosed_of_principal_shortExactSequences`.

Stacks 0DXW itself, with the source's own hypotheses and both of its clauses, is
`Stacks.Algebraization.canonicallyExtends_and_isCompletion_of_principal`, which derives the two
hypotheses below from them.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicallyExtends_of_principal_shortExactSequences (f : S.A)
    (hI : S.I = Ideal.span {f}) (h : HasPrincipalShortExactSequences S F f)
    (h0 : Module.Finite S.A ((globalSectionsSystem S F).obj (op 0)))
    (h1 : Module.Finite S.A ((openCohomologyFunctor S 1).obj (systemObj S F 0))) :
    CanonicallyExtends S F
declarations.comment: first clause (canonical extension) only; conditions (a), (b), (c) of 0EHH are proved, but hypotheses (2) and (3) of the source are replaced by the consequences its proof draws from them, namely the short exact sequences 0 → Fₙ → F₍ₙ₊₁₎ → F₁ → 0 and the finiteness of H⁰(U, F₁) and H¹(U, F₁)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.canonicallyExtends_and_isCompletion_of_principal_nonzerodivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DXW.** Let `S` be an algebraization situation and let `(F_n)` be a
coherent `I`-adic system on the open complement `U`. Assume

1. `I = (f)` is generated by a nonzerodivisor `f ∈ 𝔞`,
2. every term of the system is finite locally free over the infinitesimal neighbourhood it is
   annihilated by,
3. `H¹_𝔞(A/fA)` and `H²_𝔞(A/fA)` are finite `A`-modules.

Then `(F_n)` extends canonically to `X = Spec(A)`, and if `A` is `I`-adically complete then
`(F_n)` is the completion of a coherent `𝒪_U`-module.

Conditions (1) and (2) give the short exact sequences `0 → F_n → F_{n+1} → F_1 → 0` of the
source's proof (`Stacks.Algebraization.hasPrincipalShortExactSequences_of_locallyFree`), and
all three give the finiteness of `H⁰(U, F_1)` and `H¹(U, F_1)`
(`Stacks.Algebraization.finite_complementCohomologyBase_firstTerm`). The Mittag-Leffler criterion
Stacks 0EHH turns those into the first clause
(`Stacks.Algebraization.canonicallyExtends_of_principal_shortExactSequences`) and the chain of
Stacks 0EIL into the second
(`Stacks.Algebraization.isCompletionNearClosed_of_principal_shortExactSequences`).
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicallyExtends_and_isCompletion_of_principal_nonzerodivisor
    (S : AlgebraizationSituation.{u})
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (idealOnOpen S)) (f : S.A)
    (hI : S.I = Ideal.span {f}) (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors S.A)
    (hfree : IsFiniteLocallyFreeAdic (idealOnOpen S) F)
    (h₁ : Module.Finite S.A (localCohomologyBaseQuotient S f 1))
    (h₂ : Module.Finite S.A (localCohomologyBaseQuotient S f 2)) :
    CanonicallyExtends S F ∧
      (IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) S.A →
        (completionFunctor S.U.toScheme (S.Yι.ker.comap S.U.ι)).essImage (kerComapSystem S F))
declarations.comment: both clauses under the source's own conditions (1), (2) and (3): for I = (f) generated by a nonzerodivisor, with every term finite locally free over the infinitesimal neighbourhood it is annihilated by, and with H¹_𝔞(A/fA) and H²_𝔞(A/fA) finite, the system extends canonically to X, and over an I-adically complete A it is the completion of a coherent O_U-module

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.finiteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful_puncturedSpectrum_of_three_le_ringKrullDim
declarations.doc:
**Restriction of finite étale covers from the neighbourhoods of `U₀` in `U` is fully
faithful.**  Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring, `f ∈ A`, `X = Spec A`, `X₀ = V(f)`,
`U = X ∖ {𝔪}` and `U₀ = U ∩ V(f)`.  Assume `A` has a dualizing complex, is `f`-adically complete,
and that every irreducible component of `X` not contained in `X₀` has dimension at least `3` —
that is, `dim (A/𝔭) ≥ 3` for every minimal prime `𝔭` of `A` with `f ∉ 𝔭`.  Then the restriction
functor `colim_{U₀ ⊆ U' ⊆ U open} FÉt_{U'} ⟶ FÉt_{U₀}` is fully faithful.

The dimension hypothesis is a bound at the minimal primes, whereas the completion theorem behind
full faithfulness needs one at the associated primes; so `A` is first replaced by its reduction,
where the associated primes are the minimal primes.  The punctured spectrum of the reduction is a
thickening of `U` carrying its closed subscheme cut out by the image of `f` to `U₀`, and full
faithfulness of restriction is insensitive to such a thickening; a dualizing complex, `f`-adic
completeness and the dimension bound all survive the passage to the reduction.

The dualizing complex is asked for in an arbitrary model of the derived category of `A`-modules,
and moved to the standard model — the one the completion results are stated in — by
`Stacks.Dualizing.exists_isDualizingComplex_iff_of_models`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful_puncturedSpectrum_of_three_le_ringKrullDim (A : Type u)
    [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} A)]
    (f : A)
    (hdual : ∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K)
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) A)
    (hdim : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, IsMinimalPrime p.asIdeal → f ∉ p.asIdeal →
      (3 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p.asIdeal)) :
    FiniteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful (complementZeroLocus A (maximalIdeal A) : Scheme.{u})
      (idealSheafNearVanishing A (Ideal.span {f}) (maximalIdeal A))
declarations.comment: the whole statement, under the source's hypotheses only: a dualizing complex and f-adic completeness, and dimension at least three for every irreducible component of X not contained in the zero locus of f

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.finiteEtaleColimitEquivalence_puncturedSpectrum_of_dualizing
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0DXY].** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0BLF] — `(A, 𝔪)` a Noetherian local ring,
`f ∈ 𝔪`, `U = Spec(A) ∖ {𝔪}` the punctured spectrum of `A` and `U₀ = U ∩ V(f)` the punctured
spectrum of `A/fA`, as the closed subscheme of `U` cut out by `f 𝒪_U` — assume

1. `A` has a dualizing complex and is `f`-adically complete, and
2. one of
   * (a) `A_f` is `(S₂)` and `dim(A/𝔭) ≥ 4` for every minimal prime `𝔭` of `A` with `f ∉ 𝔭`, or
   * (b) `depth(A_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > 3` for every prime `𝔭 ∉ V(f)` with `V(𝔭) ∩ V(f) ≠ {𝔪}`.

Then the restriction functor `colim_{U₀ ⊆ U' ⊆ U open} FÉt_{U'} ⟶ FÉt_{U₀}` is an equivalence.

The colimit is directed, so the functor is an equivalence exactly when the two conjuncts below
hold. The first is that it is fully faithful, in the form
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.FiniteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful`: morphisms between restrictions to `U₀`
come from a smaller neighbourhood, and morphisms agreeing on `U₀` agree on a smaller
neighbourhood. The second is that it is essentially surjective: every finite étale cover of `U₀`
is the restriction of a finite étale cover of some open `U'` with `U₀ ⊆ U' ⊆ U`.

As in the source, this is [Stacks, Tag 0EK1] for the closed subscheme `U₀` of `U`, with the
completion equivalence of [Stacks, Tag 0EKY] as input. Full faithfulness is [Stacks, Tag 0ELA]
applied to
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.completionFullyFaithfulComplete_puncturedSpectrum_of_dualizing`, and the
essential image is the algebraization step of [Stacks, Tag 0EK1] fed by that same input together
with
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.exists_finiteLocallyFree_completion_puncturedSpectrum_of_dualizing`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteEtaleColimitEquivalence_puncturedSpectrum_of_dualizing
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} A)] (hf : f ∈ maximalIdeal A)
    (hdual : ∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K)
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) A)
    (hcond :
      (PropertySkRing (Localization.Away f) 2 ∧
          ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, IsMinimalPrime p.asIdeal → f ∉ p.asIdeal →
            (4 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p.asIdeal)) ∨
        (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
          ({q : PrimeSpectrum A | p.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal} ∩
            {q : PrimeSpectrum A | f ∈ q.asIdeal}) ≠
            {⟨maximalIdeal A, (maximalIdeal.isMaximal A).isPrime⟩} →
          (3 : WithBot ℕ∞) <
            (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
              (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
              (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) : WithBot ℕ∞) +
              ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p.asIdeal))) :
    FiniteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful (complementZeroLocus A (maximalIdeal A) : Scheme)
        (idealSheafNearVanishing A (Ideal.span {f}) (maximalIdeal A)) ∧
      ∀ C : FiniteEtaleOver
        (idealSheafNearVanishing A (Ideal.span {f}) (maximalIdeal A)).subscheme,
      ∃ (W : Neighborhood (complementZeroLocus A (maximalIdeal A) : Scheme)
          (idealSheafNearVanishing A (Ideal.span {f}) (maximalIdeal A)))
        (V : FiniteEtaleOver (Neighborhood.open _ _ W).toScheme),
        Nonempty ((finiteEtaleBaseChange (Neighborhood.toSchemeHom _ _ W)).obj V ≅ C)
declarations.comment: the restriction functor colim_{U₀ ⊆ U' ⊆ U} FÉt_{U'} → FÉt_{U₀} is an equivalence: fully faithful, and every finite étale cover of U₀ extends to a neighbourhood

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocalLefschetzSituation.hasPurity_quotientRing_of_dualizing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DXZ.**  Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring and let `f ∈ 𝔪`.
Write `X = Spec A`.  Assume

1. `A` has a dualizing complex and is `f`-adically complete,
2. one of
   * (a) `A_f` satisfies Serre's condition `(S₂)` and every irreducible component of `X` not
     contained in `V(f)` has dimension at least `4`, or
   * (b) `depth(A_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > 3` whenever `𝔭 ∉ V(f)` and `V(𝔭) ∩ V(f) ≠ {𝔪}`,
3. purity holds for `(A_f)_𝔭` for every maximal ideal `𝔭 ⊂ A_f`, and
4. purity holds for `A`.

Then purity holds for `A / fA`.

The source's argument is followed.  A finite étale cover of the punctured spectrum `U₀` of
`A / fA` is, by the essential surjectivity of `FÉt_U ⥤ FÉt_{U₀}` under (1)–(3), the restriction
of a finite étale cover of the punctured spectrum `U` of `A`; hypothesis (4) extends the latter
over `X`; and the restriction of that extension to `Spec (A / fA)` is the desired extension of
the original cover.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPurity_quotientRing_of_dualizing [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} S.A)]
    (hdual : ∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S.A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K)
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {S.f}) S.A)
    (hcond :
      (PropertySkRing (Localization.Away S.f) 2 ∧
          ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S.A, IsMinimalPrime p.asIdeal → S.f ∉ p.asIdeal →
            (4 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim (S.A ⧸ p.asIdeal)) ∨
        (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S.A, S.f ∉ p.asIdeal →
          ({q : PrimeSpectrum S.A | p.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal} ∩
            {q : PrimeSpectrum S.A | S.f ∈ q.asIdeal}) ≠
            {⟨maximalIdeal S.A, (maximalIdeal.isMaximal S.A).isPrime⟩} →
          (3 : WithBot ℕ∞) <
            (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
              (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
              (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) : WithBot ℕ∞) +
              ringKrullDim (S.A ⧸ p.asIdeal)))
    (haway : ∀ (p : Ideal (Localization.Away S.f)) [p.IsMaximal],
      HasPurity (Localization.AtPrime p))
    (hpurity : HasPurity S.A) :
    HasPurity S.quotientRing
declarations.comment: purity for A/fA under the tag's four hypotheses; nothing beyond them is assumed

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.exists_infinitesimalAutomorphismGroupMulEquivDerivation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DY3.** The infinitesimal automorphisms of the deformation category of a
commutative `k`-algebra `P` are the `k`-derivations of `P` into itself.

The statement also records the coordinates in which this holds: for any point `xε` of the
deformation category over the dual numbers and any lift `i` of the constant inclusion, there
is a ring isomorphism `c` of the flat algebra of `xε` with `P[ε]` compatible with the
reduction to `P` and carrying the lift to the constant inclusion, and the derivation attached
to an infinitesimal automorphism is the `ε`-coefficient of its value on a constant. The
scalar action of `k` on the derivations is reflected by the existence of a unique rescaled
infinitesimal automorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_infinitesimalAutomorphismGroupMulEquivDerivation
    {Λ : Type u} {k P : Type w} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k]
    [CommRing P] [Algebra k P] :
    ∃ hp : IsPredeformationCategory (ringDeformationProjection Λ k P),
      ∀ {Aε : ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, w, w} Λ k}
        {x₀ : (ringDeformationProjection Λ k P).Fiber (residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k)}
        {xε : (ringDeformationProjection Λ k P).Fiber Aε}
        (g : residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k ⟶ Aε)
        (e : Aε ⟶ residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k)
        (hpair : IsCanonicalDualNumberPair g e)
        (i : x₀.1 ⟶ xε.1) (hi : (ringDeformationProjection Λ k P).IsHomLift g i),
        ∃ c : xε.1.left.fiber ≃+* DualNumber P,
          (∀ y : xε.1.left.fiber, (c y).fst = xε.1.hom.map y) ∧
          (∀ y : x₀.1.left.fiber,
            c (i.left.map y) = TrivSqZeroExt.inl (x₀.1.hom.map y)) ∧
          ∃ E : infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi ≃*
            Multiplicative (Derivation k P P),
            (∀ (a : infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi) (y : P),
              (c (a.val.asIso.hom.val.left.map (c.symm (TrivSqZeroExt.inl y)))).snd =
                (Multiplicative.toAdd (E a)) y) ∧
            (∀ (s : k) (a : infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi),
              ∃! b : infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi,
                ∀ y : P,
                  (c (b.val.asIso.hom.val.left.map (c.symm (TrivSqZeroExt.inl y)))).snd =
                    s • (c (a.val.asIso.hom.val.left.map
                      (c.symm (TrivSqZeroExt.inl y)))).snd)
declarations.comment: infinitesimal automorphisms

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.ringDeformationTangentSpaceLinearEquivExtOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DY3, the tangent space.** Let `k` be a field and `P` a `k`-algebra. The tangent
space of the deformation category of `P` of Stacks 0DY1, with the canonical `k`-vector-space
structure of Stacks 06IH, is `Ext¹_P(NL_{P/k}, P)`:

`T𝓓_P = Ext¹_P(NL_{P/k}, P)`.

The identification is the family of extension classes
`Deformation.Examples.tangentExtClass`, which sends an isomorphism class of first-order flat
deformations of `P` over `k ⊕ V` to the class of **Stacks 0GPT** of the square-zero extension
of `P` by `P ⊗[k] V` it determines. That family is natural in `V`, injective by
`Deformation.Examples.tangentExtClass_injective` and surjective by
`Deformation.Examples.surjective_tangentExtClass`, so
`Deformation.tangentSpaceLinearEquivOfNaturalBijection` turns it into a `k`-linear equivalence
at `V = k`, and `Deformation.Examples.naiveCotangentExtOneTensorFunctorObjRankOne` replaces the
coefficients `P ⊗[k] k` by `P`.

The infinitesimal-automorphism clause `Inf(𝓓_P) = Der_k(P, P)` of the same tag is
`Deformation.Examples.exists_infinitesimalAutomorphismGroupMulEquivDerivation`; the two
declarations together cover the tag.
declarations.statement:
public def ringDeformationTangentSpaceLinearEquivExtOne :
    letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory (ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k P).p) :=
      ⟨(ringDeformationCategory_isDeformationCategory P).predeformation⟩
    letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2 (Functor.Elements.π
      (isomorphismClasses (ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k P)
        isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection))) :=
      ⟨schlessingerConditionS2_ringDeformation Λ k P⟩
    artinianTangentSpace Λ k
        (isomorphismClasses (ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k P)
          isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection)
      ≃ₗ[k] naiveCotangentExtOne k P P
declarations.comment: the tangent space

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.ringDeformationTangentSpaceLinearEquivExtOne_apply
declarations.doc:
**The identification of Stacks 0DY3 is the classification of Stacks 0GPT.** On the
isomorphism class of a point of the fibre over the square-zero extension `k ⊕ k` of
Stacks 06IB, the tangent-space identification is the class in `Ext¹_P(NL_{P/k}, P ⊗[k] k)` of
the square-zero extension of `P` the point determines, read through `P ⊗[k] k ≅ P`.

This pins the identification down: no content is left in the transport of the vector-space
structure of Stacks 06IH.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringDeformationTangentSpaceLinearEquivExtOne_apply
    (z : (associatedTangentSpaceSetFunctor (ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k P)
      isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection).obj (FGModuleCat.of k k)) :
    letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory (ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k P).p) :=
      ⟨(ringDeformationCategory_isDeformationCategory P).predeformation⟩
    letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2 (Functor.Elements.π
      (isomorphismClasses (ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k P)
        isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection))) :=
      ⟨schlessingerConditionS2_ringDeformation Λ k P⟩
    ringDeformationTangentSpaceLinearEquivExtOne Λ k P z
      = naiveCotangentExtOneTensorFunctorObjRankOne k P
        (tangentExtClass (FGModuleCat.of k k) z)
declarations.comment: the tangent space

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.finiteDimensional_naiveCotangentExtOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DY4(2)** for the Ext module. Let `k` be a field and `P` a `k`-algebra of finite
type which is smooth over `k` outside a finite set of primes. Then the first Ext module
`Ext¹_P(NL_{P/k}, P)` of the naive cotangent complex is finite-dimensional over `k`, for any
`k`-module structure on it compatible with the `P`-action. Through the identification of that
Ext module with the tangent space `T𝓓_P` of the deformation category of `P`, which is Tag
0DY3, this is the finite-dimensionality of the tangent space.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_naiveCotangentExtOne (k P : Type w) [Field k] [CommRing P]
    [Algebra k P] [Algebra.FiniteType k P]
    [Module k (Stacks.Deformation.naiveCotangentExtOne k P P)]
    [IsScalarTower k P (Stacks.Deformation.naiveCotangentExtOne k P P)]
    (hfinite : {q : PrimeSpectrum P | ¬ Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q.asIdeal}.Finite) :
    FiniteDimensional k (Stacks.Deformation.naiveCotangentExtOne k P P)
declarations.comment: part (2) for the Ext group

declarations.name: Algebra.finiteDimensional_derivation_iff_ringKrullDim_le_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DY4(1).** For a `k`-algebra `P` of finite type over a field, the `k`-derivations
of `P` into itself are a finite-dimensional `k`-vector space if and only if `P` has Krull
dimension at most zero. Through Tag 0DY3 this is the finite-dimensionality criterion for the
infinitesimal automorphisms of the deformation category of `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_derivation_iff_ringKrullDim_le_zero
    (k : Type u) (P : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing P] [Algebra k P]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k P] :
    FiniteDimensional k (Derivation k P P) ↔ ringKrullDim P ≤ 0
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.hypersurface_finiteDimensional_infinitesimalAutomorphisms_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DY5(1).** Let `k` be a field, `n` a number of variables and `f` a nonzero formal
power series in `k[[x_1, …, x_n]]` lying in the square of the ideal generated by the variables,
and let `P = k[[x_1, …, x_n]]/(f)`. At any dual-number lift of any object of the deformation
category of `P` over the residue field, the infinitesimal automorphism group carries a
`k`-vector-space structure whose addition is composition and which is carried by the
identification of Tag 0DY3 to the `k`-structure of `Derivation k P P`, and that vector space is
finite-dimensional if and only if `n = 1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hypersurface_finiteDimensional_infinitesimalAutomorphisms_iff
    {Λ : Type u} {k : Type w} [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k]
    (n : ℕ) (f : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k) (hf : f ≠ 0)
    (hord : f ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range
      (MvPowerSeries.X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k))) ^ 2) :
    let P := MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k ⧸ Ideal.span {f}
    let hp := (ringDeformationCategory_isDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) (k := k) P).predeformation
    ∀ {Aε : ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, w, w} Λ k}
      {x₀ : (ringDeformationProjection Λ k P).Fiber (residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k)}
      {xε : (ringDeformationProjection Λ k P).Fiber Aε}
      (g : residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k ⟶ Aε)
      (e : Aε ⟶ residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k)
      (hpair : IsCanonicalDualNumberPair g e)
      (i : x₀.1 ⟶ xε.1) (hi : (ringDeformationProjection Λ k P).IsHomLift g i),
      let G := infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup hp g e hpair i hi
      ∃ hA : AddCommGroup G,
        letI := hA
        ∃ hM : Module k G,
          letI := hM
          (∀ a b : G, a + b = a * b) ∧
          (∃ E : G ≃* Multiplicative (Derivation k P P), ∀ (s : k) (a : G),
            Multiplicative.toAdd (E (s • a)) = s • Multiplicative.toAdd (E a)) ∧
          (FiniteDimensional k G ↔ n = 1)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.hypersurface_finiteDimensional_tangentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DY5(2).** Let `k` be a field, `f` a nonzero formal power series in
`k[[x_1, …, x_n]]` lying in the square of the ideal generated by the variables, and
`P = k[[x_1, …, x_n]]/(f)` the formal hypersurface it cuts out. If the Jacobian ideal
`(f, ∂f/∂x_1, …, ∂f/∂x_n)` has radical the ideal generated by the variables, then the tangent
space `T𝓓_P` of the deformation category of `P` of Stacks 0DY1 — with the canonical
`k`-vector-space structure of Stacks 06IH — is finite dimensional over `k`.

The tangent space is `Ext¹_P(NL_{P/k}, P)` by the tangent-space clause of Stacks 0DY3, that
group is the conormal cokernel of the canonical presentation of `P` by Stacks 0GPU, and the
cokernel is finite dimensional by
`Deformation.Examples.finiteDimensional_conormalCokernel_hypersurface`. The source's
hypotheses that `f` is nonzero and lies in the square of the ideal of the variables are not
used, so the statement omits them.
declarations.statement:
theorem hypersurface_finiteDimensional_tangentSpace {Λ : Type u} [CommRing Λ] [Algebra Λ k]
    (hjac : (Ideal.span ({f} ∪ Set.range
      (fun i : Fin n ↦ MvPowerSeries.pderiv (R := k) i f))).radical =
      Ideal.span (Set.range (MvPowerSeries.X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k))) :
    letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory
        (ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k (Hypersurface n f)).p) :=
      ⟨(ringDeformationCategory_isDeformationCategory (Hypersurface n f)).predeformation⟩
    letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2 (Functor.Elements.π
      (isomorphismClasses (ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k (Hypersurface n f))
        isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection))) :=
      ⟨schlessingerConditionS2_ringDeformation Λ k (Hypersurface n f)⟩
    FiniteDimensional k (artinianTangentSpace Λ k
      (isomorphismClasses (ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k (Hypersurface n f))
        isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection))
declarations.comment: part (2)
