declarations.doc: Deformations of a fixed scheme over `k` form a category.
declarations.statement:
instance instCategory (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    Category (SchemeDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X)
declarations.comment: scheme_deformation_category

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.schemeDeformationCategoryProjection
declarations.doc: The canonical projection from the category of deformations of a scheme to `𝒞_Λ`.
declarations.statement:
def schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    SchemeDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X ⥤ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, u, u} Λ k
declarations.comment: scheme_deformation_category

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.schemeDeformationCategoryProjection_cofiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**The deformation category of a scheme is cofibered in groupoids.** A deformation can be
base changed along any morphism of `𝒞_Λ`
(`Deformation.Examples.baseChangeDeformation`), and an arrow out of a deformation descends
uniquely through that base change, because its component on total spaces is determined by the
universal property of the fibre product.

This is the lower half of the cofibered condition that
`Deformation.full_of_exists_lift_of_isHomLift_id` asks of the source-forgetful functor of
[Stacks, Tag 0E3X].
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeDeformationCategoryProjection_cofiberedInGroupoids
    (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    IsCofiberedInGroupoids (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X)
declarations.comment: cofibred_projection, for the deformation category of a scheme

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.isFirstOrderThickening_specialMap
declarations.doc:
**The special-fibre immersion of a first-order deformation of a scheme is a first-order
thickening.** It is a closed immersion by
`Deformation.Examples.deformationSpecialMap_isClosedImmersion`, being a base change of the
closed point, and its ideal sheaf is square-zero because the maximal ideal of the base object
is, by `Deformation.Examples.maximalIdeal_sq_eq_bot_of_dualNumberEquiv`.

This is the hypothesis `i.ker ^ 2 = ⊥` of [Stacks Project, Tag 0CK2], discharged for the
deformations over the dual numbers to which [Stacks Project, Tag 0E3V] applies it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFirstOrderThickening_specialMap {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
    (P : SchemeDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X)
    (coordinate : P.base ≃ₐ[Λ] DualNumber k) :
    Stacks.Thickenings.IsFirstOrderThickening P.specialMap
declarations.comment: the special-fibre immersion of a deformation over the dual numbers is a first-order thickening

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.isDeformationCategory_schemeDeformationCategoryProjection
declarations.doc:
The deformation category of a fixed scheme `X` over the residue field is a deformation
category: a predeformation category satisfying (RS).
declarations.statement:
theorem isDeformationCategory_schemeDeformationCategoryProjection
    (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    IsDeformationCategory.{u, u, u}
      (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection.{u} (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X)
declarations.comment: the clause that the deformation category of a fixed scheme over k is a deformation category, unconditionally; condition (RS) for the category of all flat scheme families of Example 0DY7 is Deformation.Examples.satisfiesRS_flatSchemeFamilyProjection

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.satisfiesRS_flatSchemeFamilyProjection
declarations.doc:
The category of flat families of schemes over `𝒞_Λ` satisfies the Rim-Schlessinger condition
(RS).
declarations.statement:
theorem satisfiesRS_flatSchemeFamilyProjection :
    SatisfiesRS (flatSchemeFamilyProjection.{u, v, w} (Λ := Λ) (k := k))
declarations.comment: condition (RS) for the category of flat scheme families of Example 0DY7, unconditionally. The two gluing clauses it rests on are the last assertion of Tag 07RV and the equivalence assertion of the closing paragraph of Tag 07RX, both proved in this repository: Stacks.Pushout.isPullback_of_isPushout_glued and Stacks.Pushout.isPushout_restrictions_of_flat. The pushout of spectra, the existence of the glued family, its flatness and both halves of the universal property are proved as well. The clause that the deformation category of a fixed scheme over k is a deformation category is Deformation.Examples.isDeformationCategory_schemeDeformationCategoryProjection

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.infinitesimalAutomorphismGroupTrivialDeformationChain
declarations.doc:
**The first display of [Stacks Project, Tag 0DY9].** For a scheme `X` over the field `k`,

`Inf(𝓓_X) = Ext⁰_{𝒪_X}(NL_{X/k}, 𝒪_X) = Hom_{𝒪_X}(Ω_{X/k}, 𝒪_X) = Der_k(𝒪_X, 𝒪_X)`,

given as the three identifications of those four groups.

`Inf(𝓓_X)` is the library's infinitesimal automorphism group
`Deformation.infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup` of the deformation category of `X`, which is a
predeformation category by [Stacks Project, Tag 0DY8], formed at its canonical data: the point
`X` over `k`, its pushforward the trivial deformation `X ×_{Spec k} Spec k[ε]`, and the pair
`k → k[ε] → k`. That is, the automorphisms of the trivial deformation that are the identity
modulo `ε`.

* The first identification is an isomorphism of **groups**: composition of such automorphisms
  corresponds to addition of derivations
  (`Deformation.Examples.infinitesimalAutomorphismGroupMulEquivDerivations`, at the coordinate
  `Deformation.Examples.artinianDualNumbersCoordinate` of the dual-number object).
* The second is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.naiveCotangentExtZeroAddEquiv`: `Ext⁰` out of the naive
  cotangent complex `NL_{X/k}` of the structure morphism of `X` is the `Hom` out of its degree `0`
  cohomology sheaf, which is `Ω_{X/k}` by [Stacks Project, Tag 0D0J].
* The third is `k`-linear: `Hom_{𝒪_X}(Ω_{X/k}, 𝒪_X)` carries the `k`-structure of sheaves of
  modules on a scheme over `k` (`AlgebraicGeometry.modulesLinear`), and the derivations of `𝒪_X`
  over `k` with values in `𝒪_X` the one of
  `Deformation.Examples.schemeMorphismDerivationsModule`; it is corepresentability of relative
  derivations (`Deformation.Examples.schemeMorphismDerivationsLinearEquiv`) read through the
  comparison `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.cotangentSheafIso` of the two constructions of the
  sheaf of relative differentials.

`Der_k(𝒪_X, 𝒪_X)` is written `schemeMorphismDerivations (𝟙 X.left) X.hom`, the derivations of
`𝒪_X` over `k` with values in the pushforward of `𝒪_X` along the identity of `X`, which is `𝒪_X`
itself (`Deformation.Examples.schemeMorphismPushforwardStructureSheaf_id`, by `rfl`).
declarations.statement:
def infinitesimalAutomorphismGroupTrivialDeformationChain (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
    (infinitesimalAutomorphismGroup
        (isDeformationCategory_schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) X).predeformation
        (x₀ := residueTrivialFiberObj X) (xε := dualNumbersTrivialFiberObj X)
        dualNumbersInclusion.{u, u, u}
        (residueMorphism.{u, u, u} (artinianDualNumbers.{u, u, u} Λ k))
        isCanonicalDualNumberPair_dualNumbersInclusion.{u, u, u}
        (dualNumbersTrivialDeformationHom X) (dualNumbersTrivialDeformationHom_isHomLift X)
        ≃* Multiplicative (schemeMorphismDerivations (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (𝟙 X.left) X.hom))
      × (Scheme.naiveCotangentExt X.hom (structureSheafModules X.left) 0
          ≃+ (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials X.hom ⟶ structureSheafModules X.left))
      × (letI : Module k (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials X.hom ⟶ structureSheafModules X.left) :=
            (modulesLinear k (Over.mk X.hom)).homModule _ _;
          letI := schemeMorphismDerivationsModule (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (𝟙 X.left) X.hom
            (structureSheafModules X.left);
          ((Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials X.hom ⟶ structureSheafModules X.left) ≃ₗ[k]
            schemeMorphismDerivations (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (𝟙 X.left) X.hom))
declarations.comment: first display: for a scheme X over the field k, Inf(Def_X) = Ext^0(NL_{X/k}, O_X) = Hom(Omega_{X/k}, O_X) = Der_k(O_X, O_X), as three identifications: Inf(Def_X) is the library's infinitesimal automorphism group of the deformation category of X at the trivial deformation X x_k Spec k[eps], and is isomorphic as a group to Der_k(O_X, O_X); Ext^0 out of the naive cotangent complex is additively Hom(Omega_{X/k}, O_X); and Hom(Omega_{X/k}, O_X) is k-linearly Der_k(O_X, O_X). The second display, T Def_X = Ext^1(NL_{X/k}, O_X), is registered separately

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.schemeTangentSpaceLinearEquivExt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0DY9, second display.** For a scheme `X` over the field `k`,

`T𝓓_X = Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(NL_{X/k}, 𝒪_X)`

as `k`-vector spaces.

`T𝓓_X` is the tangent space of the deformation category of `X` of [Stacks Project, Tag 0DY7]:
the value at the dual numbers `k[ε]` of its functor of isomorphism classes
([Stacks Project, Tag 06SR]), the set of isomorphism classes of flat deformations of `X` over
`k[ε]`, with the canonical `k`-vector space structure of [Stacks Project, Tag 06IH].
`Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(NL_{X/k}, 𝒪_X)` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.naiveCotangentExt` of the structure
morphism of `X` with coefficients `𝒪_X` in degree `1`, a `k`-vector space through the `k`-linear
structure of `𝒪_X`-modules.

The identification is the source's proof: a flat deformation of `X` over `k[V] = k ⊕ V` is a
solution of the deformation problem of [Stacks Project, Tag 08U7] for `Spec k ⊂ Spec k[V]` with
ideal `f^*𝒥 = 𝒪_X ⊗_k V`, and its class is the difference class of
[Stacks Project, Tag 08UC] against the trivial deformation `X ×_k Spec k[V]`
(`Deformation.Examples.tangentExtClassAt`). These classes are bijective
(`Deformation.Examples.bijective_tangentExtClassAt`) and natural in `V`
(`Deformation.Examples.tangentExtClassAt_naturality`), so they are `k`-linear for the structure of
Tag 06IH at `V = k`, where `𝒪_X ⊗_k k = 𝒪_X`. The trivial deformation goes to `0`
(`Deformation.Examples.schemeTangentSpaceLinearEquivExt_trivial`) and the class of a deformation
is its difference class (`Deformation.Examples.schemeTangentSpaceLinearEquivExt_classOf`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def schemeTangentSpaceLinearEquivExt :
    letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory (schemeDeformationBased (Λ := Λ) X).p) :=
      ⟨(isDeformationCategory_schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) X).predeformation⟩
    letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2 (Functor.Elements.π
      (isomorphismClasses (schemeDeformationBased (Λ := Λ) X) (schemeDeformation_cofibered X)))) :=
      ⟨schlessingerConditionS2_schemeDeformation X⟩
    letI := schemeTangentExtModule X (structureSheafModules X.left)
    schemeTangentSpace (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X ≃ₗ[k]
      Scheme.naiveCotangentExt X.hom (structureSheafModules X.left) 1
declarations.comment: second display: for a scheme X over the field k, T Def_X = Ext^1(NL_{X/k}, O_X) as k-vector spaces, from the tangent space of the deformation category of X (isomorphism classes of flat deformations of X over k[eps], with the canonical vector space structure of 06IH) onto Ext^1_{O_X}(NL_{X/k}, O_X); a deformation goes to its 08UC difference class with the trivial deformation X x_k Spec k[eps], which goes to 0. The first display, Inf(Def_X) = Ext^0(NL_{X/k}, O_X) = Der_k(O_X, O_X), is registered separately

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.finiteDimensional_schemeTangentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYA, the tangent space.** For a scheme `X` proper over the field `k`, the tangent
space `T𝓓_X` of its deformation category ([Stacks Project, Tag 0DY7]) — the isomorphism classes
of flat deformations of `X` over `k[ε]`, with the canonical vector-space structure of
[Stacks Project, Tag 06IH] — is finite dimensional over `k`.

By [Stacks Project, Tag 0DY9] it is `Ext¹_{𝒪_X}(NL_{X/k}, 𝒪_X)`
(`Deformation.Examples.schemeTangentSpaceLinearEquivExtRankOne` and
`Deformation.Examples.schemeTangentExtRankOneLinearEquiv`, the identification of
`Deformation.Examples.schemeTangentSpaceLinearEquivExt` before the change of model of the
derived category); `NL_{X/k}` is in `D^-_Coh(𝒪_X)` by [Stacks Project, Tag 0D0K]
(`derivedCategoryBMinus_naiveCotangentComplex`) and `𝒪_X` in `D^+_Coh(𝒪_X)`, so the `Ext` group
is finite dimensional by [Stacks Project, Tag 0D0D].
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_schemeTangentSpace [IsProper X.hom] :
    letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory (schemeDeformationBased (Λ := Λ) X).p) :=
      ⟨(isDeformationCategory_schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) X).predeformation⟩
    letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2 (Functor.Elements.π
      (isomorphismClasses (schemeDeformationBased (Λ := Λ) X) (schemeDeformation_cofibered X)))) :=
      ⟨schlessingerConditionS2_schemeDeformation X⟩
    FiniteDimensional k (schemeTangentSpace (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X)
declarations.comment: the tangent space clause: for X proper over k, T Def_X (isomorphism classes of flat deformations of X over k[eps], with the canonical vector space structure of 06IH) is finite dimensional over k

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.finiteDimensional_localizedAutomorphismFunctorTangent_schemeDeformation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYA, the infinitesimal automorphisms.** For a scheme `X` proper over the field `k`,
the `k`-vector space `Inf(𝓓_X)` of infinitesimal automorphisms of its deformation category
([Stacks Project, Tag 0DY7]) is finite dimensional. `Inf(𝓓_X)` is the tangent space at the
identity of the automorphism functor of a point `x₀` of the deformation category, with the
vector-space structure of [Stacks Project, Tag 06JV] (addition is composition, the scalar action
is transport along `ε ↦ cε`); this holds at every point `x₀` and every choice `P` of
pushforwards, in particular at the trivial deformation `X` over `k`.

The proof is the source's: `Inf(𝓓_X)` embeds `k`-linearly in `Der_k(𝒪_X, 𝒪_X)`
(`infinitesimalAutomorphismDerivationLinearMap`, injective by
`injective_infinitesimalAutomorphismDerivationLinearMap`), the identification of
[Stacks Project, Tag 0DY9], and `Der_k(𝒪_X, 𝒪_X) = Hom_{𝒪_X}(Ω_{X/k}, 𝒪_X)` is finite
dimensional by [Stacks Project, Tag 0D0D].
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_localizedAutomorphismFunctorTangent_schemeDeformation [IsProper X.hom]
    {x₀ : SchemeDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X}
    (P : ChosenPushforwardsAt (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X) x₀) :
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup P
      (isDeformationCategory_schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) X).satisfiesRS
    letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule P
      (isDeformationCategory_schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) X).satisfiesRS
    FiniteDimensional k (localizedAutomorphismFunctorTangent P)
declarations.comment: the infinitesimal automorphism clause: for X proper over k, Inf(Def_X) is finite dimensional over k, with the vector space structure of 06JV, at every point of the deformation category and every choice of pushforwards

declarations.name: IsAdicComplete.of_quotient
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian ring and let `I`, `J` be ideals of `A`. If `A` is `I`-adically
complete and `A/I` is `J`-adically complete, then `A` is `J`-adically complete.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsAdicComplete.of_quotient {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I J : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A] (hJ : IsAdicComplete J (A ⧸ I)) :
    IsAdicComplete J A
declarations.comment:
The hypothesis on `A/I` is stated along the ideal `J` of the base ring `A`,
Mathlib's normal form via `IsAdicComplete.map_algebraMap_iff`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: henselianPair_iff_of_le
declarations.doc:
For nested ideals `I ⊆ J`, the pair `(A, J)` is henselian if and only if `(A, I)` and
the induced pair `(A / I, J / I)` are henselian.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselianPair_iff_of_le {A : Type w} [CommRing A] {I J : Ideal A} (hIJ : I ≤ J) :
    (HenselianPair A I ∧
      HenselianPair (A ⧸ I) (J.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) ↔
      HenselianPair A J

declarations.name: henselization_tensorProduct_bijective_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
Henselization commutes with integral base change. For an integral map of pairs
`(A, I) → (B, J)` for which `J` and `IB` have the same vanishing locus, the canonical map
`Aʰ ⊗[A] B → Bʰ` induced by the map of henselizations is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselization_tensorProduct_bijective_of_isIntegral
    (A Ah : Type u) (B Bh : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing Ah] [CommRing Bh]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A Ah] [Algebra B Bh] [Algebra A Bh] [IsScalarTower A B Bh]
    [Algebra.IsIntegral A B] (I : Ideal A) (J : Ideal B)
    (hmap : I ≤ J.comap (algebraMap A B))
    (hzero : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set B) =
      PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I.map (algebraMap A B) : Set B))
    (hAh : HenselianPair Ah (I.map (algebraMap A Ah)))
    (hBh : HenselianPair Bh (J.map (algebraMap B Bh)))
    (hAh_univ : ∀ (C : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing C) (K : Ideal C),
      HenselianPair C K →
        ∀ f : A →+* C, I ≤ K.comap f →
          ∃! g : Ah →+* C,
            g.comp (algebraMap A Ah) = f ∧ I.map (algebraMap A Ah) ≤ K.comap g)
    (hBh_univ : ∀ (C : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing C) (K : Ideal C),
      HenselianPair C K →
        ∀ f : B →+* C, J ≤ K.comap f →
          ∃! g : Bh →+* C,
            g.comp (algebraMap B Bh) = f ∧ J.map (algebraMap B Bh) ≤ K.comap g)
    (g : Ah →ₐ[A] Bh)
    (hg : I.map (algebraMap A Ah) ≤ (J.map (algebraMap B Bh)).comap g) :
    Function.Bijective
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift g (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A B Bh)
        (fun _ _ ↦ Commute.all _ _))

declarations.name: formallySmooth_adic_iff_lifts_local_squareZero
declarations.doc:
A local homomorphism of local rings is formally smooth for the adic
topologies if and only if it lifts through all residually trivial square-zero quotients whose
source has nilpotent maximal ideal. If the target is Noetherian, testing residually trivial
small extensions suffices.
declarations.statement:
public theorem formallySmooth_adic_iff_lifts_local_squareZero
    {R : Type v} {S : Type w} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing S] (φ : R →+* S) [IsLocalHom φ] :
    (FormallySmoothAdic.{u, v, w} φ ↔ LiftsLocalSquareZero.{u, v, w} φ) ∧
      (IsNoetherianRing S →
        (FormallySmoothAdic.{u, v, w} φ ↔ LiftsLocalSmallExtension.{u, v, w} φ))

declarations.name: exact_jacobiZariski_residueField_of_formallySmoothNAdic
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings which is formally smooth for
the maximal-ideal-adic topology on `B`, and let `K` be the residue field of `B`.  Then the
canonical Jacobi–Zariski sequence

`0 → H₁(L_{K/A}) → 𝔪_B/𝔪_B² → Ω[B⁄A] ⊗[B] K → Ω[K⁄A] → 0`

is exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exact_jacobiZariski_residueField_of_formallySmoothNAdic
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f]
    (hf : RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v} f (maximalIdeal B)) :
    let K := ResidueField B
    letI : Algebra A B := f.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra A K := ((residue B).comp f).toAlgebra
    letI : IsScalarTower A B K := IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' rfl
    let e : Algebra.H1Cotangent B K ≃ₗ[B] CotangentSpace B :=
      (h1Cotangent_equiv_cotangent_of_surjective B K residue_surjective).trans
        (Ideal.Cotangent.equivOfEq _ _ (ker_residue (R := B)))
    let i : Algebra.H1Cotangent A K → CotangentSpace B :=
      fun x ↦ e (Algebra.H1Cotangent.map A B K K x)
    let d : CotangentSpace B → K ⊗[B] Ω[B⁄A] :=
      fun x ↦ Algebra.H1Cotangent.δ A B K (e.symm x)
    Function.Injective i ∧
      Function.Exact i d ∧
      Function.Exact d (KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange A B K) ∧
      Function.Surjective (KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange A B K)

declarations.name: Stacks.ExtIdealPowerImage.range_ext_map_ideal_pow_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYI.** In each degree, the image in `Ext(K, M)` of the Ext group with second
argument `I ^ n M` is eventually contained in `I ^ (n - c) Ext(K, M)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem range_ext_map_ideal_pow_le
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K) (M : ModuleCat.{v} A)
    [Module.Finite A M] (p : ℤ) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, c ≤ n →
      Set.range (fun x : DerivedCategory.Ext K
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).obj
            (ModuleCat.of A ↥(I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A M)))) p ↦
        x ≫ ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).map
          (ModuleCat.ofHom (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A M)).subtype))⟦p⟧') ⊆
        ((I ^ (n - c) • (⊤ : Submodule A
          (DerivedCategory.Ext K
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).obj M) p)) :
            Submodule A _) : Set _)

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.ExtEssentiallyConstant.ext_quotient_ideal_pow_essentially_constant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYJ.** If high-degree Ext from a pseudo-coherent complex into every finite module is
`I`-power torsion, then the inverse system `Ext^p(K, M / I ^ n M)` is essentially constant with
value `Ext^p(K, M)`, which is also its limit.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ext_quotient_ideal_pow_essentially_constant
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K) (a : ℤ)
    (h : ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{v} A) [Module.Finite A N] (j : ℤ), a ≤ j →
      IsIPowerTorsion A
        (DerivedCategory.Ext K
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).obj N) j) I)
    (p : ℤ) (hp : a ≤ p) (M : ModuleCat.{v} A) [Module.Finite A M] :
    let D : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A) :=
      Functor.ofOpSequence
        (X := fun n ↦ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A (M ⧸ (I ^ n • ⊤ : Submodule A M)))) (fun n ↦
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).map
          (ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.factorPowSucc I M n)))
    let E : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u (v + 1)} A :=
      D ⋙ shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A)) p ⋙
        (linearCoyoneda A (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A))).obj (op K)
    let X := ModuleCat.of A
      (DerivedCategory.Ext K
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).obj M) p)
    ∃ π : (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ E,
      (∀ n : ℕ, π.app (op n) = ModuleCat.ofHom (Linear.rightComp A K
        (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).map
          (ModuleCat.ofHom
            ((I ^ n • ⊤ : Submodule A M).mkQ)))⟦p⟧'))) ∧
      (∃ (n : ℕᵒᵖ) (s : E.obj n ⟶ X),
        EssentiallyConstantPro.IsEssentiallyConstantWith E (Cone.mk X π) n s) ∧
      Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk X π))

declarations.name: Deformation.smooth_formallySmooth_flat_specialFibre_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYL.** Smoothness of the restricted representable category of `R`, formal
smoothness of `Λ → R` in the `m_R`-adic topology, and the two conditions combining flatness
with regularity of the special fibre over `k' = Λ / ker(Λ → k)`, are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smooth_formallySmooth_flat_specialFibre_tfae
    (R : CompleteLocalAlgCat.{u, v, w} Λ k) :
    let k' := Λ ⧸ RingHom.ker (algebraMap Λ k)
    letI : (RingHom.ker (algebraMap Λ k)).IsMaximal :=
      Algebra.ker_algebraMap_isMaximal_of_isIntegral Λ k
    letI : Field k' := Ideal.Quotient.field _
    let Bbar := R ⊗[Λ] k'
    letI : Algebra k' Bbar := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    List.TFAE [
      IsSmooth (restrictedCoyonedaProjection R),
      RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v} (algebraMap Λ R) (maximalIdeal R),
      Module.Flat Λ R ∧ Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k' Bbar,
      Module.Flat Λ R ∧
        RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v} (algebraMap k' Bbar)
          ((maximalIdeal R).map Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom)]
declarations.comment: conditions (1)--(4)

declarations.name: Deformation.smooth_formallySmooth_flat_specialFibre_powerSeries_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYL.** If the base is classical, the four smoothness conditions are also
equivalent to `R` being a formal power series algebra in finitely many variables over `Λ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smooth_formallySmooth_flat_specialFibre_powerSeries_tfae
    (R : CompleteLocalAlgCat.{u, v, w} Λ k) (hΛ : IsClassical Λ k) :
    let k' := Λ ⧸ RingHom.ker (algebraMap Λ k)
    letI : (RingHom.ker (algebraMap Λ k)).IsMaximal :=
      Algebra.ker_algebraMap_isMaximal_of_isIntegral Λ k
    letI : Field k' := Ideal.Quotient.field _
    let Bbar := R ⊗[Λ] k'
    letI : Algebra k' Bbar := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    List.TFAE [
      IsSmooth (restrictedCoyonedaProjection R),
      RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v} (algebraMap Λ R) (maximalIdeal R),
      Module.Flat Λ R ∧ Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k' Bbar,
      Module.Flat Λ R ∧
        RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v} (algebraMap k' Bbar)
          ((maximalIdeal R).map Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom),
      ∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty (R ≃ₐ[Λ] MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ)]
declarations.comment: condition (5), classical case

declarations.name: Deformation.mapTwoFibreProductBaseChange
declarations.doc:
The canonical functor over `𝒞_Λ` from the `2`-fibre product of `ℋ₁` and `ℋ₂` over `𝒢` to
their `2`-fibre product over `ℱ`, for a morphism `q : 𝒢 → ℱ`: it keeps both components and
applies `q` to the comparison isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public def mapTwoFibreProductBaseChange
    (p₁ : BasedFunctor 𝓗₁ 𝓖) (p₂ : BasedFunctor 𝓗₂ 𝓖) (q : BasedFunctor 𝓖 𝓕) :
    BasedFunctor (twoFibreProductBasedCategory p₁ p₂)
      (twoFibreProductBasedCategory (BasedFunctor.comp p₁ q) (BasedFunctor.comp p₂ q))
declarations.comment: the canonical functor between the two 2-fibre products

declarations.name: Deformation.isSmooth_mapTwoFibreProductBaseChange'
declarations.doc:
Let `p₁ : ℋ₁ → 𝒢`, `p₂ : ℋ₂ → 𝒢` and `q : 𝒢 → ℱ` be morphisms of categories cofibered in
groupoids over `𝒞_Λ`. Assume that `ℱ` and `𝒢` are deformation categories, that `T𝒢 → Tℱ` is
injective, and that `Inf(𝒢) → Inf(ℱ)` is surjective. Then `ℋ₁ ×_𝒢 ℋ₂ → ℋ₁ ×_ℱ ℋ₂` is smooth.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSmooth_mapTwoFibreProductBaseChange'
    (p₁ : BasedFunctor 𝓗₁ 𝓖) (p₂ : BasedFunctor 𝓗₂ 𝓖) (q : BasedFunctor 𝓖 𝓕)
    (h𝓗₁ : IsCofiberedInGroupoids 𝓗₁.p) (h𝓗₂ : IsCofiberedInGroupoids 𝓗₂.p)
    (h𝓖 : IsDeformationCategory 𝓖.p) (h𝓕 : IsDeformationCategory 𝓕.p)
    (htangent : Function.Injective
      (differential h𝓖.predeformation.cofibered h𝓕.predeformation.cofibered q))
    {z₀ : 𝓖.p.Fiber (residueFieldObject.{u, w, w} Λ k)}
    (PG : ChosenPushforwardsAt 𝓖.p z₀.1) (PF : ChosenPushforwardsAt 𝓕.p (q.obj z₀.1))
    (hinf :
      letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup PG h𝓖.satisfiesRS
      letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule PG h𝓖.satisfiesRS
      letI := naturalLocalizedTangentAddCommGroup PF h𝓕.satisfiesRS
      letI := naturalLocalizedTangentModule PF h𝓕.satisfiesRS
      Function.Surjective (inducedInfinitesimalLinearMapOfEq q.toFunctor q.w
        h𝓖.satisfiesRS h𝓕.satisfiesRS PG PF)) :
    IsSmooth (mapTwoFibreProductBaseChange p₁ p₂ q)
declarations.comment: smoothness

declarations.name: Deformation.isSmooth_iff_differential_surjective_and_lifts
declarations.doc:
Surjectivity of the differential and preservation of the existence of lifts across small
extensions characterize smoothness.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSmooth_iff_differential_surjective_and_lifts
    (h𝓕 : IsDeformationCategory 𝓕.p)
    (h𝓖 : IsDeformationCategory 𝓖.p)
    (φ : BasedFunctor 𝓕 𝓖) :
    IsSmooth φ ↔
      (Function.Surjective
        (differential h𝓕.predeformation.cofibered
          h𝓖.predeformation.cofibered φ) ∧
       ∀ ⦃B A : ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, w, w} Λ k⦄
         (f : B ⟶ A),
         InfinitesimalLifting.IsSmallExtension
           (CommRingCat.ofHom f.hom.toRingHom) →
         ∀ (x : 𝓕.p.Fiber A),
           (∃ (y' : 𝓖.obj) (g : y' ⟶ φ.obj x.1),
             𝓖.p.IsHomLift f g) →
           (∃ (x' : 𝓕.obj) (h : x' ⟶ x.1),
             𝓕.p.IsHomLift f h))

declarations.name: Deformation.Obstruction.canonicalObstructionMap_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**The canonical obstruction morphism is compatible with base change.** Derived base change
along `b` carries the canonical obstruction morphism of a bounded-above `K` for the square-zero
surjection `fR` to the canonical obstruction morphism of its base change for `fS`, read through
the comparison of the two targets attached to a bounded-above free K-flat representative `P` of
`K` and a K-flat resolution `q` of `I/I²`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalObstructionMap_baseChange
    (hI : RingHom.ker fR ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (hJ : RingHom.ker fS = Ideal.map a (RingHom.ker fR))
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (hK : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := ModuleCat.{u} R)).minus K)
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (m : ℤ) (hPLE : P.IsStrictlyLE m)
    (hfree : ∀ n, Module.Free R (P.X n)) (hP : P.KFlat)
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ K)
    (T : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (k : ℤ) (hTLE : T.IsStrictlyLE k)
    (hTproj : ∀ i, Projective (T.X i)) (hT : T.KFlat)
    (q : T ⟶ kernelComplex fR hfR) (hq : QuasiIso q)
    (hQq : IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map q)) :
    (derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, u, u} b).functor.map
        (canonicalObstructionMap fR hfR hI K hK).1 ≫
      ((derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, u, u} b).functor.commShiftIso (2 : ℤ)).hom.app
          (((canonicalDerivedTensorProductFunctor R).obj K).obj
            (squareZeroKernelObject fR hfR)) ≫
        (shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S)) (2 : ℤ)).map
          (obstructionTargetBaseChangeMap fR hfR fS hfS a b hcomm P hP e T hT q hQq) =
      (canonicalObstructionMap fS hfS (ker_sq_eq_bot_baseChange fR fS a hJ hI)
        ((derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, u, u} b).functor.obj K)
        ((derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, u, u} b).maps_boundedAbove ⟨K, hK⟩)).1
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: Deformation.Obstruction.existsUnique_isCanonicalObstructionMap
declarations.doc:
There is a unique morphism represented by the squares of lifted differentials on every
bounded-above free representative, independently of the lifts and all comparison data.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isCanonicalObstructionMap
    (f : R' →+* R) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (hzero : (RingHom.ker f) ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (hK : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := ModuleCat.{u} R)).minus K) :
    ∃! ω : K ⟶ (((canonicalDerivedTensorProductFunctor R).obj K).obj
      (squareZeroKernelObject f hf))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧, IsCanonicalObstructionMap f hf K ω
declarations.comment: canonical_obstruction_map

declarations.name: Deformation.Obstruction.canonicalObstructionMap_natural
declarations.doc:
The canonical obstruction morphism commutes with every morphism of bounded-above
derived complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalObstructionMap_natural
    {R' R : Type u} [CommRing R'] [CommRing R]
    (f : R' →+* R) (hf : Function.Surjective f)
    (hzero : (RingHom.ker f) ^ 2 = ⊥)
    {K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)}
    (hK : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := ModuleCat.{u} R)).minus K)
    (hL : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := ModuleCat.{u} R)).minus L)
    (g : K ⟶ L) :
    g ≫ (Deformation.Obstruction.canonicalObstructionMap
      f hf hzero L hL).val =
      (Deformation.Obstruction.canonicalObstructionMap
        f hf hzero K hK).val ≫
        (shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (2 : ℤ)).map
          (((canonicalDerivedTensorProductFunctor R).map g).app
            (Deformation.Obstruction.squareZeroKernelObject f hf))
declarations.comment: naturality

declarations.name: Deformation.Obstruction.canonicalObstructionMap_eq_zero_iff_exists_lift
declarations.doc:
A bounded-above derived complex over `R` lifts across a square-zero surjection
`R' → R` exactly when its canonical obstruction morphism is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalObstructionMap_eq_zero_iff_exists_lift
    {R' R : Type u} [CommRing R'] [CommRing R]
    (f : R' →+* R) (hf : Function.Surjective f)
    (hzero : (RingHom.ker f) ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (hK : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := ModuleCat.{u} R)).minus K) :
      (Deformation.Obstruction.canonicalObstructionMap f hf hzero K hK).val = 0 ↔
      ∃ K' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R'),
        Nonempty ((derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, u, u} f).functor.obj K' ≅ K)
declarations.comment: vanishing_criterion

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.localizationFunctor
declarations.doc:
Localization at `S` gives a natural functor from deformations of `P` to deformations of
`S⁻¹P`, with the canonical localization map on every flat algebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationFunctor (S : Submonoid P) :
    LocalizationFunctorData (Λ := Λ) (k := k) S

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.henselizationFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYT.** For a `k`-algebra `P` and an ideal `J ⊆ P`, henselization along the
inverse image of `J` is a functor from the deformation category of `P` to that of the
henselization of the pair `(P, J)`, over the category `𝒞_Λ` of Artinian local bases.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def henselizationFunctor :
    HenselizationFunctorData (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (P := P) J

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.strictHenselizationFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYU.** Let `P` be a local `k`-algebra and let `Pˢʰ` be a strict henselization of
`P` with respect to a separable algebraic closure of its residue field. There is a natural
functor from the deformation category of `P` to that of `Pˢʰ`, over the category `𝒞_Λ` of
Artinian local bases: strict henselize the flat algebra of each deformation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def strictHenselizationFunctor
    (hsh : Stacks.StrictHenselization.IsStrictHenselization P κsep Psh) :
    StrictHenselizationFunctorData (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (P := P) Psh

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.adicCompletionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The completion functor on deformations, Stacks 0DYV.** Completion at the inverse image of
`J` is a functor over `𝒞_Λ` together with the identification of its fibres with the adic
completions; this is one such datum, chosen from the base-compatible ones so that
`Deformation.Examples.isBaseCompatible_adicCompletionFunctor` holds of it.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def adicCompletionFunctor [IsNoetherianRing P] :
    AdicCompletionFunctorData (Λ := Λ) (k := k) P J

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.openRestrictionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYW.** Let `X` be a scheme over `k` and `U ⊆ X` an open subscheme. Restricting a
deformation of `X` to the open corresponding to `U` is a functor from the deformation category
of `X` to that of `U`, over the category `𝒞_Λ` of Artinian local `Λ`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
def openRestrictionFunctor (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : X.left.Opens) :
    BasedFunctor
      (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X))
      (BasedCategory.ofFunctor
        (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Over.mk (U.ι ≫ X.hom))))

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.chartEquivalenceOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYX for an affine open presented as a spectrum.** The deformation category of an
open `U` of `X` which is presented as `Spec P` over `Spec k` is equivalent, over `𝒞_Λ`, to the
deformation category of the `k`-algebra `P`: transport the deformations along the presentation
and then take global sections.
declarations.statement:
def chartEquivalenceOver :
    StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Over.mk (U.ι ≫ X.hom)))
      (Over.forget (residueFieldAlgebra (Λ := Λ) (k := k) P) ⋙
        FlatAlgebraCategory.projection (Λ := Λ) (k := k))
declarations.comment: for an affine open presented as a spectrum by an isomorphism over Spec k, which is the form Situation 0DYY provides

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.SchemeRingDeformation.sectionsFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYX.** Global sections as a functor from deformations of `Spec P` to
deformations of `P`.
declarations.comment: the functor sending (A, Y) to the global sections of Y

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.SchemeRingDeformation.equivalenceOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYX.** For a `k`-algebra `P`, global sections are an equivalence from the
deformation category of the affine scheme `Spec P` to the deformation category of `P`, over the
category of Artinian local `Λ`-algebras with residue field `k`.
declarations.statement:
def equivalenceOver :
    StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (specOver k P))
      (Over.forget (residueFieldAlgebra (Λ := Λ) (k := k) P) ⋙
        FlatAlgebraCategory.projection (Λ := Λ) (k := k))
declarations.comment: the equivalence Def_(Spec P) = Def_P; 06AD is isAffine_of_isThickening

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.GluingSituation
declarations.doc:
A scheme over `k`, covered by two affine opens with affine intersection, together with
coordinate rings for the three affine schemes.
declarations.statement: structure GluingSituation (Λ k : Type u) [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k]

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.twoOpenComparisonFunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a scheme over `k` with two opens `U₁` and `U₂`. Restricting a deformation of `X`
to `U₁` and to `U₂`, together with the identification of the two induced deformations of
`U₁ ⊓ U₂`, is a functor from the deformation category of `X` to the 2-fibre product
`Def_{U₁} ×_{Def_{U₁ ⊓ U₂}} Def_{U₂}` over `𝒞_Λ`.
declarations.statement:
def twoOpenComparisonFunctor (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U₁ U₂ : X.left.Opens) :
    SchemeDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X ⥤
      TwoFibreProductOver
        (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Over.mk (U₁.ι ≫ X.hom)))
        (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Over.mk (U₂.ι ≫ X.hom)))
        (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Over.mk ((U₁ ⊓ U₂).ι ≫ X.hom)))
        (openRestrictionLEFunctor (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (inf_le_left : U₁ ⊓ U₂ ≤ U₁))
        (openRestrictionLEFunctor (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (inf_le_right : U₁ ⊓ U₂ ≤ U₂))
declarations.comment: the comparison functor Def_X ⥤ Def_{U_1} ×_{Def_{U_12}} Def_{U_2} only; it is not shown to be an equivalence (that needs the glueing quasi-inverse of the proof) and the translation into the ring deformation categories Def_{P_i} is not included

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.twoOpenComparisonFunctor_comp_structureFunctor
declarations.doc: The comparison functor of a two-open cover is strictly over `𝒞_Λ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem twoOpenComparisonFunctor_comp_structureFunctor (X : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (U₁ U₂ : X.left.Opens) :
    twoOpenComparisonFunctor (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X U₁ U₂ ⋙
        TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor
          (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Over.mk (U₁.ι ≫ X.hom)))
          (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Over.mk (U₂.ι ≫ X.hom)))
          (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k)
            (Over.mk ((U₁ ⊓ U₂).ι ≫ X.hom)))
          (openRestrictionLEFunctor (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (inf_le_left : U₁ ⊓ U₂ ≤ U₁))
          (openRestrictionLEFunctor (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (inf_le_right : U₁ ⊓ U₂ ≤ U₂)) =
      schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X
declarations.comment: the comparison functor Def_X ⥤ Def_{U_1} ×_{Def_{U_12}} Def_{U_2} is a functor over 𝒞_Λ; it is not shown to be an equivalence and the ring deformation categories Def_{P_i} are not involved

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.GluingSituation.comparisonFunctor
declarations.doc: The comparison functor of the two-open cover of a glueing situation.
declarations.statement:
def GluingSituation.comparisonFunctor (S : GluingSituation Λ k) :
    SchemeDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) (k := k) S.X ⥤
      TwoFibreProductOver
        (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Over.mk (S.U₁.ι ≫ S.X.hom)))
        (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Over.mk (S.U₂.ι ≫ S.X.hom)))
        (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k)
          (Over.mk ((S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂).ι ≫ S.X.hom)))
        (openRestrictionLEFunctor (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (inf_le_left : S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂ ≤ S.U₁))
        (openRestrictionLEFunctor (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (inf_le_right : S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂ ≤ S.U₂))
declarations.comment: the comparison functor in Situation 0DYY; it is not shown to be an equivalence and the translation into the ring deformation categories Def_{P_i} is not included

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.glueDeformation
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a scheme over `k` covered by two opens `U₁` and `U₂`. An object of the 2-fibre
product `Def_{U₁} ×_{Def_{U₁ ⊓ U₂}} Def_{U₂}` consists of a deformation of `U₁`, a deformation
of `U₂` and an isomorphism of their restrictions to `U₁ ⊓ U₂`; glueing the two total spaces
along that isomorphism gives a deformation of `X` over the same object of `𝒞_Λ`.
declarations.statement: def glueDeformation : SchemeDeformationCategory (Λ := Λ) (k := k) X
declarations.comment: the glueing construction of the proof, on objects only: an object of the 2-fibre product Def_{U_1} ×_{Def_{U_12}} Def_{U_2} is glued to a deformation of X over the same object of 𝒞_Λ, flat over it, with special fibre X, and restricting to U_1 and U_2 gives the two charts back. Not shown functorial in the datum, so not yet a quasi-inverse of twoOpenComparisonFunctor; neither the equivalence nor the Def_{P_i} form is proved

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.GluingSituation.glueDeformation
declarations.doc:
In a glueing situation the two affine opens cover the scheme, and an object of the 2-fibre
product of their deformation categories is glued to a deformation of the scheme itself.
declarations.comment: the glueing construction of the proof in Situation 0DYY, on objects only; see `glueDeformation` for the precise content and for what the equivalence still needs

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.comparisonGlue_w
declarations.doc:
**The two chart isomorphisms of the glued deformation are compatible with the comparison
isomorphism of the datum.** This is the `CategoryTheory.TwoFibreProductOver.Hom.w` of the pair,
that is, what makes `Deformation.Examples.restrictGlueDeformationLeft` and
`Deformation.Examples.restrictGlueDeformationRight` the two components of a *single* morphism of
the `2`-fibre product. The source of Tag 0DYZ says only "we omit the verification".
declarations.statement:
theorem comparisonGlue_w :
    (openRestrictionLEFunctor (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (inf_le_left : U₁ ⊓ U₂ ≤ U₁)).map
        (restrictGlueDeformationLeftHom X U₁ U₂ Q hcover) ≫ Q.iso.hom =
      (restrictDeformationLEIso (glueDeformation X U₁ U₂ Q hcover)
            (inf_le_left : U₁ ⊓ U₂ ≤ U₁) ≪≫
          (restrictDeformationLEIso (glueDeformation X U₁ U₂ Q hcover)
            (inf_le_right : U₁ ⊓ U₂ ≤ U₂)).symm).hom ≫
        (openRestrictionLEFunctor (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (inf_le_right : U₁ ⊓ U₂ ≤ U₂)).map
          (restrictGlueDeformationRightHom X U₁ U₂ Q hcover)
declarations.comment: the compatibility of the two chart isomorphisms of the glueing with the comparison isomorphism of the datum, i.e. that the two of them are one morphism of the 2-fibre product; the equivalence itself is not proved here

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.comparisonGlueHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYZ**, the comparison morphism out of the glueing. The two chart isomorphisms of
the glued deformation are the two components of one morphism of the `2`-fibre product from the
comparison of the glued deformation to the datum it was glued from.
declarations.statement:
def comparisonGlueHom :
    (twoOpenComparisonFunctor (Λ := Λ) X U₁ U₂).obj (glueDeformation X U₁ U₂ Q hcover) ⟶ Q
declarations.comment: the comparison morphism from the comparison of the glued deformation to the datum, built from the two chart isomorphisms; it is an isomorphism, but only the morphism is constructed here, and the equivalence of Tag 0DYZ is not proved

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.glueDeformationHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYZ**, the glueing quasi-inverse on morphisms. A morphism of the `2`-fibre product
from a datum `Q` to the comparison of a deformation `P` of `X` glues to a morphism from the
deformation glued from `Q` to `P`. The source of Tag 0DYZ says only "we omit the
verification".
declarations.statement: def glueDeformationHom : glueDeformation X U₁ U₂ Q hcover ⟶ P
declarations.comment: the glueing construction of the proof on morphisms: a morphism of the 2-fibre product into the comparison of a deformation is glued to a morphism of deformations of X; the equivalence of Tag 0DYZ is not proved here

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.twoOpenComparisonFunctor_map_glueDeformationHom
declarations.doc:
**The triangle of the lifting problem commutes**: the comparison of the glued morphism is
the comparison morphism out of the glueing followed by the given morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem twoOpenComparisonFunctor_map_glueDeformationHom :
    (twoOpenComparisonFunctor (Λ := Λ) X U₁ U₂).map (glueDeformationHom X U₁ U₂ Q hcover P g) =
      comparisonGlueHom X U₁ U₂ Q hcover ≫ g
declarations.comment: the compatibility of the glued morphism with the comparison morphism out of the glueing; the equivalence of Tag 0DYZ is not proved here

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.isSmooth_twoOpenComparisonBasedFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYZ in the form Tag 0DZN uses it.** If the two opens cover `X` then the comparison
morphism `Def_X ⟶ Def_{U₁} ×_{Def_{U₁ ⊓ U₂}} Def_{U₂}` is smooth: a lifting problem is solved by
glueing the datum over the smaller object of `𝒞_Λ` to a deformation of `X`, glueing the given
morphism to a morphism of deformations of `X`, and comparing the glued deformation with the
datum by the two chart isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_twoOpenComparisonBasedFunctor (hcover : U₁ ⊔ U₂ = ⊤) :
    IsSmooth (twoOpenComparisonBasedFunctor (Λ := Λ) X U₁ U₂)
declarations.comment: smoothness of the comparison morphism Def_X ⟶ Def_{U_1} ×_{Def_{U_12}} Def_{U_2}, which is what Tag 0DZN consumes; that the comparison morphism is an *equivalence* — the full assertion of 0DYZ — is not proved, and neither is the translation into the ring deformation categories Def_{P_i}

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.GluingSituation.deformationCategories_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DYZ.** In Situation 0DYY, `Def_X` and `Def_{P₁} ×_{Def_{P₁₂}} Def_{P₂}` are
deformation categories, and the comparison functor between them is an equivalence of
categories over `𝒞_Λ`. Here `Def_{P_i}` is the deformation category of the `k`-algebra `P_i`
of Example 0DY1, `Def_X` that of the scheme `X` of Example 0DY7, and the two legs of the
2-fibre product are the restriction functors `Def_{P_i} ⟶ Def_{P₁₂}` along `U₁₂ ⊆ U_i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem deformationCategories_equivalence :
    IsDeformationCategory.{u, u, u} (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) S.X) ∧
      IsDeformationCategory.{u, u, u} (ringChartDeformationsProjection S) ∧
      ∃ e : EquivalenceOver (schemeDeformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) S.X)
        (ringChartDeformationsProjection S), e.hom.functor = ringComparisonFunctor S
declarations.comment: Def_X = Def_{P_1} ×_{Def_{P_12}} Def_{P_2} as an equivalence over 𝒞_Λ of deformation categories, with the ring deformation categories of Example 0DY1 and the restriction functors along U_12 ⊆ U_i

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.DerivedLift.exists_flat_lift_iff_exists_derived_lift
declarations.doc:
Over a nilpotent surjection, an `A`-flat module lifts flatly if and only if
it admits a bounded-above derived lift.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_flat_lift_iff_exists_derived_lift
    (A' A P' : Type u) [CommRing A'] [CommRing A] [CommRing P']
    [Algebra A' A] [Algebra A' P']
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A' A))
    (hnil : IsNilpotent (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A' A)))
    [Module.Flat A' P']
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (TensorProduct A' P' A) M]
    [Module A M] [IsScalarTower A (TensorProduct A' P' A) M]
    [Module.Flat A M] :
    (∃ (M' : Type (max u v)) (_ : AddCommGroup M')
      (_ : Module P' M') (_ : Module A' M') (_ : IsScalarTower A' P' M'),
      Module.Flat A' M' ∧
        Nonempty
          ((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max u v}
              (algebraMap P' (TensorProduct A' P' A))).obj
                (ModuleCat.of.{max u v, u} P' M') ≅
            ModuleCat.of.{max u v, u} (TensorProduct A' P' A) (ULift.{u} M))) ↔
      ∃ (K : DerivedCategory.Minus (ModuleCat.{max u v} P')),
        Nonempty
          ((CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, v, u}
            (algebraMap P' (TensorProduct A' P' A))).functor.obj K.obj ≅
            (DerivedCategory.Q
              (C := ModuleCat.{max u v} (TensorProduct A' P' A))).obj
                ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor
                  (ModuleCat.{max u v} (TensorProduct A' P' A)) 0).obj
                    (ModuleCat.of.{max u v, u} (TensorProduct A' P' A)
                      (ULift.{u} M))))

declarations.name: Deformation.HasFlatModuleLift.baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZ2, forward implication.** In a commuting square of ring maps `P' → Q'`,
`P' → P`, `Q' → Q`, `P → Q` whose left vertical map `p` is surjective with nilpotent kernel and
whose top map `P' → Q'` is flat, a flat module lift of a `P`-module `M` base-changes to a flat
module lift of `Q ⊗[P] M`.

By Nakayama the lift `N` is generated over `P'` by a family indexed by `M`, so `Q' ⊗[P'] N` is a
quotient of `M →₀ Q'` and can be presented in the universe of `Q'` and `M`, which is what
`HasFlatModuleLift` demands of the witness.

This direction of Stacks 0DZ2 carries the source's own hypothesis on the kernel of `P' → P` —
nilpotent, not square-zero — and uses none of the obstruction calculus, so it is faithful and in
fact more general than the source: neither the Noetherian hypotheses, nor finiteness of `M`, nor
the ideal `J'`, nor the local liftability hypothesis is needed. The converse is the
obstruction-theoretic half, and is
`exists_flat_lift_iff_exists_flat_lift_baseChange_of_localizationLift_of_isNilpotent_ker` in
`StacksFrontier.Deformation.FlatModuleLiftLocalization`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem HasFlatModuleLift.baseChange
    {A' : Type u₁} {P' : Type u₃} {P : Type u₄} {Q' : Type u₅} {Q : Type u₆}
    [CommRing A'] [CommRing P'] [CommRing P] [CommRing Q'] [CommRing Q]
    [Algebra A' P'] [Algebra P' Q'] [Algebra P Q]
    {p : P' →+* P} {q : Q' →+* Q}
    (hcomm : (algebraMap P Q).comp p = q.comp (algebraMap P' Q'))
    (hflat : Module.Flat P' Q')
    (hp : Function.Surjective p) (hnp : IsNilpotent (RingHom.ker p))
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module P M]
    (h : HasFlatModuleLift (algebraMap A' P') p M) :
    HasFlatModuleLift ((algebraMap P' Q').comp (algebraMap A' P')) q (Q ⊗[P] M)
declarations.comment: the implication (1) => (2) of 0DZ2, at the source's hypotheses with nothing added; it needs neither the Noetherian hypotheses, nor finiteness of `M`, nor `J'`, nor the local liftability hypothesis. The converse (2) => (1) is false as printed (Stacks erratum, see errata.md): `Deformation.Examples.ArtinSchreier.not_flatModuleLiftBaseChangeStatementFaithful` satisfies every hypothesis of the source and (2) holds there while (1) fails. The corrected equivalence, with `ker(A' → A)^2 = ⊥` and `M` finite over `P` added, is `Deformation.exists_flatModuleLift_iff_baseChange_of_sq_zero`

declarations.name: Deformation.exists_flatModuleLift_iff_baseChange_of_sq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZ2, corrected (Stacks erratum).** Let `A' → P' → Q'` lie over `A → P → Q`, with
`A' → A`, `P' → P`, `Q' → Q` surjective, `ker(P' → P) = I·P'` and `ker(Q' → Q) = I·Q'` for
`I = ker(A' → A)` (the two squares are cocartesian), `A' → P'`, `P' → Q'`, `P → Q` flat and `P`
Noetherian. Let `J' ⊂ P'` be an ideal with `P'/J' = Q'/J'Q'`, let `M` be a `P`-module, finite over
`P` and flat over `A`, and let `N ≅ Q ⊗_P M`. If `M_g` has an `A'`-flat lift to `(P')_g` for every
`g ∈ J'` and `I² = 0`, then `M` has an `A'`-flat lift to a `P'`-module if and only if `N` has an
`A'`-flat lift to a `Q'`-module.

Stacks 0DZ2 as printed asks `I` to be nilpotent and does not ask `M` to be finite, and in that
form the implication (2) ⇒ (1) is false:
`Deformation.Examples.ArtinSchreier.not_flatModuleLiftBaseChangeStatementFaithful` is a
counterexample with `I³ = 0`, `I² ≠ 0` and `M` cyclic, satisfying every hypothesis of the source.
The two hypotheses added here are the correction recorded in `errata.md`: `I² = 0` is sharp by
that counterexample, and finiteness of `M` is what the source's own proof uses ("here we use that
`P` is Noetherian and `M` finite", at Stacks 0A6A). The implication (1) ⇒ (2) holds at the
source's hypotheses with no addition, as `Deformation.HasFlatModuleLift.baseChange`.

The proof is the source's proof with its induction step removed: it transports to this shape the
form proved in `StacksFrontier.Deformation.FlatModuleLiftLocalization`, which allows `I` to be
nilpotent provided the thickening `P' → P` is square-zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_flatModuleLift_iff_baseChange_of_sq_zero
    [IsNoetherianRing P] [Module.Flat P' Q'] [Module.Flat P Q]
    (hzeroA : RingHom.ker (algebraMap A' A) ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (J' : Ideal P')
    (hquot : Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (J'.map (algebraMap P' Q'))
      (algebraMap P' Q') Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module P M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower A P M]
      [Module.Finite P M] [Module.Flat A M] (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module Q N]
    (hMN : Nonempty ((Q ⊗[P] M) ≃ₗ[Q] N))
    (hloc : ∀ g ∈ J',
      letI : Algebra (Localization.Away g) (Localization.Away (algebraMap P' P g)) :=
        (Localization.awayMap (algebraMap P' P) g).toAlgebra
      ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup L) (_ : Module (Localization.Away g) L)
        (_ : Module A' L) (_ : IsScalarTower A' (Localization.Away g) L),
        Module.Flat A' L ∧ Nonempty
          ((Localization.Away (algebraMap P' P g) ⊗[Localization.Away g] L)
            ≃ₗ[Localization.Away (algebraMap P' P g)]
              (Localization.Away (algebraMap P' P g) ⊗[P] M))) :
    (∃ (M' : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M') (_ : Module P' M') (_ : Module A' M')
        (_ : IsScalarTower A' P' M'), Module.Flat A' M' ∧
        Nonempty ((P ⊗[P'] M') ≃ₗ[P] M)) ↔
      (∃ (N' : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup N') (_ : Module Q' N') (_ : Module A' N')
        (_ : IsScalarTower A' Q' N'), Module.Flat A' N' ∧
        Nonempty ((Q ⊗[Q'] N') ≃ₗ[Q] N))
declarations.comment: corrected form of 0DZ2 (Stacks erratum, see errata.md): the equivalence (1) <=> (2) with the two hypotheses `hzeroA : ker(A' → A)^2 = ⊥` and `Module.Finite P M` added, every other hypothesis being the source's (Noetherianity is asked of `P` alone, flatness of `A → P` and nilpotence of the kernels follow, and `Module.Flat A' Q'` is the composite of `A' → P' → Q'`). As printed, (2) => (1) is false: `Deformation.Examples.ArtinSchreier.not_flatModuleLiftBaseChangeStatementFaithful` satisfies every hypothesis of the source, with `ker(A' → A) = (t)`, `t^3 = 0`, `t^2 ≠ 0` and `M` cyclic, and (1) fails there. So `I^2 = 0` cannot be weakened to `I^3 = 0`; finiteness of `M` is used by the source's own proof at 0A6A. The implication (1) => (2) holds as printed, with no hypothesis added: `Deformation.HasFlatModuleLift.baseChange`

declarations.name: Deformation.hasFlatAlgebraLift_iff_hasFlatAlgebraLift_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZ3.** Let `A' → A` be a surjective map of Noetherian rings with nilpotent kernel,
let `A → B` be a finite type flat ring map and let `𝔟 ⊆ B` be an ideal such that
`Spec(B) → Spec(A)` is syntomic on the complement of `V(𝔟)`. Then `B` has a flat lift to `A'` if
and only if the `𝔟`-adic completion `B^∧` has a flat lift to `A'`.

`Spec(B) → Spec(A)` is syntomic at the point `𝔮` exactly when `A → B_g` is syntomic for some
`g ∉ 𝔮` (Stacks 00SY, 01UE); that is how the hypothesis `hsyn` reads the source's condition at
every point `𝔮` of the complement of `V(𝔟)`. The proof does not go through Stacks 0DZ2 (which is
false at a nilpotent kernel); see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasFlatAlgebraLift_iff_hasFlatAlgebraLift_adicCompletion
    (A' A B : Type u) [CommRing A'] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A'] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra A' A] [Algebra A B]
    (hsurjA : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A' A))
    (hnilA : IsNilpotent (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A' A)))
    [Algebra.FiniteType A B] [Module.Flat A B] (b : Ideal B)
    (hsyn : ∀ q : Ideal B, q.IsPrime → ¬ b ≤ q →
      ∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.Syntomic A (Localization.Away g)) :
    HasFlatAlgebraLift A' A B ↔ HasFlatAlgebraLift A' A (AdicCompletion b B)
declarations.comment: `Spec(B) → Spec(A)` being syntomic on the complement of `V(𝔟)` is read pointwise and affinely: for every prime `𝔮` not containing `𝔟` there is `g ∉ 𝔮` with `A → B_g` syntomic, the characterization of Stacks 00SY and 01UE. `B^∧` is `AdicCompletion 𝔟 B`. The published proof rests on Stacks 0DZ2, which is false at a nilpotent kernel; the proof here approximates a flat lift over the completed presentation by relation solutions over the polynomial presentation and corrects them one power of the kernel at a time (Artin-Rees plus Stacks 07M8 at every level). See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.exists_squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesCompletionEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZ4.** For a finite type algebra `B` over a field `k` which is smooth over `k`
outside the zero set of an ideal `J`, and a finite `B`-module `N`, completion along `J` is a
bijection from the isomorphism classes of square-zero extensions of `B` by `N` to those of `B^`
by `N^`, matching a class with its image exactly when the two extensions admit a `k`-algebra map
of middle rings over `B → B^` and over `N → N^`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesCompletionEquiv
    (k : Type uk) (B : Type uB) [Field k] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k B] (J : Ideal B)
    (hsm : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B, ¬ J ≤ q.asIdeal → Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q.asIdeal)
    (N : Type uN) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N] [Module.Finite B N] :
    ∃ e : SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.IsomorphismClasses.{uk, uk, uB, uN,
        max uB uN} (algebraExtensionProblem k B N) ≃
      SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.IsomorphismClasses.{uk, uk, uB, uN,
        max uB uN} (algebraExtensionProblem k (AdicCompletion J B) (AdicCompletion J N)),
      ∀ (X : (algebraExtensionProblem k B N).CompatibleExtension.{max uB uN})
        (Y : (algebraExtensionProblem k (AdicCompletion J B)
          (AdicCompletion J N)).CompatibleExtension.{max uB uN}),
        (∃ h : X.B' →ₐ[k] Y.B',
            (∀ z : X.B', Y.toB (h z) = algebraMap B (AdicCompletion J B) (X.toB z)) ∧
              ∀ n : N, h (kernelInclusion X n) =
                kernelInclusion Y (AdicCompletion.of J N n)) ↔
          e ⟦X⟧ = ⟦Y⟧

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.isSmooth_and_bijective_differential_adicCompletionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZ5.** Let `k` be a field, `P` a finite type `k`-algebra, `J ⊆ P` an ideal such
that `Spec(P) → Spec(k)` is smooth on the complement of `V(J)`, and `P^` the `J`-adic
completion. Then the completion functor `𝓓_P ⟶ 𝓓_{P^}` of **Stacks 0DYV**
(`Deformation.Examples.adicCompletionFunctor`) is smooth and induces an isomorphism on tangent
spaces.

As in the source, this is the criterion of **Stacks 0DYP** applied to the two inputs: the
isomorphism on tangent spaces, from **Stacks 0DZ4** with `N = B`
(`Deformation.Examples.bijective_differential_adicCompletionFunctor`), and the correspondence of
liftability, from **Stacks 0DZ3** at a small extension
(`Deformation.Examples.lifts_adicCompletionFunctorData_unconditional`), which together give
smoothness (`Deformation.Examples.isSmooth_adicCompletionFunctor`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_and_bijective_differential_adicCompletionFunctor [Algebra.FiniteType k P]
    (hsm : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum P, ¬ J ≤ q.asIdeal → Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q.asIdeal) :
    letI : IsNoetherianRing P := Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing k P
    IsSmooth (adicCompletionFunctor (Λ := Λ) (k := k) P J).functor ∧
      Function.Bijective (differential (𝓕 := ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k P)
        (𝓖 := ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k (AdicCompletion J P))
        isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection
        isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection
        (adicCompletionFunctor (Λ := Λ) (k := k) P J).functor)
declarations.comment: both conclusions, at the completion functor `Deformation.Examples.adicCompletionFunctor` of Stacks 0DYV: it is smooth, and its differential on tangent spaces is bijective. The hypotheses are the source's: `P` of finite type over the field `k`, and `P` smooth over `k` at every prime not containing `J`

declarations.name: Deformation.hasFlatAlgebraLift_iff_hasFlatAlgebraLift_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZ7.** Let `A' → A` be a surjective map of Noetherian rings with nilpotent kernel,
let `A → B` be a finite type flat ring map and let `S ⊆ B` be a multiplicative subset such that if
`Spec(B) → Spec(A)` is not syntomic at `𝔮`, then `S ∩ 𝔮 = ∅`. Then `B` has a flat lift to `A'` if
and only if `S⁻¹B` has a flat lift to `A'`.

`Spec(B) → Spec(A)` is syntomic at the point `𝔮` exactly when `A → B_g` is syntomic for some
`g ∉ 𝔮` (Stacks 00SY, 01UE); that is how the hypothesis `hS` reads the source's condition. The
proof does not go through Stacks 0DZ2 (which is false); see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasFlatAlgebraLift_iff_hasFlatAlgebraLift_localization
    (A' A B : Type u) [CommRing A'] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A'] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra A' A] [Algebra A B]
    (hsurjA : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A' A))
    (hnilA : IsNilpotent (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A' A)))
    [Algebra.FiniteType A B] [Module.Flat A B] (S : Submonoid B)
    (hS : ∀ q : Ideal B, q.IsPrime →
      (¬ ∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.Syntomic A (Localization.Away g)) → ∀ s ∈ S, s ∉ q)
    (C : Type u) [CommRing C] [Algebra B C] [IsLocalization S C] [Algebra A C]
    [IsScalarTower A B C] :
    HasFlatAlgebraLift A' A B ↔ HasFlatAlgebraLift A' A C
declarations.comment:
`S⁻¹B` is any `C` with `IsLocalization S C`. `Spec(B) → Spec(A)` being syntomic at
the point `𝔮` is read affinely as `∃ g ∉ 𝔮, A → B_g` syntomic, the characterization of Stacks 00SY
and 01UE; `S ∩ 𝔮 = ∅` is `∀ s ∈ S, s ∉ 𝔮`. The published proof rests on Stacks 0DZ2, which is false;
the proof here approximates a flat lift over the localized presentation by relation solutions over
the polynomial presentation and corrects them one power of the kernel at a time (Artin-Rees plus
Stacks 07M8 at every level). See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesLocalizationEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZ8.** If a multiplicative subset `S` of a finite type algebra `B` over a field
`k` is disjoint from every prime in the non-smooth locus of `B`, then localization at `S` is a
bijection from the isomorphism classes of square-zero extensions of `B` by `N` to those of
square-zero extensions of `S⁻¹B` by `S⁻¹N`.

The companion lemma
`Deformation.Examples.squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesLocalizationEquiv_apply` identifies the
forward map with localization.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesLocalizationEquiv
    (k : Type uk) (B : Type uB) [Field k] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k B] (S : Submonoid B)
    (hS : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
      ¬ Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q.asIdeal →
        Disjoint (S : Set B) (q.asIdeal : Set B))
    (N : Type uN) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N] :
    SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.IsomorphismClasses.{uk, uk, uB, uN,
        max uk (max uB uN)} (algebraExtensionProblem k B N) ≃
      SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.IsomorphismClasses.{uk, uk, uB,
        max uB uN, max uk (max uB uN)}
        (algebraExtensionProblem k (Localization S) (LocalizedModule S N))
declarations.comment: localization equivalence

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesLocalizationEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZ8.** The forward map of
`Deformation.Examples.squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesLocalizationEquiv` is localization of an
extension at the inverse image of `S` in its middle ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesLocalizationEquiv_apply
    (k : Type uk) (B : Type uB) [Field k] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k B] (S : Submonoid B)
    (hS : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
      ¬ Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q.asIdeal →
        Disjoint (S : Set B) (q.asIdeal : Set B))
    (N : Type uN) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (X : (algebraExtensionProblem k B N).CompatibleExtension.{max uk (max uB uN)}) :
    ∃ Y : (algebraExtensionProblem k (Localization S)
        (LocalizedModule S N)).CompatibleExtension.{max uk (max uB uN)},
      squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesLocalizationEquiv k B S hS N
          (Quotient.mk
            (SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.isomorphicSetoid
              (algebraExtensionProblem k B N)) X) =
        Quotient.mk
          (SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.isomorphicSetoid
            (algebraExtensionProblem k (Localization S)
              (LocalizedModule S N))) Y ∧
      IsLocalizedExtension k B S N X Y
declarations.comment: forward map is localization

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.IsLocalizedExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZ8.** The extension `Y` of `S⁻¹B` is obtained from the extension `X` of `B` by
localizing its middle ring at the inverse image of `S`: there is a map of the two middle rings
which is such a localization, and which is compatible both with the quotient maps down to `B`
and `S⁻¹B` and with the identifications of the two kernels with `N` and `S⁻¹N`.
declarations.statement:
def IsLocalizedExtension
    (k : Type uk) (B : Type uB) [Field k] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    (S : Submonoid B) (N : Type uN) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (X : (algebraExtensionProblem k B N).CompatibleExtension.{max uk (max uB uN)})
    (Y : (algebraExtensionProblem k (Localization S)
      (LocalizedModule S N)).CompatibleExtension.{max uk (max uB uN)}) : Prop
declarations.comment: the localization relation between two extensions

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.isSmooth_localizationFunctorData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZ9, the smoothness conclusion.** Let `k` be a field, `P` a finite type

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.bijective_differential_localizationFunctorData
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field, `P` a finite type `k`-algebra and `S ⊆ P` a multiplicative subset such
that `Spec(P) → Spec(k)` is smooth at every point of `V(g)` for every `g ∈ S`. Then the
localization functor `𝓓_P ⟶ 𝓓_{S⁻¹P}` of **Stacks 0DYS**, given by any
`LocalizationFunctorData`, induces a bijection on tangent spaces.

The proof is the source's: the family of extension classes of **Stacks 0DY3** is a bijection of
each tangent space with a first Ext group of the naive cotangent complex, by
`Deformation.Examples.bijective_tangentExtClass`; the functor is compatible with those classes
through the two comparison maps of **Stacks 0GPV**, by
`Deformation.Examples.squareZeroFiberExtClass_localization`; the bijection of **Stacks 0DZ8**
is compatible with the same two maps, by
`Deformation.Examples.naiveCotangentExtOneMap_localizationCoefficientMap`; and restriction along
`P → S⁻¹P` is injective, by
`Stacks.Deformation.injective_naiveCotangentExtOneTowerMap_isLocalization`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_differential_localizationFunctorData
    [Algebra.FiniteType k P]
    (F : LocalizationFunctorData (Λ := Λ) (k := k) S)
    (hsm : ∀ g ∈ S, ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum P, g ∈ q.asIdeal → Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q.asIdeal) :
    Function.Bijective (differential (𝓕 := ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k P)
      (𝓖 := ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k (Localization S))
      isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection
      isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection F.functor)
declarations.comment: the tangent-space assertion: the functor of Stacks 0DYS induces an isomorphism on tangent spaces. Under the tag's own hypotheses: (1) is `Algebra.FiniteType k P` and (2) is `hsm`, smoothness of `Spec(P) → Spec(k)` at every point of `V(g)` for every `g` of `S`. Stated for an arbitrary functor datum of Stacks 0DYS, with no extra hypothesis on the datum

declarations.name: Deformation.hasFlatAlgebraLift_iff_hasFlatAlgebraLift_henselization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZB.** Let `A' → A` be a surjective map of Noetherian rings with nilpotent kernel,
let `A → B` be a finite type flat ring map and let `𝔟 ⊆ B` be an ideal such that
`Spec(B) → Spec(A)` is syntomic on the complement of `V(𝔟)`, that is `A → B_h` is syntomic for
every `h ∈ 𝔟`. Let `(Bʰ, 𝔟ʰ)` be the henselization of the pair `(B, 𝔟)`. Then `B` has a flat lift
to `A'` if and only if `Bʰ` has a flat lift to `A'`.

The proof does not go through Stacks 0DZ2 (which is false); see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasFlatAlgebraLift_iff_hasFlatAlgebraLift_henselization
    (A' A B : Type u) [CommRing A'] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A'] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra A' A] [Algebra A B]
    (hsurjA : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A' A))
    (hnilA : IsNilpotent (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A' A)))
    [Algebra.FiniteType A B] [Module.Flat A B] (b : Ideal B)
    (hsyn : ∀ h ∈ b, Algebra.Syntomic A (Localization.Away h))
    (Bh : Type u) [CommRing Bh] [Algebra B Bh] [Algebra A Bh] [IsScalarTower A B Bh]
    (hhens : HenselianPair Bh (b.map (algebraMap B Bh)))
    (huniv : ∀ (D : Type u) (_ : CommRing D) (K : Ideal D), HenselianPair D K →
      ∀ f : B →+* D, b ≤ K.comap f →
        ∃! g : Bh →+* D, g.comp (algebraMap B Bh) = f ∧
          b.map (algebraMap B Bh) ≤ K.comap g) :
    HasFlatAlgebraLift A' A B ↔ HasFlatAlgebraLift A' A Bh
declarations.comment: The henselization of the pair `(B, 𝔟)` is any `Bʰ` with `(Bʰ, 𝔟Bʰ)` henselian (`hhens`) and initial among henselian pairs under `(B, 𝔟)` (`huniv`), which is the defining universal property of the henselization (Stacks 0A02). The library's construction `henselization B b` has both properties (`henselianPair_henselization`, `henselization_universalProperty`), and the statement for it is `Deformation.hasFlatAlgebraLift_iff_hasFlatAlgebraLift_canonicalHenselization`. The syntomic hypothesis is the affine reading: the complement of `V(𝔟)` is covered by the `D(h)`, `h ∈ 𝔟`, and syntomy is local on the source. Both published proofs rest on Stacks 0DZ2, which is false; the proof here approximates a flat lift over the henselized presentation by solutions over the polynomial presentation and corrects them one power of the kernel at a time (Artin-Rees plus Stacks 07M8 at every level). See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.Deformation.exists_squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesHenselizationEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZC.** Let `k` be a field, `B` a finite type `k`-algebra and `J ⊆ B` an ideal
containing the non-smooth locus of `B` over `k` in its vanishing locus, and let `(Bʰ, Jʰ)` be
the henselization of the pair `(B, J)`. For a `B`-module `N` with `Nʰ = Bʰ ⊗_B N` there is a
bijection between the isomorphism classes of square-zero extensions of `B` by `N` and those of
`Bʰ` by `Nʰ`, namely the one inducing extension of scalars along `B → Bʰ` on the groups
`Ext¹_B(NL_{B/k}, N)` and `Ext¹_{Bʰ}(NL_{Bʰ/k}, Nʰ)` that classify those classes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesHenselizationEquiv
    (k : Type uk) [Field k] (B : Type uB) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k B]
    (J : Ideal B)
    (hsmooth : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B, ¬ Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q.asIdeal → J ≤ q.asIdeal)
    (N : Type uN) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (Bh : Type uB) [CommRing Bh] [Algebra B Bh] [Algebra k Bh] [IsScalarTower k B Bh]
    (hhens : HenselianPair Bh (J.map (algebraMap B Bh)))
    (huniv : ∀ (C : Type uB) (_ : CommRing C) (JC : Ideal C), HenselianPair C JC →
      ∀ f : B →+* C, J ≤ JC.comap f →
        ∃! g : Bh →+* C, g.comp (algebraMap B Bh) = f ∧
          J.map (algebraMap B Bh) ≤ JC.comap g) :
    ∃ e : SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.IsomorphismClasses.{uk, uk, uB, uN,
          max uB uN} (algebraExtensionProblem k B N) ≃
        SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.IsomorphismClasses.{uk, uk, uB,
          max uB uN, max uB uN} (algebraExtensionProblem k Bh (Bh ⊗[B] N)),
      ∀ x, extOneCokernelHenselizationFlatBaseChangeEquiv.{uk, uB, uN} k B N Bh J hhens huniv
              (extCokernelIso k Bh (Bh ⊗[B] N)
                (squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesEquivExtOne k Bh (Bh ⊗[B] N) (e x)))
            = extCokernelIso k B N (squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesEquivExtOne k B N x)
                ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : Bh)

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.bijective_differential_henselizationFunctorData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZD, the tangent-space conclusion, for the map induced by the functor.** Let `k`
be a field, `P` a finite type `k`-algebra and `J ⊆ P` an ideal such that `Spec(P) → Spec(k)` is
smooth on the complement of `V(J)`. The henselization functor `𝓓_P ⟶ 𝓓_{Pʰ}` of **Stacks 0DYT**
induces a bijection on tangent spaces.

The proof is the source's: the family of extension classes of **Stacks 0DY3** is a bijection of
each tangent space with a first Ext group of the naive cotangent complex, by
`Deformation.Examples.bijective_tangentExtClass`; the functor is compatible with those classes
through the two comparison maps of **Stacks 0GPV**, by
`Deformation.Examples.squareZeroFiberExtClass_henselization`; the coefficient comparison is
bijective by the henselization half of **Stacks 0DZC**, in the form
`Deformation.Examples.bijective_naiveCotangentExtOneMap_tensorCoefficientMap`; and restriction
along `P → Pʰ` is injective, by
`Stacks.Deformation.injective_naiveCotangentExtOneTowerMap_henselization`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_differential_henselizationFunctorData [Algebra.FiniteType k P]
    (F : HenselizationFunctorData (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (P := P) J)
    (hsm : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum P, ¬ J ≤ q.asIdeal → Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q.asIdeal) :
    Function.Bijective (differential (𝓕 := ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k P)
      (𝓖 := ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k (henselization P J : Type w))
      isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection
      isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection F.functor)
declarations.comment: the second conclusion, the tangent-space assertion, for the map INDUCED by the functor of Stacks 0DYT: `Deformation.differential` of that functor is bijective, the tangent spaces being those of Stacks 06IH carried by the two deformation categories. Under the tag's own hypotheses and no others: (1) is `Algebra.FiniteType k P` and (2) is `hsm`, smoothness of `Spec(P) -> Spec(k)` at every prime outside `V(J)`. Stated for an arbitrary functor datum of Stacks 0DYT, with no extra hypothesis on the datum. The inputs are the classification of Stacks 0GPT through Stacks 0DY3, the comparison criterion of Stacks 0GPV, the coefficient half of Stacks 0DZC and injectivity of restriction along `P -> P^h`

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.bijective_differential_henselizationFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZD, the tangent-space conclusion, at the canonical henselization functor.** This
is `Deformation.Examples.bijective_differential_henselizationFunctorData` specialized to
`Deformation.Examples.henselizationFunctor`, the functor datum built in the proof of
**Stacks 0DYT**.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_differential_henselizationFunctor [Algebra.FiniteType k P]
    (hsm : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum P, ¬ J ≤ q.asIdeal → Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q.asIdeal) :
    Function.Bijective (differential (𝓕 := ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k P)
      (𝓖 := ringDeformationBasedCategory Λ k (henselization P J : Type w))
      isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection
      isCofiberedInGroupoids_ringDeformationProjection
      (henselizationFunctor (Λ := Λ) (k := k) J).functor)
declarations.comment: the second conclusion, the tangent-space assertion for the map induced by the functor, at the canonical henselization functor `Deformation.Examples.henselizationFunctor` of Stacks 0DYT. Under the tag's own hypotheses and no others

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.isSmooth_henselizationFunctorData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DZD, the smoothness conclusion.** Let `k` be a field, `P` a finite type
`k`-algebra and `J ⊆ P` an ideal such that `Spec(P) → Spec(k)` is smooth on the complement of
`V(J)`. The henselization functor `𝓓_P ⟶ 𝓓_{Pʰ}` of **Stacks 0DYT** is smooth.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSmooth_henselizationFunctorData [Algebra.FiniteType k P]
    (F : HenselizationFunctorData (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (P := P) J)
    (hsm : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum P, ¬ J ≤ q.asIdeal → Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q.asIdeal) :
    IsSmooth F.functor
declarations.comment: the first conclusion, smoothness: the functor of Stacks 0DYT is smooth. Under the tag's own hypotheses and no others: (1) is `Algebra.FiniteType k P` and (2) is `hsm`, smoothness of `Spec(P) -> Spec(k)` at every prime outside `V(J)`. Stated for an arbitrary functor datum of Stacks 0DYT, with no extra hypothesis on the datum. The criterion of Stacks 0DYP reduces it to surjectivity of the differential, which is `Deformation.Examples.bijective_differential_henselizationFunctorData`, and to the correspondence of liftability, which is proved here in `Deformation.Examples.lifts_henselizationFunctorData` -- that is Stacks 0DZB, which Stacks 0DYP needs only across small extensions, whose kernel is square-zero, so the form used is `Deformation.hasFlatAlgebraLift_of_hasFlatAlgebraLift_henselization_of_sqZero` and NO `h0DZ2`-style hypothesis is carried

declarations.doc:

public theorem isSmooth_henselizationFunctor [Algebra.FiniteType k P]
    (hsm : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum P, ¬ J ≤ q.asIdeal → Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q.asIdeal) :
    IsSmooth (henselizationFunctor (Λ := Λ) (k := k) J).functor

declarations.name: Stacks.Deformation.exists_squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesHenselizationTangentEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The case `N = B` of Stacks 0DZC, in the form this file's Ext comparison produces it.**
Let `k` be a field, `B` a finite type `k`-algebra and `J ⊆ B` an ideal containing the non-smooth
locus of `B` over `k` in its vanishing locus, and let `(Bʰ, Jʰ)` be the henselization of the
pair `(B, J)`.  Then the isomorphism classes of square-zero extensions of `B` by `B` are in
bijection with those of `Bʰ` by `Bʰ ⊗_B B`, compatibly with extension of scalars along
